“说自己在所擅长的领域算是个聪明人，并非过分谦虚，”格雷厄姆在回忆录中写道。他的专长在于对那些冷门投资进行精心分析：被忽视的股票或债券、清算资产、破产案例以及套利机会。至少从20世纪20年代初开始，格雷厄姆就一直在宣扬“安全边际”的理念。他在著作中强调，由于未来如同封存的书本，投资者为防范未知风险，应当设法以低于“内在价值”的价格进行投资。《证券分析》中对内在价值的定义是：“那种由事实所支撑的价值，例如资产、收益、股息以及明确的未来前景，这些与通过人为操纵或心理偏差而形成的市场报价截然不同。”（第1章）在他自己的投资生涯中，他的表现也曾从荒谬到卓越（有时又会倒退）。他对数学的快速掌握使他天生适合从事套利活动——他会卖出一只股票的同时买入另一只，或者用同一家公司的普通股票来买卖其可转换债券。通过这种方式，他能够锁定利润，即便无法保证绝对盈利，也在金融市场的波动范围内近乎确定。在20世纪20年代初的一次操作中，他利用了杜邦公司与当时势头正猛的通用汽车公司之间的失衡关系。杜邦在通用汽车中持有大量股份，市场也正是基于这一持股才给这家大型化工企业定价，这意味着该公司的其他业务实际上毫无价值。格雷厄姆利用这一异常情况，买入杜邦的股票，同时卖空相应数量的通用汽车股票。当市场恢复正常，杜邦与通用汽车之间的股价差距如预期那样扩大时，他便获利离场。²³然而，格雷厄姆与后来的许多价值投资者一样，有时也会偏离那种严守安全且低成本投资原则的准则。那位比当年卖掉通用汽车并买入杜邦的先贤稍年轻一些的格雷厄姆，竟被一个看似根本不存在的公司的高调推销者所蒙骗——至少，那家公司并不像负责管理格雷厄姆资金的人所描述的那样繁荣昌盛。曼哈顿上西区的哥伦布圆环上确实有一块电子招牌，上面写着格雷厄姆错误信任的那家公司的名字——萨沃尔德轮胎公司。但正如《证券分析》的作者在回忆录中所承认的，那或许就是该公司存在的唯一实物标志。“据我所知，”格雷厄姆补充道，“也没有人向地方检察官办公室投诉过那个推销者公然窃取公众钱财的行为。”当然，据他自己所说，他也没有这么做。²⁴到1929年，35岁的格雷厄姆已经声名鹊起、财富丰厚。他和妻子雇佣了一支庞大的仆人团队，其中还包括了他一生中第一次也是唯一一次为自己雇用的男仆。格雷厄姆与杰里·纽曼共同创造了令人艳羡的投资业绩，以至于伟大的伯纳德·M·巴鲁克也主动找上了他。格雷厄姆会结束自己的事业去管理巴鲁克的资金吗？“我回答说，”格雷厄姆写道，“他的提议让我深受荣幸——事实上甚至震惊不已——但我无法如此突然地结束与朋友和客户之间如此融洽且令人满意的关系。”²⁵不过，这些关系很快就变得不再那么令人满意了。

<!--en-->
“It’s not undue modesty,” Graham writes in his memoir, “to say that I had become something of a smart cookie in my particular field.” His specialty was the carefully analyzed out-of-the-way investment: castaway stocks or bonds, liquidations, bankruptcies, arbitrage. Since at least the early 1920s, Graham had preached the sermon of the “margin of safety.” As the future is a closed book, he urged in his writings, an investor, as a matter of self-defense against the unknown, should contrive to pay less than “intrinsic” value. Intrinsic value, as defined in *Security Analysis*, is “that value which is justified by the facts, e.g., the assets, earnings, dividends, definite prospects, as distinct, let us say, from market quotations established by artificial manipulation or distorted by psychological excesses.” (Chap. 1)
He himself had gone from the ridiculous to the sublime (and sometimes back again) in the conduct of his own investment career. His quick and easy grasp of mathematics made him a natural arbitrageur. He would sell one stock and simultaneously buy another. Or he would buy or sell shares of stock against the convertible bonds of the identical issuing company. So doing, he would lock in a profit that, if not certain, was as close to guaranteed as the vicissitudes of finance allowed. In one instance, in the early 1920s, he exploited an inefficiency in the relationship between DuPont and the then red-hot General Motors. DuPont held a sizablestake in GM. And it was for that interest alone which the market valued the big chemical company. By implication, the rest of the business was worth nothing. To exploit this anomaly, Graham bought shares in DuPont and sold short the hedge-appropriate number of shares in GM. And when the market came to its senses, and the price gap between DuPont and GM widened in the expected direction, Graham took his profit.²³
However, Graham, like many other value investor after him, sometimes veered from the austere precepts of safe-and-cheap investing. A Graham only slightly younger than the master who sold GM and bought DuPont allowed himself to be hoodwinked by the crooked promoter of a company that seems to not actually have existed—at least, not in anything like the state of glowing prosperity described by the manager of the pool to which Graham entrusted his money. An electric sign in Columbus Circle, on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, did bear the name of the object of Graham's misplaced confidence, Savold Tire. But as the author of *Security Analysis* confessed in his memoir, that could have been the only tangible marker of the company's existence. "Also, as far as I knew," Graham added, "nobody complained to the district attorney's office about the promoter's bare-faced theft of the public's money." Certainly, by his own telling, Graham didn't.²⁴
By 1929, when he was 35, Graham was well on his way to fame and fortune. His wife and he kept a squadron of servants, including—for the first and only time in his life—a manservant for himself. With Jerry Newman, Graham had compiled an investment record so enviable that the great Bernard M. Baruch sought him out. Would Graham wind up his business to manage Baruch's money? "I replied," Graham writes, "that I was highly flattered—flabbergasted, in fact—by his proposal, but I could not end so abruptly the close and highly satisfactory relations I had with my friends and clients."²⁵ Those relations soon became much less satisfactory.

格雷厄姆回忆称，尽管在市场处于顶峰时他感到担忧，却未能按照自己的悲观预感采取行动。1929年危机爆发时，格雷厄姆-纽曼合伙公司拥有250万美元的资本。他们控制着约250万美元的对冲头寸——即买入的股票与卖空的股票相互抵消，此外还持有约450万美元的直接多头仓位。后来格雷厄姆意识到，他们使用杠杆操作本身就已经很糟糕了。更糟糕的是，他们根深蒂固地认为自己持有的股票足够便宜，足以承受任何可能的冲击。

<!--en-->
Graham relates that though he was worried at the top of the market, he failed to act on his bearish hunch. The Graham-Newman partnership went into the 1929 break with $2.5 million of capital. They controlled about $2.5 million in hedged positions—stocks owned long offset by stocks sold short and held, besides, about $4.5 million in outright long positions. It was bad enough that they were leveraged, as Graham later came to realize. Compounding that tactical error was a deeply rooted conviction that the stocks they owned were cheap enough to withstand any imaginable blow.

在1929年的最后一个季度，他们的表现还算可圈可点：跌幅仅为20%，几乎堪称出色。但在1930年他们损失了50%，1931年损失了16%，1932年则仅损失了3%（这一表现同样相当不错），累计亏损达70%。²⁶ 格雷厄姆写道：“我并非主要因未能防范自己所预见的灾难而自责，而是因陷入了那种我既没有性格也不具备能力去享受的奢侈生活。我很快便说服自己，物质幸福的真正关键在于适度的生活标准——这种标准在几乎所有经济环境下都很容易实现”——这便是应用于个人财务的安全边际理念。²⁷ 不能说学术界立刻就将《证券分析》视为价值投资乃至其他相关领域的权威阐释。在《证券分析》第一版出版三年后，切尔西·C·博斯兰德针对格雷厄姆与多德做出重大贡献的领域所撰写的《普通股投资理论》一书中，引用了53个不同的资料来源和43位不同的作者，其中没有一位是格雷厄姆或多德。

<!--en-->
They came through the crash creditably: down by only 20% was, for the final quarter of 1929, almost heroic. But they gave up 50% in 1930, 16% in 1931, and 3% in 1932 (another relatively excellent showing), for a cumulative loss of 70%.²⁶ “I blamed myself not so much for my failure to protect myself against the disaster I had been predicting,” Graham writes, “as for having slipped into an extravagant way of life which I hadn’t the temperament or capacity to enjoy. I quickly convinced myself that the true key to material happiness lay in a modest standard of living which could be achieved with little difficulty under almost all economic conditions”—the margin-of-safety idea applied to personal finance.²⁷
It can’t be said that the academic world immediately clasped *Security Analysis* to its breast as the definitive elucidation of value investing, or of anything else. The aforementioned survey of the field in which Graham and Dodd made their signal contribution, *The Common Stock Theory of Investment*, by Chelcie C. Bosland, published three years after the appearance of the first edition of *Security Analysis*, cited 53 different sources and 43 different authors. Not one of them was named Graham or Dodd.

然而，埃德加·劳伦斯·史密斯确实得到了博斯兰德的全神贯注与尊重。史密斯于1924年出版的《作为长期投资的普通股》一书，挑战了长期以来认为债券本质上优于股票的观念。史密斯指出，美元（即便是1924年那种可兑换黄金的版本）也容易发生通货膨胀，这意味着债权人处于天然的不利地位，而普通股持有者则不然。如果他们投资的公司能够盈利，并且将部分利润留存在企业中（从而为未来的收益做出贡献），那么投资者投资组合的本金价值就会“随着复利的运作而增长”。²⁸史密斯的时机把握得恰到好处——他出版该书不到一年，著名的柯立芝牛市便爆发了。这本仅有129页的《作为长期投资的普通股》为追涨市场提供了有力的理论依据。事实上，股票在长期内往往表现更佳这一观点，已作为不容置疑的真理被纳入美国投资思想的经典体系之中（尽管在20世纪30年代这看起来远非如此明显）。至于格雷厄姆，则对史密斯的论点，或者更确切地说，对其不加批判的乐观应用提出了强烈反对。他指出，以10倍于盈利的价格进行股权投资是一回事，但以20到40倍于盈利的价格投资则是另一回事。此外，史密斯的分析回避了一个重要问题：人们如此热衷且不加批判地来回交易的股票背后，其资产价值究竟是什么。最后，史密斯的论证隐含着一个假设，即普通股未来能够延续其过去的表现。格雷厄姆并不认同这一点。（第27章）不过，虽然格雷厄姆是个严厉的批评者，但他也极为宽容。1939年，他受《政治经济学杂志》委托，负责评论约翰·伯尔·威廉姆斯的《投资价值理论》（这对一位华尔街的实务作家而言实属殊荣）。威廉姆斯的论点既简洁又重要：他认为，一股普通股的投资价值等于所有未来股息的现值。凭借这一关键见解，威廉姆斯希望投资者能避免再次将股价推高到虚高的水平。格雷厄姆拥有量化分析师与行为金融学家的双重才能，他对这一预测表示怀疑。他指出，要运用威廉姆斯的方法，就必须对未来利率走势、利润增长情况以及利润增长停止后的股票终值做出一些极为大胆的假设。“人们不禁会想，”格雷厄姆沉思道，“这些必然具有偶然性的假设，与它们所依赖的极其复杂的数学处理方法之间，是否存在过大的差异？”格雷厄姆以一贯友好的语气结束了文章，赞扬了威廉姆斯冷静务实的分析方式，并补充道：“这种保守主义其实并不存在于作者的公式之中；但如果更高的数学知识能够说服投资者以理智的态度看待股票价格，那么我一定会大力支持这种更高层次的数学应用。”²⁹仅凭格雷厄姆在证券分析方面的技术能力，根本无法让《证券分析》历经多次修订仍持续出版。毕竟，接替格雷厄姆担任哥伦比亚商学院证券分析课程教授的罗杰·F·默里指出，“格雷厄姆与多德的思路……会随着证券市场的周期性变化而吸引或失去追随者。”³⁰在新冠疫情时期那场投机狂潮中，Reddit论坛上的并非所有读者都觉得有必要了解“安全边际”这一概念。

<!--en-->
Edgar Lawrence Smith, however, did receive Bosland’s full and respectful attention. Smith’s *Common Stocks as Long Term Investments*, published in 1924, had challenged the long-held view that bonds were innately superior to equities. For one thing, Smith argued, the dollar (even the gold-convertible 1924 edition) was inflation-prone, which meant that creditors were inherently disadvantaged. Not so the owners of common stock. If the companies in which they invested earned a profit, and if a portion of that profit were retained in the business(thereby contributing to future earnings), the principal value of an investor's portfolio would tend "to increase in accordance with the operation of compound interest."²⁸
Smith's timing was impeccable. Not a year after he published, the great Coolidge bull market erupted. *Common Stocks as Long Term Investments*, only 129 pages long, provided a handy rationale for chasing the market higher. That stocks do, in fact, tend to excel in the long run has entered the canon of American investment thought as a revealed truth (though it looked anything but obvious in the 1930s). For his part, Graham entered a strong dissent to Smith's thesis, or more exactly, its uncritical bullish application. It was one thing to pay 10 times earnings for an equity investment, he notes, quite another to pay 20 to 40 times earnings. Besides, the Smith analysis skirted the important question of what asset values lay behind the stock certificates that people so feverishly and uncritically traded back and forth. Finally, embedded in Smith's argument was the assumption that common stocks could be counted on to deliver in the future what they had done in the past. Graham was not a believer. (Chap. 27)
If Graham was a hard critic, however, he was also a generous one. In 1939 he was given John Burr Williams's *The Theory of Investment Value* to review for the *Journal of Political Economy* (no small honor for a Wall Street author-practitioner). Williams's thesis was as important as it was concise. The investment value of a common stock is the present value of all future dividends, the author proposed. Armed with that critical knowledge, Williams ventured to hope, investors might restrain themselves from bidding stocks back up to the moon again. Graham, in whose capacious brain dwelled the talents both of the quant and of the behavioral financier, voiced his doubts about that forecast. In order to apply Williams's method, he pointed out, one needed to make some very large assumptions about the future course of interest rates, the growth of profit, and the terminal value of the shares when growth stops. "One wonders," Graham mused, "whether there may not be too great a discrepancy between the necessarily hit-or-miss character of theseassumptions and the highly refined mathematical treatment to which they are subjected.” Graham closed his essay on a characteristically friendly note, commending Williams for the refreshing level-headedness of his approach and adding: “This conservatism is not really implicit in the author’s formulas; but if the investor can be persuaded by higher algebra to take a sane attitude toward common-stock prices, the reviewer will cast a loud vote for higher algebra.”²⁹
Graham’s technical accomplishments in securities analysis, by themselves, could hardly have carried *Security Analysis* through its many editions. After all, observes Roger F. Murray, who succeeded Graham as professor of the securities analysis course at Columbia Business School, “The Graham and Dodd approach . . . gains and loses adherents with the passing phases of the securities markets.”³⁰ Not all readers of the Reddit message boards during the Covid-era speculative free-for-all found it necessary to familiarize themselves with the concept of a margin of safety.

在我看来，正是《证券分析》所展现的智慧、人文情怀与幽默感，才解释了这本书为何能长久流传，以及为何格雷厄姆的读者们会如此忠贞地喜爱它。还有哪位华尔街的赚钱高手能像格雷厄姆那样，既精通古典语言与文学，又熟悉自己所处时代的金融历史呢？我敢以价值投资者的自信断言：没有！

<!--en-->
Rather, it’s the intelligence, humanity, and good humor of *Security Analysis* that to me explain the book’s long life and the adoring loyalty of Graham’s readers. Was there ever a Wall Street moneymaker better steeped than Graham in classical languages and literature *and* in the financial history of his own time? I would bet “no” with all the confidence of a value investor laying down money to buy a bargain.

然而，这位伟大的投资思想家与实践者，在某种程度上也是他所处时代的囚徒。他能意识到自己经历的一些事情是独一无二的，大萧条实际上是一种巨大的异常现象。如果说有谁明白将当前的经验套用到不可预测的未来是多么愚蠢，那一定是格雷厄姆。然而，这位投资领域的哲学王者，在用了727页的篇幅（还不包括内容丰富的附录）描述了谨慎且风险厌恶的投资者如何在各种宏观经济环境下取得成功之后，却得出了一个惊人的结论。

<!--en-->
Yet this great investment thinker and doer was, to a degree, a prisoner of his own times. He could see that some of the experiences through which he lived were unique, that the Great Depression was, in fact, a great anomaly. If anyone understood the folly of projecting current experience into the unpredictable future, it was Graham. Yet this investment philosopher king, having spent 727 pages (not including the gold mine of an appendix) describing how a careful and risk-averse investor could prosper in every kind of macroeconomic condition, arrives at a remarkable conclusion.

“他该如何投资？”格雷厄姆提出这个问题，而他起初也有些犹豫地回答：他怎有资格为美国各类慈善与教育机构的高手们指明方向？但随后他做出了惊人的表态。“在我们看来，”格雷厄姆写道，“那些能够依靠高等级固定价值证券带来的较低收益维持运营的机构，应当将投资范围限制在这一领域。我们怀疑，过去股票指数更高的表现本身是否足以支撑股票投资计划所带来的沉重责任与持续存在的不确定性。”（第52章）这位最伟大的价值投资者真的是这个意思吗？那个在经济大萧条时期承受巨额亏损却能在战后繁荣时代继续取得成功的人，真的认为股票不值得投入精力吗？1940年，随着新世界大战推动罗斯福政府的财政与货币政策，高等级企业债券的收益率仅为2.75%，而优质股票的收益率为5.1%。格雷厄姆是想说债券比股票更安全吗？没错，他确实这么说了。如果霍默能点头，格雷厄姆也能——我们所有人也同样可以。这也应成为一条教训。

<!--en-->
How should he invest? Graham asks, and he answers, at first diffidently: Who is he to prescribe for the experienced financiers at the head of America’s philanthropic andeducational institutions? But then he takes the astonishing plunge. “An institution,” Graham writes, “that can manage to get along on the low income provided by high-grade fixed-value issues should, in our opinion, confine its holdings to this field. We doubt if the better performance of common-stock indexes over past periods will, in itself, warrant the heavy responsibilities and the recurring uncertainties that are inseparable from a common-stock investment program.” (Chap. 52)
Could the greatest value investor have meant that? Did the man who stuck it out through ruinous losses in the Depression years and went on to thrive in the prosperous postwar era really mean that common stocks were not worth the bother? In 1940, with a new world war fanning the Roosevelt administration’s fiscal and monetary policies, high-grade corporate bonds yielded just 2.75%, while blue-chip equities delivered 5.1%. Did Graham mean to say that bonds were a safer proposition than stocks? Well, he did say it. If Homer could nod, so could Graham—and so can the rest of us, whoever we are. Let that, too, be a lesson.

在回忆录即将结束时，格雷厄姆允许自己思考自己的遗产：“如果我的名字还有可能被后代记住——前提是还有后代存在的话——那一定是因为我提出了商品储备货币计划。”³¹格雷厄姆的这一计划虽曾被多次讨论但从未实施，其核心是通过让美国财政部按预定固定价格买卖30种基础原材料的组合，来稳定物价，从而平抑经济周期。实际上，金本位制将变成三十分之一的金本位制，其余的货币担保则由各种非黄金材料构成。

<!--en-->
Near the close of his memoirs, Graham allows himself to speculate on his legacy: “If my name has any chance of being remembered by future generations—assuming that there will be future generations—it will be as inventor of the Commodity Reserve Currency Plan.”³¹ Graham’s plan, intermittently discussed but never implemented, was to iron out the business cycle by directing the U.S. Treasury to stabilize the price level by standing ready to buy and sell a portfolio of 30 basic raw materials at predetermined fixed prices. In effect, the gold standard would become one-thirtieth of a gold standard, with a potpourri of nongold materials furnishing the balance of the monetary collateral.

事实上，格雷厄姆——业余剧作家、终身的古典文化爱好者，以及特许金融分析师运动的奠基人之一——将自己真正的遗产写在了这本经久不衰的著作中。当然，这也会是“市场先生”的看法。这本稀有初版的中间价高达2万美元，这意味着从1934年的原价5美元计算，年化回报率接近10%³²。即便这一数字略低于同期标准普尔500指数在股息再投资条件下的10.8%复合年化回报率，但格雷厄姆的忠实读者也能理解其中原因。《证券分析》为四代读者带来的免税股息，远比普通股东收到的股息更为珍贵。¹格雷厄姆，《华尔街院长回忆录》，西摩·查特曼编（纽约：麦格劳-希尔，1996年），第142页。²路易斯·里奇，“智慧与证券”，《纽约时报》，1934年12月2日，BR13版。³古斯塔夫·卡塞尔，“进步必须终结吗？”，《交易所报》，1940年1月。⁴《交易所报》，“为何证券经纪人仍在经营？”，1940年9月。⁵詹姆斯·格兰特，《繁荣的困境》（纽约：兰登书屋，1996年），第84页。⁶切尔西·C·博斯兰德，《普通股投资理论》（纽约：罗纳德出版社，1937年），第74页。⁷彭博新闻，“信贷宽松时代结束，美国僵尸企业面临缓慢死亡”，2022年5月31日。⁸《财富》杂志，“华尔街本身”，1937年6月。⁹《纽约时报》，1939年10月3日，第38页。¹⁰《交易所报》，1940年3月。¹¹弗雷德·施韦德，《客户的游艇去哪儿了？》（纽约：西蒙与舒斯特，1940年），第28页。¹²本杰明·M·安德森，《经济学与公共福利》（纽约：范诺斯特兰德，1949年），第431页。¹³罗伯特·A·洛维特，“金边下的不安”，《周六晚邮报》，1937年4月3日。¹⁴DTCC 2021年年度报告，第56页。¹⁵Allan Sloan在Yahoo Finance上发表的“投资的民主化”一文中引用了Morningstar Direct的数据，2022年5月22日。¹⁶《华尔街院长回忆录》，第169页。¹⁷《华尔街院长回忆录》，第106页。

<!--en-->
The truth is that Graham—amateur playwright, lifetime classicist, a founding spirit of the Chartered Financial Analyst movement—wrote his true legacy in the pages of this durable volume. Certainly, that would be Mr. Market’s view. The $20,000 median value of a rare first edition copy represents a nearly 10% per annum rate of return from the original, 1934cover price of $5.³² And if that achievement falls a little short of the 10.8% compound annual return of the Standard & Poor's 500 over the same interval, with dividends reinvested, a Graham devotee will understand why. The nontaxable dividends that *Security Analysis* has paid its four generations of readers are more precious than the kind that a stockholder gets in the mail.

INTRODUCTION TO THE SECOND EDITION

## 投资政策问题

<!--en-->
*Problems of Investment Policy*

虽然严格来说，证券分析可以在不参照任何具体的投资计划或标准的情况下进行，但这种功能上的专业化其实并不现实。对资产负债表和损益表的仔细审查、对相关或类似证券的比较、以及对债券和优先股背后条款及保护性契约的研究——这些证券分析师的典型工作总是以某种买卖的实际意图为前提，并且必须置于更广泛的投资原则或投机准则背景下加以理解。在本书中，我们不会试图在投资理论与分析技术之间划出精确的界限，而是会结合二者在金融领域中紧密关联的关系来展开论述。

<!--en-->
Although, strictly speaking, security analysis may be carried on without reference to any definite program or standards of investment, such a specialization of functions would be quite unrealistic. Critical examination of balance sheets and income accounts, comparisons of related or similar issues, studies of the terms and protective covenants behind bonds and preferred stocks—these typical activities of the securities analyst are invariably carried on with some practical idea of purchase or sale in mind, and they must be viewed against a broader background of investment principles, or perhaps of speculative precepts. In this work we shall not strive for a precise demarcation between investment theory and analytical technique but at times shall combine the two elements in the close relationship that they possess in the world of finance.

因此，最好在阐述之前先简要回顾证券购买者所面临的政策问题。这样的讨论至少在一定程度上会受到本章撰写时所处环境的影响。但我们希望能够充分考虑到变化的可能性，从而使我们的结论具有更重要的意义。事实上，我们将这种变化视为金融世界中的核心要素。为更好地理解这一点，我们以概要形式呈现了一些数据，用以说明过去二十五年间价值与标准所经历的变迁与动荡。

<!--en-->
It seems best, therefore, to preface our exposition with a concise review of the problems of policy that confront the security buyer. Such a discussion must be colored, in part at least, by the conditions prevailing when this chapter was written. But it is hoped that enough allowance will be made for the possibility of change to give our conclusions more than passing interest and value. Indeed, we consider this element of change as a central fact in the financial universe. For a better understanding of this point we are presenting some data, in conspectus form, designed to illustrate the reversals and upheavals in values and standards that have developed in the past quarter century.

选择1911–1913年、1923–1925年以及1936–1938年这三个时期，是为了尽可能接近过去二十五年中出现的“正常”或相对稳定的状态。在第一和第二个三年期之间，经历了战争带来的崩溃与短暂的繁荣，随后是战后的犹豫、通货膨胀以及严重的经济萧条。在1925年至1936年间，则出现了“新时代繁荣”、巨大的崩溃与萧条，以及向正常状态逐步恢复的过程。但如果仔细观察这三个三年期本身，就会发现即使在相对正常的时期，不稳定趋势也在不断加剧。这一点从下图A中逐渐扩大的曲线中可以清晰地看出来，该曲线反映了相关年份内整体商业与工业股票价格的波动情况。

<!--en-->
The three reference periods 1911–1913, 1923–1925, and 1936–1938 were selected to represent the nearest approximations to “normal,” or relative stability, that could be found at intervals during the past quarter century. Between the first and second triennium we had the war collapse and hecticprosperity, followed by the postwar hesitation, inflation, and deep depression. Between 1925 and 1936 we had the “new-era boom,” the great collapse and depression, and a somewhat irregular recovery towards normal. But if we examine the three-year periods themselves, we cannot fail to be struck by the increasing tendency toward instability even in relatively normal times. This is shown vividly in the progressive widening of the graphs in Chart A, that follows, which trace the fluctuations in general business and industrial stock prices during the years in question.

Axe & Co., Inc.提供。† 高价、低价及平均价格均与各时期的平均收益及股息进行对比。‡ 1936–1938年的数据已作调整，以反映40%的股票分红情况。§ 数据已作调整，以反映1913年至1930年间各种股票分红及拆股情况，相当于1912年的1股相当于1936年的约25股。|| 不包括1925年作为股息分配的Electric Bond and Share Securities Corporation的1股。¶ 1936–1938年的数据已作调整，以反映1926年的6股合1股的分红比例。从这些发展态势中推断未来将出现更严重的不稳定状况实属轻率。但同样不明智的是忽视已发生事件的重要性，过早地回到1925年那种认为我们正稳步迈向更高稳定性与更繁荣状态的乐观信念。当前形势似乎要求我们在采纳任何关于未来的理论时保持谨慎，并采取灵活且开放的投资策略。在有了这些注意事项的指引下，让我们简要探讨一些类型的投资问题。

It would be foolhardy to deduce from these developments that we must expect still greater instability in the future. But it would be equally imprudent to minimize the significance of what has happened and to return overreadily to the comfortable conviction of 1925 that we were moving steadily towards both greater stability and greater prosperity. The times would seem to call for caution in embracing any theory as to the future and for flexible and open-minded investment policies. With these caveats to guide us, let us proceed to consider briefly certain types of investment problems.

## A. 高等级债券与优先股投资

<!--en-->
*A. INVESTMENT IN HIGH-GRADE BONDS AND PREFERRED STOCKS*

如今，债券投资所面临的难题远比1913年时更为复杂。那时的主要问题是如何在保障安全的前提下获得最高收益；如果投资者对收益较低的标准债券（几乎全是铁路抵押债券）感到满意，他甚至可以“闭着眼睛购买、存放起来然后忘掉它们”。而现在，投资者必须应对三重问题：利息与本金的安全性、债券收益率与价格的未来走势，以及美元的未来价值。描述这些困境很容易，但要圆满解决它们则几乎是不可能的。

<!--en-->
Bond investment presents many more perplexing problems today than seemed to be true in 1913. The chief question then was how to get the highest yield commensurate with safety; and if the investor was satisfied with the lower yielding standard issues (nearly all consisting of railroad mortgage bonds), he could supposedly “buy them with his eyes shut and put them away and forget them.” Now the investor must wrestle with a threefold problem: safety of interest and principal, the future of bond yields and prices, and the future value of the dollar. To describe the dilemma is easy; to resolve it satisfactorily seems next to impossible.

1. **利息与本金的安全性。** 过去二十年中发生的两次严重经济衰退，以及大量曾被认为绝对安全的铁路债券的崩溃，都表明自满的债券投资者未来可能还会面临更多意外冲击。那种“永久性投资”——无需变动、无需操心的旧观念无疑已经彻底消失。不过，我们的研究认为，只要通过足够严格的筛选标准并定期进行审查，投资者就能避免过去那些导致重大损失的状况，即便在经济衰退时期，其利息与本金的回报率也能保持在令人满意的水平。仔细筛选时必须充分考虑未来前景，但我们并不认为投资者需要具备先见之明，也不必只选择那些利润增长潜力极强的公司。这些建议同样适用于（真正）高等级的优先股以及债券。

<!--en-->
1. **Safety of Interest and Principal.** Two serious depressions in the past twenty years, and the collapse of an enormous volume of railroad issues once thought safe beyond question, suggest that the future may have further rude shocks for the complacent bond investor. The old idea of “permanent investments,” exempt from change and free from care, is no doubt permanently gone. Our studies lead us to conclude, however, that by sufficiently stringent standards of selection and reasonably frequent scrutiny thereafter the investor should be able to escape most of the serious losses that have distracted him in the past, so that his collection of interest and principal should work out at a satisfactory percentage even in times of depression. Careful selection must include a due regard to future prospects, but we do not consider that theinvestor need be clairvoyant or that he must confine himself to companies that hold forth exceptional promise of expanding profits. These remarks relate to (really) high-grade preferred stocks as well as to bonds.

## 2. 利率与债券价格的未来走势。

<!--en-->
*2. Future of Interest Rates and Bond Prices.*

短期和长期债券所提供的前所未有的低收益率，很可能会让投资者担忧，原因不仅在于他们对资金带来的微薄回报感到不满。如果这些低利率只是暂时的，随后又回升到之前的水平，长期债券的市场价值可能会下跌25%甚至更多。这样的价格下跌相当于损失了大约十年的利息。1934年时我们就认为必须认真考虑这种可能性，因为当时的低利率很可能是经济不景气导致的现象，而随着商业活动的恢复，利率很可能会大幅上升。但在1936–1937年经济显著扩张的情况下，这些低利率仍持续多年，这强烈表明应将这一状况视为资本过剩、政府财政政策或两者共同作用所导致的既定结果。

<!--en-->
The unprecedentedly low yields offered by both short- and long-term bond issues may well cause concern to the investor for other reasons than a natural dissatisfaction with the small return that his money brings him. If these low rates should prove temporary and are followed by a rise to previous levels, long-term bond prices could lose some 25%, or more, of their market value. Such a price decline would be equivalent to the loss of perhaps ten years' interest. In 1934 we felt that this possibility must be taken seriously into account, because the low interest rates then current might well have been a phenomenon of subnormal business, subject to a radical advance with returning trade activity. But the persistence of these low rates for many years, and in the face of the considerable business expansion of 1936–1937, would argue strongly for the acceptance of this condition as a well-established result of a plethora of capital or of governmental fiscal policy or of both.

1939年欧洲战争的爆发给这个问题带来了新的不确定性。第一次世界大战导致了利率的急剧上升以及高等级债券价格的相应暴跌。1914年和1939年的情况既有相似之处也有差异，因此做出预测风险极高。显然，从1940年初的水平来看，债券价格出现大幅下跌的危险依然存在；然而，采取等待此类情况出现的非投资策略则面临着诸多实际障碍。或许，选择从购买日起不超过十五年到期期限的债券，是应对这种不确定局势最合理的做法。

<!--en-->
A new uncertainty has been injected into this question by the outbreak of a European war in 1939. The first World War brought about a sharp increase in interest rates and a corresponding severe fall in high-grade bond prices. There are sufficient similarities and differences, both, between the 1914 and the 1939 situations to make prediction too risky for comfort. Obviously the danger of a substantial fall in bond prices (from the level of early 1940) is still a real one; yet a policy of noninvestment awaiting such a contingency is open to many practical objections. Perhaps a partiality to maturities no longer than, say, fifteen years from purchase date may be the most logical reaction to this uncertain situation.

对于小投资者而言，美国储蓄债券为解决这个问题（以及前一个问题）提供了完美的方案，因为“由持有人自行选择赎回”的权利能够确保他们不会以过低的价格出售债券。正如我们将在后续更详细的讨论中指出的那样，这类小额储蓄债券的出现确实彻底改变了大多数证券投资者的处境。

<!--en-->
For the small investor, United States Savings Bonds present a perfect solution of this problem (as well as the one preceding), since the right of redemption at the *option of the holder* guarantees them against a lower price. As we shall point out in a more detailed discussion, the advent of these baby bonds has truly revolutionized the position of most security buyers.

**3. 美元的价值。** 如果投资者确信美元的购买力将会大幅下降，他无疑会优先选择普通股或大宗商品而非债券。只要通常意义上的通货膨胀仍有可能发生，普通债券持有者的投资策略就会变得更加复杂。支持与反对最终出现通货膨胀的观点都极具说服力，我们不得不拒绝在两者之间做出选择。自1933年以来的物价走势似乎印证了人们对于通货膨胀的担忧并不存在，但过去的情况并不一定能够决定未来。出于谨慎考虑，投资策略或许应当采取某种折中方案，纳入普通股或实物资产成分，以此为美元价值大幅下跌提供一定的保护。不过这种混合型策略本身也会带来诸多难题；归根结底，每位投资者都必须自行决定愿意承担哪种替代风险。

<!--en-->
**3. The Value of the Dollar.** If the investor were certain that the purchasing power of the dollar is going to decline substantially, he undoubtedly should prefer common stocks or commodities to bonds. To the extent that inflation, in the sense commonly employed, remains a possibility, the investment policy of the typical bond buyer is made more perplexing. Thearguments for and against ultimate inflation are both unusually weighty, and we must decline to choose between them. The course of the price level since 1933 would seem to belie inflation fears, but the past is not necessarily conclusive as to the future. Prudence may suggest some compromise in investment policy, to include a component of common stocks or tangible assets, designed to afford some protection against a serious fall in the dollar's value. Such a hybrid policy would involve difficult problems of its own; and in the last analysis each investor must decide for himself which of the alternative risks he would prefer to run.

# B. 投机性债券与优先股

<!--en-->
*B. SPECULATIVE BONDS AND PREFERRED STOCKS*

这一大类证券所面临的问题并非其自身固有的，而是源自于介于其间的投资债券和普通股所存在的问题。在我们看来，购买投机性高级证券的基本原则始终如一：（1）本金损失的风险不能仅通过更高的收益率来弥补，还必须伴随相应的本金盈利机会；（2）将这类证券视为普通股来对待，同时认识到其收益要求较低，通常比将其视为低等级的高级证券更为稳妥。

<!--en-->
The problems related to this large class of securities are not inherent in the class itself, but are rather derived from those of investment bonds and of common stocks, between which they lie. The broad principles underlying the purchase of speculative senior issues remain, in our opinion, the same as they always were: (1) A risk of principal loss may not be offset by a higher yield alone but must be accompanied by a commensurate chance of principal profit; (2) it is generally sounder to approach these issues as if they were common stocks, but recognizing their limited claims, than it is to consider them as an inferior type of senior security.

## C. 普通股投资的问题

<!--en-->
*C. THE PROBLEM OF COMMON-STOCK INVESTMENT*

通常所理解的普通股投机，其概念虽然容易理解，但要成功实施却并非易事。投机者确实会根据对整体市场、特定股票走势的判断，或是对公司未来发展的预期来冒险投入资金。毫无疑问，随着时间的推移，投机者面临的问题有所变化，但我们认为，取得成功所需的素质与技能，以及对其不利的数学概率，目前与过去并无本质区别。不过，股票投机本身并不属于本书的讨论范围。

<!--en-->
Common-stock speculation, as the term has always been generally understood, is not so difficult to understand as it is to practice successfully. The speculator admittedly risks his money upon his guess or judgment as to the general market or the action of a particular stock or possibly on some future development in the company's affairs. No doubt the speculator's problems have changed somewhat with the years, but we incline to the view that the qualities and training necessary for success, as well as the mathematical oddsagainst him, are not vitally different now from what they were before. But stock speculation, as such, does not come within the scope of this volume.

**当前实践。** 然而，我们关注的是普通股*投资*，暂将其定义为基于价值分析并在明确的本金安全标准约束下进行的购买行为。若从当前实践来探寻这些标准，我们几乎只能找到“好股票就是好的投资”这一较为模糊的概念。“好”股票指的是：（1）业绩表现良好、有望在未来带来良好回报的领先企业；或（2）财务状况稳健、被认为未来盈利前景特别诱人的企业。（截至1940年初，可口可乐可作为（1）的例子，雅培实验室可作为（2）的例子，通用电气则同时符合这两种特征。）

<!--en-->
**Current Practice.** We are concerned, however, with common-stock *investment*, which we shall define provisionally as purchases based upon analysis of value and controlled by definite standards of safety of principal. If we look to current practice to discern what these standards are, we find little beyond the rather indefinite concept that “a good stock is a good investment.” “Good” stocks are those of either (1) leading companies with satisfactory records, a combination relied on to produce favorable results in the future; or (2) any well-financed enterprise believed to have especially attractive prospects of increased future earnings. (As of early 1940, we may cite Coca-Cola as an example of (1), Abbott Laboratories as an example of (2), and General Electric as an example of both.)

尽管股市对于用于投资的普通股的*质量*有着非常明确且看似合理的标准，但其*数量*标准——即价格与可确定价值之间的关系标准——却极为模糊，几乎不存在。资产负债表上的数值被认为完全无关紧要。当存在明显趋势时，平均收益的意义也微乎其微。所谓的“市盈率”也有不同的应用方式，有时用于过去，有时用于现在，有时用于不久的将来。但这一比率本身很难被称为标准，因为它是由投资实践所决定的，而非反过来控制投资实践。换句话说，任何股票的“正确”市盈率就是市场所认定的那个数值。从1926年至今，我们找不到任何证据表明普通股投资者群体曾因市盈率过高而抛售所持股票。

<!--en-->
But although the stock market has very definite and apparently logical ideas as to the *quality* of the common stocks that it buys for investment, its *quantitative* standards—governing the relation of price to determinable value—are so indefinite as to be almost nonexistent. Balance-sheet values are considered to be entirely out of the picture. Average earnings have little significance when there is a marked trend. The so-called “price-earnings ratio” is applied variously, sometimes to the past, sometimes to the present, and sometimes to the near future. But the ratio itself can scarcely be called a standard, since it is controlled by investment practice instead of controlling it. In other words the “right” price-earnings ratio for any stock is what the market says it is. We can find no evidence that at any time from 1926 to date common-stock investors as a class have sold their holdings because the price-earnings ratios were too high.

鉴于几乎完全缺乏明确的评判标准，包括几乎所有的投资信托基金在内的普通股投资者的现行行为究竟如何才能被恰当地称为“投资”，这实在超出了我们的理解范围。将其称为“对优质公司股票的投机”要合乎逻辑得多，也更有帮助。事实上，这类“投资”在股市中的表现与过去的投机行为并无二致，或许只有保证金因素略有不同。1929年股市崩盘后的几年里，通过比较通用电气自1930年以来的股价波动幅度与普通股票的波动幅度，可以有力地印证这一观点。以下数据表明，作为当今工业领域最顶尖、根基最深厚的投资品种之一，通用电气的股价波动幅度甚至超过了普通股票。

<!--en-->
How the present practice of common-stock investors, including the investment trusts almost without exception, can properly be termed *investment*, in view of this virtual absence of controlling standards, is more than we can fathom. It would be far more logical and helpful to call it “speculation in stocks of strong companies.” Certainly the results in the stock marketof such “investment” have been indistinguishable from those of old-time speculation, except perhaps for the margin element. A striking confirmation of this statement, as applied to the years after the 1929 crash, is found by comparing the price range of General Electric since 1930 with that of common stocks generally. The following figures show that General Electric common, which is perhaps the premier and undoubtedly the longest entrenched investment issue in the industrial field today, has fluctuated more widely in market price than have the rank and file of common stocks.

1937年股市称通用电气公司的价值为18.7亿美元，而几乎一年后又称其价值仅为7.84亿美元，这种说法简直荒谬至极。显然，在短短十二个月内，并没有任何因素导致这家强大企业的价值缩水过半，投资者也从未声称1937年至1938年间收益的下降会对该公司未来产生永久性影响。由于市场情绪乐观，通用电气的股价曾达到64又7/8点；而当同样的人群变得悲观时，股价则跌至27又1/4点。将这样的股价视为“投资价值”或“投资者评估结果”，无异于对英语语言或常识的严重扭曲，甚至两者皆有。

<!--en-->
It was little short of nonsense for the stock market to say in 1937 that General Electric Company was worth $1,870,000,000 and almost precisely a year later that it was worth only $784,000,000. Certainly nothing had happened within twelve months' time to destroy more than half the value of this powerful enterprise, nor did investors even pretend to claim that the falling off in earnings from 1937 to 1938 had any permanent significance for the future of the company. General Electric sold at 64 7/8 because the public was in an optimistic frame of mind and at 27 1/4 because the same people were pessimistic. To speak of these prices as representing “investment values” or the “appraisal ofinvestors” is to do violence either to the English language or to common sense, or both.

**四个问题。**假设普通股买家希望寻找明确的投标准则来指导自己的投资行为，他很可能会关注以下四个问题：（1）企业利润的总体未来走势；（2）不同类型公司之间的质量差异；（3）利率对其应要求的股息或收益回报的影响；最后是（4）其买卖决策应在多大程度上受时机因素而非价格因素的制约。

<!--en-->
**Four Problems.** Assuming that a common-stock buyer were to seek definite investment standards by which to guide his operations, he might well direct his attention to four questions: (1) the general future of corporation profits, (2) the differential in quality between one type of company and another, (3) the influence of interest rates on the dividends or earnings return that he should demand, and finally (4) the extent to which his purchases and sales should be governed by the factor of timing as distinct from price.

*企业利润的总体未来走势。*如果结合过往经验来研究这些问题，我们最直接的感受很可能是对股市在涉及未来发展的各类重大问题上的判断能力持高度怀疑态度。第一张表格中的数据清楚地显示，在1926年之前，市场总体上低估了工业类普通股票的整体吸引力。这些股票的价格通常只是对过去和当前收益的谨慎评估，完全没有体现出对处于快速发展的经济体中那些领先企业所具备的增长潜力的溢价。1913年时，铁路及牵引类股票占据了投资债券和股票的大部分。到1925年，随着汽车的发展，许多城市铁路的投资已面临风险，但即便如此，人们仍未意识到蒸汽铁路也会面临类似的威胁。

<!--en-->
*The General Future of Corporate Profits.* If we study these questions in the light of past experience, our most pronounced reaction is likely to be a wholesome scepticism as to the soundness of the stock market’s judgment on all broad matters relating to the future. The data in our first table show quite clearly that the market underestimated the attractiveness of industrial common stocks as a whole in the years prior to 1926. Their prices generally represented a rather cautious appraisal of past and current earnings, with no signs of any premium being paid for the possibilities of growth inherent in the leading enterprises of a rapidly expanding commonwealth. In 1913 railroad and traction issues made up the bulk of investment bonds and stocks. By 1925 a large part of the investment in street railways had been endangered by the development of the automobile, but even then there was no disposition to apprehend a similar threat to the steam railroads.

人们对普通股未来增长因素的广泛认可，最初作为股市的一种影响力出现时，实际上我国经济扩张中最具活力的因素（如领土开发及人口快速增长）已经不再起作用，经济正因这些增长限制而面临严重的不稳定问题。在那个新时代，几乎所有有过一段收益上升期的股票都被高估，尤其是公用事业和连锁店类股票更受青睐。即便在1931年，人们仍以高价购买这些股票，丝毫没有意识到它们存在的固有局限；五年后，市场依然未能认识到铁路债券及股票状况正在发生的根本性变化。

<!--en-->
The widespread recognition of the factor of future growth in common stocks first asserted itself as a stock-market influence at a time when in fact the most dynamic factors in our national expansion (territorial development and rapid accretions of population) were no longer operative, and our economy was about to face grave problems of instability arising from these very checks to the factor of growth. The overvaluations of the new-era years extended to nearly every issue that had even a short period of increasing earnings to recommend it, but especial favor was accorded the public-utility and chain-store groups. Even as late as 1931 the highprices paid for these issues showed no realization of their inherent limitations, just as five years later the market still failed to appreciate the critical changes taking place in the position of railroad bonds as well as stocks.

*质量差异。* 1940年的股市具有明确的特征，这些特征主要源于近期的经验以及未来相当明显的前景。相比以往任何时候，市场更倾向于青睐规模更大、实力更强的企业。1929年以来的历史数据也支持了这一观点——我们认为，相比次要企业，领先企业不仅更能抵御经济衰退，其盈利能力的恢复也更为彻底。此外，市场还像往常一样偏爱某些行业群体，包括其中的中小型企业。其中最突出的当属化工和航空行业的股票：前者得益于其在研发方面的出色增长表现，后者则因大量军火订单的涌入而受益。

<!--en-->
*Quality Differentials.* The stock market of 1940 has its well-defined characteristics, founded chiefly on the experience of the recent past and on the rather obvious prospects of the future. The tendency to favor the larger and stronger companies is perhaps more pronounced than ever. This is supported by the record since 1929, which indicates, we believe, both better resistance to depression and a more complete recovery of earning power in the case of the leading than of the secondary companies. There is also the usual predilection for certain industrial groups, including companies of smaller size therein. Most prominent are the chemical and aviation shares—the former because of their really remarkable record of growth through research, the latter because of the great influx of armament orders.

但当前股市的这些偏好虽然容易理解，却可能在持怀疑态度的人心中引发一些疑问。首先需要考虑的是那些知名股票与不太受关注的股票之间的巨大价格差距。如果以1934–1939年的平均收益作为标准，“优质股票”的售价似乎是其他股票的2到3倍。从资产价值来看，这种差距更为显著，因为显然那些受青睐的股票所获得的资本回报要高得多。目前人们甚至几乎忽视资产价值，就连流动资产也很少被关注，因此即便是一家经营状况尚可的企业，若拥有充足的营运资金，其股价也很可能远低于其清算价值。

<!--en-->
But these preferences of the current stock market, although easily understood, may raise some questions in the minds of the sceptical. First to be considered is the extraordinary disparity between the prices of prominent and less popular issues. If average earnings of 1934–1939 are taken as a criterion, the “good stocks” would appear to be selling about two to three times as high as other issues. In terms of asset values the divergence is far greater, since obviously the popular issues have earned a much larger return on their invested capital. The ignoring of asset values has reached a stage where even current assets receive very little attention, so that even a moderately successful enterprise is likely to be selling at considerably less than its liquidating value if it happens to be rich in working capital.

在分析“优质股票”与其他股票的关系时，必须结合对美国整体商业环境的预期。对此做出任何预测都是极为不理智的；但需要指出的是，过去十五年的记录本身并不足以作为预期股价与利润长期上升的依据。既然我们是通过过去来判断未来，就必须认识到1940年的“表面”前景与1924年相比已经发生了彻底变化。在1924年，生产水平的长期上升以及被视为“正常水平”的指标的稳步提升被视为理所当然。但就我们目前的判断而言，原本在联邦储备委员会指数中定为100的1923–1925年工业生产平均水平，仍应被视为我们有资格预测的最高正常水平。毋庸置疑，投资者不会否认再次出现长期上升的*可能性*，但对他们来说重要的是，他们无法依赖这一点。

<!--en-->
The relationship between “good stocks” and other stocks must be considered in the light of what is to be expected of American business generally. Any prediction on the latter point would be highly imprudent; but it is in order to point out that the record of the last fifteen years does not in itself supply the basis for an expectation of a long-term upward movement in volume and profits. In so far as we judge the future by thepast we must recognize a rather complete transformation in the *apparent* outlook of 1940 against that in 1924. In the earlier year a secular rise in production and a steady advance in the figure taken as “normal” were accepted as a matter of course. But so far as we can see now, the 1923–1925 average of industrial production, formerly taken as 100 on the Federal Reserve Board’s index,¹ must still be considered as high a normal as we have any right to prognosticate. Needless to say, the investor will not deny the *possibility* of a renewed secular rise, but the important point for him is that he cannot count upon it.

如果这是当前股市的潜在假设，那么可以推断，股票买家普遍预期大型企业的盈利将继续增长，而这一增长的代价将是小型企业以及处于有利位置的行业的利益受损，其他所有行业也会因此受影响。这种预期似乎正是导致某些行业股票价格居高不下而其他行业股票价格低廉的理论基础。过去表现良好且前景看好的股票自然比其他股票更有价值，但这是否意味着华尔街的偏爱已经过甚——在这一点上以及其他许多方面都是如此？那些典型的大型且繁荣的企业是否可能面临双重限制：其一，其庞大的规模使其难以实现惊人的进一步增长；其二，其较高的资本回报率使其即便没有受到竞争压力，也可能因监管而陷入困境？

<!--en-->
If this is the working hypothesis of the present stock market, it follows that stock buyers are expecting in general a further growth in the earnings of large companies *at the expense* of smaller ones and of favorably situated industries at the expense of all others. Such an expectation appears to be the theoretical basis for the high price of the one group and the low prices found elsewhere. That stocks with good past trends and favorable prospects are worth more than others goes without saying. But is it not possible that Wall Street has carried its partiality too far—in this as in so many other cases? May not the typical large and prosperous company be subject to a twofold limitation: first, that its very size precludes spectacular further growth; second, that its high rate of earnings on invested capital makes it vulnerable to attack if not by competition then perhaps by regulation?

或许，从绝对价值以及相对于受青睐股票的角度来看，小型企业及那些不太受关注的行业整体上确实被低估了。从理论上讲，这种情况是有可能的，因为在某个价格水平上，优质股票的价格必然会显得过高，而其他股票的价格则显得过低。有充分但并非决定性的理由表明，1940年可能已经达到了这一临界点。“优质股票”的两个潜在弱点，在其他股票中也存在着相应的优势。即使在正常市场中，也有大量股票的售价低于其净流动资产价值，这强烈表明华尔街的偏爱已经过度。最后，如果我们进一步深入分析，就会发现那些规模较小的上市公司实际上代表了全国范围内成千上万各种规模的私营企业。华尔街似乎在预测除规模最大的企业外，所有企业的持续衰退，而只有那些最大型的企业才会蓬勃发展。在我们看来，这样的发展既不符合经济规律，也不具备政治可行性。

<!--en-->
Perhaps, also, the smaller companies and the less popular industries as a class may be definitely undervalued, both absolutely and in relation to the favored issues. Surely this can be true in theory, since at *some* price level the good stocks must turn out to have been selling too high and the others too low. There are strong, if not conclusive, reasons for arguing that this point may have already been reached in 1940. The two possible points of weakness in the “good stocks” are paralleled by corresponding favorable possibilities in the others. The numerous issues selling below net current asset value, even in normal markets, are a powerful indication that Wall Street’s favoritism has been overdone. Finally, if we carry the analysis further, we must realize that the smallerlisted companies are representative of the hundreds of thousands of private enterprises, of all sizes, throughout the country. Wall Street is apparently predicting the continued decline of *all* business except the very largest, which is to flourish mightily. In our own opinion such a development appears neither economically probable nor politically possible.

对于股市偏爱某些特定行业这一现象，人们也可能提出类似的疑问。从本质上来看，这种情况注定会过度发生——因为无法用量化手段来衡量公众对自己所喜爱领域的热情程度。市场不仅总是将这种乐观情绪推向极致，还表现出一种惊人的倾向：偏爱那些很快就会面临不利发展状况的行业。（可参见1925年的烘焙股、1927年的无线电与制冷行业股票、1928–1929年的公用事业及连锁店股票，以及1933年的酒类行业股票。）有趣的是，1939年“投资者”们竞相抢购雅培实验室的股票，而对美国家庭产品公司却相对漠不关心——前者被认为拥有光明的前景，而后者则仅被视为前景一般。这种区分或许确实合理且精明；但若想起1927年市场对美国家庭产品公司及其同类企业（尤其是兰伯特公司）也曾表现出极大的热情，就很难对最终结果抱有太大信心。² *利率问题*。接下来讨论第三个重要点，即利率与普通股价格之间的关系。显然，如果当前较低的债券收益率会持续下去，那么平均股票收益率必然会随之下降，而每单位预期收益的价值则会上升，相比1923–1925年的情况而言便是如此。正如《第二版导言》中所列的道琼斯工业平均指数相关数据所示，1936–1938年间对收益更为宽松的估值，似乎正是由长期利率的变化所支撑的。然而，一个令人不安的问题是：利率的下降是否与商业活动的非周期性扩张停止以及投资资本的平均盈利能力的下降密切相关？如果是这样，那么影响股票价值的负面因素可能会超过低利率带来的正面影响，1936–1938年间的一单位预期收益实际上可能并不比十五年前更值钱。

<!--en-->
Similar doubts may be voiced as to the stock market's emphasis on certain favored industries. This is something that, by the nature of the case, must always be overdone—since there are no quantitative checks on the public's enthusiasm for what it likes. Not only has the market invariably carried its optimism too far, but it has shown a surprising aptitude for favoring industries that soon turned out to be facing adverse developments. (Witness the baking stocks in 1925, the radio and refrigeration issues in 1927, the public utility and chain stores in 1928–1929, the liquor issues in 1933.) It is interesting to compare the “investor's” eagerness to buy Abbott Laboratories in 1939 and his comparative indifference to American Home Products—the one kind of pharmaceutical company being thought to have brilliant, and the other to have only mediocre, prospects in store. This distinction may prove to have been soundly and shrewdly drawn; but the student who remembers the market's not so remote enthusiasm for American Home Products itself and its companions (particularly Lambert) in 1927 can hardly be too confident of the outcome.²
*Interest Rates.* Coming now to the third point of importance, *viz.*, the relation between interest rates and common-stock prices, it is clear that if current low bond yields are permanent, they must produce a corresponding decline in average stock yields and an advance in the value of a dollar of expected earning power, as compared with the situation, say, in 1923–1925. The more liberal valuation of earnings in 1936–1938, as shown by the data relating to the Dow-Jones Industrial Average (found in the Introduction to the Second Edition), would thus appear to have been justified by the change in the long-term interest rate. The disconcerting question presents itself, however, whether or not the fall in interest rates is not closely bound up with the cessation of thesecular expansion of business and with a decline in the average profitability of invested capital. If this is so, the debit factors in stock values generally may outweigh the credit influence of low interest rates, and a typical dollar of earning power in 1936–1938 may not really have been worth more than it should have been worth a decade and a half previously.

*时机因素*。近年来，人们越来越重视在正确的时间进行买卖，而非仅仅追求合适的价格。在早期，由于投资证券的价格通常波动幅度不大，购买时机并未被视为特别重要。1924年至1929年间，人们对优质股票未来将实现无限增长的信心虽较为强烈，但也极具误导性，以至于任何时机上的失误都必定会被市场回升至更高水平所弥补。而在过去十年中，除了少数几只股票外，市场出现了极大的波动，却没有长期的上升趋势。在这种环境下，成功的投资似乎与成功的投机一样，不可避免地与选择恰当的买卖时机紧密相关。因此我们发现，如今预测市场的大幅波动似乎已成为普通股投资艺术中不可或缺的一部分。

<!--en-->
*The Factor of Timing.* Increasing importance has been ascribed in recent years to the desirability of buying and selling at the right time, as distinguished from the right price. In earlier periods, when the prices of investment issues did not usually fluctuate over a wide range, the time of purchase was not considered of particular importance. Between 1924 and 1929, a comfortable but quite misleading confidence developed in the unlimited future growth of sound stocks, so that any mistake in timing was sure to be rectified by the market's recovery to ever higher levels. The past decade has witnessed very wide fluctuations without a long-term upward trend, except in a relatively small number of issues. Under these conditions it is not surprising that successful investment seems, like successful speculation, to be bound up inescapably with the choice of the right moment to buy and to sell. We thus find that forecasting of the major market swings appears now to be an integral part of the art of investment in common stocks.

股市预测方法的有效性是一个需要深入研究甚至可能引发激烈争议的话题。在此，我们只能给出一个总结性的判断，这个判断可能既反映了我们的调查结果，也包含了我们的个人偏见。我们认为，除非买入时机能与通过分析标准衡量的理想价格水平相契合，否则就无法成功把握股市的时机。同样，投资者判断卖出时，也应主要依据价格水平是否超出了客观价值标准所允许的范围，而非所谓的技术面市场信号。或许在这些基本限制之下，还存在一些可以优化股市操作技巧的方法，从而实现更好的时机把握和更理想的整体效果。然而我们仍不得不得出这样的结论：最普遍接受的时机原则——即只有在上涨趋势已经明确出现之后才进行买入——从根本上违背了投资的本质。传统上，投资者应是那些具备耐心和坚定信念的人，他们会在焦虑或灰心的投机者抛售时买入。如果现在的投资者非要等到市场主动发出信号才行动，那他与投机者又有何区别？他又为何能比普通投机者有更好的结局呢？

<!--en-->
The validity of stock-market forecasting methods is a subject for extensive inquiry and perhaps vigorous controversy. At this point we must content ourselves with a summary judgment, which may reflect our own prejudices along with our investigations. It is our view that stock-market timing cannot be done, with general success, unless the time to buy is related to an attractive price level, as measured by analytical standards. Similarly, the investor must take his cue to sell primarily not from so-called technical market signals but from an advance in the price level beyond a point justified by objective standards of value. It may be that within these paramount limits there are refinements of stock-market technique that can make for better timing and more satisfactory over-all results. Yet we cannot avoid the conclusion that the most generally accepted principle oftiming—viz., that purchases should be made only *after* an upswing has definitely announced itself—is basically opposed to the essential nature of investment. Traditionally the investor has been the man with patience and the courage of his convictions who would buy when the harried or disheartened speculator was selling. If the investor is now to hold back until the market itself encourages him, how will he distinguish himself from the speculator, and wherein will he deserve any better than the ordinary speculator's fate?

**结论。** 我们为普通股投资者寻找明确的投资标准，所得到的多是警示而非具体建议。我们重新认识到那条古老的原则：投资者应等待经济与市场低迷时期再购买具有代表性的普通股，因为在其他时候买入，很可能会以日后会令自己后悔的价格购入股票。另一方面，成千上万的所谓“二线公司”在所有情况下至少应提供一定数量的真正投资机会，或许只有在牛市最鼎盛的时期除外。这个范围广泛但并不受青睐的领域，或许会对真正投资者的兴趣以及证券分析师的能力构成更合理的考验。[^345]: 1 1940年，该指数委员会对其进行了修订，新增了部分成分股，并以1935–1939年的平均值作为基准。

<!--en-->
**Conclusion.** Our search for definite investment standards for the common-stock buyer has been more productive of warnings than of concrete suggestions. We have been led to the old principle that the investor should wait for periods of depressed business and market levels to buy representative common stocks, since he is unlikely to be able to acquire them at other times except at prices that the future may cause him to regret. On the other hand, the thousands of so-called “secondary companies” should offer at least a moderate number of true investment opportunities under all conditions, except perhaps in the heydey of a bull market. This wide but quite unpopular field may present the more logical challenge to the interest of the bona fide investor and to the talents of the securities analyst.
[^345]: 1 In 1940 the Board revised this index. New components were added, and the average of 1935–1939 was adopted as the base.

2 关于这三家公司的数据见附录注1。

<!--en-->
2 Data relating to these three companies are given in Appendix Note 1.
