<!--en-->
Survey and Approach
INTRODUCTION TO PART I

# 本杰明·格雷厄姆——在他的时代与我们的时代

<!--en-->
*Benjamin Graham—in His Time and Ours*

罗杰·洛温斯坦著 在本杰明·格雷厄姆职业生涯中买过的所有股票中，最具影响力的是他母亲所购买的几股美国钢铁公司的股票。1904年成为寡妇后，她试图维持丈夫的进口业务，后又经营寄宿屋，但均以失败告终。1907年在市场情绪高涨之际，她用杠杆贷款购买了美国钢铁公司的股票。同年晚些时候，华尔街陷入恐慌，她的账户资产全部损失。13岁的本就是这样接触投资的。

<!--en-->
by Roger Lowenstein
Of all the stocks Benjamin Graham bought over the course of his career, none were more influential than the odd lot of U.S. Steel purchased by his mother. Left a widow in 1904, she tried to keep up her husband's import business, then ran a boardinghouse; both efforts failed. In 1907, with bullish sentiment riding high, she purchased Steel on margin. Later that year, Wall Street succumbed to a panic, and her account was wiped out. Such was 13-year-old Ben's introduction to investing.

格雷厄姆后来不止一次地吸取了这个教训。他的早期经历非常重要，因为正是这些经历让他形成了对投资的深刻见解。他在纽约市长大，尽管家庭积蓄微薄，仍得以进入哥伦比亚大学学习。毕业后，数学、哲学和英语三个系的系主任都向他提供了教学工作，但哥伦比亚学院的系主任¹更喜欢将优秀学生送到曼哈顿的华尔街去。1914年，格雷厄姆开始在纽伯格、亨德森与洛布公司担任债券部门职员，每周工资12美元。几个月后第一次世界大战爆发。虽然战争给华尔街带来了阴云，但随着美国决定为欧洲提供物资，市场又转为看涨。格雷厄姆以在学校时表现出的那种求知欲来研究证券。在那个监管尚未完善的年代，企业信息极为匮乏。那些投资股票的并非真正的投资者，而是赌趋势的投机者。格雷厄姆则不同。

<!--en-->
Graham was to learn the lesson more than once. His early history is important, because it was the source of his insight into investing. He grew up in New York City and managed to attend Columbia University despite his family's meager savings. Upon graduation, the deans of three departments (mathematics, philosophy, and English) offered him teaching jobs, but the dean of Columbia College¹ liked to send prize pupils downtown, to Wall Street. Graham went to work in 1914 in the bond department of Newburger, Henderson & Loeb, at $12 a week. World War I erupted months later. Although the war cast a pall on Wall Street, as it became clear that America was to provision Europe, the market turned bullish. Graham tackled securities with the same intellectual curiosity he had displayed in school. Corporate information in that preregulatory era was scarce. Investors in stocks were not truly investors; they were speculators betting on trends. Graham was different.

几乎从一开始，他就开始根据证券的资产价值进行分析，尽管获取相关信息需要付出大量努力。他早期的一个成功案例是古根海姆勘探公司，正如格雷厄姆所判断的那样，该公司拥有许多被华尔街低估的优质矿业股票。到1916年，22岁的格雷厄姆仍在纽伯格公司领薪，同时还为一名教授管理投资。格雷厄姆的许多投资都是套利行为，比如古根海姆公司——从客观上看确实是便宜货。这让他感到安心。可惜，1916年秋季股市进入了长期下跌期。尽管有母亲的先例可循，格雷厄姆还是使用了杠杆贷款购股。他被迫亏本抛售，随后花了两年时间才补回教授的资金。

<!--en-->
Almost from the first, he took to analyzing securities on the basis of their asset value, though obtaining information required considerable sleuthing. One early success wasGuggenheim Exploration Company, which, as Graham divined, owned a collection of valuable mining stocks underappreciated by Wall Street. By 1916, the 22-year-old Graham, still on salary at Newburger, was also managing investments for one of his professors. Many of Graham's investments were arbitrages such as Guggenheim—objectively a bargain. This led him to feel secure. Alas, in the fall of 1916, stocks entered a prolonged decline. Despite his mother's example, Graham had purchased on margin. He was forced to sell at a loss and spent two painful years recouping the professor's capital.

这样的循环在他整个职业生涯中不断重复；事实上，至今仍在发生。格雷厄姆在极年轻时就明白了投资与投机之间的本质区别，但即便对他而言，好景也会让人放松警惕。30岁之前，他便离开纽伯格，创办了自己的财富管理公司——格雷厄姆公司。他擅长发现套利和对冲机会的声誉迅速传播开来。例如，拥有通用汽车控股权的杜邦公司，其股票售价仅相当于其在通用汽车的投资价值，完全忽视了其化工业务的价值。对格雷厄姆来说，这简直是易得之财。但对他而言，华尔街不仅仅是数学运算的场所，他还擅长将复杂的证券简化为本质。他很早就意识到，价值并不在于证券的*形式*，而在于其对标的资产的索取权所具有的层级与价值。还在纽伯格工作时，他就得出结论：许多可转换股票能带来与普通股票相同的利润潜力，但风险更低。他将这一见解应用于联合纺织公司，购入了他认为安全的7%可转换债券，同时做空了该公司的普通股票——后者因其多家棉纺厂而备受投机者青睐。本警告持有该普通股票的一位高级合伙人自己正在冒险，但那位合伙人表示比起沉闷的债券，他更喜欢“活跃的股票”。不到一年，该普通股票的股价就从70跌至20，而可转换债券则很快以溢价被赎回。

<!--en-->
Such cycles recurred throughout his career; indeed, they recur to this day. Graham grasped, at a remarkably young age, the cardinal distinction between investment and speculation, but even for him, good times loosened the strings of prudence. Before he was 30, he had left Newburger to run a money management venture, Graham Corporation. His reputation for spotting arbitrage and hedging opportunities spread quickly. One example: DuPont, which owned a controlling interest in General Motors, was selling for no more than the value of its investment in GM, thus according *no* value to its chemical business. To Graham, that was low-hanging fruit. But Wall Street to him was more than a mathematical exercise. He had a knack for stripping complicated securities to their essence. He realized early on that value does not reside in the *form* of a security, but in the hierarchy and value of its claim on the underlying assets. While still at Newburger, he concluded that many convertible stocks offered the same potential profits as the common stock, but with less downside. He applied this insight to Consolidated Textile, acquiring its 7% convertible bond, which he judged to be safe, and selling short the common stock, a speculative favorite due to the allure of its various cotton mills. Ben warned a senior partner who owned the common that he was taking a risk, but the partner said he preferred an "active stock" to a stodgy bond. Within a year, the common plunged from 70 to 20 while the convertible was, soon, redeemed at a premium.

随着经验日益丰富，格雷厄姆开始将自己视为既是实践者也是教育者。到1919年，这位早熟的学徒就已经开始撰写名为《给投资者的启示》的小册子。1925年，他决定写一本书来传授自己的投资知识。幸运的是，他后来回忆道：“我有了进一步深入研究的灵感。”当时他所写的任何东西都不可能类似七年后他写成的、如今呈现在您手中的这部著作。当然，正是他选择了等待，才使得《证券分析》在今天依然具有如此重要的意义。

<!--en-->
With fast-accumulating experience, Graham began to think of himself as a teacher as well as practitioner. By 1919, theprecocious apprentice was writing pamphlets entitled “Lessons for Investors.” In 1925, he decided to write a book imparting his investment knowledge. Fortunately, he later recalled, “I had the inspiration to learn more on the subject.” Nothing he might have written then could have resembled the volume, now in your hands, that he was to write seven years later. That he did wait is, of course, what makes *Security Analysis* so relevant today.

20世纪20年代末的华尔街是一片繁荣景象。那种只涨不跌的股票新时代正逐渐形成势头。格雷厄姆出于本能保持谨慎，只购买那些经过大量研究后他认为价值远高于当前价格的股票。他的名声也日益响亮。1926年，他前往华盛顿，通过查阅州际商业委员会的隐秘文件，发现曾是标准石油信托公司一部分的北方管道公司持有每股价值95美元的铁路债券等证券。这一信息并未为公众所知，该公司的股价因此暴跌至65美元。此时格雷厄姆正与杰里·纽曼合伙经营，他耐心地购买了17万股股票，并施压该公司抛售这些证券并支付高额股息。当公司管理层拒绝时，他发动了代理权争夺战并成功获得董事会席位。随后该公司分发了多次股息，每股总计110美元——这是一笔巨额的意外之财。

<!--en-->
The late 1920s were a heady time on Wall Street. The new era of stocks that did not go down, only up, was gathering momentum. Graham, instinctively, was cautious. He bought only those stocks that he judged (on the basis of laborious research) worth considerably more than their price. His renown also grew. In 1926, he traveled to Washington and discovered through reading obscure filings at the Interstate Commerce Commission that Northern Pipeline, a former part of the Standard Oil Trust, was sitting on $95 a share in securities such as railroad bonds. This was unknown to the public, and the stock foundered at 65. Graham, now operating a partnership with Jerry Newman, patiently bought 170,000 shares and pressured the company to divest the securities and pay a large dividend. When management resisted, he launched a proxy fight and won a board seat. Several distributions totaling $110 a share followed—a huge windfall.

格雷厄姆对北方管道公司以及其他前标准石油子公司的追索让他结识了著名的金融家伯纳德·巴鲁克。格雷厄姆推荐那些看似安全的股票，巴鲁克则大量买入。随着牛市加速，巴鲁克和格雷厄姆都开始担心市场明显的过热现象。巴鲁克指出，当短期固定收益证券的收益率高达8%时，道琼斯工业平均指数的收益率仅为2%，这是荒谬的。格雷厄姆则意味深长地回应道：“根据补偿法则，总有一天情况会反过来。”然而格雷厄姆并未完全做好准备。1928年，他的合伙账户“本杰明·格雷厄姆联合账户”获得了60%的收益，甚至超过了道琼斯指数49%²的涨幅。格雷厄姆个人获得的利润超过了60万美元（几乎是当时贝比·鲁斯收入的10倍）。此外，他还在哥伦比亚大学开设了晚间课程，许多学生都是渴望获取投资技巧的华尔街专业人士。表面上，格雷厄姆似乎处于人生的巅峰。

<!--en-->
Graham's pursuit of Northern, and of other former Standard Oil subsidiaries, brought him into contact with the eminent financier Bernard Baruch. Graham recommended ostensibly safe stocks and Baruch gobbled them up. As the bull market accelerated, Baruch and Graham each worried about the evident excess. Baruch observed that it was absurd for the Dow Jones Industrials to be yielding only 2% when short-term fixed-income securities were yielding 8%. Graham tellingly replied, “By the law of compensation, someday the reverse should happen.” Yet Graham was not quite prepared. In 1928, his partnership, the Benjamin Graham Joint Account, gained 60%, besting even the 49%² rise in the Dow. Ben's share of the profits topped $600,000 (nearly 10 times what Babe Ruth was making at the time). Graham had also begun teaching an evening course at Columbia; many of his studentswere Wall Street pros eager for tips. Seemingly, Graham was on top of the world.

然而，1929年10月，市场崩盘了。1930年，当格雷厄姆以为最糟糕的情况已经过去时，该联合账户再次大量举债投资。据他的助手欧文·卡恩所说，格雷厄姆“没有意识到所有涉及借贷的操作，包括他自己的操作，都存在风险”。抛售行为远未结束。到了1932年大萧条最严重的时期，该联合账户的市值已下跌70%。格雷厄姆和纽曼有五年时间没有工资收入。格雷厄姆的妻子重新回去担任舞蹈教练，全家也放弃了位于中央公园的豪华复式住宅，转而住进了一间位于后面的公寓。

<!--en-->
In October 1929, however, the market broke. In 1930, when Graham presumed the worst was over, the Joint Account invested heavily, again on margin. According to Irving Kahn, his assistant, Graham “did not realize that all operations involving borrowing, including his own,” were at risk. The selling was far from over. By 1932, the depths of the Great Depression, the Joint Account had fallen 70%. Graham and Newman went five years without salary. Graham’s wife returned to work as a dance instructor, and the family abandoned their posh Central Park duplex for a rear apartment.

就在那时，格雷厄姆与哥伦比亚大学的戴维·多德与麦格劳-希尔出版社签约，共同撰写《证券分析》。（尽管当时还是助理教授的多德被格雷厄姆慷慨地列为合著者，但实际上他是格雷厄姆的助手；文本由格雷厄姆撰写，多德负责核实事实、提出建议等。）那是一个撰写投资手册的绝佳时机——美国有三分之一的企业资产售价低于其清算价值。许多所谓的专家完全否定股票投资的合理性，他们认为任何股票购买行为都纯粹是投机行为。然而格雷厄姆却有勇气看到投资机会。长期积累的智慧让他坚信市场趋势是个变幻莫测的晴雨表。他写道，股市并非“称重机”，而是“投票机”，无数人的选择在其中产生，而这些选择“部分基于理性，部分出于情感”。《证券分析》旨在帮助投资者评估证券的持久价值，使其摆脱一时的情绪波动。书中洋溢着作者古典教育所赋予的智慧。格雷厄姆从罗马诗人贺拉斯那里选取了一段题词作为序言：“如今衰落的人将再度崛起，如今得意的人也将跌落。”这一比喻简直再完美不过——因为内在价值无法仅凭价格来判断，价格如同命运般转瞬即逝。“巨额利润本可能变成更惨重的损失……无限度的乐观本可能被极度的绝望取代”，这些情况在格雷厄姆看来已不再令人惊讶。³因此，真正的投资者必须相信那些并非体现在股价或价格预测中，而是来自企业自身价值——可通过资产负债表、盈利报告及其他资料来了解的长期价值。

<!--en-->
It was then that Graham and Columbia’s David Dodd signed with McGraw-Hill to write *Security Analysis*. (Although Dodd, then an assistant professor, was generously credited by Graham as coauthor, in fact he was Graham’s assistant; Graham wrote the text and Dodd checked facts, offered suggestions, and so forth.) It was an extraordinary time to write an investment manual. A third of American industry was selling at less than its liquidation value. Many so-called experts discounted the notion of investing in stocks at all—any stock purchase, they asserted, was sheer speculation. Yet Graham had the courage to recognize a buying opportunity. Hard-won wisdom had honed his belief that the market trend was a fickle barometer. The stock market is not a “*weighing machine*,” he wrote; it was “*a voting machine*” in which countless individuals registered choices produced “partly of reason and partly of emotion.” *Security Analysis* was written to help investors appraise a security’s enduring value and divorce themselves from momentary passions. It breathes with the wisdom of the author’s classical training. Graham turned to Horace, the Roman poet, for his epigraph: “Many shall be restored that now are fallen and many shall fall that are now in favor.” The metaphor was almost too good; underlying values could not be judged on the basis of their price, for prices were as fleeting as the fates. “That enormous profits should have turned into still more colossal losses . . . that unlimited optimism should have beensucceeded by the deepest despair,” no longer struck Graham as surprising.³ The serious investor, therefore, had to trust in the long-term values reflected not by the stock price or predictions about the price, but by the intrinsic corporate worth, to be discerned from the balance sheet, earnings reports, and other sources.

这一见解在今天依然成立，正如1934年时一样，但大多数投资者进入市场时，几乎未体现出以往经验本应赋予他们的洞察力。二十世纪末和二十一世纪初出现的投资热潮与泡沫早已多到难以一一列举。站在2022年的视角来看，投资者面临着导致经济停滞的疫情、欧洲的致命战争以及国内通胀的快速回升。其中第一种情况完全超出了当代投资者的经验范围，后两种则仿佛来自遥远的过去。这些多重冲击提醒人们，除了利率变动等可测算的风险外，投资者还面临着难以预料、更不用说用数学方法估算的不确定性。这就要求投资者——即便是那些投资所谓“安全”股票的人——也要设置一层防护机制，也就是格雷厄姆所称的“安全边际”。

<!--en-->
This insight is no less true today than it was in 1934, yet the majority of investors approach the market with little trace of the enlightenment that prior experience might have taught. The list of investment fads and bubbles in the late twentieth and early twenty-first century has become well too long to enumerate. From the vantage of 2022, investors were confronted by a pandemic that shuttered the economy, a deadly war in Europe, and a rapid revival of domestic inflation. The first was utterly outside the experience of contemporary investors; the other two seemed ghosts from a distant past. These multiple shocks were a reminder that, along with many calculable risks such as interest rate movements, investors face uncertainties that defy anticipation, much less arithmetic estimation. This argues for investors—even those in reputedly “safe” stocks—to build in a layer of protection, what Graham memorably termed a margin of safety.

人们很自然会想：“如果本·格雷厄姆在今天撰写这本书，他会说些什么？”这个问题无法回答，但我们可以做出一个有用的区分。虽然我们无法猜测他会如何构建投资组合，但投资者仍可运用他的*方法论*。市场价格几乎无法反映任何有用（或持久）的未来信息这一原则至今依然成立。任何趋势都可能逆转这一常识也再次表明了保持安全边际的迫切必要性。格雷厄姆或许不会认识软件或数字应用，但我认为他在2007年至2022年的市场中会看到许多熟悉的事物——在此期间，标准普尔500指数曾三次暴跌，一次下跌一半，另一次下跌三分之一，但整体仍实现了11%的年增长率，市盈率更是上升至接近1929年的水平。⁴对于近期人们对所谓私募股权的狂热，我们设想格雷厄姆会指出，这类投资与传统公开股票之间的区别主要只是表面上的——形式上的差异。从实质上看，两者都属于所有权投资，其价值最终取决于企业的经营表现。的确，不每日（或每小时）报价的私募股权表面波动性较低，但其背后的企业同样面临相同的根本性压力。2022年，这些压力包括利率上升、通货膨胀、至少两个连续季度的GDP下滑、能源价格波动、劳动力短缺、持续的供应链延迟以及乌克兰战争。上半年公开股票下跌了23%，但私募股权经理们仍在吹嘘过去的亮眼回报。在表面之下，那3.3万亿美元的私募股权资产——其中大部分是以较高的价格投入的——也面临着同样的压力。一个用于衡量私募股权投资组合对应公开股票价值的指数则下跌了37%。⁵如果私募股权过去的良好表现得益于其更高的负债水平，格雷厄姆肯定会感到震惊。正如他所知，债务是一把双刃剑：它在市场上涨时能放大收益，但当利率上升或企业增长放缓时，又会带来巨大的成本。美国经济正同时面临这两种情况，欧洲、英国和中国也似乎出现了经济放缓的迹象。

<!--en-->
It is tempting to wonder, “If Ben Graham were writing this book today, what would he be saying?” The question is unanswerable, but we can make a useful distinction. Although we cannot guess how he would assemble a portfolio, investors can still apply his *approach*. The axiom that market prices convey little about the future that is useful (or lasting) is as valid as ever. The truism that any trend is subject to reversal still suggests an urgent need for a margin of safety. Graham would not recognize software or digital apps, but he would, I suspect, find much familiar in the markets of 2007–2022, during which the Standard & Poor’s 500 Index crashed three times, once by half and another time by a third, and yet overall rose a remarkable 11% per annum, with price-earnings ratios rising to levels close to those of 1929.⁴
On the recent fetish for so-called private equity, Graham, we imagine, would have pointed out that the distinction between such investments and traditional public stocks was chiefly superficial—one of form. Substantively, each consists of an ownership interest whose value ultimately depends on a business's performance. It is true that private equities, which are not quoted daily (or hourly) present a less-volatile surface, but the underlying businesses are subject to the same fundamental pressures. In 2022, these included rising interest rates, inflation, at least two consecutive quarters of declining GDP, volatile energy prices, labor shortages, persistent supply chain delays, and the war in Ukraine. Public shares fell 23% over the first half of the year, yet private equity managers were still touting past rosy returns. Beneath the surface, the $3.3 trillion in private equities, most of it invested at elevated prices, faced the same pressures. An index that mapped the public stock equivalents of private equity portfolios had fallen 37%.⁵ To the extent that past performance of private equity benefitted from their considerably higher levels of debt, Graham would have shuddered. As he knew, debt is a double-edged sword; it magnifies returns on the way up, but imposes killer costs as interest rates rise or alternatively, as business slows. The U.S. economy was experiencing both, and slowdowns appeared to be underway in Europe, Britain, and China as well.

格雷厄姆也会对“模因股”这一现象感到困惑。2020年代初，这类股票仅凭社交媒体的推广就吸引了大量追随者以及极高的估值。其中最著名的当属处于亏损状态的电子游戏连锁店GameStop，它引起了使用手机交易应用进行交易的中小投资者的关注。这些中小投资者将自身缺乏投资经验视为一种荣誉；有些人甚至声称，他们的动机并非追求利润，而是要让那些做空该股票的职业投资者蒙受损失。短短几个月内，GameStop的股价就从个位数跃升至483美元，总估值超过300亿美元。这些散户投资者得到了电视财经评论员吉姆·克莱默和亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克等名人的鼓动，同时也得到了那些认为他们代表着反对华尔街的民粹主义运动的政客们的支持。还有一位畅销书作者将抢购GameStop的行为描述为“千禧一代版的法国大革命”。⁶最终，该股票股价跌至峰值的一小部分，不过到2022年底仍远高于此前水平。

<!--en-->
Graham would also have been mystified by the phenomenon known as meme stocks. In the early 2020s, these attracted considerable followings (and valuations) on the sole basis of social media promotion. The most celebrated of these, GameStop, a chain of video game stores operating at a loss, caught the attention of small investors who traded on a mobile trading app. The small investors trumpeted their lack of investing experience as a badge of honor; some asserted that their motive was less profit than to inflict losses on professional investors who had sold the stock short. In a matter of months, GameStop shares vaulted from single digits to $483, representing a total valuation of more than $30 billion. The retail investors were egged on by celebrity touts such as Jim Cramer, a television financial commentator, andbillionaire Elon Musk, and encouraged by elected officials who imagined that they represented a populist crusade against Wall Street. One bestselling author portrayed the GameStop buying panic as a “millennial version of the French Revolution.”⁶ In the event, the stock plunged to a fraction of its peak, though as of late 2022 still considerably higher than before.

比模因股更为实质性的现象是对特殊目的收购公司（SPAC）的狂热。我们会详细探讨SPAC，不是因为它们真的“特别”，而是因为它们很好地体现了格雷厄姆时代以及我们这个时代的华尔街是如何脱轨的：一种巧妙但微不足道的金融创新被那些有利益诉求的人利用，然后卖给那些渴望快速获得高额利润、却忽视了根本性安全边际的投资者。2020年和2021年的短暂时间内，SPAC改变了首次公开募股的市场格局。与私募股权一样，SPAC的新颖之处也仅在于*形式*，而非实质。自华尔街诞生之初，私营企业就一直在通过IPO筹集资金。SPAC的不同之处在于它颠倒了通常的流程。通常情况下，企业在创立一段时间后会前往华尔街试图筹集资金，而SPAC则反过来——*首先*是华尔街筹集资金，*然后*发起人才去寻找合适的公司来使用这些资金。

<!--en-->
A more substantive phenomenon than meme stocks was the craze for special purpose acquisition vehicles (SPACs). We’ll discuss SPACs at some length, not because they were truly “special,” but rather they were so illustrative of the way that Wall Street, in Graham’s day and in ours, goes off the rails: a clever if minor financial innovation is exploited by those with pecuniary interest and sold to investors whose desire for large and swift profits blinded them to the utter lack of a fundamental basis, that is, of a margin of safety. For a brief moment in 2020 and 2021, SPACs transformed the market for initial public offerings. As with private equity, the novelty of SPACs was one of *form*, not substance. Private companies have been raising capital via IPOs since the early days of Wall Street. What distinguished SPACs was a twist on the usual sequence. Normally, at some point after starting a business, insiders go to Wall Street and try to raise money. SPACs inverted the order. *First*, Wall Street raised the money; *then* the sponsors looked for a company in which to deploy it.

即便是华尔街的新手——或许尤其是新手——也能察觉到这种操作方式存在一定的逻辑缺陷。在近期金融领域中，或许没有哪个领域像SPAC那样如此令人怀念本·格雷厄姆，因为尽管有大量媒体报道（其中很多都是吹捧之词），但SPAC对投资者构成的风险却普遍被忽视了。⁷ SPAC是纸面公司，通过首次公开募股出售股票，通常定价为每股10美元。与传统的首次公开募股不同，SPAC筹集资金并非用于运营业务（因为它根本没有运营业务），而是用于组建一个空壳公司，该空壳公司有义务在18或24个月内收购一家运营中的企业。如果SPAC无法完成收购，投资者将全额拿回资金，而SPAC也会被清算。

<!--en-->
Even a novice to Wall Street—maybe *especially* a novice —will detect a certain illogic to this way of doing things. Perhaps in no area of recent finance was Ben Graham so sorely missed, because despite considerable press coverage (much of it fawning), the risks to investors in SPACs were widely overlooked.⁷
SPACs are paper corporations that sell shares in IPOs, customarily priced at $10 a share. Unlike a traditional IPO, a SPAC raises capital not for an operating business (it has none) but for a corporate shell that is obligated to purchase an operating business, generally within 18 or 24 months. If the SPAC is unable to complete an acquisition, the investors get their money back in full, and the SPAC is liquidated.

此外，当SPAC同意收购目标公司时，投资者可以选择以每股10美元加利息的价格赎回股份。⁸那些不选择赎回的投资者则将拥有新合并公司的股份。换句话说，SPAC的投资者可以免费体验一次投资机会。实际上，他们的处境甚至更好。SPAC的原始投资者不仅可以用10美元获得一股股份，还能获得一份零碎的认股权证。由于选择赎回的投资者可以保留这些认股权证，他们甚至还能获得一些额外收益。

<!--en-->
Moreover, when the SPAC agrees to acquire a target, investors have the option of redeeming for $10 a share, plus interest.⁸ Those who do not redeem will own a share in the newly merged business. In other words, the SPAC investors get a free look. Actually, their situation is even better than that. Original investors in a SPAC not only get a share for their 10 bucks, they also get a fractional warrant. Since holders who redeem may keep the warrants, redeeming investors even retain some upside.

显然，SPAC的投资者有可获得的利益，但值得追问的是：谁在为这顿看似免费的午餐买单？为何要这么做？SPAC并非凭空出现，而是由发起人组建的，发起人通常是投资集团或其他金融机构。作为组织SPAC的回报，发起人几乎无需付出成本就能获得SPAC 20%的股份，尽管它确实需要投入数百万美元来设立SPAC。因此，发起人有强烈的动力去寻找目标公司并完成并购——否则SPAC就会被清算，其投资也将付诸东流。

<!--en-->
Clearly, there is a carrot for SPAC investors, but it is fair to ask, who is paying for this seemingly free lunch and why? SPACs do not materialize out of thin air; they are formed by a sponsor, generally an investor group or other financial operator. In return for organizing the SPAC, the sponsor takes a 20% slice of the SPAC essentially for free, although it does have to invest some millions in setting it up. Thus the sponsor has a powerful incentive to find a target company and execute a merger—otherwise, the SPAC liquidates and its investment is lost.

SPAC为投资者提供的这顿免费午餐，是为了吸引资本并推动项目进展的诱因。而且享受这种好处的并非只有他们。发起人还需要华尔街的银行来承销初始股份销售，投资银行会收取2%的承销费，如果SPAC完成了收购，则还会再收取3.5%的费用。SPAC还需支付各种咨询、法律及其他费用。把这些各项开支加总起来，不难看出SPAC背负着沉重的成本负担。

<!--en-->
The free lunch for the SPAC investors serves as an inducement to attract capital and get the project going. And they are not the only ones getting lunch. The sponsor needs a Wall Street bank or banks to underwrite the initial sale of shares, and the investment bank charges a 2% fee on the underwriting and another 3.5% if the SPAC completes an acquisition. The SPAC is also subject to various advisory, legal, and other fees. Adding up these sundry expenses, it should be clear that the SPAC is burdened with considerable costs.

不出所料，由于SPAC的复杂性，它们在华尔街只是一个小小的存在，且声誉也并不出众。SPAC之所以能存在，要归功于我们尚未提及的一个方的利益——即SPAC所要收购的目标公司。这些目标公司通常是规模较小的私营企业，多为初创公司。许多公司因过于投机而无法通过传统的首次公开募股筹集资金。对于这类小众公司而言，SPAC虽然并非有意为之，却提供了明显的优势。

<!--en-->
Not surprisingly, in light of their complexity, SPACs were only a tiny outpost on Wall Street and not an especially reputable outpost. That SPACs existed at all is owed to the interests of a party we have not yet considered—the target company that the SPAC acquires. The targets were generally small private firms, often early start-ups. Many were too speculative to raise money in a conventional IPO. For this small niche of companies, SPACs offered a decided though unintended advantage.

在普通的首次公开募股中，承销商若不承担巨大的诉讼风险，就无法对未来的盈利、营收等数据做出预测。这是有充分理由的。出售股票的内部人士绝非中立方，他们的预测自然容易偏向乐观，而且由于公司处于私有状态，内部人士是唯一的消息来源。由于公众实际上受制于他们，监管机构并未给予首次公开募股发布前瞻性声明的常规“安全港”保护。

<!--en-->
In an ordinary IPO, the underwriters cannot offer forecasts of future earnings, revenue, and so forth without incurring great risk of litigation. This is for good reason. Insiders selling stock are anything but neutral parties. Their forecasts are naturally prone to optimism, and the company being private, the insiders are the *only* source of information. Since the public is effectively at their mercy, regulators do not grant IPOs the customary “safe harbor” to issue forward-looking statements.

然而在SPAC的情况下，由于证券监管中存在一个未被注意到的漏洞，⁹并不存在这样的限制。请记住，SPAC走向成熟的过程包含两笔交易。首先，空壳公司通过出售股票来筹集资金。从技术层面讲，这就是它的首次公开募股，但由于SPAC没有资产可供审查，因此几乎不存在审查问题。在第二阶段，SPAC收购一家私营企业。尽管这次收购实际上起到了让目标公司上市的作用，但从技术层面讲，这并不属于首次公开募股，因为SPAC已经上市了。因此，这一流程绕过了常规的首次公开募股要求；更令人担忧的是，它剥夺了公众的监管保护。

<!--en-->
In the case of a SPAC, however, due to an inadvertent loophole in securities regulation,⁹ no such restraint exists. Recall that a SPAC’s progress to maturity consists of two transactions. First, a corporate shell raises capital by selling shares. Technically, this is its IPO, but scrutiny is hardly an issue, because the SPAC has no assets to scrutinize. In the second stage, the SPAC purchases a private business. Although this purchase *has the effect of taking the target public*, the merger, technically, is not an IPO, because the SPAC has already gone public. Thus the process offers an end run around the normal IPO requirements; worrisomely, it deprives the public of regulatory protection.

多年来，SPAC一直无关紧要。2016年，只有13家SPAC上市，而普通的首次公开募股则有75家。¹⁰随后其数量开始逐渐增加。到2019年，华尔街每周都会推出一家SPAC。理查德·布兰森甚至能为毫无营收的太空旅游公司维珍银河找到买家，以8亿美元的价格将其股权通过SPAC出售。华尔街注意到了这一点（注意到了相关费用）。2020年4月，曾有过监管问题的体育幻想博彩公司DraftKings也通过SPAC实现了上市。突然之间，SPAC变得极为热门。当新冠疫情的封锁导致经济陷入衰退，美联储开始向市场注入流动性时，拥有廉价资金的投机者纷纷涌入SPAC领域。据SPACInsider的首席执行官克里斯蒂·马文所说：“每个人都想要参与。股价飙升到了天际。”

<!--en-->
For many years, SPACs were inconsequential. In 2016, only 13 SPACs went public, compared to 75 ordinary IPOs.¹⁰ Then volume began to creep up. By 2019, Wall Street was minting a SPAC a week. Richard Branson was able to find a SPAC buyer—to the tune of $800 million—for equity in Virgin Galactic, a space tourism company with no revenue. Wall Street noticed (noticed the fees). In April 2020, DraftKings, a sports fantasy and betting company with a prior history of regulatory trouble, went public via a SPAC. Suddenly, SPACs were hot. When Covid-19 lockdowns put the economy into recession, and the Federal Reserve started pumping liquidity into markets, speculators armed with cheap money flocked to SPACs. According to Kristi Marvin, CEO of SPACInsider, “Everybody wanted one. Valuations went through the roof.”

传统上，SPAC首次公开募股的投资者多为对冲基金等金融机构。这些对冲基金会在并购消息公布后选择赎回股份，或者（如果价格合适）将股份卖给其他投资者。2020年，投资者的范围扩大到了散户和机构投资者，他们有时被称为“SPAC游客”。对于持有这些股票的人来说，问题很简单：合并后，股价是否有可能高于10美元？如果不能，投资者还不如选择赎回。对他们而言，退出总比陷入糟糕的交易要好。

<!--en-->
Traditionally, investors in SPAC IPOs were financial buyers such as hedge funds. The hedge funds either redeemedwhen an acquisition was announced or (if the price was favorable) sold to other investors. In 2020, interest broadened to retail buyers and institutions, sometimes denoted as “SPAC tourists.” The question for whomever owned the stock was simple: post-merger, were the shares likely to trade above $10? If not, investors were better off redeeming. For them, exit was preferable to a bad deal.

而发起方的考量则完全不同。激励机制不匹配的金融结构往往会导致问题，而SPAC中的激励机制就存在严重的不匹配。发起方自然希望以优惠的价格收购一家有吸引力的企业。但对它们来说，*哪怕是糟糕的交易也比毫无交易要好*。因为它们的股份价值仍会远高于其投入的成本（即零），而如果没有达成任何交易，它们就会损失为设立SPAC所花费的数百万美元。

<!--en-->
The calculus for the sponsor was quite different. Financial structures in which incentives are misaligned often lead to trouble, and the incentives in SPACs were badly misaligned. The sponsor naturally hoped to acquire an attractive business at a favorable price. But for the sponsor, *even a bad deal was preferable to no deal at all*. Its shares would still be worth a good deal more than it had paid (which was zero), whereas if no deal transpired, it would lose the millions it had spent establishing the SPAC.

赎回的可能性像一把利剑悬在各方头上，但影响方式各异。赎回行为会削弱资本结构，进而缩小分摊那些高昂成本的基数。（如果一半的股份被赎回，原本5.5%的承销费就会相当于剩余资本对应的11%的费率。）由于每个选择赎回的股东都会*增加剩余股东的负担*，SPAC结构便催生了一场潜在的退出竞争。

<!--en-->
The possibility of redemption hung over each party like a sword, but in different ways. Redemptions weakened the capital structure and shrunk the base over which those hefty costs were spread. (If half the shares were redeemed, a 5.5% underwriting fee became equal to 11% fee on the capital remaining.) Since each shareholder that redeemed *increased the burden on those that remained*, the SPAC structure spawned a potential race for the exits.

对于没有退出选项的发起方而言，首要目标是最小化赎回行为，尽可能在业务中保留更多现金。一些SPAC发起方会与大股东达成优惠且保密的协议，要求这些股东*不得*赎回股份。¹¹ 发起方还会以优惠条件筹集私人资金，用以补充被赎回的资本。

<!--en-->
For the sponsor, having no exit option, the paramount goal was to minimize redemptions and retain as much cash as possible in the business. Some SPAC sponsors cut preferential, secretive deals with large shareholders in which the shareholders agreed *not* to redeem.¹¹ Sponsors also raised private capital—again on preferential terms—to replace the capital that was redeemed.

发起方竭尽全力为这些股份打造公开市场，以便选择退出的股东可以通过出售而非赎回的方式离场。实际上，这意味着要说服公众，合并后的企业股价会高于10美元。但这带来了一个几乎无法解决的问题：从数学上来看，合并前的SPAC股份价值显然低于10美元。毕竟，它唯一的实物资产就是首次公开募股时每股筹集的10美元*减去其巨额成本*。那么，合并如何能提升其价值呢？

<!--en-->
Sponsors went to great lengths to develop a public market for the shares so that exiting shareholders could sell rather than redeem. Practically, this meant persuading the public that the merged entity would trade above $10. This presented an almost insoluble problem: as a matter of math, SPAC shares, premerger, were clearly worth less than $10. After all, its only tangible assets consisted of the $10 per share raised in the IPO*less its considerable costs.* How could a merger elevate its value?

一种解决方案是以低价收购目标公司，从而提高合并后企业的每股价值。但便宜货并非随处可得。目标公司的股东自然希望为自己的企业获得公平的价值。事实上，目标公司甚至可以要求*高于*公平价值的对价，因为它们知道发起方必须完成交易。另一种可能性是，仅仅将目标公司推向公开市场就能提升其价值——这在理论上可行，但在实践中可能性不大。或者，发起方高管（他们通常会进入目标公司的董事会）具备的专业知识和能力足以让目标企业在他们的指导下得到改善。

<!--en-->
One solution would be to purchase a target company at a bargain price, so that the per-share value of the merged enterprise would be higher. But bargains do not grow on trees. The target shareholders, naturally, want to receive fair value for their business. In fact, target companies are in a position to demand *more* than fair value, because they know that sponsors need to do a deal. Another possibility was that merely taking the target company public would enhance its value—possible in theory, though not very likely in practice. Or perhaps, the expertise and talent of the sponsor executives (who commonly go on the company's board) is such that the target business will, under their tutelage, improve.

投资者容易受外界影响，常常简单地认为发起方很聪明，是在为投资者的利益着想。信息披露并不透明，很少有投资者了解所有隐含成本的总和。根据对SPAC热潮期间18个月内所有已完成合并的SPAC的研究，在扣除发起方的利益、投资者认股权证费用、银行手续费及其他各项费用后，普通公众投资者的实际收益已从最初的10美元稀释至仅5.70美元。¹² 这意味着其内在价值减少了高达43%。¹³ 不仅投资者不了解这些费用，很多人还误以为SPAC相比传统首次公开募股更具成本效益，而实际上SPAC的成本要高得多。斯坦福大学法学院教授迈克尔·克劳斯纳在对SPAC进行深入研究后指出：“SPAC在披露其隐含成本方面远不够透明。”¹⁴ 由于相关法规存在漏洞，发起方既有动机也有机会大力推销自己的并购项目。它们会像推广传统首次公开募股一样举办路演，只不过SPAC可以更随意地给出乐观——有时甚至是极度乐观的——预测。2021年下半年经济刺激政策推动市场上涨之际，华尔街利用这一漏洞的欲望更是肆无忌惮。

<!--en-->
Investors, being impressionable, often simply assumed that sponsors were intelligent and working in the investors' interests. Disclosure was opaque, and few investors were aware of the total of embedded costs. According to a study of all SPACs that merged over an 18-month period when SPACs were hot, after accounting for the sponsor's interest, the investor warrants, the bankers' fees, and other fees, the median public investor's interest had been diluted to only $5.70 of the initial $10.¹² This amounted to a whopping 43% reduction in intrinsic value.¹³ Not only were investors unaware of the expenses, many had believed that SPACs were cost-effective compared with conventional IPOs, when in fact they were considerably more expensive. Michael Klausner, a Stanford Law School professor who examined SPACs in detail, found that, “SPACs are far less transparent than they could be with respect to their embedded costs.”¹⁴
Owing to the holes in applicable regulation, sponsors had the motive and the opportunity to aggressively promote their mergers. The sponsors conducted road shows to sell their deals, similar to road shows for conventional IPOs—except that SPACs were free to indulge in optimistic—at times, wildly optimistic—forecasts. Coinciding with the posteconomic stimulus market rally in the second half of2021, Wall Street's eagerness to exploit this loophole was unrestrained.

许多SPAC是由名人推动成立的，这些名人包括说唱歌手肖恩·“杰斯·Z”·卡特（为一家大麻公司出面）、投资者兼真人秀名人马特·希金斯、家居装饰领域的名人玛莎·斯图尔特、对冲基金巨头比尔·阿克曼、四分卫帕特里克·马霍姆斯以及网球明星塞雷娜·威廉姆斯。这些SPAC的融资则由花旗集团、高盛和瑞士信贷等顶级承销商负责。

<!--en-->
Many SPACs were promoted by celebrities, such as the rapper Shawn “Jay-Z” Carter (for a cannabis company), investor and reality television personality Matt Higgins, home décor celebrity Martha Stewart, hedge fund titan Bill Ackman, quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and tennis star Serena Williams. SPACs were financed by the bluest chip underwriters, led by Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, and Credit Suisse.

对SPAC合并的推广极为肆无忌惮。电动卡车初创公司Nikola发布了一段卡车冲下山坡的视频，并在推文中写道：“看，这就是正在行驶的Nikola One。”根据美国证券交易委员会的说法，该视频于2018年初发布在Nikola的公司推特和脸书账号上（即其在2018年5月完成SPAC合并之前），并且至少直到2020年9月仍被保留并供投资者查看。投资者们以为自己找到了下一个特斯拉，其股价一度飙升至73美元，价值甚至超过了福特汽车，尽管该公司当时还从未售出一辆汽车。根据美国证券交易委员会在其SPAC合并18个月后发布的禁令，Nikola为了抬高股价作出了“大量虚假陈述”。尤其是，该公司隐瞒了视频中的卡车并非由Nikola的电池或任何Nikola产品提供动力——它只是依靠重力在移动这一事实。¹⁵欺诈行为曝光后，该公司的股价便暴跌了。¹⁶虽然Nikola是个极端案例，但SPAC们通常都会为那些实际业务规模很小的目标公司预测大幅增长的营收和利润。此后，数十笔SPAC交易很快就未能实现其预期目标。¹⁷电动汽车行业曾是SPAC们的热门领域，电动巴士公司Arrival SA的首席执行官在2021年3月公司完成合并之前预测，其营收将在三年内从零增长到140亿美元。同年晚些时候，这位首席执行官简单而残酷地表示：“我们撤回之前的长期预测。”¹⁸生产光敏窗户的View公司在面向投资者的演示中将自己与特斯拉和亚马逊相提并论。在与SPAC合并之后，这类夸大宣传便消失了。¹⁹2020年，248家SPAC共筹集了830亿美元，这一数额极为庞大（实际上超过了此前十年的总和）。2021年，613家SPAC又筹集了1620亿美元，²⁰而且上市SPAC的数量超过了传统首次公开募股的数量。这种狂热情绪愈发严重，以至于在尚未有任何合并公告的情况下，普通SPAC的股价就已升至每股11.50美元，这意味着尽管SPAC手头的现金已被各种高昂成本消耗殆尽，但其股价仍比普通人的现金高出15%。²¹投资者们出于轻信或信任，给这些发起方开了“空白支票”。很多人心里的想法大致是：“他们是聪明人，一定能找到出路。”当然，每位投资者都认为自己行事是理性的。他们还有赎回选项作为保障——可以随时观察股价走势。既然股价已经涨到了10以上，他们又何必选择赎回呢？

<!--en-->
Promotion of SPAC mergers was unblushing. Nikola, an electric truck start-up, released a video of a truck barreling downhill, embedded in a tweet reading “Behold, the Nikola One in motion.” According to the SEC, the video was posted on Nikola's corporate Twitter and Facebook accounts in early 2018 (prior to its May 2018 SPAC merger), and it remained posted and available to investors at least until September 2020. Investors thought they had found the next Tesla, and the stock soared to 73, making it more valuable than Ford, although it had yet to sell a single vehicle. According to an SEC cease-and-desist order issued 18 months after its SPAC merger, Nikola had made “scores of misrepresentations” to inflate its stock price. In particular, it omitted the detail that the truck in the video was not powered by a Nikola battery, or any Nikola part—it was rolling under the influence of gravity.¹⁵ After the fraud was revealed, the stock crashed.¹⁶ Although Nikola was an extreme case, it was common for SPACs to project sharply rising revenue and profits for targets that had little actual business. Dozens of SPAC deals subsequently (and quickly) missed their forecasts.¹⁷ The CEO of Arrival SA, an electric bus company (electric vehicles were a hot sector for SPACs) forecast ahead of its March 2021 merger that revenue would surge from zero to $14 billion in three years. Later that year, the CEO said, simply and devastatingly, “We withdraw our long-term forecasts.”¹⁸ View, a company that made sunlight-sensitive windows, compared itself, in an investor presentation, to Tesla and Amazon. After its merger with a SPAC, the happy talk ceased.¹⁹
In 2020, 248 SPACs raised $83 billion, an enormous sum (indeed, more than in the entire previous decade). In 2021, 613 SPACs raised $162 billion,²⁰ and more SPACs went public than traditional IPOs. The mania reached such a fever that the average SPAC climbed to $11.50 per share *prior to any merger announcement*, meaning that cash held by a SPAC, though depleted by significant costs, was trading at a 15% premium to the cash in one's pocket.²¹ Investors were giving sponsors a blank check based on credulity or faith. Many reckoned, in so many words, “They are smart people; they will find something.” Of course, each individual investor believed he or she was behaving rationally. They had the comfort of the redemption option—the free look. And if the stock was trading over 10, why should they redeem?

在狂热高潮期，那些宣布完成合并的SPAC的股票价格平均飙升至每股15.77美元。鉴于如此丰厚的回报，毫不意外的是，五分之四的SPAC投资者选择*不*赎回股票。²²然而，2021年春季，那些与SPAC合并后上市的公司的真实表现暴露在公众视野中，其业绩远未达到预期。泡沫破裂，SPAC股价暴跌。随着热情消退，更多即将在未来完成合并的SPAC的投资者选择赎回股票。²³新SPAC的发行量也大幅减少。2022年7月，五年来首次没有一家新的SPAC上市。现有的SPAC越来越难以找到既能让目标公司满意又能让投资者接受的合并对象。在2021年上市的613家SPAC中，到2022年9月仍有超过70%在急切地寻找目标公司。²⁴其中许多SPAC很可能被迫清算。其投资者能够拿回资金，但那些已完成合并的公司的股东则没那么幸运。到2022年9月，那些在2020年和2021年筹集资金并完成合并的SPAC的平均股价已跌至仅5.03美元。²⁵不仅投资者的平均资本损失了一半，而且这种损失在众多SPAC中普遍存在——自2020年初以来完成合并的数百家SPAC中，只有不到15%的股价维持在每股10美元的盈亏平衡点。²⁶还有超过70家的股价跌至2美元以下。²⁷即便与纳斯达克指数及传统IPO相比，SPAC的表现也明显逊色得多。²⁸与这些损失形成对比的是，发起人平均每笔交易能获利超过1亿美元。即便在那些让普通投资者亏损的交易中，发起人通常也能获得数百万美元的收益。²⁹华尔街因助长这一泡沫而获得了丰厚回报；从2020年初到2022年第三季度，承销商共赚取了约80亿美元的手续费。³⁰2022年3月，也就是泡沫破裂之后，美国证券交易委员会才姗姗来迟地提出了监管改革方案，旨在加强信息披露要求，并在SPAC的预测落空时便于提起诉讼。³¹高盛以“监管环境发生变化”为由，迅速缩减了在该领域的业务规模。³²从形式上看，如果SPAC不能再误导投资者，华尔街也就不再有动力这么做了。

<!--en-->
At the height of the mania, shares of SPACs postmerger announcement soared to an average of $15.77 per share. Not surprisingly, given the glorious returns, four of five SPAC investors chose *not* to redeem.²² Alas, in the spring of 2021, companies that had merged with SPACs, now being public, were exposed for all to see, and performances did not live up to expectations. The bubble cracked, and SPAC prices tumbled. As enthusiasm wilted, more than half of investors in forthcoming SPAC mergers chose to redeem.²³ Volume in new SPAC issues withered. In July 2022, for the first month in five years, not a single new SPAC went to market. Existing SPACs found it increasingly hard to negotiate mergers acceptable to both target companies and to investors. Of the 613 SPACs that went public in 2021, more than 70% were, with increasing desperation, still searching for a target in September 2022.²⁴
Many of those, presumably, will be forced to liquidate. Their investors will get their money back, but shareholders in completed mergers were not so fortunate. By September 2022, the average price of SPACs that had raised money in 2020 and 2021 and completed a merger had plummeted to a mere $5.03.²⁵ Not only had investors lost half their capital on average, but the losses were widely shared—of the hundreds of SPACs that completed a merger since the start of 2020, fewer than 15% were trading at the breakeven price of $10 ashare.²⁶ More than 70 fell to less than $2.²⁷ Even in relative terms, SPACs significantly underperformed both the Nasdaq and conventional IPOs.²⁸
In contrast to these losses, the sponsors made, on average, more than $100 million per deal. Even in deals that lost money for public investors, the sponsors typically cleared millions of dollars.²⁹ Wall Street was richly rewarded for enabling the bubble; from the start of 2020 through the third quarter of 2022, underwriters pocketed an estimated $8 billion in fees.³⁰ In March 2022—that is, after the bubble burst—the SEC belatedly proposed regulatory reforms that would tighten disclosure requirements and make it easier to sue when SPAC projections missed the mark.³¹ Goldman Sachs promptly reduced its footprint in the industry, citing the “changed regulatory environment.”³² On form, if SPACs could no longer mislead investors, Wall Street was no longer so game.

回顾这一泡沫可以发现，SPAC存在的唯一目的似乎就是为目标公司提供一条绕过常规上市流程的捷径，但为此它们不得不付出规避证券法规以及由此带来的资本错配风险（和投资者损失）的巨大代价。大多数最初的SPAC投资者通过赎回或出售股票来保护自己。但那些选择不赎回的投资者，则最终承担起了为其他各方，尤其是目标公司背书的责任。克劳斯纳教授总结道：“那些选择不赎回股票的SPAC股东……在不知不觉中资助了那些他们帮助上市的公司。”³³虽然SPAC泡沫具有借鉴意义，但其持续时间很短，很快就被更为持久的加密货币投机活动所掩盖。尽管格雷厄姆可能会对比特币感到困惑不已，但他几乎就像在阅读1920年代的报道一样，能够认识到华尔街机构出于自身利益的推销行为以及小投资者的从众心理。

<!--en-->
A backward glance at the bubble suggests that the only purpose of SPACs was to provide targets a backdoor to going public, which came at the considerable cost of sidestepping securities regulations and the attendant risk of capital misallocation (and investor losses). The majority of initial SPAC investors protected themselves by redeeming or selling. But the investors who took their places—those who chose not to redeem—wound up underwriting the various other parties, in particular the targets. Professor Klausner concluded, “SPAC shareholders that choose not to redeem ... unwittingly subsidize the firms they bring public.”³³
The SPAC bubble, though instructive, was brief. It was overshadowed by the more enduring speculation in cryptocurrencies. While Graham would have blinked, uncomprehendingly, at Bitcoin, he would have recognized, almost as though reading a page from the roaring twenties, the self-interested promotion by Wall Street institutions and the herdlike credulity of small investors.

比特币及其他加密货币曾被宣传为替代货币、未来的货币，其诞生似乎源于一种摆脱政府干预的货币理念。然而，只有萨尔瓦多将比特币定为法定货币（这一决定是由该国40岁的总统在迈阿密的一场比特币会议上透露的）。这个中美洲国家投资了这种新货币，却立即遭受了50%的未实现损失。即便在萨尔瓦多，几乎没人用比特币来支付商品和服务费用，他们实际上仍然使用美元。在美国，也有数百万人购买了加密货币，但同样，它在经济中并未发挥任何作用。人们并不将其视为货币或价值基准，而是以美元来追踪加密货币的价格，而非相反。比特币的交易速度实在太慢，无法用作电子支付手段（Visa和Mastercard的速度要快数千倍）。³⁴那些支持加密货币的区块链平台确实颇具创意，或许还能用于其他一些用途。有一些投资银行会在区块链网络上交易债务证券。然而——一个常被忽视的事实是——加密货币的“投资者”并不拥有这项技术的所有权，他们只拥有自己所持有代币的代码。比特币确实被证明可用于毒品贩子、绑匪、色情制品制作者等人的非法资金转移。康奈尔大学教授兼数字专家埃斯瓦尔·普拉萨德对笔者表示，比特币仍是一种“纯粹的投机性资产，其全部价值都基于稀缺性；它有价值的唯一原因就是其他人认为它有价值。”

<!--en-->
Bitcoin and other crypto assets were touted as an alternate currency, the currency of the future, apparently spawned by an ideological desire to create a currency free of government involvement. However, only El Salvador made Bitcoin itslegal tender (a decision disclosed by its 40-year-old president while attending a Bitcoin conference in Miami). Investing in its new money, the Central American nation promptly incurred an unrealized loss of 50%. Even in El Salvador, virtually no one uses Bitcoin to pay for goods and services; they use, in fact, the U.S. dollar. In the United States, millions of people have purchased crypto, but similarly, it plays no role in the economy. People do not *think* of it as a currency or benchmark. They track the price of crypto *in dollars*, not the reverse. Bitcoin is transacted far too slowly to serve as a medium for electronic payments (Visa and Mastercard are thousands of times faster).³⁴ The blockchain platforms that support crypto are ingenious and might potentially serve some additional purposes. A few investment banks trade debt securities on blockchain networks. However—a fact often ignored—“investors” in cryptocurrency do not own a claim on the technology. They own a code to, and only to, their own coin. What Bitcoin *has* proved useful for is illicit transfers by drug cartels, kidnappers, pornographers, and the like. As Eswar Prasad, a Cornell University professor and digital expert, told this writer, Bitcoin remains a “pure speculative asset whose whole value is based on scarcity. The only reason it has value is everyone else thinks it has a value.”

很少有投机工具能获得如此广泛的普及。已有大量代币被（以数字化方式）发行，按市场价计算总价值超过一万亿美元。然而，至今仍无人给出定义，甚至没有方法来确定这些代币的任何内在价值。它们不会产生收入、股息或现金流，也不会带来任何收益。就像17世纪荷兰的郁金香热一样，人们购买它们是期望其他买家会出更高的价格。借用本书主编兼我的合作者塞思·克拉曼的话来说，它们就像西海岸的沙丁鱼——由于其并非用于食用，而只是用于交易，因此价格飙升到了任何理智的消费者都不会接受的水平。郁金香和沙丁鱼的价格都以其他实物商品的价格为参照——比如其他花卉或其他海产品。而加密货币则是毫无依托的投机行为。在2021年和2022年的六个月时间里，比特币价格曾一度超过67,000美元，随后又暴跌至20,000美元以下。根本无法理性地判断这两个价格哪个才是正确的，或者到底有没有正确的价格；比特币只是用于交易，而非用于实际消费。

<!--en-->
Few speculative vehicles have attained such widespread popularity. Scores of coins have been (digitally) minted, worth well over a trillion dollars at market prices. Yet no one has offered a definition, even an approach, to ascertaining any intrinsic value to these coins. They produce no revenue, dividends, or cash flow; they yield no earnings. Like the tulip mania in seventeenth-century Holland, they are purchased in the hope that other buyers will pay more. To borrow an example from the organizing editor of this volume and my fellow contributor, Seth Klarman, they are like the West Coast sardines whose price soared well beyond what any sane consumer would pay because, a speculator explained, these were not “eating sardines”; they were “trading sardines.” Tulip and sardine prices are anchored by the cost of other tangible goods—other flowers or other seafood. Crypto is untethered speculation. Over a six-month span in 2021 and 2022, Bitcointraded above $67,000 and then collapsed to under $20,000. There is no rational way of determining if either price was correct, or that any price is; Bitcoin is for trading, not eating.

曾经，知名投资机构将加密货币视为投机性且风险极高的产品，认为不适合客户投资。它们模仿了20世纪20年代经纪商的行为，很快便抛弃了自己所谓的原则。大型投资银行纷纷设立加密货币部门，以推动或便利投机性交易。华尔街总是追随金钱的流向。高盛集团数字资产全球负责人马修·麦克德莫特宣称，高盛将会拓展加密货币业务以满足投资者的需求。当加密货币价格暴跌时，麦克德莫特表示：“在这种环境下出现这样的行情并不令人意外。”³⁵不知道高盛的客户是否感到惊讶。

<!--en-->
Leading investment firms once shunned crypto as speculative and risky, unsuitable for clients. Mimicking the behavior of brokers in the 1920s, they soon cashiered their so-called principles. The big investment banks established crypto departments to promote or enable speculative trading. Wall Street goes where the money is. Mathew McDermott, global head of digital assets at Goldman Sachs, proclaimed that Goldman would expand in crypto to meet investor demand. When crypto prices plunged, McDermott said, “Seeing moves like this in this environment doesn’t come as a huge surprise.”³⁵ It would be interesting to hear if Goldman’s clients were surprised.

面向普通投资者的富达投资公司在2022年向劳工部施压，要求其不要对包括富达在内的企业将比特币作为401(k)计划选项的计划表达“严重担忧”。如果这一举措最终成功，加密货币将成为劳动者退休储备金的一部分。根据联邦养老金法规ERISA，许多身为富达客户的退休计划发起人必须遵循严格的专业标准，即提供给参与者的投资选项必须是“审慎的”。富达公司不愿就加密货币是否属于审慎投资发表评论；如果发起人愿意，他们就会出售该产品。在官网上，富达将比特币描述为“具有价值存储潜力的资产”。也许它认为老年人可以依靠这种幻想过上退休生活。

<!--en-->
Fidelity Investments, broker to Main Street, pushed the Department of Labor in 2022 to muzzle the latter’s “serious concerns” over plans, including those by Fidelity, to include Bitcoin as an option for 401(k) sponsors. If it ultimately succeeds, crypto will become part of the nest eggs set aside for workers’ retirements. According to the federal pension statute ERISA, retirement plan sponsors, many of whom are Fidelity clients, must adhere to an exacting standard of professionalism, which requires that the investment options offered to participants are “prudent.” Fidelity would not comment on whether cryptocurrency was prudent; if sponsors want it, they will sell it. On its website, Fidelity describes Bitcoin as an “aspirational store of value.” Perhaps it imagines that senior citizens will retire on their aspirations.

与格雷厄姆时代的投资投机市场类似，加密货币几乎处于完全不受监管的状态。这一领域吸引了诸多类似20世纪20年代推销员的欺诈行为。当时，国家城市银行的行长查尔斯·E·米切尔（又名“阳光查理”）向小投资者抛售了价值数亿美元的证券，其中包括极具投机性的秘鲁债券。危机来临时，许多人血本无归。在如今的黑暗时代，MicroStrategy的首席执行官迈克尔·塞勒借入了24亿美元并发行股票，将所得资金用于购买价值超过30亿美元的比特币。塞勒敦促追随者“把所有钱都用来买比特币，然后再想办法借更多钱来买入更多比特币”。塞勒的数字货币宣传靠的是投资者的信仰而非理性，这与格雷厄姆和多德的基本面分析理念截然相反。在比特币价格下跌三分之二后，MicroStrategy的股价暴跌，塞勒也辞职了。

<!--en-->
Not unlike the speculative markets in Graham’s day, crypto has been virtually unregulated. The field attracted huckstering reminiscent of the salesmen in the 1920s. Back then, Charles E. Mitchell (a.k.a. “Sunshine Charley”), the president of National City Bank, floated hundreds of millions’ worth of securities, including highly speculative Peruvian bonds, to small investors. Come the crash, many were wiped out. In the benighted modern era, Michael Saylor, CEO of MicroStrategy, borrowed $2.4 billion and also issued shares,the proceeds of which he plowed into more than $3 billion of Bitcoin. Saylor urged disciples to “Take all your money and buy Bitcoin. Then ... figure out how to borrow more money to buy more Bitcoin.” Saylor’s digital evangelism appealed to investors’ faith, not their reason. It was the polar opposite of Graham-and-Dodd fundamental analysis. After Bitcoin’s price fell by two-thirds, MicroStrategy stock crashed and Saylor resigned.

另一位推广者迈克·诺沃格拉茨曾经营一家对冲基金，但因巨额亏损而关闭，之后又以Galaxy Digital的首席执行官身份出现，销售加密货币投资基金。他在各类加密货币会议以及电视和社交媒体上像传教士一样，满怀热情地推广数字货币。他在一次比特币大会上表示自己的职责就是不断宣讲，称“我停不下来”。Galaxy Digital对一种名为Luna的新币进行了大规模投资，该币初始价格还不到1美元。随着包括众多小型散户在内的投资者纷纷买入，Luna的价格迅速涨至100美元。诺沃格拉茨得意地在推特上写道：“我现在正式成了‘疯子’！！！”这条推文附上了他左臂上纹着的狼对着月亮嚎叫的图片。几个月后，投资者们陷入恐慌，Luna的价格暴跌了99%，投资者损失了数十亿美元。危机发生后，诺沃格拉茨在采访中坚称自己的言论中包含“警示之词”，但也承认“看到太多人损失惨重让我很痛心”。³⁶ Luna的崩盘是所谓加密货币银行面临清算的一部分，这类银行曾向存入加密货币资产的投资者提供极高的收益。其中一家公司就是Celsius Network，它为加密货币贷款提供7%的利息（而其实际放贷利率更高）。当时普通银行的利率还不到1%。批评者质疑这样的高收益如何能够持续。另一家类似银行Voyager Digital则误导性地暗示投资者的存款受FDIC保险保障。其宣传材料承诺：“万一由于公司或我们的银行合作伙伴倒闭导致您的美元资金受损，我们将确保全额赔偿（最高可达25万美元）。”³⁷ Voyager提供的收益率为9%，因此吸引了大量存款。该公司将其资产管理方式描述为“低风险”。NBA达拉斯独行侠队的老板马克·库班还成为了Voyager的官方赞助商，他鼓励球迷在Voyager平台上进行交易，并向他们保证Voyager“非常适合我们的独行侠球迷……是加密货币领域中最接近无风险的选项”。³⁸ Voyager和Celsius各自借贷了约50亿美元。一些投资者认为他们的“存款”是安全的。但实际上这些加密货币银行并非法定银行，不受FDIC保险保护，而且大多杠杆率极高。Voyager的资产与权益比率高达23:1，Celsius则为19:1，这还不到普通银行中位数权益缓冲水平的一半。尽管如此，Celsius的创始人亚历克斯·马辛斯基仍坚称自己的公司能为客户提供更好的服务。他说：“在700年的银行业历史中，从来都没有过这样的选择。”在这700年之后，加密货币市场崩溃，投资者纷纷提取资金。Voyager和Celsius都暂停了提款服务，并相继申请破产。

<!--en-->
Another promoter, Mike Novogratz, had run a hedge fund but shuttered it after heavy losses, only to reemerge as CEO of Galaxy Digital, selling crypto-investment funds. Novogratz became a missionary at crypto conferences and on television and social media, promoting digital currencies with born-again faith. He said at a Bitcoin convention that his role was to preach without end, explaining, “I can’t stop.” Galaxy made a large investment in a new coin known as Luna, priced at less than $1. As investors, including many small retail investors, jumped aboard, Luna surged to $100. Novogratz triumphantly tweeted, “I’m officially a Lunatic!!!” The tweet included a tattooed image of a wolf baying at the moon on his left biceps. Months later, investors panicked, and Luna plunged by 99%. Investors lost billions of dollars. After the crash, Novogratz insisted in an interview that his ravings had included “words of caution,” though he conceded, “It’s painful to me that too many people lost too much.”³⁶
Luna’s collapse was part of a reckoning for so-called crypto banks, which offered very high yields to investors who deposited crypto assets. One such firm was Celsius Network, which paid 7% interest on loans of crypto coins (which it lent out at even higher rates). At the time, ordinary banks were yielding less than 1%. Critics questioned how such yields could be sustained. Another ersatz bank, Voyager Digital, misleadingly implied that investor deposits were FDIC insured. Its marketing material promised, “In the rare event your USD funds are compromised due to the company or our banking partner’s failure, you are guaranteed a full reimbursement (up to $250,000).”³⁷ Voyager offered 9% yields and was flooded with deposits. It characterized its approach to asset management as “low-risk.” Mark Cuban,owner of the NBA's Dallas Mavericks, made Voyager an official sponsor. He egged on fans to trade on the Voyager platform, assuring them that Voyager was “a perfect fit for our Mavs fans ... as close to risk-free as you’re going to get in the crypto universe.”³⁸
Voyager and Celsius each borrowed on the order of $5 billion. Some investors believed their “deposits” were safe. But crypto banks were not legally banks; they were not FDIC insured, and most were highly leveraged. Voyager had a ratio of assets to equity of 23:1; Celsius, 19:1. That was less than half the equity cushion of the median traditional bank. Nonetheless, Alex Mashinsky, the founder of Celsius, maintained that his firm offered a better deal for the customer. “For 700 years of banking,” he said, “there was never an option.” After those 700 years, the crypto market crashed, and investors withdrew funds en masse. Voyager and Celsius suspended withdrawals. Each filed for bankruptcy.

加密货币几乎满足了格雷厄姆提出的所有投机性检验标准：极度依赖市场趋势、没有明显的内在价值、杠杆率极高。与20世纪20年代一样，推销人员甚至不会讨论估值问题，反而将加密货币吹捧为“新时代”的象征。那些从事加密货币推广和交易的公司擅长招募名人代言人，比如NFL四分卫汤姆·布雷迪和喜剧演员拉里·大卫。许多退休的政府监管人员也加入了加密货币公司的董事会，为该行业增添了机构稳定的假象。美国最大的加密货币交易所Coinbase聘请了曾任美国司法部助理检察官及数字货币协调员的凯瑟琳·豪恩为其董事会成员。2021年，Coinbase上市时股价高达381美元，市值达860亿美元。上市后，有四名公司内部人士以189至422美元不等的价格卖出了价值12亿美元的股票。2022年，该公司的营收大幅下滑，股价跌至100美元以下。³⁹以类似格雷厄姆式的冷静视角来看，我们可以发现加密货币泡沫其实是技术精英崛起的副产品。技术的影响力极为深远，以至于其专家们被视作现代的“祭司”，类似于古代的占卜师，而这些科技公司则被用不同的标准来评判——仿佛它们能够免于经受价格与价值这一古老检验。软件的复杂性以及其对非专业人士的不可理解性，让这些公司能够摆脱传统的价值衡量标准，因为谁又能去评估那些自己无法理解的东西呢？许多科技企业以异常高的速度长期发展，这让人合理地认为这些企业的价值非同寻常。在持续看涨的趋势影响下，这一合理前提有时会在不知不觉中被替换为一个远不那么合理的观点——即高增长率是该行业的固有特征，而领先的科技股无论什么价格都是值得投资的。这与20世纪60年代末和70年代初所谓的“一次性决策”股票（也称为Nifty Fifty）背后的理念类似——比如ITT、雅芳和宝丽来等蓝筹股。人们认为这些是“一次性决策”股票，可以买入并永远持有。但实际上，Nifty Fifty从巅峰到低谷的跌幅可达80%。

<!--en-->
Crypto checked off almost every Graham test for speculation: utter reliance on the market trend, no discernible intrinsic value, high leverage. As in the 1920s, salesmen did not even discuss the issue of valuation. Rather, they touted crypto as the hallmark of a “New Era.” Companies in the business of promoting and trading crypto proved adept at recruiting celebrity endpoints, such as NFL quarterback Tom Brady and comedian Larry David. Numerous retired government regulators joined the boards of crypto firms, giving the industry a patina of institutional stability. Coinbase, the largest U.S.-based crypto exchange, recruited to its board Kathryn Haun, formerly assistant U.S. attorney and digital currency coordinator at the U.S. Department of Justice. Coinbase went public in 2021 at a stratospheric price of 381, or $86 billion. After the IPO, four company insiders sold $1.2 billion of stock at prices ranging from 189 to 422. In 2022, the company’s revenue plunged and the stock crashed to under 100.³⁹
With a measure of Graham-like detachment, we can see that the crypto bubble is an offshoot of the rise of a technological elite. The impact of technology has been soprofound that its experts have come to be regarded as modern priests, akin to the soothsayers of old, and its companies judged on a different standard—as if immune to the age-old test of price and value. The complexity of software, its opaqueness to the nonexpert, affords them an immunity to traditional measures of value, for who can appraise what they cannot comprehend? The fact that many technology businesses grew at unusually high rates, and did so over long periods, nurtured a reasonable premise that these businesses were uncommonly valuable. Under the influence of persistently bullish trends, this premise was exchanged, at times unconsciously, for one that was far less reasonable—that high growth rates were a fixed fact of the industry, and that leading technology stocks were worthy investments at any price. This resembled the philosophy behind the “one-decision” stocks of the late 1960s and early 1970s (also known as the Nifty Fifty)—blue chips such as ITT, Avon, and Polaroid. These were supposedly “one decision” stocks that could be bought and held forever. But peak to trough, the Nifty Fifty would plunge 80%.

尽管在数字时代，“一次性决策”的理念没那么明确，但其应用方式却相似，从而导致股价上涨——即便考虑到数字经济日益重要的地位也是如此。本世纪初，数字经济在美国GDP中的占比上升了三分之一，达到了约10%。⁴⁰虽然这一数字相当可观，但仍不及股市的表现，因为科技股在标普500指数中的占比为28%。⁴¹遵循格雷厄姆-道奇投资原则的人固然不会回避科技股，但他们也会意识到股价不可能脱离价值而长期波动。2022年的前八个月里，以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数市值蒸发了四分之一，许多数字领域的标志性企业股价更是下跌了一半以上。

<!--en-->
While the one-decision credo was less explicit in the digital era, its application was similar, with consequent inflation of share prices *even relative to digital’s growing economic importance*. Over the early part of the century, the digital share of America’s GDP rose by a third, to approximately 10%.⁴⁰ While that was impressive, it was outpaced by the action in the stock market, where technology’s share of the S&P 500 was 28%.⁴¹ A Graham-and-Dodd investor would hardly shirk technology, but he or she would be cognizant that prices will not trade without some relation to value, or not forever. Over the first eight months of 2022, the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost a quarter of its value. Many digital icons fell by more than half.

2022年的市场暴跌具有典型意义，因为它并非源于投机风气的变化，而是来自实体经济中的现实问题。科技行业曾被视为例外存在——人们认为它不受普通经济周期的影响。然而在2022年，一家又一家表现优异的科技公司纷纷报告营收和/或利润增长放缓、竞争加剧，同时还面临经济放缓及全球供应链中断带来的压力；换句话说，它们也面临着与其他行业相同的种种压力。《经济学人》杂志甚至开始思考“大型科技企业例外论”的时代是否已经结束。⁴²遵循格雷厄姆理论的投资者不会对这种笼统的论断下任何赌注。格雷厄姆的理论强调基于对具体证券的研究进行自下而上的选股。归根结底，重要的是通过合理的安全边际推算出的预期收益和自由现金流。如果没有这样的保障，格雷厄姆认为这些证券根本就不是投资，而是投机行为。模因股票、私募股权估值的过度膨胀、特殊目的公司、加密货币，以及那些虚假的加密货币银行提供的高杠杆贷款，都是这种投机行为的变体。或许由于人类行为中某些缺陷，证券市场将永远重复这类愚蠢行为；或许人类社会能够做出一些微小的改进。在那一天到来之前，阅读本书的读者所获得的收益不会少于1934年的读者。正如《纽约时报》上对《证券分析》的评论所说：“鉴于近期历史上的惨败，仍有一些人愿意投入资金，希望他们能读一读这本书。这是一部内容丰富、成熟严谨、极具价值的作品，凝聚了学术探究与实践智慧的结晶。”⁴³ [^402]：¹该学院的院长是弗雷德里克·保罗·凯佩尔。相关内容参考了欧文·卡恩与罗伯特·D·米尔恩所著的《本杰明·格雷厄姆：金融分析之父》，发表于《金融分析师研究基金会》的偶发论文第5号。²不包括股息。³本杰明·格雷厄姆与大卫·多德，《〈证券分析〉序言》，纽约：麦格劳-希尔出版社，1934年，第3页。⁴从2007年12月31日（上一轮牛市的高点）到2022年8月，复合涨幅为11％；市盈率数据见https://www.multpl.com/shiller-pe.处的席勒市盈率。⁵《经济学人》，2022年7月9日，“市盈率的启示”。⁶本·梅兹里奇，《反社会网络》。

<!--en-->
The market rout of 2022 was illustrative because it stemmed not from a shift in the speculative winds but rather from verities in the underlying economy. Technology had been treated as exceptional: it was seen as impervious to ordinary economic cycles. In 2022, however, one high-flying technology company after another reported slowing revenuesand/or profits, increased competition, and pressure from the slowing economy and worldwide supply interruptions; in other words, all of the same pressures faced in other industries. *The Economist* magazine was moved to wonder whether the era “of big tech exceptionalism” was over.⁴²
A Graham-and-Dodd investor would bet neither for nor against such a broad-brush proposition. The Graham discipline teaches bottom-up securities selection based on research into specific securities. Ultimately, what counts is prospective earnings and free cash flow deduced with a reliable margin of safety. Absent such assurance, Graham counseled, securities were not investments at all; they were speculations. Meme stocks, the excesses in private equity valuations, SPACs, crypto, and high-leverage lending by phony crypto banks, were all variations on this speculative theme. Perhaps securities markets, captive to some faulty wiring in human behavior, are bound forever to repeat such follies. Perhaps human society will be capable of making modest improvements. Until that day, the reader of this volume will profit no less than the reader in 1934. As the review of *Security Analysis* that appeared in the *New York Times* said: “On the assumption that despite the debacle of recent history there are still left people whose money burns a hole in their pockets, it is to be hoped that they will read this book. It is a full-bodied, mature, meticulous, and wholly meritorious outgrowth of scholarly probing and practical sagacity.”⁴³

CHAPTER 1

# 证券分析的范围与局限：内在价值的概念

<!--en-->
*The Scope and Limitations of Security Analysis. The Concept of Intrinsic Value*

分析意味着对现有事实进行仔细研究，并试图基于既定原则和合理逻辑得出结论。它是科学方法的一部分。但在将分析应用于证券领域时，我们会遇到一个严重障碍：投资本质上并非一门精确的科学。法律和医学也是如此，因为在这两个领域中，个人技能（艺术性）和运气也是决定成败的重要因素。尽管如此，在这些职业中分析不仅有用，而且不可或缺，因此投资领域乃至投机领域或许也应如此。

<!--en-->
ANALYSIS CONNOTES the careful study of available facts with the attempt to draw conclusions therefrom based on established principles and sound logic. It is part of the scientific method. But in applying analysis to the field of securities we encounter the serious obstacle that investment is by nature not an exact science. The same is true, however, of law and medicine, for here also both individual skill (art) and chance are important factors in determining success or failure. Nevertheless, in these professions analysis is not only useful but indispensable, so that the same should probably be true in the field of investment and possibly in that of speculation.

在过去的三十年里，华尔街上的证券分析声誉经历了辉煌的上升与耻辱的下降——这一历程虽与股价走势相关，但绝非完全同步。直到1927年左右，证券分析一直持续发展，期间各方越来越重视财务报告和统计数据。但从1927年开始的“新时代”实际上意味着分析方法的放弃；虽然表面上仍强调事实和数据，但这些数据和事实却被一种伪分析手段所操纵，用以支撑当时的错误观念。对于那些保持清醒头脑的分析师而言，1929年10月的市场崩溃并不意外，但随后出现的严重经济危机及其对企业盈利能力的毁灭性影响，再次让他们的预测失灵。最终，严肃的分析工作遭到了双重贬损：第一次是在危机之前，由于虚假价值的存在；第二次是在危机之后，由于真实价值的消失。

<!--en-->
In the last three decades the prestige of security analysis in Wall Street has experienced both a brilliant rise and an ignominious fall—a history related but by no means parallel to the course of stock prices. The advance of security analysis proceeded uninterruptedly until about 1927, covering a long period in which increasing attention was paid on all sides to financial reports and statistical data. But the “new era” commencing in 1927 involved at bottom the abandonment of the analytical approach; and while emphasis was still seemingly placed on facts and figures, these were manipulated by a sort of pseudo-analysis to support the delusions of the period. The market collapse in October 1929 was no surprise to such analysts as had kept their heads, but the extent of the business collapse which later developed, with its devastating effects on established earning power, again threw theircalculations out of gear. Hence the ultimate result was that serious analysis suffered a double discrediting: the first—prior to the crash—due to the persistence of imaginary values, and the second—after the crash—due to the disappearance of real values.

1927年至1933年的经历极为特殊，几乎无法作为评判证券分析实用性的有效标准。至于1933年之后的年份，或许还存在不同意见的空间。在债券和优先股领域，我们认为合理的筛选与剔除原则已经充分证明了其有效性。而在普通股市场，市场的偏见往往使保守的观点变得混乱，反之，许多经分析看似便宜的股票表现却令人失望。另一方面，从分析的角度来看，有充分理由认为1937年初的股价偏高，而一年后则偏低。

<!--en-->
The experiences of 1927–1933 were of so extraordinary a character that they scarcely provide a valid criterion for judging the usefulness of security analysis. As to the years since 1933, there is perhaps room for a difference of opinion. In the field of bonds and preferred stocks, we believe that sound principles of selection and rejection have justified themselves quite well. In the common-stock arena the partialities of the market have tended to confound the conservative viewpoint, and conversely many issues appearing cheap under analysis have given a disappointing performance. On the other hand, the analytical approach would have given strong grounds for believing representative stock prices to be too high in early 1937 and too low a year later.

## 分析的三大功能：1. 描述性功能

<!--en-->
*THREE FUNCTIONS OF ANALYSIS: 1. DESCRIPTIVE FUNCTION*

安全分析的功能可归纳为三大类：描述性、选择性及批判性。在最直观的形式中，描述性分析旨在整理与某一问题相关的重要事实，并以连贯、易于理解的方式呈现出来。各类手册、标准统计资料以及惠誉等服务已充分履行了这一功能，适用于所有可供交易的公司证券。更为深入的描述性分析则试图揭示某项证券的优势与劣势，将其表现与其他同类证券进行比较，并评估可能影响其未来表现的各项因素。这类分析几乎可应用于所有公司证券，它不仅可作为投资的辅助工具，也可用于明智的投机活动，因为其为判断提供有条理的事实依据。

<!--en-->
The functions of security analysis may be described under three headings: descriptive, selective, and critical. In its more obvious form, descriptive analysis consists of marshalling the important facts relating to an issue and presenting them in a coherent, readily intelligible manner. This function is adequately performed for the entire range of marketable corporate securities by the various manuals, the Standard Statistics and Fitch services, and others. A more penetrating type of description seeks to reveal the strong and weak points in the position of an issue, compare its exhibit with that of others of similar character, and appraise the factors which are likely to influence its future performance. Analysis of this kind is applicable to almost every corporate issue, and it may be regarded as an adjunct not only to investment but also to intelligent speculation in that it provides an organized factual basis for the application of judgment.

## 2. 安全分析的选择性功能

<!--en-->
*2. THE SELECTIVE FUNCTION OF SECURITY ANALYSIS*

在选择性功能方面，安全分析会进一步给出自身的具体判断。它旨在确定某项证券应当买入、卖出、持有还是兑换为其他证券。哪些类型的证券或情形最适合作为分析师进行此类积极分析的对象？又存在哪些障碍或限制？不妨先列举一些分析判断的实例，这些实例日后可作为开展更广泛研究的依据。

<!--en-->
In its selective function, security analysis goes further and expresses specific judgments of its own. It seeks to determine whether a given issue should be bought, sold, retained, or exchanged for some other. What types of securities or situations lend themselves best to this more positive activity of the analyst, and to what handicaps or limitations is it subject? It may be well to start with a group of examples of analytical judgments, which could later serve as a basis for a more general inquiry.

**分析判断的示例。**1928年，圣路易斯-旧金山铁路公司发行了大量票面利率为6%、非累积优先股，发行价为100美元。历史记录显示，该公司在任何一年里的盈利都从未达到固定费用与优先股股息总和的$1\frac{1}{2}$倍。若运用既定的筛选标准来分析此案例，就会因保护力度不足而拒绝购买该证券。

<!--en-->
**Examples of Analytical Judgments.** In 1928 the public was offered a large issue of 6% noncumulative preferred stock of St. Louis-San Francisco Railway Company priced at 100. The record showed that in no year in the company's history had earnings been equivalent to as much as $1\frac{1}{2}$ times the fixed charges and preferred dividends combined. The application of well-established standards of selection to the facts in this case would have led to the rejection of the issue as insufficiently protected.

一个对比案例：1932年6月，人们可以以70美元的价格购买欧文斯-伊利诺伊玻璃公司1939年到期的5%债券，到期收益率为11%。即便在经济严重萧条的时期，该公司的盈利也远高于利息支出——不仅是平均水平如此。仅流动资产就足以充分覆盖该债券的本息，之后该公司还发行了总市值极高的普通股和优先股，即便按最低价计算也是如此。在这种情况下，分析会认为这是一项安全性极高且定价具有吸引力的投资。

<!--en-->
A contrasting example: In June 1932 it was possible to purchase 5% bonds of Owens-Illinois Glass Company, due 1939, at 70, yielding 11% to maturity. The company's earnings were many times the interest requirements—not only on the average but even at that time of severe depression. The bond issue was amply covered by current assets alone, and it was followed by common and preferred stock with a very large aggregate market value, taking their lowest quotations. Here, analysis would have led to the recommendation of this issue as a strongly entrenched and attractively priced investment.

让我们以普通股领域的一个例子来看。1922年，在航空证券热潮之前，莱特航空公司的股票在纽约证券交易所的成交价仅为8美元，尽管该公司每股派发1美元股息，此前一段时间的每股收益已超过2美元，且库房中的现金资产每股也有超过8美元。

<!--en-->
Let us take an example from the field of common stocks. In 1922, prior to the boom in aviation securities, Wright Aeronautical Corporation stock was selling on the New York Stock Exchange at only $8, although it was paying a $1 dividend, had for some time been earning over $2 a share, and showed more than $8 per share in cash assets in the treasury.

在这种情况下，分析很容易就能得出结论：该证券的内在价值远高于市场价格。

<!--en-->
In this case analysis would readily have established that the intrinsic value of the issue was substantially above the market price.

再来看看1928年同一只股票的股价，当时已升至每股280美元。此时的每股收益为8美元，而1927年为3.77美元。股息率为2美元，每股净资产值不到50美元。对这一情况的分析必然会明确指出，市场价格在很大程度上反映了完全基于猜测的未来前景的资本化价值——换言之，其内在价值远低于市场报价。

<!--en-->
Again, consider the same issue in 1928 when it had advanced to $280 per share. It was then earning at the rate of $8 per share, as against $3.77 in 1927. The dividend rate was $2; the net-asset value was less than $50 per share. A study of this picture must have shown conclusively that the market price represented for the most part the capitalization of entirely conjectural future prospects—in other words, that the intrinsic value was far less than the market quotation.

第三种分析结论可通过对比1933年售价相同的两种证券来说明：即Interborough Rapid Transit Company发行的第一类及可赎回5美元债券，与该公司发行的7%抵押票据。显然，7%抵押票据的价值远高于5美元债券。每张面值为1,000美元的7%票据都由面值为1,736美元的5美元债券作为抵押；这些票据的本金已到期，持有人有权要求全额偿付，或要求出售抵押物以获得补偿。每张7%票据从抵押物中获得的年利息约为87美元（这一金额实际上会分配给票据持有人），因此7%票据的当前收益明显高于5美元债券。无论人们提出何种技术性理由试图阻止票据持有人及时、彻底地行使合同权利，都很难想象会出现7%票据的内在价值不远远高于5美元债券的情况。

<!--en-->
A third kind of analytical conclusion may be illustrated by a comparison of Interborough Rapid Transit Company First and Refunding 5s with the same company's Collateral 7% Notes, when both issues were selling at the same price (say 62) in 1933. The 7% notes were clearly worth considerably more than the 5s. Each $1,000 note was secured by deposit of $1,736 face amount of 5s; the principal of the notes had matured; they were entitled either to be paid off in full or to a sale of the collateral for their benefit. The annual interest received on the collateral was equal to about $87 on each 7% note (which amount was actually being distributed to the note holders), so that the current income on the 7s was considerably greater than that on the 5s. Whatever technicalities might be invoked to prevent the note holders from asserting their contractual rights promptly and completely, it was difficult to imagine conditions under which the 7s would not be intrinsically worth considerably more than the 5s.

对于同一类型的股票，还可以进行更近期的对比：1936年10月Paramount Pictures发行的First Convertible Preferred股价为113，而同期普通股的股价为15又7/8美元。该优先股持有人可选择将其转换为数量是普通股七倍的股份，且每股还包含约11美元的累积股息。显然，优先股比普通股更便宜，因为在普通股获得任何收益之前，优先股就已经能拿到相当可观的股息；同时，凭借转换权，它还能完全分享普通股股价上涨带来的收益。如果普通股股东接受这一分析并用自己的股份换取数量为七分之一的优先股，那么他很快就能在股息收入和本金价值两方面实现大幅盈利。¹ **内在价值与价格。**从上述例子可以看出，证券分析师的工作并非没有实际价值，其方法也适用于多种情况。在所有这些案例中，他们似乎都在关注证券的内在价值，尤其是内在价值与市场价格之间的差异。不过我们必须认识到，内在价值是一个难以捉摸的概念。一般来说，它指的是由事实所支撑的价值，比如资产、收益、股息、明确的未来前景等，这些与通过人为操纵或心理因素扭曲形成的市场报价是有区别的。但认为内在价值像市场价格那样明确且可确定，其实是一个很大的错误。不久前，人们认为普通股的内在价值大致等同于“账面价值”，即等于企业经合理定价后的净资产。这种对内在价值的理解虽然很明确，但在实践中几乎毫无用处，因为无论是平均收益还是平均市场价格，都不存在受账面价值支配的趋势。

<!--en-->
A more recent comparison of the same general type could have been drawn between Paramount Pictures First Convertible Preferred selling at 113 in October 1936 and the common stock concurrently selling at $15 7/8. The preferred stock was convertible at the holders' option into seven times as many shares of common, and it carried accumulated dividends of about $11 per share. Obviously the preferred was cheaper than the common, since it would have to receive very substantial dividends before the common received anything,and it could also share fully in any rise of the common by reason of the conversion privilege. If a common stockholder had accepted this analysis and exchanged his shares for one-seventh as many preferred, he would soon have realized a large gain both in dividends received and in principal value.¹
**Intrinsic Value vs. Price.** From the foregoing examples it will be seen that the work of the securities analyst is not without concrete results of considerable practical value, and that it is applicable to a wide variety of situations. In all of these instances he appears to be concerned with the intrinsic value of the security and more particularly with the discovery of discrepancies between the intrinsic value and the market price. We must recognize, however, that intrinsic value is an elusive concept. In general terms it is understood to be that value which is justified by the facts, e.g., the assets, earnings, dividends, definite prospects, as distinct, let us say, from market quotations established by artificial manipulation or distorted by psychological excesses. But it is a great mistake to imagine that intrinsic value is as definite and as determinable as is the market price. Some time ago intrinsic value (in the case of a common stock) was thought to be about the same thing as “book value,” i.e., it was equal to the net assets of the business, fairly priced. This view of intrinsic value was quite definite, but it proved almost worthless as a practical matter because neither the average earnings nor the average market price evinced any tendency to be governed by the book value.

**内在价值与“盈利能力”。**因此，这一观点被一种新的观点所取代，即企业的内在价值由其盈利能力决定。但“盈利能力”这一表述必然意味着对未来某些结果的相当有信心的预期。仅仅知道过去的平均收益是多少，或者知道收益呈现上升或下降的趋势，是不够的。必须要有合理的依据来相信这一平均值或趋势能够可靠地预示未来。经验充分表明，在许多情况下事实远非如此。这意味着，将“盈利能力”表述为一个确定的数字，以及由此得出的所谓确定且可测量的内在价值概念，不能被安全地视为证券分析的*通用前提*。

<!--en-->
**Intrinsic Value and “Earning Power.”** Hence this idea was superseded by a newer view, viz., that the intrinsic value of a business was determined by its earning power. But the phrase “earning power” must imply a fairly confident expectation of certain future results. It is not sufficient to know what the past earnings have averaged, or even that they disclose a definite line of growth or decline. There must be plausible grounds for believing that this average or this trend is a dependable guide to the future. Experience has shown only too forcibly that in many instances this is far from true. This means that the concept of “earning power,” expressed as a definite figure, and the derived concept of intrinsic value, as something equallydefinite and ascertainable, cannot be safely accepted as a *general premise* of security analysis.

*示例：*为使这一推理更加清晰，让我们来看一个具体且典型的例子。比如说在1933年初对J. I. Case Company的普通股进行内在价值分析时，我们所说的内在价值指的是什么？当时的市场价格为30美元；每股资产价值为176美元；没有派发股息；十年来的平均每股收益为9.50美元；1932年的业绩则显示每股出现17美元的*亏损*。如果我们采用常规的评估方法，可以取十年间普通股的平均每股收益，再乘以10，从而得出95美元的内在价值。但让我们仔细看看构成这一十年平均值的各个数据。它们如下表所示。显然，9.50美元这个平均值只不过是十个互不相关的数字的算术平均值而已。很难说这个平均值能代表过去的*典型*状况，或是未来可能出现的状况。因此，从这个平均值得出的任何“真实”或内在价值数值，也都同样具有偶然性或人为性。² *J.I. Case普通股每股收益*

<!--en-->
*Example:* To make this reasoning clearer, let us consider a concrete and typical example. What would we mean by the intrinsic value of J. I. Case Company common, as analyzed, say, early in 1933? The market price was $30; the asset value per share was $176; no dividend was being paid; the average earnings for ten years had been $9.50 per share; the results for 1932 had shown a *deficit* of $17 per share. If we followed a customary method of appraisal, we might take the average earnings per share of common for ten years, multiply this average by ten, and arrive at an intrinsic value of $95. But let us examine the individual figures which make up this ten-year average. They are as shown in the table that follows. The average of $9.50 is obviously nothing more than an arithmetical resultant from ten unrelated figures. It can hardly be urged that this average is in any way representative of *typical* conditions in the past or representative of what may be expected in the future. Hence any figure of “real” or intrinsic value derived from this average must be characterized as equally accidental or artificial.²
