(d) 赤字。**内在价值在分析师工作中的作用**。让我们试着阐述一下内在价值在分析师工作中的作用，以此调和我们各种例子中相互矛盾的结论。关键在于，证券分析并不试图精确确定某只证券的内在价值，它只需判断该价值是否*足够*——例如足以保障债券的安全或为股票购买提供依据——或者该价值明显高于或低于市场价格。为此，一个模糊且近似的内在价值衡量标准或许就足够了。用一个通俗的比喻来说，无需知道一个人的年龄就能判断其是否已到投票年龄，也无需知道一个人的确切体重就能判断其是否超重。

<!--en-->
(d) Deficit.
**The Role of Intrinsic Value in the Work of the Analyst.** Let us try to formulate a statement of the role of intrinsic value in the work of the analyst which will reconcile the rather conflicting implications of our various examples. The essential point is that security analysis does not seek to determine exactly what is the intrinsic value of a given security. It needs only to establish either that the value is *adequate*—e.g., to protect a bond or to justify a stock purchase —or else that the value is considerably higher or considerably lower than the market price. For such purposes an indefinite and approximate measure of the intrinsic value may be sufficient. To use a homely simile, it is quite possible to decide by inspection that a woman is old enough to vote without knowing her age or that a man is heavier than he should be without knowing his exact weight.

通过简要回顾我们的例子，这一观点可以更加清晰。拒绝收购圣路易斯-旧金山优先股时，并不需要精确计算该铁路系统的内在价值，只需从收益记录中简单证明：用于偿还债券持有人和优先股持有人债权的价值余量太小，无法确保安全即可。而欧文斯-伊利诺伊玻璃公司5年期债券的情况则完全相反。在这种情况下，要给出该企业的公平估值无疑也很困难；但很容易判断出其价值无论如何都远高于公司的债务总额。

<!--en-->
This statement of the case may be made clearer by a brief return to our examples. The rejection of St. Louis-San Francisco Preferred did not require an exact calculation of the intrinsic value of this railroad system. It was enough to show, very simply from the earnings record, that the margin of value above the bondholders' and preferred stockholders' claims was too small to assure safety. Exactly the opposite was true for the Owens-Illinois Glass 5s. In this instance, also, it would undoubtedly have been difficult to arrive at a fair valuation of the business; but it was quite easy to decide that this value in any event was far in excess of the company's debt.

在莱特航空公司的例子中，早期的情况表明该企业的价值远高于每股8美元，即1,800,000美元。而在随后的一年里，有同样确凿的证据表明该企业的合理价值并非每股280美元，即总计70,000,000美元。分析师很难确定1922年莱特航空公司的实际价值是每股20美元还是40美元，或是1929年为每股50美元或80美元。但幸运的是，为了得出“股价8美元时具有吸引力，而280美元时从内在价值角度看缺乏吸引力”的结论，并不需要确定这些数值。

<!--en-->
In the Wright Aeronautical example, the earlier situation presented a set of facts which demonstrated that the business was worth substantially more than $8 per share, or $1,800,000. In the later year, the facts were equally conclusive that the business did not have a reasonable value of $280 per share, or $70,000,000 in all. It would have been difficult for the analyst to determine whether Wright Aeronautical was actually worth $20 or $40 a share in 1922—or actually worth $50 or $80 in 1929. But fortunately it was not necessary to decide these points in order to conclude that the shares were attractive at $8 and unattractive, intrinsically, at $280.

J. I. Case公司的例子则展示了更为常见的普通股情形，即分析师无法可靠地判断内在价值与市场价格之间的关系。但即便如此，*如果价格足够低或足够高*，或许也能得出结论。为了表达这种不确定性，我们可以说1933年初很难判断Case公司普通股的内在价值更接近30美元还是130美元。然而，如果该股票的售价低至10美元，分析师无疑有理由宣称其价值高于市场价。

<!--en-->
The J. I. Case example illustrates the far more typical common-stock situation, in which the analyst cannot reach adependable conclusion as to the relation of intrinsic value to market price. But even here, *if the price had been low or high enough*, a conclusion might have been warranted. To express the uncertainty of the picture, we might say that it was difficult to determine in early 1933 whether the intrinsic value of Case common was nearer $30 or $130. Yet if the stock had been selling at as low as $10, the analyst would undoubtedly have been justified in declaring that it was worth more than the market price.

**内在价值概念的灵活性**。这说明了内在价值概念在证券分析中的应用具有多大的灵活性。我们对内在价值的理解会因具体案例的不同而有所差异。这种差异的程度可以用一个假设的“近似价值范围”来表示，随着不确定性的增加，这个范围会变宽——例如1922年莱特航空公司的范围是20美元到40美元，而1933年Case公司的范围则是30美元到130美元。由此可见，即使对内在价值只有非常模糊的概念，只要当前价格远远偏离最高或最低估值，依然可以得出结论。

<!--en-->
**Flexibility of the Concept of Intrinsic Value.** This should indicate how flexible is the concept of intrinsic value as applied to security analysis. Our notion of the intrinsic value may be more or less distinct, depending on the particular case. The degree of indistinctness may be expressed by a very hypothetical “range of approximate value,” which would grow wider as the uncertainty of the picture increased, e.g., $20 to $40 for Wright Aeronautical in 1922 as against $30 to $130 for Case in 1933. It would follow that even a very indefinite idea of the intrinsic value may still justify a conclusion if the current price falls far outside either the maximum or minimum appraisal.

**特殊情况下更明确的概念**。跨区快速交通系统的例子比其他任何例子都更便于进行精确推理。在这里，5%利率债券的既定市场价格可以直接推导出7%利率债券的明确估值。如果能够确定用于担保这些债券的抵押品会被收购并分配给债券持有者，那么数学上的关系——即7%利率债券的价值为1,736美元，而5%利率债券的价值为1,000美元——最终会在市场上以这一比例体现出来。但由于其中存在类似政治层面的复杂因素，无法确定这一正常流程一定会发生。因此，实际上无法断言7%利率债券的价值确实比5%利率债券高出74%，但可以肯定地说其价值*显著更高*——当两种债券以相同价格出售时，这是一个非常有用的结论。

<!--en-->
**More Definite Concept in Special Cases.** The Interborough Rapid Transit example permits a more precise line of reasoning than any of the others. Here a given market price for the 5% bonds results in a very definite valuation for the 7% notes. If it were certain that the collateral securing the notes would be acquired for and distributed to the note holders, then the mathematical relationship—*viz.*, $1,736 of value for the 7s against $1,000 of value for the 5s—would eventually be established at this ratio in the market. But because of quasi-political complications in the picture, this normal procedure could not be expected with certainty. As a practical matter, therefore, it is not possible to say that the 7s are actually worth 74% more than the 5s, but it may be said with assurance that the 7s are worth *substantially more*—which is a very useful conclusion to arrive at when both issues are selling at the same price.

Interborough股票案例属于一类较为特殊的情形，在这类情形下，分析得出的关于内在价值的结论往往比普通情况下更为明确。这些情形可能涉及资产清算，或产生被称为“套利”或“对冲”的金融操作。虽然从抽象层面来看，它们或许是分析师工作最理想的领域，但由于其专业性较强且发生频率较低，从更广泛的投资理论与实践角度而言，其重要性相对较低。

<!--en-->
The Interborough issues are an example of a rather special group of situations in which analysis may reach more definiteconclusions respecting intrinsic value than in the ordinary case. These situations may involve a liquidation or give rise to technical operations known as “arbitrage” or “hedging.” While, viewed in the abstract, they are probably the most satisfactory field for the analyst’s work, the fact that they are specialized in character and of infrequent occurrence makes them relatively unimportant from the broader standpoint of investment theory and practice.

**分析师取得成功的主要障碍。** *a. 数据不足或错误。* 不言而喻，分析师不可能永远正确。此外，一个在逻辑上正确的结论在实际操作中也可能导致糟糕的结果。分析师工作成功的主要障碍有三个方面，即：（1）数据不足或错误；（2）未来的不确定性；（3）市场的非理性行为。其中，尽管第一种缺陷很严重，但在三者中却是最不重要的。故意篡改数据的情况很少见；大多数数据失真源于会计手段的运用，而能力强的分析师应当能够察觉这些手段。隐瞒信息比虚假陈述更为常见。不过，由于纽约证券交易所以及后来的美国证券交易委员会制定了要求更全面披露会计处理方式并作出更详细解释的法规，此类隐瞒行为的程度已大大降低。如果仍存在重要信息的隐瞒，分析师的经验和技能应使其能够注意到这一缺陷并加以考虑——当然，前提是他必须通过适当的调查和施压来获取事实真相。在某些情况下，这种隐瞒无疑会逃脱检测，从而导致错误的结论。*b. 未来的不确定性。* 未来变化因素的重要性要高得多。基于事实及表面前景得出的结论，可能会因新的发展而失效。这就引出了一个问题：证券分析在多大程度上应承担预测形势变化的功能。我们将在讨论影响分析过程的各种因素时再探讨这一点。显然，未来变化在很大程度上是不可预测的，因此证券分析通常必须假设过去的记录至少能为未来提供大致的参考。这一假设的可信度越低，分析的价值就越低。因此，该分析方法在应用于抗风险能力较强的高级证券时，比应用于普通股票更为有效；在应用于本身稳定性较高的企业时，比应用于波动剧烈的企业更为有效；最后，在相对正常的整体环境下进行时，比在极度不确定和剧烈变革的时期更为有效。c. *市场的非理性行为。* 证券分析的第三个障碍来自市场本身。从某种意义上说，市场与未来都带来了类似的困难。分析师既无法预测也无法控制它们，但其工作的成败在很大程度上取决于这两者。投资分析师的主要工作似乎与市场价格关系不大。他的典型职责是挑选那些经评估在利息和本金方面都具备安全性的高等级固定收益债券。购买者本不应关注这些债券后续的市场波动，而只需关心它们是否依然属于优质投资。在我们看来，这种对投资者态度的传统看法并不准确，甚至有些虚伪。无论何种类型的证券持有者，都会关心其市场报价。投资实践中始终强调的*流动性*这一概念，正是对这一事实的认可。如果一项证券易于出售固然重要，但能获得合理的价格则更为重要。虽然出于显而易见的原因，高等级债券的投资者对市场波动的关注程度低于投机者，但这些波动仍然会对他们产生强烈的心理影响，即便没有直接的经济影响。因此，即便在这一领域，分析师也必须考虑所有可能对市场价格产生不利影响的因素，以及那些影响证券基本安全性的因素。

<!--en-->
**Principal Obstacles to Success of the Analyst.** *a. Inadequate or Incorrect Data.* Needless to say, the analyst cannot be right all the time. Furthermore, a conclusion may be logically right but work out badly in practice. The main obstacles to the success of the analyst’s work are threefold, *viz.*, (1) the inadequacy or incorrectness of the data, (2) the uncertainties of the future, and (3) the irrational behavior of the market. The first of these drawbacks, although serious, is the least important of the three. Deliberate falsification of the data is rare; most of the misrepresentation flows from the use of accounting artifices which it is the function of the capable analyst to detect. Concealment is more common than misstatement. But the extent of such concealment has been greatly reduced as the result of regulations, first of the New York Stock Exchange and later of the S.E.C., requiring more complete disclosure and fuller explanation of accounting practices. Where information on an important point is still withheld, the analyst’s experience and skill should lead him to note this defect and make allowance therefor—if, indeed, he may not elicit the facts by proper inquiry and pressure. In some cases, no doubt, the concealment will elude detection and give rise to an incorrect conclusion.
*b. Uncertainties of the Future.* Of much greater moment is the element of future change. A conclusion warranted by the facts and by the apparent prospects may be vitiated by new developments. This raises the question of how far it is the function of security analysis to anticipate changed conditions. We shall defer consideration of this point until our discussion of various factors entering into the processes of analysis. It is manifest, however, that future changes are largely unpredictable, and that security analysis must ordinarilyproceed on the assumption that the past record affords at least a rough guide to the future. The more questionable this assumption, the less valuable is the analysis. Hence this technique is more useful when applied to senior securities (which are protected against change) than to common stocks; more useful when applied to a business of inherently stable character than to one subject to wide variations; and, finally, more useful when carried on under fairly normal general conditions than in times of great uncertainty and radical change.
c. *The Irrational Behavior of the Market.* The third handicap to security analysis is found in the market itself. In a sense the market and the future present the same kind of difficulties. Neither can be predicted or controlled by the analyst, yet his success is largely dependent upon them both. The major activities of the investment analyst may be thought to have little or no concern with market prices. His typical function is the selection of high-grade, fixed-income-bearing bonds, which upon investigation he judges to be secure as to interest and principal. The purchaser is supposed to pay no attention to their subsequent market fluctuations, but to be interested solely in the question whether the bonds will continue to be sound investments. In our opinion this traditional view of the investor's attitude is inaccurate and somewhat hypocritical. Owners of securities, whatever their character, are interested in their market quotations. This fact is recognized by the emphasis always laid in investment practice upon *marketability*. If it is important that an issue be readily salable, it is still more important that it command a satisfactory price. While for obvious reasons the investor in high-grade bonds has a lesser concern with market fluctuations than has the speculator, they still have a strong psychological, if not financial, effect upon him. Even in this field, therefore, the analyst must take into account whatever influences may adversely govern the market price, as well as those which bear upon the basic safety of the issue.

在分析师工作中负责发现被低估、甚至可能被高估的证券的部分，他需要更直接地关注市场价格。

<!--en-->
In that portion of the analyst's activities which relates to the discovery of undervalued, and possibly of overvalued securities, he is more directly concerned with market prices.

在此，对其判断的正确性之证明主要在于该证券最终的市场表现。这类分析工作基于两个假设：其一，市场价格常常与真实价值不符；其二，这些差异具有自我修正的固有趋势。关于前一个论点的真实性几乎无需怀疑——尽管华尔街常常夸耀“市场判断无懈可击”，并声称“股票的价值取决于其售价，多一分少一分都不行”。

<!--en-->
For here the vindication of his judgment must be found largely in the ultimate market action of the issue. This field of analytical work may be said to rest upon a twofold assumption: first, that the market price is frequently out of line with the true value; and, second, that there is an inherent tendency for these disparities to correct themselves. As to the truth of the former statement, there can be very little doubt— even though Wall Street often speaks glibly of the “infallible judgment of the market” and asserts that “a stock is worth what you can sell it for—neither more nor less.”

**价格价值调整滞后的风险。**第二个假设在理论上同样成立，但在实践中往往效果不佳。因疏忽或偏见导致的低估可能会持续过长的时间，而因过度热情或人为刺激导致的过高价格也是如此。对分析师而言，特别的危险在于：由于这种延迟，在市场价格根据他所确定的价值进行调整之前，可能会出现新的决定性因素。换言之，当价格最终反映价值时，该价值可能已经发生了显著变化，而他当初做出决策所依据的事实和推理也可能不再适用。

<!--en-->
**The Hazard of Tardy Adjustment of Price Value.** The second assumption is equally true in theory, but its working out in practice is often most unsatisfactory. Undervaluations caused by neglect or prejudice may persist for an inconveniently long time, and the same applies to inflated prices caused by overenthusiasm or artificial stimulants. The particular danger to the analyst is that, because of such delay, new determining factors may supervene before the market price adjusts itself to the value as he found it. In other words, by the time the price finally does reflect the value, this value may have changed considerably and the facts and reasoning on which his decision was based may no longer be applicable.

分析师必须尽最大努力防范这一风险：一方面，尽量选择那些不会突然发生变化的证券；另一方面，选择那些公众兴趣足够浓厚、能够对其率先识别的价值因素作出较快反应的证券；再一方面，根据整体金融形势调整自己的操作策略——在经济和市场状况较为平稳时，更注重发现被低估的证券；而在异常压力和不确定性时期，则需更加谨慎行事。

<!--en-->
The analyst must seek to guard himself against this danger as best he can: in part, by dealing with those situations preferably which are not subject to sudden change; in part, by favoring securities in which the popular interest is keen enough to promise a fairly swift response to value elements which he is the first to recognize; in part, by tempering his activities to the general financial situation—laying more emphasis on the discovery of undervalued securities when business and market conditions are on a fairly even keel, and proceeding with greater caution in times of abnormal stress and uncertainty.

**内在价值与市场价格的关系。**下图展示了导致市场价格的各个步骤，有助于更清晰地理解内在价值与市场报价之间的关系。从图中可以看出，我们所说的分析因素对市场价格的影响既是*部分的*，也是*间接的*——部分是因为它常常与起相反作用的纯粹投机因素相互竞争；间接则是因为它是通过人们的情感和决策来发挥作用的。换句话说，市场并非一台*称重机*，不会根据每只证券的具体特质通过精确且客观的机制记录其价值。相反，市场更像一台*投票机*，无数个体在其中表达的选择既包含理性成分，也包含情感因素。

<!--en-->
**The Relationship of Intrinsic Value to Market Price.** The general question of the relation of intrinsic value to the market quotation may be made clearer by the following chart, which traces the various steps culminating in the market price. It will be evident from the chart that the influence of what we call analytical factors over the market price is both *partial* and*indirect*—partial, because it frequently competes with purely speculative factors which influence the price in the opposite direction; and indirect, because it acts through the intermediary of people's sentiments and decisions. In other words, the market is not a *weighing machine*, on which the value of each issue is recorded by an exact and impersonal mechanism, in accordance with its specific qualities. Rather should we say that the market is a *voting machine*, whereon countless individuals register choices which are the product partly of reason and partly of emotion.

## 分析与投机

<!--en-->
*ANALYSIS AND SPECULATION*

人们或许认为，合理的分析在任何情况下都能带来成功结果，包括那些明显属于投机性质的、即充满高度不确定性和风险的情境。如果对投机性证券的选择是基于对该公司状况的专家研究，这种方法难道不会为投资者带来巨大优势吗？既然未来事件具有不确定性，难道有利与不利的发展不会大致相互抵消，从而使合理分析带来的初始优势最终转化为平均利润吗？这是个看似合理的论点，实则具有欺骗性；人们轻易接受这一观点，导致许多分析师误入歧途。因此，有必要详细阐述几个反对在投机情境中过度依赖分析的有效论据。

<!--en-->
It may be thought that sound analysis should produce successful results in any type of situation, including the confessedly speculative, *i.e.*, those subject to substantial uncertainty and risk. If the selection of speculative issues is based on expert study of the companies' position, should notthis approach give the purchaser a considerable advantage? Admitting future events to be uncertain, could not the favorable and unfavorable developments be counted on to cancel out against each other, more or less, so that the initial advantage afforded by sound analysis will carry through into an eventual average profit? This is a plausible argument but a deceptive one; and its over-ready acceptance has done much to lead analysts astray. It is worth while, therefore, to detail several valid arguments against placing chief reliance upon analysis in speculative situations.

首先，所谓投机的运作机制会给投机者带来严重的障碍，这些障碍可能超过分析研究所带来的好处。这些不利因素包括佣金和利息支出、所谓的“市场差价”（即买价与卖价之间的差额），以及最重要的一点：除非采用某种与分析方法相悖的特定交易技巧，否则平均亏损往往会超过平均盈利。

<!--en-->
In the first place, what may be called the mechanics of speculation involves serious handicaps to the speculator, which may outweigh the benefits conferred by analytical study. These disadvantages include the payment of commissions and interest charges, the so-called "turn of the market" (meaning the spread between the bid and asked price), and, most important of all, an inherent tendency for the average loss to exceed the average profit, unless a certain technique of trading is followed, which is opposed to the analytical approach.

第二个反对意见是：在投机性情境中，作为分析基础的各种因素会迅速且突然地发生变动。此前已经提到过，内在价值可能在市场价格反映出来之前就发生变化，这一风险在投机情境中要比投资情境严重得多。第三个难题则源于那些必然被排除在证券分析之外的未知因素。从理论上讲，这些未知因素有好有坏的可能性各半，因此从长远来看应该会相互抵消。例如，通过比较分析往往很容易发现，同一行业中的两家公司，尽管前景看似相似，但其中一家的股价相对于其盈利水平来说要低得多；不过，那只看似具有吸引力的股票的低价，很可能是因为存在某些重要的不利因素，而这些因素虽然未被公开，但公司内部人士却是知晓的——反之，那些股价高于其相对价值的股票，也可能存在类似的情况。在投机情境中，那些“内行”往往拥有这种优势，这便否定了“有利与不利的变化应当相互抵消”这一前提，同时也让那些只能依据部分被隐瞒的事实进行分析的分析师处于不利地位。³ **随着随机因素的增加，分析的价值也会降低。**最后一个反对意见基于更为抽象的原理，但其实际重要性依然极高。即便我们承认分析能够为投机者带来数学上的优势，这也并不能保证他一定能获利。他的投资行为依然充满风险；在任何具体案例中都可能遭受损失；而在交易结束后，也很难判断分析师的贡献究竟是带来了好处还是害处。因此，分析师在投机领域的地位充其量只是不确定的，而且还略显缺乏专业尊严。这就好比分析师与命运女神在投机的“钢琴”上合奏，而多变的命运女神掌控着所有的旋律。

<!--en-->
The second objection is that the underlying analytical factors in speculative situations are subject to swift and sudden revision. The danger, already referred to, that the intrinsic value may change before the market price reflects that value, is therefore much more serious in speculative than in investment situations. A third difficulty arises from circumstances surrounding the unknown factors, which are necessarily left out of security analysis. Theoretically these unknown factors should have an equal chance of being favorable or unfavorable, and thus they should neutralize each other in the long run. For example, it is often easy to determine by comparative analysis that one company is selling much lower than another in the same field, in relation to earnings, although both apparently have similar prospects. But it may well be that the low price for the apparently attractive issue is due to certain important unfavorable factors which, though not disclosed, are known to those identified with the company—and *vice versa* for the issue seemingly selling above its relative value. In speculative situations, those "onthe inside” often have an advantage of this kind which nullifies the premise that good and bad changes in the picture should offset each other, and which loads the dice against the analyst working with some of the facts concealed from him.³
**The Value of Analysis Diminishes as the Element of Chance Increases.** The final objection is based on more abstract grounds, but, nevertheless, its practical importance is very great. Even if we grant that analysis can give the speculator a mathematical advantage, it does not assure him a profit. His ventures remain hazardous; in any individual case a loss may be taken; and after the operation is concluded, it is difficult to determine whether the analyst’s contribution has been a benefit or a detriment. Hence the latter’s position in the speculative field is at best uncertain and somewhat lacking in professional dignity. It is as though the analyst and Dame Fortune were playing a duet on the speculative piano, with the fickle goddess calling all the tunes.

用另一个不那么富有想象力的类比，我们可以更直观地说明为何分析本质上更适合投资而非投机情境。（为了在后续章节中进行更详细的探讨，本章一直假设投资意味着预期的安全性，而投机则意味着明确存在的风险。）在蒙特卡洛赌场中，轮盘赌的赔率是19比18，有利于轮盘所有者，这意味着平均而言，每有37美元的投注，他就能赢1美元。这或许暗示了未经训练的投资者或投机者的不利处境。假设某位轮盘赌玩家通过某种类似分析的方法，能够在有限的几次投注中将赔率逆转，使其变为18比19，有利于自己。如果他将投注金额平均分配到所有数字上，那么无论哪个数字出现，他都能获得一定的收益。这一操作可以类比为在有利的一般条件下，基于扎实分析所进行的投资计划。

<!--en-->
By another and less imaginative simile, we might more convincingly show why analysis is inherently better suited to investment than to speculative situation. (In anticipation of a more detailed inquiry in a later chapter, we have assumed throughout this chapter that investment implies expected safety and speculation connotes acknowledged risk.) In Monte Carlo the odds are weighted 19 to 18 in favor of the proprietor of the roulette wheel, so that on the average he wins one dollar out of each 37 wagered by the public. This may suggest the odds against the untrained investor or speculator. Let us assume that, through some equivalent of analysis, a roulette player is able to reverse the odds for a limited number of wagers, so that they are now 18 to 19 in his favor. If he distributes his wagers evenly over all the numbers, then whichever one turns up he is certain to win a moderate amount. This operation may be likened to an investment program based upon sound analysis and carried on under propitious general conditions.

但如果玩家将全部资金押在同一个数字上，那微小的胜算与“运气是否会选中他所选的数字”这一关键问题相比就显得无关紧要了。如果他运气好，“分析”或许能让他多赢一点；但若运气不佳，这种分析就毫无用处。或许稍加夸张地说，这正是处理纯粹投机性交易的分析师所处的境地。在投资领域中几乎能确保良好结果的那种数学优势，在运气起主导作用的情况下可能会完全失效。

<!--en-->
But if the player wagers all his money on a single number, the small odds in his favor are of slight importance compared with the crucial question whether chance will elect the number he has chosen. His “analysis” will enable him to win a littlemore if he is lucky; it will be of no value when luck is against him. This, in slightly exaggerated form perhaps, describes the position of the analyst dealing with essentially speculative operations. Exactly the same mathematical advantage which practically assures good results in the investment field may prove entirely ineffective where luck is the overshadowing influence.

因此，将分析视为投机的*辅助工具*而非*指导原则*似乎更为明智。只有当运气处于次要地位时，分析师才能以权威的口吻发表意见，并对其判断结果负责。

<!--en-->
It would seem prudent, therefore, to consider analysis as an *adjunct* or *auxiliary* rather than as a *guide* in speculation. It is only where chance plays a subordinate role that the analyst can properly speak in an authoritative voice and accept responsibility for the results of his judgments.

## 3. 证券分析的关键功能

<!--en-->
*3. THE CRITICAL FUNCTION OF SECURITY ANALYSIS*

投资金融的原理以及企业融资的方法，都属于证券分析的范畴。分析判断是通过将标准应用于事实得出的。因此，分析师需要关注选择标准是否合理且具备可行性。他还希望看到证券，尤其是债券和优先股，在发行时能配备足够的保护条款，更重要的是，确保执行这些条款的适当方法能成为公认的金融惯例。

<!--en-->
The principles of investment finance and the methods of corporation finance fall necessarily within the province of security analysis. Analytical judgments are reached by applying standards to facts. The analyst is concerned, therefore, with the soundness and practicability of the standards of selection. He is also interested to see that securities, especially bonds and preferred stocks, be issued with adequate protective provisions, and—more important still—that proper methods of enforcement of these covenants be part of accepted financial practice.

对分析师而言，公正地呈现事实至关重要，这意味着他必须对会计方法保持高度的批判性。最后，他还必须关注所有可能影响证券持有人的公司政策，因为他所分析的证券价值在很大程度上可能取决于管理层的决策。这类问题包括资本化处理方式、股息与扩张政策、管理层薪酬，甚至是对亏损企业的继续经营还是清算决策。

<!--en-->
It is a matter of great moment to the analyst that the facts be fairly presented, and this means that he must be highly critical of accounting methods. Finally, he must concern himself with all corporate policies affecting the security owner, for the value of the issue which he analyzes may be largely dependent upon the acts of the management. In this category are included questions of capitalization set-up, of dividend and expansion policies, of managerial compensation, and even of continuing or liquidating an unprofitable business.

在这些重要性各异的问题上，安全分析能够提供关键的判断，有助于避免错误、纠正不当行为，并更好地保护债券或股票持有者。[^458]：¹ 关于上述六个案例的后续情况，请参见附录注2。² 1933年至1939年间，Case普通股的收益在每股亏损14.66美元到盈利19.20美元之间波动，平均为3.18美元；股价则在30又1/2美元到191又3/4美元之间变动，1939年的收盘价为73又3/4美元。³ 关于“高市盈率股票”与“低市盈率股票”市场表现对比的研究结果，请参见附录注3。第二章

<!--en-->
On these matters of varied import, security analysis may be competent to express critical judgments, looking to theavoidance of mistakes, to the correction of abuses, and to the better protection of those owning bonds or stocks.
[^458]: ¹ For the sequels to the six examples just given, see Appendix Note 2.
² Between 1933 and 1939 the earnings on Case common varied between a deficit of $14.66 and profits of $19.20 per share, averaging $3.18. The price ranged between $30\frac{1}{2}$ and $191\frac{3}{4}$, closing in 1939 at $73\frac{3}{4}$.
³ See Appendix Note 3 for the result of a study of the market behavior of “high price-earnings ratio stocks” as compared with “low price-earnings ratio stocks.”
CHAPTER 2

# 分析问题中的基本要素：定量与定性因素

<!--en-->
*Fundamental Elements in the Problem of Analysis. Quantitative and Qualitative Factors*

在上一章中，我们从分析者希望实现的目标出发，探讨了一些分析相关的概念与方法。现在，让我们设想分析者正在开展工作，思考在处理特定问题时需要考虑的总体因素，以及面对各种信息时应持有的总体态度。

<!--en-->
IN THE PREVIOUS chapter we referred to some of the concepts and materials of analysis from the standpoint of their bearing on what the analyst may hope to accomplish. Let us now imagine the analyst at work and ask what are the broad considerations which govern his approach to a particular problem, and also what should be his general attitude toward the various kinds of information with which he has to deal.

## 四大基本要素

<!--en-->
*FOUR FUNDAMENTAL ELEMENTS*

安全分析的目的是回答或协助回答一些极具实用性的问题。其中，最常见的或许包括以下几类：为了特定目的应购买哪些证券？应当买入、卖出还是持有$S$？

<!--en-->
The object of security analysis is to answer, or assist in answering, certain questions of a very practical nature. Of these, perhaps the most customary are the following: What securities should be bought for a given purpose? Should issue $S$ be bought, or sold, or retained?

在所有此类问题中，可以说有四个主要因素以明示或隐含的方式参与其中。它们分别是：

<!--en-->
In all such questions, four major factors may be said to enter, either expressly or by implication. These are:

1. 安全性。
2. 价格。
3. 时间。
4. 人。更完整地来说，第二个典型问题会是：此时，在价格$P$、当前时间$T$的情况下，个人$I$是否应该购买（或出售、或持有）安全证券$S$？因此，讨论这四个因素的相对重要性是相关的，我们觉得按相反顺序考虑它们更为方便。**个人因素**。个人因素在不同程度上影响每一笔证券购买决策。通常最重要的因素是潜在买方的财务状况。对商人来说可能具有吸引力的投资，受托人或收入有限的寡妇绝不应尝试。同样，对于那些完全享受税收减免的权益毫无好处的群体，不应购买美国自由证券$3\frac{1}{2}$，因为从部分应税政府债券中可以获得高得多的收益。¹其他偶尔可能影响个人证券选择的个人特征包括他的财务培训和能力、性格以及偏好。但无论这些考虑因素多么重要，它们通常不是分析中的决定性因素。大多数从分析中得出的结论可以用非个人化的术语来表达，适用于所有投资者或投机者。**时间**。分析证券的时间方式会以多种方式影响结论。某家公司的表现可能有时更好，前景也可能看起来更乐观，这些变化的环境必然会对分析师对该证券的看法产生不同影响。此外，证券的选择是基于质量和收益标准，这两个标准——尤其是后者——会随整体金融状况而变化。1931年6月，一张最高等级、收益为5%的铁路债券看起来很有吸引力，因为这类债券的平均收益为4.32%。但六个月后推出的同一款债券则非常不吸引人，因为在此期间债券价格大幅下跌，该群体的收益上升到了5.86%。最后，几乎所有证券投资都在一定程度上受到当前金融和商业前景的影响。在投机操作中，这些考虑因素具有关键性；虽然保守投资通常认为可以忽略这些因素，但在压力与不确定时期，它们也可能被忽视。作为研究，证券分析必须尽可能关注在所有时间——或至少在所有正常条件下——都有效的原则和方法。然而，需要注意的是，分析的实际应用是在不断变化的时代背景下进行的。**价格**。价格是与证券相关的完整判断不可或缺的一部分。在选择优质投资债券时，价格通常是次要因素，不是因为无关紧要，而是因为实际上价格很少过高。因此，几乎全部重点都放在该证券是否具备充分保障上。但在特殊情况下，如购买高等级*可转换*债券时，价格可能与保障程度同样重要。以美国电话电报公司1939年到期的4 1/2美元可转换债券为例，1929年其售价超过200美元。本金和利息确实安全无虞，但这并不妨碍该证券以该价格进行购买时极具风险——事实上，之后其市场价值损失了超过一半。²对于普通股而言，考虑价格的重要性更为突出，因为支付错误价格的风险几乎与购买错误证券的风险一样大。 我们稍后会指出，新时代的投资理论忽略了价格因素，这种遗漏导致了最灾难性的后果。**证券：企业的性质与承诺条款。**如果我们以不同的形式重新表述问题，就能更清晰地说明证券及其价格在投资决策中扮演的角色。与其问：$P$ 购买什么证券？$T$ 以什么价格购买？不如问：(1) 投资的是哪种企业？(2) 承诺的条款是什么？这样就能更全面地、均衡地对比分析中的两个基本要素。所谓投资的"条款"或"投机条款"，不仅指价格，还包括发行条款及其当时的情况或表现。**以不利条款进行的承诺示例。**对最稳健类型的企业进行投资，也可能采用不稳健且不利的条款。在1929年之前，城市房地产的价值在多年间持续稳定增长，因此许多人将其视为"最安全"的投资工具。但1929年，在纽约市房地产开发项目中购买优先股，其投资条款可能极其不利，以至于完全失去了稳健性。这样一份股票发行条款可以概括如下：³
1. *发行条款。* 这是一种优先股，其优先级低于第一顺位的抵押贷款，且不享有无限制的股息或本金偿还权。它的优先级高于普通股，因为普通股并不涉及现金投资，因此普通股股东没有损失，反而可能获得巨大收益；而优先股股东则可能面临全部损失，仅能分得少量潜在收益。
2. *发行状况。* 这是一项针对新建建筑的投资，建设成本极高，且若出现问题时没有储备金或其他次级资本可供依靠。
3. *发行价格。* 按面值计算，其股息回报率为6%，远低于具有诸多优势的房地产第二顺位抵押贷款的收益率。⁴ **优质条款下的投资示例。** 我们只需看看近年来的电力与照明融资项目，就能发现许多在本质上极具吸引力的行业中存在不良证券的例子。作为对比，我们可以举1950年到期的布鲁克林联合高架铁路第一系列5年期债券的案例，该债券于1932年以60的价格出售，到期时的收益率为9.85%。这些债券属于布鲁克林-曼哈顿交通系统的债务。由于汽车竞争以及监管和票价合同方面的问题，铁路运输行业长期以来一直被视为不利行业。因此，这类证券代表的企业类型相对缺乏吸引力。然而，正如以下内容所示，此处的投资条款却可能使其成为一项不错的投资选择：
1. *发行条款。* 根据运营公司与纽约市之间的协议，这是对该系统由公司和市政府共同拥有的地铁及高架线路收益的第一顺位抵押，其投资规模远远超过此次发行的金额。
2. *发行状况。* 除了上文所述的极为特殊的特殊保护措施外，这些债券还属于一家盈利稳定且似乎完全具备足够盈利能力的公司的债务。
3. *发行价格。* 购买该债券的收益率略高于1968年到期的布鲁克林-曼哈顿交通公司6年期债券，后者的优先级较低。（1932年时，后者的发行价格为68，收益率为9%，而布鲁克林联合高架铁路5年期债券的收益率为9.85%。⁵） **投资条款与企业性质的相对重要性。** 我们将企业性质与投资条款区分开来，这就引出了一个问题：哪个要素更为重要？是在条件不佳的企业中进行投资，还是在条件优秀的企业中进行投资？大众观点毫不犹豫地倾向于前者，但从直觉而非逻辑上来看，这种选择是正确的。从长期经验来看，绝大多数投资者因为为最受看好的企业的证券支付过高价格而损失的资金，肯定少于那些试图从质量较差的企业中获得更高收入或利润而损失的资金。不过，从分析的角度来看，这一经验结果并不能彻底解决这个问题。它仅仅体现了一个适用于所有商品的规则，即*缺乏经验的买家*通过购买声誉最佳的商品，即便需要支付较高的价格，也能获得最佳结果。但显然，这并非指导专业商品买家的规则，因为专业人士应通过实际检验来判断质量，而不仅仅依赖声誉；有时，如果所购商品能够满足需求且价格合理，他们甚至可以牺牲一定的质量标准。这一区别既适用于证券购买，也适用于油漆或手表的购买。它导致了两种截然相反的原则：一种适合缺乏经验的投资者，另一种仅对分析师有用。
1. 缺乏经验的证券买家的原则：*无论何种条件，都不要将资金投入低质量企业。*
2. 证券分析师应遵循的原则：*几乎所有证券在某个价格区间可能显得便宜，而在另一个区间则可能显得昂贵。*我们曾批评过分侧重于企业选择的做法，因为这往往会导致为优质证券支付过高的价格。第二个反对意见是，所选企业本身可能并非明智之选。当然，人们会倾向于选择规模大、管理良好、业绩出色且未来盈利有望持续增长的企业，但这些看似合理的预期往往无法实现。许多昔日的领军企业如今已落后众多。明天也很可能上演类似的故事。最有力的例证便是过去二十年来铁路行业整体投资地位的持续下滑。企业的状况部分取决于事实，部分则取决于主观看法。近年来，关于投资的观点表现得极为不稳定且不可靠。1929年时，西屋电气制造公司被普遍认为拥有极为有利的行业地位；两年后，其股票售价甚至低于其流动资产净值，这显然表明市场对其未来能否获得任何利润存在广泛疑虑。1929年被视为近乎奇迹般的企业——大西洋太平洋茶业公司，其股价从那年的494点跌至1938年的36点。到那时，其普通股售价甚至低于其现金资产，而优先股则有足够的其他流动资产作为支撑。这些因素并不否定“未经专业培训的投资者应仅投资于最受认可的企业”这一原则。不过需要明白，之所以建议他们如此选择，是因为其他投资方向的风险更高，而非因为最受欢迎的股票就一定最安全。分析师必须认真关注市场的判断以及市场大力青睐的企业，但同时也要保持独立且批判性的视角。当有足够充分且有说服力的理由时，他也应毫不犹豫地谴责那些受欢迎但实际不佳的投资标的，而支持那些不那么受欢迎但更优的选择。

<!--en-->
1. The security.
2. The price.
3. The time.
4. The person.
More completely stated, the second typical question would run, Should security $S$ be bought (or sold, or retained) at price $P$, at this time $T$, by individual $I$? Some discussion of the relative significance of these four factors is therefore pertinent, and we shall find it convenient to consider them in inverse order.
**The Personal Element.** The personal element enters to a greater or lesser extent into every security purchase. The aspect of chief importance is usually the financial position of the intending buyer. What might be an attractive speculation for a business man should under no circumstances be attempted by a trustee or a widow with limited income. Again, United States Liberty $3\frac{1}{2}$s should not have been purchased by those to whom their complete tax-exemption feature was of no benefit, when a considerably higher yield could be obtained from partially taxable governmental issues.¹
Other personal characteristics that on occasion might properly influence the individual's choice of securities are his financial training and competence, his temperament, and his preferences. But however vital these considerations may prove at times, they are not ordinarily determining factors in analysis. Most of the conclusions derived from analysis can be stated in impersonal terms, as applicable to investors or speculators as a class.
**The Time.** The time at which an issue is analyzed may affect the conclusion in various ways. The company's showing may be better, or its outlook may seem better, at one time than another, and these changing circumstances are bound to exert a varying influence on the analyst's viewpoint toward the issue. Furthermore, securities are selected by the application of standards of quality and yield, and both of these—particularly the latter—will vary with financial conditions in general. A railroad bond of highest grade yielding 5% seemed attractive in June 1931 because the average return on this type of bond was 4.32%. But the same offering made six months later would have been quite unattractive, for in the meantime bond prices had fallen severely and the yield on this group had increased to 5.86%. Finally, nearly all security commitments
are influenced to some extent by the current view of the financial and business outlook. In speculative operations these considerations are of controlling importance; and while conservative investment is ordinarily supposed to disregard these elements, in times of stress and uncertainty they may not be ignored.
Security analysis, as a study, must necessarily concern itself as much as possible with principles and methods which are valid at all times—or, at least, under all ordinary conditions. It should be kept in mind, however, that the practical applications of analysis are made against a background largely colored by the changing times.
**The Price.** The price is an integral part of every complete judgment relating to securities. In the selection of prime investment bonds, the price is usually a subordinate factor, not because it is a matter of indifference but because in actual practice the price is rarely unreasonably high. Hence almost entire emphasis is placed on the question whether the issue is adequately secured. But in a special case, such as the purchase of high-grade *convertible* bonds, the price may be a factor fully as important as the degree of security. This point is illustrated by the American Telephone and Telegraph Company Convertible 4 1/2s, due 1939, which sold above 200 in 1929. The fact that principal (at par) and interest were safe beyond question did not prevent the issue from being an extremely risky purchase *at that price*—one which in fact was followed by the loss of over half its market value.²
In the field of common stocks, the necessity of taking price into account is more compelling, because the danger of paying the wrong price is almost as great as that of buying the wrong issue. We shall point out later that the new-era theory of investment left price out of the reckoning, and that this omission was productive of most disastrous consequences.
**The Security: Character of the Enterprise and the Terms of the Commitment.** The roles played by the security and its price in an investment decision may be set forth more clearly if we restate the problem in somewhat different form. Instead of asking, (1) In what security? and (2) At what price? let usask, (1) In what enterprise? and (2) On what terms is the commitment proposed? This gives us a more comprehensive and evenly balanced contrast between two basic elements in analysis. By the *terms* of the investment or speculation, we mean not only the price but also the provisions of the issue and its status or showing at the time.
**Example of Commitment on Unattractive Terms.** An investment in the soundest type of enterprise may be made on unsound and unfavorable terms. Prior to 1929 the value of urban real estate had tended to grow steadily over a long period of years; hence it came to be regarded by many as the “safest” medium of investment. But the purchase of a preferred stock in a New York City real estate development in 1929 might have involved *terms* of investment so thoroughly disadvantageous as to banish all elements of soundness from the proposition. One such stock offering could be summarized as follows:³
1. *Provisions of the Issue.* A preferred stock, ranking junior to a large first mortgage and without unqualified rights to dividend or principal payments. It ranked ahead of a common stock which represented no cash investment so that the common stockholders had nothing to lose and a great deal to gain, while the preferred stockholders had everything to lose and only a small share in the possible gain.
2. *Status of the Issue.* A commitment in a new building, constructed at an exceedingly high level of costs, with no reserves or junior capital to fall back upon in case of trouble.
3. *Price of the Issue.* At par the dividend return was 6%, which was much less than the yield obtainable on real-estate second mortgages having many other advantages over this preferred stock.⁴
**Example of a Commitment on Attractive Terms.** We have only to examine electric power and light financing in recent years to find countless examples of unsound securities in a fundamentally attractive industry. By way of contrast let us cite the case of Brooklyn Union Elevated Railroad First 5s, due 1950, which sold in 1932 at 60 to yield 9.85% to maturity. They are an obligation of the Brooklyn-Manhattan TransitSystem. The traction, or electric railway, industry has long been unfavorably regarded, chiefly because of automobile competition but also on account of regulation and fare-contract difficulties. Hence this security represents a comparatively unattractive *type* of enterprise. Yet the *terms* of the investment here might well make it a satisfactory commitment, as shown by the following:
1. *Provisions of the Issue.* By contract between the operating company and the City of New York, this was a first charge on the earnings of the combined subway and elevated lines of the system, both company and city owned, representing an investment enormously greater than the size of this issue.
2. *Status of the Issue.* Apart from the very exceptional specific protection just described, the bonds were obligations of a company with stable and apparently fully adequate earning power.
3. *Price of Issue.* It could be purchased to yield somewhat more than the Brooklyn-Manhattan Transit Corporation 6s, due 1968, which occupied a subordinate position. (At the low price of 68 for the latter issue in 1932, its yield was 9% against 9.85% for the Brooklyn Union Elevated 5s.⁵)
**Relative Importance of the Terms of the Commitment and the Character of the Enterprise.** Our distinction between the character of the enterprise and the terms of the commitment suggests a question as to which element is the more important. Is it better to invest in an attractive enterprise on unattractive terms or in an unattractive enterprise on attractive terms? The popular view unhesitatingly prefers the former alternative, and in so doing it is instinctively, rather than logically, right. Over a long period, experience will undoubtedly show that less money has been lost by the great body of investors through paying too high a price for securities of the best regarded enterprises than by trying to secure a larger income or profit from commitments in enterprises of lower grade.
From the standpoint of analysis, however, this empirical result does not dispose of the matter. It merely exemplifies a rule that is applicable to all kinds of merchandise, *viz.*, that the*untrained buyer* fares best by purchasing goods of the highest reputation, even though he may pay a comparatively high price. But, needless to say, this is not a rule to guide the expert merchandise buyer, for he is expected to judge quality by examination and not solely by reputation, and at times he may even sacrifice certain definite degrees of quality if that which he obtains is adequate for his purpose and attractive in price. This distinction applies as well to the purchase of securities as to buying paints or watches. It results in two principles of quite opposite character, the one suitable for the untrained investor, the other useful only to the analyst.
1. Principle for the untrained security buyer: *Do not put money in a low-grade enterprise on any terms.*
2. Principle for the securities analyst: *Nearly every issue might conceivably be cheap in one price range and dear in another.*
We have criticized the placing of exclusive emphasis on the choice of the enterprise on the ground that it often leads to paying too high a price for a good security. A second objection is that the enterprise itself may prove to be unwisely chosen. It is natural and proper to prefer a business which is large and well managed, has a good record, and is expected to show increasing earnings in the future. But these expectations, though seemingly well-founded, often fail to be realized. Many of the leading enterprises of yesterday are today far back in the ranks. Tomorrow is likely to tell a similar story. The most impressive illustration is afforded by the persistent decline in the relative investment position of the railroads as a class during the past two decades. The standing of an enterprise is in part a matter of fact and in part a matter of opinion. During recent years investment opinion has proved extraordinarily volatile and undependable. In 1929 Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company was quite universally considered as enjoying an unusually favorable industrial position. Two years later the stock sold for much less than the net current assets alone, presumably indicating widespread doubt as to its ability to earn *any* profit in the future. Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company, viewed as little short of a miraculous enterprise in 1929, declined from494 in that year to 36 in 1938. At the latter date the common sold for less than its cash assets, the preferred being amply covered by other current assets.
These considerations do not gainsay the principle that untrained investors should confine themselves to the best regarded enterprises. It should be realized, however, that this preference is enjoined upon them because of the greater risk for them in other directions, and not because the most popular issues are necessarily the safest. The analyst must pay respectful attention to the judgment of the market place and to the enterprises which it strongly favors, but he must retain an independent and critical viewpoint. Nor should he hesitate to condemn the popular and espouse the unpopular when reasons sufficiently weighty and convincing are at hand.

## 分析中的定性因素与定量因素

<!--en-->
*QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE FACTORS IN ANALYSIS*

分析证券实际上就是分析其背后的企业。这类研究可以做到无限细致的程度，因此必须运用实际判断来决定研究的深度。具体情况自然会影响这一决策。购买1,000美元债券的投资者不会像大型保险公司考虑购买500,000美元的债券那样进行如此彻底的分析；而后者的分析程度仍会低于最初提供贷款的银行家所做的分析。或者从另一个角度来说，选择收益率为3%的高等级债券时所需的分析强度，要低于寻找收益率为6%的优质担保证券或股票市场中所谓的“绝对划算”的投资标的时的分析强度。

<!--en-->
Analyzing a security involves an analysis of the business. Such a study could be carried to an unlimited degree of detail; hence practical judgment must be exercised to determine how far the process should go. The circumstances will naturally have a bearing on this point. A buyer of a $1,000 bond would not deem it worth his while to make as thorough an analysis of an issue as would a large insurance company considering the purchase of a $500,000 block. The latter's study would still be less detailed than that made by the originating bankers. Or, from another angle, a less intensive analysis should be needed in selecting a high-grade bond yielding 3% than in trying to find a well-secured issue yielding 6% or an *unquestioned bargain* in the field of common stocks.

**分析的技术与范围应依据投资目的的性质来限定。**分析师在运用分析技术时必须具备分寸感。在挑选和处理分析资料时，他不仅要考虑资料本身的重要性和可靠性，还要考虑获取的便利性。他不应被大量数据的存在——例如铁路公司向州际商业委员会提交的报告——所误导，从而对无关紧要的内容进行过度研究。另一方面，他也常常不得不接受信息不足的现实，因为只有付出超出其能力或问题所需范围的努力才能获得这些信息。对于完整的“企业分析”中所涉及的某些要素而言，情况往往如此——比如，企业对专利保护、地理优势或有利劳动力条件的依赖程度，而这些条件可能并不会长久存在。

<!--en-->
**Technique and Extent of Analysis Should Be Limited by Character and Purposes of the Commitment.** The equipment of the analyst must include a sense of proportion in the use of his technique. In choosing and dealing with the materials of analysis he must consider not only inherent importance and dependability but also the question of accessibility and convenience. He must not be misled by the availability of a mass of data—e.g., in the reports of therailroads to the Interstate Commerce Commission—into making elaborate studies of nonessentials. On the other hand, he must frequently resign himself to the lack of significant information because it can be secured only by expenditure of more effort than he can spare or the problem will justify. This would be true frequently of some of the elements involved in a complete “business analysis”—as, for example, the extent to which an enterprise is dependent upon patent protection or geographical advantages or favorable labor conditions which may not endure.

**数据价值因企业类型而异。**最重要的是，分析师必须认识到，某种特定类型的数据的价值会随着所研究企业的不同而有很大差异。铁路公司或大型连锁店企业五年的毛利润或净利润记录，即便无法提供决定性结论，至少也能为衡量其优先股的安全性及普通股的吸引力提供较为合理的依据。然而，同一家小型石油公司的同类统计数据却很可能具有更大的误导性，因为这些数据主要取决于两个因素——即售价与产量，而这两个因素在未来很可能会与过去有显著不同。

<!--en-->
**Value of Data Varies with Type of Enterprise.** Most important of all, the analyst must recognize that the value of a particular kind of data varies greatly with the type of enterprise which is being studied. The five-year record of gross or net earnings of a railroad or a large chain-store enterprise may afford, if not a conclusive, at least a reasonably sound basis for measuring the safety of the senior issues and the attractiveness of the common shares. But the same statistics supplied by one of the smaller oil-producing companies may well prove more deceptive than useful, since they are chiefly the resultant of two factors, *viz.*, price received and production, both of which are likely to be radically different in the future than in the past.

**分析中的定量要素与定性要素。**有时将分析中涉及的要素分为两类较为方便：定量要素和定性要素。前者可称为企业的统计表现，其中包含收入表和资产负债表中的所有有用信息，以及有关产量、单价、成本、产能、未完成订单等额外具体数据。这些项目可进一步细分为以下几类：（1）资本化情况；（2）收益与股息；（3）资产与负债；（4）运营统计数据。

<!--en-->
**Quantitative vs. Qualitative Elements in Analysis.** It is convenient at times to classify the elements entering into an analysis under two headings: the quantitative and the qualitative. The former might be called the company’s statistical exhibit. Included in it would be all the useful items in the income account and balance sheet, together with such additional specific data as may be provided with respect to production and unit prices, costs, capacity, unfilled orders, etc. These various items may be subclassified under the headings: (1) capitalization, (2) earnings and dividends, (3) assets and liabilities, and (4) operating statistics.

另一方面，定性要素则涉及业务性质、企业在行业中的相对地位、其物理条件、地理位置及运营特点、管理层的素质，以及最终对该企业、该行业乃至整个商业领域的未来前景的判断。这类问题通常不会出现在企业的报告中，分析师必须从各种可靠性差异极大的信息来源中寻找答案——其中还包括大量纯粹的主观意见。

<!--en-->
The qualitative factors, on the other hand, deal with such matters as the nature of the business; the relative position of the individual company in the industry; its physical, geographical, and operating characteristics; the character of the management; and, finally, the outlook for the unit, for theindustry, and for business in general. Questions of this sort are not dealt with ordinarily in the company's reports. The analyst must look for their answers to miscellaneous sources of information of greatly varying dependability—including a large admixture of mere opinion.

总体而言，定量要素比定性要素更便于进行深入分析。定量要素数量较少，更容易获取，且更有利于得出明确可靠的结论。此外，财务业绩本身就能体现许多定性要素的内容，因此对后者进行详细研究可能并不会对整体情况带来太大影响。典型的证券分析——比如在券商发布的通函或统计机构出具的报告中——通常只是浅尝辄止地提及定性要素，而将大部分篇幅用于数据分析。

<!--en-->
Broadly speaking, the quantitative factors lend themselves far better to thoroughgoing analysis than do the qualitative factors. The former are fewer in number, more easily obtainable, and much better suited to the forming of definite and dependable conclusions. Furthermore the financial results will themselves epitomize many of the qualitative elements, so that a detailed study of the latter may not add much of importance to the picture. The typical analysis of a security—as made, say, in a brokerage-house circular or in a report issued by a statistical service—will treat the qualitative factors in a superficial or summary fashion and devote most of its space to the figures.

**定性要素：业务性质及其未来前景。**最受重视的定性要素是业务性质和管理层素质。这些要素极为重要，但同时也极难进行合理分析。首先来看业务性质，这一概念中也包含了对其未来前景的总体判断。大多数人对“好生意”与“坏生意”的标准都有相当明确的认识，这些看法部分基于财务业绩，部分基于对行业具体状况的了解，还有部分则源于猜测或偏见。

<!--en-->
**Qualitative Factors: Nature of the Business and Its Future Prospects.** The qualitative factors upon which most stress is laid are the nature of the business and the character of the management. These elements are exceedingly important, but they are also exceedingly difficult to deal with intelligently. Let us consider, first, the nature of the business, in which concept is included the general idea of its future prospects. Most people have fairly definite notions as to what is “a good business” and what is not. These views are based partly on the financial results, partly on knowledge of specific conditions in the industry, and partly also on surmise or bias.

在1923年至1929年这段整体繁荣的时期里，仍有不少主要行业处于落后状态，其中包括雪茄、煤炭、棉制品、化肥、皮革、木材、肉类加工、造纸、航运、有轨电车、糖业以及羊毛制品行业。其根本原因通常是竞争产品或服务的出现（如煤炭、棉制品、汽车），或是过度生产以及不良的商业行为（如造纸、木材、糖业）。在同一时期，也有其他行业表现得远好于平均水平，例如罐头制造商、连锁店、香烟生产商、电影业以及公用事业企业。这些行业表现优异的原因可能是需求异常增长（如香烟、电影业），或是缺乏竞争或能够控制竞争（如公用事业、罐头制造商），又或是具备从其他机构手中抢夺业务的能力（如连锁店）。

<!--en-->
During most of the period of general prosperity between 1923 and 1929, quite a number of major industries were backward. These included cigars, coal, cotton goods, fertilizers, leather, lumber, meat packing, paper, shipping, street railways, sugar, woolen goods. The underlying cause was usually either the development of competitive products or services (e.g., coal, cotton goods, tractions) or excessive production and demoralizing trade practices (e.g., paper, lumber, sugar). During the same period other industries were far more prosperous than the average. Among these were can manufacturers, chain stores, cigarette producers, motionpictures, public utilities. The chief cause of these superior showings might be found in unusual growth of demand (cigarettes, motion pictures) or in absence or control of competition (public utilities, can makers) or in the ability to win business from other agencies (chain stores).

人们往往会认为那些表现低于平均水平的行业“处境不利”，因而应该避开。当然，对于那些表现优异的行业，则会持相反的看法。但这种结论往往是大错特错的。极端良好的或极差的状况都不会永远持续下去，这不仅适用于整体经济，也适用于各个特定行业。通常会有各种调节力量发挥作用，要么让已经消失的利润重新出现，要么在利润相对于资本过高时将其降低。

<!--en-->
It is natural to assume that industries which have fared worse than the average are “unfavorably situated” and therefore to be avoided. The converse would be assumed, of course, for those with superior records. But this conclusion may often prove quite erroneous. Abnormally good or abnormally bad conditions do not last forever. This is true not only of general business but of particular industries as well. Corrective forces are often set in motion which tend to restore profits where they have disappeared, or to reduce them where they are excessive in relation to capital.

那些因需求增长而备受青睐的行业，可能会因供应增速更快而陷入困境。无线电、航空、电冰箱、公共汽车运输以及丝袜行业便是如此。1922年，由于在1920–1921年的经济萧条中表现优异，百货公司备受推崇；但随后几年它们并未保持这一优势。在1919年的经济繁荣期，由于成本过高，公用事业公司并不受欢迎；而在1927–1929年间，它们又因具有投机性而成为投资热点；1933–1938年间，人们对通货膨胀、费率管制以及政府直接竞争的担忧再次削弱了公众对它们的信心。另一方面，长期处于萧条状态的棉制品行业在1933年的发展速度却超过了大多数其他行业。

<!--en-->
Industries especially favored by a developing demand may become demoralized through a still more rapid growth of supply. This has been true of radio, aviation, electric refrigeration, bus transportation, and silk hosiery. In 1922 department stores were very favorably regarded because of their excellent showing in the 1920–1921 depression; but they did not maintain this advantage in subsequent years. The public utilities were unpopular in the 1919 boom, because of high costs; they became speculative and investment favorites in 1927–1929; in 1933–1938 fear of inflation, rate regulation, and direct governmental competition again undermined the public’s confidence in them. In 1933, on the other hand, the cotton-goods industry—long depressed—forged ahead faster than most others.

**管理因素。**虽然我们认识到选择“优质行业”的重要性，但也必须明白这绝非听起来那么简单。在试图挑选出能力出众的管理层时，也会遇到类似的困难。用于评估管理能力的客观标准寥寥无几，且远非科学可靠。在大多数情况下，投资者只能依赖某种声誉，而这种声誉或许当之无愧，也可能名不副实。最能证明管理层能力出色的证据，是其在一段时间内取得的优于同行的业绩记录。但这又把我们带回了定量数据的问题上。

<!--en-->
**The Factor of Management.** Our appreciation of the importance of selecting a “good industry” must be tempered by a realization that this is by no means so easy as it sounds. Somewhat the same difficulty is met with in endeavoring to select an unusually capable management. Objective tests of managerial ability are few and far from scientific. In most cases the investor must rely upon a reputation which may or may not be deserved. The most convincing proof of capable management lies in a superior comparative record over a period of time. But this brings us back to the quantitative data.

股市中存在一种强烈的倾向，即在估值时重复计算管理因素的影响。股价不仅反映了优秀管理所带来的高收益，还额外包含了单独为“优秀管理”计量的可观加成。这相当于“重复计算同一项因素”，也是导致股票被高估的常见原因。

<!--en-->
There is a strong tendency in the stock market to value the management factor twice in its calculations. Stock prices reflect the large earnings which the good management has produced, *plus* a substantial increment for “good management” considered separately. This amounts to “counting the same trick twice,” and it proves a frequent cause of overvaluation.

**未来收益趋势。**近年来，“收益趋势”的重要性日益凸显。显然，利润持续增长的记录是个好迹象。然而，金融理论更进一步，试图通过将过去的趋势延伸到未来，再以此作为企业估值的依据来估算未来收益。由于这一过程使用了数字，人们便误以为其“在数学上是严谨的”。但尽管过去的趋势是事实，“未来趋势”终究只是一种假设。我们之前提到的那些会阻碍异常繁荣或萧条持续的因素，同样也会阻碍上升或下降趋势的无限制延续。等到趋势变得明显时，情况很可能已经到了发生变化的临界点。

<!--en-->
**The Trend of Future Earnings.** In recent years increasing importance has been laid upon the *trend of earnings*. Needless to say, a record of increasing profits is a favorable sign. Financial theory has gone further, however, and has sought to estimate future earnings by projecting the past trend into the future and then used this projection as a basis for valuing the business. Because figures are used in this process, people mistakenly believe that it is “mathematically sound.” But while a trend shown in the past is a fact, a “future trend” is only an assumption. The factors that we mentioned previously as militating against the maintenance of abnormal prosperity or depression are equally opposed to the indefinite continuance of an upward or downward trend. By the time the trend has become clearly noticeable, conditions may well be ripe for a change.

有人可能会反对说，就未来而言，预期过去趋势会持续下去与预期过去平均水平会再次出现一样合乎逻辑。这或许没错，但这并不意味着趋势比过去的个别数据或平均数据更有利于分析。因为证券分析并非假设过去平均水平会重复出现，而只是认为它能提供一个关于未来情况的“大致指标”。然而，趋势并不能作为大致指标；它代表的是对未来结果好坏的明确预测，而且这种预测非对即错。

<!--en-->
It may be objected that as far as the future is concerned it is just as logical to expect a past trend to be maintained as to expect a past average to be repeated. This is probably true, but it does not follow that the trend is more useful to analysis than the individual or average figures of the past. For security analysis does not assume that a past average will be repeated, but only that it supplies a *rough index* to what may be expected of the future. A trend, however, cannot be used as a rough index; it represents a definite prediction of either better or poorer results, and it must be either right or wrong.

这一区别对于分析师的态度具有重要影响，通过举例可以使其更加清晰。假设1929年某家铁路公司的利息支出仅为前七年平均水平的三分之一。分析师会将这一点视为该公司债券质量良好的重要信号，并给予高度重视。这是基于定量数据和标准做出的判断。但它并不意味着未来七年的收益平均将为利息支出的三分之一；它只是表明，收益不太可能降至低于利息支出三分之一的程度，从而危及债券的安全。在几乎所有实际案例中，尽管随后发生了经济崩溃，这样的结论都被证明是正确的。

<!--en-->
This distinction, important in its bearing on the attitude of the analyst, may be made clearer by the use of examples. Let us assume that in 1929 a railroad showed its interest charges earned three times on the average during the preceding seven years. The analyst would have ascribed great weight to this point as an indication that its bonds were sound. This is a judgment based on quantitative data and standards. But it doesnot imply a prediction that the earnings in the next seven years will average three times interest charges; it suggests only that earnings are not likely to fall so much under three times interest charges as to endanger the bonds. In nearly every actual case such a conclusion would have proved correct, despite the economic collapse that ensued.

现在让我们考虑一种主要基于趋势的类似判断。1929年，几乎所有公用事业公司的收益都在持续增长，但由于金字塔式的资本结构，许多公司的固定成本极高，几乎耗尽了所有净收入。投资者们认为，既然收益肯定会继续增长，那么微小的安全边际并无大碍，于是纷纷购买这些公司的债券。他们实际上是在对未来做出明确的预测，而他们的投资是否合理取决于这一预测的正确性。如果他们的预测错误——事实也确实如此——他们必将遭受严重损失。

<!--en-->
Now let us consider a similar judgment based primarily upon the trend. In 1929 nearly all public-utility systems showed a continued growth of earnings, but the fixed charges of many were so heavy—by reason of pyramidal capital structures—that they consumed nearly all the net income. Investors bought bonds of these systems freely on the theory that the small margin of safety was no drawback, since earnings were certain to continue to increase. They were thus making a clear-cut prediction as to the future, upon the correctness of which depended the justification of their investment. If their prediction were wrong—as proved to be the case—they were bound to suffer serious loss.

**趋势本质上属于定性因素。**在本书后面关于普通股估值的讨论中，我们将指出：过度强调趋势很可能会导致高估或低估的错误。这是因为无法确定趋势应被预测多远；因此，尽管估值过程看似具有数学性，但实际上是心理层面的，且相当随意。正因如此，即便趋势可以用定量术语来表述，我们在实际应用中仍将其视为*定性*因素。

<!--en-->
**Trend Essentially a Qualitative Factor.** In our discussion of the valuation of common stocks, later in this book, we shall point out that the placing of preponderant emphasis on the trend is likely to result in errors of overvaluation or undervaluation. This is true because no limit may be fixed on how far ahead the trend should be projected; and therefore the process of valuation, while seemingly mathematical, is in reality psychological and quite arbitrary. For this reason we consider the trend as a *qualitative* factor in its practical implications, even though it may be stated in quantitative terms.

**定性因素难以实现合理准确的评估。**实际上，趋势是对未来前景的一种精确预测表达。同样地，关于企业性质及管理层能力的判断，其重要性也主要体现在对未来前景的影响上。这些定性因素都具有相同的总体特征，即分析师都面临着同样的基本难题：无法判断它们能在多大程度上恰当地反映在某只证券的价格中。在大多数情况下，如果这些因素被察觉到，往往会被过度强调。我们在整个市场中也始终能看到这种影响——市场的反复大幅上涨与下跌，归根结底是因为当价值主要由前景决定时，由此产生的判断便不受任何数学约束，几乎不可避免地会走向极端。

<!--en-->
**Qualitative Factors Resist Even Reasonably Accurate Appraisal.** The trend is, in fact, a statement of future prospects in the form of an exact prediction. In similar fashion, conclusions as to the nature of the business and the abilities of the management have their chief significance in their bearing on the outlook. These qualitative factors are therefore all of the same general character. They all involve the same basic difficulty for the analyst, *viz.*, that it is impossible to judge how far they may properly reflect themselves in the price of a given security. In most cases, ifthey are recognized at all, they tend to be overemphasized. We see the same influence constantly at work in the general market. The recurrent excesses of its advances and declines are due at bottom to the fact that, when values are determined chiefly by the outlook, the resultant judgments are not subject to any mathematical controls and are almost inevitably carried to extremes.

分析主要关注那些有事实依据的价值，而非那些主要依赖预期的价值。在这方面，分析师的方法与投机者的方法截然相反，后者是指那些依靠预测或猜测未来发展来取得成功的投资者。当然，分析师必须考虑未来可能发生的变化，但他的首要目标并非从中*获利*，而是*防范*风险。总体而言，他将企业的未来视为一场必须面对的风险，而非证明自己正确的来源。

<!--en-->
Analysis is concerned primarily with values which are supported by the facts and not with those which depend largely upon expectations. In this respect the analyst's approach is diametrically opposed to that of the speculator, meaning thereby one whose success turns upon his ability to forecast or to guess future developments. Needless to say, the analyst must take possible future changes into account, but his primary aim is not so much to *profit* from them as to *guard against* them. Broadly speaking, he views the business future as a hazard which his conclusions must encounter rather than as the source of his vindication.

**内在稳定性是重要的定性因素。**因此，分析师最应关注的定性因素就是*内在稳定性*。因为稳定性意味着抗变化能力，从而使得过去的表现更具可靠性。与趋势一样，稳定性也可以用定量术语来表示——例如，可以说通用烘焙公司在1923年至1932年间的盈利从未低于1932年利息支出的10倍，或者伍尔沃斯公司在1924年至1933年间每股的营业利润仅在2.12美元至3.66美元之间波动。但在我们看来，稳定性实际上是一种定性特征，因为它首先源于企业的性质，而非其统计记录。稳定的记录表明企业本身具有稳定性，但这一结论也可能被其他因素推翻。

<!--en-->
**Inherent Stability a Major Qualitative Factor.** It follows that the qualitative factor in which the analyst should properly be most interested is that of *inherent stability*. For stability means resistance to change and hence greater dependability for the results shown in the past. Stability, like the trend, may be expressed in quantitative terms—as, for example, by stating that the earnings of General Baking Company during 1923–1932 were never less than ten times 1932 interest charges or that the operating profits of Woolworth between 1924 and 1933 varied only between $2.12 and $3.66 per share of common. But in our opinion stability is really a qualitative trait, because it derives in the first instance from the character of the business and not from its statistical record. A stable record suggests that the business is inherently stable, but this suggestion may be rebutted by other considerations.

*示例：*可以通过比较1932年初发行的两种优先股来说明这一点，即斯图贝克（汽车制造）和第一国民（杂货零售）商店发行的优先股，这两种股票的发行价均高于面值。这两者的表现相似，都显示出持续高于优先股股息要求的理想盈利空间。不过，如下表所示，斯图贝克的数据更为出色：

<!--en-->

The two exhibits were similar, in that both disclosed a continuously satisfactory margin above preferred-dividend requirements. TheStudebaker figures were more impressive, however, as the following table will indicate:

但分析师必须超越单纯的数字，深入考量这两家企业的固有特性。连锁杂货业本身具有诸多相对稳定的因素，如稳定的需求、多元化的门店布局以及快速的库存周转率。只要不采取鲁莽的扩张策略，这类行业中的大型企业其盈利就不太可能出现剧烈波动。而典型汽车制造商的情况则大不相同。尽管整个行业整体上还算稳定，但由于消费者偏好变化无常，各企业之间的业绩差异却极为显著。无法用任何合理的逻辑证明斯图贝克公司的盈利稳定性意味着它能永远免受大多数竞争对手所面临的种种变动影响。因此，斯图贝克优先股的价值在很大程度上依赖于与其所属行业整体特性相悖的稳定统计数据。另一方面，第一国民商店优先股的良好表现则完全符合人们对该行业固有特性的普遍认知。对于分析师而言，后者本应更具说服力，即便该汽车公司的*统计*数据更为亮眼，也应使其看起来比斯图贝克优先股更适合作为固定价值投资。⁶ **总结。** 总结关于定性因素与定量因素的讨论，我们可以得出这样的结论：分析师的判断必须始终以数据以及既定的测试标准为基础。仅靠这些数据是*不够的*；相反的定性因素可能会彻底扭曲这些数据。某只证券的统计表现可能不错，但如果对其未来前景存疑或对管理层缺乏信任，也有理由拒绝投资它。同样，分析师往往会特别重视*稳定性*这一定性因素，因为它的存在意味着基于过往业绩得出的结论不太可能被意外情况打破。此外，如果能在良好的定量数据基础上再辅以极为有利的定性因素，分析师在选择投资标的时也会更有信心。

<!--en-->
But the analyst must penetrate beyond the mere figures and consider the inherent character of the two businesses. The chain-store grocery trade contained within itself many elements of relative stability, such as stable demand, diversified locations, and rapid inventory turnover. A typical large unit in this field, provided only it abstained from reckless expansion policies, was not likely to suffer tremendous fluctuations in its earnings. But the situation of the typical automobile manufacturer was quite different. Despite fair stability in the industry as a whole, the individual units were subject to extraordinary variations, due chiefly to the vagaries of popular preference. The stability of Studebaker's earnings could not be held by any convincing logic to demonstrate that this company enjoyed a special and permanent immunity from the vicissitudes to which most of its competitors had shown themselves subject. The soundness of Studebaker Preferred rested, therefore, largely upon a stable statistical showing which was at variance with the general character of the industry, so far as its individual units were concerned. On the other hand, the satisfactory exhibit of First National Stores Preferred was in thorough accord with what was generally thought to be the inherent character of thebusiness. The later consideration should have carried great weight with the analyst and should have made First National Stores Preferred appear intrinsically sounder as a fixed-value investment than Studebaker Preferred, despite the more impressive *statistical* showing of the automobile company.⁶
**Summary.** To sum up this discussion of qualitative and quantitative factors, we may express the dictum that the analyst's conclusions must always rest upon the figures and upon established tests and standards. These figures alone are not *sufficient*; they may be completely vitiated by qualitative considerations of an opposite import. A security may make a satisfactory statistical showing, but doubt as to the future or distrust of the management may properly impel its rejection. Again, the analyst is likely to attach prime importance to the qualitative element of *stability*, because its presence means that conclusions based on past results are not so likely to be upset by unexpected developments. It is also true that he will be far more confident in his selection of an issue if he can buttress an adequate quantitative exhibit with unusually favorable qualitative factors.

但每当投资决策在很大程度上取决于这些定性因素——也就是说，当股价远高于仅凭数据所能支撑的水平时——那么该投资的分析依据就不足了。用数学术语来说，良好的统计表现是分析师做出有利决策的*必要条件*，但绝非*充分条件*。[^518]：¹ 1927年，这些面值为3\frac{1}{2}美元的债券收益率为3.39%，而大致在同一时期发行的美国自由号面值为4\frac{1}{4}美元的债券收益率为4.08%。² 1939年到期的美国电话电报公司可转换面值为4\frac{1}{2}美元的债券，其年度价格区间如下：

<!--en-->
But whenever the commitment depends to a substantial degree upon these qualitative factors—whenever, that is, the price is considerably higher than the figures alone would justify—then the analytical basis of approval is lacking. In the mathematical phrase, a satisfactory statistical exhibit is a *necessary* though by no means a *sufficient condition* for a favorable decision by the analyst.
