# 第3章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 3*

# 信息来源

<!--en-->
*Sources of Information*

要逐一列举分析师在工作中可能随时需要参考的所有信息来源是不可能的，甚至也无法进行全面讨论。本章我们将简要概述其中较为重要的信息来源，并对其做一些评析；同时还会通过实例来说明各类特殊信息渠道的特点与作用。

<!--en-->
IT IS IMPOSSIBLE to discuss or even to list all the sources of information which the analyst may find it profitable to consult at one time or another in his work. In this chapter we shall present a concise outline of the more important sources, together with some critical observations thereon; and we shall also endeavor to convey, by means of examples, an idea of the character and utility of the large variety of special avenues of information.

## 发行条款的相关数据

<!--en-->
*DATA ON THE TERMS OF THE ISSUE*

假设在典型情况下，分析师需要获取以下方面的数据：（1）特定发行的条款，（2）该公司的情况，（3）所在行业的情况。发行条款本身会在证券手册或统计服务中有所总结。若需了解更详细的债券合同信息，分析师应查阅债券契约（或信托契据），其副本可在受托人办公室获取或查阅。一家公司各次股票发行的条款则完整地记载在公司章程（或注册章程）及附属规章中。如果该股票已上市，这些文件会存放在美国证券交易委员会以及相应的证券交易所。对于债券和股票而言，那些容易获取的上市申请文件中几乎包含了所有重要条款，新发行的招股说明书中也会有这些条款。

<!--en-->
Let us assume that in the typical case the analyst seeks data regarding: (1) the terms of the specific issue, (2) the company, and (3) the industry. The provisions of the issue itself are summarized in the security manuals or statistical services. For more detailed information regarding a bond contract the analyst should consult the indenture (or deed of trust), a copy of which may be obtained or inspected at the office of the trustee. The terms of the respective stock issues of a company are set forth fully in the charter (or articles of incorporation), together with the by-laws. If the stock is listed, these documents are on file with the S.E.C. and also with the proper stock exchange. In the case of both bonds and stocks, the listing applications—which are readily obtainable—contain nearly all the significant provisions. Prospectuses of new issues also contain these provisions.

### 公司的相关数据

<!--en-->
*DATA ON THE COMPANY*

## 致股东报告（包括中期新闻稿）

<!--en-->
*Reports to Stockholders (Including Interim News Releases).*

接下来谈到*公司*，统计数据的主要来源当然是发给股东的报告。如下文总结所示，这些报告在发布频率和内容完整性方面差异很大：

<!--en-->
Coming now to the *company*, the chief source of statistical data is, of course, the reports issued to the stockholders. These reports vary widely with respect to both frequency and completeness, as the following summary will show:

所有重要的铁路公司都会*每月*提供扣除租金后的净收入（即铁路运营净收入）数据。大多数公司还会提供可用于派发股息的余额（即净收入）数据。许多公司会*每周*公布载货量数据，还有少数公司会每周公布总收入。年度小册子形式的报告中会详细列出财务和运营数据。¹ 公用事业公司的报告周期在*季度*和*月度*之间不等，常规数据通常包括总收入、税后净收入以及用于派发股息的余额。有些公司只公布12个月的累计数据——例如，美国水务电力公司（按月）、北美公司（按季度）。许多公司会*每周*或*每月*公布售出的千瓦时数。

<!--en-->
All important railroads supply *monthly* figures down to net after rentals (net railway operating income). Most carry the results down to the balance for dividends (net income). Many publish carloading figures *weekly*, and a few have published gross earnings weekly. The pamphlet annual reports publish financial and operating figures in considerable detail.¹
The ruling policy of public-utility companies varies between *quarterly* and *monthly* statements. Figures regularly include gross, net after taxes, and balance for dividends. Some companies publish only a moving twelve-month total—*e.g.*, American Water Works and Electric Company (monthly), North American Company (quarterly). Many supply *weekly* or *monthly* figures of kilowatt-hours sold.

*工业类企业*。工业企业的做法通常由各自公司自行决定，但在某些行业集团中，集团内的多数公司往往倾向于采用相同的做法。

<!--en-->
*Industrials*. The practices followed by industrial companies are usually a matter of individual policy. In some industrial groups there is a tendency for most of the companies therein to follow the same course.

1. *月度报表*。大多数连锁店会以美元金额公布其月度销售额。1931年之前，铜矿生产商会定期公布月度产量。通用汽车则按辆数公布月度销售数据。1902年至1933年间，美国钢铁公司每月都会公布未完成订单数量，但在1933年改为公布月度吨位交付量。鲍德温机车厂会以美元金额公布月度发货量、新订单量和未完成订单量。管道运输领域的“标准石油集团”会按月公布运营量数据（以桶计）。个别公司偶尔也会公布月度净收益数据，但这种做法往往较为零星或只是暂时性的（例如，奥的斯钢铁公司、穆林斯制造公司、阿拉斯加朱诺市的公司）。² 企业往往在经营状况好转时开始发布月度报表，而在收益下降时则停止发布。有时季度报表中也会包含按月划分的数据——例如，1932年之前的美国钢铁公司。
2. *季度报表*。在几乎所有行业领域，按季度公布业绩都被视为标准做法。纽约证券交易所不断加大力度要求企业提交季度报告，并且通常能在新证券或新增证券上市时迫使企业遵守这一要求。由于某些行业的业绩具有季节性特征，这类企业被认为或自认为可免于此项规定。这些行业包括糖业、化肥业以及农具制造业。企业可以通过公布12个月的滚动盈利数据来掩盖季节性波动，大陆罐头公司就是如此做的。³ 很难理解为何所有大型香烟制造商以及大多数百货公司都要将全年业绩推迟一年才公布。像伍尔沃斯这样的公司每月公布销售额，却不公布中期净利润报表，这也显得不合常理。实际上属于各个行业领域的许多企业至今仍未开始发布季度报告。在几乎所有情况下，管理层都能获取这些中期数据，但却无正当理由地拒绝向股东公开。季度报表中的数据从仅列一个净利润数字（有时未扣除折旧或联邦税）到详细呈现损益表和资产负债表并附上总裁的评论不等。通用汽车公司便是后一种做法的典型代表。
3. *半年度报告*。除橡胶企业外，似乎没有哪个行业群体将这份报告作为标准做法。有一些企业会每半年发布一次报告，例如美国机车公司和美国羊毛公司。
4. *年度报告*。每家上市公司都会发布某种形式的年度报告。年度报告通常比中期报告更为详细，其中常常包含总裁或董事会主席关于过去一年业绩及未来前景的评论——但这些评论并不总是有启发性。不过，年度报告的独特之处在于它一定会展示公司的资产负债表状况。而损益表中的信息详略程度差异很大。有些报告仅列出可用于分配股息的利润及已支付的股息金额，例如美国皮革公司。⁴ *损益表*。在我们看来，除非包含以下项目，否则年度损益表就不算足够完整：(1) 销售额；(2) 净利润（不包括后续项目）；(3) 折旧（及耗竭费用）；(4) 利息支出；(5) 非经营收入（需详细列出）；(6) 所得税；(7) 已支付的股息；(8) 盈余调整（需详细列出）。在《证券交易法》通过之前，不幸的是，不到一半的工业企业能提供这么基本的信息量。（相比之下，铁路和公用事业领域的相关数据长期以来一直都很齐全。）如今，美国证券交易委员会的规定要求几乎所有这些信息都必须在最初的注册申请表（10表格）及后续的年度报告（10-K表格）中公布。有不少公司以公开销售数据会损害企业利益为由，请求SEC对其销售数据保密。这些请求大多已被撤回或被驳回。⁵ 上文所述的年度报告“合理完整性”标准绝非指所有可能向股东提供的信息。美国钢铁公司的报告堪称全面性的典范，除了满足我们的基本要求外，其报告还包含了以下内容：
1. 按单位计算的产量和销售额，以及产能利用率。
2. 销售额的构成：国内与国外、内部交易与外部交易。
3. 运营费用的明细：工资、工资率及员工人数；已缴纳的州税和地方税；销售及一般管理费用；维护支出及其金额和细节。
4. 当年资本支出的明细。
5. 库存的明细。
6. 所拥有资产的明细。
7. 股东数量。*资产负债表*。资产负债表的格式比利润表更为规范，因此也较少受到批评。过去，资产负债表的一个普遍缺陷是未能将无形资产与有形固定资产区分开来，但在上市公司中这种情况现已极为罕见。（自1935年以来，公开披露其资产账户中所含商誉金额的公司包括美国钢铁铸造厂、美国罐头公司、哈比森·沃克耐火材料公司、洛斯-威尔斯饼干公司以及美国钢铁公司。在几乎所有这些案例中，商誉都被从盈余中冲销。）许多公司仅公布资产账户的*净值*而不显示折旧扣除额的做法确实值得批评。其他常见的缺陷还包括：不说明所持有证券的市场价值——例如1932年的奥本海姆·柯林斯公司；不标明“投资”属于可交易资产还是非流动性资产——例如匹兹堡平板玻璃公司；按成本与市场价值中的较低者来评估存货价值——例如1931年的美国西莱尼塞公司；不说明各种储备的性质——例如黑泽尔-阿特拉斯玻璃公司；以及不说明公司库房中持有的自身证券的数量——例如美国阿奇公司。⁶ **向公共机构提交的定期报告**。铁路公司以及大多数公用事业企业都必须向各类联邦及州级委员会提供信息。由于这些数据通常比面向股东的报表更为详细，因此可以作为有用的补充资料来源。以下是一些关于这些报告对相关委员会具有价值的实际例子。在1927年之前的许多年里，纽约联合煤气公司（现为纽约联合爱迪生公司）因为几乎不向股东透露任何信息，而成为华尔街的“神秘股票”。投机者们极度关注其在众多子公司中所持有的权益的未公开价值。然而，纽约公共服务委员会发布的年度报告始终包含该公司及其子公司的完整运营与财务数据。麦凯公司长期也存在类似情况：该公司控制着邮政电报电缆公司，虽不向股东披露任何细节，却向州际商业委员会提供了大量信息。第五大道巴士证券公司向股东提交的报告内容贫乏，而其运营子公司则向纽约交通委员会提交了详尽的信息，两者之间也存在类似的反差。最后，我们还可以提到那些极其不愿向股东透露信息的管道运输公司“标准石油集团”。但这些公司受州际商业委员会管辖，必须向华盛顿提交详尽的年度报告。几年前对这些报告的审查便能揭示出这些公司在现金及可交易证券持有方面的惊人状况。美国商务部每月出版的《当前商业调查》中包含了大量数据，其中包括一些连锁零售公司的销售数字，而这些数字并未对外公开——例如沃尔多夫连锁店、J.R.汤普森公司、联合雪茄店、哈特曼公司等。有关特定公司的最新统计信息往往可以在行业出版物或服务中找到。*示例*：《克拉姆汽车服务》每周都会公布各家汽车公司的产量数据；威尔莱特与格雷公司则会发布各公司在一个种植年度内的糖产量估算值；《石油与天然气杂志》则经常刊登有关各大油田公司生产情况的数据。 《铁路时代》会提供有关已下达的设备采购订单的详细信息。道琼斯公司每周都会估算美国钢铁公司的生产率。**上市申请文件**。在证券交易委员会成立之前，这些是最重要的非定期信息来源。纽约证券交易所为将证券纳入其上市名单而要求的报告，其详细程度远高于通常向股东提交的报告。这些额外数据可能包括以美元计的销售额、以单位计的生产量、联邦税额、子公司运营详情，以及折旧和损耗费用的依据与金额。此外，这些报告还会提供有关公司拥有的资产、合同条款以及所采用的会计方法的宝贵信息。分析师会发现这些上市申请文件极具参考价值。遗憾的是，它们的发布时间不固定，因此无法作为稳定的信息来源。**注册声明与招股说明书**。由于证券交易委员会的立法与法规，如今所有已上市证券以及所有*新*发行的证券（无论是否已上市）的相关信息都比以往更为全面。这些数据都包含在提交给华盛顿证券交易委员会的注册声明中，公众可以前往查阅或在支付费用后获取副本。注册声明中更重要的信息还必须被纳入承销商提供给新股潜在购买者的招股说明书之中。根据1935年的《公共事业法》，控股公司也必须提交类似的注册声明，而这些公司可能并不受其他相关法规的约束。虽然这些注册声明的篇幅确实过大，普通投资者难以通读，而且他们是否愿意仔细研读篇幅仍可能超过100页的简略版招股说明书也值得怀疑，但毫无疑问，这些资料对分析师而言具有极高的价值，进而也能为广大投资者服务。**各类官方报告**。各种官方文件中也可能找到关于个别公司的信息。以下几个例子就能体现这类报告的多样性。1923年美国煤炭委员会发布的报告（最终于1925年作为参议院文件出版）提供了此前未曾公开的无烟煤企业的财务与运营数据。联邦贸易委员会最近通过历时约九年的深入调查，提供了大量此前不存在的关于公用事业运营与控股公司、天然气及管道公司的信息。1938年和1939年，该委员会发布了关于农用机械及汽车制造商的详细报告。1933年，在众议院州际与对外贸易委员会的指导下，一份关于管道公司的全面研究报告得以发布。根据1935年国会通过的决议，联邦通信委员会开展的调查也产生了大量关于美国电话电报系统的研究报告。⁷州际商业委员会的一些意见中也包含了极具价值的分析内容。承担抵押贷款的受托人可能掌握着契约条款要求提供的信息，这些数据可能具有重要意义。 例如，梅森城与福特多奇铁路公司受托人未公开的报告显示，这些债券的利息并未真正产生，芝加哥大西部铁路公司只是出于政策考虑才继续支付相关款项，因此这些债券的处境比人们普遍认为的要脆弱得多。**统计与金融出版物**。证券分析师在日常工作中所需的大部分信息，都可以通过各种统计服务便捷地获取且呈现得相当完整。这些服务包括每年出版并定期补充内容的综合手册（如普尔、穆迪）；描述性股票和债券卡片以及经常修订的手册（如标准普尔、惠誉）；以及针对个别公司的每日新闻摘要（如标准公司记录、惠誉）。⁸ 在过去的20年里，这些服务在事实呈现的完整性及准确性方面取得了巨大进步。然而，它们仍无法提供上述各类原始资料中的所有数据——有些资料根本不在其覆盖范围内，而在其他情况下则可能遗漏一些重要内容。因此，在对某家特定公司进行深入研究时，分析师应尽可能查阅原始报告及其他文件，而非依赖汇总版或转录本。在金融期刊领域，特别值得一提的是《商业与金融纪事报》，这是一份每周发行的刊物，附有大量统计补充内容。它对金融和工业领域的报道极为全面，最值得称道的特点或许是其对企业报告及其他文件的详细转载。

<!--en-->
1. *Monthly Statements*. Most chain stores announce their monthly sales in dollars. Prior to 1931, copper producers regularly published their monthly output. General Motors publishes monthly sales in units.
Between 1902 and 1933, United States Steel Corporation published its unfilled orders each month, but in 1933 it replaced this figure by monthly deliveries in tons. Baldwin Locomotive Works has published monthly figures of shipments, new orders, and unfilled orders in dollars. The “Standard Oil Group” of pipeline companies publish monthly statistics of operations in barrels.
Monthly figures of net earnings are published by individual companies from time to time, but such practices have tended to be sporadic or temporary (*e.g.*, Otis Steel,Mullins Manufacturing, Alaska Juneau).² There is a tendency to inaugurate monthly statements during periods of improvement and to discontinue them with earnings decline. Sometimes figures by months are included in the quarterly statements—e.g., United States Steel Corporation prior to 1932.
2. *Quarterly Statements.* Publication of results quarterly is considered as the standard procedure in nearly all lines of industry. The New York Stock Exchange has been urging quarterly reports with increasing vigor and has usually been able to make its demands effective in connection with the listing of new or additional securities. Certain types of businesses are considered—or consider themselves—exempt from this requirement, because of the seasonal nature of their results. These lines include sugar production, fertilizers, and agricultural implements. Seasonal fluctuations may be concealed by publishing quarterly a moving twelve-months' figure of earnings. This is done by Continental Can Company.³
It is not easy to understand why all the large cigarette manufacturers and the majority of department stores should withhold their results for a full year. It is inconsistent also for a company such as Woolworth to publish sales monthly but no interim statements of net profits. Many individual companies, belonging to practically every division of industry, still fail to publish quarterly reports. In nearly every case such interim figures are available to the management but are denied to the stockholders without adequate reason.
The data given in the quarterly statements vary from a single figure of net earnings (sometimes without allowance for depreciation or federal taxes) to a fully detailed presentation of the income account and the balance sheet, with president's remarks appended. General Motors Corporation is an outstanding example of the latter practice.
3. *Semiannual Reports.* These do not appear to be standard practice for any industrial group, except possibly the rubber companies. A number of individual enterprises reportsemiannually—e.g., American Locomotive and American Woolen.
4. *Annual Reports.* Every listed company publishes an annual report of some kind. The annual statement is generally more detailed than those covering interim periods. It frequently contains remarks—not always illuminating—by the president or the chairman of the board, relating to the past year's results and to the future outlook. The distinguishing feature of the annual report, however, is that it invariably presents the balance-sheet position.
The information given in the income account varies considerably in extent. Some reports give no more than the earnings available for dividends and the amount of dividends paid, e.g., United States Leather Company.⁴
*The Income Account.* In our opinion an annual income account is not reasonably complete unless it contains the following items: (1) sales, (2) net earnings (before the items following), (3) depreciation (and depletion), (4) interest charges, (5) nonoperating income (in detail), (6) income taxes, (7) dividends paid, (8) surplus adjustments (in detail).
Prior to the passage of the Securities and Exchange Act it was unfortunately true that less than half of our industrial corporations supplied this very moderate quota of information. (By contrast, data relative to railroads and public utilities have long been uniformly adequate.) The S.E.C. regulations now require virtually all this information to be published in the original registration statement (Form 10) and the succeeding annual reports (Form 10-K). Quite a number of companies have requested the S.E.C. to keep their sales figures confidential, on the ground that publication would be detrimental to the enterprise. Most of these requests have been either withdrawn or denied.⁵
The standard of *reasonable completeness* for annual reports, suggested above, by no means includes all the information which might be vouchsafed to shareholders. The reports of United States Steel Corporation may be taken as a model of comprehensiveness. The data there suppliedembrace, in addition to our standard requirements, the following items:
1. Production and sales in units. Rate of capacity operated.
2. Division of sales as between:
Domestic and foreign.
Intercompany and outsiders.
3. Details of operating expenses:
Wages, wage rates, and number of employees.
State and local taxes paid.
Selling and general expense.
Maintenance expenditures, amount and details.
4. Details of capital expenditures during the year.
5. Details of inventories.
6. Details of properties owned.
7. Number of stockholders.
*The Balance Sheet.* The form of the balance sheet is better standardized than the income account, and it does not offer such frequent grounds for criticism. Formerly a widespread defect of balance sheets was the failure to separate intangible from tangible fixed assets, but this is now quite rare in the case of listed issues. (Among the companies that since 1935 have disclosed the amount of good-will formerly included in their property accounts are American Steel Foundries, American Can, Harbison Walker Refractories, Loose-Wiles Biscuit, and United States Steel. In nearly all these cases the good-will was written off against surplus.)
Criticism may properly be voiced against the practice of a great many companies in stating only the *net* figure for their property account without showing the deduction for depreciation. Other shortcomings sometimes met are the failure to state the market value of securities owned—*e.g.*, Oppenheim Collins and Company in 1932; to identify “investments” as marketable or nonliquid—*e.g.*, PittsburghPlate Glass Company; to value the inventory at lower of cost or market—e.g., Celanese Corporation of America in 1931; to state the nature of miscellaneous reserves—e.g., Hazel-Atlas Glass Company; and to state the amount of the company's own securities held in the treasury—e.g., American Arch Company.⁶
**Periodic Reports to Public Agencies.** Railroads and most public utilities are required to supply information to various federal and state commissions. Since these data are generally more detailed than the statements to shareholders, they afford a useful supplementary source of material. A few practical illustrations of the value of these reports to commissions may be of interest.
For many years prior to 1927 Consolidated Gas Company of New York (now Consolidated Edison Company of New York) was a “mystery stock” in Wall Street because it supplied very little information to its stockholders. Great emphasis was laid by speculators upon the undisclosed value of its interest in its numerous subsidiary companies. However, complete operating and financial data relating to both the company and its subsidiaries were at all times available in the annual reports of the Public Service Commission of New York. The same situation pertained over a long period with respect to the Mackay Companies, controlling Postal Telegraph and Cable Corporation, which reported no details to its stockholders but considerable information to the Interstate Commerce Commission. A similar contrast exists between the unilluminating reports of Fifth Avenue Bus Securities Company to its shareholders and the complete information filed by its operating subsidiary with the New York Transit Commission.
Finally, we may mention the “Standard Oil Group” of pipeline companies, which have been extremely chary of information to their stockholders. But these companies come under the jurisdiction of the Interstate Commerce Commission and are required to file circumstantial annual reports at Washington. Examination of these reports several years ago would have disclosed striking facts about these companies' holdings of cash and marketable securities.
The voluminous data contained in the *Survey of Current Business*, published monthly by the United States Department of Commerce, have included sales figures for individual chain-store companies which were not given general publicity —e.g., Waldorf System, J. R. Thompson, United Cigar Stores, Hartman Corporation, etc. Current statistical information regarding particular companies is often available in trade publications or services.
*Examples: Cram's Auto Service* gives weekly figures of production for each motor-car company. Willett and Gray publish several estimates of sugar production by companies during the crop year. The *Oil and Gas Journal* often carries data regarding the production of important fields by companies. The *Railway Age* supplies detailed information regarding equipment orders placed. Dow, Jones and Company estimate weekly the rate of production of United States Steel.
**Listing Applications.** In pre-S.E.C. days these were the most important nonperiodic sources of information. The reports required by the New York Stock Exchange, as a condition to admitting securities to its list, are much more detailed than those usually submitted to the stockholders. The additional data may include sales in dollars, output in units, amount of federal taxes, details of subsidiaries' operations, basis and amount of depreciation and depletion charges. Valuable information may also be supplied regarding the properties owned, the terms of contracts, and the accounting methods followed.
The analyst will find these listing applications exceedingly helpful. It is unfortunate that they appear at irregular intervals, and therefore cannot be counted upon as a steady source of information.
**Registration Statements and Prospectuses.** As a result of the S.E.C. legislation and regulations, the information available regarding all listed securities and all *new* securities (whether listed or not) is much more comprehensive than heretofore. These data are contained in registration statements filed with the Commission in Washington and available for inspection or obtainable in copy upon payment of a fee. Themore important information in the registration statement must be included in the prospectus supplied by the underwriters to intending purchasers of new issues. Similar registration statements must be filed with the S.E.C. under the terms of the Public Utility Act of 1935, which applies to holding companies, some of which might not come under the other legislation. Although it is true that the registration statements are undoubtedly too bulky to be read by the typical investor, and although it is doubtful if he is even careful to digest the material in the abbreviated prospectus (which still may cover more than 100 pages), there is no doubt that this material is proving of the greatest value to the analyst and through him to the investing public.
**Miscellaneous Official Reports.** Information on individual companies may be unearthed in various kinds of official documents. A few examples will give an idea of their miscellaneous character. The report of the United States Coal Commission in 1923 (finally printed as a Senate Document in 1925) gave financial and operating data on the anthracite companies which had not previously been published. Reports of the Federal Trade Commission have recently supplied a wealth of information heretofore not available concerning utility operating and holding companies, and natural-gas and pipe-line companies, unearthed in an elaborate investigation extending over a period of about nine years. In 1938 and 1939 the Commission published detailed reports on the farm implement and automobile manufacturers. In 1933 a comprehensive study of the pipe-line companies was published under the direction of the House Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce. Voluminous studies of the American Telephone and Telegraph System have emanated from the investigation carried on by the Federal Communications Commission pursuant to a Congressional resolution adopted in 1935.⁷ Some of the opinions of the Interstate Commerce Commission have contained material of great value to the analyst. Trustees under mortgages may have information required to be supplied by the terms of the indenture. These figures may be significant. For example, unpublished reports with the trustee of Mason City and FortDodge Railroad Company 4s, revealed that the interest on the bonds was not being earned, that payment thereof was being continued by Chicago Great Western Railroad Company as a matter of policy only, and hence that the bonds were in a far more vulnerable position than was generally suspected.
**Statistical and Financial Publications.** Most of the information required by the securities analyst in his daily work may be found conveniently and adequately presented by the various statistical services. These include comprehensive manuals published annually with periodic supplements (Poor's, Moody's); descriptive stock and bond cards, and manuals frequently revised (Standard & Poor's, Fitch); daily digests of news relating to individual companies (Standard Corporation Records, Fitch).⁸ These services have made great progress during the past 20 years in the completeness and accuracy with which they present the facts. Nevertheless they cannot be relied upon to give all the data available in the various original sources above described. Some of these sources escape them completely, and in other cases they may neglect to reproduce items of importance. It follows therefore that in any thoroughgoing study of an individual company, the analyst should consult the original reports and other documents wherever possible, and not rely upon summaries or transcriptions.
In the field of financial periodicals, special mention must be made of *The Commercial and Financial Chronicle*, a weekly publication with numerous statistical supplements. Its treatment of the financial and industrial field is unusually comprehensive; and its most noteworthy feature is perhaps its detailed reproduction of corporate reports and other documents.

## **向公司直接索取信息。**

<!--en-->
**Requests for Direct Information from the Company.**

已公开的信息往往可以通过私下询问管理层或与他们面谈来在很大程度上得到补充。股东完全没有理由不询问特定问题，而且在许多情况下，至少会部分满足其需求。必须牢记，股东既是企业的*所有者*，也是其管理人员的*雇主*。他不仅有权提出合理的问题，也有权获得答复，除非有令人信服的理由表明不应如此。

<!--en-->
Published information may often be supplemented to an important extent by private inquiry of or by interview with the management. There is no reason why stockholders should not ask for information on specific points, and in many cases part at least of the data asked for will be furnished. It must never be forgotten that a stockholder is an *owner* of the business and an *employer* of its officers. He is entitled not only to asklegitimate questions but also to have them answered, unless there is some persuasive reason to the contrary.

这一至关重要的问题一直未受到足够重视。法院通常认为，诚意的股东与私营企业的合伙人拥有同等的获取完整信息的权利。行使此项权利不得损害公司利益，但需由管理层承担举证责任，证明该请求存在不当动机，或披露信息会对企业造成伤害。

<!--en-->
Insufficient attention has been paid to this all-important point. The courts have generally held that a bona fide stockholder has the same right to full information as a partner in a private business. This right may not be exercised to the detriment of the corporation, but the burden of proof rests upon the management to show an improper motive behind the request or that disclosure of the information would work an injury to the business.

强制公司提供信息需要昂贵的法律诉讼，因此很少有股东能够充分维护自己的权益。不过经验表明，即便是对抗最激烈的管理层，对于合理的信息公开要求也常常会予以满足。尤其是当所要求的资料仅与其他同行业公司常规公布的资料相同之时。

<!--en-->
Compelling a company to supply information involves expensive legal proceedings and hence few shareholders are in a position to assert their rights to the limit. Experience shows, however, that vigorous demands for legitimate information are frequently acceded to even by the most recalcitrant managements. This is particularly true when the information asked for is no more than that which is regularly published by other companies in the same field.

## 关于该行业的信息

<!--en-->
*INFORMATION REGARDING THE INDUSTRY*

有关整个行业的统计数据极为丰富。美国商务部出版的《当前商业调查》每月都会提供多种不同行业的产量、消费量、库存、未完成订单等数据。年度数据则见于《统计摘要》、《世界年鉴》及其他汇编中。更详细的数字可在《制造业双年度普查》中找到。

<!--en-->
Statistical data respecting industries as a whole are available in abundance. The *Survey of Current Business*, published by the United States Department of Commerce, gives monthly figures on output, consumption, stocks, unfilled orders, etc., for many different lines. Annual data are contained in the Statistical Abstract, the World Almanac, and other compendiums. More detailed figures are available in the Biennial Census of Manufactures.

各类行业期刊会定期刊登许多重要的汇总数据。这些刊物还能提供关于该行业当前及未来状况的持续且详尽的描述。因此，分析人士通常可以较为轻松地掌握其所研究行业的历史与问题的相当完整的背景知识。

<!--en-->
Many important summary figures are published at frequent intervals in the various trade journals. In these publications will be found also a continuous and detailed picture of the current and prospective state of the industry. Thus it is usually possible for the analyst to acquire without undue difficulty a background of fairly complete knowledge of the history and problems of the industry with which he is dealing.

近年来，主要的统计机构还开发了更多服务，包括对主要行业群体的基础调查，并经常通过最新数据来更新这些基础调查内容。⁹ ¹ 现在一些铁路公司会向所有股东发送简化的年度报表，但也愿意应要求提供更全面的报告。² 阿拉斯加朱诺的相关数据——略有简化——从大约1925年持续到1939年底。1938年，卡特彼勒拖拉机公司开始每月发布完整的损益表和资产负债表。这其实并不罕见，因为大多数公司都会向董事提供这些数据。³ 1936年3月，纽约证券交易所建议所有上市公司采用这种方式，而非发布常规的季度财报。这一建议引发了强烈反对，次月便被撤回。⁴ 波卡洪塔斯燃料公司似乎是唯一一家虽在纽约证券交易所上市，却仅公布年度资产负债表而不提供任何损益表的企业。其债券于1934年10月被摘牌。

<!--en-->
In recent years the leading statistical agencies have developed additional services containing basic surveys of theprincipal industrial groups, supplemented frequently by current data designed to keep the basic surveys up to date.⁹
¹ Some railroads now send all stockholders a condensed annual statement but offer to send a more comprehensive report on request.
² The Alaska Juneau figures—somewhat abbreviated—have continued from about 1925 to the end of 1939. In 1938 Caterpillar Tractor began to publish monthly a complete income account and a balance sheet. This is not really so extraordinary, for most companies supply these data to their directors.
³ In March 1936 the New York Stock Exchange suggested that all listed companies follow this procedure instead of publishing the usual quarterly earnings. This suggestion aroused great opposition and was withdrawn the next month.
⁴ Pocahontas Fuel Company appears to have been the only enterprise that, although listed on the New York Stock Exchange, published an annual balance sheet only and provided no income statement of any kind. Its bonds were removed from listing in October 1934.

纽约场外交易市场中包含一些所谓的“非上市发行”产品——可追溯至证券交易委员会成立之前——它们不受证券交易委员会的规定约束。其中就有美国图书公司这类不公布损益表的公司，以及新泽西锌业公司这类虽然公布损益表但不公布资产负债表的公司。

<!--en-->
The New York Curb dealings include a number of so called “unlisted issues”— dating from pre-S.E.C. days—which are not subject to requirements of the S.E.C. Among these are companies like American Book, which does not publish an income account, and New Jersey Zinc, which publishes an income account but no balance sheet.

那些在“场外市场”进行交易、因而不受证券交易委员会监管的公司，通常只发布年度报告。这类报告的详细程度往往低于上市公司的报告，尤其容易遗漏销售额和折旧数据。绝大多数此类公司会同时提供资产负债表和损益表，但也有不少例外。一个有趣的例子是邓恩与布拉德斯特里特公司。这家金融信息提供商不会向其股东披露自身的盈利情况。其他不公布损益表的公司还包括贝米斯兄弟包袋公司、约瑟夫·迪克森坩埚公司（自1935年起）、格伦伍德矿业公司、古德曼制造公司、完美炉具公司、雷格尔鞋业公司等。

<!--en-->
Companies whose issues are dealt in “over-the-counter,” and are thus not subject to S.E.C. regulation, generally publish annual reports only. They tend to be less detailed than the statements of listed companies, being especially prone to omit sales and depreciation figures. The great majority supply both a balance sheet and income account, but exceptions are fairly numerous. An amusing example is Dun & Bradstreet Corporation. This purveyor of financial information does not reveal its own earnings to its stockholders. Other companies omitting income accounts are Bemis Brothers’ Bag, Joseph Dixon Crucible (since 1935), Glenwood Range, Goodman Manufacturing, Perfection Stove, Regal Shoe, etc.

⁵ 例如美国塞拉尼斯公司等少数企业，成功获得了1938年之前某些年度销售数据的保密资格。在部分案例中，很可能在大多数案例中，后续的保密申请被拒，这些销售数据随后便被公开了。

<!--en-->
⁵ A few companies, e.g., Celanese Corporation of America, succeeded in obtaining a confidential status for their sales figures in certain years prior to 1938. In some, possibly most, of the cases later requests were denied, and sales figures were subsequently published.

我们对纽约证券交易所上市的几乎所有工业公司（共648家）1938年的报告进行了研究，发现只有8家公司在次年年底仍未公布其销售数据。美国证券交易委员会表示，仅有一家公司（联合水果公司）获得了销售数据保密处理资格，而另外7家公司（美国苏门答腊烟草公司、邦阿米公司、柯林斯与艾克曼公司、马西森碱业公司、梅斯塔机械公司、谢弗笔公司、联合工程与铸造公司）截至1939年12月仍未有定论。

<!--en-->
Our study of the 1938 reports of practically all the industrial companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange (648 enterprises) disclosed that only eight had failed to reveal their sales figures by the end of the following year. The S.E.C. advised that confidential treatment of the sales figure had been granted to one company (United Fruit) and that no decision had been reached with respect to the other seven (American Sumatra Tobacco, Bon Ami, Collins & Aikman, Mathieson Alkali, Mesta Machine, Sheaffer Pen, United Engineering and Foundry), as late as December 1939.

诸如特里科产品公司之类的多家企业因不愿提供销售数据而未能完成注册，最终从上市名单中被剔除。马林洛克威尔公司1938年退出上市可能也是出于同样的原因。各证券交易所主张修改法律，要求场外交易企业必须完全披露信息，以消除他们认为存在的不公平优势。

<!--en-->
Various issues, e.g., Trico Products Corporation, failed to register and were dropped from listing, presumably because of their unwillingness to supply sales figures. The withdrawal of Marlin Rockwell Corporation from listing in 1938 maybe ascribed to the same reason. The stock exchanges have favored an amendment to the law requiring full disclosure in the case of over-the-counter issues, to remove what they regard as an unfair advantage.

许多公司在其年度报告中向股东提供的信息仍远少于向美国证券交易委员会提交的资料。不过，标准统计公司记录服务部门会定期将美国证券交易委员会的统计数据作为补充资料予以发布。

<!--en-->
Many companies still provide their stockholders in their annual reports with much less information than they file with the S.E.C. The Standard Statistics Corporation Records Service, however, regularly publishes the S.E.C. figures as supplementary data.

⁶ 纽约证券交易所与联合化学染料公司之间曾因上述几项问题陷入长期纠纷，该纠纷于1933年以令证券交易所满意的方式告终。但该公司向股东提交的年度报告仍然不够完善，因为其中未提供销售额、运营费用或折旧等相关数据。

<!--en-->
6 Several of these points were involved in a protracted dispute between the New York Stock Exchange and Allied Chemical and Dye Corporation, which was terminated to the satisfaction of the Stock Exchange in 1933. But the annual reports of the company to shareholders are still inadequate in that they fail to furnish figures for sales, operating expenses, or depreciation.

CHAPTER 4

## 投资与投机的区别

<!--en-->
*Distinctions Between Investment and Speculation*

## “投资”一词的一般含义

<!--en-->
*General Connotations of the Term “Investment.”*

投资或从事投资活动，就像布兰代斯大法官那句名言中的“价值”一样，是“一个含义多样的词”。其中有三种含义与我们此处讨论的内容相关。第一种含义，或者说这一组含义，指的是将资金投入某项业务。有人会投入1,000美元来开一家杂货店；在1929–1938年间，钢铁行业的“投资回报率”（包括债券债务和留存利润）平均为2.40%¹。这里的含义纯粹是描述性的，不作任何区分，也不做任何评判。不过需要注意的是，它承认而非否定风险因素——通常认为普通商业投资是在“企业自担风险”的前提下进行的。

<!--en-->
Investment or investing, like “value” in the famous dictum of Justice Brandeis, is “a word of many meanings.” Of these, three will concern us here. The first meaning, or set of meanings, relates to putting or having money in a business. A man “invests” $1,000 in opening a grocery store; the “return on investment” in the steel industry (including bonded debt and retained profits) averaged 2.40% during 1929–1938.¹ The sense here is purely descriptive; it makes no distinctions and pronounces no judgments. Note, however, that it accepts rather than rejects the element of risk—the ordinary business investment is said to be made “at the risk of the business.”

第二组用法是将这一术语类似地应用于金融领域。在这种意义上，所有证券都属于“投资”。我们有投资经销商或经纪人、投资公司²或信托机构、投资清单。在这里，投资与其他类型的金融活动（如投机）之间同样没有真正的区别。它只是一个方便的统称，或许还带有一些委婉语的意味——也就是说，人们希望给各种性质的金融交易赋予一定的体面性。

<!--en-->
The second set of uses applies the term in a similar manner to the field of finance. In this sense all securities are “investments.” We have investment dealers or brokers, investment companies² or trusts, investment lists. Here, again, no real distinction is made between investment and other types of financial operations such as speculation. It is a convenient omnibus word, with perhaps an admixture of euphemism—*i.e.*, a desire to lend a certain respectability to financial dealings of miscellaneous character.

除了这两种不加区分的“投资”用法之外，一直还存在第三种更为有限的含义——即投资与投机的对比。人们普遍认为这种区分是有用的，并且通常认为在这种特殊意义上，投资对所有人、在任何时候都是有益的。

<!--en-->
Alongside of these two indiscriminate uses of the term “investment” has always been a third and more limited connotation—that of investment as opposed to speculation. That such a distinction is a useful one is generally taken for granted. It is commonly thought that investment, in this special sense, is good for everybody and at all times.

另一方面，投机行为的好坏则取决于具体环境和投机者本身。因此，任何从事金融活动的人都必须清楚自己是在投资还是在投机，如果是后者，还需确保自己的投机行为是合理的。

<!--en-->
Speculation, on the other hand, may be good or bad, depending on the conditions and the person who speculates. It should be essential, therefore, for anyone engaging in financial operations to know whether he is investing or speculating and, if the latter, to make sure that his speculation is a justifiable one.

当投资与投机被如此对立起来时，几乎所有人都能大致理解二者之间的区别；但当我们试图给出精确的定义时，就会遇到令人困惑的难题。事实上，那种认为“投资是成功的投机，而投机是失败的投资”的愤世嫉俗定义也有一定道理。人们或许会想当然地认为美国政府债券属于投资工具，而像美国无线电公司这样的公司的普通股——在1931年至1935年间既没有股息、盈利，也没有实物资产作为支撑——肯定属于投机行为。然而，美国政府债券中也可能存在纯粹的投机操作（例如，一些专业人士会大量买入，期望股价迅速上涨）；另一方面，在1929年时，美国无线电公司的普通股却被广泛视为投资品，甚至被纳入众多顶尖“投资信托基金”的投资组合中。

<!--en-->
The difference between investment and speculation, when the two are thus opposed, is understood in a general way by nearly everyone; but when we try to formulate it precisely, we run into perplexing difficulties. In fact something can be said for the cynic's definition that an investment is a successful speculation and a speculation is an unsuccessful investment. It might be taken for granted that United States government securities are an investment medium, while the common stock, say, of Radio Corporation of America—which between 1931 and 1935 had neither dividends, earnings, nor tangible assets behind it—must certainly be a speculation. Yet operations of a definitely speculative nature may be carried on in United States government bonds (e.g., by specialists who buy large blocks in anticipation of a quick rise); and on the other hand, in 1929 Radio Corporation of America common was widely regarded as an investment, to the extent in fact of being included in the portfolios of leading “Investment Trusts.”

如果能得出一个准确且可接受的定义来区分这两个术语，当然是非常理想的，至少这样我们就能尽可能清楚地知道自己在谈论什么。或许还有一个更有力的理由：未能正确区分投资与投机，在很大程度上导致了1928–1929年的市场过度波动及随之而来的灾难，同时我们认为，这也造成了潜在投资者在观念与策略上的持续混乱。因此，我们将对这个问题进行比通常更为深入的研究。最好的做法或许是首先批判性地审视人们在使用这两个术语时通常所指的各种含义，然后再努力从中提炼出一个清晰、明确的关于投资的定义。

<!--en-->
It is certainly desirable that some exact and acceptable definition of the two terms be arrived at, if only because we ought as far as possible to know what we are talking about. A more forceful reason, perhaps, might be the statement that the failure properly to distinguish between investment and speculation was in large measure responsible for the market excesses of 1928–1929 and the calamities that ensued—as well as, we think, for much continuing confusion in the ideas and policies of would-be investors. On this account we shall give the question a more thoroughgoing study than it usually receives. The best procedure might be first to examine critically the various meanings commonly intended in using the two expressions, and then to endeavor to crystallize therefrom a single sound and definite conception of investment.

## 通常用于区分这两个术语的标准。

<!--en-->
*Distinctions Commonly Drawn Between the Two Terms.*

常见的主要区别可列于下表：

<!--en-->
The chief distinctions in common use may be listed in the following table:

<table><thead><tr><td>投资</td><td>投机</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1. 债券方面。</td><td>股票方面。</td></tr><tr><td>2. 全额购买。</td><td>保证金购买。</td></tr><tr><td>3. 长期持有。</td><td>短期套利。</td></tr><tr><td>4. 为获取收益。</td><td>为获取利润。</td></tr><tr><td>5. 安全的证券。</td><td>风险较高的证券。</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><td>Investment</td><td>Speculation</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1. In bonds.</td><td>In stocks.</td></tr><tr><td>2. Outright purchases.</td><td>Purchases on margin.</td></tr><tr><td>3. For permanent holding.</td><td>For a “quick turn.”</td></tr><tr><td>4. For income.</td><td>For profit.</td></tr><tr><td>5. In safe securities.</td><td>In risky issues.</td></tr></tbody></table>

前四种区别的优点在于完全明确，而且每一条都阐述了一个适用于大多数投资或投机行为的特征。不过，它们都存在一个缺陷：在许多具体案例中，这些标准可能并不适用。

<!--en-->
The first four distinctions have the advantage of being entirely definite, and each of them also sets forth a characteristic which is applicable to the *general run* of investment or speculation. They are all open to the objection that in numerous individual cases the criterion suggested would not properly apply.

**1. 债券与股票。**先来看第一种区别，它符合人们通常认为的投资与投机的对比观念，而且至少有一位投资领域的权威人士也支持这一观点，认为只有债券才属于投资范畴。³ 然而，这一观点与高评级优先股几乎被普遍视为投资工具的事实相悖。此外，认为债券本身就具备投资属性是非常危险的，因为那些担保不足的债券不仅可能属于纯粹的投机行为，甚至可能是最无吸引力的投机形式。另外，仅仅因为某只股票具有盈利潜力就否认其投资评级，在逻辑上也是站不住脚的。就连大众的观点也承认这一点，因为一直以来，某些特别稳健的普通股都被评定为投资品种，其购买者也被视为投资者而非投机者。

<!--en-->
**1. Bonds vs. Stocks.** Taking up the first distinction, we find it corresponds to a common idea of investing as opposed to speculating, and that it also has the weight of at least one authority on investment who insists that only bonds belong in that category.³ The latter contention, however, runs counter to the well-nigh universal acceptance of high-grade preferred stocks as media of investment. Furthermore, it is most dangerous to regard the bond form as possessing inherently the credentials of an investment, for a poorly secured bond may not only be thoroughly speculative but the most unattractive form of speculation as well. It is logically unsound, furthermore, to deny investment rating to a strongly entrenched common stock merely because it possesses profit possibilities. Even the popular view recognizes this fact, since at all times certain especially sound common stocks have been rated as investment issues and their purchasers regarded as investors and not as speculators.

**2和3. 全额购买与保证金购买；长期持有与短期持有。**第二和第三种区别涉及的是惯用的*方式*和*意图*，而非投资与投机行为本身的内在特性。显然，全额购买股票并不意味着该交易就一定是投资。实际上，最具投机性的证券，比如“低价矿业股”，必须以全额资金购买，因为没人愿意为这类股票提供贷款。相反，在战争期间美国民众被鼓励用借来的钱购买自由债券，但这些购买行为仍被普遍视为投资。如果在金融操作中严格遵循逻辑——这是个极不可能的假设！——那么常规做法就会被颠倒过来：更安全的（投资型）证券会被认为更适合通过保证金购买，而风险更高的（投机型）证券则需全额支付。

<!--en-->
**2 and 3. Outright vs. Marginal Purchases; Permanent vs. Temporary Holding.** The second and third distinctions relate to the customary *method* and *intention*, rather than to theinnate character of investment and speculative operations. It should be obvious that buying a stock outright does not *ipso facto* make the transaction an investment. In truth the most speculative issues, e.g., “penny mining stocks,” *must* be purchased outright, since no one will lend money against them. Conversely, when the American public was urged during the war to buy Liberty Bonds with borrowed money, such purchases were nonetheless universally classed as investments. If strict logic were followed in financial operations—a very improbable hypothesis!—the common practice would be reversed: the safer (investment) issues would be considered more suitable for marginal purchase, and the riskier (speculative) commitments would be paid for in full.

同样，永久性持有与临时性持有之间的区别也仅能以一种宽泛且不精确的方式加以应用。有一位研究普通股的专家将投资定义为任何意图持有一年或更长时间的购买行为；但这一定义显然更多是出于便利性而非深刻洞察力而提出的。⁴“短期投资”作为一种早已存在的做法，恰恰证明了这一建议性规则的不精确性。“长期投机”同样是一种普遍存在的现象——当投资者持筹希望弥补损失时便是如此，而在某种程度上它也被视为一种有意识的商业行为。

<!--en-->
Similarly the contrast between permanent and temporary holding is applicable only in a broad and inexact fashion. An authority on common stocks has defined an investment as any purchase made with the intention of holding it for a year or longer; but this definition is admittedly suggested by its convenience rather than its penetration.⁴ The inexactness of this suggested rule is shown by the circumstance that *short-term investment* is a well-established practice. *Long-term speculation* is equally well established as a rueful fact (when the purchaser holds on hoping to make up a loss), and it is also carried on to some extent as an intentional undertaking.

**4和5. 收入与利润；安全与风险。**第四与第五种区分也属于同一范畴，结合在一起后无疑比其他区分更接近于对该主题的理性及大众层面的理解。的确，在1928年之前的许多年里，典型投资者的首要关注点一直是本金的安全以及持续稳定的收入。然而，“普通股是最理想的长期投资”这一观念导致人们的重点从当前收入转向未来收入，进而不可避免地转向未来本金价值的提升。这种将收入要素完全置于对利润追求之下的投资方式，再加上其对未来有利发展的过度依赖，使得以投资信托的总体策略为代表的新时代投资风格实际上与投机毫无二致。事实上，这种所谓的“投资”完全可以被准确地定义为对那些经营状况良好的公司普通股的投机行为。

<!--en-->
**4 and 5. Income vs. Profit; Safety vs. Risk.** The fourth and fifth distinctions also belong together, and so joined they undoubtedly come closer than the others to both a rational and a popular understanding of the subject. Certainly, through many years prior to 1928, the typical investor had been interested above all in safety of principal and continuance of an adequate income. However, the doctrine that common stocks are the best long-term investments has resulted in a transfer of emphasis from current income to future income and hence inevitably to future enhancement of principal value. In its complete subordination of the income element to the desire for profit, and also in the prime reliance it places upon favorable developments expected in the future, the new-era style of investment—as exemplified in the general policy ofthe investment trusts—is practically indistinguishable from speculation. In fact this so-called “investment” can be accurately defined as speculation in the common stocks of strongly situated companies.

回归到“收入是投资的核心动机”这一公认理念，将追求利润或资本增值视为投机的典型特征，无疑会是一个有益的举措。但即便如此，投资真正的本质是否仍体现在这种区分之中，仍值得怀疑。回顾过去的常规投资实践，我们会发现有些情况下，当前收入并非真正正规投资操作的主要考量因素。例如银行股在很长一段时间内都被视为只有富有的投资者才能涉足的领域，这种情况就很常见。这类股票的股息率低于高等级债券，但人们购买它们是期望其盈利和盈余的持续增长能够带来额外的分红以及本金价值的上升。换言之，驱动投资者购买的动力是计入股东名下的收益，而非实际分发的股息。然而，将这种态度称为投机似乎并不恰当，因为那样一来我们就必须认为，只有那些将大部分盈利以股息形式发放（从而提供足够当前回报）的银行股才能被视为投资，而那些采取保守策略积累盈余的股票则应被归类为投机。这样的结论显然是自相矛盾的；正因如此，我们必须承认：对普通股的投资完全可以基于其盈利能力，而无需考虑当前的股息支付情况。这是否意味着我们又回到了新时代的投资理论？我们是否必须认为，1929年购买低收益工业股的行为与战前购买低收益银行股的行为具有同等的“投资”资格？对这个问题的回答应该能让我们结束探索，但要妥善解答它，我们必须将注意力转向列表中的第五个也是最后一个区分——即安全与风险之间的区别。

<!--en-->
It would undoubtedly be a wholesome step to go back to the accepted idea of income as the central motive in investment, leaving the aim toward profit, or capital appreciation, as the typical characteristic of speculation. But it is doubtful whether the true inwardness of investment rests even in this distinction. Examining standard practices of the past, we find some instances in which current income was not the leading interest of a bona fide investment operation. This was regularly true, for example, of bank stocks, which until recent years were regarded as the exclusive province of the wealthy investor. These issues returned a smaller dividend yield than did high-grade bonds, but they were purchased on the expectation that the steady growth in earnings and surplus would result in special distributions and increased principal value. In other words, it was the earnings accruing to the stockholder's credit, rather than those distributed in dividends, which motivated his purchase. Yet it would not appear to be sound to call this attitude speculative, for we should then have to contend that only the bank stocks which paid out most of their earnings in dividends (and thus gave an adequate current return) could be regarded as investments, while those following the conservative policy of building up their surplus would therefore have to be considered speculative. Such a conclusion is obviously paradoxical; and because of this fact it must be admitted that an investment in a common stock might conceivably be founded on its earning power, without reference to current dividend payments
Does this bring us back to the new-era theory of investment? Must we say that the purchase of low-yielding industrial shares in 1929 had the same right to be called investment as the purchase of low-yielding bank stocks in prewar days? The answer to this question should bring us to the end of our quest, but to deal with it properly we must turn our attention to the fifth and last distinction in our list—that between safety and risk.

这一区分体现了所有与“投资”一词相关的概念中最广泛的定义，但其实际应用却因种种缺陷而受到限制。如果用最终结果来评判安全性，那实际上就是在回避问题，而且极易滑向那种将投资定义为成功的投机行为的愤世嫉俗定义。⁵当然，安全性必须事先设定，但即便如此，其中仍存在大量不确定且纯粹主观的因素。在赛马场上赌“稳赢”的赌徒也坚信自己的投注是安全的。1929年那些投资高价普通股的“投资者”同样认为，凭借对未来增长的预期，他们所支付的高价是合理的，因此自己是安全的。

<!--en-->
This distinction expresses the broadest concept of all those underlying the term *investment*, but its practical utility is handicapped by various shortcomings. If safety is to be judged by the result, we are virtually begging the question, and come perilously close to the cynic's definition of an investment as a successful speculation.⁵ Naturally the safety must be posited in advance, but here again there is room for much that is indefinite and purely subjective. The race-track gambler, betting on a "sure thing," is convinced that his commitment is safe. The 1929 "investor" in high-priced common stocks also considered himself safe in his reliance upon future growth to justify the figure he paid and more.

**安全标准。**只有以比购买者心理更具体的标准为基础，安全的概念才能真正发挥作用。安全必须通过适用明确且既定的标准来得到保障，或至少有充分的体现。正是这一点区分了1912年的银行股买家与1929年的普通股投资者：前者会根据经验判断价格处于保守水平，并凭借对机构资源与盈利能力的了解，确信自己买到了物有所值的产品；如果投机性市场导致股价上升至与这些价值标准不符的水平，他就会卖出股票，等待合理价格回归后再重新买入。

<!--en-->
**Standards of Safety.** The concept of safety can be really useful only if it is based on something more tangible than the psychology of the purchaser. The safety must be assured, or at least strongly indicated, by the application of definite and well-established standards. It was this point which distinguished the bank-stock buyer of 1912 from the common-stock investor of 1929. The former purchased at price levels which he considered conservative in the light of experience; he was satisfied, from his knowledge of the institution's resources and earning power, that he was getting his money's worth in full. If a strong speculative market resulted in advancing the price to a level out of line with these standards of value, he sold his shares and waited for a reasonable price to return before reacquiring them.

如果1928–1929年的普通股买家也能采取同样的态度，“投资”这个词就不会成为如今这个具有悲剧色彩的误称。但当公众自豪地将“蓝筹股”这一称号赋予那些他们偏爱的高价股票时，实际上无意中暴露了其所谓投资选择背后的赌博动机。这些投资与过去的银行股购买有一个关键区别：买家并未通过既定的价值标准来判断这些股票是否值得当前的价格。市场则自行制定了新的标准，将当前价格——无论多高——视为唯一的价值衡量标准。基于这种不加批判的态度所形成的任何安全观念显然都是虚幻的，且充满风险。将其推到极端，就意味着对于优质股票而言，没有过高的价格，而且这类股票在股价涨到200点时与25点时一样“安全”。

<!--en-->
Had the same attitude been taken by the purchaser of common stocks in 1928–1929, the term *investment* would not have been the tragic misnomer that it was. But in proudly applying the designation "blue chips" to the high-priced issues chiefly favored, the public unconsciously revealed the gambling motive at the heart of its supposed investment selections. These differed from the old-time bank-stock purchases in the one vital respect that the buyer did not determine that they were worth the price paid by the application of firmly established standards of value. The market made up new standards as it went along, by accepting the current price—however high—as the sole measure of value. Any idea of safety based on this uncritical approachwas clearly illusory and replete with danger. Carried to its logical extreme, it meant that no price could possibly be too high for a good stock, and that such an issue was equally “safe” after it had advanced to 200 as it had been at 25.

**投资的拟议定义。**通过上述比较可以看出，仅仅将投资等同于预期的安全性是不够的；这种预期必须建立在研究及标准之上。同时，投资者并不一定需要对当前收益感兴趣；他有时完全可以根据未来会累积到自己账户中的回报，并在经过或长或短的等待后实现该回报，从而合理地做出购买决策。基于这些观察，我们提出以下符合大众对该词的理解以及合理精确性要求的投资定义：

<!--en-->
**A Proposed Definition of Investment.** This comparison suggests that it is not enough to identify investment with expected safety; the expectation must be based on study and standards. At the same time, the investor need not necessarily be interested in current income; he may at times legitimately base his purchase on a return which is accumulating to his credit and realized by him after a longer or shorter wait. With these observations in mind, we suggest the following definition of investment as one in harmony with both the popular understanding of the term and the requirements of reasonable precision:

*投资行为是指经过全面分析后，能够确保本金安全并带来理想回报的行为；不符合这些要求的行为属于投机行为。*这一定义的某些含义值得进一步探讨。我们之所以使用“投资行为”而非“某只股票”或“某次购买”，是有几层原因的：认为投资属性天然存在于某只股票本身是不对的。价格往往是关键因素，因此同一只股票（甚至债券）在某个价格区间可能具备投资价值，而在另一个区间则未必。此外，某种投资可能在一系列股票中是合理的，而单独投资其中任何一只都不足以保证足够的安全性。换言之，为了将各类股票带来的风险降至符合投资要求的最低水平，多元化投资可能是必要的。（这通常也适用于用于投资的普通股购买。）

<!--en-->
*An investment operation is one which, upon thorough analysis, promises safety of principal and a satisfactory return. Operations not meeting these requirements are speculative.*
Certain implications of this definition are worthy of further discussion. We speak of an *investment operation* rather than an issue or a purchase, for several reasons. It is unsound to think always of investment character as inhering in an issue *per se*. The price is frequently an essential element, so that a stock (and even a bond) may have investment merit at one price level but not at another. Furthermore, an investment might be justified in a group of issues, which would not be sufficiently safe if made in any one of them singly. In other words, diversification might be necessary to reduce the risk involved in the separate issues to the minimum consonant with the requirements of investment. (This would be true, in general, of purchases of common stocks for investment.)

在我们看来，某些涉及用一种证券出售来换取另一种证券购买的套利和对冲交易也应被视为投资行为。在这些交易中，买卖相结合的方式便提供了安全保障。

<!--en-->
In our view it is also proper to consider as investment operations certain types of arbitrage and hedging commitments which involve the sale of one security against the purchase of another. In these operations the element of safety is provided by the combination of purchase and sale.

这是对传统投资概念的延伸，但在作者看来是完全合乎逻辑的。

<!--en-->
This is an extension of the ordinary concept of investment, but one which appears to the writers to be entirely logical.

“全面分析”、“确保安全”以及“理想回报”这些表述都存在一定的模糊性，但重要的是它们的含义足够清晰，不会造成严重的误解。所谓“全面分析”，当然指的是依据既定的安全与价值标准对相关事实进行研究。那种仅仅因为通用电气前景广阔，就建议以40倍于其历史最高盈利水平的股价购买该公司股票的分析，显然因缺乏全面性而被排除在外。

<!--en-->
The phrases *thorough analysis*, *promises safety*, and *satisfactory return* are all chargeable with indefiniteness, but the important point is that their meaning is clear enough to prevent serious misunderstanding. By *thorough analysis* we mean, of course, the study of the facts in the light of established standards of safety and value. An “analysis” that recommended investment in General Electric common at a price forty times its highest recorded earnings merely because of its excellent prospects would be clearly ruled out, as devoid of all quality of thoroughness.

投资所追求的*安全性*并非绝对或完全的；这一概念实际上指的是在所有正常或合理可能的情况下免于损失的保护。例如，安全的债券是指只有在极其罕见且概率极低的情形下才会出现违约的债券。同样，安全的股票是指除了极不可能发生的意外情况外，始终有价值与其购买价格相等的股票。当研究及经验表明必须承认并考虑存在相当大的损失风险时，那就属于投机性投资。

<!--en-->
The *safety* sought in investment is not absolute or complete; the word means, rather, protection against loss under all normal or reasonably likely conditions or variations. A safe bond, for example, is one which could suffer default only under exceptional and highly improbable circumstances. Similarly, a safe stock is one which holds every prospect of being worth the price paid except under quite unlikely contingencies. Where study and experience indicate that an appreciable chance of loss must be recognized and allowed for, we have a speculative situation.

*令人满意的回报*这一表述比*足够的收入*更为宽泛，因为它不仅包括当前的利息或股息收益，还涵盖资本增值或利润。“令人满意”是一个主观术语，它指投资者在具备合理判断力的前提下愿意接受的任何回报率或回报金额，无论其多低。

<!--en-->
A *satisfactory return* is a wider expression than *adequate income*, since it allows for capital appreciation or profit as well as current interest or dividend yield. “Satisfactory” is a subjective term; it covers any rate or amount of return, however low, which the investor is willing to accept, provided he acts with reasonable intelligence.

从略有不同的角度来阐述我们的定义或许会有所帮助，这一角度旨在强调投资必须始终同时考虑证券的*价格*与*质量*。严格来说，从绝对意义上讲并不存在所谓的“投资品种”，即不考虑价格仍可视为投资的品种。对于高等级债券而言，这一点可能并不重要，因为其价格极少会高到足以带来严重的本金损失风险。但在普通股领域，这种风险往往可能因价格过度上涨而产生——事实上，在我们看来，大多数实力强劲公司的普通股在大部分时间里都应被视为投机性资产，仅仅因为其价格过高，无法在任何合理的意义上保证本金安全。我们必须提醒读者，华尔街的主流观点与我们在此问题上的看法并不一致；读者需要自行判断谁是错的。

<!--en-->
It may be helpful to elaborate our definition from a somewhat different angle, which will stress the fact that investment must always consider the *price* as well as the *quality* of the security. Strictly speaking, there can be no such thing as an “investment issue” in the absolute sense, *i.e.*, implying that it remains an investment regardless of price. In the case of high-grade bonds, this point may not be important, for it is rare that their prices are so inflated as to introduce serious risk of loss of principal. But in the common-stock field this risk may frequently be created by an undue advance inprice—so much so, indeed, that in our opinion the great majority of common stocks of strong companies must be considered speculative during most of the time, simply because their price is too high to warrant safety of principal in any intelligible sense of the phrase. We must warn the reader that prevailing Wall Street opinion does not agree with us on this point; and he must make up his own mind which of us is wrong.

尽管如此，我们仍会将这一原则体现在以下额外的投资标准中：

<!--en-->
Nevertheless, we shall embody our principle in the following additional criterion of investment:

*投资行为是指既能在质量层面又在数量层面得到合理解释的行为。*投资与投机之间的界限可能在多大程度上取决于具体事实，包括价格因素，而非某种简单的普遍规律，这一点可以通过基于通用电气特别股（即优先股）在连续数月内发生的两个对比案例以较为极端的方式加以说明。

<!--en-->
*An investment operation is one that can be justified on both qualitative and quantitative grounds.*
The extent to which the distinction between investment and speculation may depend upon the underlying facts, including the element of price, rather than on any easy generalization, may be brought home in somewhat extreme fashion by two contrasting examples based upon General Electric Special (i.e., Preferred) stock, which occurred in successive months.

*案例1：*1934年12月，该股票以$12\frac{3}{4}$的价格出售。其面值为10美元，每年支付6%的股息，且在任何发薪日都可按11美元的价格被赎回。尽管该股票的股息安全性极高，但以$12\frac{3}{4}$的价格购买的投资者其实是在进行超过本金10%的投机行为。他实际上是在赌该股票在未来几年内不会被赎回。⁶事实上，就在同一个月，该公司宣布将于1935年4月15日以每股11美元的价格赎回该股票。

<!--en-->
*Example 1:* In December 1934 this issue sold at $12\frac{3}{4}$. It paid 6% on $10 par and was callable on any dividend date at 11. In spite of the preeminent quality of this issue, as far as safety of dividends was concerned, the buyer at $12\frac{3}{4}$ was *speculating* to the extent of more than 10% of his principal. He was virtually wagering that the issue would not be called for some years to come.⁶ As it happened, the issue was called that very month for redemption at $11 per share on April 15, 1935.

*案例2：*股票被赎回后，其价格迅速跌至11美元。此时，该股票为通过保证金进行盈利的*短期投资*提供了难得的机会。例如在1935年1月15日，经纪商可以以11美元的价格买入这些股票（无需支付佣金），然后以每年不超过2%的利率为此借款10美元。通过以下计算可以看出，这种操作能确保投资者获得每年40%的净回报：

<!--en-->
*Example 2:* After the issue was called, the price promptly declined to 11. At that time the issue offered an unusual opportunity for profitable *short-term investment on margin*. Brokers buying the shares at 11 (without paying commission), say on January 15, 1935, could have borrowed $10 per share thereon at not more than 2% per annum. This operation would have netted a sure return at the rate of 40% per annum on the capital invested—as shown by the following calculation:

<table><tr><td>以11美元的净价购买1,000股股票的成本</td><td>$11,000</td></tr><tr><td>1935年4月15日以11美元加股息的价格赎回</td><td>11,150</td></tr><tr><td>毛利润</td><td>150</td></tr><tr><td>减去10,000美元按2%利率计算的3个月利息</td><td>50</td></tr><tr><td>净利润</td><td>100</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>Cost of 1,000 shares at 11 net</td><td>$11,000</td></tr><tr><td>Redeemed Apr. 15, 1935, at 11 plus dividend</td><td>11,150</td></tr><tr><td>Gross profit</td><td>150</td></tr><tr><td>Less 3 months' interest at 2% on $10,000</td><td>50</td></tr><tr><td>Net profit</td><td>100</td></tr></table>

1,000股股票在3个月内获得100美元的净利润，相当于每年40%的回报率。

<!--en-->
Net profit of $100 on $1,000 in 3 months is equivalent to annual return of 40%.

毋庸置疑，这种特殊操作的安全性以及由此产生的*投资*属性，完全源于持有者能够绝对确定这些股票会在1935年4月被赎回这一事实。

<!--en-->
Needless to say, the safety, and the resultant *investment* character, of this unusual operation derived solely from the fact that the holder could count absolutely on the redemption of the shares in April 1935.

上述所提出的投资概念比大多数常用的概念更为宽泛。根据这一概念，虽然通常不会如此，但理论上也可以对股票进行保证金交易，并以快速获利为主要目的进行购买。在这些方面，它与我们最初列出的前四项区分标准相悖。但为了弥补这种看似宽松的标准，我们坚持要求基于充分分析给出令人满意的安全保障。因此我们得出结论：分析视角与投资视角在范围上大体上是相同的。

<!--en-->
The conception of investment advanced above is broader than most of those in common use. Under it investment may conceivably—though not usually—be made in stocks, carried on margin, and purchased with the chief interest in a quick profit. In these respects it would run counter to the first four distinctions which we listed at the outset. But to offset this seeming laxity, we insist on a satisfactory assurance of safety based on adequate analysis. We are thus led to the conclusion that the viewpoint of analysis and the viewpoint of investment are largely identical in their scope.

### 投资与投机的其他方面

<!--en-->
*OTHER ASPECTS OF INVESTMENT AND SPECULATION*

**未来与投资及投机之间的关系。**可以大致地说，投资以过去为基础，而投机则主要着眼于未来。但这一表述远非完整。投资与投机都必须经受未来的考验；它们会受到未来局势变化的影响，并依据未来的结果来评判。不过，我们关于分析师与未来的论述同样适用于投资的概念。对投资而言，未来本质上是需要防范的对象，而非获取利润的来源。如果未来带来改善，那当然更好；但投资本身在很大程度上不能建立在对改善的期望之上。另一方面，投机则总能——而且常常是合理地——从不同于过去表现的未来发展态势中找到其依据与合理性。

<!--en-->
**Relation of the Future to Investment and Speculation.** It may be said, with some approximation to the truth, that investment is grounded on the past whereas speculation looks primarily to the future. But this statement is far from complete. Both investment and speculation must meet the test of the future; they are subject to its vicissitudes and are judged by its verdict. But what we have said about the analyst and the future applies equally well to the concept of investment. For investment, the future is essentially something to be guarded against rather than to be profited from. If the future brings improvement, so much the better; but investment as such cannot be founded in any important degree upon theexpectation of improvement. Speculation, on the other hand, may always properly—and often soundly—derive its basis and its justification from prospective developments that differ from past performance.

**“投资”的类型。**假设读者已经对我们刚刚阐述的独特意义上的投资有了较为清晰的理解，但本章开头提到的该术语在更广泛意义上的普遍使用仍会带来混淆。在需要明确具体含义时，定期使用一些描述性形容词或许会有所帮助。我们暂且提出以下建议：

<!--en-->
**Types of “Investment.”** Assuming that the student has acquired a fairly clear concept of investment in the distinctive sense that we have just developed, there remains the confusing effect of the prevalent use of the term in the broader meanings referred to at the beginning of this chapter. It might be useful if some descriptive adjective were regularly employed, when care is needed, to designate the particular meaning intended. Let us tentatively suggest the following:

<table><tr><td>1. 商业投资</td><td>指投入或持有于企业中的资金。</td></tr><tr><td>2. 金融投资或一般意义上的投资</td><td>指一般的证券。</td></tr><tr><td>3. 低风险投资</td><td>指因享有优先收益权或基于完善的征税机制而被视为风险较低的证券。</td></tr><tr><td>4. 分析师的投资</td><td>指经过深入研究后有望保障本金安全并带来足够回报的投资行为。</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>1. Business investment</td><td>Referring to money put or held in a business.</td></tr><tr><td>2. Financial investment or investment generally</td><td>Referring to securities generally.</td></tr><tr><td>3. Sheltered investment</td><td>Referring to securities regarded as subject to small risk by reason of their prior claim on earnings or because they rest upon an adequate taxing power.</td></tr><tr><td>4. Analyst’s investment</td><td>Referring to operations that, upon thorough study, promise safety of principal and an adequate return.</td></tr></table>

显然，这些不同类型的投资并非相互排斥。例如，一张优质债券就属于上述四种类别。除非另有说明，否则我们将使用“投资”及其相关词汇，指代本章所阐述的“分析师的投资”这一含义。

<!--en-->
Evidently these different types of investment are not mutually exclusive. A good bond, for example, would fall under all four headings. Unless we specify otherwise, we shall employ the word “investment,” and its relatives, in the sense of “analyst’s investment,” as developed in this chapter.

**投机的类型。**当对华尔街的各类活动进行严格审视时，投机与赌博之间的区别便显得尤为重要。纽约证券交易所的官方立场大致认为，“赌博”是指创造原本不存在的风险——比如赛马投注——而“投机”则是指承担某种情境中固有的、必须由某人承担的风险。虽然“理性投机”与“非理性投机”之间的正式区分可能会受到强烈的理论质疑，但我们认为它具有实际意义。因此我们提出以下分类：

<!--en-->
**Types of Speculation.** The distinction between speculation and gambling assumes significance when the activities of Wall Street are subjected to critical scrutiny. It is more or less the official position of the New York Stock Exchange that “gambling” represents the creation of risks not previously existing—e.g., race-track betting—whereas “speculation” applies to the taking of risks that are implicit in a situation and so must be taken by someone. A formal distinction between “intelligent speculation” and “unintelligent speculation” is no doubt open to strong theoretical objections, but we do think that it has practical utility. Thus we suggest the following:

<table><tr><td>1. 理性投机</td><td>在仔细权衡利弊后认为值得承担的风险。</td></tr><tr><td>2. 非理性投机</td><td>未充分研究情况便盲目承担风险的行为。</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>1. Intelligent speculation</td><td>The taking of a risk that appears justified after careful weighing of the pros and cons.</td></tr><tr><td>2. Unintelligent speculation</td><td>Risk taking without adequate study of the situation.</td></tr></table>

在普通商业领域，大多数经过深思熟虑的企业既属于理性投机，也属于大众意义上所说的“商业投资”。如果损失风险极小——属于罕见情况——那么某个特定商业项目可能符合我们特殊定义下的分析师投资标准。另一方面，许多考虑不周的企业则应被归类为非理性投机。同样，在金融领域，许多股票购买行为是在经过合理考量后进行的，可视为理性投机；但也有很多是在缺乏充分思考且出于不合理动机的情况下进行的，因此应被称为非理性投机；在极少数情况下，某只股票的质地与价格条件极为优越，使其内在风险降至最低，从而符合分析师投资的定义。

<!--en-->
In the field of general business most well-considered enterprises would belong in the class of intelligent speculations as well as representing “business investments” in the popular sense. If the risk of loss is very small—an exceptional occurrence—a particular business venture may qualify as an analyst’s investment in our special sense. On the other hand, many ill-conceived businesses must be called unintelligent speculations. Similarly, in the field of finance, a great deal of common-stock buying is done with reasonable care and may be called intelligent speculation; a great deal, also, is done upon inadequate consideration and for unsound reasons and thus must be called unintelligent; in the exceptional case a common stock may be bought on such attractive terms, qualitative and quantitative, as to set the inherent risk at a minimum and justify the title of analyst’s investment.

**投资成分与投机成分。** 无法被归类为“分析师的投资”的拟议购买行为自动属于投机类别。但有时，从不同角度看待此类购买并将支付价格分为投资成分与投机成分会更有用。因此，若以1939年通用电气股票的38美元平均价为例，分析师可能会认为，从严格的投资价值角度而言，每股25美元是合理的。剩余的每股13美元则代表了股市对该公司卓越长期前景的平均估值，其中或许还包含了对这家杰出企业的较强心理偏好。基于这样的分析，分析师会宣称通用电气的38美元股价中，每股约25美元为投资成分，每股约13美元为投机成分。如果这一观点成立，那么当股价在25美元或以下时，通用电气的普通股就完全构成“分析师的投资”；而高于该价格的买入者则应意识到，自己正在为该公司实际的投机可能性付费。⁷

<!--en-->
**Investment and Speculative Components.** A proposed purchase that cannot qualify as an “analyst’s investment” automatically falls into the speculative category. But at times it may be useful to view such a purchase somewhat differently and to divide the price paid into an investment and a speculative component. Thus the analyst, considering General Electric common at its average price of $38 in 1939, might conclude that up to, say, $25 per share is justified from the strict standpoint of investment value. The remaining $13 per share will represent the stock market’s average appraisal of the company’s excellent long-term prospects, including therein, perhaps, a rather strong psychological bias in favor of this outstanding enterprise. On the basis of such a study, the analyst would declare that the price of $38 for General Electric includes an investment component of some $25 per share and a speculative component of about $13 per share. If this is sound, it would follow that at a price of 25 or less, General Electric common would constitute an “analyst’s investment” completely; but above that price the buyer shouldrecognize that he is paying something for the company's very real speculative possibilities.⁷

## 投资价值、投机价值与内在价值。

<!--en-->
*Investment Value, Speculative Value, and Intrinsic Value.*

前文的讨论进一步扩展了第1章中关于“内在价值”概念的阐述，该章将内在价值定义为“由事实所支撑的价值”。需要明确的是，这种价值绝不仅限于“投资价值”——即总价值中的投资成分——只要这种投机价值是通过合理方式得出的，它也可以合理地包含相当大的投机成分。因此，只有当市场价格明显反映了非理性的投机行为时，才能说市场价格高于内在价值。

<!--en-->
The foregoing discussion suggests an amplification of what was said in Chap. 1 on the concept of “intrinsic value,” which was there defined as “value justified by the facts.” It is important to recognize that such value is by no means limited to “value for investment”—i.e., to the investment component of total value—but may properly include a substantial component of speculative value, provided that such speculative value is intelligently arrived at. Hence the market price may be said to exceed intrinsic value only when the market price is clearly the reflection of unintelligent speculation.

一般来说，评估某只普通股的投机因素是股票市场的职能，而非分析师的职能。在这一点上，正是市场而非分析师决定了内在价值。这种评估的范围可能非常广泛，正如我们之前所提到的，1933年J. I. Case公司的股票内在价值可能高达130，也可能低至30。在这两个极端数值之间的任何水平，都不得不接受每日都在变化的市场判断，将其视为对这只波动较大的股票内在价值的最佳估算。[^638]: ¹ *Dollars Behind Steel*，美国钢铁协会小册子，纽约，1939年。

<!--en-->
Generally speaking, it is the function of the stock market, and not of the analyst, to appraise the speculative factors in a given common-stock picture. To this important extent the market, not the analyst, determines intrinsic value. The range of such an appraisal may be very wide, as illustrated by our former suggestion that the intrinsic value of J. I. Case common in 1933 might conceivably have been as high as 130 or as low as 30. At any point between these broad limits it would have been necessary to accept the market's verdict—changeable as it was from day to day—as representing the best available determination of the intrinsic value of this volatile issue.
[^638]: ¹ *Dollars Behind Steel*, pamphlet of American Iron and Steel Institute, New York, 1939.
