(These structured debt securities are particularly complex, and it was mostly underestimation of the riskiness of sub-prime mortgage-backed securities that led to the Global Financial Crisis.)

20世纪70年代，低于投资级别的债券开始公开发行时，通常会附带“契约条款”：即发行方做出的承诺（或施加的限制），旨在保护债券持有人免受发行方可能采取的损害性行为的影响。但随着岁月推移，投资者对高风险债务的接受度逐渐提高，近期资本的大量流入又形成了卖方市场，迫使投资者通过接受更低收益率或承担更高风险来争夺提供融资的机会。在此过程中，新贷款中的契约条款大多被取消，这意味着贷款方的保护措施大幅减少。

<!--en-->
When below-investment-grade bonds began to be publicly issued in the 1970s, they usually carried “covenants”: representations from (or limitations on) the issuers that would protect bondholders from potentially deleterious actions on the issuers’ part. But investors became more comfortable with risky debt over the years, and more recently heavy inflows of capital created a seller’s market in which investors were forced to compete for the opportunity to provide financing by accepting lower yields or increased risk. In the process, covenants are mostly gone from new loans, meaning lenders came to enjoy less protection.

在结束关于我们所见变化的话题之前，我想提及其中最显著的一点：即贯穿当今大多数投资者整个投资生涯的利率下行趋势。20世纪70年代，我从银行申请了一笔个人贷款，利率比基准利率高出四分之三；我还保留着1980年通知我利率上升至22¼%的记录。40年后，也就是2020年，我竟然能以2%的利率借款。这一2000个基点的利率下降得益于该时期的低通胀水平。由于较低的利率意味着未来现金流的折现值更高，而且债券与其他资产的竞争减弱，从而提升了后者的价值，因此这一利率下降为所有投资者——不仅仅是固定收益领域的投资者——带来了巨大的利好。2021年至2022年，通货膨胀再度出现，导致债券及大多数其他资产的价格下跌。未来的读者会比我在撰写本文时更了解这一趋势的延续情况及其影响。

<!--en-->
Before I leave the topic of changes we’ve seen, I want to mention one of the most significant: the downtrend in interest rates that has prevailed over the working lives of most of today’s investors. In the 1970s, I took out a personal loan from a bank at “three-quarters over prime,” and I’ve framed the slip from 1980 notifying me that the interest rate had risen to 22¼%. Forty years later, in 2020, I was able to borrow at 2%. The 2,000-basis-point decline in rates was the result of the low level of inflation over the period. Because lower rates mean higher discounted values for future cash flows—and less competition from bonds against other assets, enhancing the value of the latter—this rate decline was a massive tailwind behind the returns enjoyed by all investors, not just those in fixed income. We saw the return of inflation in 2021–2022, and corresponding drops in the prices of bonds and most other assets. Readers in future years will know more about thecontinuation of this trend and its ramifications than I do as of this writing.

最后，如果你想紧跟固定收益市场的动态，就必须不断学习新的术语。我敢肯定，格雷厄姆和多德根本无法理解如今投资者所说的内容：

<!--en-->
Finally, if you’ve wanted to keep abreast of the fixed–income markets, you had to constantly learn new terminology. I’m confident Graham and Dodd would have no idea what today’s investors are saying:

“我做长久期策略”，意思是“我的投资组合的久期高于平均水平，也就是说我看好利率下降、债券价格上升的趋势。”

<!--en-->
“I’m long duration,” meaning “The duration of my portfolio is longer than average, meaning I’m betting that interest rates will fall and bond prices will rise.”

“我做短利差策略”，意思是“我认为高收益债券的收益率与国债收益率之间的利差——这一利差源于对企业信用风险的考量——未来会扩大。这意味着风险较高的债券价格将会下跌。”

<!--en-->
“I’m short spreads,” meaning “I believe the spread by which the yield on high yield bonds exceeds the yield on Treasury bonds—which results from perceived corporate credit risk—will increase in the future. That means the prices of risky bonds will fall.”

“我做信用多头策略”，意思是“我的债券投资组合中企业债的比例高于政府债，因为我相信经济增长和企业盈利的积极趋势会让企业表现更好。”

<!--en-->
“I’m long credit,” meaning “My bond portfolio is overweighted in corporate bonds relative to government bonds, meaning I think positive trends in economic growth and corporate profits will cause corporates to outperform.”

“我做利率交易”，意思是“我从事政府债务及相关产品的交易，比如通胀挂钩债券、期货、远期合约、期权、互换以及交换期权[别问了]。”

<!--en-->
“I trade rates,” meaning “I deal in government debt and anything related to it, such as inflation-indexed bonds, futures, forwards, options, swaps, and swaptions [don’t ask].”

# 回顾过去

<!--en-->
*LOOKING BACK*

在过去45年里，我有幸能够参与信用市场，并从中受益：首先是从那些其他人未能把握的市场机会中获利，其次是在我发现这些市场并投入资金后，随着它们逐渐普及而继续获得收益。这让我保持了稳定的工作，并获得了极大的精神满足感。

<!--en-->
I was exceptionally fortunate to participate in the credit markets over the last 45 years and to have benefited, first from the emergence of markets most others failed to capitalize on, and second from the popularization of these markets after I found them and staked my position. The result has been steady employment and untold intellectual satisfaction.

在面对这些看似充满风险的新兴市场时，我和橡树资本的合伙人决定建立一家注重风险控制、投资一致性、长期投资以及限制管理资本规模的公司。我们还坚持营造一种强调这些原则的企业文化。总而言之，我们试图提供一种“低风险选择”，让客户以较低的风险参与其中。橡树资本成立时的座右铭是“只要避开亏损项目，盈利项目自然会带来回报”，这一理念至今仍是我们的指引，即便我们现在增加了许多需要寻找盈利机会的“进取型”策略，风险意识依然被置于首要位置。

<!--en-->
In dealing with these emergent markets, with their appearance of riskiness, my Oaktree partners and I chose to build a firm that would emphasize risk control, consistency, long-term investment, and limits on the amount of capital we would manage. We also insisted on creating a culture thatwould emphasize these things. In sum, we tried to offer a “low-risk option,” giving clients a way to participate with less-than-full risk. Our motto at Oaktree’s founding was “if we avoid the losers, the winners will take care of themselves,” and that remains our lodestar, putting a high priority on risk consciousness even now that we’ve added a number of “aspirational” strategies that demand that winners be found.

对于在经济繁荣时期能取得怎样的业绩，我们并没有做过过高的承诺。毕竟在经济好的时候大家都能赚很多钱，我也从不认为有必要在经济好的时候追求超越平均水平的回报（因为这样做通常要求投资者承担高于平均水平的风险）。相反，我们更注重在经济低迷时期的超额表现：因为正是在那种时期，超额表现才真正至关重要。同样也是在经济低迷时期——通常伴随着大量债务违约——通过有针对性的筛选和精湛的信用研究，避免持有受负面影响的资产，才能最大程度地创造价值。

<!--en-->
We’ve made only modest claims regarding what our results would be in good times. After all, everyone makes a lot of money in good times, and I’ve never understood the need for outperformance in good times (given that pursuing it usually requires an investor to carry above-average risk). Instead, we’ve emphasized outperformance in bad times: it’s really then that outperformance is essential. It’s also in bad times—usually marked by large number of defaults—that selectivity and highly proficient credit research can best add value through the avoidance of holdings that are negatively affected.

我的另一个幸运之处在于，在利率下降40年、幅度达2000个基点的过程中，以及随之而来的信用资产牛市中，我一直是一名信用市场投资者。我并没有促成那次牛市，也没有预见到它，只是恰好在正确的时间进入了正确的市场。但利率下降带来的积极影响绝不能被低估，其带来的回报也不应被误判。

<!--en-->
Another way in which I’ve been fortunate was to have been an investor in credit over the course of the 40-year, 2,000-basis-point decline of interest rates and the resulting bull market in credit assets. I didn’t do anything to produce that bull market, and I didn’t foresee it; I was merely in the right market at the right time. But the salutary impact of declining interest rates must not be underestimated or the resulting returns misattributed.

回顾我和合伙人们投资的这段时期，我们本可以采取更激进的策略。我们可以承担更多风险，主动寻找更多优质投资机会，也愿意冒险投资一些风险较高的项目。我们本可以更加信任美联储有能力维持经济增长和市场稳定。考虑到这一时期整体投资环境相当温和，这样做很可能会带来更高的回报。不过，由于橡树资本在这方面不太可能改变策略，我恐怕没有机会知道这些方法在未来几年是否真的能带来成功。

<!--en-->
When I look back at the period in which my partners and I have invested, we could have been more aggressive than we were. We could have taken more risk. We could have actively pursued more winners and taken a chance on more iffy credits. We could have put more faith in the Fed to keep the economy growing and the markets aloft. Given how benign the investment climate turned out to be in this period overall, doing these things may well have led to higher returns. I’m unlikely to get a chance to find out if they will constitute a winning approach for the years ahead, however, as Oaktree isn’t likely to change its spots in this regard.

当前的各种有利条件确实共同使得过去45年的信贷市场成为了“最美好的时期”。信贷投资者受益于经济增长、违约率下降、通货膨胀率较低、利率呈下行趋势，以及信贷资产受欢迎程度的提升。未来的几年还会如此理想吗？这无从知晓。但我认为大家都能认同，鉴于目前利率已处于历史低位，进一步下降的空间不大，因此这一因素不会再带来显著利好。此外，与大多数其他市场一样，如今的信贷市场也变得更加“高效”，这意味着我们很难再像过去那样找到那么多划算的投资机会。正如我在回答有关宏观前景的大多数问题时所说：“走着瞧吧。”• • • 债券市场与投资的所有方面——事实上，也与人类活动的绝大多数领域一样——都发生了巨大变化，并且必将持续发展。为解决当下问题而写的操作指南或许能立即提供帮助，但它们不太可能长期保持相关性。另一方面，1940年版的《证券分析》蕴含着永恒的智慧，无论在写作时还是如今乃至未来都适用。更重要的是，它教会读者如何思考投资，而这比告诉他们该想什么更为重要。我相信它在未来多年仍将是投资的经典之作。[^810]：约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯，《就业、利息和货币通论》，伦敦：麦克米伦出版社，1936年，第153页。

<!--en-->
Prevailing conditions truly have combined to make the last 45 years in the credit market the “best of times.” Credit investors have benefited from economic growth, declining default rates, low inflation, the downtrend in interest rates, and the increased popularity of credit assets. Will the coming years be as kind? There’s no way to know. But I think we can all agree that we’re unlikely to see much more in the way of interest rate declines, given today’s historic lows, meaning there won’t be a significant tailwind from that source. In addition, the credit market, like most others, is now much more “efficient,” meaning it’ll be harder to find as many bargains as we did in the past. As I say in response to most questions about the macro future, “We’ll see.”
• • •
The market for debt securities, like all aspects of investing—and, in fact, most areas of human endeavor—has evolved greatly and is sure to continue to do so. How-to books written to treat the questions of the day may be immediately helpful, but they’re unlikely to remain relevant for long. On the other hand, the 1940 edition of *Security Analysis* contains wisdom for the ages, applicable at the time it was written as well as today and tomorrow. Importantly, it shows the reader how to think about investing, which is more valuable than what to think. I’m sure it will remain a bible of investing for years to come.
[^810]: 1 John Maynard Keynes, *The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money*, London: Macmillan, 1936, p. 153.

2 *洛杉矶时报杂志*，1991年4月7日。第六章

<!--en-->
2 *Los Angeles Times Magazine*, April 7, 1991.
CHAPTER 6

## 固定价值投资的选择

<!--en-->
*The Selection of Fixed-Value Investments*

在提出了按证券属性而非名称进行分类的建议后，我们现在将依次介绍适用于每类证券的选择原则与方法。我们之前已经提到，固定价值类包括：

<!--en-->
HAVING SUGGESTED a classification of securities by character rather than by title, we now take up in order the principles and methods of selection applicable to each group. We have already stated that the fixed-value group includes:

1. 高等级普通债券和优先股。
2. 高等级特权发行证券，其特权价值过于微小，不足以作为选择时的考量因素。
3. 通过担保或优先股地位而具备高级次优先证券属性的普通股。**对高级次优先股的基本态度。** 将优质优先股与高级债券归为同一类别，意味着这两种资产适用相同的投资态度和分析方法。此处未考虑优先股持有人的法定索赔权明显处于劣势这一因素，其逻辑在于，最佳投资的稳健性不应依赖于法律权利或救济手段，而应取决于企业充足的财务实力。这一观点可从投资者对国家饼干公司优先股的态度中得到印证——近40年来，该股票一直被认为具有与优质债券相同的*本质投资特性*。¹ **优先股在投资价值上通常不等于债券。** 但需立即指出的是，具有国家饼干公司优先股这般历史与地位的证券在所有优先股中所占比例极小。因此，我们绝非主张债券与优先股*总体上*具有同等的投资价值。相反，我们在后续章节中将详细论证，*平均*优先证券的等级应低于平均债券，而且投资大众往往过于轻易地接受优先股。这些证券中的大多数并未获得充分保护，无法*毫无疑虑地*确保持续派发股息。因此，它们应属于变动型或投机性高级证券（第二类），在这一类别中，债券与优先股之间的契约差异很可能变得极为重要。因此，必须严格区分典型的优先股与异常的优先股。只有后者才配被视为固定价值投资，并与优质债券享有同等的地位。为避免表述上的繁琐，在本讨论中我们将经常使用“投资债券”或简称“债券”来指代所有属于固定价值类别的证券。**债券投资合理吗？** 在本书1934年的版本中，我们认真探讨了前几年极端的金融与工业波动是否已经破坏了债券投资的基本逻辑这一问题。如果即便做出这些牺牲，投资者仍必须面对巨大的损失风险，那么限制收益并放弃所有投机获利机会是否值得？我们当时认为，1927–1933年的现象极其反常，根本无法为投资理论与实践提供合理的依据。后续的经验似乎证实了我们的观点，但债券购买者仍面临诸多不确定性，或许在很长一段时间内都无法恢复以往那种完全安全的感觉。债券价格创历史新高的情况……
1940) 在过去的二十年里曾发生过两次严重的价格暴跌，且目前还有一场大规模战争正在进行，这样的状况绝不能成为对未来抱有盲目乐观的理由。**债券形式本身缺乏吸引力：安全性的量化保障。**这种情况显然要求投资者、发行机构以及投资教材的作者以比以往更为审慎和严格的态度来选择债券。此前已经提到过，将债券的*形式*视为安全保障，甚至认为其风险低于股票，是存在危险的。与其像长期以来那样将债券主要与*安全性*联系在一起，不如从事实而非假设出发——即（普通）债券是一种*回报有限*的投资。作为放弃分享未来利润的交换，债券持有人能获得优先受偿权以及确定的还款承诺，而优先股持有人仅拥有优先权，却没有此类承诺。但无论是优先权还是承诺本身都并非*还款的保证*。这种保证取决于企业履行承诺的能力，必须通过考察其财务状况、经营记录及发展前景来判断。因此，正确选择债券的本质在于，为放弃分享利润而获得具体且令人信服的安全性依据。**重点在于避免损失。**我们将债券视为一种回报有限的承诺这一核心观念，引出了关于债券投资的另一个重要观点。由于首要任务应是避免损失，因此债券选择本质上是一门“否定艺术”——它是一个排除和拒绝的过程，而非寻找和接受的过程。在这方面，它与普通股的选择有着本质上的区别。潜在的普通股购买者会受到避免损失与获取利润这两种愿望大致同等程度的影响。错误地拒绝某只股票可能带来的后果，与错误地买入它一样严重。但只要投资者最终没有买入不良证券，他完全可以拒绝许多优质债券而几乎不会承担任何代价。因此，广义而言，在购买固定价值投资产品时并不存在过于挑剔或苛刻的问题。沃尔特·白芝浩对商业银行家提出的那句忠告同样适用于投资债券的选择：“如果有任何困难或疑点，就应该拒绝该证券。”² **选择固定价值型证券的四大原则。**在确立了这一总体方法后，我们现在可以提出四项更具针对性的原则，用于挑选具体的证券：I. *安全性的衡量标准不是特定的留置权或其他合同权利，而是发行方履行所有义务的能力。*³ II. *应在其处于经济低迷时期而非繁荣时期来评估这种能力。* III. *低下的安全性无法通过异常高的票面利率来弥补。* IV. *所有用于投资的债券选择都应遵循排除规则以及与储蓄银行投资管理法规相对应的具体量化标准。*基于上述原则的债券选择方法将与传统观念和方法有显著不同。不过，摒弃旧有观念并不意味着创新，而是认可并倡导那些在聪明且经验丰富的投资者中日益普及的观点。接下来的讨论旨在阐明这些新理念的性质及其合理性。⁴

<!--en-->
1. High-grade straight bonds and preferred stocks.
2. High-grade privileged issues, where the value of the privilege is too remote to count as a factor in selection.
3. Common stocks which through guaranty or preferred status occupy the position of a high-grade senior issue.
**Basic Attitude Toward High-Grade Preferred Stocks.** By placing gilt-edged preferred stocks and high-grade bonds in a single group, we indicate that the same investment attitude and the same general method of analysis are applicable to both types. The very definite inferiority of the preferred stockholders' legal claim is here left out of account, for the logical reason that the soundness of the best investments must rest not upon legal rights or remedies but upon ample financial capacity of the enterprise. Confirmation of this viewpoint is found in the investor's attitude toward such an issue as National Biscuit Company Preferred, which for nearly 40 years has been considered as possessing the same *essential investment character* as a good bond.¹
**Preferred Stocks Not Generally Equivalent to Bonds in Investment Merit.** But it should be pointed out immediately that issues with the history and standing of National Biscuit Preferred constitute a very small percentage of all preferredstocks. Hence, we are by no means asserting the investment
equivalence of bonds and preferred stocks *in general*. On the
contrary, we shall in a later chapter be at some pains to show
that the *average* preferred issue deserves a lower rank than the
average bond, and furthermore that preferred stocks have been
much too readily accepted by the investing public. The
majority of these issues have not been sufficiently well
protected to assure continuance of dividends *beyond any
reasonable doubt*. They belong properly, therefore, in the class
of variable or speculative senior issues (Group II), and in this
field the contractual differences between bonds and preferred
shares are likely to assume great importance. A sharp
distinction must, therefore, be made between the typical and
the exceptional preferred stock. It is only the latter which
deserves to rank as a fixed-value investment and to be viewed
in the same light as a good bond. To avoid awkwardness of
expression in this discussion we shall frequently use the terms
“investment bonds” or merely “bonds” to represent all
securities belonging to the fixed-value class.
**Is Bond Investment Logical?** In the 1934 edition of this
work we considered with some seriousness the question
whether or not the extreme financial and industrial
fluctuations of the preceding years had not impaired the
fundamental logic of bond investment. Was it worth while for
the investor to limit his income return and to forego all
prospect of speculative gain, if despite these sacrifices he must
still subject himself to serious risk of loss? We suggested in
reply that the phenomena of 1927–1933 were so completely
abnormal as to afford no fair basis for investment theory and
practice. Subsequent experience seems to have borne us out,
but there are still enough uncertainties facing the bond buyer
to banish, perhaps for a long time, his old sense of complete
security. The combination of a record high level for bonds (in
1940) with a history of two catastrophic price collapses in the
preceding twenty years and a major war in progress is not one
to justify airy confidence in the future.
**Bond Form Inherently Unattractive: Quantitative Assurance of Safety Essentials.** This situation clearly calls for a more critical and exacting attitude towards bondselection than was formerly considered necessary by investors, issuing houses, or authors of textbooks on investment. Allusion has already been made to the dangers inherent in the acceptance of the bond *form* as an assurance of safety, or even of smaller risk than is found in stocks. Instead of associating bonds primarily with the presumption of *safety* as has long been the practice—it would be sounder to start with what is not presumption but fact, *viz.*, that a (straight) bond is an investment with *limited return*. In exchange for limiting his participation in future profits, the bondholder obtains a prior claim and a definite promise of payment, while the preferred stockholder obtains only the priority, without the promise. But neither priority nor promise is itself an *assurance* of payment. This assurance rests in the ability of the enterprise to fulfill its promise, and must be looked for in its financial position, record, and prospects. The essence of proper bond selection consists, therefore, in obtaining specific and convincing factors of safety in compensation for the surrender of participation in profits.
**Major Emphasis on Avoidance of Loss.** Our primary conception of the bond as a commitment with limited return leads us to another important viewpoint toward bond investment. Since the chief emphasis must be placed on avoidance of loss, bond selection is primarily a negative art. It is a process of exclusion and rejection, rather than of search and acceptance. In this respect the contrast with common-stock selection is fundamental in character. The prospective buyer of a given common stock is influenced more or less equally by the desire to avoid loss and the desire to make a profit. The penalty for mistakenly rejecting the issue may conceivably be as great as that for mistakenly accepting it. But an investor may reject any number of good bonds with virtually no penalty at all, provided he does not eventually accept an unsound issue. Hence, broadly speaking, there is no such thing as being unduly captious or exacting in the purchase of fixed-value investments. The observation that Walter Bagehot addressed to commercial bankers is equally applicable to the selection of investment bonds. “If there is a difficulty or a doubt the security should be declined.”²
**Four Principles for the Selection of Issues of the Fixed-Value Type.** Having established this general approach to our problem, we may now state four additional principles of more specific character which are applicable to the selection of individual issues:
I. *Safety is measured not by specific lien or other contractual rights, but by the ability of the issuer to meet all of its obligations.*³
II. *This ability should be measured under conditions of depression rather than prosperity.*
III. *Deficient safety cannot be compensated for by an abnormally high coupon rate.*
IV. *The selection of all bonds for investment should be subject to rules of exclusion and to specific quantitative tests corresponding to those prescribed by statute to govern investments of savings banks.*
A technique of bond selection based on the above principles will differ in significant respects from the traditional attitude and methods. In departing from old concepts, however, this treatment represents not an innovation but the recognition and advocacy of viewpoints which have been steadily gaining ground among intelligent and experienced investors. The ensuing discussion is designed to make clear both the nature and the justification of the newer ideas.⁴

## I. 安全性不以留置权衡量，而以支付能力衡量

<!--en-->
*I. SAFETY NOT MEASURED BY LIEN BUT BY ABILITY TO PAY*

最根本的区别从一开始就显现出来。过去，人们主要关注的是具体的担保物，即债券所拥有的留置权的标的物的性质及其预期价值。但从我们的角度来看，这一因素其实相当次要；最重要的应是债务企业的实力与健康状况。这里存在着两种截然不同的观点：一方面，债券被视为对*财产*的索赔权；另一方面，则被视为对*企业*的索赔权。

<!--en-->
The basic difference confronts us at the very beginning. In the past the primary emphasis was laid upon the specific security, *i.e.*, the character and supposed value of the property on which the bonds hold a lien. From our standpoint this consideration is quite secondary; the dominant element must be the strength and soundness of the obligor enterprise. There is here a clearcut distinction between two points of view. On the onehand the bond is regarded as a claim against *property*; on the other hand, as a claim against a *business*.

旧有的观念在最初的设计与目的上其实颇具逻辑性。它旨在通过为债券持有人提供充分的担保，使其在企业破产时能够获得补偿，从而让其免受企业经营风险的威胁。如果企业无力偿还其债权，债券持有人便可接管抵押财产并从中获取赔偿。这种安排若能实现本会非常理想，但现实中却很少可行。其原因有三：

<!--en-->
The older view was logical enough in its origin and purpose. It desired to make the bondholder independent of the risks of the business by giving him ample security on which to levy in the event that the enterprise proved a failure. If the business became unable to pay his claim, he could take over the mortgaged property and pay himself out of that. This arrangement would be excellent if it worked, but in practice it rarely proves to be feasible. For this there are three reasons:

1. 企业破产时财产价值的缩水。
2. 行使债券持有人所谓法定权利的困难。
3. 破产清算过程中出现的延误及其他不利因素。**留置权无法防止价值缩水。**将抵押留置权视为一种独立于企业经营状况之外的保障措施，在大多数情况下纯属谬论。在典型情况下，抵押财产的价值在很大程度上取决于企业的盈利能力。债券持有人通常会对铁路线、工厂建筑与设备、发电厂及其他公用设施，或是桥梁或酒店建筑拥有留置权。这些财产很少能用于其原始设计之外的用途。因此，一旦企业破产，其固定资产的变现价值往往会大幅缩水。正因如此，那种以抵押财产的原始成本或评估价值作为吸引人们购买债券的手段的做法，完全是具有误导性的。抵押资产的价值只有在违约时才具有实际意义，而在这类情况下，账面数值几乎总是不可靠且无关紧要的。1931年该铁路建成不久后，Seaboard-All Florida Railway的第一顺位抵押贷款证券就以1美分兑换1美元的价格出售，便是例证。⁵

<!--en-->
1. The shrinkage of property values when the business fails.
2. The difficulty of asserting the bondholders' supposed legal rights.
3. The delays and other disadvantages incident to a receivership.
**Lien Is No Guarantee Against Shrinkage of Values.** The conception of a mortgage lien as a guaranty of protection independent of the success of the business itself is in most cases a complete fallacy. In the typical situation, the value of the pledged property is vitally dependent on the earning power of the enterprise. The bondholder usually has a lien on a railroad line, or on factory buildings and equipment, or on power plants and other utility properties, or perhaps on a bridge or hotel structure. These properties are rarely adaptable to uses other than those for which they were constructed. Hence if the enterprise proves a failure its fixed assets ordinarily suffer an appalling shrinkage in realizable value. For this reason the established practice of stating the original cost or appraised value of the pledged property as an inducement to purchase bonds is entirely misleading. The value of pledged assets assumes practical importance only in the event of default, and in any such event the book figures are almost invariably found to be unreliable and irrelevant. This may be illustrated by Seaboard-All Florida Railway First Mortgage 6s, selling in 1931 at 1 cent on the dollar shortly after completion of the road.⁵

# 难以切实行使留置权的法定权利

<!--en-->
*Impracticable to Enforce Basic Legal Rights of Lien*

**抵押权人。**在抵押财产的实际价值恰好等于债务金额的情况下，债券持有人很少能获得该财产的占有权并对其进行变现。必须认识到，企业债券违约后的处理程序与私人房产抵押贷款的常规程序已存在显著差异。理论上，两种情况下留置权持有人的基本法律权利应当是相同的。但实践中，只要这些资产有可能具有高于其债权的公允价值，法院就极不愿意允许企业债券持有人通过行使留置权来接管相关财产。⁶显然，让那些对财产拥有潜在利益却无力保护它的股东或次级债券持有人受损被视为不公平的行为。由于这种做法，除非抵押财产当时的价值远低于债权金额，否则债券持有人几乎从未真正获得过该抵押财产的所有权。在大多数情况下，他们只能在公司重组后获得新的证券。有时利息拖欠问题可以得到解决，债券发行也会恢复正常。⁷在极为罕见的情况下，违约的债券才可能最终得到全额偿付，但也需要经历漫长的拖延过程。⁸**拖延令人困扰。**这种拖延构成了将抵押财产作为债券投资保障的第三个弊端。抵押资产的价值相对于留置权金额越高，通过强制执行接管这些资产就越困难，同时要在各类债券和股票之间实现“公平”的利益分配也需要更长的时间。让我们来看看破产清算情况下对债券持有人最为有利的情况：他持有的可能是金额相对较小的第一顺位抵押贷款，其后则是一项导致公司破产的重大次级留置权。第一顺位抵押贷款持有人的地位可能十分稳固，以至于他根本不存在最终遭受损失的风险。然而，公司的财务困境通常会对其所有证券的市场价格产生负面影响，即便那些实际价值似乎并未受损的证券也不例外。随着破产清算进程的拖延，市场下跌的趋势会愈发严重，因为投资者天生就不愿意在局势动荡时买入资产。最终，第一顺位抵押贷款债券或许能在重组后不受影响地存续下来，但在那段漫长而艰难的时期里，持有者始终面临着所持资产估值大幅缩水的问题，同时对最终结果也难免心存疑虑与担忧。密苏里、堪萨斯和德克萨斯铁路公司第一系列4期债券以及布鲁克林联合高架铁路公司第一系列5期债券就是此类情况的典型例子。⁹关于破产清算与重组实务，尤其是其对债券持有人的影响，将在后续章节中进行更详细的探讨。

<!--en-->
**Holder.** In cases where the mortgaged property is actually worth as much as the debt, the bondholder is rarely allowed to take possession and realize upon it. It must be recognized that the procedure following default on a corporation bond has come to differ materially from that customary in the case of a mortgage on privately owned property. The basic legal rights of the lien holder are supposedly the same in both situations. But in practice we find a very definite disinclination on the part of the courts to permit corporate bondholders to take over properties by foreclosing on their liens, if there is any possibility that these assets may have a fair value in excess of their claim.⁶ Apparently it is considered unfair to wipe out stockholders or junior bondholders who have a potential interest in the property but are not in a position to protect it. As a result of this practice, bondholders rarely, if ever, come into actual possession of the pledged property unless its value at the time is substantially less than their claim. In most cases they are required to take new securities in a reorganized company. Sometimes the default in interest is cured and the issue reinstated.⁷ On exceedingly rare occasions a defaulted issue may be paid off in full, but only after a long and vexing delay.⁸
**Delays Are Wearisome.** This delay constitutes the third objection to relying upon the mortgaged property as protection for a bond investment. The more valuable the pledged assets in relation to the amount of the lien, the more difficult it is to take them over under foreclosure, and the longer the time required to work out an “equitable” division of interest among the various bond and stock issues. Let us consider the most favorable kind of situation for a bondholder in the event of receivership. He would hold a comparatively small first mortgage followed by a substantial junior lien, the requirements of which have made the company insolvent. It may well be that the strength of the first-mortgage bondholder’s position is such that at no time is there any real chance of eventual loss to him. Yet the financial difficulties of the company usually have a depressing effect on the market price of all its securities, even those presumably unimpaired inreal value. As the receivership drags on, the market decline becomes accentuated, since investors are constitutionally averse to buying into a troubled situation. Eventually the first-mortgage bonds may come through the reorganization undisturbed, but during a wearisome and protracted period the owners have faced a severe impairment in the quoted value of their holdings and at least some degree of doubt and worry as to the outcome. Typical examples of such an experience can be found in the case of Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railway Company First 4s and Brooklyn Union Elevated Railroad First 5s.⁹ The subject of receivership and reorganization practice, particularly as they affect the bondholder, will receive more detailed consideration in a later chapter.

**基本原则是避免麻烦。**上述讨论应能支持我们的观点：债券购买者的首要目标必须是避免麻烦，而非在出现麻烦时寻求自我保护。即便在特定留置权确实能带来实际好处的情况下，这种好处也是在违背“固定价值”投资本质的条件下实现的。鉴于破产清算几乎总会伴随市场价格的急剧下跌，投资者不得不求助于债券契约这一事实本身，就表明他的投资是不明智或不幸的。抵押财产所提供的保护充其量也只能减轻他的错误带来的后果。

<!--en-->
**Basic Principle Is to Avoid Trouble.** The foregoing discussion should support our emphatic stand that the primary aim of the bond buyer must be to avoid trouble and not to protect himself in the event of trouble. Even in the cases where the specific lien proves of real advantage, this benefit is realized under conditions which contravene the very meaning of *fixed-value* investment. In view of the severe decline in market price almost invariably associated with receivership, the mere fact that the investor must have recourse to his indenture indicates that his investment has been unwise or unfortunate. The protection that the mortgaged property offers him can constitute at best a mitigation of his mistake.

**这一基本原则的推论。**1. **无留置权影响较小。**从原则一可以得出若干具有重要现实意义的推论。由于在选择高等级债券时特定留置权的重要性较低，因此没有留置权的影响也同样微小。由实力强劲的公司发行的无担保债券，即信用债，完全有能力支付其利息，其被接受的几率几乎与有抵押担保的债券相当。此外，强势企业的信用债无疑比弱势公司的抵押债券是更稳健的投资选择。例如，没有任何第一顺位抵押的债券，其投资评级能优于1961年到期的新泽西标准石油公司信用债3期。通过查看债券列表就会发现，那些没有优先担保债务的公司发行的信用债，在投资属性上至少可与普通抵押债券相媲美，因为企业必须具备较高的信用评级才能通过无担保长期债券获得资金。¹¹

<!--en-->
**Corollaries from This First Principle.** 1. *Absence of Lien of Minor Consequence.* From Principle I there follow a number of corollaries with important practical applications. Since specific lien is of subordinate importance in the choice of high-grade bonds, the absence of lien is also of minor consequence. The debenture,¹⁰ i.e., unsecured, obligations of a strong corporation, amply capable of meeting its interest charges, may qualify for acceptance almost as readily as a bond secured by mortgage. Furthermore the debentures of a strong enterprise are undoubtedly sounder investments than the mortgage issues of a weak company. No first-lien bond, for example, enjoys a better investment rating than Standard Oil of New Jersey Debenture 3s, due 1961. An examination of the bond list will show that the debenture issues of companieshaving no secured debt ahead of them will rank in investment character at least on a par with the average mortgage bond, because an enterprise must enjoy a high credit rating to obtain funds on its unsecured long-term bond.¹¹

2. *购买稳健企业中收益最高的债券的理论*。由此可推，如果某企业的任何债券都符合固定价值投资的条件，那么该企业的所有债券也都应如此。换言之，如果一家公司的次级债券并不安全，其第一抵押债券也就无法成为理想的固定价值投资对象。因为若第二抵押债券都不安全，说明该公司本身实力薄弱，而一般来说，实力薄弱的企业不可能拥有高等级的债券。因此，理论上正确的债券投资步骤应是：首先挑选出符合所有实力与稳健性标准的公司，然后再购买其收益最高的债券，这通常意味着购买其次级债券而非第一抵押债券。假设我们在选择企业时从不犯错，这一方法在实践中会表现得非常理想。然而，出错的可能性越大，为了降低资本价值的潜在损失而牺牲收益的理由也就越充分。但我们必须认识到，债券购买者选择收益较低的 первоначальный抵押债券，实际上是在表明对自己对企业稳健性的判断缺乏信心——如果这种态度持续下去，甚至会让人质疑其是否应该对该企业的任何债券进行投资。*示例*：为说明这一点，让我们以库达希包装公司1946年到期的第一抵押5英镑债券，以及同公司1937年到期的5.5英镑债券为例。1932年6月，前者以面值的95%价格出售，收益约为5.5%，而后者则以面值的59%价格出售，到期时的收益超过20%。只有当投资者坚信该公司能够保持偿付能力并保持相对繁荣时，才有可能以接近面值的价格购买这些收益为5%的债券，否则这些债券的市场价格无疑会大幅下跌。但如果投资者对库达希公司的未来充满信心，他为何不购买债券来获得更高的回报呢？唯一的答案是，投资者希望在自己的判断出现错误、公司陷入困境时，能获得第一抵押债券带来的更强的保护。在这种情况下，作为第一抵押债券的持有者，他的损失可能会比持有次级债券要少。即便如此，也需指出：如果库达希包装公司遭遇了菲斯克橡胶公司那样的困境，其第一抵押债券的市场价值跌幅将与债券的跌幅一样大；因为在1932年4月，菲斯克橡胶公司的第一抵押8英镑债券的售价低至17，而无担保的5.5%债券的售价仅为12。无论如何，显然那些偏好库达希公司第一抵押5英镑债券的投资者，只是为了获得*部分*损失保障，就每年支付约15%的额外成本（即收益差）。基于此，他们所付出的代价显然远远超过了所得回报。由此得出的结论是：要么不要投资库达希公司的债券，要么就以高得多的收益购买其次级债券。¹² 这一规则适用于一般情况，即当第一抵押债券以固定价值价格（如接近面值）出售，而同公司的次级债券却能带来更高收益时。¹³
3. *除非次级债券具有显著优势，否则应优先考虑第一抵押债券*。显然，只有当次级债券在收益回报方面具有显著优势时，才值得优先考虑。如果第一抵押债券的收益仅略低一些，那么为防范意外风险而支付少量的保险费无疑是明智之举。*示例*：阿奇森-托皮卡和圣达菲铁路公司1995年到期的普通（第一）4英镑债券与调整（第二抵押）4英镑债券的相对市场价格便可以说明这一点。**阿奇森普通4英镑债券与调整4英镑债券在不同日期的股价**在1924年之前，阿奇森普通4英镑债券的售价通常比调整4英镑债券高出约7到10个点，且收益低约0.5%。由于这两种债券都被视为绝对安全，因此以低10%的成本购买次级债券本更为合理。1923年后，这种观点逐渐占据上风，两者之间的价格差距不断缩小。1930年及1931年的部分时间里，次级债券的售价多次与普通4英镑债券几乎相同。这种情况比1922–1923年的巨大价差更为不合理，因为即便两种抵押债券都被视为绝对安全，其价格和收益上的优势也微不足道，不足以成为选择次级债券的理由。

<!--en-->
2. *The Theory of Buying the Highest Yielding Obligation of a Sound Company.* It follows also that if any obligation of an enterprise deserves to qualify as a fixed-value investment, then all its obligations must do so. Stated conversely, if a company's junior bonds are not safe, its first-mortgage bonds are not a desirable fixed-value investment. For if the second mortgage is unsafe the company itself is weak, and generally speaking there can be no high-grade obligations of a weak enterprise. The theoretically correct procedure for bond investment, therefore, is first to select a company meeting every test of strength and soundness, and then to purchase its highest yielding obligation, which would usually mean its junior rather than its first-lien bonds. Assuming no error were ever made in our choice of enterprises, this procedure would work out perfectly well in practice. The greater the chance of mistake, however, the more reason to sacrifice yield in order to reduce the potential loss in capital value. But we must recognize that in favoring the lower yielding first-mortgage issue, the bond buyer is in fact expressing a lack of confidence in his own judgment as to the soundness of the business—which, if carried far enough, would call into question the advisability of his making an investment in *any* of the bonds of the particular enterprise.
*Example:* As an example of this point, let us consider the Cudahy Packing Company First Mortgage 5s, due 1946, and the Debenture 5½s of the same company, due 1937. In June 1932 the First 5s sold at 95 to yield about 5½%, whereas the junior 5½s sold at 59 to yield over 20% to maturity. The purchase of the 5% bonds at close to par could only be justified by a confident belief that the company would remain solvent and reasonably prosperous, for otherwise the bonds would undoubtedly suffer a severe drop in market price. But if the investor has confidence in the future of Cudahy, why should he not buy the debenture issue and obtain anenormously greater return on his money? The only answer can be that the investor wants the superior protection of the first mortgage in the event his judgment proves incorrect and the company falls into difficulties. In that case he would probably lose less as the owner of the first-mortgage bonds than through holding the junior issue. Even on this score it should be pointed out that if by any chance Cudahy Packing Company were to suffer the reverses that befell Fisk Rubber Company, the loss in market value of the first-mortgage bonds would be fully as great as those suffered by the debentures; for in April 1932 Fisk Rubber Company First 8s were selling as low as 17 against a price of 12 for the unsecured 5½% Notes. It is clear, at any rate, that the investor who favors the Cudahy first-lien 5s is paying a premium of about 15% per annum (the difference in yield) for only a *partial* insurance against loss. On this basis he is undoubtedly giving up too much for what he gets in return. The conclusion appears inescapable either that he should make no investment in Cudahy bonds or that he should buy the junior issue at its enormously higher yield.¹² This rule may be laid down as applying to the general case where a first-mortgage bond sells at a fixed-value price (e.g., close to par) and junior issues of the same company can be bought to yield a much higher return.¹³
3. *Senior Liens Are to Be Favored, Unless Junior Obligations Offer a Substantial Advantage.* Obviously a junior lien should be preferred only if the advantage in income return is substantial. Where the first-mortgage bond yields only slightly less, it is undoubtedly wise to pay the small insurance premium for protection against unexpected trouble.
*Example:* This point is illustrated by the relative market prices of Atchison Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company General (first) 4s and Adjustment (second mortgage) 4s, both of which mature in 1995.
**Price of Atchison General 4s and Adjustment 4s at Various Dates**Prior to 1924 the Atchison General 4s sold usually at about 7 to 10 points above the Adjustment 4s and yielded about ½% less. Since both issues were considered safe without question, it would have been more logical to purchase the junior issue at its 10% lower cost. After 1923 this point of view asserted itself, and the price difference steadily narrowed. During 1930 and part of 1931 the junior issue sold on numerous occasions at practically the same price as the General 4s. This relationship was even more illogical than the unduly wide spread in 1922–1923, since the advantage of the Adjustment 4s in price and yield was too negligible to warrant accepting a junior position, even assuming unquestioned safety for both liens.

在1932年6月债券市场情绪低迷的背景下，利差扩大至14点以上，这一显而易见的规律便得到了有力的印证。由于相关记录出现在1934年，可以推断两种债券之间的合理利差应在5点左右，而当利差大幅扩大或几乎消失时，便会出现以一种债券交换另一种债券的良机。

<!--en-->
Within a very short time this rather obvious truth was brought home strikingly by the widening of the spread to over 14 points during the demoralized bond-market conditions of June 1932. As the record appeared in 1934, it could be inferred that a reasonable differential between the two issues would be about 5 points and that either a substantial widening or a virtual disappearance of the spread would present an opportunity for a desirable exchange of one issue for another.

正如我们的表格所示，1934年和1936年确实出现了两次这样的机会。

<!--en-->
Two such opportunities did in fact appear in 1934 and 1936, as shown in our table.

但这个例子更有助于说明变化这一普遍存在的因素，以及在进行债券分析时必须将其考虑在内的必要性。到1937年，阿奇逊公司的盈利仍未能恢复到接近正常水平，且按照保守标准衡量，其利息保障倍数也明显不足，这些情况本应提醒投资者：次级债券中的“调整”（即或有）因素绝不能被忽视。因此，在之前利息安全从未成问题的情况下看似合理的定价关系，在新环境下已不可依赖。1938年，糟糕的盈利状况迫使该公司推迟调整债券的5月1日利息支付，导致其价格跌至75¼，利差扩大至24点。尽管后来利息已全部支付，且价格在1939年回升至96，但对这类债券仍采用1932年之前的标准显然十分不明智。

<!--en-->
But this example is of further utility in illustrating the all-pervasive factor of change and the necessity of taking it into account in bond analysis. By 1937 the failure of Atchison's earnings to recover within striking distance of its former normal, and the actual inadequacy of the margin above interest requirements as judged by conservative standards, should have warned the investor that the “adjustment” (i.e., contingent) element in the junior issue could not safely be ignored. Thus a price relationship that was logical at a time when safety of interest was never in question could not be relied upon under the new conditions. In 1938 the poor earnings actually compelled the road to defer the May 1 interest payment on the adjustment bonds, as a result of which their price fell to 75¼ and the spread widened to 24 points. Although the interest was later paid in full and the price recovered to 96 in 1939, it would seem quite unwise for the investor to apply pre-1932 standards to this bond issue.

选择公司*X*的次级抵押债券而非公司*Y*的第一顺位抵押债券，可能有以下两个理由：

<!--en-->
A junior lien of Company *X* may be selected in preference to a first-mortgage bond of Company *Y*, on one of two bases:

1. 公司*X*的全部债务得到充分保障，且该次级抵押债券的收益率远高于公司*Y*的债券；或者
2. 如果收益率没有显著优势，那么公司*X*的全部债务所获得的保障程度必须远远优于公司*Y*。*示例2：*

<!--en-->
1. The protection for the total debt of Company *X* is adequate and the yield of the junior lien is substantially higher than that of the Company *Y* issue; or
2. If there is no substantial advantage in yield, then the indicated protection for the total debt of Company *X* must be considerably better than that of Company *Y*.

* 平均结果大致相同。当美国天然气电力公司的总负债覆盖率明显更高时，即便两者售价相近，也有理由选择其次级债券而非太平洋电力照明公司的第一抵押贷款证券。¹⁴ **“基础债券”的特殊地位**。在铁路领域，通常认为所谓的“基础债券”具有特殊的投资属性。这类债券发行规模相对较小，以债务人对系统中关键部分的留置权作为担保，之后往往还会有一系列“整体抵押”。基础债券通常享有第一留置权，但如果更高级别的债券规模也相对较小，它也可能属于第二甚至第三抵押的债券。*示例*：纽约伊利铁路的第三抵押4½分券，到期日为1938年，其优先级低于之前针对伊利铁路主干线关键部分设置的两项小型留置权；在这些留置权之后还有四项针对该铁路系统的连续整体抵押，因此这类债券一直享有基础债券的优惠地位。人们认为，无论整个铁路系统发生何种变化，此类债券都是完全安全的。它们几乎总是在重组过程中毫发无损；即使在破产管理期间，由于涉及金额相对较少，利息支付通常也会照常进行。不过，如果整个系统陷入无力偿债状态，这类债券的市场价值仍可能出现大幅下跌。*示例*：纽约伊利铁路的第三4½分券（曾在1923年和1933年自愿延长到期日），在伊利铁路两个月前破产后，其本金和利息于1938年3月出现违约，投标价格一度跌至61。然而，截至1939年底提交的各项重组计划都规定要全额偿还该债券的本金和利息。芝加哥与伊利诺伊东部合并铁路的6分券，到期日为1934年，最终在1940年全额偿付，同时还按4%的利率继续支付利息——但在此之前其价格已于1933年跌至32。密苏里太平洋铁路的第一4分券、第二5分券以及密苏里太平洋铁路的第三4分券，它们的原到期日均被延长至1938年，属于密苏里太平洋铁路系统的基础债券。在1915年的破产管理期间，它们仍能持续获得利息且未受影响。1933年第二次破产之后，它们继续获得利息直至到期日，到期时本金出现违约，但利息支付一直持续到1939年。各项重组计划实际上都为这些债券提供了保障，让它们成为新公司具有优先留置权且利率固定的债务。但从1931年起，这三类债券的价格分别低至65、60和53。不过，其他曾被视为基础债券的债券在系统无力偿债后表现则没那么好。*示例*：密尔沃基、斯帕塔和西北铁路的第一4分券，到期日为1947年，属于芝加哥与西北铁路的基础债券，多年来其价格几乎与同年到期的联合太平洋铁路第一4分券持平。然而，在芝加哥与西北铁路进入破产管理阶段后，该债券在1935年就出现了利息违约，其价格甚至在1939年跌至极低的$8\frac{1}{8}$。从上述情况来看，*在某些情况下*，基础债券可被视为我们“除非公司状况良好，否则债券也不可靠”这一规则的例外。这类债券大多由机构或大型投资者持有。（同样的情况也可能适用于公用事业控股公司旗下运营子公司的某些第一抵押贷款债券。）对于这类铁路债券而言，所覆盖线路的位置及其战略价值至关重要。 针对系统中非核心且无盈利价值的部分的优先抵押债券，有时也被称为“部门性留置权”，但并不符合我们此前所定义的真正底层债券的标准。那些位于不利位置的里程相关优先抵押债权，在重组过程中往往会比那些表面上看似次级的全面抵押债券获得更差的待遇。*示例：* 应于1938年到期的联合太平洋铁路中央支线第一系列4美元债券，据称是用于偿还密苏里太平洋铁路第一系列及再融资抵押债券的“底层”资产，而后者正是用于清偿前者。然而，截至1939年底提交的各项重组计划，对密苏里太平洋铁路第一系列及再融资5美元债券的待遇，都要优于那些表面上看似优先级的中央支线债券。实际上，要事先区分哪些底层债券能在重组中完好无损，哪些会遭受严重处理，并非易事。因此，普通投资者最好将这类债券排除在考虑范围之外，坚持“只有实力雄厚的公司才能拥有优质债券”的原则。[^868]：1 在美国金融实践中，“债券”一词的含义为“无担保债券或票据”。出于某些不明原因，这一名称有时也被用于其他类型的证券，但似乎并无特殊含义。历史上出现过不少“有担保债券”，例如应于1950年到期的芝加哥先驱报与审查报有担保债券6美元\frac{1}{2}系列，以及应于1953年到期的孤星天然气公司债券3美元\frac{1}{2}系列。此外，还有许多优先股也被称作债券优先股或简称为债券股，例如1939年发行的杜邦公司债券股；1927年发行的通用雪茄公司优先债券股。有时，那些原本属于无担保债券的证券，后来通过保护性契约的设定获得了特定担保，例如第19章中提到的纽约、纽黑文和哈特福德铁路公司债券。另一个例子是1933年进行重组的福克斯新英格兰剧院公司的6美元\frac{1}{2}系列债券，这些债券通过获得同一家公司的优先抵押债券作为担保，而这些抵押债券则是由于剧院业主无法履行未来收益保障承诺而被其放弃的。需要注意的是，“债券”与“票据”之间并无明确区别，唯一的差异在于后者通常指期限相对较短的债务，即发行后最多十年左右到期的债务。11 1935年至1939年的企业债券融资情况充分证明了这一点。在那几年里，只有高等级债券才能出售，而所有债券中的绝大部分都是*债券*。12 两批库达希公司的债券均在$102\frac{1}{2}$1935年完成了偿付。 13 在极少数情况下，如果某种高级证券拥有异常优先的地位——*例如*，某种根深蒂固的铁路债券——则可以为此规则设定例外。（第6章）14 1937年，Pacific Power and Light 5s的最低价格为51，而American Gas and Electric债券的最低价格为104。第7章

* Average results approximately the same.
The appreciably higher coverage of total charges by American Gas and Electric would have justified preferring itsjunior bonds to the first-mortgage issue of Pacific Power and Light, when both were selling at about the same price.¹⁴
**Special Status of “Underlying Bonds.”** In the railroad field an especial investment character is generally supposed to attach to what are known as “underlying bonds.” These represent issues of relatively small size secured by a lien on especially important parts of the obligor system, and often followed by a series of “blanket mortgages.” The underlying bond usually enjoys a first lien, but it may be a second- or even a third-mortgage issue, provided the senior issues are also of comparatively small magnitude.
*Example:* New York and Erie Railroad Third Mortgage Extended ⁴¹/₂s, due 1938, are junior to two small prior liens covering an important part of the Erie Railroad’s main line. They are followed by four successive blanket mortgages on the system, and they have regularly enjoyed the favored status of an underlying bond.
Bonds of this description have been thought to be entirely safe, regardless of what happens to the system as a whole. They have almost always come through reorganization unscathed; and even during a receivership interest payments are usually continued as a matter of course, largely because the sum involved is proportionately so small. They are not exempt, however, from fairly sharp declines in market value if insolvency overtakes the system.
*Examples:* In the case of New York and Erie Third ⁴¹/₂s (which had been voluntarily extended on maturity in 1923 and again in 1933), principal and interest were defaulted in March 1938, following the bankruptcy of the Erie two months earlier. The bid price declined to as low as 61. However, the various reorganization plans filed to the end of 1939 all provided for the payment of principal and interest in full on this issue.
Chicago and Eastern Illinois Consolidated 6s, due 1934, were finally paid off in full in 1940, with further interest at 4% —but not until their price had fallen as low as 32 in 1933.
Pacific Railway of Missouri First 4s and Second 5s and Missouri Pacific Railway Third 4s, all extended from theiroriginal maturities to 1938, are underlying bonds of the Missouri Pacific system. They continued to receive interest and were left undisturbed in the receivership of 1915. Following the second bankruptcy in 1933, they continued to receive interest until their maturity date. At that time payment of principal was defaulted, but interest payments were continued through 1939. The various reorganization plans virtually provided for these bonds in full, by offering them prior-lien, fixed-interest obligations of the new company. But since 1931, the price of these three issues has been as low as 65, 60, and 53, respectively.
Other bonds, however, once regarded as underlying issues, have not fared so well following insolvency.
*Example:* Milwaukee, Sparta and Northwestern First 4s, due 1947, ranked as an underlying bond of the Chicago and North Western Railway, and for many years their price was not far below that of the premier Union Pacific First 4s, due the same year. Yet the receivership of the Chicago and North Western was followed by default of interest on this issue in 1935 and collapse of its price to the abysmal low of $8\frac{1}{8}$ as late as 1939.
From the foregoing it would appear that *in some cases* underlying bonds may be viewed as exceptions to our rule that a bond is not sound unless the company is sound. For the most part such bonds are owned by institutions or large investors. (The same observations may apply to certain first-mortgage bonds of operating subsidiaries of public-utility holding-company systems.)
In railroad bonds of this type, the location and strategic value of the mileage covered are of prime importance. First-mortgage bonds on nonessential and unprofitable parts of the system, referred to sometimes as “divisional liens,” are not true underlying bonds in the sense that we have just used the term. Divisional first liens on poorly located mileage may receive much less favorable treatment in a reorganization than blanket mortgage bonds ostensibly junior to them.
*Example:* Central Branch Union Pacific Railway First 4s, due 1938, were said to “underly” the Missouri Pacific Firstand Refunding mortgage, which provided for their retirement. Yet the reorganization plans presented to the end of 1939 all offered better treatment for the Missouri Pacific First and Refunding 5s than for the ostensibly senior Central Branch bonds.
As a practical matter it is not so easy to distinguish in advance between the underlying bonds that come through reorganization unscathed and those which suffer drastic treatment. Hence the ordinary investor may be well advised to leave such issues out of his calculations and stick to the rule that only strong companies have strong bonds.

CHAPTER 7

# 固定价值投资的选择：第二与第三原则

<!--en-->
*The Selection of Fixed-Value Investments: Second and Third Principles*

## II. 债券应于经济衰退时期购买

<!--en-->
*II. BONDS SHOULD BE BOUGHT ON A DEPRESSION BASIS*

“优质投资必须能够抵御困境”这一规则显然不言而喻，堪称真理。任何债券在环境良好时都可能表现良好；唯有在经济衰退的严峻考验下，强健债券相较于弱质债券的优势才会显现并变得至关重要。正因如此，谨慎的投资者历来更青睐那些已证明具备在顺境与逆境中都能生存能力的成熟企业发行的债券。

<!--en-->
The rule that a sound investment must be able to withstand adversity seems self-evident enough to be termed a truism. Any bond can do well when conditions are favorable; it is only under the acid test of depression that the advantages of strong over weak issues become manifest and vitally important. For this reason prudent investors have always favored the obligations of old-established enterprises which have demonstrated their ability to come through bad times as well as good.

**基于行业特性或安全缓冲度的安全性假设。** 对债券能否抵御经济衰退的信心可能源于两种不同的理由。投资者可能认为该企业不会面临盈利能力的急剧下降，或者认为其安全缓冲度足够大，即便出现下降也不会带来风险。轻工业与电力公司发行的债券主要因第一种理由受到青睐，而美国钢铁公司子公司发行的债券则因第二种理由受青睐。前者是凭借行业的*特性*，后者则是依靠安全缓冲度的*程度*来支撑购买决策。在这两种观点中，试图规避经济衰退风险的那种更符合普通债券投资者的需求——与依赖企业的财务实力来帮助其债券度过业绩不佳的时期相比，投资于具备抗衰退能力的企业似乎要简单得多。

<!--en-->
**Presumption of Safety Based upon Either the Character of the Industry or the Amount of Protection.** Confidence in the ability of a bond issue to weather depression may be based on either of two different reasons. The investor may believe that the particular business will be immune from a drastic shrinkage in earning power, or else that the margin of safety is so large that it can undergo such a shrinkage without resultant danger. The bonds of light and power companies have been favored principally for the first reason, the bonds of United States Steel Corporation subsidiaries for the second. In the former case it is the *character* of the industry, in the latter it is the *amount* of protection, which justifies the purchase. Of the two viewpoints, the one which tries to avoid the perils ofdepression appeals most to the average bond buyer. It seems much simpler to invest in a depression-proof enterprise than to have to rely on the company's financial strength to pull its bonds through a period of poor results.

**没有哪个行业能完全免受经济衰退的影响。** 对这一投资理论的反对意见自然是：并不存在所谓“能抵御经济衰退的行业”，即那种完全不会遭受任何盈利能力下降风险的行业。的确，与钢铁制造商相比，爱迪生旗下的公司利润下降幅度较小。但即便降幅微小，如果企业的盈利始终处于较高水平，这样的下降也可能致命。一旦承认——而这始终是必须的——某个行业可能会出现一定程度的利润下滑，投资者就不得不估算可能的下降幅度，并将其与高于利息支出要求的盈余部分进行比较。这样一来，他就会处于与其他类型债券持有者相同的境地，必须密切关注企业应对未来各种变化的能力。¹ 因此，需要区分的并非那些“不受经济衰退影响”的行业与那些“受其影响”的行业，而是那些波动较小的行业与那些波动较大的行业。企业类型越稳定，就越适合通过债券融资，其正常盈利中可用于支付利息的比例也就越高。随着不稳定性的增加，为确保能够支付利息，就必须有更大的安全边际；换言之，用于发行债券的总资本比例就会降低。如果企业缺乏足够的稳定性，以至于在持续不利的条件下难以生存（这在规模较小的工业企业中较为常见），那么即便以过往表现衡量的安全边际非常大，发行债券也无法满足固定价值投资的要求。这类债券虽然能通过数量上的检验，却无法通过质量上的检验，而这两方面对我们理解投资而言都是不可或缺的。² **投资实践重视行业特性。** 这种关于不同安全边际的理念多年来已在投资实践中得到充分体现。将企业分为铁路、公用事业或工业企业三类，正是为了反映它们在稳定性方面的固有差异，进而确定其在债券利息之外的额外保障需求。例如，投资者认为那些能够赚取两倍于债券利息的铁路公司表现良好，但对于工业企业的债券，同样的安全边际通常被认为不够。在1920年至1930年的十年间，公用事业领域的状况发生了巨大变化。此前紧密相关的轻工业、供热业和电力服务与城市铁路线路被明确区分开来。由于表现不佳，无轨电车公司被默认排除在金融界所使用的“公用事业”范畴之外，在大众认知中，这一名称也仅限于电力、燃气、供水和电话公司。（后来，一些发起人试图利用公用事业这一概念的知名度，将其应用于各类业务的公司，包括天然气、冰块、煤炭甚至仓储行业。）尽管在1924年和1927年经历了轻微的工业衰退，公用事业板块仍持续发展，其在投资者心目中的地位大幅提升，到1929年时，其信用评级已与铁路公司完全相当。在随后的经济衰退中，该行业的总收益和净收益的下降幅度远小于交通行业，因此有理由预计，那些资本实力雄厚的轻工业和电力公司的债券将取代高等级的铁路债券，成为最理想的企业投资品种。 （尽管自1933年以来，由于利率下调、政府间的竞争以及通货膨胀带来的威胁等多种因素，公用事业债券和股票的受欢迎程度出现了明显下滑，但作者们仍认为这一观点是正确的。）

<!--en-->
**No Industry Entirely Depression-Proof.** The objection to this theory of investment is, of course, that there is no such thing as a depression-proof industry, meaning thereby one that is immune from the danger of *any* decline in earning power. It is true that the Edison companies have shown themselves subject to only minor shrinkage in profits, as compared, say, with the steel producers. But even a small decline may prove fatal if the business is bonded to the limit of prosperity earnings. Once it is admitted—as it always must be—that the industry can suffer *some* reduction in profits, then the investor is compelled to estimate the possible extent of the shrinkage and compare it with the surplus above the interest requirements. He thus finds himself in the same position as the holder of any other kind of bond, vitally concerned with the ability of the company to meet the vicissitudes of the future.¹
The distinction to be made, therefore, is not between industries which are *exempt* from and those which are *affected* by depression, but rather between those which are more and those which are less subject to fluctuation. The more stable the type of enterprise, the better suited it is to bond financing and the larger the portion of the supposed normal earning power which may be consumed by interest charges. As the degree of instability increases, it must be offset by a greater margin of safety to make sure that interest charges will be met; in other words, a smaller portion of total capital may be represented by bonds. If there is such a lack of inherent stability as to make survival of the enterprise doubtful under continued unfavorable conditions (a question arising frequently in the case of industrial companies of secondary size), then the bond issue cannot meet the requirements of fixed-value investment, even though the margin of safety—measured by past performance—may be exceedingly large. Such a bond will meet the quantitative but not the qualitative test, but both are essential to our concept of investment.²
**Investment Practice Recognizes Importance of Character of the Industry.** This conception of diverse margins of safety has been solidly grounded in investment practice for many years. The threefold classification of enterprises—as railroads, public utilities, or industrials—was intended to reflect inherent differences in relative stability and consequently in the coverage to be required above bond interest requirements. Investors thought well, for example, of any railroad which earned its bond interest twice over, but the same margin in the case of an industrial bond was ordinarily regarded as inadequate. In the decade between 1920 and 1930, the status of the public-utility division underwent some radical changes. A sharp separation was introduced between light, heat, and power services on the one hand, and street-railway lines on the other, although previously the two had been closely allied. The trolley companies, because of their poor showing, were tacitly excluded from the purview of the term “public utility,” as used in financial circles, and in the popular mind the name was restricted to electric, gas, water, and telephone companies. (Later on, promoters endeavored to exploit the popularity of the public utilities by applying this title to companies engaged in all sorts of businesses, including natural gas, ice, coal, and even storage.) The steady progress of the utility group, even in the face of the minor industrial setbacks of 1924 and 1927, led to an impressive advance in its standing among investors, so that by 1929 it enjoyed a credit rating fully on a par with the railroads. In the ensuing depression, it registered a much smaller shrinkage in gross and net earnings than did the transportation industry, and its seems logical to expect that bonds of soundly capitalized light and power companies will replace high-grade railroad bonds as the premier type of corporate investment. (This seems true to the authors despite the distinct recession in the popularity of utility bonds and stocks since 1933, due to a combination of rate reductions, governmental competition and threatened dangers from inflation.)

**以经济衰退期间的表现作为衡量投资价值的标准。** 现在让我们来看看这三大投资群体在最近两次经济衰退测试中的表现——即1931–1933年那次以及1937–1938年那次。其中，1931–1933年的经济衰退严重程度堪称史无前例，因此要求当前正在考虑的任何投资都需以其在那段灾难性时期的表现来衡量，似乎既不公平也不切实际。不过，我们认为1931–1933年的经历可以被视为对投资标准的“实验室测试”，其带来的压力程度是未来普通市场波动所无法预见的。尽管那些年份的条件可能无法重现，但当时各类证券的表现仍能为投资问题提供有用的参考。

<!--en-->
**Depression Performance as a Test of Merit.** Let us turn our attention now to the behavior of these three investment groups in the two recent depression tests—that of 1931–1933 and that of 1937–1938. Of these, the former was of such unexampledseverity that it may seem unfair and impractical to ask that any investment now under consideration should be measured by its performance in those disastrous times. We have felt, however, that the experiences of 1931–1933 may be profitably viewed as a “laboratory test” of investment standards, involving degrees of stress not to be expected in the ordinary vicissitudes of the future. Even though the conditions prevalent in those years may not be duplicated, the behavior of various types of securities at the time should throw a useful light on investment problems.
