CHAPTER 10

## 债券投资具体标准（继续）

<!--en-->
*Specific Standards for Bond Investment (Continued)*

## 资产价值与已融资债务之间的关系

<!--en-->
*THE RELATION OF THE VALUE OF THE PROPERTY TO THE FUNDED DEBT*

在我们之前的讨论（第6章）中，我们指出，典型的债券投资是否稳健，取决于债务发行企业偿还债务的能力，而非债券所担保的资产价值。这一基本原则自然就排除了基于抵押资产价值来设定任何*通用*债券安全性测试的可能性，因为这种测试会将资产价值与企业自身的成败割裂开来考虑。

<!--en-->
In our earlier discussion (Chap. 6) we pointed out that the soundness of the typical bond investment depends upon the ability of the obligor corporation to take care of its debts, rather than upon the value of the property on which the bonds have a lien. This broad principle naturally leads directly away from the establishment of any *general* tests of bond safety based upon the value of the mortgaged assets, where this value is considered apart from the success or failure of the enterprise itself.

换句话说，我们认为对于普通的 corporate债券——无论是铁路、公用事业还是工业领域的债券——规定抵押的实物资产价值（按原始成本或重置成本计算）与债务金额之间的最低比例并无好处。在这方面，我们不同意许多州（包括纽约州）的法律规定，因为这些规定仍沿袭着对资产价值的传统重视。例如，纽约州法律规定，除非燃气、电力或电话债券的抵押资产价值$66^{2}/_{3}\%$高于债券发行额，否则此类债券不得被视为合格。这个价值 presumedly 是账面价值，可能是原始成本减去折旧后的数值，也可能是由于资产转让或重新评估而设定的某种人为数值。

<!--en-->
Stating the matter differently, we do not believe that in the case of the ordinary corporation bond—whether railroad, utility, or industrial—it would be advantageous to stipulate any minimum relationship between the value of the physical property pledged (taken at either original or reproduction cost) and the amount of the debt. In this respect we are in disagreement with statutory provisions in many states (including New York) which reflect the traditional emphasis upon property values. The New York law, for example, will not admit as eligible a gas, electric, or telephone bond, unless it is secured by property having a value $66^{2}/_{3}\%$ in excess of the bond issue. This value is presumably book value, which either may be the original dollar cost less depreciation or may be some more or less artificial value set up as a result of transfer or reappraisal.

**特殊类型的债券：1. 设备类债券。** 我们认为，公用事业资产——以及铁路和典型工业设施的账面价值——并不能作为判断以其为担保发行的债券安全性的依据。不过，存在多种*特殊*类型的债券，其安全性在很大程度上取决于为其提供担保的资产，而非企业整体的持续经营价值。其中最具代表性的是铁路设备信托凭证，它以机车、货运车或客车的所有权以及铁路使用这些设备所依据的租赁协议作为担保。这类设备类债券的投资表现十分理想，尤其是因为直到最近，即便发行方面临极为严重的财务困难，也很少出现无法按时支付利息和本金的情况。¹ 这些良好业绩的主要原因是，被抵押的具体资产是可以转移并由其他铁路运营商使用的，因此它们拥有类似于汽车、珠宝及其他可用于个人贷款的动产那样的独立可变现价值。即便实际上很难以合理价格将这些车辆出售给其他铁路公司，这种流动性依然使设备类债券相比针对铁路本身的抵押贷款具有显著优势。这两种资产对铁路的运营都至关重要，但铁路债券持有人别无选择，只能允许接管人继续使用其资产，而设备留置权的持有者至少可以威胁要拿走这些车辆。正是这种*替代选择*的存在，实际上为设备信托的持有者带来了巨大价值，因为它几乎迫使那些持有铁路本身第一顺位抵押权的人也不得不将其债权置于后者之后。

<!--en-->
**Special Types of Obligations: 1. Equipment Obligations.** It is our view that the book value of public-utility properties— and of railroads and the typical industrial plant as well—is no guidance in determining the safety of the bond issues secured thereon. There are, however, various *special* types of obligations, the safety of which is in great measure dependent upon the assets securing them, as distinguished from the going-concern value of the enterprise as a whole. The most characteristic of these, perhaps, is the railroad-equipment trust certificate, secured by title to locomotives, freight cars, or passenger cars, and by the pledge of the lease under which the railroad is using the equipment. The investment record of these equipment obligations is very satisfactory, particularly because until recently even the most serious financial difficulties of the issuing road have very rarely prevented the prompt payment of interest and principal.¹ The primary reason for these good results is that the specific property pledged is removable and usable by other carriers. Consequently it enjoys an independent salable value, similar to automobiles, jewelry, and other chattels on which personal loans are made. Even where there might be great difficulty in actually selling the rolling stock to some other railroad at a reasonable price, this mobility still gives the equipment obligation a great advantage over the mortgages on the railroad itself. Both kinds of property are essential to the operation of the line, but the railroad bondholder has no alternative save to permit the receiver to operate his property, while the holder of the equipment lien can at least threaten to take the rolling stock away. It is the possession of this *alternative* which in practice has proved of prime value to the owner of equipment trusts because it has virtually compelled the holders even of the first mortgages on the road itself to subordinate their claim to his.

因此，设备信托凭证的持有者拥有两重独立的保障来源：其一为借款铁路的信用状况与经营业绩，其二为被抵押车辆的价值。如果后者的价值远高于以此为担保的贷款金额，他或许完全可以忽略前者或信用因素，就如同当铺老板在放贷时不会考虑借款人的财务状况，而只依赖被抵押的财产。

<!--en-->
It follows that the holder of equipment-trust certificates has two separate sources of protection, the one being the credit and success of the borrowing railway, the other being the value of the pledged rolling stock. If the latter value is sufficiently in excess of the money loaned against it, he may be able to ignore the first or credit factor entirely, in the same way as a pawn-broker ignores the financial status of theindividual to whom he lends money and is content to rely exclusively on the pledged property.

设备信托通常设立时的相关条款能为购买方提供相当程度的保护。这些法律形式旨在便于在债务人违约时行使留置权人的权利。实际上，在所有案例中，至少有20%的设备成本由铁路公司承担，因此这类设备类债券的初始金额不会超过其所担保资产价值的80%。本金通常分15期等额偿还，从发行之日起算，每年一期，这样债务的减少速度就会快于普通折旧的速度。

<!--en-->
The conditions under which equipment trusts are usually created supply a substantial degree of protection to the purchaser. The legal forms are designed to facilitate the enforcement of the lienholder's rights in the event of nonpayment. In practically all cases at least 20% of the cost of the equipment is provided by the railway, and consequently the amount of the equipment obligations is initially not more than 80% of the value of the property pledged behind them. The principal is usually repayable in 15 equal annual installments, beginning one year from issuance, so that the amount of the debt is reduced more rapidly than ordinary depreciation would require.

近年来，由于商品价格下跌导致资产的再生产价值（进而也是可变现价值）远低于原始成本，加之运输量减少使得对新旧设备的需求下降，这些安排为设备信托持有者提供的保护有所减弱。自1930年以来，一些处于接管状态的铁路公司（如Seaboard Air Line和Wabash）要求即将到期的设备类债券持有者延长期限一段时间，或将其兑换为票面利率更低的受托人凭证或接管人凭证。在佛罗里达东海岸铁路公司发行的一批（“D”系列）债券的独特案例中，接管人允许设备信托持有者接管并出售被抵押的设备，而这些设备的价值似乎低于其他系列所对应的设备。在此案例中，持有者通过出售仅能收回本金的43美分，剩余款项则需向铁路公司申请追偿（但追偿价值存疑）。这些操作及损失表明，人们常说的设备类债券“几乎绝对安全”的说法需要适度调整；但不可否认的是，由于被抵押资产的可变现性，这类投资确实具有积极且显著的优点。² （这一结论可通过1939年11月芝加哥西北铁路公司新发行的1940–1949年到期的设备信托2½s债券的出售情况来佐证，尽管当时该公司的所有抵押贷款均已违约，但这些债券的售价所能产生的收益率仅为0.45%至2.35%。）

<!--en-->
The protection accorded the equipment-trust holder by these arrangements has been somewhat diminished in recent years, due partly to the drop in commodity prices which has brought reproduction (and therefore, salable) values far below original cost, and also to the reduced demand for equipment, whether new or used, because of the smaller traffic handled. Since 1930 certain railroads in receivership (e.g., Seaboard Air Line and Wabash) have required holders of maturing equipment obligations to extend their maturities for a short period or to exchange them for trustee's or receiver's certificates carrying a lower coupon. In the unique case of one Florida East Coast Railway issue (Series "D") the receivers permitted the equipment-trust holders to take over and sell the pledged equipment, which seemed to have been less valuable than that securing other series. In this instance the holders realized only 43 cents on the dollar from the sale and have a deficiency judgment (of doubtful value) against the road for the balance. These maneuvers and losses suggest that the claim of "almost absolute safety" frequently made in behalf of equipment issues will have to be moderated; but it cannot be denied that this form of investment enjoys a positive and substantial advantage through the realizability of the pledged assets.² (This conclusion may be supported by a concrete reference to the sale in November 1939 of Chicago and North Western new Equipment Trust 2½s, due 1940–1949, at pricesto yield only from 0.45 to 2.35%, despite the fact that all the mortgage issues of that road were then in default.)

**2. 抵押信托债券。** 抵押信托债券是以股票或其他债券作为抵押物来担保的债务工具。通常情况下，抵押物为债务发行公司自身的债券，或是其子公司的债券或股票。因此，抵押物的可变现价值在很大程度上取决于整个企业的经营状况。但对于近年来出现的投资公司发行的抵押信托债券而言，持有者可以说对抵押证券的市场价值拥有优先权益，这样一来，借助契约中的保护条款，他们很可能在股东几乎面临损失的情况下仍能得到充分保障。因此，这类抵押信托债券可与设备信托债务一同被视为例外情况，打破了“债券购买者应主要依赖企业的发展而非具体抵押的资产”这一普遍规则。

<!--en-->
**2. Collateral-Trust Bonds.** Collateral-trust bonds are obligations secured by the pledge of stocks or other bonds. In the typical case, the collateral consists of bonds of the obligor company itself, or of the bonds or stocks of subsidiary corporations. Consequently the realizable value of the collateral is usually dependent in great measure on the success of the enterprise as a whole. But in the case of the collateral-trust issues of investment companies, a development of recent years, the holder may be said to have a primary interest in the market value of the pledged securities, so that it is quite possible that by virtue of the protective conditions in the indenture, he may be completely taken care of under conditions which mean virtual extinction for the stockholders. This type of collateral-trust bond may therefore be ranked with equipment-trust obligations as exceptions to our general rule that the bond buyer must place his chief reliance on the success of the enterprise and not on the property specifically pledged.

若深入探究其本质而非仅看表面形式，我们可以发现这一特点在投资信托*债券*债务中同样适用。因为无论是在抵押信托契约下将投资组合实际交由受托人保管，还是由公司持有但需满足债券持有人的索赔要求，在实际操作中并无太大区别。通常情况下，这类债券都配有防止债务增加的充足条款，还常常有要求公司资产的市场价格必须保持在债券面值一定百分比之上的约束条款。

<!--en-->
Going behind the form to the substance, we may point out that this characteristic is essentially true also of investment-trust *debenture* obligations. For it makes little practical difference whether the portfolio is physically pledged with a trustee, as under a collateral-trust indenture, or whether it is held by the corporation subject to the claim of the debenture bondholders. In the usual case the debentures are protected by adequate provisions against increasing the debt, and frequently also by a covenant requiring the market price of the company's assets to be maintained at a stated percentage above the face amount of the bonds.

*示例：* 1954年到期的Reliance Management Corporation 5便士债券，正是这些保护条款发挥作用的一个实例。该企业整体经营极为不善，其股票价格从1929年的69美元跌至1933年的1美元，充分体现了这一点。在普通债券发行中，股价的如此暴跌几乎必然会导致违约以及本金的巨大损失。但在此例中，由于相关资产能够轻易变现，债券背后的保护性约束条款才发挥了作用。这使得公司不得不回购超过四分之三的已发行债券，甚至还迫使股东投入额外资金以弥补资产不足的问题。结果在1932年，这些债券的售价高达88美元，而同一时间股票的售价仅为$2\frac{1}{2}$美元。剩余的债券则于1937年2月以$104\frac{1}{4}$美元的价格被赎回。

<!--en-->
*Example:* The Reliance Management Corporation Debenture 5s, due 1954, are an instance of the working of these protective provisions. The enterprise as a whole was highly unsuccessful, as is shown vividly by a decline in the price of the stock from 69 in 1929 to 1 in 1933. In the case of the ordinary bond issue, such a collapse in the stock value would have meant almost certain default and large loss of principal. But here the fact that the assets could be readilyturned into cash gave significance to the protective covenants behind the debentures. It made possible and compelled the repurchase by the company of more than three-quarters of the issue, and it even forced the stockholders to contribute additional capital to make good a deficiency of assets below the indenture requirements. This resulted in the bonds selling as high as 88 in 1932 when the stock sold for only $2\frac{1}{2}$. The balance of the issue was called at $104\frac{1}{4}$ in February 1937.

在专门讨论保护性约束条款的第18章中，我们将介绍一家投资公司（金融投资公司）发行的抵押信托债券的案例，并指出我们认为，由于债券持有人在行使权利时犹豫不决，这类债务的内在价值往往会被不必要的削弱。

<!--en-->
In Chap. 18, devoted to protective covenants, we shall refer to the history of a collateral-trust bond issue of an investment company (Financial Investing Company), and we shall point out that the intrinsic strength of such obligations is often impaired—unnecessarily, in our opinion—by hesitation in asserting the bondholders' rights.

**3. 房地产债券。** 相比于前两种证券，规模更为庞大的房地产抵押贷款及房地产抵押贷款债券要重要得多。后者允许投资者以合适的规模参与大型单一抵押贷款项目。毫无疑问，对于这类债务而言，作为抵押的土地和建筑物的价值至关重要。经验丰富的投资者在进行普通房地产贷款时，主要依据的是其对作为抵押物的财产公允价值的判断。然而在我们看来，从更广泛的意义上讲，房地产抵押贷款背后的价值实际上是*持续经营价值*；也就是说，它们从根本上源自该财产的实际或预期的盈利能力。换言之，抵押资产的价值并非与企业的发展状况相分离（如铁路设备信托凭证的情况可能如此），而是与其完全一致。

<!--en-->
**3. Real Estate Bonds.** Of much greater importance than either of the two types of securities just discussed is the large field of real estate mortgages and real estate mortgage bonds. The latter represent participations of convenient size in large individual mortgages. There is no doubt that in the case of such obligations the value of the pledged land and buildings is of paramount importance. The ordinary real estate loan made by an experienced investor is based chiefly upon his conclusions as to the fair value of the property offered as security. It seems to us, however, that in a broad sense the values behind real estate mortgages are *going-concern values*; *i.e.*, they are derived fundamentally from the earning power of the property, either actual or presumptive. In other words, the value of the pledged asset is not something *distinct* from the success of the enterprise (as is possibly the case with a railroad-equipment trust certificate), but is rather *identical* therewith.

通过参考最典型的房地产贷款形式——单户住宅的第一抵押贷款，可以更清楚地说明这一点。在正常情况下，一套价值10,000美元的房屋，其年租金价值（或类比业主与租客的关系下的等值价值）约为1,200美元，扣除税费及其他开支后，净收入约为800美元。按储蓄银行的标准，即贷款额为房屋价值的60%，也就是6,000美元，这样一笔5%的首次抵押贷款就能得到足以覆盖两倍以上利息要求的正常*收益能力*作为保障。换言之，即使租金价值下降超过三分之一，该房屋的偿息能力也不会受到影响。因此，抵押权人认为，无论房屋当时的所有者是否有能力支付相关费用，总能够找到租客或新买家，以至少足以覆盖60%贷款金额的价格承租或购买该房产。（作为对比，可以指出，一座价值1,000,000美元、并设有600,000美元担保的典型*工业厂房*，如果发行该债券的公司破产，其售价或租金恐怕也难以覆盖5%的抵押贷款。）

<!--en-->
This point may be made clearer by a reference to the most typical form of real estate loan, a first mortgage on a single-family dwelling house. Under ordinary conditions a home costing $10,000 would have a rental value (or an equivalent value to an owner-tenant) of some $1,200 per year, and would yield a net income of about $800 after taxes and other expenses. A 5% first-mortgage loan on the savings-bank basis,i.e., 60% of value, or $6,000, would therefore be protected by a normal *earning power* of over twice the interest requirements. Stated differently, the rental value could suffer a reduction of over one-third before the ability to meet interest charges would be impaired. Hence the mortgagee reasons that regardless of the ability of the then owner of the house to pay the carrying charges, he could always find a tenant or a new purchaser who would rent or buy the property on a basis at least sufficient to cover his 60% loan. (By way of contrast, it may be pointed out that a typical *industrial plant*, costing $1,000,000 and bonded for $600,000, could not be expected to sell or rent for enough to cover the 5% mortgage if the issuing company went into bankruptcy.)

*房产价值与收益能力密切相关*。这一例证表明，在*住宅*、*办公室*和*商店*领域，正常情况下房产价值与租金价值是同步变化的。从这个意义上说，贷款机构是将这类抵押房产视为具有可销售价值的事物，还是视为具备相当于持续经营企业的收益能力的事物，其实并无太大区别。对于空地以及未使用的房屋或商店而言，这种情况也在一定程度上成立，因为这些资产的市场价值与其经过改造或出租后的*预期*租金紧密相关。（不过，对于工厂等为特定目的而建造的建筑物来说，情况显然并非如此。）

<!--en-->
*Property Values and Earning Power Closely Related.* This illustration shows that under normal conditions obtaining in the field of *dwellings*, *offices*, and *stores*, the property values and the rental values go hand in hand. In this sense it is largely immaterial whether the lender views mortgaged property of this kind as something with salable value or as something with an earning power, the equivalent of a going concern. To some extent this is true also of vacant lots and unoccupied houses or stores, since the market value of these is closely related to the *expected* rental when improved or let. (It is emphatically not true, however, of buildings erected for a special purpose, such as factories, etc.)

*评估结果的误导性*。上述讨论对于房地产债券潜在投资者应如何正确看待所提交的债券背后所宣称的房产价值至关重要。在1923年至1929年那段房地产抵押贷款债券业务迅猛发展却又灾难频发的时期，除了对未来收益的估算之外，通常用来支持债券发行的唯一数据就是房产的*评估价值*，而这一数值几乎总是比抵押贷款的发行额高出一些$66\frac{2}{3}\%$。如果这些评估结果能够反映房地产买家或贷款方实际给出的市场价值，那么它们在筛选优质房地产债券时就会发挥真正的作用。但遗憾的是，这些只是纯粹人为编造的估值，评估师们愿意收取费用为其背书，而这些估值的唯一作用就是误导投资者，让他们误以为自己获得了足够的保障。

<!--en-->
*Misleading Character of Appraisals.* The foregoing discussion is important in its bearing on the correct attitude that the intending investor in real estate bonds should take towards the property values asserted to exist behind the issues submitted to him. During the great and disastrous development of the real estate mortgage-bond business between 1923 and 1929, the only datum customarily presented to support the usual bond offering—aside from an estimate of future earnings—was a statement of the *appraised value* of the property, which almost invariably amounted to some $66\frac{2}{3}\%$ in excess of the mortgage issue. If these appraisals had corresponded to the market values which experienced buyers of or lenders on real estate would place upon the properties, they would have been of real utility in the selection of soundreal estate bonds. But unfortunately they were purely artificial valuations, to which the appraisers were willing to attach their names for a fee, and whose only function was to deceive the investor as to the protection which he was receiving.

这些评估所采用的方法，是对房产预期能带来的租金进行大幅度的资本化处理。通过这种方式，一座包括高额融资成本在内总计价值1,000,000美元的典型建筑，其“评估价值”立刻就会被定为1,500,000美元。这样一来，就可以以几乎等于整个项目成本的金额发行债券，从而使建筑商或开发商无需投入一分钱，就能保留该建筑的产权，而且在很多情况下还能获得可观的现金利润。³整个房地产融资体系存在着极其严重的缺陷，而在其不可避免地崩溃之前还能发展到如此庞大的规模，实在反映出所有相关方都缺乏原则、洞察力以及基本常识。⁴*以异常高的租金作为估值依据*。的确，1928–1929年间普遍存在的较高租金水平，确实能让新的房地产项目获得极高的投资回报率。但这种状况并不能被合理地理解为意味着新建建筑的价值会立即超过其实际成本50%。因为这种高收益状况注定只是暂时的，它必然会刺激更多的建筑建设，直到房源过剩导致租金水平下跌。由于建筑商可以从公众那里筹集所需的所有资金，因此这种过度建设更是不可避免的。

<!--en-->
The method followed by these appraisals was the capitalization on a liberal basis of the rental expected to be returned by the property. By this means, a typical building which cost $1,000,000, including liberal financing charges, would immediately be given an “appraised value” of $1,500,000. Hence a bond issue could be floated for almost the entire cost of the venture so that the builders or promoters retained the equity (i.e., the ownership) of the building, without a cent’s investment, and in many cases with a goodly cash profit to boot.³ This whole scheme of real estate financing was honeycombed with the most glaring weaknesses, and it is sad commentary on the lack of principle, penetration, and ordinary common sense on the part of all parties concerned that it was permitted to reach such gigantic proportions before the inevitable collapse.⁴
*Abnormal Rentals Used as Basis of Valuation.* It was indeed true that the scale of rentals prevalent in 1928–1929 would yield an abundantly high rate of income on the cost of a new real estate venture. But this condition could not properly be interpreted as making a new building immediately worth 50% in excess of its actual cost. For this high income return was certain to be only temporary, since it could not fail to stimulate more and more building, until an oversupply of space caused a collapse in the scale of rentals. This overbuilding was the more inevitable because it was possible to carry it on without risk on the part of the owner, who raised all the money needed from the public.

*因过度建设成本导致的债务问题。* 过度建设的另一个后果是建筑成本上升至异常高的水平。因此，即便在1928年或1929年发放的贷款看似较为保守，金额也不超过*实际成本*的三分之二，却仍无法提供足够的保障，因为存在一种明显的风险（后来确实发生了）：建筑成本的急剧下降会将资产价值降至低于贷款金额的水平。

<!--en-->
*Debt Based on Excessive Construction Costs.* A collateral result of this overbuilding was an increase in the cost of construction to abnormally high levels. Hence even an apparently conservative loan made in 1928 or 1929, in an amount not exceeding two-thirds of *actual cost*, did not enjoy a proper degree of protection, because there was the evident danger (subsequently realized) that a sharp drop inconstruction costs would reduce fundamental values to a figure below the amount of the loan.

*专用建筑的弱点。* 房地产债券投资的第三个普遍弱点在于完全不区分不同类型的建筑项目。传统的标准房地产贷款通常针对住宅，其优势在于有大量潜在的购买者或租户可供选择，因此总能以略低于当前价值的价格出售。普通公寓楼、商店或办公大楼也通常呈现类似的情况。但当某座建筑是为特定用途而建造时，如酒店、车库、俱乐部、医院、教堂或工厂，它就失去了这种快速变现的特性，*其价值便与最初设计用途的相关企业的经营状况紧密相连。* 因此，这类建筑的抵押债券实际上并非传统意义上的房地产债券，而是*向企业提供的贷款*；其安全性必须依据评估工业债券时所使用的严格标准来判定。

<!--en-->
*Weakness of Specialized Buildings.* A third general weakness of real estate-bond investment lay in the entire lack of discrimination as between various types of building projects. The typical or standard real estate loan was formerly made on a home, and its peculiar virtue lay in the fact that there was an indefinitely large number of prospective purchasers or tenants to draw upon, so that it could always be disposed of at some moderate concession from the current scale of values. A fairly similar situation is normally presented by the ordinary apartment house, or store, or office building. But when a structure is built for some *special* purpose, such as a hotel, garage, club, hospital, church, or factory, it loses this quality of rapid disposability, and *its value becomes bound up with the success of the particular enterprise for whose use it was originally intended.* Hence mortgage bonds on such structures are not actually real estate bonds in the accepted sense, but rather *loans extended to a business*; and consequently their safety must be judged by all the stringent tests surrounding the purchase of an industrial obligation.

在房地产价值暴跌前的房地产融资热潮中，这一点完全被忽视了。人们以与公寓楼贷款几乎相同的方式发行债券，用于建造酒店、车库甚至医院。换句话说，只要评估显示的“价值”比债券发行价高出二分之一到三分之二，就几乎足以被认为能够保证贷款的安全。然而事实证明，当这些新项目在商业上失败且无法支付利息时，“房地产”债券持有人的处境几乎与那些持有无利可图的铁路或工厂房产的抵押贷款持有人的处境并无二致。⁵ *基于初始租金的估值具有误导性。* 关于公寓楼融资还有另一个弱点需要指出：用于确定评估价值的租金收入是基于项目开业初的预期租金。但公寓楼的租户习惯于为新建建筑支付较高的租金，而且他们认为，建筑使用几年后就会显得陈旧，或者至少不再那么现代化和有吸引力。因此，在正常情况下，项目前几年的实际租金远高于整个债券存续期内可以保守预计的租金水平。

<!--en-->
This point was completely lost sight of in the rush of real estate financing preceding the collapse in real estate values. Bonds were floated to build hotels, garages, and even hospitals, on very much the same basis as loans made on apartment houses. In other words, an appraisal showing a “value” of one-half to two-thirds in excess of the bond issue was considered almost enough to establish the safety of the loan. It turned out, however, that when such new ventures proved commercially unsuccessful and were unable to pay their interest charges, the “real estate” bondholders were in little better position than the holders of a mortgage on an unprofitable railroad or mill property.⁵
*Values Based on Initial Rentals Misleading.* Another weakness should be pointed out in connection with apartment-house financing. The rental income used in determining the appraised value was based on the rentals to be charged at the outset. But apartment-house tenants are accustomed to pay a substantial premium for space in a new building, and theyconsider a structure old, or at least no longer especially modern and desirable, after it has been standing a very few years. Consequently, under normal conditions the rentals received in the first years are substantially larger than those which can conservatively be expected throughout the life of the bond issue.

*缺乏财务信息。* 与上述问题相关但性质不同的一个缺陷是，几乎所有情况下，债券购买者在购入后都得不到该项目的运营和财务数据。这一弊端普遍存在于那些向公众发行债券但其股票由私人持有的公司——这是房地产融资的典型特征。结果，不仅大多数债券持有者在违约发生之前根本不知道该项目的经营状况不佳，更严重的是，到那时他们常常发现，尽管业主已经抽走了所有可用资金，但该资产仍积压了大量未缴税款。

<!--en-->
*Lack of Financial Information.* A defect related to those discussed above, but of a different character, was the almost universal failure to supply the bond buyer with operating and financial data after his purchase. This drawback applies generally to companies that sell bonds to the public but whose stock is privately held—an arrangement characteristic of real estate financing. As a result, not only were most bondholders unaware of the poor showing of the venture until default had actually taken place, but—more serious still—at that time they frequently found that large unpaid taxes had accrued against the property while the owners were “milking” it by drawing down all available cash.

*建议的操作规则。* 通过对上述过去十年中房地产债券融资缺陷的详细分析，可以制定出若干具体的操作规则，为未来的投资者提供指导。

<!--en-->
*Suggested Rules of Procedure.* From this detailed analysis of the defects of real estate bond financing in the past decade, a number of specific rules of procedure may be developed to guide the investor in the future.

对于独栋住宅而言，贷款通常由抵押贷款机构直接发放给房屋所有者，*即*无需通过房产发行机构出售的房地产抵押贷款*债券*作为中介。不过，也有不少抵押贷款公司（*例如*：律师抵押贷款公司、产权担保与信托公司）从事以此类住宅为抵押的担保抵押贷款及抵押贷款参与证业务。⁶在进行此类投资时，贷款方应确保：(a) 贷款金额不超过该房产价值的66²/₃%，该价值可依据近期实际成本或经验丰富的房地产专业人士认为的合理售价来确定；(b) 此类成本或合理售价并未反映近期的投机性通胀，且未大幅超过以往长期存在的价格水平。若存在上述情况，则必须适当降低抵押贷款债务额与当前房产价值之间的最高比例。

<!--en-->
In the case of single-family dwellings, loans are generally made directly by the mortgage holder to the owner of the home, *i.e.*, without the intermediary of a real estate mortgage *bond* sold by a house of issue. But an extensive business has also been transacted by mortgage companies (*e.g.*, Lawyers Mortgage Company, Title Guarantee and Trust Company) in guaranteed mortgages and mortgage-participation certificates, secured on such dwellings.⁶
Where investments of this kind are made, the lender should be certain: (a) that the amount of the loan is not over 66²/₃% of the value of the property, as shown either by actual recent cost or by the amount which an experienced real estate man would consider a fair price *to pay* for the property; and (b) that this cost or fair price does not reflect recent speculative inflation and does not greatly exceed the price levels existing for a long period previously. If so, a properreduction must be made in the maximum relation of the amount of mortgage debt to the current value.

更为常见的房地产抵押贷款*债券*实际上是对新公寓楼或办公楼的优先抵押贷款的一种参与权。在考虑此类产品时，投资者应忽略所提交的常规“评估价值”，并要求以公平的方式呈现的实际成本至少比债券发行金额高出50%。其次，投资者还应要求获得一份保守估算的收益报表，该报表需充分考虑空置带来的损失以及建筑老化导致的租金下降因素。在从收益中扣除用于逐步偿还债券的折旧准备金后，该收益报表预测的盈余应至少能覆盖利息支出，并留有100%的缓冲空间。借款人应同意定期向债券持有人提供运营状况报表和财务报告。

<!--en-->
The more usual real estate mortgage *bond* represents a participation in a first mortgage on a new apartment house or office building. In considering such offerings the investor should ignore the conventional “appraised values” submitted and demand that the actual cost, fairly presented, should exceed the amount of the bond issue by at least 50%. Secondly, he should require an estimated income account, conservatively calculated to reflect losses through vacancies and the decline in the rental scale as the building grows older. This income account should forecast a margin of at least 100% over interest charges, after deducting from earnings a depreciation allowance to be actually expended as a sinking fund for the gradual retirement of the bond issue. The borrower should agree to supply the bondholders with regular operating and financial statements.

被称为“第一顺位租赁抵押债券”的证券实际上属于第二顺位抵押债券。这类债券是以建在租赁土地上的建筑物为担保发行的，而地租实际上相当于对该不动产整体的第一顺位留置权或优先债权。在分析此类证券时，应将地租计入债券利息要求之中，从而得出该不动产的总利息负担。此外，还需认识到，在房地产债务领域，第一顺位抵押权相较于次级留置权的优势要远比普通商业企业中更为明显。⁷ 除了上述定量分析外，投资者还应在心中确信，该建筑的位置与类型足以吸引租户，并能最大程度降低因周边环境不利变化而导致价值大幅下跌的可能性。⁸ 不应为酒店、车库等具有特殊或有限用途的建筑物提供房地产贷款。此类投资必须作为独立业务在相关项目中进行。从我们之前关于优质工业债券购买标准的讨论来看，很难理解为何会有人基于单纯的投资目的去购买新开的酒店或类似项目的债券。所有这类企业都应首先由私人资本提供融资，只有在其能够连续多年成功运营之后，才可向公众发行债券或股票。⁹ 详情请参见在线资源中的第11章“债券投资的特定标准（续）”；第12章“铁路及公用事业债券分析中的特殊因素”；第13章“债券分析中的其他特殊因素”；第14章“优先股理论”；第15章“选择优先股进行投资的技术”；以及第16章“收益债券与担保证券”，网址为www.mhprofessional.com/SecurityAnalysis7. [^1010]：¹ 关于此类证券的投资记录，请参阅附录注释17。² 评论及相关数据见附录注释18。³ 1927年，419–4th Avenue Corporation（鲍克大厦）发行了面值为1,230,000美元的债券，但其实收股本仅为75,000美元。（按照常规的评估方法，价值约1,300,000美元的土地和建筑物被估价为1,897,788美元。）1931年至1932年间，该企业违约并进入破产清算程序是不可避免的。⁴ 美国投资银行家协会房地产证券委员会关于该领域违约情况的报告见附录注释19。⁵ 示例（哈德逊大厦）见附录注释20。⁶ 自1933年起，联邦政府通过联邦住房管理局（F.H.A.）对单户住宅的房地产融资进行了大规模干预，几乎不再有此类房地产债券出售给投资者。大型建筑物的融资也受到了极大限制，几乎所有的融资都由金融机构（保险公司等）提供，直到1939年底，几乎都没有向普通公众出售过房地产证券。⁷ 示例及评论见附录注释21。⁸ 1934年版脚注：“1933年现存的为数不多的采用保守融资方式的房地产债券示例之一，是纽约Trinity Buildings Corporation发行的1939年到期的First 5 1/2s债券，该债券以位于纽约市金融区的两栋地理位置优越的办公大楼作为担保。该债券的未偿还金额为4,300,000美元，其担保物为价值13,000,000美元用于征税的土地和建筑物，享有第一顺位留置权。1931年，该项目的总收入为2,230,000美元，扣除折旧后的净收入约为第一顺位抵押债券利息的六倍。1932年，租金收入降至1,653,000美元，但第一顺位抵押债券的利息负担仍约为所需金额的$3\frac{1}{2}$倍。1933年9月，这些债券以接近面值的价格售出。”

<!--en-->
Issues termed “first-*leasehold* mortgage bonds” are in actuality second mortgages. They are issued against buildings erected on leased land and the ground rent operates in effect as a first lien or prior charge against the entire property. In analyzing such issues the ground rent should be added to the bond-interest requirements to arrive at the total interest charges of the property. Furthermore, it should be recognized that in the field of real estate obligations the advantage of a first mortgage over a junior lien is much more clean-cut than in an ordinary business enterprise.⁷
In addition to the above quantitative tests, the investor should be satisfied in his own mind that the location and type of the building are such as to attract tenants and to minimize the possibility of a large loss of value through unfavorable changes in the character of the neighborhood.⁸
Real estate loans should not be made on buildings erected for a special or limited purpose, such as hotels, garages, etc. Commitments of this kind must be made in the venture itself, considered as an individual business. From our previous discussion of the standards applicable to a high-grade industrial-bond purchase, it is difficult to see how any bondissue on a new hotel, or the like, could logically be bought on a straight investment basis. All such enterprises should be financed at the outset by private capital, and only after they can show a number of years of successful operation should the public be offered either bonds or stock therein.⁹
See Chapter 11, “Specific Standards for Bond Investment (Continued)”; Chapter 12, “Special Factors in the Analysis of Railroad and Public-Utility Bonds”; Chapter 13, “Other Special Factors in Bond Analysis”; Chapter 14, “The Theory of Preferred Stocks.”; Chapter 15, “Technique of Selecting Preferred Stocks for Investment”; and Chapter 16, “Income Bonds and Guaranteed Securities” online at www.mhprofessional.com/SecurityAnalysis7.
[^1010]: ¹ See Appendix Note 17 for information on the investment record of such issues.
² See Appendix Note 18 for comment and supporting data.
³ The 419–4th Avenue Corporation (Bowker Building) floated a $1,230,000 bond issue in 1927 with a paid-in capital stock of only $75,000. (By the familiar process, the land and building which cost about $1,300,000 were appraised at $1,897,788.) Default and receivership in 1931–1932 were inevitable.
⁴ See Appendix Note 19 for a report of Real Estate Securities Committee of the Investment Bankers Association of America commenting on defaults in this field.
⁵ See Appendix Note 20 for an example (Hudson Towers).
⁶ Since 1933 real estate financing on single-family homes has been taken over so substantially by the Federal government, through the Federal Housing Administration (F.H.A.), that practically no real estate bonds of this type have been sold to investors. Financing on larger buildings has been greatly restricted. Practically all of it has been provided by financial institutions (insurance companies, etc.), and there have been virtually no sales of real estate securities to the general public (to the end of 1939).
⁷ See Appendix Note 21 for examples and comment.
⁸ Footnote to 1934 edition: “One of the few examples of a conservatively financed real estate-bond issue extant in 1933 is afforded by the Trinity Buildings Corporation of New York First 5 1/2s, due 1939, secured on two well-located office buildings in the financial district of New York City. This issue was outstanding in the amount of $4,300,000, and was secured by a first lien on land and buildings assessed for taxation at $13,000,000. In 1931, gross earnings were $2,230,000 and the net after depreciation was about six times the interest on the first-mortgage bonds. In 1932, rent income declined to $1,653,000, but the balance for first-mortgage interest was still about $3\frac{1}{2}$ times the requirement. In September 1933 these bonds sold close to par.”

这一脚注及后续内容充分体现了文中提到的地理位置因素的重要性。尽管自1933年以来整体商业环境有所改善，但金融区的业务活动减少导致租户流失，租金水平大幅下降。1938年，Trinity Building Corporation的净收益甚至无法覆盖折旧费用，即便不考虑折旧，也低于利息支出；1939年到期时，本金与利息均未能按时偿还；其母公司United States Realty and Improvement Company提供的担保也不足以解决问题；债权人不得不延长还款期限并接受固定票面利率的下调。在这个案例中，无疑较为保守的财务结构（即*量化因素*）不足以抵消该地区租金价值的下跌（即*质量因素*）。[^1013]：⁹有关担保型房地产抵押贷款的主题将在第17章探讨。第17章

<!--en-->
This footnote and the sequel well illustrate the importance of the location factor referred to in the text. Despite the improvement in general business conditions since 1933, the lessened activity in the financial district resulted in a loss of tenants and a severe decline in rental rates. The net earnings of Trinity Building Corporation failed even to cover depreciation charges in 1938 and were less than interest charges, even ignoring depreciation; principal and interest were defaulted at maturity in 1939; the guarantee by United States Realty and Improvement Company, the parent enterprise, proved inadequate; and the holders were faced with the necessity of extending their principal and accepting a reduction in the fixed coupon rate. In this instance an undoubtedly conservative financial set-up (a *quantitative factor*) did not prove strong enough to offset a decline in the rental value of the neighborhood (a *qualitative factor*).
[^1013]: ⁹ The subject of guaranteed real estate mortgage issues is treated in Chap. 17.
CHAPTER 17

## 担保证券（续）

<!--en-->
*Guaranteed Securities (Continued)*

## 担保型房地产抵押贷款与抵押债券

<!--en-->
*GUARANTEED REAL ESTATE MORTGAGES AND MORTGAGE BONDS*

证券担保的做法在房地产抵押贷款领域发展最为广泛。这类担保分为两种类型：第一种由从事抵押贷款或抵押股份销售的公司（或其关联企业）提供；第二种也是较新的形式，则是由独立的担保公司提供，该公司通过收取费用来承担潜在责任。

<!--en-->
The practice of guaranteeing securities reached its widest development in the field of real estate mortgages. These guarantees are of two different types: the first being given by the corporation engaged in the sale of the mortgages or mortgage participations (or by an affiliate); the second and more recent form being the guaranty given by an independent surety company, which assumes the contingent liability in return for a fee.

房地产抵押贷款担保背后的理念显然源自保险。对于抵押贷款持有人而言，以一定的收益损失为代价，为自己特定的房产可能面临的负面情况（如周边环境变化）做好防范是有益的。只要各项业务都能得到审慎处理，通过收取合理的保费来提供此类保障，就符合良好的保险实践标准。这样的安排只有在以下情况下才最有可能成功：

<!--en-->
The idea underlying real estate mortgage guarantees is evidently that of insurance. It is to the mortgage holder's advantage to protect himself, at some cost in income return, against the possibility of adverse developments affecting his particular property (such as a change in the character of the neighborhood). It is within the province of sound insurance practice to afford this protection in return for an adequate premium, provided of course, that all phases of the business are prudently handled. Such an arrangement will have the best chance of success if:

1. 抵押贷款最初应以保守的方式发放。
2. 担保公司规模庞大、管理完善，独立于抵押贷款销售机构，并且在房地产以外的领域拥有多元化的业务。
3. 经济形势并未出现异常剧烈的波动。1929年之后的房地产价值暴跌极为严重，甚至违背了上述第三项条件。因此，这一时期房地产抵押贷款担保的表现可能无法真正准确地预示其未来价值。尽管如此，这些担保所展现的一些特征仍值得探讨。**曾经较为保守的管理方式**。首先，1924年左右之前抵押贷款担保业务的运作方式与此后出现的松懈管理方式之间存在显著差异，而后者恰恰发生在该金融领域重要性达到顶峰的时期。如果考察纽约市那些主要从事房地产抵押贷款担保的机构（如债券与抵押贷款担保公司、律师抵押贷款公司）的政策，可以说多年来这些业务都是以较为保守的方式管理的：每笔抵押贷款的金额都被严格控制在房产价值的60%以内，并且会仔细评估；大型个人抵押贷款会被避免；同时从地域分布的角度来看，风险也得到了合理的分散。的确，这些担保公司并非独立于房产销售公司，也没有其他类型的担保业务。此外，通常只在抵押贷款发行后三到五年才提供担保的做法，确实存在后来被证实的风险——即在极其不合适的时机面临大量债务到期的问题。然而，正是由于他们谨慎的经营方式，这些公司才得以成功度过1908年和1921年那样的严重房地产萧条。**新兴的、更为激进的运营方式**。“新时代”期间出现的建筑热潮带动了房地产抵押贷款业务以及此类债务担保业务的迅猛发展。新的人、新的资本以及新的方法纷纷进入这个领域。一些长期从事该业务的中小本地企业则转型为极具进取心的组织，开展大规模的全国性业务。它们极力强调过去的成功记录，让公众深感印象——却未意识到其规模、经营方式和人员配置已发生巨大变化，实际上已经变成了另一家机构。在前一章中，我们指出过这一时期用于为房地产项目融资的方法是多么 reckless且不稳健。抵押贷款本身的弱点同样存在于那些常常需要额外费用才能获得的担保之中。这些担保公司实际上只是债券销售公司的子公司。因此，当危机来临时，房产价值、房地产债券公司以及相关的担保公司全都一同崩溃了。**竞争与传染的恶劣影响**。新兴的、更具进取心的房地产债券机构的崛起，对老牌企业的经营策略产生了极其不利的影响。在竞争压力之下，这些老牌企业不得不放宽贷款标准。新的抵押贷款以越来越宽松的条件被批准，而当旧抵押贷款到期时，往往还会以更高的金额续贷。此外，所担保的抵押贷款面额与担保公司资本的比率高得惊人，本应显而易见的是，一旦整体价值下跌，这类担保所提供的保护将极为薄弱。1931年房地产市场崩溃后，首先出现的后果就是几乎所有新兴的房地产债券公司及其附属担保公司都彻底垮台了。随着经济萧条的持续，老牌机构也相继倒下。 那些持有有担保抵押贷款或其相关权益的人（仅纽约的产权与抵押贷款公司就为这些贷款提供了约30亿美元的担保）发现，这些担保实际上只是虚名而已，他们完全依赖于相关房产的价值。在大多数情况下，这些房产的抵押程度远远超出了合理审慎原则所允许的范围。显然，在1932年尚未偿还的抵押贷款中，只有极小一部分是按照此前八年间所遵循的保守条件与原则设立的。**独立担保公司的担保。**在1924年至1930年期间，一些独立的担保与信用保险公司开始提供房地产抵押贷款担保服务，并收取费用或保险费。从理论上讲，这应该是开展此类业务最稳妥的方式。除了担保公司的实力与丰富经验之外，还有一个重要因素：由于这类担保方是完全独立的，它们应当会对提交给其担保的项目进行严格审查。然而，这一理论上的优势在很大程度上被以下事实所抵消：这些担保公司在遭遇危机前不久才开始从事房地产抵押贷款债券的担保业务，且当时普遍存在的过度乐观情绪导致它们做出了严重的判断失误。在大多数情况下，担保方因此承受的损失超出了其承受能力；有几家公司甚至被迫进入破产清算程序（尤其是National Surety Company），而持有此类担保债券的人也未能获得充分的保护。¹

<!--en-->
1. The mortgage loans are conservatively made in the first instance.
2. The guaranty or surety company is large, well managed, independent of the agency selling the mortgages, and has a diversification of business in fields other than real estate.
3. Economic conditions are not undergoing fluctuations of abnormal intensity.
The collapse in real estate values after 1929 was so extreme as to contravene the third of these conditions. Accordingly the behavior of real estate mortgage guarantees during this period may not afford a really fair guide to their future value. Nevertheless, some of the characteristics which they revealed are worthy of comment.
**This Business Once Conservatively Managed.** In the first place a striking contrast may be drawn between the way in which the business of guaranteeing mortgages had been conducted prior to about 1924 and the lax methods which developed thereafter, during the very time that this part of the financial field was attaining its greatest importance.
If we consider the policies of the leading New York City institutions which guaranteed real estate mortgages (e.g., Bond and Mortgage Guarantee Company, Lawyers Mortgage Company), it is fair to say that for many years the business was conservatively managed. The amount of each mortgage was limited to not more than 60% of the value, carefully determined; large individual mortgages were avoided; and a fair diversification of risk, from the standpoint of location, was attained. It is true that the guarantor companies were not independent of the selling companies, nor did they have other types of surety business. It is true also that the general practice of guaranteeing mortgages due only three to five years after their issuance contained the possibility, later realized, of a flood of maturing obligations at a most inconvenient time. Nevertheless, the prudent conduct of their activities had enabled them successfully to weather severe real estate depressions such as occurred in 1908 and 1921.
**New and Less Conservative Practices Developed.** The building boom which developed during the “new era” was marked by an enormous growth of the real estate mortgage business and of the practice of guaranteeing obligations of this kind. New people, new capital, and new methods entered the field. Several small local concerns which had been in the field for a long period were transformed into highly aggressiveorganizations doing a gigantic and nation-wide business. Great emphasis was laid upon the long record of success in the past, and the public was duly impressed—not realizing that the size, the methods, and the personnel were so changed that they were in fact dealing with a different institution. In a previous chapter we pointed out how recklessly unsound were the methods of financing real estate ventures during this period. The weakness of the mortgages themselves applied equally to the guarantees which were frequently attached thereto for an extra consideration. The guarantor companies were mere subsidiaries of the sellers of the bonds. Hence, when the crash came, the value of the properties, the real estate bond company, and the affiliated guarantor company all collapsed together.
**Evil Effects of Competition and Contagion.** The rise of the newer and more aggressive real estate bond organizations had a most unfortunate effect upon the policies of the older concerns. By force of competition they were led to relax their standards of making loans. New mortgages were granted on an increasingly liberal basis, and when old mortgages matured, they were frequently renewed in a larger sum. Furthermore, the face amount of the mortgages guaranteed rose to so high a multiple of the capital of the guarantor companies that it should have been obvious that the guaranty would afford only the flimsiest of protection in the event of a general decline in values.
When the real estate market broke in 1931, the first consequence was the utter collapse of virtually every one of the newer real estate bond companies and their subsidiary guarantor concerns. As the depression continued, the older institutions gave way also. The holders of guaranteed mortgages or participations therein (aggregating about $3,000,000,000 guaranteed by New York title and mortgage companies alone) found that the guaranty was a mere name and that they were entirely dependent upon the value of the underlying properties. In most cases these had been mortgaged far more heavily than reasonable prudence would have permitted. Apparently only a very small fraction of the mortgages outstanding in 1932 were created under theconservative conditions and principles that had ruled up to, say, eight years previously.
**Guarantees by Independent Surety Companies.** During the 1924–1930 period several of the independent surety and fidelity companies extended their operations to include the guaranteeing of real-estate mortgages for a fee or premium. Theoretically, this should have represented the soundest method of conducting such operations. In addition to the strength and general experience of the surety company there was the important fact that such a guarantor, being entirely independent, would presumably be highly critical of the issues submitted for its guaranty. But this theoretical advantage was offset to a great extent by the fact that the surety companies began the practice of guaranteeing real estate mortgage bonds only a short time prior to their debacle, and they were led by the general overoptimism then current to commit serious errors in judgment. In most cases the resultant losses to the guarantor were greater than it could stand; several of the companies were forced into receivership (notably National Surety Company), and holders of bonds with such guarantees failed to obtain full protection.¹

## 相当于担保的租赁义务

<!--en-->
*LEASEHOLD OBLIGATIONS EQUIVALENT TO GUARANTEES*

一家公司的资产常常被租给另一家公司，年租金金额足以支付该公司发行债券的利息和股息。此类租赁通常会附带针对这些利息及股息支付的特定担保，事实上，大多数有担保的公司债券都是通过这种方式发行的。²即便没有明确的担保，提供固定年度付款的租赁协议或其他合同也能为承租公司的证券提供等同于担保的作用。

<!--en-->
The property of one company is often leased to another for a fixed annual rental sufficient to pay interest and dividends on the former's capital issues. Frequently the lease is accompanied by a specific guaranty of such interest and dividend payments, and in fact the majority of guaranteed corporate issues originate in this fashion.² But even if there is no explicit guaranty, a lease or other contract providing fixed annual payments will supply the equivalent of a guaranty on the securities of the lessee company.

*示例：*1927年发行、1937年到期的Westvaco氯产品公司5 1/2s债券便是这种安排价值的绝佳例证。Westvaco公司同意将其部分产品出售给联合碳化物与碳公司的子公司，而后者承诺向受托人支付足够的月度款项，用以支付$5\frac{1}{2}\%$号债券的利息并实现其赎回。实际上，这种安排相当于由实力雄厚的联合碳化物与碳公司为Westvaco的债券提供利息和本金担保。得益于这一担保以及据此进行的持续回购，该债券在1932年至1933年间的价格始终保持在99或更高水平。相比之下，Westvaco普通股的价格则从1929年的$116\frac{1}{2}$跌至1932年的3。（整批债券于1935年9月以$100\frac{1}{2}$的价格被提前赎回。）

<!--en-->
*Examples:* An excellent instance of the value of such an arrangement is afforded by the Westvaco Chlorine Products Corporation 5 1/2s, issued in 1927 and maturing in 1937. The Westvaco Company agreed to sell part of its output to asubsidiary of Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation, and the latter enterprise guaranteed that monthly payments would be made to the trustee sufficient to take care of the interest and retirement of the $5\frac{1}{2}\%$ bonds. In effect this arrangement was a guaranty of interest and principal of the Westvaco issue by Union Carbide and Carbon, a very strong concern. By reason of this protection and the continuous purchases for redemption made thereunder, the price of the issue was maintained at 99 or higher throughout 1932–1933. This contrasts with a decline in the price of Westvaco common stock from $116\frac{1}{2}$ in 1929 to 3 in 1932. (The entire bond issue was called at $100\frac{1}{2}$ in September 1935.)

另一个有趣的例子是新泽西烟草产品公司2022年到期的6\frac{1}{2}美元债券。该公司的资产根据一份同样在2022年到期的99年期合同被租给美国烟草公司，合同规定每年需支付2,500,000美元（承租方有权选择以相当于当时按7%年利率折现后的租金现值的一次性付款方式履行支付义务）。通过设立偿债基金，这些租金款项被设定为足以在债券到期前全额偿还本金并支付利息。这些6\frac{1}{2}美元的烟草产品债券实际上相当于美国烟草公司的固定债务，因此其优先级高于美国烟草公司的优先股——后者的股息显然并非固定支出。1931年这些债券发行时，投资者要么对租赁协议的效力持怀疑态度，要么很可能并不了解这种情况，因为美国烟草公司的优先股售价远高于这些烟草产品债券。1932年时，这些债券以73的低价交易，收益率为8.90%，而美国烟草公司的优先股则以95的价格交易，收益率为6.32%。1935年1月，通过一次性付款的方式修改了租赁协议，使得6\frac{1}{2}美元的烟草产品债券得以按面值赎回。**租赁的具体条款至关重要。** *示例：*与有担保的债券发行情况类似，租赁协议的细节可能对受益债券的地位产生重大影响，以下示例可说明其中的一些要素：

<!--en-->
Another interesting example is supplied by the Tobacco Products Corporation of New Jersey $6\frac{1}{2}$s, due 2022. The properties of this company were leased to American Tobacco Company under a 99-year contract, expiring also in 2022, providing for annual payments of $2,500,000 (with the privilege to the lessee to settle by a lump-sum payment equivalent to the then present value of the rental, discounted at 7% per annum). By means of a sinking-fund arrangement these rental payments were calculated to be sufficient to retire the bond issue in full prior to maturity, in addition to taking care of the interest. These Tobacco Products $6\frac{1}{2}$s were the equivalent of fixed obligations of American Tobacco Company. As such they ranked ahead of American Tobacco Preferred, dividends on which, of course, are not a fixed charge. When the bonds were created in 1931 the investing public was either sceptical of the validity of the lease or—more probably—was not familiar with this situation, for American Tobacco Preferred sold at a much higher relative price than the Tobacco Products bonds. At the low price of 73 in 1932 the bonds yielded 8.90%, while American Tobacco preferred was selling at 95, to yield 6.32%. In January 1935 the lease was commuted by a lump-sum payment resulting in the redemption of the Tobacco Products $6\frac{1}{2}$s at par.
**Specific Terms of Lease Important.**
*Example:* As in the case of guaranteed issues, the details of the lease arrangement may have a vital bearing on the status of the issue benefiting therefrom. Some of the elements here involved are illustrated by the following example:

乔治亚米德兰铁路1946年到期的首批3美元债券。虽无担保，但其资产被租给南方铁路公司直至1995年，租金金额相当于债券当前的利息。（1939年1月的价格为35。）

<!--en-->
Georgia Midland Railway First 3s, due 1946. Not guaranteed, but property leased to Southern Railway until 1995, at a rental equal to present bond interest. (Price in January 1939, 35.)

在此案例中，租赁协议完全等同于对截至到期日甚至到期日后利息的担保。担保本身的价值取决于南方铁路公司的偿付能力。不过，1946年债券到期时的状况还将受其他多种因素的影响，*例如*：

<!--en-->
In this case the lease agreement is fully equivalent to a guarantee of *interest* up to and far beyond the maturity date. The value of the guaranty itself depends upon the solvency of the Southern Railway. The status of the bond issue at maturity in 1946 will depend, however, on a number of other factors as well, *e.g.*:

1. 南方铁路公司长期租赁义务的市值。如果利率足够低，且南方铁路公司的信用足够高，该债券就可以以同样的3%利率重新发行，且到期日可以延长。（但在1939年，这种情况似乎极不可能发生。）
2. 乔治亚米德兰铁路线路的收益价值。如果该线路的实际收益远高于所支付的租金，那么南方铁路公司为了避免失去对该资产的控制权，很可能会尽力在债券到期时予以偿还。这需要双方达成协议，支付必要的更高租金（即更高的利率），以便延长债券的到期日或实现其赎回。（然而，1939年私人手中掌握的客流量数据表明，这条线路并非南方铁路系统中价值较高的部分。）
3. 出于便利等原因，有可能选择延期支付。如果南方铁路公司在1946年状况良好，它或许会仅为避免部分业务板块破产而承担起偿还这笔债务的责任。从技术层面来看，根据其自身的“综合”发展与一般抵押条款（该条款规定需预留足够债券以在到期时偿还乔治亚中部3号债券），该公司可能被认为有义务在1946年支付这些债券的款项。（与前两段相同，1939年的债券持有人也无法对其自身立场的有力性抱太大信心。）上述讨论或许足以解释1939年初乔治亚中部3号债券价格低廉的原因。作为安全性分析的一个要素，值得注意的是，这一情况中的关键因素——即相关线路运营无利可图——并非公开记录中的内容，而需要通过其他补充信息来源进行核实。**有担保发行的证券往往被低估。**烟草产品案例就说明了，与其他由担保企业发行的证券相比，有担保或准有担保发行的证券往往会被低估。一个著名的例子是圣安东尼奥与阿兰萨斯帕斯铁路公司1943年到期的第一类4号债券，其本金和利息均由南太平洋公司提供担保。尽管这类债券除了有担保外还拥有抵押担保，但其售价通常仍能带来比南太平洋公司无担保债务更高的收益。³ *示例：*巴恩哈特兄弟公司与斯平德勒公司的第一类及第二类优先股（其本金和股息均由美国印刷公司提供担保），与担保方自身非固定义务的优先股价格相比，便呈现出更为显著的差异。更多此类例证包括：由舒尔特零售商店公司提供担保的特拉华州赫伊勒斯公司的优先股价格，与其担保方伊利诺伊州阿穆尔公司的优先股价格之间的对比；以及特拉华州阿穆尔公司担保的优先股价格，与其担保方伊利诺伊州阿穆尔公司的优先股价格之间的对比。下文列出了与这些示例相关的部分对比数据。**有担保证券与担保方证券的对比价格及收益率**** 如果读者追踪表中各类证券后续的发展历程，会发现各种不同的结果，包括通过合并而被接管（圣安东尼奥与阿兰萨斯帕斯铁路公司）、被赎回（巴恩哈特兄弟公司与斯平德勒公司），以及违约（特拉华州赫伊勒斯公司）。但每一种情况下有担保证券都被*相对*低估的事实，正是后续发展所证明的。

<!--en-->
1. The market value of a long-term rental obligation of Southern Railway. If interest rates are low enough, and the credit of Southern Railway high enough, the issue could be refunded at the same 3% interest rate into a longer maturity. (This would seem far from probable in 1939.)
2. The value of the Georgia Midland mileage. If this mileage actually earns substantially more than the rental paid, then Southern Railway could be expected to make a special effort to pay the bonds at maturity, for fear of otherwise losing control of the property. This would involve an agreement to pay such higher rental (*i.e.*, interest rate) as may be necessary to permit extension or refunding of the bond maturity. (However, traffic-density data in private hands in 1939 indicated that this mileage was not a valuable part of the Southern Railway System.)
3. Possible payment on grounds of convenience, etc. If the Southern Railway is prosperous in 1946, it may take care of this maturity merely to avoid insolvency for part of the system. There is also the technical possibility that by the terms of its own “blanket” Development and General Mortgage (under which sufficient bonds are reserved to refund the Georgia Midland 3s at maturity), it may be considered to have an obligation to provide for payment of these bonds in 1946. (Here also, as in the two previous paragraphs, the bondholderin 1939 could not be too confident of the strength of his position).
The foregoing discussion will perhaps adequately explain the low price of the Georgia Midland 3s at the beginning of 1939. It is interesting to note, as an element of security analysis, that the key fact in this situation—the unprofitable character of the mileage covered—was not a matter of public record but required a check into supplementary sources of information.
**Guaranteed Issues Frequently Undervalued.** The Tobacco Products example illustrates the fairly frequent undervaluation of guaranteed or quasi-guaranteed issues as compared with other securities of the guarantor enterprise. A well-known instance was that of San Antonio and Aransas Pass Railway Company First 4s, due 1943, guaranteed as to principal and interest by Southern Pacific Company. Although these enjoyed a mortgage security in addition to the guaranty they regularly sold at prices yielding higher returns than did the unsecured obligations of the Southern Pacific.³
*Examples:* A more striking contrast was afforded by the price of Barnhart Bros. and Spindler Company First and Second Preferred (both guaranteed as to principal and dividends by American Type Founders Company) in relation to the price of the guarantor's own preferred stock which was not a fixed obligation. Additional examples of this point are afforded by the price of Huyler's of Delaware, Inc., Preferred, guaranteed by Schulte Retail Stores Corporation, as compared with the price of Schulte Preferred; and by the price of Armour and Company of Delaware guaranteed preferred, as compared with the preferred stock of the guarantor company, Armour and Company of Illinois. Some comparative quotations relating to these examples are given below.
**Comparative Prices and Yields of Guaranteed Securities and Securities of the Guarantor**** If the reader traces the subsequent history of the various issues in this table, he will find a great variety of developments, including assumption through merger (San Antonio and Aransas Pass Railroad), redemption (Barnhart Brothers and Spindler), and default (Huylers of Delaware, Inc.). But the fact that the guaranteed issues were *relatively* undervalued is demonstrated by the sequel in each case.

显然，在这类情况下，可以将低收益的证券转换成高收益的证券，而不会影响安全性；或者以几乎不牺牲收益的方式转换成安全性更高的证券，有时甚至还能获得实际收益。⁴

<!--en-->
It is obvious that in cases of this sort advantageous exchanges can be made from the lower yielding into the higher yielding security with no impairment of safety; or else into a much better secured issue with little sacrifice of yield, and sometimes with an actual gain.⁴

## 在固定费用计算中纳入担保与租金

<!--en-->
*INCLUSION OF GUARANTEES AND RENTALS IN THE CALCULATION OF FIXED CHARGES*

在计算公司债券发行的偿付能力时，所有相当于债券利息的债务都应计入该公司的利息支出中。这一点在讨论铁路公司的固定费用时已有过详细说明，在探讨公用事业债券时也简要提及过。这些领域的处理方式并无特殊困难。但对于某些类型的工业企业而言，租金和担保的处理方式可能存在令人困惑的差异。对于零售企业、剧院公司等而言，这一问题尤为重要，因为与所使用的建筑物相关的租金或其他债务可能是其整体财务状况中的重要因素。如果此类建筑物归公司所有，并通过发行债券来支付款项，那么该项债务将在资产负债表和利润表中完整披露。但如果另一家公司通过长期租赁使用类似的建筑物，则利润表中不会出现单独的租金负债项目，资产负债表中也找不到相关迹象。第二家公司可能*看起来*比第一家公司更稳健，但这只是因为其债务未被披露；实际上，两家的负担大致相同。相反，完全拥有无抵押的房产（尤其是从优先股的角度来看）相比长期租赁具有明显优势，尽管资本化处理方式无法体现这一优势。

<!--en-->
All obligations equivalent to bond interest should be included with a company's interest charges when calculating the coverage for its bond issues. This point has already been explained in some detail in connection with railroad fixed charges, and it was touched upon briefly in our discussion of public-utility bonds. The procedure in these groups offers no special difficulties. But in the case of certain types of industrial companies, the treatment of rentals and guarantees may offer confusing variations. This question is of particular moment in connection with retail enterprises, theater companies, etc., in which rent or other obligations related to buildings occupied may be an important element in the general picture. Such a building may be owned by the corporation and paid for by a bond issue, in which case the obligation will be fully disclosed in both the balance sheet and the income account. But if another company occupies asimilar building under long-term lease, no separate measure of the rental obligation appears in the income account and no indication thereof can be found in the balance sheet. The second company may *appear* sounder than the first, but that is only because its obligations are undisclosed; essentially, both companies are carrying a similar burden. Conversely, the outright ownership of premises free and clear carries an important advantage (from the standpoint of preferred stock, particularly) over operation under long-term lease, although the capitalization set-up will not reveal this advantage.

*示例：*如果在1929年将Interstate Department Stores Preferred与The Outlet Company Preferred进行比较，两者可能会显得非常相似；两者的盈利覆盖率大致相同，且两家公司都没有任何债券或抵押贷款负债。但实际上The Outlet Company的情况要强得多，因为它拥有自己的土地和建筑物，而Interstate的公司（少数例外情况除外）都是通过租赁取得这些资产的。这种情况的真正影响是给Interstate Department Stores Preferred带来了沉重的固定债务负担，而The Outlet Company则不存在此类问题。在连锁店领域，1932年对J. C. Penney Preferred与S. H. Kress Preferred的比较也能得出类似结论；后者的门店中有超过一半是其自有财产，而Penney的门店几乎都是租用的。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* If Interstate Department Stores Preferred had been compared with The Outlet Company Preferred in 1929 the two exhibits might have appeared closely similar; the earnings coverage averaged about the same, and neither company showed any bond or mortgage liability. But Outlet's position was in actuality by far the stronger, because it owned its land and buildings while those of Interstate (with a minor exception) were held under lease. The real effect of this situation was to place a substantial fixed obligation ahead of Interstate Department Stores Preferred which did not exist in the case of Outlet. In the chain-store field a similar observation would apply to a comparison of J. C. Penney Preferred and S. H. Kress Preferred in 1932; for the latter company owned more than half of its store properties, while nearly all the Penney locations were leased.

**长期租赁负债常被忽视。**直到1931年和1932年，此前经济繁荣时期累积的高额租金给许多商业公司带来了难以承受的负担，长期租赁下的负债问题才引起金融界的重视。

<!--en-->
**Lease Liabilities Generally Overlooked.** The question of liability under long-term leases received very little attention from the financial world until its significance was brought home rudely in 1931 and 1932, when the high level of rentals assumed in the preceding boom years proved intolerably burdensome to many merchandising companies.

*示例：*这一因素对所谓投资证券的影响在United Cigar Stores Preferred的案例中表现得尤为明显。该债券及其前身多年来一直表现出稳定态势，价格也一直保持在较高水平。1928年，该公司报告称“没有有息债务”，且盈利约为优先股股息的七倍。然而，由于其长期租赁负债（以及子公司所持有资产的负债）极为沉重，以至于在1932年公司不得不申请破产，优先股也面临消失的危险。

<!--en-->
*Example:* The influence of this factor upon a supposed investment security is shown with striking force in the case of United Cigar Stores Preferred. This issue, and its predecessor, had for many years shown every sign of stability and had sold accordingly at a consistently high level. For 1928 the company reported "no funded debt" and earnings equal to about seven times the preferred dividend. Yet so crushing were the liabilities under its long-term leases (and to carryproperties acquired by subsidiaries), that in 1932 bankruptcy was resorted to and the preferred stock was menaced with extinction.

**此类负债使分析变得复杂。**必须承认，在那些租金因素至关重要的公司中，租金问题的存在极大地增加了债券或优先股分析的复杂性。幸运的是，由于现在要求在向美国证券交易委员会提交的注册文件中汇总此类租赁负债信息，且每年都必须在10-K表格中注明实际的租金支付金额，投资者现在能够掌握一些相关数据。⁵但问题仍然存在：这些租金是否应全部或部分视为固定费用。当然，在某种程度上，它们确实与固定“间接费用”——如折旧、税收、一般管理费用——类似，而目前人们认为无法将这些费用与债券利息一起计入以计算安全边际。有一种显而易见的解决方案：如果公司在计入租金后的盈利仍能满足标准，那么投资者就不必担心租金问题。*示例：*

<!--en-->
**Such Liabilities Complicated Analysis.** It must be admitted that in the case of companies where the rental factor is important, its obtrusion has badly complicated the whole question of bond or preferred stock analysis. Fortunately the investor now has some data as to the extent of such leasehold obligations, since they are now required to be summarized in registration statements filed with the S.E.C., and the actual rent payments must be stated each year (on Form 10-K).⁵ But the problem remains whether or not these rentals should be treated, in whole or in part, as the equivalent of fixed charges. To some extent, certainly, they are identical rather with fixed “overhead”—e.g., depreciation, taxes, general expense— which it has not been found feasible to add in with bond interest for the purpose of figuring a margin of safety. One type of solution is obvious: If the company meets the earnings test, even after adding rents paid to bond interest, the rent situation need not worry the investor.
*Example:*

### Swift and Company 3³/₄s，到期日1950年

<!--en-->
*Swift and Company 3³/₄s, Due 1950*

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>1934-1938 Average Results</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Balance for dividends</td><td>$8,630,000</td></tr><tr><td>Interest paid</td><td>2,107,000</td></tr><tr><td>Rentals paid</td><td>996,000</td></tr><tr><td>Interest earned</td><td>5.1 times</td></tr><tr><td>Interest and rentals earned</td><td>3.8 times</td></tr></tbody></table>

然而，我们认为要求所有公司都达到如此严格的标准既不公平也不现实。基于对实际数据的分析，可提出以下折中建议：(1) 在计算收益覆盖比率时，将年度租金（用于办公场所）的三分之一计入固定费用（及优先股股息）中；(2) 对于零售企业（连锁店、百货公司），利息加上租金三分之一的最低覆盖比率从3降至2。这一调整是在考虑到租金因素带来的特殊负担后，对零售业相对稳定性的认可。相应地，零售公司优先股所需的覆盖比率将从4降至$2\frac{1}{2}$。

<!--en-->
We feel, however, that it would be neither fair nor practicable to require every company to meet a test so severe. A compromise suggestion based on some study of actual exhibits may be hazarded, viz.: (1) that one-third the annual rentals (for building space) be included with fixed charges (and preferred dividends), to compute the earnings coverage; and (2) that in the case of retail establishments (chain stores, department stores) the minimum coverage required for interest plus one-third of rentals be reduced from 3 to 2. This reduction would recognize the relative stability of retail business, after allowance is made for the special burdenattaching to the rental factor. The corresponding coverage required for a retail company's preferred stock would be reduced from 4 to $2\frac{1}{2}$.

T. Grant 5%优先股——这是一只高价的股票，在1934–1938年间其股息收入几乎是市值的十倍——我们会发现，优先股股息加上三分之一的租金并未完全 $2\frac{1}{2}$次覆盖。**担保债务的状况**。关于担保债务下的收益覆盖计算，还有一些额外的观察值得提出。典型情况下，担保涉及的资产属于整个企业的一部分；因此，由此产生的收益和担保支付都包含在一个单一的损益表中。*示例：* Neisner Realty Corporation 6s，于1948年到期，由Neisner Brothers, Inc.提供担保。该公司的运营和利息费用包含在母公司的合并报表中。当担保证券针对单独运营的资产未偿还时，其状况可能取决于自身业绩或担保人的业绩。因此，该问题只需通过以下三种替代测试中的一种即可： (1) 发行公司的收益，与担保无关；或 (2) 发行公司和担保人公司的综合收益和费用；或 (3) 担保公司的收益与其自身费用及担保相结合。*示例：* Indiana Harbor Belt Railway General 4s和$4\frac{1}{2}$s，于1957年到期。由纽约中央铁路公司及其重要子公司为本金和利息提供担保。Standard Statistics Bond Guide将担保人的收益表示为纽约中央系统。但公司自身的表现要更好，*例如：*

* 1935–1938 average.
Conclusions: Loew's $3\frac{1}{2}$s pass our quantitative test for nonretail bond issues. McLellan Preferred does, but McCrory Preferred does not, pass our suggested test for retail-store preferred stocks.
The four preceding examples illustrate a simplified technique for earnings coverage. Instead of first computing the amount available for the charges, we divide the charges (and preferred dividends) into the balance *after* charges (and preferred dividends) and add 1 to the quotient.
The reader is warned that these suggested standards and the calculations illustrating them are submitted with considerable hesitation. They represent a new departure in analytical method; the data for rentals paid are available only at some effort; most serious of all, the arithmetical standards proposed are arbitrary and perhaps not the best that can bedevised. We might point out, further, that the new test may yield some unexpected results. Note that McLellan Preferred has sold (in 1939) at a lower price than McCrory Preferred—a point that *may* be justified by other factors. Note, further, that if the same calculation as above is applied to W. T. Grant 5% Preferred—a high-priced issue, which earned its dividend nearly ten times over in 1934–1938—we should find that the preferred dividend plus one-third of rentals was covered not quite $2\frac{1}{2}$ times.⁶
**Status of Guaranteed Obligations.** Some additional observations may properly be made as to the computation of earnings coverage in the case of guaranteed obligations. In the typical case the properties involved in the guarantee form part of the whole enterprise; hence both the earnings therefrom and the guaranteed payments are included in a single income statement.
*Example:* Neisner Realty Corporation 6s, due 1948, are guaranteed by Neisner Brothers, Inc. The corporation's operations and interest charges are included in the parent company's consolidated statement.
When the guaranteed security is outstanding against a separately operated property, its standing may depend either on its own results or on those of the guarantor. Hence the issue need be required to pass only one of three alternative tests, based on (1) earnings of issuing company, independent of the guarantee; or (2) combined earnings and charges of the issuing and guarantor companies; or (3) earnings of guarantor company applied to its own charges plus its guarantees.
*Examples: a.* Indiana Harbor Belt Railway General 4s and $4\frac{1}{2}$s, due 1957. Guaranteed as to principal and interest by New York Central Railroad and an important subsidiary. The Standard Statistics Bond Guide gives as the interest coverage that of the guarantor, the New York Central System. But the showing of the company itself is much better, *e.g.*:

Coverage for this issue might best be computed by applying earnings of Canadian Pacific Railway to the total of its own interest charges plus the guaranteed interest on these and other bonds guaranteed by Canadian Pacific Railway.

## 子公司债券

<!--en-->
*SUBSIDIARY COMPANY BONDS*

强势公司的子公司发行的债券通常被认为具有较高的安全性，因为人们认为母公司会承担其所有子公司的债务责任。这种观点得益于常见的合并收益账户设置方式——在这种方式下，所有子公司债券的利息都作为费用从整体收益中扣除，其优先级甚至高于母公司的优先股和普通股。然而，如果母公司并未通过合同约定以担保、租赁或直接承担的方式对子公司债券负责，那么这种表述方式可能会产生误导。因为如果某个子公司出现亏损，母公司可能不会为其债券利息买单，反而可能愿意放弃在该业务领域的投资，并将其转交给该子公司的债券持有人。尽管这种情况较为罕见，但1932–1933年联合药品公司5期债券的案例就有力地证明了这种可能性，该债券1953年到期。

<!--en-->
The bonds of a subsidiary of a strong company are generally regarded as well protected, on the theory that the parent company will take care of all its constituents’ obligations. This viewpoint is encouraged by the common method of setting up consolidated income accounts, under which all the subsidiary bond interest appears as a charge against all the combined earnings, ranking ahead of the parent company’s preferred and common stocks. If, however, the parent concern is not contractually responsible for the subsidiary bonds, by guaranty or lease (or direct assumption), this form of statement may prove to be misleading. For if a particular subsidiary proves unprofitable, its bond interest may conceivably not be taken care of by the parent company, which may be willing to lose its investment in this part of its business and turn it over to the subsidiary’s bondholders. Such a development is unusual, but the possibility thereof wasforcibly demonstrated in 1932–1933 by the history of United Drug Company 5s, due 1953.

*示例：*联合药品公司是药品公司的重要子公司，后者依靠生产专利药品及其他药物持续获得丰厚的利润并派发大量股息。1932年上半年，合并收益账户显示的收益是联合药品公司5期债券利息的十倍，以往几年的数据更是更好。虽然药品公司并未为这些债券提供担保或承担责任，但投资者仍认为综合数据十分理想，因此认为联合药品公司5期债券的安全性毫无问题。然而，作为其资产和业务的一部分，联合药品公司持有路易斯·K·利格特公司的股票，而利格特公司经营着众多药店，同样面临着类似联合雪茄店的租金过高问题。1932年9月，利格特公司通知其房东，若不降低租金，公司将不得不破产。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* United Drug was an important subsidiary of Drug, Inc., which had regularly earned and paid large dividends, gained chiefly from the manufacture of proprietary medicines and other drugs. In the first half of 1932, the consolidated income account showed earnings equal to ten times the interest on United Drug 5s, and the record of previous years was even better. While this issue was not assumed or guaranteed by Drug, Inc., investors considered the combined showing so favorable as to assure the safety of the United Drug 5s beyond question. But United Drug owned, as part of its assets and business, the stock of Louis K. Liggett Company, which operated a large number of drug stores and which was burdened by a high-rental problem similar to that of United Cigar Stores. In September 1932 Liggett's notified its landlords that unless rents were reduced it would be forced into bankruptcy.

这一公告让投资者猛然意识到，尽管药品公司依然繁荣，但它并未为其（间接）子公司利格特公司的债务承担责任，他们立刻也意识到药品公司也不承担联合药品公司5期债券的利息支付责任。这一发现导致这些债券的售价从年初的93点下跌至42点。按此价格计算，4000万美元面值的联合药品公司5期债券仅值1700万美元，而母公司股票的市值仍超过1亿美元（350万股，每股约30美元）。次年，“药品公司体系”被自愿拆分为各个独立部分——这是个不同寻常的情况——联合药品公司重新恢复了完全独立的运营。（此后，该公司的5%利率债券的覆盖率也被证明不足。）

<!--en-->
This announcement brought rudely home to investors the fact that the still prosperous Drug, Inc., was not assuming responsibility for the liabilities of its (indirect) subsidiary, Liggett's, and they immediately became nervously conscious of the fact that Drug, Inc., was not responsible for interest payments on United Drug 5s either. Sales of these bonds resulting from this discovery depressed the price from 93 earlier in the year down to 42. At the latter figure, the $40,000,000 of United Drug 5s were quoted at only $17,000,000, although the parent company's stock was still selling for more than $100,000,000 (3,500,000 shares at about 30). In the following year the “Drug, Inc., System” was voluntarily dissolved into its component parts—an unusual development—and the United Drug Co. resumed its entirely separate existence. (It has since shown an inadequate coverage for the 5% bonds.)

新泽西州综合牵引公司第一系列5期债券，是由新泽西州公共服务公司旗下一家规模庞大但亏损严重的子公司发行的债务。这些债券并未得到母公司的担保。1933年债券到期时，许多持有者接受了母公司提出的每张债券65美元的收购报价。

<!--en-->
Consolidated Traction Company of New Jersey First 5s were obligations of a large but unprofitable subsidiary of Public Service Corporation of New Jersey. The bonds were not guaranteed by the parent company. When they matured in1933 many of the holders accepted an offer of 65 for their bonds made by the parent company.

盐业织布公司第一系列6期债券，1954年到期，是由西德尼·布卢门撒尔公司的一家子公司发行的债务，但同样没有得到母公司的任何担保。布卢门撒尔的合并收益报表在列出可用于支付优先股的资金之前，会先扣除盐业织布公司债券的利息。不过，这些债券在1939年出现了利息违约；1940年时，这些债券的售价仅为7点，而布卢门撒尔的优先股则交易在70点以上。

<!--en-->
Saltex Looms, Inc., 1st 6s, due 1954, were obligations of a subsidiary of Sidney Blumenthal & Co., Inc., but in no way guaranteed by the parent company. The consolidated earning statements of Blumenthal regularly deducted the Saltex bond interest before showing the amount available for its own preferred stock. Interest on the bonds was defaulted, however, in 1939; and in 1940 the bonds sold at 7 while Blumenthal preferred was quoted above 70.

**必须对子公司的利息保障能力进行单独分析。**这些例子表明，正如投资者容易低估强势公司的担保价值一样，他们有时也会犯相反的错误，过分看重一家公司受另一家公司控制这一事实。从固定价值投资的角度来看，没有任何事情是可以想当然的。因此，除非母公司直接为相关债券承担责任，否则不应仅凭母公司的表现就购买子公司债券。在其他情况下，只有子公司自身的财务报告才能作为认可其债券发行的唯一依据。⁷ 如果将上述讨论与第13章的内容进行比较，就会发现，*控股公司*债券的投资者必须坚持要求获得合并财务报表，在该报表中，无论是否有担保，子公司的利息都应作为优先扣除项列示；而非有担保的*子公司*债券的购买者则不能将此类合并报表视为衡量安全性的依据，而必须要求获得仅涉及该子公司的独立报表。这类报表虽然像联合药品5s债券的情况那样难以获取，但仍然必须争取得到。[^1084]：¹ 不过，对于独立的担保公司而言，其担保即便只能提供部分价值，也依然具有实质意义。国家担保公司的破产资产为持有其担保债券的持有人支付了巨额现金。其他一些公司则通过与债券持有人达成某种和解协议来维持偿付能力，即发行新的债券，为利息提供相对较低的担保，但本金则不担保。*示例*：大都会意外伤害公司、马里兰意外伤害公司、美国忠诚与担保公司。2 例如，匹兹堡、韦恩堡和芝加哥铁路公司的优先股及普通股因与宾夕法尼亚铁路公司签订了为期999年的租赁协议而可获得7%的股息，而这些股息也由宾夕法尼亚铁路公司提供担保。

<!--en-->
**Separate Analysis of Subsidiary Interest Coverage Essential.** These examples suggest that just as investors are prone to underestimate the value of a guaranty by a strong company, they sometimes make the opposite mistake and attach undue significance to the fact that a company is controlled by another. From the standpoint of fixed-value investment, nothing of importance may be taken for granted. Hence a subsidiary bond should not be purchased on the basis of the showing of its parent company, unless the latter has assumed direct responsibility for the bond in question. In other cases the exhibit of the subsidiary itself can afford the only basis for the acceptance of its bond issues.⁷
If the above discussion is compared with that in Chap. 13, it will be seen that investors in bonds of a *holding company* must insist upon a consolidated income account, in which the subsidiary interest—whether guaranteed or not—is shown as a prior charge; but that purchasers of unguaranteed *subsidiary* bonds cannot accept such consolidated reports as a measure of their safety, and must require a statement covering the subsidiary alone. These statements may be obtainable only with some difficulty, as was true in the case of United Drug 5s, but they must nevertheless be insisted upon.
[^1084]: ¹ But in the case of the independent surety companies the guarantees proved of substantial, if only partial, value. The bankruptcy estate of National Surety Company yielded a large cash payment to holders of bonds bearing its guarantee. Some of the other companies managed to remain solvent by affecting a kind of composition with bondholders, involving the issuance of new bonds carrying a guarantee of interest at rather low rates, though not of principal. *Examples:*
Metropolitan Casualty Company, Maryland Casualty Company, United States
Fidelity and Guaranty Company.
2 For example Pittsburgh, Fort Wayne and Chicago Railway Company Preferred and Common receive 7% dividends under a 999-year lease to the Pennsylvania Railroad Company. These dividends are also guaranteed by the Pennsylvania.

3 A. S. Dewing在其1934年于纽约出版的《公司证券研究》一书的第293–297页中，对有担保债券作出了如下论述：

<!--en-->
3 A. S. Dewing, in his *A Study of Corporation Securities*, pp. 293–297, New York, 1934, makes the following statements with respect to guaranteed bonds:

“不过，也可能出现这样的情况：出于战略考虑，控股公司或控制公司会继续为亏损的子公司债券支付利息或租金。”（随后列举了一些案例，包括1943年到期的圣安东尼奥和阿兰萨斯帕斯第一4s债券的详细情况，显示发行人在大多数年份都无法覆盖相关费用。）“然而，该铁路线对南太平洋铁路公司线路的重要性使得担保公司非常明智地弥补了债券利息的缺口……尽管存在此类情况，但基本规则依然是：有担保债券的强度不会超过发行它的公司以及其直接覆盖的资产所带来的盈利能力。”

<!--en-->
"There may be, however, instances in which a holding or controlling corporation will maintain the interest or rental on an unprofitable subsidiary's bonds for strategic reasons." (Here follow examples, including details concerning San Antonio and Aransas Pass First 4s, due 1943, showing failure of the issuer to earn its charges in most years.) "Yet its [San Antonio and Aransas Pass Railway's] importance to the Southern Pacific Company's lines is such that the guarantor company very wisely meets the bond interest deficit... In spite of such instances, the rule holds good almost always that the strength of a guaranteed bond is no greater than that of the corporation issuing it and the earning capacity of the property directly covered by it."

在我们看来，这些论述误解了担保项下义务的本质。南太平洋铁路公司弥补圣安东尼奥和阿兰萨斯帕斯债券的利息缺口并非出于“明智”，而是迫于无奈。有担保债券的强度*可能远远高于*发行它的公司，因为这种强度源于持有者对发行公司和担保公司*双重*的索赔权。

<!--en-->
It seems clear to us that these statements misinterpret the essential character of the obligation under a guarantee. Southern Pacific met the San Antonio and Aransas Pass bond interest deficit, not out of "wisdom" but by compulsion. The strength of a guaranteed bond *may be very much greater than* that of the corporation issuing it, because that strength rests upon the dual claim of the holder against *both* the issuing corporation and the guarantor.

4 附录注释31中对担保和租金的一些有趣现象进行了简明阐述，以纽约和哈莱姆铁路公司以及莫比尔和俄亥俄铁路公司的情况为例。
