CHAPTER 21

## 投资持仓的监管

<!--en-->
*Supervision of Investment Holdings*

**“永久性投资”的传统概念。**上一代人眼中，“永久性投资”是金融领域的常用术语之一。它用于形容保守型投资者的典型投资行为，可以说包含三个核心要素：（1）打算无限期持有；（2）仅关注年度收益，而不考虑本金价值的波动；（3）无需担心会影响公司的未来发展。按照定义，优质投资就是那种可以买入后置之不理、除非在付息日才需要关注的资产。

<!--en-->
**Traditional Concept of “Permanent Investment.”** A generation ago “permanent investment” was one of the stock phrases of finance. It was applied to the typical purchase by a conservative investor and may be said to have embraced three constituent ideas: (1) intention to hold for an indefinite period; (2) interest solely in annual income, without reference to fluctuations in the value of principal; and (3) freedom from concern over future developments affecting the company. A sound investment was by definition one that could be bought, put away, and forgotten except on coupon or dividend dates.

1920–1922年的经济萧条所带来的糟糕经历首次严重动摇了这种对高等级投资的传统看法。那些被投资者视为绝对安全、无需仔细审视的证券却遭受了巨大损失。随后的七年虽然总体较为繁荣，但对不同类别的投资产品的影响却大相径庭，以至于“金边证券”所代表的那种绝对安全的感觉逐渐受到削弱。因此，早在1929年市场崩溃之前，华尔街就已经认识到忽视先前投资可能带来的风险，以及定期审查或监督所有持仓的必要性，这已成为一项新的准则。这一原则与以往的做法截然相反，常被概括为“不存在永久性投资”。

<!--en-->
This traditional view of high-grade investments was first seriously called into question by the unsatisfactory experiences of the 1920–1922 depression. Large losses were taken on securities that their owners had considered safe beyond the need of examination. The ensuing seven years, although generally prosperous, affected different groups of investment issues in such divergent ways that the old sense of complete security—with which the term “gilt-edged securities” was identified—suffered an ever-increasing impairment. Hence even before the market collapse of 1929, the danger ensuing from neglect of investments previously made, and the need for periodic scrutiny or supervision of all holdings, had been recognized as a new canon in Wall Street. This principle, directly opposed to the former practice, is frequently summed up in the dictum, “There are no permanent investments.”

## **定期检查持仓是必要的——但**

<!--en-->
**Periodic Inspection of Holdings Necessary—but**

**麻烦重重。** 新观点能够以固定价值投资的现实作为依据，这一点几乎无可争议。但必须坦率地承认，对所有证券持有量进行监管的这一必要性，实际上是对固定价值投资理念本身相当严重的质疑。如果除了最初的艰难选择之外，还必须通过持续的监管才能将损失风险降至最低，那么这种投资方式难道不比其价值带来的好处更多麻烦吗？假设普通投资者遵循此处推荐的保守选择标准，在多元化的企业证券组合中能获得$3\frac{1}{2}\%$的平均收益。这一$3\frac{1}{2}\%$的回报率显然高于长期美国国债所能提供的$2\frac{1}{2}\%$，也优于储蓄银行给出的2或$2\frac{1}{2}\%$的收益。然而，如果我们不仅考虑进行恰当选择所需的努力，还要考虑后续反复检查所带来的更大负担，再加上依然无法避免的贬值或实际损失风险，就必须承认，确实存在相当有力的论据可以质疑固定价值投资整体的合理性。过去那种认为投资应永久且毫无麻烦的观点，是基于这样一种合乎逻辑的想法：如果一种回报有限的投资都不能被视为毫无麻烦，那它根本就不值得投入。

<!--en-->
**Troublesome.** That the newer view is justified by the realities of fixed-value investment can scarcely be questioned. But it must be frankly recognized also that this same necessity for supervision of all security holdings implies a rather serious indictment of the whole concept of fixed-value investment. If risk of loss can be minimized only by the exercise of constant supervisory care, in addition to the painstaking process of initial choice, has not such investment become more trouble than it is worth? Let it be assumed that the typical investor, following the conservative standards of selection herein recommended, will average a yield of $3\frac{1}{2}\%$ on a diversified list of corporate securities. This $3\frac{1}{2}\%$ return appears substantially higher than the $2\frac{1}{2}\%$ obtainable from long-term United States government bonds and also more attractive than the 2 or $2\frac{1}{2}\%$ offered by savings banks. Nevertheless, if we take into account not only the effort required to make a proper selection but also the greater efforts entailed by the subsequent repeated check-ups, and if we then add thereto the still inescapable risk of depreciation or definite loss, it must be confessed that a rather plausible argument can be constructed against the advisability of fixed-value investments in general. The old idea of permanent, trouble-free holdings was grounded on the not illogical feeling that if a limited-return investment could not be regarded as trouble-free it was not worth making at all.

**美国储蓄债券的优势。** 客观来看，过去十年的投资经验无疑表明，人们更倾向于选择（1）美国国债或储蓄银行存款；（2）虽具有投机性，但通过巧妙操作试图降低风险并提高利润的投资方式；或（3）寻求本金安全与较高盈利机会相结合的特殊投资产品。对于所有收入水平适中的人而言，美国储蓄债券无疑是固定价值投资最合适的工具。事实上，我们甚至可以断言，按照1940年的利率水平计算，它们相比其他同类产品具有明显优势，是这类投资中*唯一*明智的选择。原因在于，除少数例外情况外，其他投资产品很难在不承担本金风险的情况下获得更高的回报，而这种风险会使得投资行为变得不可取。此外，持有者可在债券到期前随时赎回，这也是该债券极为宝贵的特点。倘若广大小投资者能够坚决拒绝那些打着“4%到6%稳定收益”旗号、名目繁多的“储蓄计划”，转而选择美国储蓄债券2.90%的收益，我们相信他们总体上能够节省大量金钱、麻烦以及心理上的痛苦。

<!--en-->
**Superiority of United States Savings Bonds.** Objectively considered, investment experience of the last decade undoubtedly points away from the fixed-value security field and into the direction of (1) United States government bonds or savings-bank deposits; or (2) admittedly speculative operations, with endeavors to reduce risk and increase profits by means of skillful effort; or (3) a search for the exceptional combination of safety of principal with a chance for substantial profit. For all people of moderate means United States Savings Bonds undoubtedly offer the most suitable medium for fixed-value investment. In fact we are inclined to state categorically that, on the basis of 1940 interest yields,their superiority to other issues makes them the *only* sensible purchase of this type. The reason is, of course, that it is not possible to obtain a significantly higher return on investment issues (save for a few obscure exceptions) without injecting an element of principal risk which makes the commitment unsound. In addition the holder's redemption right before maturity is a very valuable feature of the bonds. If only small investors as a class would resolutely reject the various types of "savings plans," with their multifarious titles, now being offered to them with an ostensible "sure income return" of 4 to 6%, and thankfully take advantage of the 2.90% available on United States Savings Bonds, we are convinced that they would save in the aggregate an enormous amount of money, trouble and heartbreak.

即便大多数投资者的常规投资问题都能如此轻易解决，仍会有许多投资者需要考虑其他类型的固定价值投资。这些投资者包括：（1）各类机构投资者，*例如*储蓄银行、商业银行、保险公司、教育及慈善机构；（2）其他大型投资者，*例如*企业和富人；（3）那些全部收入来自投资且收入水平适中的人群，因为美国储蓄债券每年可获得的最高回报上限仅为2,500美元。¹ 同样，也有许多小型投资者会出于各种原因，选择将部分资金投入其他类型的固定价值投资中。

<!--en-->
But even if the ordinary investment problems of most investors could be thus simply disposed of, many investors would remain who must consider other types of fixed-value investment. These include: (1) institutional investors of all kinds, *e.g.*, savings and commercial banks, insurance companies, educational and philanthropic agencies; (2) other large investors, *e.g.*, corporations and wealthy individuals; (3) those with moderate income derived wholly from investments, since the maximum annual return ultimately obtainable from United States Savings Bonds is limited to $2,500 per annum.¹ It is true also that many smaller investors will for one reason or another prefer to place part of their funds in other types of fixed-value investment.

第二种选择，即通过投机而非投资来获利，对于那些依靠储蓄或企业利润积累资本的普通人而言，风险实在太大。无知、人类贪婪、从众心理、交易成本，以及内部人士和操纵者对市场规则的扭曲，²这些负面因素的综合影响，将远远超过投机在理论上所谓的优势——投机虽然需要承担风险，但能带来盈利可能。的确，我们一直反对在没有相应盈利机会的情况下承担明确的风险。不过，我们并非主张用投机取代投资，而只是认为在那些明显不合理且不明智的投资方式面前，应选择明智的投机策略。我们坚信，只要精心挑选，固定价值投资能为公众带来远比投机更好的回报，即便投机可能借助大量的金融知识作为支撑。投资的结果或许会令人失望；但若是如此，投机带来的后果则将是灾难性的。

<!--en-->
The second alternative, *viz.*, to speculate instead of investing, is entirely too dangerous for the typical person who is building up his capital out of savings or business profits. The disadvantages of ignorance, of human greed, of mob psychology, of trading costs, of weighting of the dice by insiders and manipulators,² will in the aggregate far overbalance the purely theoretical superiority of speculation in that it offers profit possibilities in return for the assumption of risk. We have, it is true, repeatedly argued against the acceptance of an admitted risk to principal without the presence of a compensating chance for profit. In so doing, however, we have not advocated speculation in place ofinvestment but only intelligent speculation in preference to obviously unsound and ill-advised forms of investment. We are convinced that the public generally will derive far better results from fixed-value investments, if selected with exceeding care, than from speculative operations, even though these may be aided by considerable education in financial matters. It may well be that the results of investment will prove disappointing; but if so, the results of speculation would have been disastrous.

第三种选择——寻找兼具投资价值与盈利机会的资产——我们认为，这正是证券分析师才能得以发挥的合适领域。但对于未经培训的投资者来说，这是一个危险的目标。他们很容易被说服，认为只有有前景的资产才是安全的，或者相反，认为仅凭吸引人的统计数据就足以成为购买的理由。

<!--en-->
The third alternative—to look for investment merit combined with an opportunity for profit—presents, we believe, a suitable field for the talents of the securities analyst. But it is a dangerous objective to hold before the untrained investor. He can readily be persuaded that safety exists where there is only promise or, conversely, that an attractive statistical showing is alone sufficient to warrant purchase.

在探讨了资本持有者可选择的三种策略之后，我们发现，对于许多个人和企业而言，在传统的高等级债券和优先股领域进行固定价值投资仍是一项必要且理想的活动。同时也很明显，为了降低损失风险，有必要定期重新审视投资组合。那么，在这种监督过程中可以遵循哪些原则和实用方法呢？

<!--en-->
Having thus considered the three alternative policies open to those with capital funds, we see that fixed-value investment in the traditional field of high-grade bonds and preferred stocks remains a necessary and desirable activity for many individuals and corporate bodies. It is quite clear also that periodic reexamination of investment holdings is necessary to reduce the risk of loss. What principles and practical methods can be followed in such supervision?

**系统监督的原则与问题；资产转换。**人们普遍认为，投资者应定期检查自己的持仓，判断这些资产是否仍然完全安全；如果某只资产的状况出现疑问，就应将其替换为更优质的资产。在进行此类“转换”时，投资者必须准备好接受所出售资产带来的适度损失，并将该损失从其总投资收益中扣除。

<!--en-->
**Principles and Problems of Systematic Supervision; Switching.** It is generally understood that the investor should examine his holdings at intervals to see whether or not all of them may still be regarded as entirely safe and that if the soundness of any issue has become questionable, he should exchange it for a better one. In making such a “switch” the investor must be prepared to accept a moderate loss on the holding he sells out, which loss he must charge against his aggregate investment income.

在系统投资监督的早期，这一策略效果极为出色。高等级的成熟证券往往能顽强地维持其既定的价格水平，其内在价值的逐步恶化往往要等到通过分析才发现。因此，敏锐的投资者可以将这类资产卖给那些被该证券的声誉以及相比同类其他资产较低的折价所吸引、却毫无戒心的投资者。证券市场的非人格化特性使得这种做法免于道德上的指责，人们仅仅将其视为对聪明才智的合理回报，以及对疏忽大意的应有惩罚。

<!--en-->
In the early years of systematic investment supervision, this policy worked out extremely well. Seasoned securities of the high-grade type tended to cling rather tenaciously to their established price levels and frequently failed to reflect a progressive deterioration of their intrinsic position until sometime after this impairment was discoverable by analysis. It was possible, therefore, for the alert investor to sell out such holdings to some heedless and unsuspecting victim, who was attracted by the reputation of the issue and the slight discount at which it was obtainable in comparison with other issues of its class. The impersonal character of the securities market relieves this procedure of any ethical stigma, and it is considered merely as establishing a proper premium for shrewdness and a deserved penalty for lack of care.

*证券价格的敏感度提升。*然而近年来，投资标的已经失去了所谓的“价格惯性”，其报价能够迅速反映任何重大的不利变化。这一事实给保持投资质量所需的有效资产转换带来了严重困难。等到证券的实际价值确实出现下降时，其价格可能不仅已跌至投机性水平，甚至低于基于收益下降幅度所预期的水平。³（这种过度下跌的一个原因是，不利的表面趋势对价格的影响甚至超过了绝对收益数据本身。）投资者天生不愿承受巨大损失，再加上他们合理地认为自己正在以过低的價格出售该资产，这往往使他们几乎不可避免地不得不对该证券采取投机态度。

<!--en-->
*Increased Sensitivity of Security Prices.* In more recent years, however, investment issues have lost what may have been called their “price inertia,” and their quotations have come to reflect promptly any materially adverse development. This fact creates a serious difficulty in the way of effective switching to maintain investment quality. By the time that any real impairment of security is manifest, the issue may have fallen in price not only to a speculative level but to a level even lower than the decline in earnings would seem to justify.³ (One reason for this excessive price decline is that an unfavorable apparent *trend* has come to influence prices even more severely than the absolute earnings figures.) The owner’s natural reluctance to accept a large loss is reinforced by the reasonable belief that he would be selling the issue at an unduly low price, and he is likely to find himself compelled almost unavoidably to assume a speculative position with respect to that security.

**极高的安全边际，为投资免于疑虑提供保障。** 应对这一难题的唯一有效方法，就是在最初进行投资时遵循尽善尽美的原则。从量化指标来看，该投资所享有的安全程度必须远远超过最低标准，即便出现大幅贬值，其地位也不必受到质疑。这样的策略能将投资者日后会对其产生疑虑的资产比例降至极低水平。同时，它还能让投资者在相关资产的表现仍相对强劲、市场价格更有可能保持稳定的时候进行交易。

<!--en-->
**Exceptional Margins of Safety as Insurance Against Doubt.** The only effective means of meeting this difficulty lies in following counsels of perfection in making the original investment. The degree of safety enjoyed by the issue, as shown by quantitative measures, must be so far in *excess* of the minimum standards that a large shrinkage can be suffered before its position need be called into question. Such a policy should reduce to a very small figure the proportion of holdings about which the investor will subsequently find himself in doubt. It would also permit him to make his exchanges when the showing of the issue is still comparatively strong and while, therefore, there is a better chance that the market price will have been maintained.

*案例与结论。* 举个具体例子，假设投资者购买了利吉特与迈尔斯烟草公司1951年到期的5美元债券。在1934年至1938年间，该债券的利息收益平均接近20倍，而最低要求仅为3倍。如果利润下降导致收益倍数降至4倍，他可能会考虑转投其他能带来8至10倍利息收益的债券（如果能找到的话）。基于这些假设，他仍有较大机会以全价卖出利吉特与迈尔斯公司的债券，因为其表现依然十分出色。但如果盈利下滑的趋势导致该债券的报价出现大幅折价，他则可能选择继续持有，而非承受可观的损失。这样一来，他就能享受到一个巨大优势：即能够确信自己的投资安全并未真正面临危险。

<!--en-->
*Example and Conclusion.* As a concrete example, let us assume that the investor buys an issue such as the Liggett and Myers Tobacco Company Debenture 5s, due 1951, which earned their interest an average of nearly twenty times in 1934–1938, as compared with the minimum requirement of three times. If a decline in profits should reduce the coverage to four times, he might prefer to switch into some other issue (if one can be found) that is earning its interest eight to ten times. On these assumptions he would have a fair chance of obtaining a full price for the Liggett and Myers issue, since it would still be making an impressive exhibit. But if the influence of the downward trend of earnings has depressed the quotation to a large discount, then he could decide to retain the issue rather than accept an appreciable loss. In so doing he would have the great advantage of being able to feel that the safety of investment was still not in any real danger.

在出现严重经济衰退和市场动荡时期，这种要求极高安全边际的策略显然会尤为有益。然而，将其作为所有投资者的标准做法并不可行，因为这类具备强大支撑力的资产供应极为有限，而且当当前市场状况乐观时，投资者采取极端预防措施以避免未来崩溃也违背了人性。⁴ **经济衰退时期的策略。** 假设投资者在选择固定价值资产时仅采取了合理的谨慎态度，那么在经济衰退期间他会如何应对？又应遵循何种策略？如果衰退程度较轻，他的投资在市场价格方面只会受到轻微影响，其内在价值受到的影响则更小。但如果情况类似1930年至1933年，他便无法避免股价大幅下跌以及对资产安全性的极大担忧。但任何理性的固定价值投资策略都需假定1930年至1933年那种规模的波动不会再次发生，因此无需专门防范。如果将1921年至1922年及1937年至1938年的情况视为“周期性严重衰退”的典型，那么精心挑选的投资组合在这种时期仍能取得相当不错的表现。投资者不应因当前盈利下降就匆忙抛售那些过往表现良好的资产。不过，他们很可能会比平时更加重视提升证券质量的问题，在许多情况下，通过经过深思熟虑的资产置换也能获得一些收益。

<!--en-->
Such a policy of demanding very high safety margins would obviously prove especially beneficial if a period of acute depression and market unsettlement should supervene. It is not practicable, however, to recommend this as a standard practice for all investors, because the supply of such strongly buttressed issues is too limited, and because, further, it is contrary to human nature for investors to take *extreme* precautions against future collapse when current conditions make for optimism.⁴
**Policy in Depression.** Assuming that the investor has exercised merely reasonable caution in the choice of his fixed-value holdings, how will he fare and what policy should he follow in a period of depression? If the depression is a moderate one, his investments should be only mildly affected marketwise and still less in their intrinsic position. If conditions should approximate those of 1930–1933, he could not hope to escape a severe shrinkage in the quotations and considerable uneasiness over the safety of his holdings. But any reasoned policy of fixed-value investment requires the assumption that disturbances of the 1930–1933 amplitude are nonrecurring in their nature and need not be specifically guarded against in the future. If the 1921–1922 and the 1937–1938 experiences are accepted instead as typical of the“recurrent severe depression,” a carefully selected investment list should give a reasonably good account of itself in such a period. The investor should not be stampeded into selling out holdings with a strong past record because of a current decline in earnings. He is likely, however, to pay more attention than usual to the question of improving the quality of his securities, and in many cases it should be possible to gain some benefits through carefully considered switches.

1937年至1938年的“经济衰退”为上述分析提供了有力佐证。实际上，几乎所有在1936年底就能满足我们严格标准的优质证券，都在随后的经济低迷期中未遭受严重的市场损害。但那些尽管整体收益倍数不足却仍以高价格出售的债券——尤其是大量铁路行业发行的债券——其价值则出现了巨大缩水。（详见第7章的相关讨论以及附录注释11和13。）

<!--en-->
The experiences of the 1937–1938 “recession” offer strong corroboration of the foregoing analysis. Practically all senior securities that would have met our stringent requirements at the end of 1936 came through the ensuing setback without serious damage marketwise. But bonds that have sold at high levels despite an inadequate over-all earnings coverage—particularly a large number of railroad issues—suffered an enormous shrinkage in value. (See our discussion in Chap. 7 and also Appendix Notes 11 and 13.)

**投资建议与监管的来源。** 对证券的监管涉及谁来监管以及如何监管的问题。投资者可以选择多种机构来承担这一职责，其中较为重要的包括以下几类：

<!--en-->
**Sources of Investment Advice and Supervision.** Supervision of securities involves the question of who should do it as well as how to do it. Investors have the choice of various agencies for this purpose, of which the more important are the following:

1. 投资者本人。
2. 他的商业银行。
3. 投资银行（或承销机构）。
4. 纽约证券交易所的会员公司。
5. 大型信托公司的咨询部门。
6. 独立投资顾问或监管服务。后两家机构会就其服务收取费用，而前三家则免费提供建议与信息。⁵ *来自商业银行家的建议。* 除非投资者具备足以专业指导他人的培训与经验，否则不应仅依赖自己作为唯一顾问。在大多数情况下，他至少应通过与他人商讨来补充自己的判断。向自己的银行咨询投资事宜的做法十分普遍，且无疑能带来巨大益处，尤其是对小型投资者而言。若能坚持这样做，几乎可以完全避免受到高压股票推销员及其毫无价值的“美好前景”营销手段的欺骗。⁶ 然而，商业银行家是否最适合为有资金的投资者提供顾问服务仍值得怀疑。尽管他们的判断通常较为可靠，但对证券的了解可能略显肤浅，而且无法指望他们投入足够时间来全面分析客户的持仓与问题。*来自投资银行的建议。* 对投资银行的顾问服务还有另一种反对意见：一家自身也有证券需要出售的机构，难以做到完全公正的指导。无论其目标多么合乎道德，自身利益的驱使必然会影响其判断。尤其是当提供建议的是那些依靠说服客户购买公司“库存”证券为生的债券推销员时，这种情况更为明显。的确，声誉良好的承销机构会认为自己在某种程度上对客户负有信托责任。它们努力为客户提供合理的建议并销售合适的证券，这不仅源于良好的商业惯例，更源于职业伦理准则的要求。尽管如此，证券销售并非一种职业，而是一种商业行为，因此必然以商业方式开展。虽然在典型交易中，让买家获得完整价值与满意体验对卖方有利，但有时双方的利益可能会出现严重冲突。因此，要求投资银行充当证券买方的公正顾问既不现实，在某种意义上也不公平；总体而言，投资者主要依赖证券卖方的建议也是不明智的。*来自纽约证券交易所公司的建议。* 大型证券交易所公司的投资部门则呈现出略有不同的状况。虽然它们在客户的交易中也有经济利益，但其建议往往更加严谨且完全公正。证券交易所公司通常并不拥有待售证券。尽管有时它们会参与销售业务，并从中获得比普通市场佣金更高的报酬，但与实际持有这些证券的承销机构相比，它们推动此类个别证券发行的积极性要低得多。归根结底，对于这些公司而言，投资业务或债券部门更多是作为其信誉的象征，而非盈利来源。针对它们是投机机构的指责，可以通过指出其为保守型投资者提供的必要服务来部分回应。因此，若投资者就小额债券购买事宜咨询大型证券交易所公司，很可能会得到与其所支付的佣金完全不成比例的时间与关注。诚然，从纯粹的商业角度来看，这种做法最终是盈利的，因为一部分债券客户日后会转变为活跃的股票交易者。 代表各证券交易所需要说明的是，它们并不会试图劝说其债券客户转而从事股票投机，但证券经纪公司的氛围或许仍具有某种诱惑力。*投资顾问的建议*。虽然按费用提供投资建议的理念并非新鲜事，但它直到最近才发展成一项重要的金融业务。目前，这项工作由大型信托公司的专门部门、统计服务部门的某个分支，以及自称为投资顾问或投资咨询师的私人公司负责。这类机构的优势在于能够保持完全的公正性，既无销售任何证券的动机，也不从客户的交易中获取佣金。其主要缺点则是服务成本，平均约为相关本金的每年1/2%。若严格应用于投资基金，这一费用将约占其年收益的1/7或1/8，这一比例显然相当可观。为让收费显得不那么沉重，一些私人投资咨询师会试图预测债券市场的整体走势，并向客户建议何时买入或卖出。不过，投资者能否通过买卖债券来把握市场波动并取得成功仍值得怀疑。如果能够预测债券市场的走势，那么股票市场的走势也应同样可以预测，此时在股票交易方面无疑会比债券交易更具技术优势。我们对任何付费机构能否提供关于债券或股票市场走势的可靠预测持怀疑态度。此外，我们坚信，试图同时就个别高评级投资的选择以及债券*价格*的走势提供建议的做法在根本上是不合逻辑且令人困惑的。尽管投资者很希望能在恰当时机买入，在价格即将下跌时卖出，但经验表明，他们很难在这方面取得巨大成功；而且，将交易因素引入投资操作只会扰乱资本的收益回报，使其兴趣不可避免地转向投机领域。由于标准高评级投资的收益相对较低，目前尚不清楚按费用提供建议是否能在该领域取得理想效果。在纯粹的投机领域，反对付费咨询的理由是：如果顾问真的懂行，他就不必从事咨询工作了。或许，证券顾问这一职业最适宜的应用领域位于中间地带——即处理因投资贬值而产生的问题，提出有利的交换方案，并推荐那些售价远低于其内在价值的廉价债券。[^1242]：¹ 此数据基于每人每年允许的最高7,500美元限额。在持续投资满十年后，由于每年有10,000美元的债券到期并更换为新的7,500美元投资额，因此每年可获得2,500美元的收益。² 1934年《证券交易法》的实施大大降低了这一数值。³ 自1933年以来，许多铁路债券成了这一规律的例外。例如，1948年到期的巴尔的摩与俄亥俄铁路第一系列4年期债券，在1936年的售价为$109\frac{1}{2}$，尽管其利息支出总额的覆盖比率早已过低。1938年，这些债券的售价则为$34\frac{1}{4}$。⁴ 然而，我们必须提醒读者，仅凭极高的利息支出覆盖比率并不能完全保证安全性。一旦出现经营亏损，无论原本的安全边际有多高，都会被消除。因此，正如我们在第2章的斯图贝克案例中所强调的那样，内在稳定性才是不可或缺的要求。 5 越来越多的证券交易所公司开始按收费模式提供投资建议。6 在美国证券交易委员会的监管下，传统意义上的“天马行空式上市”已基本从州际商业活动中消失，取而代之的是那些规模虽小但看似合法的企业，它们却以过高的价格向公众出售。正如纽约市商业改进局1938年的报告所示，其他多种类型的欺诈行为依然相当普遍。

<!--en-->
1. The investor himself.
2. His commercial bank.
3. An investment banking (or underwriting) house.
4. A New York Stock Exchange firm.
5. The advisory department of a large trust company.
6. Independent investment counsel or supervisory service.
The last two agencies charge fees for their service, whereas the three preceding supply advice and information gratis.⁵
*Advice from Commercial Bankers.* The investor should not be his own sole consultant unless he has training and experience sufficient to qualify him to advise others professionally. In most cases he should at least supplement his own judgment by conference with others. The practice ofconsulting one's bank about investments is widespread, and it is undeniably of great benefit, especially to the smaller investor. If followed consistently it would afford almost complete protection against the hypnotic wiles of the high-pressure stock salesman and his worthless "blue sky" flotations.⁶ It is doubtful, however, if the commercial banker is the most suitable adviser to an investor of means. Although his judgment is usually sound, his knowledge of securities is likely to be somewhat superficial, and he cannot be expected to spare the time necessary for a thoroughgoing analysis of his clients' holdings and problems.
*Advice from Investment Banking Houses.* There are objections of another kind to the advisory service of an investment banking house. An institution with securities of its own to sell cannot be looked to for entirely impartial guidance. However ethical its aims may be, the compelling force of self-interest is bound to affect its judgment. This is particularly true when the advice is supplied by a bond salesman whose livelihood depends upon persuading his customers to buy the securities that his firm has "on its shelves." It is true that the reputable underwriting houses consider themselves as bound in some degree by a fiduciary responsibility toward their clients. The endeavor to give them sound advice and to sell them suitable securities arises not only from the dictates of good business practice but more compellingly from the obligations of a professional code of ethics.
Nevertheless, the sale of securities is not a profession but a business and is necessarily carried on as such. Although in the typical transaction it is to the advantage of the seller to give the buyer full value and satisfaction, conditions may arise in which their interests are in serious conflict. Hence it is impracticable, and in a sense unfair, to require investment banking houses to act as impartial advisers to buyers of securities; and, broadly speaking, it is unwise for the investor to rely primarily upon the advice of sellers of securities.
*Advice from New York Stock Exchange Firms.* The investment departments of the large Stock Exchange firms present a somewhat different picture. Although they also havea pecuniary interest in the transactions of their customers, their advice is much more likely to be painstaking and thoroughly impartial. Stock Exchange houses do not ordinarily own securities for sale. Although at times they participate in selling operations, which carry larger allowances than the ordinary market commission, their interest in pushing such individual issues is less vital than that of the underwriting houses who actually own them. At bottom, the investment business or bond department of Stock Exchange firms is perhaps more important to them as a badge of respectability than for the profits it yields. Attacks made upon them as agencies of speculation may be answered in part by pointing to the necessary services that they render to conservative investors. Consequently, the investor who consults a large Stock Exchange firm regarding a small bond purchase is likely to receive time and attention out of all proportion to the commission involved. Admittedly this practice is found profitable in the end, as a cold business proposition, because a certain proportion of the bond customers later develop into active stock traders. In behalf of the Stock Exchange houses it should be said that they make no effort to persuade their bond clients to speculate in stocks, but the atmosphere of a brokerage office is perhaps not without its seductive influence.
*Advice from Investment Counsel.* Although the idea of giving investment advice on a fee basis is not a new one, it has only recently developed into an important financial activity. The work is now being done by special departments of large trust companies, by a division of the statistical services, and by private firms designating themselves as investment counsel or investment consultants. The advantage of such agencies is that they can be entirely impartial, having no interest in the sale of any securities or in any commission on their client's transactions. The chief disadvantage is the cost of the service, which averages about 1/2% per annum on the principal involved. As applied strictly to investment funds this charge would amount to about 1/7 or 1/8 of the annual income, which must be considered substantial.
In order to make their fees appear less burdensome, some of the private investment consultants endeavor to forecast the general course of the bond market and to advise their clients as to when to buy or sell. It is doubtful if trading in bonds, to catch the market swings, can be carried on successfully by the investor. If the course of the bond market can be predicted, it should be possible to predict that of the stock market as well, and there would be undoubted technical advantages in trading in stocks rather than in bonds. We are sceptical of the ability of any paid agency to provide reliable forecasts of the market action of either bonds or stocks. Furthermore we are convinced that any combined effort to advise upon the choice of individual high-grade investments and upon the course of bond *prices* is fundamentally illogical and confusing. Much as the investor would like to be able to buy at just the right time and to sell out when prices are about to fall, experience shows that he is not likely to be brilliantly successful in such efforts and that by injecting the trading element into his investment operations he will disrupt the income return on his capital and inevitably shift his interest into speculative directions.
It is not clear as yet whether or not advice on a fee basis will work out satisfactorily in the field of standard high-grade investments, because of their relatively small income return. In the purely speculative field the objection to paying for advice is that if the adviser *knew* whereof he spoke he would not need to bother with a consultant's duties. It may be that the profession of adviser on securities will find its most practicable field in the intermediate region, where the adviser will deal with problems arising from depreciated investments, and where he will propose advantageous exchanges and recommend bargain issues selling considerably below their intrinsic value.
[^1242]: ¹ This is based on the maximum $7,500 permitted each year to one individual. After the tenth year of continued investment, an annual income of $2,500 would accrue via the maturity of a $10,000 unit each year and its replacement by a new $7,500 subscription.
² This factor has been greatly reduced by the operation of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
3 Many railroad bonds have proved an exception to this statement since 1933. Note, for example, that Baltimore and Ohio Railroad First 4s, due 1948, sold at $109\frac{1}{2}$ in 1936, although the margin over total interest charges had long been much too small. In 1938 these bonds sold at $34\frac{1}{4}$.
4 We must caution the reader, however, against assuming that very large coverage of interest charges is, in itself, a complete assurance of safety. An operating loss eliminates the margin of safety, however high it may have been. Hence, inherent stability is an essential requirement, as we emphasize in our Studebaker example given in Chap. 2.
5 A growing number of Stock Exchange firms now supply investment advice on a fee basis.
6 Under S.E.C. supervision the “blue-sky flotation” of the old school has largely disappeared from interstate commerce, its place being taken by small but presumably legitimate enterprises which are sold to the public at excessively high prices. Numerous other types of fraud are still fairly prevalent, as can be seen from the 1938 report of the Better Business Bureau of New York City.

## 投资困境信贷资产

*Investing in Distressed Credit*

作者：多米尼克·米埃尔 《格雷厄姆与多德》这本书给人一种沉甸甸的厚重感——书本很重，书脊格外宽厚。作者的名字听起来就带有权威感，仿佛直接出自《了不起的盖茨比》的宾客名单。他们的用词充满富有感染力的华丽表达。或许我显得乏味，但我从未想过工作中会有什么东西会“轻易成为粗心者代价高昂的陷阱。”（第22章）本杰明·格雷厄姆创造的“市场先生”这一隐喻会让你不寒而栗，因为它太精准地描绘了业内人士的形象。

<!--en-->
by Dominique Mielle
There is a certain gravity to Graham and Dodd. The book in your hands feels heavy and substantial, the spine is extra wide. There is a sense of the Establishment in the authors' names, sounding like something straight out of a *Great Gatsby* guestlist. Their vocabulary tickles with evocative flourishes. Call me dull, but I never thought anything in my job could “easily prove a costly snare to the unwary.” (Chap. 22) You flinch at the allegory of “Mr. Market” created by Benjamin Graham, because it is too apt a description of the people in the industry.

据《华尔街日报》报道，这就是现代价值投资的源头著作。¹ 是的，我也得查一下这个词的意思。

<!--en-->
This, according to the *Wall Street Journal*, is the urtext of modern value investing.¹ Yes, I too had to look up this word.

因此，Z世代认为《证券分析》的最佳用途是支撑笔记本电脑以便进行Zoom视频通话，这并非完全不合逻辑。而且你的判断没错——这本出色的书籍除了诸多优点外，还会让摄像头正好处于与你眼睛平行的位置，这无疑是最具吸引力的拍摄角度。

<!--en-->
Thus it would not be entirely illogical for Generation Z to conclude that the best use of *Security Analysis* is to prop up their laptop for a Zoom call. And you would be correct in assessing that this remarkable book, among many benefits, will put the camera exactly at your eye level, which is undeniably the most attractive video angle.

在让价值投资的奠基者们重新焕发21世纪的活力之后，让我来澄清一下本杰明·格雷厄姆的真实面貌，因为他的故事远不止表面所见。首先，格雷厄姆出生时姓格罗斯鲍姆，是一名贫困的犹太移民，为了融入美国社会并避免反犹主义，他的姓氏被改掉了。其次，他似乎很喜欢这样一句座右铭：“希望每天都能做点愚蠢的事、创造点新意，再行点慷慨之举。”我想，如果封面上有这样的副标题，我们的资产管理业务会吸引不同的人群。的确，这是一句亲切且易于共鸣的格言，非常适合那些极其成功的投资者。我说的就是你，沃伦·巴菲特——91岁高龄仍坐着高尔夫球车四处奔波，承诺捐出99%的财富，却依然掌管着地球上最值钱的公司之一。更不用说波士顿的预言家塞思·克拉曼了，他恰好邀请我为本书撰写序言，这样一来“慷慨”与“愚蠢”这两点就同时得到了体现。最后，格雷厄姆还能引用克尔凯郭尔的话（给各位对冲基金经理的提示：这不是某种手工啤酒的名字）。这是《格雷厄姆与多德》给我们的第一课：不要以貌取人，不要轻信第一印象，不要草率下结论。

<!--en-->
Having propelled the founding fathers of value investing into acute twenty-first century relevance, let me set the record straight on Benjamin Graham, for there is more to him than meets the eye. First, Graham was born Grossbaum, a poor Jewish immigrant whose family name was changed to assimilate into American society and avoid antisemitism. Second, he was apparently fond of the axiom that he wished “every day to do something foolish, something creative, and something generous.” I suspect we would attract a different crowd to asset management with that subtitle on the cover. Indeed, it is an endearing and relatable motto, well-suited to some spectacularly successful investors. I am looking at you,Warren Buffett, zipping around on the back of a golf cart at 91 years old, having pledged 99% of your fortune and still leading one of the most valuable companies on earth. Not to mention Seth Klarman, the Oracle of Boston, who incidentally invited me to write this introduction, thereby checking off *generous* and *foolish* in a single stroke. Last, Graham could quote Kierkegaard (note to my fellow hedge fund managers: this is not the name of an artisanal beer). Here is the first lesson from Graham and Dodd: don't rely on appearances, don't trust first impressions, don't jump to conclusions.

不过我跑题了。想象一下，当我被要求为《证券分析》中关于投资困境信贷资产的部分撰写序言时的反应：“我不适合写这个，”我心想，而且绝不是因为我是法国人、女性，或是性格幽默。让我们看看背后的思想背景：在过去的80多年里，有两个派系一直在争夺投资理论领域的主导权。一方是捍卫价值投资理念的格雷厄姆与多德阵营，他们将纽约的哥伦比亚商学院视为自己的领地，认为金融工具——尤其是股票——拥有独立于其交易价格的内在价值。投资策略就是购买那些交易价格远远低于内在价值的股票（即被低估的股票），并在其交易价格不可避免但未必很快接近内在价值时获利了结。他们的对手则是来自芝加哥街头的现代投资组合学派，以马科维茨和夏普为首，他们基于有效市场理论，认为每个股票价格都反映了所有可用信息。除此之外不存在其他价值——换句话说，内在价值其实就是交易价格。因此，投资并非挑选被低估的股票，而是构建一个能在特定风险水平下实现预期回报最优化的证券组合。虽然芝加哥学派将波动性等同于风险，但价值投资者往往将波动性视为机会的来源。

<!--en-->
But I digress. Imagine my reaction when asked to write an introduction to the investing in distressed credit section of *Security Analysis*: “I don't belong,” I thought, and not in the least because I'm French, female, and funny. Consider the intellectual context: two clans have battled to gain control of the investing theory landscape over the last 80-odd years. The Graham and Dodd gang, defenders of the value investing credo, who call New York's Columbia Business School their turf, posit that financial instruments—stocks in particular—have an intrinsic value that is separate and different from their trading value. Investing consists of buying stocks where the latter is below the former by a considerable “margin of safety” (*i.e.*, undervalued stocks), and cashing in when inevitably albeit not necessarily swiftly, their trading value approaches intrinsic value. Their rivals, the Modern Portfolio clan from the mean streets of Chicago, led by Markowitz and Sharpe, start with the Efficient Market Theory that every stock price reflects all available information. There is no other value than the trading value—in other words, the intrinsic value *is* the trading value. Investing is therefore not about selecting undervalued stocks; it's about building a portfolio of securities that optimize expected return for a given level of risk. While the Chicago School equates volatility with risk, value investors tend to view volatility as a source of opportunity.

我知道你在想什么。史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格怎么会错过为《西区故事》重制这部完美作品的机会呢：穿着巴塔哥尼亚背心的舞动着的基金经理们，以及穿着灯芯绒裤子的诺贝尔奖得主们，为“有效前沿”的形态展开激烈角逐？

<!--en-->
I know what you are thinking. How did Steven Spielberg miss this perfect reboot for his *West Side Story* movie: dancing fund managers in Patagonia vests and singing Nobel Prize winners in corduroy pants duking it out over the shape of the Efficient Frontier?

写这本书时，我处于完全错误的立场。我不仅没有就读哥伦比亚商学院，反而去了斯坦福大学，师从比尔·夏普本人。开始撰写这篇文章时，我对他第一堂课的回忆又浮现在脑海中——25年来我从未再想起过它。夏普教授计算了班上两名学生生日日期和月份相同的概率。与所有人的直觉相反，我们算出的比例并非微不足道，而是有三个人符合条件。他接着告诉我们，这样的概率大致相当于一名投资者连续15年跑赢市场。对任何单个投资者而言，这种概率都极低。但考虑到投资者数量庞大，总会有*某人*做到这一点。事实证明确实如此，比如价值投资的坚定支持者与实践者、莱格梅森公司的投资组合经理比尔·米勒就做到了。据夏普教授所说，米勒的持续优异表现并不能证明价值投资方法的正确性；他只不过是结果正态分布曲线上的一个点而已。总得有人做到吧。当时天真的我，只将这一事实当作一个有趣的统计案例。其实不然：比尔·夏普正在传播他的理念，而他讲授的《投资组合管理》课程对我的思维产生了深远影响。

<!--en-->
I was raised on the wrong side of the rumble for this book. Not only did I not go to Columbia Business School, I attended Stanford, where I was taught by Bill Sharpe himself. As I started writing this essay, a recollection of his first lecture resurfaced—I hadn’t given it a thought in 25 years. Professor Sharpe considered the probability of two students in class sharing the same day and month for their birthday. Contrary to everyone’s instinct, we calculated a nontrivial percentage and not two but three of us qualified. He proceeded to tell us that these odds are roughly the same as an investor beating the market 15 years in a row. For any one investor, those odds are infinitesimally low. But given the vast number of investors, it is reasonably likely that *someone* will do it. That turned out to be the case for Bill Miller, portfolio manager at Legg Mason, a staunch proponent and practitioner of value investing. According to Professor Sharpe, Miller’s streak of outperformance was not a validation of the value investing method; he was simply a dot on a normal distribution curve of outcomes. Somebody had to be. In my naiveté, I registered the fact as a tidbit of statistics. Not so: Bill Sharpe was proselytizing, and his class, Portfolio Management, had an indelible effect on my thinking.

“真正价值”的概念在我看来，往好了说是模糊不清的，往坏了说则是玄乎其妙的。格雷厄姆和多德本人对此似乎也存在矛盾，他们解释说内在价值“是由事实所支撑的价值，例如资产、收益、股息以及明确的未来前景，这些有别于因市场操纵或心理偏差而形成的市场报价。”（第1章）但他们也警告说：“必须始终记住，分析师发现的真相首先并非全部真相，其次也不是永恒不变的真相。”（第31章）在其他地方，他们承认“内在价值是个难以捉摸的概念”，但可以加以估算，就像“无需知道年龄就能判断一个女人是否到了投票年龄，无需知道体重就能判断一个男人是否超重一样”。我不知道你们怎么想，但自从我在比弗利山的牙医开始提供肉毒杆菌注射服务后，我就很难判断女人的年龄了；至于评价男人的体重，我绝对不会这么做，至少不会当面评价。我深信“证券分析绝不能妄图为任何特定普通股设定‘适当价值’的通用规则。实际上，根本不存在这样的东西。”（第39章）我之前的雇主是一家多资产类别的管理公司，属于注重价值投资且以事件驱动策略运作的对冲基金，我在那里担任投资组合经理长达20年。然而，在所有合伙人的投资组合中，我的公开股票持仓始终是最少的，几乎从不持有任何股票。显然，我不是选股高手；这要归咎于我的成长环境。如果把我形容成《007》系列中的女特工，我想没人会觉得奇怪。

<!--en-->
The idea of a “true value” has always struck me as nebulous at best and mystical at worse. Graham and Dodd themselves appeared conflicted on the matter, explaining that intrinsic value “is that value, which is justified by the facts, e.g., the assets, earnings, dividends, and definite prospects, as distinct, let us say, from market quotations established by market manipulation or distorted by psychological excesses.” (Chap. 1) But they also warned that “it must always be remembered that the truth that the analyst uncovers is first of all not the whole truth and, secondly, not the immutable truth.” (Chap. 31) Elsewhere they admit that “intrinsic value is an elusive concept” but can be approximated, just like “it is quite possible to decide by inspection that a woman is old enough to vote without knowing her age or that a man is heavier than he should be without knowing his weight.” I don’t know about you, but I’ve had a tough time estimating women’s ages since my Beverly Hills orthodontist diversified into Botox, and I most definitely wouldn’t pass judgment on a man’s weight, at least not to his face. I believe deeply that “security analysis cannot presume to lay down general rules as to the ‘proper value’ of any given common stock. Practically speaking, there is no such thing.” (Chap. 39)
My former employer, where I invested for 20 years as a portfolio manager, was a multi-asset class manager, a value-oriented and event-driven hedge fund. However, of all the partners’ portfolios, mine was consistently the lightest in public equities, rarely having any exposure at all. Plainly, I am not a stock picker; blame it on my upbringing. If you described me as a Bond girl, I bet no one would bat an eye.

然而，我最幸运的是发现，在企业债券市场的某个角落——困境投资领域，存在着将这两种投资理念融合在一起的绝佳机会，从而形成一种完美的组合，并借此打造自己的事业。困境投资指的是购买那些处于严重经营或财务压力下的公司的债券或贷款，这类公司要么已经破产，要么即将申请破产。债券本身具有合同规定的价值，即便是以远低于面值的价格出售的困境债券也是如此。因此，我无需再纠结那个模糊的“真正价值”概念。只要公司资产或业务价值足以覆盖我的债权面值，我就知道能收回多少资金。其次，有效市场假说基于一个重要前提，即市场具有完美的流动性，意味着总有愿意买卖的买家和卖家。虽然大市值股票的流动性即便算不上完美也相当不错，但困境资产的流动性却像流沙一般，被迫出售的情况十分普遍。这意味着我可以忽略“证券价格总是完全合理”这一荒谬观念。对于困境投资者来说，剩下的挑战就是评估能获得多少补偿以及如何获取这些补偿。在这方面，格雷厄姆和多德堪称困境投资的救世主，他们的方法极具实用性且常常具有前瞻性，他们的书更是长期投资成功的绝佳指南。

<!--en-->
My supreme luck, however, was to discover that in a corner of the corporate bond market, distressed investing, lay the extraordinary opportunity to fuse both schools of thought to form a glorious ménage à trois—building a career along the way. Stressed and distressed investing entails buying the bonds or the loans of a company under severe operational or financial duress, either within bankruptcy or on the verge of filing for it. A bond has a contractual value, even a distressed bond selling at a deep discount to par. Thus I could do away with the nebulous concept of a “true value.” I knew what I would recover if the value of the assets or business covered the face value of my claims. Second, the Efficient Market Hypothesis starts with the important assumption of perfect liquidity, meaning that there are always willing buyers and sellers. While liquidity is, if not perfect, excellent for large capitalization stocks, distressed assets are liquid as quicksand and forced sellers abound. This means that I could ignore the debilitating notion that securities are perfectly priced. The distressed investor is left with the challenge of evaluating what payment is available and how to get it. In that respect, Graham and Dodd are the messiahs of distressed investing, their method highly relevant and oftentimes prescient, their book a terrific recipe for long-term investment success.

陷入困境的投资者首要遵守的准则就是关注负面风险。这正是我对格雷厄姆与多德提出的“安全边际”概念的理解：重点不在于距离内在价值目标还有多远，而在于一旦情况恶化——对于一家处境不佳的公司而言，这种情况极有可能发生——债券价格还会下跌多少。当读到“债券购买者的首要目标应是避免麻烦，而非在麻烦出现时自我保护”时，你或许会发笑：我们面对困境企业时不就已经处于麻烦之中了吗？（第6章）相信我，情况总有可能变得更糟。请将这句话重复100遍直至牢记：“低价债券的购买者完全清楚自己所面临的风险；他更有可能对相关债券进行彻底调查，并仔细评估亏损与盈利的可能性；最后——也是最重要的一点——他已为可能遭受的任何损失做好准备，且其收益形式足以弥补这些损失。”（第7章）那么，这位购买者要如何进行彻底的调查呢？他们不仅会查看利润表，还会查看资产负债表。“我们坚信，多年来华尔街一直不愿给予足够的重视，其实资产负债表更值得关注。”（第42章）我十分珍视格雷厄姆与多德对这种“关注”的描述——这正是我20年来一直在做的工作，与其说是因为其量化上的精确性，不如说是出于其生动的表达力。“这里存在着无限的机会，可以开展细致的调查研究、进行批判性比较，从而发现并指出与公开披露的每股收益所反映的情况截然不同的真实状况。”（第31章）在我看来，这正是困境投资的乐趣所在：令人兴奋的调查、惊人的发现，以及那些能带来独特见解的创造性与战略性思维（又是“创造性”这个词！）。企业债务作为一种私人契约，存在无数种变体。即便是在发展成熟的美国杠杆贷款和垃圾债券市场，各条款、优先级、担保方式、提前赎回权等方面也存在差异——这些差异有时极为微妙，往往也极具争议——足以决定一笔交易是盈利还是亏损。当一家公司逐渐陷入困境时，关于如何在债权人之间分配企业价值就会产生冲突，无论是有担保贷款方与无担保贷款方、次级债券持有者与高级债券持有者，还是循环贷款银行家与定期贷款银行家、第一顺位抵押债权人与第二顺位抵押债权人之间，各方往往会同时展开一场激烈的博弈。优秀的困境投资者确实就像一位聪明的侦探、一位棋艺高超的棋手、一位军队将领和一位外交家，他们会研究各种情景、制定投资策略，并预判每个利益相关方的下一步行动。众多困境投资项目都如同最精彩的电视剧一般充满波折，有着个性鲜明的主角与配角、黑暗的时刻与充满希望的黎明、好运与厄运的交替，以及不同的结局。这简直就是《权力的游戏》，而你就是龙之母丹妮莉丝。

<!--en-->
The first commandment of the distressed investor is to focus on the downside. That is my read of Graham and Dodd’s “margin of safety” concept: not the distance to the promised land of an intrinsic value, but how much further a bond will drop if things go wrong, which, for a distressed company, isquite probable. When reading “the primary aim of the bond buyer must be to avoid trouble and not to protect himself in the event of trouble,” you may chuckle: aren’t we already in trouble with distressed companies? (Chap. 6) Trust me, things can always get uglier. Repeat 100 times until memorized: “The purchaser of low-priced bonds is fully aware of the risk he is running; he is more likely to make a thorough investigation of the issue and to appraise carefully the chances of loss and of profit; finally—most important of all—he is prepared for whatever losses he may sustain, and his profits are in a form available to meet his losses.” (Chap. 7)
How, pray, will this purchaser make a thorough investigation? Why, they will look not only at the income statement, but also at the balance sheet. “We have expressed our conviction that the balance sheet deserves more attention than Wall Street has been willing to accord it for many years past.” (Chap. 42) I cherish Graham and Dodd’s description of the “attention” that was my work for 20 years, less for their quantitative accuracy than their evocative quality. “There are unbounded opportunities for shrewd detective work, for critical comparisons, for discovering and pointing out a state of affairs quite different from that indicated by the publicized per-share earnings.” (Chap. 31) *That* is the joy of distressed investing as I saw it: the thrilling investigations, the exciting discoveries, the creative and strategic thinking (the *creative* word again!) that deliver unique insights. A corporate indebtedness, being a private contract, has infinite variations. Even in the well-established U.S. leveraged loan and junk bond markets, there are differences in covenants, seniority, security, callability—sometimes extremely subtle and often highly controversial—that can make the difference between a losing trade and a winning one. As a company slides into trouble, conflicts arise over how to divide the corporate value pie among creditors, be it between secured and unsecured lenders, junior and senior bondholders, revolver and term loan bankers, first lien and second lien creditors—and all of them at once in an epic creditor battle. A good distressed investor is indeed a shrewd detective and a chess master, an army general and a diplomat, studying scenarios, positioning their bets,anticipating each stakeholder's next move. Scores of distressed investments have the twists and turns of the best TV drama, with colorful protagonists and supporting characters, dark hours and hopeful dawns, spells of luck and misfortune, good and bad endings. It's *Game of Thrones* and you're Daenerys, Mother of Dragons.

格雷厄姆与多德早就提出了一个具有前瞻性的建议：不要单独分析资产负债表或利润表，因为它们可能不完整且容易被操纵，而应关注两者之间的关系，就像拼图碎片共同构成企业的整体形象。他们比时代领先了五十年，便预见到了现金流量表的必要性。他们还描述了那些导致2001年左右许多大型企业破产的欺诈行为和会计操纵手段。再加上2000年代初电信业和互联网行业的崩溃，这些因素共同推动了困境投资作为对冲基金行业中一个高利润领域的兴起。

<!--en-->
A prescient recommendation from Graham and Dodd is to avoid analyzing the balance sheet or the income statement separately because these can be incomplete and manipulated, focusing instead on their relationship, like pieces of a puzzle that form a corporate picture. Fifty years ahead of their time, they foresaw the imperative of the cash flow statement. They also described the frauds and accounting manipulations that led to many of the largest ever corporate bankruptcies around 2001. These, helped along by the telecom and dot-com debacle in the early aughts, launched distressed investing as a lucrative branch of the hedge fund industry.

格雷厄姆与多德坚持认为，财务报表之间的关联比单独研究每一份报表更能提供信息，他们强调“必须将利润表的分析与相关资产负债表的审查联系起来”（重点为我所加）。（第33章）“如果不参考期初和期末的资产负债表，就无法正确理解任何利润表的含义。”（第31章）现金流量表则将静态的资产负债表与动态但多为非现金、易被操纵的利润表巧妙地联系在一起。直到1987年，SFAS第95号准则才要求企业必须提供现金流量表，而这一披露内容正是当今困境投资者广泛依赖的依据。

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd insisted that the connection between the financial statements is more informative than the static study of each, highlighting "the necessity of *relating* an analysis of income accounts to an examination of the appurtenant balance sheets" (emphasis mine). (Chap. 33) "The meaning of any income statement cannot properly be understood except with reference to the balance sheet at the beginning and at the end of the period." (Chap. 31) The cash flow statement is the report that neatly links the frozen picture of the balance sheet to the dynamic but mostly noncash, manipulable income statement. Not until 1987 did SFAS Statement No. 95 mandate that firms provide a cash flow statement, a disclosure that present-day distressed investors rely on extensively.

在《收益账户分析》一章的后续章节中，格雷厄姆与多德继续阐述了利润表上的各种会计手段与诡计，从略有误导性的到完全欺诈性的都有。身处困境中的投资者不妨仔细研究这些内容，因为“忘记过去的人注定要重蹈覆辙。”²困境投资的历史渊源就在其中：操纵折旧准备金？世界通信公司就是典型案例；通过将根本不存在的收入计入利润来虚增收益？（第33章）全球交叉通信公司便是例证；并购过程中经常出现的609折旧问题？（第31章）泰科公司就是例子；利润在很大程度上取决于随意的判定与操纵？（第31章）安然公司便是明证。

<!--en-->
In the subsequent chapters of the "Analysis of the Income Account" section, Graham and Dodd proceed to describe accounting tricks and schemes on the income statement, from slightly deceptive to outright fraudulent. The current distressed investor would do well to study them, as "those who do not remember the past are condemned to repeat it."² The prehistory of distressed investing is in there. Manipulation of depreciation reserve? WorldCom is exhibit A. "Padding income by including items in earnings that have no realexistence”? (Chap. 33) I give you Global Crossing. “Depreciating 609 often an issue in mergers”? (Chap. 31) Ask Tyco. “Earnings subject in extraordinary degree to arbitrary determination and manipulation”? (Chap. 31) Here’s Enron.

我曾简单地将困境投资描述为购买问题公司的债务，但实际上购买只是开始而非最终目的。要取得理想结果需要付出巨大的努力。除非通过资本重组、业务扭亏为盈，或两者兼施来让公司恢复健康，否则这些债务可能毫无价值。目标是通过可持续的融资计划让公司重新具备生存能力并实现盈利，从而提升其证券的价值。简而言之，困境投资者就是*积极主义股东*。如今这个术语常用于指股东，但在破产情境下也适用于那些可能成为新所有者的债权人。我们的作者用一整章探讨股东与管理层的关系，在其中他们谴责了“典型的美国股东是圈养动物中最温顺、最冷漠的这一臭名昭著的事实。”（第44章）他们列出了股东与管理层之间可能存在的冲突，包括业务扩张、薪酬、分红政策、信息透明度，甚至企业存续问题。他们呼吁采取行动：“警觉的股东绝不会放弃要求企业仅为自身利益运营的权利！”这对困境投资者来说正是福音；他们的职责就是设计并实施重组计划，解决导致企业倒闭的问题，并因此获得丰厚的回报。过度杠杆化的资产负债表、仓促的扩张、亏损的收购、过高的分红、无能的管理团队——所有这些问题都需要以富有创意且严谨的方式在最终获得破产法官及债权人批准的方案中得到解决。

<!--en-->
I glibly described distressed investing as buying troubled companies’ debt, but buying it is only the beginning, not the end game. A phenomenal amount of work is required to achieve a favorable outcome. This debt may be worthless unless and until we manage to clean up the company through a capital restructuring, or an operational turnaround, or more likely, both. The goal is to make the company viable and profitable again with a sustainable financing plan, thereby increasing the value of its securities. In short, the distressed investor is an *activist*. That term is often used for shareholders these days, but it is applicable in a bankruptcy to creditors, who stand to be the new owners. Our authors devote an entire chapter to stockholders-management relationships, in which they denounce the “notorious fact that the typical American stockholder is the most docile and apathetic animal in captivity.” (Chap. 44) They list potential conflicts between shareholders and management, including expansion, compensation, dividend policy, information, even business continuation. They urge action: “Alert shareholders will not surrender their right that a corporation should operate in their sole interest!” That is music to the distressed investor’s ears; it is their job to design and implement a restructuring plan that redresses the issues that led to failure—and collect a hefty return in so doing. Overleveraged balance sheet, hasty expansion, unprofitable acquisitions, excessive dividends, incompetent management team—all of it needs to be creatively and rigorously addressed in a plan ultimately approved by the bankruptcy judge and creditors.

两位作者预测了这一领域的巨大盈利潜力，指出破产清算时价格与价值之间的差异，即“这些债务的售价与其拥有的流动资产相比低得离谱。”（第50章）这“此前曾让我们强烈建议不要以投资水平购买那些可能陷入财务困境的公司的任何证券；而现在则让我们认为，一旦这些困境出现，反而可能会带来有吸引力的分析机会”（强调为原文所加）。（第50章）这两位目光敏锐的学者指出，“投资者天生就不愿意介入困境中的资产。”（第6章）可以说，不仅出于天性，很多时候还出于制度因素，这使得那些能够以较低价格买入并持有其他投资者不得不抛售的证券的困境投资者拥有极大的优势。

<!--en-->
The writers predicted the immense profit potential of the discipline, highlighting discrepancies between prices and values in receivership, as “obligations sold at a ridiculous low price compared with the current assets available to them.” (Chap. 50) This had “previously led us to advise strongly against buying at investment levels *any* securities of a company that is likely to fall into financial difficulties; it nowleads us to suggest *that* after these difficulties have arisen, they may produce attractive analytical opportunities” (emphasis their own). (Chap. 50) Our perceptive duo points out that “investors are constitutionally averse to buying into a troubled situation” (Chap. 6); not only constitutionally, one might add, but in many cases also institutionally, which confers a formidable edge to the distressed investor able to buy and hold securities that others must dump at inefficient prices.

本书的杀手级应用（前几代人称之为“捕鼠器”）就在“破产产生的价格形态”一节中。请看这段具有预见性的论述：“因此，一项富有成效的分析工作应当是密切关注此类状况，努力发现那些看似远低于其内在价值出售的证券，并大致确定介入的最佳时机。”（第50章）遗憾的是，关于这一充满前景的主题几乎没有进一步阐述；书中没有从买入角度来探讨破产重组的案例，仅有从卖出或“转换”（升级投资组合）的角度。令人震惊的是，在这本拥有800多页的《证券分析》经典著作中，竟然没有专门讨论困境企业分析的章节。为何如此？直到我查看了各版本的出版日期，这个疑问才得以解答。显然，在格雷厄姆和多德所处的时代，还不存在通过破产获利的有效途径。直到20世纪30年代，破产通常意味着清算，破产法院主要处理的是对企业资产的扣押——当“实际上我们发现，只要这些资产有可能具有高于债权人债权的公允价值，法院就极不愿意允许公司债券持有人通过扣押抵押物来接管这些资产”时，这显然无法为债券持有人带来利润。（第6章）然而，《企业重组法》，以及之后的《钱德勒法》和1939年的《信托契约法》，引入了企业重组规则，旨在让企业继续生存并获得重生机会，而非将其拆解。虽然这显然是对1929年经济危机及20世纪30年代严峻经济形势的回应，但该法案的初衷是为“陷入困境的企业提供永久性的帮助”，在破产法院的监督与保护下，为债务人与债权人提供友好协商的机会，并尽可能保持企业资产的完整，减少运营干扰。³ 我们今天所熟知的破产制度，尤其是破产法典中的第11章，源自1978年的改革，其目的是在冻结起诉前的债务追讨直至问题得以逐步解决的同时，维持企业运营、保住就业岗位并吸引新的信贷来源。正如顶尖破产学专家查尔斯·J·塔布教授所言：“为第11章最常提出的理由是最大化债务人企业的价值。其基本假设是，经过重组后的企业比其清算价值还具有持续经营带来的额外价值。简而言之，设立诸如第11章这样的企业救援程序，最根本的目的是为企业所有利益相关方创造最大价值——钱越多越好。”⁴ 如此，真正的困境投资便可以开始了。格雷厄姆和多德确实认为这一机制会带来益处，但“新法律尚无时间在实际操作中证明其优缺点。”（第18章）简而言之，我们的先驱们只是走得有点太早了。

<!--en-->
The killer app (what previous generations called a “mouse trap”) of the book resides under “Price Patterns Produced by Insolvency.” Consider this prophetic sentence: “a profitable field of analytical activity should be found therefore in keeping in close touch with such situations, endeavoring to discover securities that appear to be selling far under their intrinsic values and to determine approximately the best time for making a commitment in them.” (Chap. 50)
Alas, there is little elaboration on this promising topic; there is no example that considers receivership from the point of view of buying—only from selling or “switching” (upgrading a portfolio). There is, shockingly, no chapter on distressed analysis in the 800-some pages of the *Security Analysis* bible. Why? This omission baffled me until I looked back at the edition dates. Plainly, in the original Graham and Dodd world, there was no adequate process to make money in bankruptcy. Until the 1930s, bankruptcy generally meant liquidation, and bankruptcy courts dealt primarily with foreclosure of a firm’s assets—hardly a way to make a profit for a bondholder when “in practice we find a very definite disinclination on the part of the courts to permit corporate bondholders to take over properties by foreclosing on their liens if there is any possibility that these assets may have a fair value in excess of their claim.” (Chap. 6)
However, the Corporate Reorganization Act, followed by the Chandler Act and the Trust Indenture Act of 1939, introduced corporate reorganization rules with the purpose of keeping businesses alive and giving them a chance to emerge rather than dismantling them. While it was obviously a response to the crash of 1929 and the dire economicconditions of the 1930s, the charter of the bill was to be of “permanent helpful assistance to distressed corporations,” providing “the opportunity for amicable adjustment by debtor and creditors, under the supervision and protection of the bankruptcy courts, and for holding the property of the debtor intact with its operation disturbed as little as practicable.”³
Bankruptcy as we know it today, particularly Chapter 11 of the bankruptcy code, emerged from the 1978 reform, furthering the goal to maintain corporate operations, save jobs, and attract new sources of credit, while freezing pre-petition debt collection until it could be sorted out over time. As described by Professor Charles J. Tabb, a leading bankruptcy scholar, “the most often repeated justification for chapter 11 is to maximize the value of the debtor firm. The operative assumption is that there is a going-concern surplus for a reorganized firm over and above its liquidation value. In short, the most fundamental reason for having a corporate rescue procedure such as chapter 11 is to maximize value for the benefit of all stakeholders in the enterprise. More money is better than less.”⁴ Voila! Distressed investing could begin in earnest. Graham and Dodd indeed presumed that the process would be beneficial, but “the new laws have not yet had time to prove their merits or deficiencies in actual practices.” (Chap. 18) Our scribes were, simply put, too early.

尽管如此，他们还是为我提供了一份工作。这是事实！我作为投资者取得的重大突破，源于《证券分析》中“特殊类型债券”这一鲜为人知的章节（第10章），该章节介绍了铁路设备证书，以及以机车、货运车或客车所有权为担保、或以铁路公司使用这些设备的租赁权为质押的债券。根据书中严谨的论述，“这类设备相关债券的投资表现非常令人满意，尤其是因为直到最近，即便发行方面临最严重的财务困境，也很少会妨碍其按时支付利息和本金。”（第10章）作者们进一步指出，“设备留置权的持有者可以威胁要夺走这些铁路车辆。实际上，这种*替代性*保障对设备信托的持有者而言具有极高的价值。”（第10章）格雷厄姆和多德当时并不知道，几十年后银行家们会巧妙地利用这一基本结构为商用飞机融资。他们通过设计增强型设备信托证书（EETC债券），使其具备抗破产能力，将其分为优先级和次级层级，并增设流动性保障机制，确保即使航空公司破产也能继续支付利息。因此，EETC债券比普通的航空公司企业债券更安全，评级机构给它们的评级也更高，还吸引了投资级投资者的购买。1994年，西北航空率先发行了EETC债券。随着这种债券获得广泛认可，到2001年其发行规模已膨胀至150亿美元，并有望继续保持指数级增长。这些债券堪称“坚不可摧”，“只有在极其罕见且不太可能发生的情况下才会出现违约。”（第4章）不幸的是，那种极端、罕见且悲惨的情况终究发生了。2001年9月11日的恐怖袭击之后，EETC债券的价格暴跌。次日，我就被派去负责报道这一行业动态。

<!--en-->
Nevertheless, they managed to give me a career. It’s true! My big breakthrough as an investor finds its origin in *Security Analysis*, deep in an obscure section on “Special Types of Obligations” (Chap. 10) that describes railroad equipment certificates, bonds secured by title to locomotives, freight, or passenger cars, and by the pledge of the lease under which the railroad is using the equipment. According to our exacting authors, “the investment record of these equipment obligations is very satisfactory, particularly because until recently even the most serious financial difficulties of the issuing road have very rarely prevented the prompt payment of interest and principal.” (Chap. 10) They continue, “the holder of the equipment lien can threaten to take the rolling stock away. It is the possession of this *alternative* which in practice has proved of prime value to the owner of equipment trusts.” (Chap. 10)
Little did Graham and Dodd know that decades later, bankers would ingeniously use this basic structure to finance commercial aircraft. They enhanced it by making EETC bonds (Enhanced Equipment Trust Certificates) bankruptcy-remote, tranched in senior and junior layers, and strengthened by a liquidity facility that enabled interest payments even if the airline went bankrupt. Thus EETC bonds were safer than regular airline corporate bonds, rated higher by rating agencies, and purchased by investment grade investors. Northwest Airlines was the first to issue an EETC in 1994. Gaining widespread acceptance, issuance ballooned to $15 billion as we entered 2001, and promised continued exponential growth. These were bulletproof bonds “which could suffer default only under exceptional and highly improbable circumstances.” (Chap. 4)
Unfortunately, the exceptional and improbable and tragic did happen. After the terror attacks of September 11, 2001, EETCs plunged in price. The next day, I was tapped to cover the sector.

整个美国航空业都处于濒临破产的边缘。各航空公司很快就被下调信用评级，除一家外，其余都在五年内申请了破产。飞机价格也大幅下跌。我们面临着前所未有的状况：一种全新的金融工具在负面市场环境下的表现尚无先例，而那些被其安全性及投资级评级所吸引的债券持有者，既没有处理危机投资的经验，也没有相应的职责要求。他们纷纷恐慌抛售，试图以任何价格脱手。突然间，这些债券的交易价格甚至低于作为抵押的飞机价值——有时甚至低于其废铁价！根据破产法中的特定条款，债券持有者可以像处理旧的铁路设备债券那样，收回或威胁收回这些飞机，从而在对破产资产及其他债权人拥有巨大影响力的同时，确保能够实现债券的内在价值。

<!--en-->
The entire U.S. airline industry teetered on insolvency. Carriers were promptly downgraded, and all but one filed for bankruptcy within five years. Aircraft prices cratered. We were in uncharted territory, with a new financial instrument that was still untried in a downside scenario, and holders who had been attracted to its safety and investment-grade rating and lacked any mandate or expertise in distressed investing. They stampeded for the exit, forcefully selling for whatever they could get. Suddenly bonds traded at prices below the value of the aircraft that served as collateral—sometimes even below their scrap value! Under a specific section of the bankruptcy code, bondholders could—as in the old railroad equipment bonds—repossess or threaten to repossess the aircraft, thereby gaining considerable leverage over the estate and other creditors while securing the ability to realize the bonds’ intrinsic value.

这完全是格雷厄姆和多德所描述的经典案例，堪称所有价值投资的典范。作为最大的EETC债券发行方，联合航空在破产状态下持续了三年多，期间我拼命学习，努力成为航空业和飞机方面的专家。在此之前，我对这个行业的了解仅限于购买机票，最好是商务舱。等到联合航空从破产中走出来时，西北航空和达美航空正准备申请破产并带来新的投资机会。飞机及相关航空债券已经成了我们基金的重要盈利来源，而我也成为了投资组合经理。

<!--en-->
It was a textbook Graham and Dodd setup, the mother of all value investments. United, the largest EETC issuer, stayed in bankruptcy for over three years, during which I scrambled to become an airline and aircraft expert. Until then, myknowledge of the industry consisted of buying a ticket, preferably in business class. By the time United emerged from its bankruptcy, Northwest and Delta were getting ready to file and provide new investment opportunities. Aircraft and airline bonds had developed into a profitable mainstay of our fund, and I had become a portfolio manager.

现在，这可能会让我的仰慕者们感到震惊——我曾经也做过一些糟糕的投资。很多投资本可以通过仔细重读《证券分析》来避免。其中有一笔尤其惨痛。在我首次投资航空业多年后，我试图将在航空领域的成功扩展到航运业：两者都是固定成本高、投入要素（燃料）价格波动大的运输行业，拥有可在全球交易的长期资产，还有有时能以折扣价购买的优先抵押债务——会有多大的不同呢？结果却截然不同，只是我的投资回报前面出现了负号而非正号。船舶融资方无法像航空业那样，在债务人违约或破产时没收其抵押物。首先，扣押船只极其困难；其次，即便是优先抵押债务，也要排在船员工资、未付运费、燃油费或港口费用等海事债权之后。换句话说，你缺乏“抵押资产可变现这一积极且重大的优势。”（第10章）最后，航运业没有客户忠诚度，也没有品牌价值或企业差异化优势，运价波动极大，地理套利空间很小。你可以从一家陷入困境的美国航空公司手中收回购机，然后将其卖给一家发展良好的巴西国内航空公司，从而获得盈利——但航运业做不到这一点。2013年我投资鹰式散货航运公司时，要是能意识到“将抵押权视为独立于企业经营状况之外的保障手段，在大多数情况下纯属谬论”该有多好。（第6章）然而鹰式散货航运公司最初是一次成功的重组，在包括我在内的贷款方的支持下顺利度过了破产程序——甚至可以说是“安然渡过”。业务得以持续，新的融资到位，对客户和员工的债务也得到了偿还，六个月后该公司便以全新的资本结构和光明的发展前景重新崛起。几个月后，运价骤降，就连经过重组的优先抵押债务也出现了问题。贷款的流动性不足加剧了价格下跌，而抵押资产也无法为资产提供最低价值。由此得出的教训是：“安全并非由抵押权决定，而是由偿付能力决定。”（第6章）那只象征希望的鹰终于着陆了……却又紧急降落在危机四伏的土地上。

<!--en-->
Now, it will come as a shock to my admirers, but I’ve had lousy investments in my days. A good many could have been avoided with a careful rereading of *Security Analysis*. One is particularly searing. Years after my first airline investment, I sought to expand my success in airlines to shipping: both transportation businesses with a high fixed-cost structure and volatile input (fuel), supported by long-life assets that can be traded worldwide, and first mortgage debt that could sometimes be purchased at a discount—how different could it be? Not at all, it turned out, except for the minus instead of the plus sign in front of my return. Financiers of ships do not benefit from the same ability to seize their collateral upon a default or a bankruptcy. First, it is exceedingly difficult to arrest a vessel. Second, even first lien debt is subordinated to maritime liens such as crew wages or unpaid freight, fuel, or port charges. In other words, you lack the “positive and substantial advantage of the realizability of the pledged assets.” (Chap. 10) Last, shipping commands no customer loyalty, no brand value or corporate differentiation, hair-raisingly volatile rates, and low geographic arbitrage availability. You can repossess a plane from a distressed U.S. carrier and sell it to a thriving Brazilian domestic airline for a profitable route—not so in shipping. It would have been handy to realize in 2013 when I invested in Eagle Bulk Shipping that “the conception of a mortgage lien as a guaranty of protection independent of the success of the business itself is in most cases a complete fallacy.” (Chap. 6) Yet Eagle Bulk started as a successful restructuring, smoothly navigating through the bankruptcy process (dare I say “sailing”) with the support of lenders—including yours truly. Business continued uninterrupted, new financing was obtained, obligations to customers and employees were fulfilled, and the company emerged within six months with a brand spanning new capital structure and bright business prospects. Within months,shipping rates plummeted, and even the restructured first lien blew up. The illiquidity of the loan exacerbated the drop in price. The mortgaged assets provided no floor value. “Safety is not measured by lien but by the ability to pay” (Chap. 6) was the lesson. The proverbial Eagle had landed ... but it was an emergency descent into distressed land again.

自从我经历EETC项目以及航运业的惨败之后，许多因素都扰乱了不良资产投资领域的发展。按时间顺序，我可以列举出三个重大变化。首先是自2001年电信危机以来，不良债务投资已经变得主流化并制度化。当时，卡兰周期表估计不良对冲基金的资产管理规模为240亿美元，多策略对冲基金的规模则为660亿美元。由于大多数基金采用多种策略，要统计出确切总数十分困难，但仅2022年规模最大的25家不良资产投资机构管理的资产就高达约6000亿美元。如今，重组越来越多地是由大型基金推动并旨在实现最大化的资产回收。正如伊吉·波普所说，其他任何一方（供应商、次级债权人、劳工）都只是被动跟随的乘客。债权人间互相争斗的情况确实存在，或者用一位富有表现力的律师的话来说，就是“联合贷款团中的一组贷款方对另一组发起的同类相食式的攻击”。第11章所倡导的、为所有债权人最大化债务人价值并公平分配这些价值的崇高目标，更不用说实现友好解决了，难道已经是陈旧的历史了吗？我不这么认为。

<!--en-->
A lot has muddled the craft of distressed investing since my EETC encounter and shipping debacle. In chronological order, I would cite three seismic shifts. The first is that investing in distressed debt has become mainstream and institutionalized since the telecom crisis of 2001. Back then, the Callan Periodic Tables estimated distressed hedge funds at $24 billion in assets under management and multi-strategy hedge funds at $66 billion. While it would be arduous to circle a total number because most funds straddle multiple strategies, the largest 25 distressed players alone managed around $600 billion in 2022. Restructurings are increasingly imposed by and designed to maximize recovery for the megafunds. Anyone else (vendor, junior creditor, labor) is, as Iggy Pop used to say, a passenger who rides and who rides. Creditor-on-creditor violence is real, or as one expressive lawyer put it, the “cannibalistic assault by one group of lenders in a syndicate against another.” Is the laudable goal of Chapter 11 to maximize the value of the debtor for all creditors and distribute it fairly and equitably, let alone amicably, ancient history? I don’t believe so.

值得指出的是，不良资产投资并非葬礼上的舞蹈，而是一种重建行为，这符合所有相关方的最大利益。通过资本重组、业务转型，或者两者结合，一家公司可以重新具备生存能力，按时支付员工和供应商的工资，并依靠可持续的融资渠道维持发展前景。

<!--en-->
It’s worth noting that distressed investing is not graveyard dancing; it’s rebuilding, which is in the best interest of all constituencies. Through a capital restructuring, or an operational turnaround, or most likely both, a company can become viable again, with employees and vendors paid on time and growth prospects supported by sustainable financing sources.

第二波海啸是美联储对资本市场（包括企业债务市场）的干预。这是一种价值投资理论的创立者与芝加哥学派学者们都未曾预料到的新现象。毕竟，量化宽松政策直到2008年才在美国推出。当时这样做合情合理：那场严重的金融衰退本质上是流动性和偿付能力危机，应对方法自然是注入流动性。但后来的危机并非如此，然而美联储推出的量化宽松版本数量却比《黑客帝国》的续集还要多（包括QE 1、QE 2、QE 3、QE 4，以及2008年至2014年间的“扭转操作”）。由于新冠疫情的冲击，美联储还实施了影响范围更广的计划，甚至开始购买高收益债券。其直接后果之一就是债务错配的周期大幅缩短，困境债券的供应量也少得令人失望。在全球金融危机和电信行业危机期间，困境期的峰值到谷值持续时间超过一年，而在2013年的“缩减恐慌”、2016年的能源价格危机以及2020年的疫情灾难中，这一周期则缩短到了短短三个月。简而言之，美联储已经学会了快速、大规模且果断地采取行动；它简直就是那个“偷走困境资产”的格林奇。

<!--en-->
The second tsunami is the Federal Reserve’s intervention in the capital markets, including corporate debt. This is a new phenomenon that neither the value investing creators nor the Chicago School academics envisioned. After all, quantitative easing (QE) was introduced in the United States only in 2008. It made sense then: the Great Financial Recession was aliquidity and solvency crisis. How do you combat it? By injecting liquidity. Subsequent crises were neither, yet the Fed has used more versions of QE than there are sequels of *The Matrix* (QE 1, 2, 3 and 4, and Operation Twist between 2008 and 2014). As a result of the Covid-19 crisis, it deployed an even greater-reaching program, dipping its toes into purchasing high-yield bonds. One of many direct results is that episodes of debt dislocation have dramatically shortened, and supply of distressed bonds has become disappointingly shallow. While the peak-to-trough distressed bout persisted for over a year during the Global Financial Crisis and the telecom crisis, it shortened to barely three months through the taper tantrum of 2013, the energy price crunch of 2016, and the pandemic catastrophe of 2020. Simply put, the Fed has learned to act fast, wide, and decisively; it's the Grinch Who Stole Distressed.

第三场革命源自大规模的在线零售式投资，这一现象在价值投资理论和有效市场理论看来都十分有趣。我们的新古典主义投资者很可能不会将Robinhood、Reddit或WallStreetBets用户的操作视为投资行为，因为我觉得格雷厄姆也不会把阅读推文定义为“彻底的分析”。但无论你将其称为投机、股票的博弈化还是交易的民主化，它都已成为一股重要的市场力量，会产生深远甚至持久的影响，足以让大型机构基金陷入困境，也能推动大规模破产案件走向特定结局。这远非那些“模因股”和“垃圾股”所出现的短暂波动所能比拟。以规模达125亿美元的对冲基金Melvin Capital为例，它在因GameStop股价剧烈波动而遭受重创后需要资金注入救助，几个月后仍被迫关闭。再看看Hertz，该公司连续的两项重组计划最初都让其股票股价几乎归零，但随后由于散户对低价股的投机行为导致股价突然上涨，先是引发了失败的股权融资尝试，接着又出现了反对重组计划的诉讼，这些因素最终使得公司股价有所回升，让破产前的股东们获得了可观的收益。

<!--en-->
The third revolution comes from mass retail online investing, an interesting phenomenon in the lenses of both value investing and efficient market theories. Our neoclassical investors probably wouldn't classify the actions of Robinhood, Reddit, or WallStreetBets users as investing, because I doubt Graham would define reading a tweet as "thorough analysis." But whether you call it speculation, gamification of stocks, or democratization of trading, it has become a critical market force with deep and sometimes lasting consequences, capable of bringing a large institutional fund to its knees and driving a large bankruptcy process to a specific outcome. It is well beyond the temporary yo-yo moves on "meme" stocks and "stonks." Ask Melvin Capital, the $12.5 billion hedge fund that required a capital infusion rescue after a devastating loss inflicted by the whiplash on GameStop and was still shut down a few months later. Or look at Hertz, where two successive restructuring plans initially left the equity for dead. A pop in the stock, unexplainable but for retail gambling in penny stocks, led first to a failed equity raise, then to a legal objection against restructuring plans that wiped out the equity, and finally to a 36-hour bidding auction that ascribed meaningful recovery to prebankruptcy equity holders.

也许这种现象只是毫无意义的群体投机行为。但倘若我们运用格雷厄姆和多德的框架来看，某些证券的内在价值之所以高于其经济效用，是因为它们还提供了其他价值：娱乐性以及让持有者融入一个共同体的机会。或许马科维茨和夏普会认为，这个共同体拥有了一种机构投资者无法使用的工具——在社交媒体时代之前这种工具根本难以想象，而且也与有效市场假说背道而驰：那就是能够集体行动的能力。

<!--en-->
Maybe the phenomenon is mere senseless mob speculation. But maybe, if we want to use the Graham and Dodd framework, the intrinsic value of some securities exceeds their economic utility because they deliver something more: entertainment value and membership in a community of holders. And maybe Markowitz and Sharpe would posit that this community holds a tool that is illegal for institutional investors, unfathomable until the era of social media, and antithetical to the Efficient Market Hypothesis: the ability to act as a group.

从这些发展态势我们可以得出结论：进行困境投资时，必须具备大象般的庞大实力、兔子般的敏捷速度以及“咆哮猫咪”般的聪明才智。⁵换言之，这极其复杂。对于未来那些年轻且冲动的困境投资者们，我告诉你们：不必害怕！因为答案就在这里，就在格雷厄姆和多德睿智的论述之中。首先，是关于资本运用的建议，尽管多年来许多资深同行都忽视了这一点，但在我的经验中它却始终具有很高的价值：“我们应当尽可能清楚自己在谈论什么。”（第4章）其次，如果其他方法都无效，请记住这句话：“正如丹麦哲学家索伦·克尔凯郭尔所说，人生只能向后理解——但必须向前度过。”⁶ [^1285]: ¹ “格雷厄姆与大卫·多德于1934年合著的《证券分析》被广泛视为现代价值投资的经典著作。”Ari Weinburg，《指数基金能否实现‘价值’？》，《华尔街日报》，2015年9月8日，https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/can-an-index-fund-deliver-the-value-1441764704.

<!--en-->
From these developments we would conclude that the imperative for distressed investing is to be as big as an elephant, quick as a bunny, and clever as a Roaring Kitty.⁵ In other words: it’s complicated. To the young and impetuous distressed investors of tomorrow, I say, fear not! For the answers are here, in the wise prose of Graham and Dodd. First, the capital advice, disregarded by many an esteemed colleague over the years yet reliably valuable in my experience: “We ought as far as possible to know what we are talking about.” (Chap. 4) Second, if all else fails, remember this: “As the Danish philosopher Soren Kierkegaard noted, life can only be understood backward—but it must be lived forward.”⁶
