CHAPTER 22

## 特权类证券

<!--en-->
*Privileged Issues*

接下来我们来看修订后的证券分类中的第二个主要类别，即买方认为其本金价值可能发生大幅变动的债券和优先股。在之前的讨论中（第5章），我们将这一类别细分为两类：一类是由于安全性不足而具有投机性的证券，另一类则是由于拥有转换权或类似特权、从而导致市场价格可能出现大幅波动的投机性证券。¹

<!--en-->
WE COME now to the second major division of our revised classification of securities, *viz.*, bonds and preferred stocks presumed by the buyer to be subject to substantial change in principal value. In our introductory discussion (Chap. 5) we subdivided this group under two heads: those issues which are speculative because of inadequate safety, and those which are speculative because they possess a conversion or similar privilege which makes possible substantial variations in market price.¹

## 具有投机性特权的优先类证券

<!--en-->
*SENIOR ISSUES WITH SPECULATIVE PRIVILEGES*

除了享有固定金额的本金和利息的优先索取权外，债券或优先股还可能被赋予分享普通股收益的权利。这类特权共有三种，具体如下：

<!--en-->
In addition to enjoying a prior claim for a fixed amount of principal and income, a bond or preferred stock may also be given the right to share in benefits accruing to the common stock. These privileges are of three kinds, designated as follows:

1. 可转换型——赋予持有人在约定条件下将优先类证券转换为普通股的权利。
2. 分红参与型——通常根据宣布的普通股股息金额，向优先类证券持有者支付额外收入。
3. 认购权——即债券或优先股持有者可按既定价格、数量及时间范围购买普通股。²由于转换权是这三种权利中最为人所熟知的，我们今后将经常使用“可转换证券”这一术语来指代所有具有此类特权的证券。**此类证券在形式上极具吸引力。**通过上述三种机制中的任何一种，高级证券几乎都能享有与企业普通股相同的盈利机会。因此，从*形式*角度来看，这类证券无疑是最具吸引力的，因为它们能够同时实现最大的安全性与价值无限上升的可能性。若某债券不仅符合优质投资的所有标准，还具备有趣的转换权，那它无疑会是一笔极为值得购买的资产。**其投资表现并不理想：原因所在。**尽管有如此有力的论据支持将这类具有特权的高级证券视为一种*形式*上的优质投资，但我们必须承认，实际投资经验并未普遍令人满意。对于这种预期与现实之间的差距，可以提出两种不同的原因。第一种原因是，仅有极少数具有特权的证券真正满足了优质投资的高标准。转换功能往往只是为了弥补安全性的不足而设计的。³在1926年至1929年可转换证券最流行的时期，这一缺陷尤为明显。⁴在那些年里，实力雄厚的工业企业通常通过发行普通股来筹集资金，而实力较弱或资本规模较小的企业则不得不依赖具有特权的高级证券。第二种原因与通过转换权获得利润的条件有关。虽然可转换债券的价格确实没有上限，但持有者在保持*投资头寸*的同时所能实现的利润却存在实际的限制。一旦具有特权的证券与普通股同步上涨，其价格很快就会在两个方向上都受到股票行情变动的影响，这样一来，继续持有该高级证券就变成了*投机性*操作。以下举例说明：假设有人以面值购买了某只3.5%高评级债券，该债券每100美元可转换为2股普通股（即转换比例为50）。购买时该普通股的价格为45美元。*第一阶段：*（1）如果股价下跌至35美元，该债券的价格可能仍接近面值。这体现了可转换证券相比普通股的显著技术优势。（2）如果股价上涨至55美元，该债券的价格很可能会升至115美元甚至更高。（其“即时转换价值”为110美元，但由于相比普通股具有优势，因此仍存在溢价空间。）这体现了此类可转换证券无疑具备的投机潜力。*第二阶段：*股价进一步上涨至65美元。此时该债券的转换价值为130美元，其售价也将处于这一水平或略高一些。此时，最初的购买者面临着一个问题：其债券的未来价格在很大程度上取决于普通股的走势。若想获得更高利润，他必须承担失去手中现有利润的风险，而这些利润实际上构成了其证券当前市场价值的重要部分。（普通股的下跌很容易导致该债券的价格从130美元降至110美元。）如果他选择继续持有该证券，那么他在很大程度上就处于普通股股东的处境，而且随着股价的进一步上涨，这种相似性会迅速加剧。 例如，如果他持有的债券价值仍为180（股票则为90），那么实际上他就已承担起了普通股股东的地位与风险。*此类具有股东属性的发行方式能带来无限利润。*因此，优先发行方式所带来的无限利润可能性在很大程度上是虚幻的。它们不应被视作债券或优先股的所有权，而应被视为承担了普通股股东的身份——任何不可转换债券的持有者都可以通过将其债券兑换成股票来实现这一身份。从实际角度来看，尽管可转换发行方式仍保留着投资持有的优势，但其利润空间通常只能限制在其面值的25%到35%之间。正因如此，优先发行方式的初始购买者通常不会持有这些证券超过最成功投资者所能获得的最高市场收益的一小部分，因而也就无法真正实现那些巨大的潜在利润。这样一来，所获得的利润可能无法弥补该领域不当投资所带来的损失。**具有吸引力的发行案例。**上述两个反对意见无疑会大大削弱我们对优先类高级证券的整体热情，但它们绝不会消除这些证券的固有优势，也不会消除以合理成功率利用这些优势的可能性。虽然*大多数*新的可转换证券发行可能缺乏足够的担保，⁵但这一规则也有不少例外情况，而对这些例外情况，敏锐的投资者应当格外关注。我们在文中附上了来自公用事业、铁路和工业领域的三个典型案例。
1. *Commonwealth Edison Company Convertible Debenture 3¹/₂s，到期日为1958年。* 这些债券于1938年6月和9月按面值向股东发行。该公司的财务数据充分证明，以该价格发行这些债券是稳妥的投资选择。在到期或提前赎回之前，这些债券可转换为40股普通股。1938年9月，当股票价格为24¹/₂时，这些债券可在纽约证券交易所按面值购买。在此价格水平下，债券与股票的售价极为接近，只要股票价格略有上涨，债券持有者即可获利出售。不到一年后（1939年7月），股票价格升至31³/₈，而债券价格则升至124³/₄。
2. *Chesapeake and Ohio Railway Company Convertible 5s，到期日为1946年。* 这些债券最初于1916年6月向股东发行。在1920年4月1日之前，它们可按75的价格转换为普通股；从该日期起至1923年4月1日，转换价格为80；至1926年4月1日，价格为90；至1936年4月1日，则为100。1924年末，当股票价格为91时，这些债券可以接近面值的价格购买，即无需支付转换特权溢价。具体而言，1924年11月28日，债券的售价为101，而股票价格为91。当时该公司的盈利状况持续改善，表明这些债券有充分的担保。（1924年，固定费用已由公司利润覆盖两次。）次年股票价格升至131，使得这些债券的价值达到145，这一事实也体现了转换特权的价值。
3. *Rand Kardex Bureau, Inc. 5¹/₂s，到期日为1931年。* 这些债券最初于1925年12月以99¹/₂的价格发行。它们附带股票购买认股权证（1927年1月1日后可分离），持有人有权在1926年以每股40美元、1927年每股42.50美元、1928年每股45美元、1929年每股47.50美元、1930年每股50美元的价格购买22¹/₂股A类普通股。（实际上，A类股票属于参与型优先股。）持有人可将债券按面值兑换用于支付通过认股权证购买的股票，这一规定实际上使这些债券具备了转换为股票的功能。这些债券似乎也有充分的担保。之前的财务数据（基于前身公司的盈利情况）显示了新发行的债券利息的覆盖程度如下：

<!--en-->
1. Convertible—conferring the right to exchange the senior issue for common stock on stipulated terms.
2. Participating—under which additional income may be paid to the senior security holder, dependent usually upon the amount of common dividends declared.
3. Subscription—by which holders of the bond or preferred stock may purchase common shares, at prices, in amounts, and during periods, stipulated.²
Since the conversion privilege is the most familiar of the three, we shall frequently use the term “convertible issues” torefer to privileged issues in general.
**Such Issues Attractive in Form.** By means of any one of these three provisions a senior security can be given virtually all the profit possibilities that attach to the common stock of the enterprise. Such issues must therefore be considered as the most attractive of all in point of *form*, since they permit the combination of maximum safety with the chance of unlimited appreciation in value. A bond that meets all the requirements of a sound investment and in addition possesses an interesting conversion privilege would undoubtedly constitute a highly desirable purchase.
**Their Investment Record Unenviable: Reasons.** Despite this impressive argument in favor of privileged senior issues as a *form* of investment, we must recognize that actual experience with this class has not been generally satisfactory. For this discrepancy between promise and performance, reasons of two different kinds may be advanced.
The first is that only a small fraction of the privileged issues have actually met the rigorous requirements of a sound investment. The conversion feature has most often been offered to compensate for inadequate security.³ This weakness was most pronounced during the period of greatest vogue for convertible issues, between 1926 and 1929.⁴ During these years it was broadly true that the strongly entrenched industrial enterprises raised money through sales of common stock, whereas the weaker—or weakly capitalized— undertakings resorted to privileged senior securities.
The second reason is related to the conditions under which profit may accrue from the conversion privilege. Although there is indeed no upper limit to the price that a convertible bond may reach, there is a very real limitation on the amount of profit that the holder may realize while still maintaining an *investment position*. After a privileged issue has advanced with the common stock, its price soon becomes dependent *in both directions* upon changes in the stock quotation, and to that extent the continued holding of the senior issue becomes a *speculative* operation. An example will make this clear:Let us assume the purchase of a high-grade 3½% bond at par, convertible into two shares of common for each $100 bond (i.e., convertible into common stock at 50). The common stock is selling at 45 when the bond is bought.
*First Stage:* (1) If the stock declines to 35, the bond may remain close to par. This illustrates the pronounced technical advantage of a convertible issue over the common stock. (2) If the stock advances to 55, the price of the bond will probably rise to 115 or more. (Its “immediate conversion value” would be 110, but a premium would be justified because of its advantage over the stock.) This illustrates the undoubted speculative possibilities of such a convertible issue.
*Second Stage:* The stock advances further to 65. The conversion value of the bond is now 130, and it will sell at that figure, or slightly higher. At this point the original purchaser is faced with a problem. Within wide limits, the future price of his bond depends entirely upon the course of the common stock. In order to seek a larger profit he must risk the loss of the profit in hand, which in fact constitutes a substantial part of the present market value of his security. (A drop in the price of the common could readily induce a decline in the bond from 130 to 110.) If he elects to hold the issue, he places himself to a considerable degree in the position of the stockholders, and this similarity increases rapidly as the price advances further. If, for example, he is still holding the bond at a level say of 180 (90 for the stock), he has for all practical purposes assumed the status and risks of a stockholder.
*Unlimited Profit in Such Issues Identified with Stockholder's Position.* The unlimited profit possibilities of a privileged issue are thus in an important sense illusory. They must be identified not with the ownership of a bond or preferred stock but with the assumption of a common stockholder's position—which any holder of a nonconvertible may effect by exchanging his bond for a stock. Practically speaking, the range of profit possibilities for a convertible issue, *although still maintaining the advantage of an investment holding*, must usually be limited to somewhere between 25 and 35% of its face value. For this reason originalpurchasers of privileged issues do not ordinarily hold them for more than a small fraction of the maximum market gains scored by the most successful among them, and consequently they do not actually realize these very large possible profits. Thus the profits taken may not offset the losses occasioned by unsound commitments in this field.
**Examples of Attractive Issues.** The two objections just discussed must considerably temper our enthusiasm for privileged senior issues as a class, but they by no means destroy their inherent advantages nor the possibilities of exploiting them with reasonable success. Although *most* new convertible offerings may have been inadequately secured,⁵ there are fairly frequent exceptions to the rule, and these exceptions should be of prime interest to the alert investor. We append three leading examples of such opportunities, taken from the utility, the railroad, and the industrial fields.
1. *Commonwealth Edison Company Convertible Debenture 3¹/₂s, Due 1958.* These bonds were offered to shareholders in June and September 1938 at par. The statistical exhibit of the company gave every assurance that the debentures were a sound commitment at that price. They were convertible into 40 shares of common stock until maturity or prior redemption.
In September 1938 the debentures could have been bought on the New York Stock Exchange at par when the stock was selling at 24¹/₂. At these prices the bonds and stock were selling very close to a parity, and a slight advance in the price of the stock would enable the holder of the bond to sell at a profit. Less than a year later (July 1939) the stock had risen to 31³/₈, and the bonds to 124³/₄.
2. *Chesapeake and Ohio Railway Company Convertible 5s, Due 1946.* These bonds were originally offered to shareholders in June 1916. They were convertible into common stock at 75 until April 1, 1920; at 80 from the latter date until April 1, 1923; at 90 from the latter date until April 1, 1926; and at 100 from the latter date until April 1, 1936.
Late in 1924 they could have been bought on a parity basis (i.e., without payment of a premium for the conversion privilege) at prices close to par. Specifically, they sold on November 28, 1924, at 101 when the stock sold at 91. At that time the company's earnings were showing continued improvement and indicated that the bonds were adequately secured. (Fixed charges were covered twice in 1924.) The value of the conversion privilege was shown by the fact that the stock sold at 131 in the next year, making the bonds worth 145.
3. *Rand Kardex Bureau, Inc., 5¹/₂s, Due 1931.* These bonds were originally offered in December 1925 at 99¹/₂. They carried stock-purchase warrants (detachable after January 1, 1927) entitling the holder to purchase 22¹/₂ shares of Class *A* common at $40 per share during 1926, at $42.50 per share during 1927, at $45 per share during 1928, at $47.50 per share during 1929, and at $50 per share during 1930. (The Class *A* stock was in reality a participating preferred issue.) The bonds could be turned in at par in payment for the stock purchased under the warrants, a provision that virtually made the bonds convertible into the stock.
The bonds appeared to be adequately secured. The previous exhibit (based on the earnings of the predecessor companies) showed the following coverage for the interest on the new bond issue:

当这些债券向公众发行时，A类股票的报价约为42，这表明股票购买认股权证具有即时价值。次年，股票价格升至53，而债券价格则降至$130\frac{1}{2}$。1927年（Rand Kardex与Remington Typewriter合并时），股票价格升至76，债券价格则升至190。

<!--en-->
When the bonds were offered to the public, the Class *A* stock was quoted at about 42, indicating an immediate value for the stock-purchase warrants. The following year the stockadvanced to 53, and the bonds to $130\frac{1}{2}$. In 1927 (when Rand Kardex merged with Remington Typewriter) the stock advanced to 76, and the bonds to 190.

**缺乏吸引力的发行案例。** 作为对比，我们将举一个表面上看似有吸引力但实际上并不稳健的可转换债券发行案例，这类案例在1928–1929年间较为常见。

<!--en-->
**Example of an Unattractive Issue.** By way of contrast with these examples we shall supply an illustration of a superficially attractive but basically unsound convertible offering, such as characterized the 1928–1929 period.

*National Trade Journals, Inc. 6%可转换票据，到期日为1938年。* 该公司成立于1928年2月，旨在收购并出版大约十几本行业杂志。1928年11月，它以$97\frac{1}{2}$的价格出售了价值2,800,000美元的此类票据。最初，这些票据可在1930年11月1日之前按每股37.03美元的价格转换为27股普通股；从该日期起至1932年11月1日，可转换为25股，价格为每股40美元；在债券存续的最后两年，转换价格逐渐上升至每股52.63美元。

<!--en-->
*National Trade Journals, Inc., 6% Convertible Notes, Due 1938.* The company was organized in February 1928 to acquire and publish about a dozen trade journals. In November 1928 it sold $2,800,000 of the foregoing notes at $97\frac{1}{2}$. The notes were initially convertible into 27 shares of common stock (at $37.03 per share) until November 1, 1930; into 25 shares (at $40 a share) from the latter date until November 1, 1932; and at prices that progressively increased to $52.63 a share during the last two years of the life of the bonds.

在发行时以及之后的数月里，这些债券的购买价格仅略高于其面值，相比同类股票的市值而言。具体而言，1928年11月30日，当股票价格为$34\frac{1}{8}$时，这些债券的购买价格为$97\frac{1}{2}$，这意味着股票只需上涨两点，持有者就能通过转换获得利润。

<!--en-->
These bonds could have been purchased at the time of issuance and for several months thereafter at prices only slightly above their parity value as compared with the market value of the equivalent stock. Specifically, they could have been bought at $97\frac{1}{2}$ on November 30, when the stock sold at $34\frac{1}{8}$, which meant that the stock needed to advance only two points to assure a profit on conversion.

然而，尽管发行通函中描绘了光鲜的景象，但这些债券似乎从未获得过充分的担保。该通函根据此前$3\frac{1}{2}$年的数据展示了前身企业的“预计”盈利情况，其平均数值是债券发行费用的4.16倍。但其中近一半的预计盈利预计将来自合并带来的成本削减（如工资降低等）所带来的经济效益。对于保守型投资者而言，绝不能将这些“盈利”视为理所当然，尤其是在这种风险高、竞争激烈且实物资产相对较少的业务领域中。

<!--en-->
However, at no time did the bonds appear to be adequately secured, despite the attractive picture presented in the offering circular. The circular exhibited “estimated” earnings of the predecessor enterprise based on the $3\frac{1}{2}$ years preceding, which averaged 4.16 times the charges on the bond issue. But close to half of these estimated earnings were expected to be derived from economies predicted to result from the consolidation in the way of reduction of salaries, etc. The conservative investor would not be justified in taking these “earnings” for granted, particularly in a hazardous and competitive business of this type, with a relatively small amount of tangible assets.

为1928年最后10个月及随后历年的实际收益。1931年6月任命了接管人，同年8月这些资产被出售，债券持有人最终每美元仅获得约$8\frac{1}{2}$美分。**推导出的原则。**通过这些对比案例，可以总结出一条投资原则，为选择具有优先权的优先股提供有价值的指导。该原则如下：*那些以接近或高于面值出售的优先权优先股，必须符合纯粹固定价值投资或纯粹普通股投机中的某一要求，并且购买时必须明确具备其中一种资格。*这一选项提供了两种不同的购买此类优先证券的方式：既可以将其作为稳健的投资，附带因本金增值而带来利润的*偶然*机会，也可以主要将其视为一种具有吸引力的普通股投机方式。一般来说，不应存在中间路线。注重本金安全的*投资者*不应为了转换特权而降低自己的要求；而*投机者*也不应因为债券合约所提供的虚假安全感而被前景一般的企业所吸引。我们反对在纯粹投资态度与明显具有投机性质的态度之间进行任何妥协，这一立场主要基于主观考量。一旦采取中间立场，通常会导致混乱、思维不清以及自我欺骗。那些为获得分红特权而放宽安全要求的投资者，往往在财务或心理上都没有准备好应对投资失败所带来的不可避免的损失。那些希望通过可转换证券来降低风险的投机者，很可能会发现自己的主要兴趣在企业本身与特权条款之间摇摆不定，而且很可能对自己究竟是股东还是债券持有人感到迷茫。（*以大幅折价出售的优先权证券*通常不受此原则约束，因为它们属于稍后将讨论的第二类投机性优先证券。）回到我们的例子中，可以立即看出，Commonwealth Edison的3\frac{1}{2}美元债券本应作为普通投资品进行购买，无需考虑其转换功能。由于该转换特权可能带来价值，使得该债券在发行时具有近乎独一无二的吸引力。对于Chesapeake and Ohio以及Rand Kardex的债券，也能做出类似的论述。对于那些认为相关普通股价格即将上涨的投机者而言，这三类证券同样具有吸引力。另一方面，National Trade Journals的债券则无法通过严格的定性和定量安全测试。因此，它们只应吸引那些对相关股票的未来价值充满信心的人。不过，这类债券的大部分购买行为很可能并非出于投资或投机于National Trade Journals普通股的主要目的，而是基于其具有吸引力的转换特权条款，以及认为其作为债券投资“相当安全”的感觉。正是这种介于真正投资与真正投机之间的妥协让我们不予认可，主要是因为购买者对其投资目的或所承担的风险没有清晰的认识。**关于持有或出售的规则。**在阐述了用于指导*选择*优先权证券的基本原则之后，接下来我们要探讨的是，针对这些证券之后的持有或出售能制定哪些规则。 那些主要是作为对普通股的持有承诺而购买的可转换债券，若能持有到期，往往能获得比从投资角度买入的同类债券更高的利润。如果这类债券的价格从100上涨到150，较高的溢价本身并不一定就是必须卖出的决定性理由；投资者应依据自己对普通股是否已涨至足以让其获利离场的判断来做出决策。但若是出于安全债券投资的目的而购买，则保守计算的预期利润上限便会直接发挥作用。基于上文详细阐述的原因，那些以保守态度购买此类特殊债券的投资者通常不会持有超过25%至35%涨幅的债券。这意味着，在可转换债券领域中，真正成功的投资操作所维持的时间并不会很长。因此，购买这类债券时应考虑到长期持有的*可能性*，同时也抱有希望尽快实现潜在利润的*期望*。上述讨论引出了另一条投资准则，即：*在通常情况下，投资者不应将可转换债券进行转换，而应选择持有或卖出*。的确，这类特殊债券的存在目的就是在看似有利时促成转换。如果债券价格大幅上涨，其当前收益率会降至不具吸引力的水平，而通过转换成股票通常能获得可观的收益。然而，一旦投资者真的将债券转换成股票，他就放弃了当初购买时所依赖的本金及利息的优先受偿权。如果转换后情况恶化，他的股票价值可能会远低于其债券的原始成本，他不仅会损失利润，还会损失部分本金。此外，他还有可能——无论是在一般情况下还是具体案例中——从债券投资者转变为股票投机者。必须认识到，即便是优质的可转换债券也存在一定的隐蔽风险，对于缺乏警惕的人来说，它很容易变成一个代价高昂的陷阱。为避免这种危险，投资者必须坚定地保持保守的投资观念。当其债券价格超出投资范围时，就必须将其卖出；最重要的是，即使之后该债券价格大幅上涨，他也不应认为自己的判断有误。一旦这类债券进入投机范畴，其市场走势就不再由投资者掌控，就如同他对那些完全不了解的投机股票的价格波动无能为力一样。如果大多数投资者都遵循这里推荐的行事方式，那么债券的转换将只能由那些明确出于投机或所谓投资目的而主动购买股票的人来实现。⁶反对投资者转换可转换债券的论点，同样适用于他们行使为投资目的购买的债券附带的股票认购权的情况。在有利条件下，持续投资于这类特殊债券意味着需要频繁地获取利润，并用价格并非过高溢价的新型证券进行替换。更具体地说，以100的价格购入的债券会在比如125的价格卖出，然后用面值附近价格可买到的另一只优质可转换债券进行替换。这类理想的投资机会不太可能持续出现，投资者也未必有能力找到所有现成的机会。不过，近年来的融资趋势表明，可能会有相当数量极具吸引力的可转换债券再次出现。 在1926–1929年期间大量发行质量较差的优先债券，以及1930–1934年期间出于安全考虑新发行的债券几乎不再包含转换优先权之后，市场趋势明显转向了中间状态——即有时会运用某些激励措施来促进优质债券的销售。⁷ 1934年至1939年间售出的那些债券，要么票面利率极低，要么很快就会出现过高的溢价。不过我们认为，精明且慎重的投资者仍有可能在这一领域找到相当数量的有吸引力的投资机会。[^1334]：¹ 在1934年的版本中，这里曾设有一个关于能以优惠价格获得的投资级高级债券的板块。尽管这类债券在1931–1933年期间较为常见，但此后便变得极为稀缺——即便在1937–1938年的市场低迷期也是如此。因此，为节省篇幅，我们现在决定省略这一板块。

Receivers were appointed in June 1931. The properties were sold in August of that year, and bondholders later received about $8\frac{1}{2}$ cents on the dollar.
**Principle Derived.** From these contrasting instances an investment principle may be developed that should afford a valuable guide to the selection of privileged senior issues. The principle is as follows: *A privileged senior issue, selling close to or above face value, must meet the requirements either of a straight fixed-value investment or of a straight common-stock speculation, and it must be bought with one or the other qualification clearly in view.*
The alternative given supplies two different approaches to the purchase of a privileged security. It may be bought as a sound investment with an *incidental* chance of profit through an enhancement of principal, or it may be bought *primarily* as an attractive form of speculation in the common stock. Generally speaking, there should be no middle ground. The *investor* interested in safety of principal should not abate his requirements in return for a conversion privilege; the *speculator* should not be attracted to an enterprise of mediocre promise because of the pseudo-security provided by the bond contract.
Our opposition to any compromise between the purely investment and the admittedly speculative attitude is based primarily on subjective grounds. Where an intermediate stand is taken, the result is usually confusion, clouded thinking, and self-deception. The investor who relaxes his safety requirements to obtain a profit-sharing privilege is frequently not prepared, financially or mentally, for the inevitable loss if fortune should frown on the venture. The speculator who wants to reduce his risk by operating in convertible issues is likely to find his primary interest divided between the enterprise itself and the terms of the privilege, and he will probably be uncertain in his own mind as to whether he is at bottom a stockholder or a bondholder. (Privileged issues *selling at substantial discounts from par* are not in general subject to this principle, since they belong to the second category of speculative senior securities to be considered later.)
Reverting to our examples, it will be seen at once that the Commonwealth Edison $3\frac{1}{2}$s could properly have been purchased as an investment without any regard to the conversion feature. The strong possibility that this privilege would be of value made the bond almost uniquely attractive at the time of issuance. Somewhat similar statements could be made with respect to the Chesapeake and Ohio and the Rand Kardex bonds. Any of these three securities should also have been attractive to a speculator who was persuaded that the related common stock was due for an advance in price.
On the other hand the National Trade Journals Debentures could not have passed stringent qualitative and quantitative tests of safety. Hence they should properly have been of interest only to a person who had full confidence in the future value of the stock. It is hardly likely, however, that most of the buying of this issue was motivated by the primary desire to invest or speculate in the National Trade Journals common stock, but it was based rather on the attractive terms of the conversion privilege and on the feeling that the issue was “fairly safe” as a bond investment. It is precisely this compromise between true investment and true speculation that we disapprove, chiefly because the purchaser has no clear-cutidea of the purpose of his commitment or of the risk that he is incurring.
**Rules Regarding Retention or Sale.** Having stated a basic principle to guide the *selection* of privileged issues, we ask next what rules can be established regarding their subsequent retention or sale. Convertibles bought primarily as a form of commitment in the common stock may be held for a larger profit than those acquired from the investment standpoint. If a bond of the former class advances from 100 to 150, the large premium need not in itself be a controlling reason for selling out; the owner must be guided rather by his views as to whether or not the common stock has advanced enough to justify taking his profit. But when the purchase is made primarily as a safe bond investment, then the limitation on the amount of profit that can conservatively be waited for comes directly into play. For the reasons explained in detail above, the conservative buyer of privileged issues will not ordinarily hold them for more than a 25 to 35% advance. This means that a really successful investment operation in the convertible field does not cover a long period of time. Hence such issues should be bought with the *possibility* of long-term holding in mind but with the *hope* that the potential profit will be realized fairly soon.
The foregoing discussion leads to the statement of another investment rule, *viz.*:
*In the typical case, a convertible bond should not be converted by the investor. It should be either held or sold.*
It is true that the object of the privilege is to bring about such conversion when it seems advantageous. If the price of the bond advances substantially, its current yield will shrink to an unattractive figure, and there is ordinarily a substantial gain in income to be realized through the exchange into stock. Nevertheless when the investor does exchange his bond into the stock, he abandons the priority and the unqualified claim to principal and interest upon which the purchase was originally premised. If after the conversion is made things should go badly, his shares may decline in value far below theoriginal cost of his bond, and he will lose not only his profit but part of his principal as well.
Moreover he is running the risk of transforming himself—generally, as well as in the specific instances—from a bond investor into a stock speculator. It must be recognized that there is something insidious about even a good convertible bond; it can easily prove a costly snare to the unwary. To avoid this danger the investor must cling determinedly to a conservative viewpoint. When the price of his bond has passed out of the investment range, he must sell it; most important of all, he must not consider his judgment impugned if the bond subsequently rises to a much higher level. The market behavior of the issue, once it has entered the speculative range, is no more the investor's affair than the price gyrations of any speculative stock about which he knows nothing.
If the course of action here recommended is followed by investors generally, the conversion of bonds would be brought about only through their purchase for this specific purpose by persons who have decided independently to acquire the shares for either speculation or supposed investment.⁶ The arguments against the investor's converting convertible issues apply with equal force against his exercising stock-purchase warrants attached to bonds bought for investment purposes.
A continued policy of investment in privileged issues would, under favorable conditions, require rather frequent taking of profits and replacement by new securities not selling at an excessive premium. More concretely, a bond bought at 100 would be sold, say, at 125 and be replaced by another good convertible issue purchasable at about par. It is not likely that satisfactory opportunities of this kind will be continuously available or that the investor would have the means of locating all those that are at hand. But the trend of financing in recent years offers some promise that a fair number of really attractive convertibles may again make their appearance. Following the 1926–1929 period, marked by a flood of privileged issues generally of poor quality, and the 1930–1934 period, in which the emphasis on safety caused the virtual disappearance of conversion privileges from new bondofferings, there has been a definite swing of the pendulum towards a middle point, where participating features are at times employed to facilitate the sale of sound bond offerings.⁷ Most of those sold between 1934 and 1939 either carried very low coupon rates or immediately jumped to a prohibitive premium. But we incline to the view that the discriminating and careful investor is again likely to find a reasonable number of attractive opportunities presented in this field.
[^1334]: ¹ In the 1934 edition we had here a section on investment-quality senior issues obtainable at bargain levels. Although these were plentiful in the 1931–1933 period, they have since grown very scarce—even in the market decline of 1937–1938. To save space, therefore, we are now omitting this section.

² 还存在第四种利润分享安排，其重要性低于前三种，首次出现于1928–1929年的牛市中。这就是所谓的“可选”债券或优先股。该选项允许持有人以固定数量的普通股（即按每股固定价格）来替代现金获取利息或股息。例如，1929年发行的Commercial Investment Trust $6可转换优先股可选系列，就赋予持有人选择权：可以按每年1/13股的普通股形式获得股息，而非6美元现金。这相当于普通股的股价为78美元/股，因此只要股票售价高于78美元，该选项就会具有价值。类似地，1929年发行的Warner Brothers Pictures, Inc. 1939年到期的6%可选可转换债券，也赋予持有人选择权：可以按每年1股普通股的形式获取利息，而非60美元现金。

<!--en-->
² There is still a fourth type of profit-sharing arrangement, of less importance than the three just described, which made its first appearance in the 1928–1929 bull market. This is the so-called “optional” bond or preferred stock. The option consists of taking interest or dividend payments in a fixed amount of common stock (i.e., at a fixed price per share) in lieu of cash. For example, Commercial Investment Trust $6 Convertible Preference, Optional Series of 1929, gave the holder the option to take his dividend at the annual rate of one-thirteenth share of common instead of $6 in cash. This was equivalent to a price of $78 per share for the common, which meant that the option would be valuable whenever the stock was selling above 78. Similarly, Warner Brothers Pictures, Inc., Optional 6% Convertible Debentures, due 1939, issued in 1929, gave the owner the option to take his interest payments at the annual rate of one share of common stock instead of $60 in cash.

可以说，这种可选安排是转换特权的改良形式，其中利息或股息金额可分别转换为普通股。在大多数，甚至可能是所有这类发行中，本金也是可转换的。收益支付的独立转换性虽在一定程度上提升了该特权的吸引力，但提升幅度并不大。

<!--en-->
It may be said that this optional arrangement is a modified form of conversion privilege, under which the interest or dividend amounts are made separately convertible into common stock. In most, possibly all, of these issues, the principal is convertible as well. The separate convertibility of the income payments adds somewhat, but not a great deal, to the attractiveness of the privilege.

³ 1927年《美国投资银行家协会工业证券委员会报告》引用了某项建议——大概是在得到认可的情况下——称由于中等规模工业公司的一部分高级证券“在五到十年内可能会出现大幅亏损”，因此应通过转换或其他特权让这些证券的投资者能够分享未来的盈利，以此弥补风险。参见《美国投资银行家协会第十六届年度会议论文集》，第144–145页，1927年。

See *Proceedings of the Sixteenth Annual Convention of the Investment Bankers Association of America*, pp. 144–145, 1927.

CHAPTER 23

## 特权高级证券的技术特征

<!--en-->
*Technical Characteristics of Privileged Senior Securities*

在前一章中，我们已从投资与投机的一般原则角度探讨了特权高级证券。为了从实际应用层面充分了解这类证券，现在有必要对其特征进行更深入的讨论。此类研究可从三个连续的角度展开：（1）三种特权类型——转换、参与和认购（即“认股权证”）共有的特征；（2）每种类型相对于其他类型的优劣；（3）每种类型本身的技术层面。¹

<!--en-->
IN THE PRECEDING chapter privileged senior issues were considered in their relationship to the broader principles of investment and speculation. To arrive at an adequate knowledge of this group of securities from their practical side, a more intensive discussion of their characteristics is now in order. Such a study may conveniently be carried on from three successive viewpoints: (1) considerations common to all three types of privilege—conversion, participation, and subscription (i.e., “warrant”); (2) the relative merits of each type, as compared with the others; (3) technical aspects of each type, considered by itself.¹

## 普遍适用于特权发行证券的考量因素

<!--en-->
*CONSIDERATIONS GENERALLY APPLICABLE TO PRIVILEGED ISSUES*

利润分享机制的吸引力取决于两个主要但彼此无关的因素：（1）该安排的*条款*；（2）可分享的*利润前景*。用一个简单的例子来说明：

<!--en-->
The attractiveness of a profit-sharing feature depends upon two major but entirely unrelated factors: (1) the *terms* of the arrangement and (2) the *prospects* of profits to share. To use a simple illustration:

<table><thead><tr><th>公司A</th><th>公司B</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>4%利率的债券，售价100美元</td><td>4%利率的债券，售价100美元</td></tr><tr><td>可按50美元的价格转换为股票（即100美元的债券可换得2股股票）</td><td>可按33又1/3美元的价格转换为股票（即100美元的债券可换得3股股票）</td></tr><tr><td>股票的售价为30美元</td><td>股票的售价为30美元</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th>Company A</th><th>Company B</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>4% bond selling at 100</td><td>4% bond selling at 100</td></tr><tr><td>Convertible into stock at 50 (i.e., two shares of stock for a $100 bond)</td><td>Convertible into stock at 33 1/3 (i.e., three shares of stock for a $100 bond)</td></tr><tr><td>Stock selling at 30</td><td>Stock selling at 30</td></tr></tbody></table>

**转换优惠的条款与企业前景对比。** 在债券*B*的情况下，转换优惠的*条款*显然更具吸引力；因为该股票只需上涨略高于3点即可实现盈利，而股票*A*则需要上涨超过20点才能使转换有利可图。尽管如此，债券*A*反而可能成为更划算的购买选择。因为有可能股票*B*根本不会上涨，而股票*A*的股价却可能翻倍甚至三倍。

<!--en-->
**Terms of the Privilege vs. Prospects for the Enterprise.** The *terms* of the conversion privilege are evidently more attractive in the case of Bond *B*; for the stock need advance only a little more than 3 points to assure a profit, whereas Stock *A* must advance over 20 points to make conversion profitable. Nevertheless, it is quite possible that Bond *A* may turn out to be the more advantageous purchase. For conceivably Stock *B* may fail to advance at all while Stock *A* may double or triple in price.

在这两个因素之间，选择合适的*公司*无疑比选择条款最优的发行项目更具盈利性。企业本身的吸引力与特权条款之间并不存在任何可以用来进行权衡的数学依据，也无法在这两个完全独立的价值要素之间找到平衡点。但在分析投资级特权发行项目时，必须更加重视特权*条款*，并非因为它们更为重要，而是因为它们更易于明确处理。判断某家企业比另一家更有前景似乎是件相对容易的事，但要确定在特定价格下的某只普通股明显优于当前价格下的另一只股票，则绝非如此简单。

<!--en-->
As between the two factors, it is undoubtedly true that it is more profitable to select the right *company* than to select the issue with the most desirable *terms*. There is certainly no mathematical basis on which the attractiveness of the enterprise may be offset against the terms of the privilege, and a balance struck between these two entirely dissociated elements of value. But in analyzing privileged issues of the investment grade, the *terms* of the privilege must receive the greater attention, not because they are more important but because they can be more definitely dealt with. It may seem a comparatively easy matter to determine that one enterprise is more promising than another. But it is by no means so easy to establish that one common stock at a given price is clearly preferable to another stock at its current price.

回到我们的例子，如果可以十分确定，甚至有合理的可能性认为股票*A*比股票*B*更有可能涨至50点而非33点，那么这两只股票的报价就不会都是30点了。当然，股票*A*的售价会更高。我们想表达的是，市场价格通常已经*反映*了一家企业相对于另一家企业的任何优势。那些因为预期股票*A*的涨幅会远快于股票*B*而选择债券*A*的投资者，其实是在一个缺乏确定性且错误频发的语境下进行独立判断的。正因如此，我们怀疑从投资角度出发、通过购买具有优势的证券来获取收益的策略，能否主要基于购买者对企业未来利润增长的预期。（阐述这一点只是重复了固定价值投资领域早已确立的一项原则。）

<!--en-->
Reverting to our example, if it were quite certain, or even reasonably probable, that Stock *A* is more likely to advance to 50 than Stock *B* to advance to 33, then both issues would not be quoted at 30. Stock *A*, of course, would be selling higher. The point we make is that the market price in general *reflects* already any superiority that one enterprise has demonstrated over another. The investor who prefers Bond *A* because he expects its related stock to rise a great deal faster than Stock *B*, is exercising independent judgment in a field where certainty is lacking and where mistakes are necessarily frequent. For this reason we doubt that a successful policy of buying privileged issues *from the investment approach* can be based primarily upon the purchaser's view regarding the future expansion of the profits of the enterprise. (In stating this point we are merely repeating a principle previously laid down in the field of fixed-value investment.)

在采取投机性做法的情况下，*即*主要将购买该股票视为获取其权益的一种理想方式时，当然很合理地应当给予买家对公司未来发展的判断以更大的权重。

<!--en-->
Where the speculative approach is followed, *i.e.*, where the issue is bought primarily as a desirable method of acquiring an interest in the stock, it would be quite logical, of course, to assign dominant weight to the buyer's judgment as to the future of the company.

**三个重要要素。** 1. *特权的范围。* 在审视利润分享特权的*条款*时，可以发现其中包含三个构成要素。它们分别是：a. 每美元投资所能获得的利润分享或投机收益的*幅度*；b. 购买时该特权与实际可实现的利润之间的*接近程度*；c. 该特权的*有效期*。附属于可转换证券或认股权证型优先证券的投机收益金额，等于该特权所覆盖的股票数量在当前市场价值下的总额。在其他条件相同的情况下，每美元投资对应的投机收益幅度越大，该特权就越有吸引力。

<!--en-->
**Three Important Elements.** 1. *Extent of the Privilege.* In examining the *terms* of a profit-sharing privilege, three component elements are seen to enter. These are:
a. The *extent* of the profit-sharing or speculative interest per dollar of investment.
b. The *closeness* of the privilege to a realizable profit at the time of purchase.
c. The *duration* of the privilege.
The amount of speculative interest attaching to a convertible or warrant-bearing senior security is equal to the current market value of the number of shares of stock covered by the privilege. Other things being equal, the larger the amount of the speculative interest per dollar of investment the more attractive the privilege.

*示例：* 此前介绍过的 Rand Kardex $5\frac{1}{2}$s 期权，赋予持有人以初始价格 40 美元购买$22\frac{1}{2}$股*A*类股票的权利。此时*A*类股票的当前价格为 42 美元。该“投机收益”为$22\frac{1}{2} \times 42$，即每 1,000 美元债券可获得$945$的收益。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Rand Kardex $5\frac{1}{2}$s, previously described, carried warrants to buy $22\frac{1}{2}$ shares of Class *A* stock initially at 40. Current price of Class *A* stock was 42. The “speculative interest” amounted to $22\frac{1}{2} \times 42$, or $945$ per $1,000 bond.

Reliable Stores Corporation在1927年发行的6s债券最初附带仅可购买5股普通股的认股权，发行价为10美元/股。该普通股的当前价格为12美元/股。因此，“投机收益”为$5 \times 12$，即每1,000美元的债券仅有$60$的收益。

<!--en-->
Reliable Stores Corporation 6s, offered in 1927, carried warrants to buy only 5 shares of common stock initially at 10. Current price of the common was 12. Hence the “speculative interest” amounted to $5 \times 12$, or only $60$ per $1,000 bond.

Intercontinental Rubber Products Co. 7s 是债券背后存在巨大投机性需求的典型例子。由于1922年发行时的一些特殊条款，每张面值为1,000美元的债券可转换为100股股票，同时持有人还拥有以10美元的价格额外购买400股股票的权利。当1925年这些股票以10美元的价格出售时，每张1,000美元债券的投机性收益为$500 \times 10$，或$5,000$。如果此时这些债券的售价为120美元，其投机性收益将相当于该债券面值的417%，也就是Reliable Stores案例中投机性收益的70倍。

<!--en-->
Intercontinental Rubber Products Co. 7s offered an extraordinary example of a large speculative interest attaching to a bond. As a result of peculiar provisions surrounding their issuance in 1922, each $1,000 note was convertible into 100 shares of stock and also carried the right to purchase 400 additional shares at 10. When the stock sold at 10 in 1925, the speculative interest per $1,000 note amounted to $500 \times 10$, or $5,000$. If the notes were then selling, say, at 120, the speculative interest would have equalled 417% of the bond.
investment—or 70 *times* as great as in the case of the Reliable Stores offering.

投机性利息规模的实际重要性可通过以下对比来说明，这些对比涵盖了上述三个案例。

<!--en-->
The practical importance of the amount of speculative interest can be illustrated by the following comparison, covering the three examples above given.

<table><thead><tr><th>项目</th><th>Reliable Stores 6s</th><th>Rand Kardex 5½s</th><th>洲际橡胶7人制橄榄球赛</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>每1,000美元债券所对应的股数</td><td>5</td><td>22½</td><td>500</td></tr><tr><td>基准价格</td><td>$10.00</td><td>$40.00</td><td>$10.00</td></tr><tr><td>当股价上涨时，债券价值上升：</td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td>比基础价格高25%</td><td>12.50</td><td>225.00</td><td>1,250.00</td></tr><tr><td>比基础价格高50%</td><td>25.00</td><td>450.00</td><td>2,500.00</td></tr><tr><td>比基础价格高100%</td><td>50.00</td><td>900.00</td><td>5,000.00</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th>Item</th><th>Reliable Stores 6s</th><th>Rand Kardex 5½s</th><th>Intercontinental Rubber 7s</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Number of shares covered by each $1,000 bond</td><td>5</td><td>22½</td><td>500</td></tr><tr><td>Base price</td><td>$10.00</td><td>$40.00</td><td>$10.00</td></tr><tr><td>Increase in value of bond when stock advances:</td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr><tr><td>25% above base price</td><td>12.50</td><td>225.00</td><td>1,250.00</td></tr><tr><td>50% above base price</td><td>25.00</td><td>450.00</td><td>2,500.00</td></tr><tr><td>100% above base price</td><td>50.00</td><td>900.00</td><td>5,000.00</td></tr></tbody></table>

对于可转换债券，当股票以转换价格出售时，投机性收益始终为债券面值的100%。因此，在这些情况下，我们的第一和第二成分元素表达相同的事实。如果以面值出售的债券可以转换为股票，转换价为50，而股票以30出售，则投机性收益为承诺金额的60%，即股票当前价格相当于转换前所需价格的60%才能盈利。股票购买权证发行并不披露投机性收益与实际利润之间的固定关系。在Reliable Stores 6s案例中，投机性收益很小，但在发行时确实实现了实际利润，因为股票售价*高于*认购价。

<!--en-->
In the case of convertible bonds the speculative interest always amounts to 100% of the bond at par when the stock sells at the conversion price. Hence in these issues our first and second component elements express the same fact. If a bond selling at par is convertible into stock at 50, and if the stock sells at 30, then the speculative interest amounts to 60% of the commitment, which is the same thing as saying that the current price of the stock is 60% of that needed before conversion would be profitable. Stock-purchase-warrant issues disclose no such fixed relationship between the amount of the speculative interest and the proximity of this interest to a realizable profit. In the case of the Reliable Stores 6s, the speculative interest was very small, but it showed an actual profit at the time of issuance, since the stock was selling *above* the subscription price.

*低价大量股份投机的意义。*顺便说一下，技术上，大量低价股份的投资比高价少量股份的投资更有吸引力。这是因为低价股份在百分比上更容易波动，比高价股票更不稳定。因此，如果债券有良好担保且可以以低价转换为大量股份，那么就有很好的机会获得巨大利润，而不必面临因股票价格下跌导致更大损失的风险。

<!--en-->
*Significance of Call on Large Number of Shares at Low Price.* It may be said parenthetically that a speculative interest in a large number of shares selling at a low price is technically more attractive than one in a smaller number of shares selling at a high price. This is because low-priced shares are apt to fluctuate over a wider range *percentagewise* than higher priced stocks. Hence if a bond is both well secured and convertible into many shares at a low price, it will have anexcellent chance for very large profit without being subject to the offsetting risk of greater loss through a speculative dip in the price of the stock.

例如，作为*特权形式*，Ohio Copper Company 7s，到期日为1931年，可转换为1,000股价格为1美元的普通股，其可能性比Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Convertible $4\frac{1}{2}$s，到期日为1948年，可转换为6股价格为$166\frac{2}{3}$的普通股，更有优势，尽管每种情况下投机性收益均为每张债券1,000美元。结果，Ohio Copper股票从1928年的每股不到1美元上升到1929年的$4\frac{7}{8}$，使债券价值接近面值的500%。要使可转换$4\frac{1}{2}$s获得相同利润，Atchison的价格需要从166美元升至800美元，但1929年达到的最高价格低于300美元。

<!--en-->
For example, as a matter of *form* of privilege, the Ohio Copper Company 7s, due 1931, convertible into 1,000 shares of stock selling at $1, had better possibilities than the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Convertible $4\frac{1}{2}$s, due 1948, convertible into 6 shares of common, selling at $166\frac{2}{3}$, although in each case the amount of speculative interest equalled $1,000 per bond. As it turned out, Ohio Copper stock advanced from less than $1 a share in 1928 to $4\frac{7}{8}$ in 1929, making the bond worth close to 500% of par. It would have required a rise in the price of Atchison from 166 to 800 to yield the same profit on the convertible $4\frac{1}{2}$s, but the highest price reached in 1929 was under 300.

对于*参与式发行*，利润分享收益的幅度通常根据因特权可能获得的额外收入金额来考虑。有限的额外支付（例如Bayuk Cigars, Inc., 7%优先股，可能获得不超过1%的额外收益）当然不如无限参与更有吸引力（例如White Rock Mineral Springs Company 5%第二优先股，在1930年获得了总计$26\frac{1}{4}\%$）。

<!--en-->
In the case of *participating issues*, the extent of the profit-sharing interest would ordinarily be considered in terms of the amount of extra income that may conceivably be obtained as a result of the privilege. A limited extra payment (e.g., Bayuk Cigars, Inc., 7% Preferred, which may receive not more than 1% additional) is of course less attractive than an unlimited participation (e.g., White Rock Mineral Springs Company 5% Second Preferred, which received a total of $26\frac{1}{4}\%$ in 1930).

*2和3.特权的接近性和持续时间。*评估特权的第二个和第三个因素的影响非常明显。具有长期期的特权比短期到期的特权更理想。股票当前价格越接近转换或认购开始盈利的水平，特权就越有吸引力。对于参与式特权，普通股当前的股息或收益也应接近高级发行开始额外分配的水平。

<!--en-->
*2 and 3. Closeness and Duration of the Privilege.* The implications of the second and third factors in valuing a privilege are readily apparent. A privilege having a long period to run is in that respect more desirable than one expiring in a short time. The nearer the current price of the stock to the level at which conversion or subscription becomes profitable the more attractive does the privilege become. In the case of a participation feature, it is similarly desirable that the current dividends or earnings on the common stock should be close to the figure at which the extra distribution on the senior issue commences.

“转换价格”指的是与可转换发行价格相当于100美元相对应的普通股价格。如果优先股可以转换为$1\frac{2}{3}$股普通股，则普通股的转换价格为60。术语“转换平价”或“转换水平”可用于表示与普通股的对应价格，或*反之亦然*。可以通过将可转换发行价格乘以普通股的转换价格得到。如果上述优先股售价为90，则普通股的转换平价为$60 \times 90\% = 54$。这意味着，对于以90出售的优先股买家，普通股价格超过54将产生实际利润。相反，如果普通股售价为66，可以说优先股的转换平价为110。

<!--en-->
By “conversion price” is meant the price of the common stock equivalent to a price of 100 for the convertible issue. If a preferred stock is convertible into $1\frac{2}{3}$ as many shares ofcommon, the conversion price of the common is therefore 60. The term “conversion parity,” or “conversion level,” may be used to designate that price of the common which is equivalent to a given quotation for the convertible issue, or *vice versa*. It can be found by multiplying the price of the convertible issue by the conversion price of the common. If the preferred stock just mentioned is selling at 90, the conversion parity of the common becomes $60 \times 90\% = 54$. This means that to a buyer of the preferred at 90 an advance in the common above 54 will create a realizable profit. Conversely, if the common sold at 66, one might say that the conversion parity of the preferred is 110.

特权的“接近度”可以用市场价格与普通股转换平价的比率来数学表达。在上面的例子中，如果普通股售价为54，优先股售价为110（相当于普通股的66），则“接近指数”为$54 \div 66$，即0.82。

<!--en-->
The “closeness” of the privilege may be stated arithmetically as the ratio between the market price and the conversion parity of the common stock. In the foregoing example, if the common is selling at 54 and the preferred at 110 (equivalent to 66 for the common), the “index of closeness” becomes $54 \div 66$, or 0.82.

## 三种特权类型的比较优势

<!--en-->
*COMPARATIVE MERITS OF THE THREE TYPES OF PRIVILEGES*

从理论角度而言，那种在时间上和数量上均无限制的参与型权益，是最理想的利润分享特权类型。这种安排能让投资者在不改变其作为优先股持有者原有地位的前提下，获得参与利润分配的具体好处（即增加收入），而这些好处可在数年时间内逐步兑现。相比之下，转换特权只有通过实际转换为股票并因此放弃优先股地位，才能带来更高收入。因此，它的真正优势仅在于能够在合适时机通过出售可转换证券来获利。同样，认购特权带来的好处也通常只能通过出售认股权证（或通过认购股票后迅速出售）才能实现。如果购买普通股是为了获取永久性收入，那么这种操作所承担的风险与最初购买优先股时的风险完全不同。

<!--en-->
From the theoretical standpoint, a participating feature—unlimited in time and possible amount—is the most desirable type of profit-sharing privilege. This arrangement enables the investor to derive the specific benefit of participation in profits (*viz.*, increased income) without modifying his original position as a senior-security holder. These benefits may be received over a long period of years. By contrast, a conversion privilege can result in higher income only through actual exchange into the stock and consequent surrender of the senior position. Its real advantage consists, therefore, only of the opportunity to make a profit through the sale of the convertible issue at the right time. Similarly the benefits from a subscription privilege may conservatively be realized only through sale of the warrants (or by the subscription to and prompt sale of the stock). If the common stock is purchased and held for permanent income, the operation involves therisking of additional money on a basis entirely different from the original purchase of the senior issue.

### 无限参与特权的示例

<!--en-->
*Example of Advantage of Unlimited Participation*

**特权。**西屋电气制造公司优先股为具有深厚参与机制的证券所带来的理论优势提供了极佳的实践案例。该证券每年享有3.50美元的累积前期股息（按50美元面值计算为7%），此外，对于普通股派发的超过3.50美元的任何股息，它还能与普通股按同等比例分享。早在1917年，西屋优先股的价格就为52½美元，这本身已是一笔颇具吸引力的直接投资，同时还因其参与机制而具备更多潜在收益。在接下来的15年直至1932年间，除了基础的7%股息外，每股还额外获得了约7美元的股息。在此期间也曾出现过以高额利润套现的机会（1929年的股价高达284点），这相当于可转换证券或认股权证所具有的增值潜力。如果未出售该股票，那么在随后的市场下跌中自然会损失这些利润。但投资者的原有地位并未受损，因为在1932年的最低点时，该证券仍能支付7%的股息，股价也为52½美元——尽管普通股的股息早已结束，股价已跌至15⅝美元。

<!--en-->
**Privilege.** An excellent practical example of the theoretical advantages attaching to a well-entrenched participating security is afforded by Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company Preferred. This issue is entitled to cumulative prior dividends of $3.50 per annum (7% on $50 par) and in addition participates equally per share with the common in any dividends paid on the latter in excess of $3.50. As far back as 1917 Westinghouse Preferred could have been bought at $52½, representing an attractive straight investment with additional possibilities through its participating feature. In the ensuing 15 years to 1932 a total of about $7 per share was disbursed in extra dividends above the basic 7%. In the meantime an opportunity arose to sell out at a large profit (the high price being 284 in 1929), which corresponded to the enhancement possibilities of a convertible or subscription-warrant issue. If the stock was not sold, the profit was naturally lost in the ensuing market decline. But the investor's original position remained unimpaired, for at the low point of 1932 the issue was still paying the 7% dividend and selling at $52½—although the common had passed its dividend and had fallen to $15⅝.

在这个例子中，投资者能够在经济状况良好的年份享受普通股的剩余利润，同时保持其优先股地位；因此当经济状况恶化时，他损失的仅是暂时的“利润”。如果该证券是可转换型而非参与型，投资者则只能通过转换才能获得更高的股息，之后还会发现其持有的普通股不再有股息分配，且股价远低于其初始投资成本。

<!--en-->
In this instance the investor was able to participate in the surplus profits of the common stock in good years while maintaining his preferred position, so that, when the bad years came, he lost only his temporary *profit*. Had the issue been convertible instead of participating, the investor could have received the higher dividends only through converting and would later have found the dividend omitted on his common shares and their value fallen far below his original investment.

### 从市场角度看，参与型证券处于劣势。

<!--en-->
*Participating Issues at Disadvantage, Marketwise.*

尽管从长期持有的角度来看，参与型证券在理论上是最理想的，但在市场大幅上涨时期，它们的表现可能不如可转换证券或认股权证那样理想。在这样的时期，具有参与机制的优先股往往其价格会低于其应有的合理水平。例如，西屋优先股在1929年的价格通常比普通股低5到10个点，尽管其每股的内在价值不可能低于普通股。²这种现象的原因如下：普通股的价格主要由那些追求快速利润的投机者决定，而为了实现这一目标，他们需要一个活跃的市场。由于优先股被大量持有，市场流动性相对较低。因此，投机者愿意为流动性更好的普通股支付更高的价格，因为这类股票更容易买卖，而且其他投机者也可能会为其支付更高价格。

<!--en-->
Although from the standpoint of long-pull-investment holding, participating issues are theoretically the most desirable, they may behave somewhat less satisfactorily in a major market upswing than do convertible or subscription-warrant issues. During such a period a participating senior security mayregularly sell below its proper comparative price. In the case of Westinghouse Preferred, for example, its price during 1929 was usually from 5 to 10 points lower than that of the common, although its intrinsic value per share could not be less than that of the junior stock.²
The reason for this phenomenon is as follows: The price of the common stock is made largely by speculators interested chiefly in quick profits, to secure which they need an active market. The preferred stock, being closely held, is relatively inactive. Consequently the speculators are willing to pay several points more for the inferior common issue simply because it can be bought and sold more readily and because other speculators are likely to be willing to pay more for it also.

在同一家公司的、流动性较好的无投票权普通股与流动性较差的有投票权普通股之间，也会出现同样的异常现象。美国烟草*B*股和利格特迈尔斯烟草*B*股（均为无投票权股）多年来其售价一直高于有投票权股。伯利恒钢铁、泛美石油等公司的两种普通股也曾出现过类似情况。在证券市场普遍适用的一个矛盾原则是：*在缺乏特殊需求的情况下*，相对稀缺性往往会导致价格更低而非更高。

<!--en-->
The same anomaly arises in the case of closely held common stocks with voting power, compared with the more active nonvoting issue of the same company. American Tobacco *B* and Liggett and Myers Tobacco *B* (both nonvoting) have for years sold higher than the voting stock. A similar situation formerly existed in the two common issues of Bethlehem Steel, Pan American Petroleum and others.³ The paradoxical principle holds true for the securities market generally that *in the absence of a special demand* relative scarcity is likely to make for a lower rather than a higher price.

在西屋电气和美国烟草这样的案例中，合理的公司政策应是让那些持有本质上价值更高的证券的人享有将其兑换为流动性更强但本质上价值较低的证券的特权。怀特洛克公司实际上就采取了这一措施。尽管参与转换的优先股持有人可能会因接受此类提议而犯错，但他们无法反对公司向他们提出该提议，而且普通股股东通过接受该提议只会受益而不会受损。

<!--en-->
In cases such as Westinghouse and American Tobacco the proper corporate policy would be to extend to the holder of the intrinsically more valuable issue the privilege of exchanging it for the more active but intrinsically inferior issue. The White Rock company actually took this step. Although the holders of the participating preferred might make a mistake in accepting such an offer, they cannot object to its being made to them, and the common stockholders may gain but cannot lose through its acceptance.

**可转换证券与附认股权证证券的相对价格表现。** 从市场环境良好的价格表现角度来看，拥有可分离股票购买认股权证的高级证券持有者能获得最佳收益。

<!--en-->
**Relative Price Behavior of Convertible and Warrant-Bearing Issues.** From the standpoint of price behavior under favorable market conditions the best results are obtained byholders of senior securities with detachable stock-purchase warrants.

为阐明这一点，我们将比较1929年四种优先股与相应的普通股之间的某些价格关系。这些股票如下：

<!--en-->
To illustrate this point we shall compare certain price relationships shown in 1929 between four privileged issues and the corresponding common stocks. The issues are as follows:

1. 莫霍克哈德逊电力公司7%第二优先股，附有权利可按每股优先股50美元的价格购买2股普通股。
2. White Sewing Machine Corporation 6%债券，到期日为1936年，每100美元债券附有权利可购买$2\frac{1}{2}$股普通股。
3. 中央州电力公司6%优先股，可按每股118美元的价格转换为普通股。
4. 独立石油天然气公司债券6s，到期日为1939年，可按每股32美元的价格转换为普通股。下表清楚地表明，在投机市场中，带有购买权条款的债券往往以远高于普通股价格的溢价出售，且这种溢价远高于类似情况的可转换债券。

<!--en-->
1. Mohawk Hudson Power Corporation 7% Second Preferred, carrying warrants to buy 2 shares of common at 50 for each share of preferred.
2. White Sewing Machine Corporation 6% Debentures, due 1936, carrying warrants to buy $2\frac{1}{2}$ shares of common stock for each $100 bond.
3. Central States Electric Corporation 6% Preferred, convertible into common stock at $118 per share.
4. Independent Oil and Gas Company Debentures 6s, due 1939, convertible into common stock at $32 per share.
The following table shows in striking fashion that in speculative markets issues with purchase warrants have a tendency to sell at large premiums in relation to the common-stock price and that these premiums are much greater than in the case of similarly situated convertible issues.

* 包含107份优先股、前认股权证，以及56份认股权证。† 包含98<sup>1</sup>/<sub>2</sub>份债券、前认股权证，以及25份认股权证。**投机成分可分离的优势。**认购认股权证发行的这种优势主要源于其投机成分（即认购认股权证本身）可以与投资成分（即债券或优先股前认股权证）完全分离。投机者总是寻求在少量现金投入下获得巨大利润的机会。这是股票期权认股权证的独特特征，我们将在后续对这些工具的讨论中详细说明。因此，在市场上涨时，投机者会争相购买这些特权发行的认股权证，从而以较高价格将其单独出售，即使它们可能没有直接行使价值。这些投机者更倾向于购买期权认股权证，而非相应的*可转换债券*，因为后者每单位普通股需要更大的现金投入。⁴ 因此，债券与期权认股权证各自的市价之和（共同构成“带认股权证的债券”价格）可能显著高于类似的可转换债券的单重报价。

<!--en-->
* Consisting of 107 for the preferred stock, ex-warrants, plus 56 for the warrants.
† Consisting of 98<sup>1</sup>/<sub>2</sub> for the bonds, ex-warrants, plus 25 for the warrants.
**Advantage of Separability of Speculative Component.** This advantage of subscription-warrant issues is due largely to the fact that their speculative component (i.e., the subscription warrant itself) can be entirely separated from their investment component (i.e., the bond or preferred stock ex-warrants). Speculators are always looking for a chance to make large profits on a small cash commitment. This is a distinguishing characteristic of stock option warrants, as will be shown in detail in our later discussion of these instruments. In an advancing market, therefore, speculators bid for the warrants attached to these privileged issues, and hence they sell separately at a substantial price even though they may have no immediate exercisable value. These speculators greatly prefer buying the option warrants to buying a corresponding *convertible bond*, because the latter requires a much larger cash investment per share of common stock involved.⁴ It follows, therefore, that the separate market values of the bond plus the option warrant (which combine to make the price of the bond “with warrants”) may considerably exceed the single quotation for a closely similar convertible issue.

## **持有认股权证证券的第二个优势。**

<!--en-->
**Second Advantage of Warrant-Bearing Issues.**

相较于可赎回条款，附认股权证的发行方式还有第二个优势。公司保留的在到期前赎回已发行证券的权利通常会被视为对持有人的不利因素；因为这种权利大概只会在对发行方有利时才会被行使，而这意味着该证券的售价通常会高于赎回价格。⁵除非赎回溢价极高，否则可赎回条款可能会完全破坏参与型权益的价值。因为一旦公司发展得足够好、能够获得额外分红，就存在被赎回的风险。⁶在某些情况下，具有可赎回性质的同时也是参与型的证券还会被设定为可转换型，以便让持有人有机会从普通股在赎回前可能出现的股价大幅上涨中获利。（例如：National Distillers Products Corporation发行的2.50美元累积参与型可转换优先股；⁷Kelsey-Hayes Wheel Company发行的1.50美元参与型可转换A类股票。）参与型*债券*通常在参与盈余收益方面的权利较为有限，且往往具备可赎回性。（参见White Sewing Machine Corporation发行的1940年到期的6先令参与型债券；United Steel Works Corporation发行的1947年到期的A系列6.5先令参与型债券；这两者均不可转换。）有时，为了防止通过赎回导致持有人的参与权益丧失，人们会将赎回价格设定得非常高。San Francisco Toll-Bridge Company发行的1942年到期的7先令参与型债券显然就尝试过这种方法，该债券在1933年11月1日之前可按120的价格赎回，之后则可按更低价格赎回。Celluloid Corporation发行的第二优先级参与型债券可按150的价格赎回，而Celanese Corporation发行的第一优先级参与型债券则不可赎回。

<!--en-->
Subscription-warrant issues have a second point of superiority,in respect to callable provisions. A right reserved by the corporation to redeem an issue prior to maturity must in general be considered as a disadvantage to the holder; for presumably it will be exercised only when it is to the benefit of the issuer to do so, which means usually that the security would otherwise sell for more than the call price.⁵ A callable provision, unless at a very high premium, might entirely vitiate the value of a participating privilege. For with such a provision there would be danger of redemption as soon as the company grew prosperous enough to place the issue in line for extra distributions.⁶ In some cases participating issues that are callable are made convertible as well, in order to give them a chance to benefit from any large advance in the market price of the common that may have taken place up to the time of call. (See for examples: National Distillers Products Corporation $2.50 Cumulative Participating Convertible Preferred;⁷ Kelsey-Hayes Wheel Company $1.50 Participating Convertible Class A stock.) Participating *bonds* are generally limited in their right to participate in surplus earnings and are commonly callable. (See White Sewing Machine Corporation Participating Debenture 6s, due 1940; United Steel Works Corporation Participating 6½s, Series A, due 1947; neither of which is convertible.) Sometimes participating issues are protected against loss of the privilege through redemption by setting the call price at a very high figure. Something of this sort was apparently attempted in the case of San Francisco Toll-Bridge Company Participating 7s, due 1942, which were callable at 120 through November 1, 1933, and at lower prices thereafter. Celluloid Corporation Participating Second Preferred is callable at 150, whereas Celanese Corporation Participating First Preferred is non callable.

另一种防止通过赎回破坏参与权益的方法是，让该证券以直接取决于其参与权益价值的金额设定为可赎回。例如，Siemens and Halske公司在1930年发行的参与型债券，在1942年4月1日后可赎回，赎回价格*为提前通知赎回前六个月的平均市场价格，但不得低于最初的发行价格*（该价格是面值的230%以上）。Kreuger and Toll公司发行的5%参与型债券也有类似规定。

<!--en-->
Another device to prevent vitiating the participating privilege through redemption is to make the issue callable at a price that may be directly dependent upon the value of the participating privilege. For example, Siemens and Halske Participating Debentures, due in 1930, are callable after April 1, 1942, *at the average market price for the issue during the six months preceding notice of redemption but at not less than the original issue price* (which was over 230% of the parvalue). The Kreuger and Toll 5% Participating Debentures had similar provisions.

即便对于*可转换*型证券而言，可赎回特性在技术层面上也是一项严重缺陷，因为它可能会缩短该权益的有效期限。可以想象，当参与型权益即将产生实际价值时，可转换债券就可能会被赎回。⁸

<!--en-->
Even in the case of a *convertible* issue a callable feature is technically a serious drawback because it may operate to reduce the duration of the privilege. Conceivably a convertible bond may be called just when the privilege is about to acquire real value.⁸

但对于带有股票认购权证的证券而言，尽管优先级更高的证券本身可能在到期前被赎回，但认购权益几乎总能完整存续至期满。如果权证是可分离的，它就会独立存在直至自身到期日。通常，这类认购权益会被设定为“不可分离”的，即只能通过出示优先级更高的证券才能行使。但即便如此，如果该证券在购买选择期结束前被赎回，惯例是会给持有人一份新的独立权证，其有效期为原定期限的剩余时间。

<!--en-->
But in the case of issues with stock-purchase warrants, the subscription privilege almost invariably runs its full time even though the senior issue itself may be called prior to maturity. If the warrant is detachable, it simply continues its separate existence until its own expiration date. Frequently, the subscription privilege is made “nondetachable”; *i.e.*, it can be exercised only by presentation of the senior security. But even in these instances, if the issue should be redeemed prior to the expiration of the purchase-option period, it is customary to give the holder a separate warrant running for the balance of the time originally provided.

*示例：*在1934年1月1日之前，United Aircraft and Transport Corporation拥有150,000股6%累积优先股。这些股票附带不可分离的权证，每持有2股优先股即可按30美元的价格认购1股普通股。该认购权益的有效期为1938年11月1日，并且有相应条款保障：如果优先股在1938年11月1日之前被赎回，会为每股优先股发行一份体现相同权益的独立权证。1933年1月1日，部分优先股被赎回，相关权证也随之发放给了持有者。（一年后，剩余的优先股也被赎回，并又发行了额外的权证。）

<!--en-->
*Example:* Prior to January 1, 1934, United Aircraft and Transport Corporation had outstanding 150,000 shares of 6% Cumulative Preferred stock. These shares carried nondetachable warrants for one share of common stock at $30 a share for each two shares of preferred stock held. The subscription privilege was to run to November 1, 1938, and was protected by a provision for the issuance of a detached warrant evidencing the same privilege per share in case the preferred stock was redeemed prior to November 1, 1938. Some of the preferred stock was called for redemption on January 1, 1933, and detached warrants were accordingly issued to the holders thereof. (A year later the remainder of the issue was called and additional warrants issued.)

**附权证证券的第三个优势。**附认股权证的发行方式相比其他具有特殊权益的证券还有第三个优势，从实际意义上看，这可能是所有优势中最重要的一点。让我们来看看，如果公司发展良好、普通股能获得高股息且股价居高不下，各类证券的持有者分别有哪些可行的选择。

<!--en-->
**Third Advantage of Warrant-Bearing Issues.** Subscription-warrant issues have still a third advantage over other privileged securities, and this is in a practical sense probably the most important of all. Let us consider what courses of conduct are open to holders of each type in the favorable event that the company prospers, that a high dividend is paid on the common, and that the common sells at a high price.

1. 参与型证券的持有者：a. 可以卖出获利；b. 可以持有并获取参与型股息收入。
2. 可转换型证券的持有者：a. 可以卖出获利；b. 可以持有，但无法从普通股的高股息中获益；c. 可以转换以获得更高收入，但需放弃其优先地位。
3. 持有股票购买权证股票： a. 可以盈利出售。b. 可以持有，但无法从高普通股息中获益。c. 可以认购普通股以获得高股息。他可以投入新资金，也可以出售或运用其权证证券来提供资金支付普通股费用。无论哪种情况，他都承担普通股股东的风险，以获取高股息收入。d. 可以以现金利润出售其权证，同时保留原始证券（权证）。（权证可以直接出售，或者他可以认购股票并立即以当前标明的利润价格出售。）上述第四种选择仅适用于认购权证发行，不可用于可转换或参与型证券。它允许持有人从发行的投机部分获得现金利润，同时保持原有的*投资*状态。由于特权优先股的典型买家主要希望进行稳健投资——其次希望利用特权获利——这种第四种可选行为方式可能非常方便。他无需出售全部承诺份额，因为如果他拥有可转换证券，则必须寻找新的资金渠道。典型的投资者不愿出售一种资产而购买另一种资产，这是高价可转换证券持有者倾向于转换而非处置的原因之一。对于参与型发行，所有者也只能通过出售来保护其*主要*利润，从而造成再投资问题。*示例：* 认购权证发行在这一点上的理论和实际优势，可以通过商业投资信托公司6 1/2%优先股案例来说明。该股票于1925年发行，附带权证，初始价格为每股80美元。1929年，权证价格高达每股优先股69.50美元。因此，该股票的持有者能够以高价出售其投机部分，同时保持原有的优先股承诺，在整个经济萧条期间仍保持投资状态，直到1933年4月1日最终以110的价格要求赎回。在要求赎回时，普通股的价格约为每旧股50美元。如果优先股是可转换的，而不是带有权证，许多持有者无疑会选择转换并保留普通股。他们不会获得巨大利润，反而面临重大损失。**总结。**概括本节内容，可以说，对于*长期持有*而言，稳健的参与型发行代表了最佳的利润分享特权。从有利市场条件下最大*价格提升*的角度来看，可分离股票购买权优先股很可能会取得最佳效果。此外，认购权证发行作为一个类别具有明确优势：特权通常不会因提前赎回证券而被削减，并且允许在保持原有投资状态的同时实现投机利润。[^1410]：¹ 由于特权发行的重要性日益增加，且标准描述性教科书中缺乏深入讨论，本主题的描述可能显得过长。2 1929年和1930年，白岩矿物泉参与优先股和普通股存在更大的价格差异。由于这种市场状况，几乎所有参与优先股持有者都接受了转换为普通股的建议，尽管这意味着没有收益增长，也失去了优先地位。 3 R. J. Reynolds Tobacco Company普通股与B类股的市场价格持续存在巨大差距，原因是持有普通股的公司高管和员工享有B类股股东没有的某些利润分享福利。纽约证券交易所将不再上市无投票权的普通股，根据1938年破产法第十章进行的重组也不允许发行此类股票。

4 请注意，独立石油和天然气债券代表每股普通股的33.60美元承诺；而白缝纫机认股权证仅代表每股普通股的10美元承诺。但前者意味着对固定权益或股票份额的*所有权*，而后者仅意味着以高于市场价格购买股票*权利*。

5 可赎回特性可能——而且最近确实如此——即使在“纯”不可转换债券中也是非常重要的不利因素。在少数情况下，可赎回特性对持有人有利，因为它有助于新的融资，即以高于之前市场价格赎回旧发行股票。但如果没有赎回权，通过“买入”证券的方式也可以获得相同结果。美国钢铁公司1951年到期的5s债券就是这种情况，这些债券不可赎回，但以110的价格被买入。

6 Dewing引用了联合太平洋铁路公司——俄勒冈短线参与4s债券的案例，该债券于1903年发行，以北方证券公司的股票作为担保。债券持有人有权分享所存放担保物中宣布的超过4%的股息。当参与分配似乎即将发生时，债券被赎回了。参见Arthur S. Dewing，《公司证券研究》，第328页，纽约，1934年。

7 与1933年普通股价格从1美元涨到2美元同时，所有国家蒸馏商优先股都在那一年转换为普通股。几乎所有转换都是由于1933年6月30日之后转换率发生变化而加速的。少量余额是由于在40美元价格发行并于8月发放股息后进行了赎回而转换的。

8 在阿奇森、托皮卡和圣塔菲铁路可转换4½美元债券案例中，1948年到期，这种风险被避免：允许仅在1938年转换特权到期后才进行赎回。（另一方面，附属基金担保可转换债券可在任何时间提前30天通知后按面值赎回，实际上使公司可以消除从转换特权中获利的机会。）最近使用的另一种保护机制是，在赎回时向可转换债券持有人提供股票购买认股权证，使持有人有权购买如果未赎回高级债券本应获得的普通股数量。参见德克萨斯自由港公司1933年1月发行的6%累积可转换优先股；联合饼干7%优先股可转换为3美元普通股，可按110美元赎回；但如果在1935年12月31日之前被赎回，持有人可以选择以100美元现金加上认股权证，在1月1日前以40美元价格购买4美元普通股。第24章

<!--en-->
1. Holder of a participating issue:
a. May sell at a profit.
b. May hold and receive participating income.
2. Holder of a convertible issue:
a. May sell at a profit.
b. May hold but will receive no benefit from high common dividend.
c. May convert to secure larger income but sacrifices his senior position.
3. Holder of an issue with stock-purchase warrants:
a. May sell at a profit.
b. May hold but will receive no benefit from high common dividend.
c. May subscribe to common to receive high dividend. He may invest new capital, or he may sell or apply his security ex-warrants to provide funds to pay for the common. In either case he undertakes the risks of a common stockholder in order to receive the high dividend income.
d. May dispose of his warrants at a cash profit and retain his original security, ex-warrants. (The warrant may be sold directly, or he may subscribe to the stock and immediately sell it at the current indicated profit.)
The fourth option listed above is peculiar to a subscription-warrant issue and has no counterpart in convertible or participating securities. It permits the holder to cash his profit from the speculative component of the issue and still maintain his original *investment* position. Since the typical buyer of a privileged senior issue should be interested primarily in making a sound investment—with a secondary opportunity to profit from the privilege—this fourth optional course of conduct may prove a great convenience. He is not under the necessity of selling the entire commitment, as he would be if he owned a convertible, which would then require him to find some new medium for the funds involved. Thereluctance to sell one good thing and buy another, which characterizes the typical investor, is one of the reasons that holders of high-priced convertibles are prone to convert them rather than to dispose of them. In the case of participating issues also, the owner can protect his *principal* profit only by selling out and thus creating a reinvestment problem.
*Example:* The theoretical and practical advantage of subscription-warrant issues in this respect may be illustrated in the case of Commercial Investment Trust Corporation 6 1/2% Preferred. This was issued in 1925 and carried warrants to buy common stock at an initial price of $80 per share. In 1929 the warrants sold as high as $69.50 per share of preferred. The holder of this issue was therefore enabled to sell out its speculative component at a high price and to retain his original preferred-stock commitment, which maintained an investment status throughout the depression until it was finally called for redemption at 110 on April 1, 1933. At the time of the redemption call the common stock was selling at the equivalent of about $50 per old share. If the preferred stock had been convertible, instead of carrying warrants, many of the holders would undoubtedly have been led to convert and to retain the common shares. Instead of netting a large profit they would have been faced with a substantial loss.
**Summary.** To summarize this section, it may be said that, for *long-pull holding*, a sound participating issue represents the best form of profit-sharing privilege. From the standpoint of maximum *price advance* under favorable market conditions, a senior issue with detachable stock-purchase warrants is likely to show the best results. Furthermore, subscription-warrant issues as a class have definite advantages in that the privilege is ordinarily not subject to curtailment through early redemption of the security, and they permit the realization of a speculative profit while retaining the original investment position.

Because of this market situation, holders of nearly all the participating preferred shares accepted an offer to exchange into common stock, although this meant no gain in income and the loss of their senior position.
3 The persistently wide spread between the market prices for R. J. But the former meant *ownership* of either a fixed claim or a share of stock, whereas the latter meant only the *right to buy* a share of stock at a price above the market.

In a few cases a callable feature works out to the advantage of the holder, by facilitating new financing which involves the redemption of the old issue at a price above the previous market. But the same result could be obtained, if there were no right to call, by an offer to “buy in” the security. This was done in the case of United States Steel Corporation 5s, due 1951, which were not callable but were bought in at 110.
