CHAPTER 24

## 可转换证券的技术方面

<!--en-->
*Technical Aspects of*

可转换证券  关于特权证券的主题中的第三部分，涉及每种类型证券的技术方面，将分别讨论。我们先讨论可转换证券。

<!--en-->
Convertible Issues
THE THIRD DIVISION of the subject of privileged issues relates to technical aspects of each type, separately considered. We shall first discuss convertible issues.

转换权的有效条款在证券存续期间经常发生变化。这些变化有两种类型：(1) 转换价格下降，以保护持有人免受“稀释”影响；(2) 转换价格上升（通常按照“滑动比例”安排），以造福公司。

<!--en-->
The effective terms of a conversion privilege are frequently subject to change during the life of the issue. These changes are of two kinds: (1) a decrease in the conversion price, to protect the holder against “dilution”; and (2) an increase in the conversion price (in accordance usually with a “sliding-scale” arrangement) for the benefit of the company.

**稀释条款与反稀释条款。**如果股份数量增加，但资产和盈利能力没有相应增加，则称普通股的价值被稀释了。稀释可能通过分拆、股票红利、以低价提供认购权，以及按低每股估值发行股票用于财产或服务等方式产生。可转换证券的标准“反稀释”条款旨在按比例降低转换价格，以应对因稀释行为导致的每股价值下降。

<!--en-->
**Dilution, and Antidilution Clauses.** The value of a common stock is said to be diluted if there is an increase in the number of shares without a corresponding increase in assets and earning power. Dilution may arise through split-ups, stock dividends, offers of subscription rights at a low price, and issuance of stock for property or services at a low valuation per share. The standard “antidilution” provisions of a convertible issue endeavor to reduce the conversion price proportionately to any decrease in the per-share value arising through any act of dilution.

该方法可以用以下公式表示：设$C$为转换价格，$O$为当前已发行的股份数量，$N$为将发行的新股份数量，$P$为发行价格。那么

<!--en-->
The method may be expressed in a formula, as follows: Let $C$ be the conversion price, $O$ be the number of shares now outstanding, $N$ be the number of new shares to be issued, and $P$ be the price at which they are to be issued.
Then

$$
C' \text{ (the new conversion price)} = \frac{CO + NP}{O + N}
$$

该公式在1947年到期的Chesapeake Corporation可转换债券5s中应用的情况见附录注36。一个更简单的反稀释调整例子是之前提到的Central States Electric Corporation 6%可转换优先股（第23章）。1928年发行后，普通股连续获得了100%和200%的股票红利。因此，转换价格首先减半（从每股118美元降至59美元），然后再次降低三分之二（至每股19.66美元）。

<!--en-->
The application of this formula to Chesapeake Corporation Convertible Collateral 5s, due 1947, is given in Appendix Note 36. A simpler example of an antidilution adjustment is afforded by the Central States Electric Corporation 6% Convertible Preferred previously referred to (Chap. 23). After its issuance in 1928, the common stock received successive stock dividends of 100 and 200%. The conversion price was accordingly first cut in half (from $118 to $59 per share) and then again reduced by two-thirds (to $19.66 per share).

较为少见的条款仅将转换价格降低到可以发行新股份的最低水平。当然，这对可转换证券的持有人更有利。¹ *防止稀释的保护并不完整。*虽然现在几乎所有可转换证券都有反稀释条款，但也存在例外情况。² 预期购买者应确保所考虑的证券具有此类保护。

<!--en-->
A much less frequent provision merely reduces the conversion price to any lower figure at which new shares may be issued. This is, of course, more favorable to the holder of the convertible issue.¹
*Protection Against Dilution Not Complete.* Although practically all convertibles now have antidilution provisions, there have been exceptions.² As a matter of course, a prospective buyer should make certain that such protection exists for the issue he is considering.

需要注意的是，这些条款的作用只是保护特权证券的本金或面值免受稀释。如果可转换证券的售价远高于面值，*溢价*仍可能因额外发行股票或特别股息而贬值。一个简单的例子就能说明这一点。

<!--en-->
It should be borne in mind that the effect of these provisions is to preserve only the principal or par value of the privileged issue against dilution. If a convertible is selling considerably above par, the *premium* will still be subject to impairment through additional stock issues or a special dividend. A simple illustration will make this clear.

债券可以转换为股票，按面值转换。通常会有反稀释条款。债券和股票都以200的价格出售。

<!--en-->
A bond is convertible into stock, par for par. The usual antidilution clauses are present. Both bond and stock are selling at 200.

股东有权按面值（100美元）购买新股票，一对一购买。这些权利的价值为每股50美元，新股票（或旧股票“除权后”价值）为150美元。转换基础不会发生变化，因为新股票不是低于旧转换价格发行的。然而，提供这些权利的效果必然是强制立即转换债券，否则它们会损失25%的价值。由于股票“除权后”的价值仅为150美元，而非200美元，未转换债券的价值也会按比例下降。

<!--en-->
Stockholders are given the right to buy new stock, share for share, at par ($100). These rights will be worth $50 per share, and the new stock (or the old stock “ex-rights”) will be worth 150. No change will be made in the conversion basis, because the new stock is not issued below the old conversion price. However, the effect of offering these rights must be to compel immediate conversion of the bonds, since otherwise they would lose 25% of their value. As the stock will be worth only 150 “ex-rights,” instead of 200, the value of the unconverted bonds would drop proportionately.

上述讨论表明，当特权证券产生较大溢价或市场利润时，情况容易突然变化。尽管及时行动总能避免因这种变化造成的损失，但其效果总是会终止特权的有效期限。³ 当然，以低于当时转换价值的价格赎回特权证券，也会产生同样的结果。

<!--en-->
The foregoing discussion indicates that, when a large premium or market profit is created for a privileged issue, the situation is vulnerable to sudden change. Although prompt action will always prevent loss through such changes, their effect is always to terminate the effective life of the privilege.³ The same result will follow, of course, from the calling of a privileged issue for redemption at a price below its then conversion value.

当通过资本重组使股份数量*减少*时，通常会*相应提高*转换价格。这种资本重组措施包括提高面值、进行“反向拆分”（例如，发行1股无面值股票来替代5股旧股票），以及通过与另一家公司合并，用旧股票交换较少的新股票。⁴ **滑动比例机制以加速转换。**刚才讨论的条款旨在在后续资本化变化中公平维持最初的转换基础。另一方面，“滑动比例”安排显然会逐渐降低该特权的价值。其根本目的是加速转换，即缩短实际期限，从而降低期权的实际价值。显然，特权价值的任何下降必然使特权授予方受益，即公司的普通股股东。

<!--en-->
Where the number of shares is *reduced* through recapitalization, it is customary to *increase* the conversion price proportionately. Such recapitalization measures include increases in par value, “reverse split-ups” (e.g., issuance of 1 no-par share in place of, say, 5 old shares), and exchanges of the old stock for fewer new shares through consolidation with another company.⁴
**Sliding Scales Designed to Accelerate Conversion.** The provisions just discussed are intended to maintain equitably the original basis of conversion in the event of subsequent capitalization changes. On the other hand, a “sliding-scale” arrangement is intended definitely to reduce the value of the privilege as time goes on. The underlying purpose is to accelerate conversion, in other words, to curtail the effective duration and hence the real value of the option. Obviously, any diminution of the worth of the privilege to its recipients must correspondingly benefit the donors of the privilege, who are the company’s common shareholders.

更常见的滑动比例条款规定，在连续时间段内逐步提高转换价格。较新的变体规定，一旦一定比例的股票被交换，转换价格就会立即上升。

<!--en-->
The more usual terms of a sliding scale prescribe a series of increases in the conversion price in successive periods of time. A more recent variation makes the conversion price increase as soon as a certain portion of the issue has been exchanged.

*示例：*美国电话电报公司十年债券4½美元，于1939年到期，于1929年发行。在1930年，这些债券可转换为普通股，价格为每股180美元；在1931年和1932年，价格为每股190美元；在1933年至1937年之间，价格为每股200美元。后来根据标准反稀释条款，通过发行额外股票每股100美元，这些价格被降低了。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* American Telephone and Telegraph Company Ten-year Debenture 4½s, due 1939, issued in 1929, were made convertible into common at $180 per share during 1930, at $190 per share during 1931 and 1932, and at $200 per share during 1933 to 1937, inclusive. These prices were later reduced through the issuance of additional stock at $100, in accordance with the standard antidilution provision.

Anaconda铜矿公司债券7美元，于1938年到期，发行金额为50,000,000美元。前10,000,000美元可转换为普通股，价格为每股53美元；后10,000,000美元可转换为每股56美元；第三批为59美元；第四批为62美元；最后一批为65美元。Hiram Walker-Goderham and Worts 4 1/4美元债券，于1945年到期，可按以下方式转换：前2,000,000美元债券块价格为每股40美元；接下来2,000,000美元债券块价格为每股45美元；第三批为55美元；最后一批为每股60美元。

<!--en-->
Anaconda Copper Mining Company Debenture 7s, due 1938, were issued in the amount of $50,000,000. The first $10,000,000 presented were convertible into common stock at $53 per share; the second $10,000,000 were convertible at $56; the third at $59; the fourth at $62, and the final lot at $65. An $8,000,000 issue of Hiram Walker-Goderham and Worts 4 1/4s, due 1945, was convertible as follows: at $40 per share for the first $2,000,000 block of bonds; at $45 per share for the next block of $2,000,000; the third block at $55; and the final block at $60 per share.

*基于时间间隔的滑动比例。*第一种基于时间间隔的滑动比例是一种容易理解的方法，用于降低转换特权的慷慨程度。其效果可见于波多黎各-美国烟草公司6美元债券，于1942年到期。这些债券可在1929年1月2日之前转换为抵押的国会雪茄公司股票，价格为每股80美元；在接下来的三年中为85美元；之后为90美元。1928年，国会雪茄公司的最高价格为87 1/4美元，仅比转换价格略高一些。然而，由于转换基础即将上升，许多持有者选择在年底前转换，因为转换基础即将上升。这些转换非常不明智，因为1929年普通股价格降至43美元，而债券的最低价格为89美元。在这种情况下，转换基础的负面变化不仅意味着那些延迟转换到1928年之后的人的潜在利润减少，还带来了在错误时间促使转换导致严重损失的风险。

<!--en-->
*Sliding Scale Based on Time Intervals.* The former type of sliding scale, based on time intervals, is a readily understandable method of reducing the liberality of a conversion privilege. Its effect can be shown in the case of Porto Rican-American Tobacco Company 6s, due 1942. These were convertible into pledged Congress Cigar Company, Inc., stock at $80 per share prior to January 2, 1929, at $85 during the next three years and at $90 thereafter. During 1928 the highest price reached by Congress Cigar was 87 1/4, which was only a moderate premium above the conversion price. Nevertheless a number of holders were induced to convert before the year-end, because of the impending rise in the conversion basis. These conversions proved very ill-advised, since the price of the common fell to 43 in 1929, against a low of 89 for the bonds. In this instance, the adverse change in the conversion basis not only meant a smaller potential profit for those who delayed conversion until after 1928 but also involved a risk of serious loss through inducing conversion at the wrong time.

*基于行使特权程度의滑动比例。*然而，第二种基于转换数量的 방법并不那么简单。由于第一批债券转换后比后续批次有优势，它显然为早期转换提供了*竞争性*激励。这样，持有者在保留优先地位与因其他债券持有人先行动而失去更有利的转换基础之间的意愿之间产生了冲突。这种被提前替代的恐惧通常会导致大规模转换，一旦股票略微高于初始转换价格，即股票价值略高于原始成本时。因此，在普通股进展和连续批次债券被转换期间，优先发行的价格应在一个相对狭窄的范围内波动。

<!--en-->
*Sliding Scale Based on Extent Privilege Is Exercised.* The second method, however, based on the quantities converted, is not so simple in its implications. Since it gives the first lot of bonds converted an advantage over the next, it evidently provides a *competitive* stimulus to early conversion. By so doing it creates a conflict in the minds of the holder between the desire to retain his senior position and the fear of losing the more favorable basis of conversion through prior action by other bondholders. This fear of being forestalled will ordinarily result in large-scale conversions as soon as thestock advances moderately above the initial conversion price, i.e., as soon as the bond is worth slightly more than the original cost. Accordingly, the price of the senior issue should oscillate over a relatively narrow range while the common stock is advancing and while successive blocks of bonds are being converted.

*示例：* 上一页中描述的 Hiram Walker-Goderham 和 Worts Convertible 4 1/4s 的市场表现，很好地展现了通常会出现的事件发展顺序。这些于1936年按面值发行的债券，在1936年至1939年间的价格在100到111 1/4之间波动。同一时期，其对应的股票价格则在26 1/8到54之间变动。如果整个期间股票的初始转换价始终为40，那么当股票价格为54时，这些债券的售价至少应为135。但与此同时，随着股票价格上涨，陆续有债券被转换（部分是由于不断有人要求赎回部分债券所推动的），这就使得转换价不断上升，直至1937年达到55美元的水平。因此，这些债券的升值幅度并未与股票价格的上涨保持同步。⁵ 当达到这种渐进式转换机制中的最后一批债券时，“竞争”因素便消失了，此时该债券或优先股就变成了普通的可转换证券，可以随股票价格无限上涨。

<!--en-->
*Example:* The sequence of events normally to be expected is shown fairly well by the market action of Hiram Walker-Goderham and Worts Convertible 4 1/4s described on the previous page. The bonds, issued in 1936 at par, ranged in price between 100 and 111 1/4 during 1936–1939. In the same period the stock ranged between 26 1/8 and 54. If the initial conversion price of 40 for the stock had prevailed throughout the period, the bonds should have sold for at least 135 when the stock sold at 54. But meanwhile, as the price of the stock rose, successive blocks of the bonds were converted (partly under the impetus supplied by successive calls for redemption of parts of the issue), thus tipping off higher conversion prices until the $55 bracket was reached in 1937. In consequence the bonds did not appreciate commensurately with the rise in the price of the stock.⁵
When the last block under such a sliding scale is reached, the *competitive* element disappears, and the bond or preferred stock is then in the position of an ordinary convertible, free to advance indefinitely with the stock.

需要指出的是，具备此类渐进式转换条款的证券并不总是遵循这一理论上的行为模式。例如，Anaconda Copper Company的Convertible 7s在1928年，即在第一批债券被转换完毕之前，实际上就以30%的高溢价售出。这似乎是当时高度投机氛围下出现的异常现象之一。⁶ 从批判性分析的角度来看，这类可转换证券在普通股价格接近最后一个也是最高的转换价之前，其增值空间极为有限。⁷ 基于“批次”来设定渐进式转换特权的做法，属于那些容易误导证券持有者对其所持资产真实性质和价值认知的负面设计。为了抓住有限的机会而产生的竞争压力，会给行使转换权带来强制因素，这与这类特权所追求的、让持有者在合理时间内拥有选择自由的本质优势背道而驰。投资银行家似乎没有理由在证券发行中加入如此令人困惑且矛盾的设定。合理的做法应是完全摒弃此类设计，或者至少让明智的投资者避免购买这类证券。

<!--en-->
It should be pointed out that issues with such a sliding-scale provision do not always follow this theoretical behavior pattern. The Anaconda Copper Company Convertible 7s, for example, actually sold at a high premium (30%) in 1928, before the first block was exhausted. This seems to have been one of the anomalous incidents of the highly speculative atmosphere at the time.⁶ From the standpoint of critical analysis, a convertible of this type must be considered as having very limited possibilities of enhancement until the common stock approaches the last and highest conversion price.⁷
The sliding-scale privilege on a “block” basis belongs to the objectionable category of devices that tend to mislead the holder of securities as to the real nature and value of what he owns. The competitive pressure to take advantage of a limited opportunity introduces an element of compulsion into the exercise of the conversion right which is directly opposed to that freedom of choice for a reasonable time which is the essential merit of such a privilege. There seems no reason why investment bankers should inject so confusing and contradictory a feature into a security issue. Sound practice would dictate its complete abandonment or in any event the avoidance of such issues by intelligent investors.

**可转换为优先股的证券。** 过去有许多债券发行时都设有可转换为优先股的功能。通常，发行方会通过提高收益水平来使这一选项更具吸引力。（例如，Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Company的Adjustment 5s，到期日为1967年，可在1932年1月1日之前转换为面值为7美元的优先股；Central States Electric Corporation的Debenture 5s，到期日为1948年，可转换为面值为6美元的优先股；G. R. Kinney Company的Secured $7 1/2s，到期日为1936年，可转换为面值为8美元的优先股；American Electric Power Corporation的6s，到期日为1957年，可转换为面值为7美元的优先股。）

<!--en-->
**Issues Convertible into Preferred Stock.** Many bond issues were formerly made convertible into preferred stock. Ordinarily some increase in income was offered to make the provision appear attractive. (For examples, see Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad Company Adjustment 5s, due 1967, convertible prior to January 1, 1932 into $7 preferred stock; Central States Electric Corporation Debenture 5s, due 1948, convertible into $6 preferred stock; G. R. Kinney Company Secured $7 1/2s, due 1936, convertible into $8 preferred stock; American Electric Power Corporation 6s, due 1957, convertible into $7 preferred stock.)

也曾有过通过此类转换权获得可观利润的案例，但由于普通优先股的市场价值存在上限，这一特权的最大收益往往只能维持在较低水平。此外，由于近年来的发展使得优先股的整体吸引力远低于过去，因此将面率为4%的债券转换为面率为5%的优先股的权利，对那些缺乏警惕的人而言更可能构成风险，而非对精明投资者的激励。如果后者正在寻找可转换证券，他应该彻底调研市场，努力寻找那些可转换为普通股的、有足够担保的证券。在少数债券可转换为优先股，而该优先股又可进一步转换为普通股或享有与普通股相同权益的情况下，这种双重安排实际上可能等同于债券可直接转换为普通股。例如，International Hydro-Electric System的6s，到期日为1944年，可转换为A类股票，而这类股票实际上属于具有参与权的第二类优先股。

<!--en-->
There have been instances in which a fair-sized profit has been realized through such a conversion right, but the upper limitation on the market value of the ordinary preferred stock is likely to keep down the maximum benefits from such a privilege to a modest figure. Moreover, since developments in recent years have made preferred stocks in general appear far less desirable than formerly, the right to convert, say, from a 4% bond into a 5% preferred is likely to constitute more of a danger to the unwary than an inducement to the alert investor. If the latter is looking for convertibles, he should canvass the market thoroughly and endeavor to find a suitably secured issue convertible into common stock. In a few cases where bonds are convertible into preferred stock, the latter is in turn convertible into common or participates therewith, and this double arrangement may be equivalent to convertibility of the bond into common stock. For example, International Hydro-Electric System 6s, due 1944, are convertible into Class *A* stock, which is in reality a participating second preferred.

还有一些债券发行时可转换为优先股或普通股，或转换为一定比例的二者组合。⁸ 虽然个别此类证券的运作效果可能不错，但总体而言，无论是发行方还是证券购买方都应避免采用这类复杂的条款，因为它们容易引发混淆。

<!--en-->
There are also bond issues convertible into either preferred or common or into a combination of certain amounts of each.⁸ Although any individual issue of this sort may turn out well, in general it may be said that complicated provisions of this sort should be avoided (both by issuing companies and by security buyers) because they tend to create confusion.

**公司选择可转换债券。** 20世纪20年代，转换条款和其他权益的变更不断出现，使得未经训练的投资者难以区分具有吸引力、仅无害以及严重有害的条款。因此，他们很容易成为不当融资行为的受害者，过去这些行为因偏离标准而显得可疑。例如，联合燃气与电力公司发行的“可转换债务”，根据其条款，公司可以选择将其转换为优先股或A类股票。这种构造实际上只是以债券名义掩盖的优先股。如果购买者完全了解这一点并愿意投资优先股，大概没有理由抱怨。但显然，这种手段极易被隐藏和可能误导。⁹ **可转换为其他债券。** 有些债券可以转换为其他债券。常见的情况是短期债券，持有者有权将其兑换为同一公司的长期债券。通常，长期债券作为票据的担保物。（例如，Interborough Rapid Transit Company 7s，到期日为1932年，以该公司First and Refunding 5s中每1000美元票据对应1736美元的存款作为担保；它们也可以转换为所存的担保物，最终比例为1000美元5s债券对应900美元7%票据。）因此，持有者可以选择提前偿还，或对企业进行长期承诺。实际上，这仅仅意味着在公司盈利、利率下降或两者同时发生的情况下，有机会在到期时获得适度利润。

<!--en-->
**Bonds Convertible at the Option of the Company.** The unending flood of variations in the terms of conversion and other privileges that developed during the 1920s made it difficult for the untrained investor to distinguish between the attractive, the merely harmless, and the positively harmful. Hence he proved an easy victim to unsound financing practices which in former times might have stood out as questionable because of their departure from the standard. As an example of this sort we cite the various Associated Gas and Electric Company “Convertible Obligations” which were made convertible by their terms into preferred or Class *A* stock *at the option of the company*. Such a contraption was nothing more than a preferred stock masquerading as a bond. If the purchasers were entirely aware of this fact and were willing to invest in the preferred stock, they would presumably have no cause to complain. But it goes without saying that an artifice of this kind lends itself far too readily to concealment and possible misrepresentation.⁹
**Bonds Convertible into Other Bonds.** Some bonds are convertible into other bonds. The usual case is that of a short-term issue, the holder of which is given the right to exchange into a long-term bond of the same company. Frequently the long-term bond is deposited as collateral security for the note. (For example, Interborough Rapid Transit Company 7s, due 1932, were secured by deposit of $1,736 of the same company’s First and Refunding 5s, due 1966, for each $1,000 note, and they were also convertible into the deposited collateral, the final rate being $1,000 of 5s for $900 of 7% notes.) The holder thus has an option either to demand repayment at an early date or to make a long-termcommitment in the enterprise. In practice, this amounts merely to the chance of a moderate profit at or before maturity, in the event that the company prospers, or interest rates fall, or both.

与可转换为优先股的债券不同，当短期票据转换为长期债券时，票息率通常会**降低**。原因是，当整体或特定公司的利率被认为异常高时，通常会发行短期票据，因此公司不愿为长期债券承担如此高的利率。因此，人们期望当正常条件恢复时，长期债券可以以更低利率发行；因此，即使收入有所减少，也有权将票据转换为长期债券，这可能非常有价值。¹⁰ **原始市场价值超过面值的可转换债券。** 1928-1929年金融动荡中的一项特殊现象是，发行了原始市场价值远超过面值的可转换债券。例如，Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company 可转换4½s，到期日为1948年；American Telephone and Telegraph Company 可转换4½s，到期日为1939年。前者在1928年11月纽约Curb市场（按“发行时”基准）的初始交易价约为125，后者在1929年5月1日纽约证券交易所（按“发行时”基准）的初始交易价为142。显然，在这些价格水平下投资债券主要是一种对普通股票的承诺，因为如果股票下跌，立即面临本金价值大幅损失的风险。此外，收益回报完全低于我们的投资定义。虽然可能认为股东通过行使认购权以面值购买债券，属于正常投资，但他们承诺的本质是由所认购证券的初始市场价值决定的。因此，我们认为这种融资方式应受到谴责，因为以有吸引力的投资名义，它实际上创造了一种投机性证券形式。

<!--en-->
Unlike the case of a bond convertible into a preferred stock, there is usually a *reduction* in the coupon rate when a short-term note is converted into a long-term bond. The reason is that short-term notes are ordinarily issued when interest rates, either in general or for the specific company, are regarded as abnormally high, so that the company is unwilling to incur so steep a rate for a long-term bond. It is thus expected that, when normal conditions return, long-term bonds can be floated at a much lower rate; and hence the right to exchange the note for a long-term bond, even on a basis involving some reduction in income, may prove to be valuable.¹⁰
**Convertible Bonds with an Original Market Value in Excess of Par.** One of the extraordinary developments of the 1928–1929 financial pyrotechnics was the offering of convertible issues with an original market value greatly in excess of par. This is illustrated by Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company Convertible 4½s, due 1948, and by American Telephone and Telegraph Company Convertible 4½s, due 1939. Initial trading in the former on the New York Curb Market (on a “when issued” basis) in November 1928 was around 125, and initial trading in the latter on the New York Stock Exchange (on a “when issued” basis) on May 1, 1929, was at 142. Obviously investment in the bonds at these levels represented primarily a commitment in the common stock, since they were immediately subject to the danger of a substantial loss of principal value if the stock declined. Furthermore the income return was entirely too low to come under our definition of investment. Although it may be thought that the stockholders were acquiring a normal investment through the exercise of their subscription right to purchase the issues at par, the essential nature of their commitment was determined by the initial market value of the security to which they were subscribing. For this reason we think such financing should be condemned, because under theguise of an attractive investment it created a basically speculative form of security.

**某些可转换债券的技术特点。** 美国电话电报公司可转换债券有一个技术特点值得注意。这些债券按180美元可转换，但持有者不必提供180美元债券以获得股份，而是可以提供100美元债券和80美元现金。这种选择的效果是，当股票价格高于180时（即债券转换价值超过100时），债券的价值会更高。如下所示：

<!--en-->
**A Technical Feature of Some Convertible Issues.** A technical feature of the American Telephone and Telegraph convertible issue deserves mention. The bonds were made convertible at 180, but, instead of presenting $180 of bonds to obtain a share of stock, the holder might present $100 of bonds and $80 in cash. The effect of such an option is to make the bond more valuable whenever the stock sells above 180 (i.e., whenever the conversion value of the bond exceeds 100). This is illustrated as follows:

如果股票价格为360，180美元的直接转换基准会使债券价值变为200。但通过接受每股80美元现金的条款，债券价值变为360 - 80 = 280。

<!--en-->
If the stock sells at 360, a straight conversion basis of 180 would make the bond worth 200. But by the provision accepting $80 per share in cash, the value of the bond becomes $360 - $80 = $280.

这种安排可以描述为180美元转换特权与100美元股票购买权的结合。

<!--en-->
This arrangement may be characterized as a combination of a conversion privilege at 180 with a stock purchase right at 100.

**延迟转换特权。** 转换特权有时在债券发行后并不立即生效。

<!--en-->
**Delayed Conversion Privilege.** The privilege of converting is sometimes not operative immediately upon issuance of the obligation.

*示例：* 例如布鲁克林联合燃气公司5 1/2s可转换债券，详见附录注释38。尽管这些债券于1925年12月发行，但转换权直到1929年1月1日才生效。同样，纽约、纽黑文和哈特福德铁路公司6s可转换债券于1907年发行，但直到1923年1月15日才可转换；切萨皮克公司5s可转换债券于1927年发行，但直到1932年5月15日才变为可转换状态。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* This was true, for example, of Brooklyn Union Gas Company Convertible 5 1/2s, discussed in Appendix Note 38. Although they were issued in December 1925, the right to convert did not accrue until January 1, 1929. Similarly, New York, New Haven, and Hartford Railroad Company Convertible Debenture 6s, due in 1948, although issued in 1907, were not convertible until January 15, 1923; Chesapeake Corporation Convertible 5s, due 1947, were issued in 1927 but did not become convertible until May 15, 1932.

通常，转换特权的暂停时间并不像这些例子所显示的那样长，但无论如何，这种做法引入了额外的不确定性因素，使得该特权比其他情况下更不值钱。这一特性可能部分解释了附录注释38中提到的、曾经存在的扩散现象。

<!--en-->
More commonly the suspension of the conversion privilege does not last so long as these examples indicate, but in any event this practice introduces an additional factor of uncertainty and tends to render the privilege less valuable than it would be otherwise. This feature may account in part for the spread, indicated in Appendix Note 38, which existed during

CHAPTER 26

## 高级证券

<!--en-->
*Senior Securities of*

可疑的安全性  在1932年证券市场初期，至少80%的企业债券和优先股的安全性存在相当程度的疑问。¹甚至早在1929年股市崩盘之前，投机性高级证券的数量就非常庞大，未来几年数量可能还会更大。因此，金融界面临一个令人不快的事实：相当比例的美国证券属于所谓“不匹配”类别。低等级债券或优先股是一种相对不受欢迎的承诺形式。投资者不应购买它们，投机者通常更愿意关注普通股票。一种合理的观点是：如果决定进行投机，应选择完全投机的工具，不要受到市场价值上限和收益回报限制的影响，也不要陷入低价债券和优先股所伴随的投机与投资混淆的困境。

<!--en-->
Questionable Safety
AT THE LOW POINT of the 1932 securities market the safety of at least 80% of all corporate bonds and preferred stocks was open to some appreciable degree of doubt.¹ Even prior to the 1929 crash the number of speculative senior securities was very large, and it must inevitably be still larger for some years to come. The financial world is faced, therefore, with the unpleasant fact that a considerable proportion of American securities belong to what may be called a misfit category. A low-grade bond or preferred stock constitutes a relatively unpopular form of commitment. The investor must not buy them, and the speculator generally prefers to devote his attention to common stocks. There seems to be much logic to the view that if one decides to speculate he should choose a thoroughly speculative medium and not subject himself to the upper limitations of market value and income return, or to the possibility of confusion between speculation and investment, which attach to the lower priced bonds and preferred stocks.

**低价债券的利润限制并非真正缺陷。**然而，尽管对这些无特定特征的证券有诸多反对意见，但事实是它们数量巨大，无数持有人持有这些证券，因此在任何证券分析中都必须认真考虑它们。可以合理推断，这种证券的大量供应加上缺乏自然需求，会导致价格低于其内在价值。即使承认这类证券的*形式*存在固有吸引力不足的问题，其*价格*的吸引力也可能足以抵消这一点。此外，与普通股票相比，低价债券的实际*实现利润*可能只有很小实际意义，因为普通股票买家实际获得的利润通常并不比投机性高级证券更高。例如，如果我们考虑一只4%的债券以35的价格出售，其最大价格涨幅约为70点，即200%。以35的价格购买普通股票，无法获得超过此水平的利润，否则就会陷入“牛市心理”的陷阱。

<!--en-->
**Limitation of Profit on Low-Priced Bonds Not a Real Drawback.** But however impressive may be the objection to these nondescript securities, the fact remains that they exist in enormous quantities, that they are owned by innumerable security holders, and that hence they must be taken seriously into account in any survey of security analysis. It is reasonable to conclude that the large supply of such issues, coupled with the lack of a natural demand for them, will make for a level of prices below their intrinsic value. Even if an inherent unattractiveness in the *form* of such securities be admitted, this may be more than offset by the attractive *price* at whichthey may be purchased. Furthermore, the limitations of principal profit in the case of a low-priced bond, as compared with a common stock, may be of only minor practical importance, because the profit actually *realized* by the common-stock buyer is ordinarily no greater than that obtainable from a speculative senior security. If, for example, we are considering a 4% bond selling at 35, its maximum possible price appreciation is about 70 points, or 200%. The average common-stock purchase at 35 cannot be held for a greater profit than this without a dangerous surrender to “bull-market psychology.”

**关于投机性债券的两种观点。**从两个完全对立的角度可以看待投机性债券。一种是从投资标准和收益角度考虑，主要问题是低价和较高收益能否弥补安全性方面的牺牲；另一种是从普通股票承诺角度考虑，则会产生相反的问题：即“与普通股票相比，这种低价债券较小的风险是否足以弥补较低的利润可能性？”债券越接近满足投资要求——且售价越接近投资价格——那些希望从投资角度看待它的人就越可能接受它。相反的做法显然适用于违约或以极低价格出售的债券。这里面临的是因缺乏明确界限而产生的分类困难。有些债券总是能体现从完全无价值到绝对安全之间的任何状态。

<!--en-->
**Two Viewpoints with Respect to Speculative Bonds.** There are two directly opposite angles from which a speculative bond may be viewed. It may be considered in its relation to investment standards and yields, in which case the leading question is whether or not the low price and higher income return will compensate for the concession made in the safety factor. Or it may be thought of in terms of a common-stock commitment, in which event the contrary question arises; *viz.*, “Does the *smaller* risk of loss involved in this low-priced bond, as compared with a common stock, compensate for the smaller possibilities of profit?” The nearer a bond comes to meeting investment requirements—and the closer it sells to an investment price—the more likely are those interested to regard it from the investment viewpoint. The opposite approach is evidently suggested in the case of a bond in default or selling at an extremely low price. We are faced here with the familiar difficulty of classification arising from the absence of definite lines of demarcation. Some issues can always be found reflecting any conceivable status in the gamut between complete worthlessness and absolute safety.

*普通股方法更可取。* 然而，我们认为，处理投机性高级证券领域更合理、更有成效的方法应基于普通股思路。这将使对风险有更深入的理解，因此会更加强调对安全性的合理保障，或利润前景的显著优势，或两者兼而有之。至少对于明智的证券买家来说，这还会促使他们比从投资角度看待证券时进行更细致的分析。

<!--en-->
*Common-Stock Approach Preferable.* We believe, however, that the sounder and more fruitful approach to the field of speculative senior securities lies from the direction of common stocks. This will carry with it a more thorough appreciation of the risk involved and therefore a greater insistence upon either reasonable assurance of safety or especially attractive possibilities of profit or both. It induces also—among intelligent security buyers at least—a moreintensive examination of the corporate picture than would ordinarily be made in viewing a security from the investment angle.

这种方法显然不利于购买略低于标准标准的债券，这些债券以适度折扣的价格出售。它们以及高票面利率二流债券属于“商人投资”类别，我们在第7章中已考虑并决定不采用这种投资方式。有人可能会反对说，普遍采用这种态度会导致许多证券价格出现剧烈波动。假设4%的债券只要符合严格的投资标准，就应该按面值出售，那么一旦其价格略低于这些标准，价格就会急剧下降，比如降至70；反之，若价格略有改善，价格就会突然回到面值。显然，70到100之间的中间报价没有理由存在。

<!--en-->
Such an approach would be distinctly unfavorable to the purchase of slightly substandard bonds selling at moderate discounts from par. These, together with high-coupon bonds of second grade, belong in the category of “business men’s investments” which we considered and decided against in Chap. 7. It may be objected that a general adoption of this attitude would result in wide and sudden fluctuations in the price of many issues. Assuming that a 4% bond deserves to sell at par as long as it meets strict investment standards, then as soon as it falls slightly below these standards its price would suffer a precipitous decline, say, to 70; and, conversely, a slight improvement in its exhibit would warrant its jumping suddenly back to par. Apparently there would be no justification for intermediate quotations between 70 and 100.

然而，实际情况并不如此简单。投资者在是否认为某只证券具有充分保障方面可能存在意见分歧，尤其是因为标准既涉及质量与个性，也涉及算术与客观性。因此，70到100之间的范围可以逻辑地反映关于该证券安全性的不同程度认同。这意味着，如果投资者自己认为该债券可靠，那么以85的价格购买它是合理的，尽管他会意识到其他投资者对此有疑问，这也是其价格低于理想投资价格的原因。根据这种观点，大约70到100之间的水平可以被称为该证券状态的“主观差异”范围。

<!--en-->
The real situation is not so simple as this, however. Differences of opinion may properly exist in the minds of investors as to whether or not a given issue is adequately secured, particularly since the standards are qualitative and personal as well as arithmetical and objective. The range between 70 and 100 may therefore logically reflect a greater or lesser agreement concerning the safety of the issue. This would mean that an investor would be justified in buying such a bond, say, at 85, if his own considered judgment regarded it as sound, although he would recognize that there was doubt on this score in the minds of other investors that would account for its appreciable discount from a prime investment price. According to this view, the levels between 70 and 100, approximately, may be designated as the range of “subjective variations” in the status of the issue.

因此，真正的投机价值领域大约始于70水平附近（针对票面利率为4%或更高的债券），并提供至少50%成本增值的最大可能性。（对于其他高级证券，可把70%的*正常价值*作为分界线。）在做出此类承诺时，建议采取与谨慎购买普通股相同的态度；换句话说，收入表和资产负债表应接受同样细致的分析，并努力评估未来可能的情况——无论是有利还是不利。

<!--en-->
The field of speculative values proper would therefore commence somewhere near the 70 level (for bonds with a coupon rate of 4% or larger) and would offer maximum possibilities of appreciation of at least 50% of the cost. (In the case of other senior issues, 70% of *normal value* might be taken as the dividing line.) In making such commitments, it is recommended that the same general attitude be taken as in thecareful purchase of a common stock; in other words, that the income account and the balance sheet be submitted to the same intensive analysis and that the same effort be made to evaluate future possibilities—favorable and unfavorable.

**普通股与投机性高级证券的重要区别。** 因此，我们不会试图为投机性高级证券建立与固定价值证券适用的定量标准相对应的选择标准。另一方面，虽然最好将其与普通股方法和技术联系起来考虑，但有必要认识到普通股作为一个类别与投机性高级证券之间存在某些相当重要的差异。

<!--en-->
**Important Distinctions Between Common Stocks and Speculative Senior Issues.** We shall not seek, therefore, to set up standards of selection for speculative senior issues in any sense corresponding to the quantitative tests applicable to fixed-value securities. On the other hand, although they should preferably be considered in their relationship to the common-stock approach and technique, it is necessary to appreciate certain rather important points of difference that exist between common stocks as a class and speculative senior issues.

*与公司实力弱相关的低价债券。* 高级证券的利润潜力限制已经提到过。其重要性因具体情况而异，但通常我们不认为这是主要劣势。对低价债券和优先股更为强烈的反对理由是，它们与公司实力弱、衰退或经济萧条有关。显然，这类证券背后的企业并不非常成功，而且由于最初出售价格远高于当前水平，它肯定处于下滑状态。在1928年和1929年，这一因素足以让公众完全否定所有此类证券。企业被分为两组：成功且发展良好的企业，以及处于下滑或毫无进展的企业。第一组的普通股无论价格多高都值得购买；但第二组任何证券，无论售价多低，都不具有吸引力。

<!--en-->
*Low-Priced Bonds Associated with Corporate Weakness.* The limitation on the profit possibilities of senior securities has already been referred to. Its significance varies with the individual case, but in general we do not consider it a controlling disadvantage. A more emphatic objection is made against low-priced bonds and preferred stocks on the ground that they are associated with corporate weakness, retrogression, or depression. Obviously the enterprise behind such a security is not highly successful, and furthermore, it must have been following a downward course, since the issue originally sold at a much higher level. In 1928 and 1929 this consideration was enough to condemn all such issues absolutely in the eyes of the general public. Businesses were divided into two groups: those which were successful and progressing, and those which were on the downgrade or making no headway. The common shares of the first group were desirable no matter how high the price; but no security belonging to the second group was attractive, irrespective of how low it sold.

"永久强公司"与"永久弱公司"这一概念已因随后的经济萧条而基本消失，我们又回到了更传统的认识：时间会带来商业经营状况的不可预测变化。² 债券或优先股价格较低是由于收益下降，但这并不一定意味着公司前景毫无希望，未来也不会有更好的结果。许多在1931–1933年表现极差的公司，重新获得了大部分昔日的盈利能力，其高级证券价格也从极低水平回升到投资水平。因此，对于低迷的高级证券价格而言，与普通股票价格一样，存在大量理由期待其显著恢复。

<!--en-->
This concept of permanently strong and permanently weak corporations has been pretty well dissipated by the subsequent depression, and we are back to the older realization that time brings unpredictable changes in the fortunes of business undertakings.² The fact that the low price of a bond or preferred stock results from a decline in earnings need notsignify that the company's outlook is hopeless and that there is nothing ahead but still poorer results. Many of the companies that fared very badly in 1931–1933 regained a good part of their former earning power, and their senior securities recovered from exceedingly low prices to investment levels. It turned out, therefore, that there was just as much reason to expect substantial recoveries in the quotations of depressed senior securities as in the price of common stocks generally.

*许多证券与其地位和合同关系相比价值偏低。* 我们已经提到，投机性高级证券的不受欢迎程度使其以低于其内在价值的价格出售。从理性买家的角度来看，这应被视为其优势。就内在地位而言，投机性债券——以及程度较小的优先股——因其合同权利而获得重要优势。固定支付债券利息的义务通常会导致只要可能，就会继续支付这些利息。假设一组精心挑选的低价债券中，相当大比例不会违约，那么整个组合在一段时间内的收入无疑会远远超过同等价格普通股票的股息回报。

<!--en-->
*Many Undervalued in Relation to Their Status and Contractual Position.* We have already mentioned that the unpopularity of speculative senior securities tends to make them sell at lower prices than common stocks, in relation to their intrinsic value. From the standpoint of the intelligent buyer this must be considered a point in their favor. With respect to their intrinsic position, speculative bonds—and, to a lesser degree, preferred stocks—derive important advantages from their contractual rights. The fixed obligation to pay bond interest will usually result in the continuation of such payments as long as they are in any way possible. If we assume that a fairly large proportion of a group of carefully selected low-priced bonds will escape default, the income received on the group as a whole over a period of time will undoubtedly far exceed the dividend return on similarly priced common stocks.

优先股在这方面处于弱得多的情况，但即便如此，某些情况下，将投票控制权转移给高级证券的股息暂停条款也会促使股息继续支付。当现金资源充足时，保持良好记录并避免积累的愿望通常会促使即使收益不佳导致市场价格下跌，仍会支付优先股股息。

<!--en-->
Preferred shares occupy an immeasurably weaker position in this regard, but even here the provisions transferring voting control to the senior shares in the event of suspension of dividends will be found in some cases to impel their continuance. Where the cash resources are ample, the desire to maintain an unbroken record and to avoid accumulations will frequently result in paying preferred dividends even though poor earnings have depressed the market price.

*示例：* Century Ribbon Mills, Inc.在1926年至1938年的13年中，有8年未能支付7%的优先股股息，价格多次跌至约50美元。然而，在这整段时间内，优先股股息持续支付，而普通股的股息总额仅50美分。同样，1929年以约30美元购买Universal Pictures Company First Preferred的人，在三次经济萧条期间会收到8%的股息，直到最终停止支付为止。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Century Ribbon Mills, Inc., failed to earn its 7% preferred dividend in eight out of the thirteen years from 1926 to 1938, inclusive, and the price repeatedly declined to about 50. Yet the preferred dividend was continued without interruption during this entire period, while the common received a total of but 50 cents. Similarly, a purchaser of Universal Pictures Company First Preferred at about 30 in1929 would have received the 8% dividend during three years of depression before the payment was finally suspended.

*投机与投资中合同条款的对比重要性。* 读者应理解优先股在股息持续支付方面，投资属性与投机属性之间的区别。从投资角度——即股息的可靠性——与债券相比，缺乏可强制执行的权利是一个劣势。从投机角度——即在不理想条件下仍可能继续支付股息——优先股具有某些半合同性质的要求，这些要求来自董事，无疑使其比普通股票具有优势。

<!--en-->
*Contrasting Importance of Contractual Terms in Speculation and Investment.* The reader should appreciate the distinction between the *investment* and the *speculative* qualities of preferred stocks in this matter of dividend continuance. From the investment standpoint, *i.e.*, the *dependability* of the dividend, the absence of an enforceable claim is a disadvantage as compared with bonds. From the speculative standpoint, *i.e.*, the possibility of dividends' being continued under unfavorable conditions, preferred stocks have certain semicontractual claims to consideration by the directors that undoubtedly give them an advantage over common stocks.

**营运资本和沉没基金因素对投机性高级证券安全性的影响。** 多年以来，即使是不盈利的工业企业也具备大量营运资本，这对高级证券比普通股票更有直接优势。它不仅使利息或优先股股息的支付得以继续，还对本金的偿还有重要影响，无论是到期偿还、通过沉没基金操作还是自愿回购。无论是债券还是优先股，沉没基金条款都能改善市场的报价和证券的内在价值。这种优势在普通股票中不存在。

<!--en-->
**Bearing of Working-Capital and Sinking-Fund Factors on Safety of Speculative Senior Issues.** A large working capital, which has been characteristic of even nonprosperous industrials for some years past, is much more directly advantageous to the senior securities than to the common stock. Not only does it make possible the continuance of interest or preferred-dividend payments, but it has an important bearing also on the retirement of the principal, either at maturity or by sinking-fund operations or by voluntary repurchase. Sinking-fund provisions, for bonds as well as preferred stocks, contribute to the improvement of both the market quotation and the intrinsic position of the issue. This advantage is not found in the case of common stocks.

*示例：* Francis H. Leggett Company作为食品产品制造商和批发商，发行了200万美元7%优先股，包含每年偿还3%本金的沉没基金条款。到1932年6月30日，未偿还金额降至608,500美元，由于剩余余额很少，该证券在经济萧条时期以110美元的价格被要求赎回。同样，Century Ribbon Mills Preferred在1922年至1938年间从200万美元降至544,000美元；Lawrence Portland Cement Company Debenture 5 1/2s在1938年12月31日从200万美元降至650,000美元，余额于1939年4月1日被要求赎回。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Francis H. Leggett Company, manufacturers and wholesalers of food products, issued $2,000,000 of 7% preferred stock carrying a sinking-fund provision which retired 3% of the issue annually. By June 30, 1932, the amount outstanding had been reduced to $608,500, and, because of the small balance remaining, the issue was called for redemption at 110, *in the depth of the depression*. Similarly, Century Ribbon Mills Preferred was reduced from $2,000,000 to $544,000 between 1922 and 1938; and Lawrence Portland Cement Company Debenture 5 1/2s were reduced from$2,000,000 to $650,000 on December 31, 1938, the balance being called for redemption on April 1, 1939.

*大流动资产覆盖的重要性。* 当低价债券被大量流动资产覆盖时，它呈现一种特殊机会，因为经验表明即使收益可能较低或不稳定，偿还的可能性也很大。

<!--en-->
*Importance of Large Net-Current-Asset Coverage.* Where a low-priced bond is covered several times over by net current assets, it presents a special type of opportunity, because experience shows that the chances of repayment are good, even though the earnings may be poor or irregular.

*示例：* 电气制冷公司（Kelvinator）6s债券，到期日为1936年。1929年11月，当该公司最新报告显示其流动资产为6,008,900美元，未偿还债券为2,528,500美元时，该债券以66美元的价格出售。确实，公司在1927年和1928年处于亏损状态，但截至1929年9月30日的年度中，固定费用收入几乎是债券金额的九倍，流动资产几乎是债券发行市场价值的四倍。该债券在1930年恢复至接近面值的价格，并在1931年以105美元的价格赎回。同样，电气制冷建筑公司第一6s债券，到期日为1936年，由Kelvinator公司通过租赁提供担保，在1932年7月以70美元的价格出售。当时母公司的流动资产约为未偿还债券1,073,000美元的六倍，超过发行总市场价值的八倍。该债券于1933年以$101\frac{1}{2}$价格赎回。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Electric Refrigeration Corporation (Kelvinator) 6s, due 1936, sold at 66 in November 1929 when the net current assets of the company according to its latest statement amounted to $6,008,900 for the $2,528,500 of bonds outstanding. It is true that the company had operated at a deficit in 1927 and 1928, but fixed charges were earned nearly nine times in the year ended September 30, 1929, and the net current assets were nearly four times the market value of the bond issue. The bonds recovered to a price close to par in 1930 and were redeemed at 105 in 1931. Similarly, Electric Refrigeration Building Corporation First 6s, due 1936, which were in effect guaranteed by Kelvinator Corporation under a lease, sold at 70 in July 1932 when the net current assets of the parent company amounted to about six times the $1,073,000 of bonds outstanding and over eight times the total market value of the issue. The bonds were called at $101\frac{1}{2}$ in 1933.

与此相关的其他示例包括Murray公司第一6\frac{1}{2}$s债券，到期日为1934年。由于当前运营亏损，该债券在1932年以68美元的价格出售，尽管该公司的流动资产超过发行面值的$2\frac{1}{2}$倍，且在该价格下接近市场价值的四倍；Sidney Blumenthal and Company 7% Notes债券，到期日为1936年。1926年，当该公司流动资产是发行面值的两倍，接近总市场价值的三倍时，该债券以70美元的价格出售（1930年以103美元赎回）；Belding, Heminway Company 6s债券，到期日为1936年。1930年，该公司流动资产接近发行面值的三倍，超过市场价值的四倍。在后一种情况下，1930年和1931年发生了库存大幅清理，所得资金用于通过市场购买赎回约80%的债券。1934年初，剩余债券以101美元的价格赎回。

<!--en-->
Other examples that may be cited in this connection are Murray Corporation First $6\frac{1}{2}$s, due 1934, which sold at 68 in 1932 (because of current operating deficits) although the company had net current assets of over $2\frac{1}{2}$ times the par value of the issue and nearly four times their market value at that price; Sidney Blumenthal and Company 7% Notes, due 1936, which sold at 70 in 1926 when the company had net current assets of twice the par value of the issue and nearly three times the total market value thereof (they were called at 103 in 1930); Belding, Heminway Company 6s, due 1936, which sold at 67 in 1930 when the company had net current assets of nearly three times the par value of the issue and over four times its market value. In the latter case drastic liquidation of inventories occurred in 1930 and 1931, proceedsfrom which were used to retire about 80% of the bond issue through purchases in the market. The balance of the issue was called for payment at 101 early in 1934.

在这种典型情况下，盈利机会将超过损失机会，预期利润将超过预期损失。每个具体案例中的风险可能仍然相当大，以至于我们无法将这种承诺称为“投资”。然而，我们建议，如果遵循保险原则——即通过同时进行多次此类承诺来分散风险，最终结果应足够可靠，使我们能够将这种集体购买称为*投资操作*。这是我们在第4章中给出的投资广义定义中所设想的可能性之一。

<!--en-->
In the typical case of this kind the chance of profit will exceed the chance of loss, and the probable amount of profit will exceed the probable amount of loss. It may well be that the risk involved in each individual case is still so considerable as to preclude us from applying the term “investment” to such a commitment. Nevertheless, we suggest that if the insurance principle of diversification of risk be followed by making a number of such commitments at the same time, the net result should be sufficiently dependable to warrant our calling the group purchase an *investment operation*. This was one of the possibilities envisaged in our broadened definition of investment as given in Chap. 4.

*流动资产状况重要性的限制。* 显然，在选择投机性债券时，营运资本指标具有重大权重。然而，不应过度强调这一重要性，以至于认为只要债券完全被流动资产覆盖，其安全性就得到了保障。任何资产负债表中显示的流动资产可能会因后续运营亏损而大幅减少；更重要的是，在破产情况下，这些价值往往完全不可靠。³关于此点的许多示例，我们将提到R. Hoe and Company 7% Notes和Ajax Rubber Company First 8s债券。虽然这些债务在1929年被流动资本覆盖，但随后以低至1美元兑2美分的价格出售。（另见附录注34中对Willys-Overland Company First 6½s和Berkey and Gay Furniture Company First 6s的讨论。⁴）**1932年流动资产覆盖的低价工业债券示例**** 有关这些示例后续内容的简要讨论，请参见本著作1934年版的附录注43。**

<!--en-->
*Limitations upon Importance of Current-Asset Position.* It is clear that considerable weight attaches to the working-capital exhibit in selecting speculative bonds. This importance must not be exaggerated, however, to the point of assuming that, whenever a bond is fully covered by net current assets, its safety is thereby assured. The current assets shown in any balance sheet may be greatly reduced by subsequent operating losses; more important still, the stated values frequently prove entirely undependable in the event of insolvency.³
Of the many examples of this point which can be given, we shall mention R. Hoe and Company 7% Notes and Ajax Rubber Company First 8s. Although these obligations were covered by net working capital in 1929, they subsequently sold as low as 2 cents on the dollar. (See also our discussion of Willys-Overland Company First 6½s and Berkey and Gay Furniture Company First 6s in Appendix Note 34.⁴)
**Examples of Low-Priced Industrial Bonds Covered by Net Current Assets, 1932**** See Appendix Note 43 for a brief discussion of the sequel to these examples first given in the 1934 edition of this work.

因此，我们必须区分两个事实：其一是报告中的营运资金足以覆盖已融资债务，其二是该金额远远超过债券发行额*数倍之多*。前者固然值得关注，但绝非决定性证据。若再结合其他有利因素，比如正常年份良好的收益覆盖率以及总体令人满意的质地表现，这些因素或许会让该债券极具吸引力，但最好还是作为批量购买的一部分。

<!--en-->
We must distinguish, therefore, between the mere fact that the working capital, as reported, covers the funded debt and the more significant fact that it exceeds the bond issue *many times over*. The former statement is always interesting, but by no means conclusive. If added to other favorable factors, such as a good earnings coverage in normal years and a generally satisfactory qualitative showing, it might make the issue quite attractive but preferably as part of a group-purchase in the field.

**投机性优先股。*其价格历史的发展阶段。**投机性优先股比投机性债券更容易出现非理性波动，因此这类优先股有时会在市场上像普通股一样被高估。据此，我们可以将一种优先股的价格历史划分为三个可能的阶段，在每个阶段中，市场报价往往都与其实际价值不符：

<!--en-->
**Speculative Preferred Stocks.** *Stages in Their Price History.*
Speculative preferred stocks are more subject than speculative bonds to irrational activity, so that from time to time such preferred shares are overvalued in the market in the same way as common stocks. We thus have three possible stages in the price history of a preferred issue, in each of which the market quotation tends to be out of line with the value:

1. 第一阶段是初始发行阶段，此时投资者会在其内在价值并不支持的情况下，以全价购买这些股票。
2. 在第二阶段，股票的内在投资价值已显露无遗，价格随之降至投机性水平。由于前述原因，此阶段的股价下跌很可能过于剧烈。
3. 有时会出现第三阶段，在这一阶段，该证券的走势会像普通股票一样以投机方式发展。在这种情况下，一些重要性存疑的因素——比如累积股息的数额——会被过度强调。稍后我们将给出这种第三阶段或非理性阶段的例子。*“优先股最高估值规则”*。为避免被第三阶段特有的误导性宣传所迷惑，同时也作为处理投机性优先股的一般指导原则，这里提出以下证券分析原则，我们将其称为“优先股最高估值规则”。*从内在价值来看，优先股的价值不可能超过：如果该优先股的位置被普通股票取代且不存在其他次级证券时，那普通股票应有的价值。*通过一个例子可以更直观地理解这一表述。公司*X*和公司*Y*的价值相同。公司*X*拥有80,000股优先股和200,000股普通股；而公司*Y*仅有80,000股普通股，没有优先股。根据我们的原则，公司*X*的优先股每股价值不可能高于公司*Y*的普通股每股价值。这是因为公司*Y*的普通股所代表的价值，恰好等于公司*X*的优先股与普通股共同对应的价值。我们不必比较像*X*和*Y*这样价值相当的公司，也可以假设对公司*X*进行资本重组，消除原有的普通股，让优先股成为唯一的股票种类，即新的普通股。（为了方便表述，我们可以将这种假设性的变化称为优先股的“普通化”。）那么我们的原则实际上只是在陈述一个显而易见的事实：这种假设中的普通股价值不可能低于它所替代的优先股价值，因为它相当于优先股价值加上原有的普通股价值。同样的思路也可应用于投机性债券，之后可能只出现普通股，也可能同时出现优先股和普通股。如果该债券被“普通化”，即假设其转变为普通股并消除原有的股票种类，那么由此产生的新普通股价值不可能低于该债券的当前价值。无论优先股或次级证券的票面利率、面值或赎回价格有多高，尤其是无论累积的未付利息或股息有多少，这一关系都始终成立。因为即使某优先股每股有1,000美元的累积股息，其价值也不可能超过等同于完全拥有该公司所有权的普通股（无累积股息）的价值。未付股息无法为公司整体证券创造额外价值，它们只会影响总价值在优先股与普通股之间的分配。*过度强调累积股息的数额*。尽管稍加分析就能发现上述观点几乎是不言而喻的真理，但一旦人们陷入投机心态，就会忽视最基本的逻辑规则。因此，那些累积股息较高的优先股很容易成为市场操纵的对象，操纵者会利用这些累积股息作为推动优先股和普通股股价大幅上涨的依据。1928年美国锌铅冶炼公司的股票就提供了此类操作的典型例子。该公司的优先股是在1916年作为普通股的股票红利而设立的，这一操作实际上相当于将原有的普通股拆分为优先股和新的普通股。该优先股的名义面值为25美元，但却具备面值为100美元的股票的所有特征（6美元的累积股息，赎回及清算价值为100美元）。 这种安排显然是一种手段，旨在让资产负债表上的优先股负债显得远低于其实际规模。1920年至1927年间，该公司持续出现亏损（1922年仅有微不足道的盈利）；1921年优先股股息被暂停发放，到1928年时每股累计未付股息已达约40美元。1928年，得益于整体经济繁荣，该公司优先股的每股收益勉强达到6美元。然而，公司的股票发行遭到了操纵，使得优先股的价格从1927年的35美元上涨至1928年的118美元，而普通股的价格则更惊人地从6美元升至57美元。在这些股价上涨的同时，还出现了关于偿还累计未付股息计划的传闻——但具体方式并未说明。自然，这一计划并未实现。⁵此处充分体现了投机心理的荒谬性：人们竟将未支付的优先股股息视为优先股和普通股价值的来源。支持购买普通股的投机论点如下：“那些累计的优先股股息终将被偿还，这对普通股有利，因此我们应该购买普通股。”按照这种颠倒的逻辑，如果普通股在优先股之前没有未支付的股息，那么即便价格相同，它的吸引力也会降低，因为届时就不会有清理这些累计债务的妙计。我们可以以美国锌业为例来展示我们“优先股最高估值规则”的实际应用。1928年时，美国锌业的优先股价格118美元是否过高？假设优先股股东完全拥有该公司，那就意味着在经历八年亏损后，1928年每股收益仅为6美元的普通股，其价格却高达118美元。即便在1928年那段动荡的时期，投机者也不会对如此高价的普通股感兴趣，因此我们的规则本应阻止人们以虚高的价格购买优先股。美国锌业普通股最终达到的57美元这一价格显然是荒谬至极的，因为它代表了该公司如下的估值水平：

<!--en-->
1. The first stage is that of original issuance, when investors are persuaded to buy the offering at a full investment price not justified by its intrinsic merit.
2. In the second stage the lack of investment merit has become manifest, and the price drops to a speculative level. During this period the decline is likely to be overdone, for reasons previously discussed.
3. A third stage sometimes appears in which the issue advances speculatively in the same fashion as common stocks.
On such occasions certain factors of questionable importance —such as the amount of dividend accumulations—are overemphasized.
An example of this third or irrational stage will be given a little later.
*The Rule of “Maximum Valuation for Senior Issues.”* Both as a safeguard against being led astray by the propaganda that is characteristic of the third stage and also as a general guide in dealing with speculative senior issues, the following principle of security analysis is presented, which we shall call “the rule of maximum valuation for senior issues.”
*A senior issue cannot be worth, intrinsically, any more than a common stock would be worth if it occupied the position of that senior issue, with no junior securities outstanding.*
This statement may be understood more readily by means of an example.
Company *X* and Company *Y* have the same value. Company *X* has 80,000 shares of preferred and 200,000 shares of common. Company *Y* has only 80,000 shares of common and no preferred. Then our principle states that a share of Company *X* preferred cannot be worth more than a share of Company *Y* common. This is true because Company *Y* common represents the same value that lies behind *both* the preferred and common of Company *X*.
Instead of comparing two equivalent companies such as *X* and *Y*, we may assume that Company *X* is recapitalized so that the old common is eliminated and the preferred becomes the sole stock issue, *i.e.*, the new common stock. (To coin a term, we may call such an assumed change the “communizing” of a preferred stock.) Then our principle merely states the obvious fact that the value of such a hypothetical common stock cannot be *less* than the value of the preferred stock it replaces, because it is equivalent to the preferred *plus* the old common. The same idea may be applied to a speculative bond, followed either by common stock only or by both preferred and common. If the bond is “commonized,” *i.e.*, if it is assumed tobe turned into a common stock, with the old stock issues eliminated, then the value of the new common stock thus created cannot be less than the present value of the bond.
This relationship must hold true regardless of how high the coupon or dividend rate, the par value or the redemption price of the senior issue may be and, particularly, regardless of what amount of unpaid interest or dividends may have accumulated. For if we had a preferred stock with accumulations of $1,000 per share, the value of the issue could be no greater than if it were a common stock (without dividend accumulations) representing complete ownership of the business. The unpaid dividends cannot create any additional value for the company's securities in the aggregate; they merely affect the division of the total value between the preferred and the common.
*Excessive Emphasis Placed on Amount of Accrued Dividends.* Although a very small amount of analysis will show the above statements to be almost self-evident truths, the public fails to observe the simplest rules of logic when once it is in a gambling mood. Hence preferred shares with large dividend accruals have lent themselves readily to market manipulation in which the accumulations are made the basis for a large advance in the price of both the preferred and common. An excellent example of such a performance was provided by American Zinc, Lead, and Smelting Company shares in 1928.
American Zinc preferred stock was created in 1916 as a stock dividend on the common, the transaction thus amounting to a split-up of old common into preferred and new common. The preferred was given a stated par of $25 but had all the attributes of a $100-par stock ($6 cumulative dividends, redemption and liquidating value of $100). This arrangement was evidently a device to permit carrying the preferred issue in the balance sheet as a much smaller liability than it actually represented. Between 1920 and 1927 the company reported continuous deficits (except for a negligible profit in 1922); preferred dividends were suspended in 1921, and by 1928 about $40 per share had accumulated.
In 1928 the company benefited moderately from the prevailing prosperity and barely earned $6 per share on the preferred. However, the company's issues were subjected to manipulation that advanced the price of the preferred from 35 in 1927 to 118 in 1928, while the common rose even more spectacularly from 6 to 57. These advances were accompanied by rumors of a plan to pay off the accumulated dividends—exactly how, not being stated. Naturally enough, this development failed to materialize.⁵
The irrationality of the gambling spirit is well shown here by the absurd acceptance of unpaid preferred dividends as a *source of value for both the preferred and the common*. The speculative argument in behalf of the common stock ran as follows: "The accumulated preferred dividends are going to be paid off. This will be good for the common. Therefore let us buy the common." According to this topsy-turvy reasoning, if there were no unpaid preferred dividends ahead of the common it would be less attractive (even at the same price), because there would then be in prospect no wonderful plan for clearing up the accumulations.
We may use the American Zinc example to demonstrate the practical application of our "rule of maximum valuation for senior issues." Was American Zinc Preferred too high at 118 in 1928? Assuming the preferred stockholders owned the company completely, this would then mean a price of 118 for a *common* stock earning $6 per share in 1928 after eight years of deficits. Even in the hectic days of 1928 speculators would not have been at all attracted to such a common stock at that price, so that the application of our rule should have prevented the purchase of the preferred stock at its inflated value.
The quotation of 57 reached by American Zinc common was evidently the height of absurdity, since it represented the following valuation for the company:

<table><tr><td>优先股，80,000 盾，价格为 118</td><td>$ 9,440,000</td></tr><tr><td>普通股，200,000 盾，价格为 57</td><td>11,400,000</td></tr><tr><td>总估值</td><td>$20,840,000</td></tr><tr><td>收益，1928年</td><td>481,000</td></tr><tr><td>平均收益，1920-1927年</td><td>188,000 盾</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>Preferred stock, 80,000 sh. @ 118</td><td>$ 9,440,000</td></tr><tr><td>Common stock, 200,000 sh. @ 57</td><td>11,400,000</td></tr><tr><td>Total valuation</td><td>$20,840,000</td></tr><tr><td>Earnings, 1928</td><td>481,000</td></tr><tr><td>Average earnings, 1920-1927</td><td>188,000(d)</td></tr></table>

为了与美国锌公司的上述估值相等，假设普通股（以80,000股为基准）的售价应为每股260美元，仅能获得6美元收益，且不支付股息。这一数字表明，公众在本案中因未支付股息的剥削而严重被误导。

<!--en-->
In order to equal the above valuation for the American Zinc Company the hypothetical common stock (80,000 shares basis) would have had to sell at $260 *per share*, earning a bare $6 and paying no dividend. This figure indicates the extent to which the heedless public was led astray in this case by the exploitation of unpaid dividends.

美国皮革公司提供了另一个类似案例，但效果稍弱。从1922年到1928年之间，该公司没有任何一年优先股的收益超过4.41美元，平均利润也非常低。然而在这七年中，优先股的价格最高曾达到66美元或更高。这种持续的高价主要源于大量累积优先股息的投机吸引力——在此期间，累积股息从每股约120美元增长到175美元。

<!--en-->
American Hide and Leather Company offers another, but less striking, example of this point. In no year between 1922 and 1928, inclusive, did the company earn more than $4.41 on the preferred, and the average profits were very small. Yet in each of these seven years, the preferred stock sold as high as 66 or higher. This recurring strength was based largely on the speculative appeal of the enormous accumulated preferred dividends which grew from about $120 to $175 per share during this period.

根据我们的规则，可以将美国皮革公司的优先股视为完全拥有企业所有权，实际上也确实如此。那么应该有一只普通股，多年未支付过股息，且使用1922-1927年期间的数据，平均收益仅为每股2美元。显然，这样一只普通股的价格超过65美元会过高。因此，美国皮革公司的优先股价格过高，无论累积股息规模多大，都无法轻微影响这一结论。

<!--en-->
Applying our rule, we may consider American Hide and Leather Preferred as representing complete ownership of the business, which to all intents and purposes it did. We should then have a common stock which had paid no dividends for many years and with average earnings at best (using the 1922–1927 period) of barely $2 per share. Evidently a price of above 65 for such a common stock would be far too high. Consequently this price was excessive for American Hide and Leather Preferred, nor could the existence of accumulated dividends, however large, affect this conclusion in the slightest.

**资本结构的变化会影响证券的总市场价值。**从以上讨论可以推断，单次发行优先股的价值必须等于其可能被分割的所有优先股和普通股的价值之和。理论上这是正确的，但实际上可能并非如此，因为将资本划分为高级证券和普通股可能比单独发行普通股具有实际优势。这一主题将在第40章“资本结构”部分详细讨论。

<!--en-->
**Variation in Capital Structure Affects Total Market Value of Securities.** From the foregoing discussion it might be inferred that the value of a single capital-stock issue must always be equivalent to the combined values of any preferred and common stock issues into which it might be split. In a theoretical sense this is entirely true, but in practice it may not be true at all, because a division of capitalization into senior securities and common stock may have a real advantage over a single common-stock issue. This subject will receive extended treatment under the heading of “Capitalization Structure” in Chap. 40.

刚刚提出的观点与我们的“最大估值规则”之间的区别可以如下澄清：

<!--en-->
The distinction between the idea just suggested and our “rule of maximum valuation” may be clarified as follows:

1. 假设公司$X$ = 公司$Y$
2. 公司$X$有优先股（$P$）和普通股（$C$）；公司$Y$只有普通股（$C'$）
3. 那么似乎

<!--en-->
1. Assume Company $X$ = Company $Y$
2. Company $X$ has preferred ($P$) and common ($C$); Company $Y$ has common only ($C'$)
3. Then it *would appear* that

$$
\text{Value of } P + \text{value of } C = \text{value of } C'
$$

因为方程的每一边代表相同的事物，即每家公司的总价值。

<!--en-->
since each side of the equation represents equal things, namely the total value of each company.

但这种表面关系在实践中可能不成立，因为优先股和普通股的资本分配方法可能比单独发行普通股具有实际优势。

<!--en-->
But this apparent relationship may not hold good in practice because the preferred-and-common capitalization method may have real advantages over a single common-stock issue.

另一方面，我们的“最大估值规则”仅指出$P$单独的价值不能超过$C'$的价值。这一规则在理论和实践中都应成立，除非操纵性或无理性的投机行为完全忽略所有理性考虑。

<!--en-->
On the other hand, our “rule of maximum valuation” merely states that the value of $P$ *alone* cannot exceed value of $C'$. This should hold true in practice as well as in theory, except in so far as manipulative or heedlessly speculative activity brushes aside all rational considerations.

我们的规则以否定形式表述，因此在应用时本质上具有负面性。它最适用于识别优先股或债券*不值*其市场价格的情况。要正面应用它，首先需要在“合并”基础上确定优先股的价值（即完全拥有企业），然后确定应从该价值中扣除多少，以反映可公平归属于现有普通股的部分。有时这种方法有助于确认某个高级证券的价值高于其市场价格。但这样的程序使我们远离数学公式，进入普通股票估值的复杂且不确定的领域，我们将在接下来讨论该领域。[^1526]：¹ 关于1931-1934年和1939年债券价格的数据，请参见附录注释42。² 但请参阅Mead和Grodinski于1939年出版的《投资价值的起伏》，其中强烈支持前一段（第28章和附录注释71）中的论点。

<!--en-->
Our rule is stated in negative form and is therefore essentially negative in its application. It is most useful in detecting instances where preferred stocks or bonds are *not worth* their market price. To apply it positively it would be necessary, first, to arrive at a value for the preferred on a “communized” basis (*i.e.*, representing complete ownership of the business) and then to determine what deduction from this value should be made to reflect the part of the ownership fairly ascribable to the existing common stock. At times this approach will be found useful in establishing the fact that a given senior issue is worth more than its market price. But such a procedure brings us far outside the range of mathematical formulas and into the difficult and indefinite field of common-stock valuation, with which we have next to deal.
[^1526]: ¹ See Appendix Note 42 for data on bond prices in 1931–1934 and 1939.
² But see later references to *The Ebb and Flow of Investment Value*, by Mead and Grodinski, published in 1939, which strongly espouses the thesis stated in the previous paragraph (Chap. 28 and Appendix Note 71).

³ 当前资产指标中各组成部分的对比可靠性（现金资产、应收账款、存货）将在第六部分资产负债表分析中详细讨论。

<!--en-->
³ The comparative reliability of the various components in the current-assets figure (cash assets, receivables, inventories) will receive detailed treatment in a discussion of balance-sheet analysis in Part VI.

⁴ 或许还应补充一点，本段提到的四项发行中，有三项在经济萧条期间从低价中显著复苏（例如，新的Hoe 7s以1937年100盾的价格换成了旧的7s）。

<!--en-->
⁴ Perhaps it should be added that three of the four issues mentioned in this paragraph had spectacular recoveries from the low prices of the depression (e.g., the new Hoe 7s, which were exchanged for the old 7s, sold at 100 in 1937).

⁵ 但多年后，即1936年，累积的优先股息通过重组计划得到了处理，该计划让优先股股东获得了扩大后的普通发行股份的大部分。

<!--en-->
⁵ But years later, in 1936, accumulated preferred dividends were taken care of by a recapitalization plan which gave the preferred stockholders the bulk of the enlarged common issue.
