## 在普通股中寻找价值

<!--en-->
*Finding Value in Common Stocks*

作者：Todd Combs 在格雷厄姆和多德首次出版《证券分析》约九十年后，其中许多原则至今仍然适用。当然，对潜在投资进行彻底分析的需求以及风险防护的重要性，现在与多年前我第一次阅读《证券分析》时一样重要。考虑到作者们在1929年经济崩溃后仅几年内写作，且处于大萧条期间，他们的投资方法完全可以理解。根据格雷厄姆和多德的观点，投资可以被视为一种“负面艺术”，更注重风险防护而非追求收益。

<!--en-->
by Todd Combs
Some nine decades after Graham and Dodd's *Security Analysis* was first published, many if not most of the principles it laid out still hold true. Certainly, the need to perform thorough analysis of potential investments and the importance of downside protection resonate as much with me now as when I read *Security Analysis* the first time many years ago. Given the authors were writing only a few years removed from the 1929 crash and in the middle of the Great Depression, their approach to investing was completely understandable. Investing, according to Graham and Dodd, could be considered a "negative art," focused more on downside protection than on the pursuit of upside.

当投资做得好时，意味着要学习如何处理信息，以确定何时机会对我们有利；目标是基于事实而非故事做出明智的投资决策。在投资中，甚至在生活中，你无法选择结果，但可以选择能带来你想要结果的决策。有了这样的永恒智慧，《证券分析》依然具有相关性，确实是我职业生涯中不可或缺的支柱。

<!--en-->
When done well, investing involves learning how to process information in order to determine when the odds are in your favor; the goal is to make educated bets based on facts and not stories. In investing, and in life for that matter, you can't choose outcomes, but you can choose the decisions that may get you the outcomes you want. With timeless wisdom like this, *Security Analysis* retains its relevance and, indeed, has been an invaluable pillar of my career.

《证券分析》是在工业革命后期出版的，当时大型企业都是资本密集型项目。维护工厂和设备需要大量资本投入，发展企业还需要更多资金，因此与今天的最大企业相比，投资资本的回报率较低。

<!--en-->
*Security Analysis* was published during the latter stages of the industrial revolution, a time when the great businesses of the day were massively capital-intensive endeavors. Maintaining plant and equipment required significant capital spending, and growing a business necessitated still more, the end result being low returns on invested capital compared to today's largest enterprises.

过去一个世纪里，商业和投资领域发生了显著变化，如今许多最大公司仅在有形资产方面投入有限资金，却拥有非凡的现金生成能力。在许多情况下，它们的主要资产是人才、知识产权和品牌；没有流水线或高炉，没有机车或蒸汽铲。这类企业的利润率远高于过去那些以资产为主的典型企业。因此，当代公司的价值不再完全取决于其物理资产的价值。这可能需要我们调整分析视角以适应当前现实，但格雷厄姆和多德提出的原始概念仍然不变：(1) 可以通过对盈利能力的仔细评估和分析确定不精确但相对准确的内在价值；(2) 可以通过以低于这些内在价值的价格购买公司股票来获得投资机会。

<!--en-->
The world of business and investment has changed significantly over the past century, and many of today's largest companies have only a limited amount invested in tangibleassets, yet extraordinary cash-generation capability. In many cases, their primary assets are people, intellectual property, and brands; there are no assembly lines or blast furnaces, no locomotives or steam shovels. Profit margins for such businesses are far above those of the typical asset-heavy firms from generations past. The value of a contemporary company is consequently less bound up with the value of its physical assets. This may require us to tilt the prism of analysis to adjust to today's reality, but the original concepts put forward by Graham and Dodd remain the same: (1) that imprecise but reasonably accurate intrinsic values can be determined through careful assessment and analysis of earnings power, and (2) there are investment opportunities to be had in purchasing shares of a company at a price below these intrinsic values.

但如今，要确定公司的内在价值需要什么？我们将逐步找到答案。

<!--en-->
But what does it take these days to determine a company's intrinsic value? We will work our way to the answer.

## 所学经验

<!--en-->
*LESSONS LEARNED*

股票投资被描述为简单但不容易。诸如“不要支付过高价格”、“识别优秀的管理团队”、“避免投机”、“保持耐心”、“验证财务报表的准确性”、“市场是投票机而非称重机”以及“关注企业的质量和数量方面”等概念常被提及，但在实践中比在理论上更容易应用。

<!--en-->
Investing in equities has been described as simple but not easy. Concepts such as "don't overpay," "identify good management teams," "avoid speculation," "be patient," "verify the accuracy of financial statements," "the market is a voting machine and not a weighing machine," and "focus on qualitative, as well as quantitative aspects of a business" are all bandied about, but they are easier to invoke in principle than in practice.

在我的职业生涯中试图评估公司价值的过程中，我意识到优秀分析师与杰出分析师的区别在于能否保持简单并确定最重要的因素。有些人误解这意味着投资者应该停留在表面层面。实际上，保持简单反而需要极高的深度。分析师的工作是拆解投资项目以了解其基本要素。优秀的证券分析师愿意将公司分析到最底层，了解每个部分后再重新组合。在分析师不断接收的大量信息中，总有一部分比其他部分更重要。找到这一部分就是保持简单的意义所在。

<!--en-->
In attempting to value companies over my career, I've come to appreciate that the difference between a good analyst and a great one lies in the ability to keep things simple and determine what matters most. People misinterpret this to mean that investors should keep things at the surface level. In fact, it paradoxically takes a great deal of depth to stay simple. The analyst's job is to tear apart an investment in order to understand its essential elements. A great security analyst is willing to rip a company down to its studs and understand each part before they reassemble it. In the massive sea of information that an analyst is continuously ingesting, there isalways one piece that matters more than the others. Finding that morsel is what keeping it simple means.

我记忆中最突出的一个例子是2002年。当时我是一名年轻分析师，参加一场“支付”会议，第一次接触Mastercard。虽然它仍是一家私人公司，但管理层还是对公司的状况进行了介绍，这让我很感兴趣。或许因为它是私人企业，没有明确的投资或研究获利方式，只有少数人在场听演讲。我继续密切关注这家公司，到2006年春季该公司公开上市时，我觉得自己已经充分理解它了。该公司上市是为了筹集资金用于大型法律和解。当时华尔街对Mastercard首次公开募股的说法是，公司没有定价权。银行整合肯定会压缩其利润空间。但我们的看法不同。

<!--en-->
An example that stands out most in my mind dates back to 2002. I was a young analyst attending a “payments” conference, and I was looking at Mastercard for the first time. Although it was still a private company, management was nevertheless presenting on the company, which intrigued me. Perhaps because it was private and therefore not offering a clear way to invest in or profit from researching it, only a few of us were on hand for the presentation. I continued to follow the company closely and felt I understood it well by the time it came public in the spring of 2006. The company was being brought public to fund a large legal settlement. The Wall Street narrative at the time of Mastercard’s IPO was that the company did not have pricing power. Surely bank consolidation was destined to squeeze its margins. But we saw things differently.

我在分析Mastercard时考虑了几个关键的质量因素。例如，由于银行从更高的交易收入中获益，它们的激励措施实际上与Mastercard一致，长期定价权很可能保持强劲。我们认为，随着信用卡持续替代现金使用，增长将持续很长时间。而作为上市公司（而非银行所有），有助于建立管理层的激励机制（就像许多保险公司和其他客户所有公司的过去拆分一样），以推动公司高效运营。此外，许多表面上的风险似乎被夸大了。银行行业整合远非必然持续下去。而且，公司面临的法律风险似乎可以解决，不会造成重大减值。

<!--en-->
There were several key qualitative considerations in my Mastercard analysis. For example, as banks benefited from higher interchange revenues, their incentives were actually aligned with Mastercard’s, and long-term pricing power was likely to remain strong. We believed growth would continue for a long time as credit cards continued to replace cash. And having publicly traded shares (rather than being owned by banks) facilitated creation of an incentive structure for management (just as in many past demutualizations of insurance companies and other customer-owned companies) to run a tight ship. Also, many of the apparent risks seemed overstated. Banking industry consolidation was far from certain to continue unabated. Also, legal risks facing the company seemed likely to be resolved without significant impairment.

投资者必须记住，无论电子表格多么好，都不代表商业现实。电子表格中的数字讲述了一个精确的故事，但有时并非正确的故事。例如，过度强调定量因素可能导致忽略定性因素，反之亦然。最终，同时考虑两者非常有价值。因为寻找简单性可能很复杂，我将我的流程分为三个部分：找到一家优秀的企业、优秀的管理层、合理的估值。不需要也无需在每个投资中都能同时满足这三个条件；可能存在程度不同的要求。不过，这三个条件都必须存在。可以将其视为乘法序列：任何单元格为零，整体结果也将为零，无论其他元素数值如何高。

<!--en-->
Investors must always remember that a spreadsheet, no matter how good, is not business reality. The numbers laid out in a spreadsheet tell a precise story, but sometimes it’s not the right story. For example, overemphasis of the quantitative can lead to missing the qualitative, and vice versa. In the end, assessing both can be very valuable. Because finding simplicity can be complicated, I break down my process intothree buckets—find a good business, with good management, at a good valuation. You don’t need or expect to find all three of these to the same degree in every investment; there can be a sliding scale with puts and takes. Nonetheless, all three must be present. Think of it as a multiplicative series where a zero in any of the cells will yield a zero overall regardless of how high the other elements may rate.

## 保持简单原则 1：找到优秀的企业

<!--en-->
*KEEPING IT SIMPLE PRINCIPLE 1: FINDING A GOOD BUSINESS*

人们最常问的问题是，什么才是优秀的企业？简短的回答是拥有竞争优势，即沃伦·巴菲特所说的“护城河”。护城河越宽越好。再加上低资本密集型、定价权、经常性收入、持久性以及长期增长潜力等特征，就构成了一个优秀的企业。在判断企业是否优秀时，我喜欢从定量方面开始：关注资产负债表、会计政策和单位经济模型，然后转向现金流生成情况。而定性方面则涉及参考电话评估管理质量，以及渠道检查以了解产品实时销售情况。

<!--en-->
The question I’m asked most often is what exactly constitutes a good business? The short answer begins with having a competitive advantage, or what Warren Buffett calls a “moat.” The wider the moat the better. Add on characteristics like low capital intensity, pricing power, recurring revenues, staying power, and the likelihood of long-term growth, and you have a great business. In determining if a business is great, I like to start on the quantitative side: I focus on the balance sheet, accounting practices, and unit economics, and then turn to cash flow generation. Meanwhile, the qualitative side involves reference calls to assess the quality of management and channel checks to reveal how a company’s products are selling in real time.

### *资产负债表和会计*

<!--en-->
*Balance Sheet and Accounting*

虽然分析重点大多集中在损益表上，但正确且全面分析资产负债表和公司的会计记录，就像建筑项目中的坚实基础。它们容易被普通观察者忽视或视为理所当然，可能偶尔才重要。但当它们重要时，就像氧气一样——至关重要。

<!--en-->
While much of the analytical focus will be on the income statement, proper and thorough analysis of the balance sheet and a company’s accounting are like having a solid foundation in a construction project. They are easy for a casual observer to overlook or take for granted and may matter only once in a while. But when they matter, it’s like access to oxygen—it’s all that matters.

在确定内在价值时，我喜欢从“内部工作”与“外部工作”的概念开始。从事实出发，而不是观点。如果你从观点开始，即使事实与普遍说法相反，也很容易陷入这些观点。从SEC文件、年度报告和行业杂志文章开始——而不是从管理层或同事的观点或卖方报告开始。分析师在研究初期的最大错误就是从查看收益（甚至更糟糕的是，管理层对调整收益的陈述）开始评估。当你查看这些报告的数字时，要记住，你看到的不是完全客观的事实，而是管理团队对这些数字的看法。损益表只是近期事件的快照，这个快照很可能是经过修改的。我想关注过程而非结果，因此从损益表开始是本末倒置。

<!--en-->
In seeking to determine intrinsic values, I like to start with the concept of working inside out versus outside in. Start with facts and not opinions. If you start with opinions, it’s very easy to become wedded to them even when the facts run counter to the popular narrative. Start with SEC filings, annualreports, and trade magazine articles—not with management or colleagues' narratives or sell-side reports. The biggest mistake an analyst can make in the initial stage of their research is to start their assessment by looking at earnings (or even worse, management's presentation of adjusted earnings). When you look at these reported numbers, keep in mind that you're not looking at completely objective facts so much as a management team's perception of them. The income statement is a snapshot of what has recently transpired, and this snapshot may well have been photoshopped. I want to focus on process rather than outcomes, so starting with the income statement is putting the cart before the horse.

当我们从现金流和资产负债表开始时，我们会关注运作过程，了解维持企业运营所需的资源流动情况。我喜欢从宏观和微观经济角度来思考企业，即考虑每美元收入如何通过现金流表、资产负债表以及损益表流转。最终，我们就是通过这些来计算公司的投资资本回报率（ROIC），这通常是衡量企业质量的一个可靠指标。不同时期的财务数据是必要的，但还不够。我喜欢回顾过去10年，观察留存收益、债务及整体资本强度与业务营收增长之间的关系变化。我通常会用杜邦分析法对这10年进行总结，这是杜邦公司推广的一种分析基本绩效的框架。这种技术用于分解股本回报率（ROE）的不同驱动因素，将利润率、资产周转率和资产回报率按年份分解。

<!--en-->
When we start with cash flow and the balance sheet, we focus on the process and understand the flow of the resources required to run the business. I like to think of the business not only in broad terms but also in terms of its unit economics. Think in terms of a dollar of revenue that flows into a business and runs through the cash flow statement, then the balance sheet, and last the income statement. This is ultimately how we derive a company's return on invested capital, which is usually a reliable shorthand for the quality of the business. Financial snapshots from various points in time are necessary but not sufficient. I like to review the last 10 years and examine the changes in retained earnings, debt, and overall capital intensity as compared to the top-line growth of the business itself. I will often summarize this over 10 years in a DuPont analysis, a framework for analyzing fundamental performance popularized by the DuPont Corporation. This technique is used to decompose the different drivers of return on equity (ROE), with profit margin, asset turns, and return on assets broken out by year.

正是通过这种分析，才能看到盈利能力随时间的变化。当公司或行业获得超额回报时，会引发竞争。对这种竞争的回应通常可以在企业的资产负债表中看到。如果一家公司在过去10年中创造了100亿美元的利润，但留存收益保持不变而债务显著增加，那么虽然利润可能有所增长，但资产负债表上不断增长的杠杆率表明，该公司可能必须更加努力才能维持现状。

<!--en-->
It is through this kind of analysis that one can see changes in earning power over time. When companies or industries earn excess returns, it invites competition. The response to that competition can often be seen in a company's balance sheet. If a company generated $10 billion of earnings over a trailing 10-year period, but its retained earnings remained flat while debt increased significantly, earnings may have grown,but the growing leverage on the balance sheet indicates that the company may need to run harder merely to stand still.

资产负债表在识别融资来源和盈利质量方面也非常有用。例如，我们可能会发现一家公司拥有短期浮动利率融资，而非长期固定利率负债。在这种情况下，损益表可能报告出因高风险融资决策而人为夸大的利润，使公司极易受到利率上升的影响。风险较高的资产负债表加上激进的会计做法，可能是灾难的诱因。我发现比较两家非常相似的公司，并对比它们的会计处理方式很有趣。当我比较费用化与资本化、出售收益会计与长期持有抵押贷款证券、收购会计做法以及资产负债表差异等因素时，常常对差异感到惊讶。关键在于，利润是管理层做出的许多假设和选择的结果。储备处理方式、或有估值折现率的选择、假设的养老金回报以及融资方式，都会导致结果被严重高估或低估。

<!--en-->
Balance sheets are also incredibly useful in identifying both funding sources and quality of earnings. We may find, for example, that a company has short-term variable-rate funding rather than longer-term fixed-rate liabilities. In such a situation, the income statement may report earnings that are artificially inflated because of a risky financing decision, making the company extremely vulnerable to rising rates. A risky balance sheet together with aggressive accounting practices can be a recipe for disaster. I find it interesting to take two very similar companies and align their accounting practices. When I compare such factors as their expensing versus capitalizing of expenses, gain on sale accounting versus long-term holding of mortgage securities, acquisition accounting practices, and balance sheet variances, I'm often flabbergasted at the difference. The point is that earnings are a by-product of many assumptions and choices made by management. The treatment of reserves, choice of a discount rate on contingent valuations, assumed pension returns, and method of funding lead to a result that can be either significantly overrated or underrated.

这里可以分析的游戏数量几乎无限。这些激进措施继续影响美国企业的盈利质量，甚至聪明的投资者也常常无法察觉。不要认为任何事情都是理所当然的；如果某件事看起来好得令人难以置信，那很可能就是如此。激进的资产负债表和会计政策通常与保守的管理团队或那些为未来培养人才的人无关。它们通常与向未来借款有关。验证和探索这一点，是我们定性分析的基础。

<!--en-->
The number of games that can be played here is almost limitless. These aggressive measures continue to infect the quality of earnings at American firms and are often undetected even by smart investors. Take nothing for granted; if it seems too good to be true, it probably is. Aggressive balance sheets and accounting are typically not associated with conservative management teams or those planting seeds for future generations. They are typically associated with borrowing from the future. Verifying and exploring this is the basis from which our qualitative analysis flows.

## 微观经济分析

<!--en-->
*Unit Economics*

充分理解资产负债表的运作机制，能帮助我们识别资产负债表上的关键项目，并在微观层面进一步分析，从而了解企业的微观经济特征。就像你可以通过现金流表和资产负债表将每美元收入或成本代入其中一样，你也可以模拟公司的微观经济特征。例如，查看Costco的盈利情况是一回事，分析资产负债表是另一回事，但理解单个门店的微观经济特征则更有意义。虽然公司不会公开每个门店的微观经济数据，但在Costco的情况下，我们可以利用公司披露的信息来估算建店的平均成本。然后，通过估算达到运营收入水平和利润率的大致时间，我们可以估算单个门店的投资回报率。

<!--en-->
Acquiring a thorough understanding of the balance sheet mechanics will allow us to then identify the key items on the balance sheet and drill down into them at a micro level, in order to understand attributes like the unit economics of abusiness. Just as you can drop a dollar of revenue or cost through the cash flow statement and balance sheet, you can do the same in replicating unit economics of the company. For example, looking at the earnings for Costco is one thing, examining the balance sheet another, but understanding the unit economics of an individual store is far more powerful than either of those. While the company doesn't overtly disclose store-by-store unit economics, in the case of Costco we can use company disclosures to triangulate into the average cost to build a store. Then by estimating the approximate time to get to run rate revenues and margins, we can approximate the individual store ROI.

这种计算应该能揭示很多关于整体商业经济状况的信息，但往往无法做到，通常有两个原因。首先，管理团队常常呈现最佳叙事，例如只包括可变成本，而低估维护资本支出。当投资者排除重要的固定成本，并夸大增长资本支出以让业务看起来比实际更好时，项目或单位经济IRR几乎总是被高估了。这直接类似于依赖不太严格的指标EBITDA，而格雷厄姆则注重“所有者收益”。

<!--en-->
This calculation should reveal much about the overall business economics but often does not, typically for one of two reasons. One, management teams often present the best possible narrative, for example, by including only variable costs and understating maintenance capital expenditures. Project or unit economic IRRs are almost always overstated for investors when they exclude important fixed costs and overstate growth capital expenditures to make the business appear better than it is. This is directly akin to relying on the undemanding metric EBITDA compared to Graham's focus on "owner earnings."

第二个原因是，会计记录往往反映前期费用，未能反映达到正常状态所需的持续时间。手机塔行业、一些“剃刀刀片”类企业以及某些零售和软件企业就是如此。美国塔公司曾处于盈亏平衡状态，每座手机塔平均有两名租户，但增加第三名租户后，每座塔的单位经济效益变得非常吸引人，整体投资回报率也令人满意。同样，沃尔玛在增长期间十年多没有产生收益或现金流，但查看门店单位经济效益后，就能了解真实情况，并预见到未来的发展态势。

<!--en-->
The second reason is that the accounting often reflects front-loaded expenses while failing to match the duration required to get to a normalized state. This was the case with the cell tower industry, some "razor-razor blade" businesses, and certain retail and software businesses. American Tower was a breakeven business when it had an average of two tenants per cellphone tower, but adding a third tenant led to extremely attractive unit economics per tower and a compelling overall ROI. Similarly, Walmart did not generate earnings or cash flow for over a decade while they were growing, but a look at the store unit economics led to the true story and foreshadowed what the picture would look like in the future.

目标是超越管理讨论或分析师报告，像所有者一样深入了解业务。只有如此，才能开始把各种信息联系起来。

<!--en-->
The goal is to get past management discussion or analyst reports and drill down into the business as if you were theowner. Then, and only then, can you begin connecting the dots.

## 保持简单原则 原则2：找到优秀的管理团队

<!--en-->
*KEEPING IT SIMPLE PRINCIPLE 2: FIND GOOD MANAGEMENT TEAMS*

优秀管理的重要性几乎被普遍低估，但它却是决定公司内在价值的最关键因素之一。正如格雷厄姆和多德所说：“你不能做出定量推断来容忍不道德的管理；处理这种情况的唯一方法就是避免它。”（第33章）我们必须认识到，企业由个人组成，他们的决策和判断决定了整个企业的运行方式。许多分析师似乎倾向于根据传统市场叙事来评估管理的质量。必须深入探究。

<!--en-->
The importance of good management is almost universally underestimated, yet it is one of the most crucial determinants of a company's intrinsic value. As Graham and Dodd said, "You cannot make a quantitative deduction to allow for an unscrupulous management; the only way to deal with such situations is to avoid them." (Chap. 33) We must recognize that businesses are composed of individuals whose decisions and judgments set the metabolism for the entire enterprise. Many analysts seem inclined to assess the quality of management based on conventional marketplace narratives about a business. One must go deeper.

评估管理业绩的方法包括检查他们的激励因素、了解他们如何安排时间，以及进行传闻研究。请注意，我没有提到听取投资者日演讲或与管理层会面。审查管理团队的业绩需要全面、详细且细致的角度。企业可能需要很长时间才能扭转局面或走向衰退。3年、5年甚至10年前做出的决策可能至今仍影响最终结果。看似表现良好的管理者实际上可能受益于多年前种下的种子。同时，公司运营的经济环境经常发生变化，有时是显著的变化。就像上涨的市场能让任何投资专业人士看起来比实际更聪明一样，持续的利好因素也可能让企业管理团队看起来比实际更聪明。今天的优势可能成为明天的弱点，要么是因为固有的脆弱性，要么因为竞争动态已经改变。例如，外包可以让公司的利润率提高数十年，直到明显出现过度外包的情况，公司的基本能力被削弱。良好的资本配置至关重要；出色的业务和有才华的CEO不足以弥补糟糕的资本配置。太多公司以高于内在价值的价格回购股票，进行破坏价值的并购，或未能根据变化的条件或新出现的机会调整资本配置。资本配置是业绩中必须由潜在投资者审查的最重要部分之一。

<!--en-->
The way to assess management's track record is to examine their incentives, learn how they spend their time, and perform scuttlebutt research. Notice that I did not mention listening to investor day presentations or meeting with management. Examining a management team's track record requires a holistic, detailed, and nuanced perspective. Businesses can take a long time to either turn around or to decay. Decisions made 3, 5, and even 10 years ago are likely still impacting the bottom-line today. A manager who appears to be doing a great job may, in fact, be benefiting from seeds planted many years before. Meanwhile, the economic environment in which a company operates often changes, sometimes dramatically. Just as a rising market can make any investment professional seem smarter than he or she is, persistent tailwinds can also make a corporate management team seem smarter than they are. A strength today can be a weakness tomorrow, either through ingrained fragility or simply because the competitive dynamic has shifted. Outsourcing, for example, can fatten a company's profit margins for decades until it becomes evident that it's been taken too far, and the company's basic competencies have been hollowed out. Good capital allocation is crucial; awonderful business and a talented CEO is not enough to offset poor capital allocation. Too many companies repurchase shares above intrinsic value, pursue value destructive mergers and acquisitions, or fail to adapt their capital allocation in response to changing conditions or emergent opportunities. Capital allocation is one of the most important parts of the track record that must be examined by prospective investors.

## 检查激励因素

<!--en-->
*Examine Incentives*

有人说，看到激励措施就能理解结果。虽然我们知道长期视角对于经营企业至关重要，但常常会出现不理想的激励措施，导致企业过度关注短期利益。一家优秀企业的私人所有者不会担心季度收益、满足市场期望、填满销售渠道、采用激进的会计处理，或保留长期投资以改善报告的短期业绩。为了更好地理解管理层的激励因素，我从代理声明开始，观察年度变化。管理层薪酬和股票期权奖励的依据是否合理？它们是基于持久成就，还是基于可能纯属运气甚至操纵导致的短期股价波动？它们是否奖励资本的实际回报，还是仅仅奖励无利可图的增长？它们是否为首席执行官承担过大风险提供不对称的好处？首席执行官是否经常因“个人原因”出售股票，还是像真正的所有者和受托人一样行事？如果公司是私企，首席执行官的薪酬和激励结构会有何不同？

<!--en-->
It has been said that seeing the incentives will explain the outcome. While we know that a long-term perspective is crucial in running a business, there are often unfortunate incentives to become overly short-term oriented. The private owner of a great business isn't worried about quarterly earnings, meeting market expectations, stuffing sales channels, pursuing aggressive accounting treatments, or withholding long-term investments to improve reported short-term results. To better understand management's incentives, I start with the proxy statement and look for changes year to year. Is the basis for management compensation and stock option awards sensible? Are they being measured for enduring accomplishments or instead for favorable short-term share price fluctuations that could be purely the result of luck or even manipulation? Do they reward actual returns on capital or simply profitless growth? Do they create asymmetric upside for the CEO for taking outsized risks? Is the CEO regularly selling his or her shares for "personal reasons," or are they acting like a true owner and fiduciary? If the company were private, how different would the structure of the CEO's compensation and incentives be?

市场专家可能会过度关注管理层的绝对薪酬水平，而忽视获得该薪酬所需的条件。当薪酬能奖励实现苛刻目标并取得卓越成果时，高绝对薪酬是合理的。

<!--en-->
Market pundits can focus excessively on the absolute level of management compensation rather than the context of what was required to achieve that compensation. High absolute compensation can be warranted when it rewards the achievement of demanding goals and the delivery of exceptional results.

### 了解首席执行官如何分配时间

<!--en-->
*Learn How CEOs Spend Their Time*

时间管理也很重要。我从未遇到过每年在路上数百天、与投资者会面、推广自己或股票的首席执行官——他完全熟悉公司的细节。问问自己：如果这是你的家族企业，你不会希望首席执行官专注于经营企业吗？我希望支持那些注重实质而非追求风格积分的首席执行官。*对首席执行官进行传闻研究*最后，我喜欢与当前和前任高管交谈，他们要么向所考虑的首席执行官汇报过，要么曾收到过该人的汇报。这是获取信息的好方法。我想深入了解人物性格，以获得背景信息。例如，一个强调超效率的激烈执行人员，可能在某个时候变得文化有害，让员工感到恐惧，公司脆弱，团队缺乏坦诚，企业无法应对变化。智力诚实也是管理团队的关键。正如美国理论物理学家理查德·费曼所说：“你不能欺骗自己，而你是最容易被欺骗的人。”¹

<!--en-->
Time management is also important. I have never met a CEO who is on the road for hundreds of days a year, meeting investors and promoting themselves or their stock—who is fully steeped in the details of their company. Ask yourself, if this were your family business, wouldn’t you want your CEO single-mindedly focused on running the business? I want to back CEOs who are focused on substance, not collecting style points.
*Perform Scuttlebutt Research on CEOs*
Finally, I like to speak to current and former executives who have either reported to the CEO under consideration or have had that individual report to them. This provides a good way to triangulate information. I want to go deeply into personalities in order to gain context. For example, an intense executive with an emphasis on hyperefficiency may at some point become culturally toxic, leaving employees afraid, the company fragile, the team less than candid, and the business unable to respond to change. Intellectual honesty is also crucial in a management team. As American theoretical physicist Richard Feynman said, “You must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.”¹

## 保持简单原则 3：找到“正确”的价格

<!--en-->
*KEEPING IT SIMPLE PRINCIPLE 3: FINDING THE “RIGHT” PRICE*

关于定价，传奇投资者兼作家菲利普·A·费舍尔说：“判断一只股票是‘便宜’还是‘贵’的唯一真正标准，不是其当前价格与某个过去价格的比较，无论我们多么习惯那个过去价格，而是该公司的基本面是否明显比当前金融界对该股票的评估更有利或更不利。”²投资者必须深入了解股票背后的公司情况。*研究过程*传闻研究（本章前面也提到过）是菲利普·A·费舍尔使用的术语，意味着投资者要扮演调查记者的角色，尽可能接近真相。我见过许多投资者，他们通过听故事、联系朋友验证故事、参加电话会议、阅读研究报告开始工作，并逐渐形成意见。这种过程的危险在于，它往往基于他人的感知和分析形成意见，而不是自己的。

<!--en-->
About pricing, legendary investor and author Philip A. Fisher said, “The only true test of whether a stock is ‘cheap’ or ‘high’ is not its current price in relation to some former price, no matter how accustomed we may have become to that former price, but whether the company’s fundamentals are significantly more or less favorable than the current financial-community appraisal of that stock.”² Investors must deeply understand the companies behind the stock prices.
*The Research Process*
Scuttlebutt research (also mentioned earlier in the chapter) is a term used by Philip A. Fisher that suggests the investor play the role of an investigative journalist, trying to get as close to the truth as possible. I've seen many investors who start their work on a potential holding by hearing a story, calling some friends to vet the story, listening to some conference calls, reading some research reports, and starting to form an opinion. The danger of this process is that it often leads to the formation of an opinion based on someone else's perception and analysis, rather than your own.

相反，我从公司的年度信函、年度报告、10K和10Q文件以及其他SEC备案文件，以及过去10年的商业杂志文章和新闻稿开始。公司是否过度承诺或交付不足？然后我转向财报电话会议，再次判断公司是否按承诺行事。一旦基于事实而不是故事得到这一情况，就像调查记者一样，我开始描绘现实图景。但仍有问题需要解答，现在是时候进行渠道核查了。

<!--en-->
Instead, I start with the company's annual letters, annual reports, 10Ks and 10Qs, and other SEC filings, as well as trade magazine articles and press releases for the last 10 years. Has the company underpromised and overdelivered or vice versa? Then I work my way to earnings calls, again painting a picture of whether the company does what they say they are going to do. Once I have this picture based on facts instead of a story, then like an investigative reporter, I start to develop a picture of reality. But questions remain to be answered, and it's time to do channel checks.

## 评估竞争优势

<!--en-->
*Assessing Moats*

如何准确评估企业的护城河深度与广度？企业的竞争优势究竟是什么，又有多不可侵犯？显然，长期获得高投资回报率似乎是一种快速简便的方法。但资本主义的“墓地”中遍布着一些企业：它们确实在很长一段时间内获得了高ROIC，但最终还是被竞争所击败——可能是直接被更敏锐的竞争对手击败，也可能是因经济环境变化而失败。投资者必须深入细节，进行信息调研，以判断企业的护城河是否坚固或脆弱。

<!--en-->
How does one go about actually assessing the depth and breadth of a business moat? Precisely what is a company's competitive advantage, and how unassailable is it? Certainly, a long track record of high returns on invested capital seems like a quick and easy way to determine this. But the graveyards of capitalism are littered with companies that did, in fact, earn high ROICs for prolonged periods of time only to ultimately succumb to competition, either directly from a more astute rival or from a changing economic landscape. An investor must get down in the weeds and conduct scuttlebutt research to ascertain whether moats around a business are strong or porous.

## 渠道调查

<!--en-->
*Channel Checks*

渠道调查相当于侦探式调研。它涉及与客户、供应商及前员工交谈。我总是问自己：如果我要将全部净资产投入这家企业，我想知道什么？管理层是否已经在为未来做准备，或者只是在借鉴过去？企业拥有怎样的定价权，公司是否采取了措施来最大化这种权力，还是存在漏洞表明还有进一步增长空间？企业护城河并非固定不变，具有不同特征——品牌、低成本、便利性以及网络效应都构成真正的、但截然不同的护城河。

<!--en-->
Channel checks are the proverbial equivalent of gumshoe research. They entail speaking to customers, suppliers, and former employees. I always ask myself, if I were considering putting 100% of my net worth in this business, what would Iwant to know? Has management been laying the groundwork for the future or borrowing from it? What kind of pricing power does the business have, and has the company taken steps to maximize it, or is there slack in the system that indicates further upside? Business moats are not static and come with different characteristics—brands, low costs, convenience, and network effects all constitute real but very different moats.

这种深入细致的内部调研有多种作用。首先，它帮助我们深入了解企业实际运作方式及护城河质量。其次，它帮助我们通过主要驱动因素理解企业发展趋势，从而判断护城河是缩小还是扩大。第三，它有助于基于事实而非主观意见进行客观分析，消除情绪影响，因为情绪是理性决策的大敌。经过如此广泛的分析，如果购买后股价下跌，我们可能会更安心持有更多股份。第四，它帮助我们理解企业的脆弱性或“反脆弱”特性——这是作者纳什姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布提出的概念，指在其他企业脆弱时反而变得更强的特性。最好的企业就是反脆弱的；即在逆境和波动时期仍能持续繁荣并加深护城河，比如当竞争对手遇到麻烦时，他们的最佳客户和员工也可能面临风险。第五，它帮助我们在多个企业和行业层面建立基础认知，使我们可以随时间逐步整合和扩展知识。这项工作可以设定预期和进展的里程碑，以便随时间调整。第六，广泛调研的方法在形成视角方面具有巨大力量。结合外部知识和视角，以及通过这些调查获得的行业知识，可以放大效果。

<!--en-->
This deep and detailed inside-out research serves multiple purposes. For one, it helps us gain a deep understanding of how the business actually works, as well as the quality of the moat. Two, it helps us understand the trend of the business through the primary levers, which can help us understand whether the moat is shrinking or growing. Three, it facilitates developing a dispassionate analysis based on a foundation of facts versus opinions. This helps eliminate emotions, which are the enemy of rational decision-making. After such extensive analysis, if our security falls in price following our purchase, we will likely feel more comfortable owning more of it. Four, it helps us understand the fragility or “*anti-fragile*” nature of the business, a term coined by author Nassim Nicholas Taleb, to mean one that gets stronger under circumstances where others’ fragility breaks them. The best businesses are anti-fragile; that is, they continue to thrive and even deepen their moats in times of adversity and volatility, such as when competitors get in trouble and their best customers and employees may be up for grabs. Five, it helps us create a base layer of understanding across many businesses and industries, which allows us to triangulate and compound our knowledge over time. This work can create mile markers of expectations and progress that we can compare and as necessary adjust over time. Six, there is great power to a broad-gauged approach in developing perspectives. Coming at this research with outside knowledge and perspective, combined with industry knowledge via these checks, can be a force multiplier.

通过注册文件和渠道调查进行详细研究，能让我们对企业有更清晰的了解。彻底的工作能让投资者自信回答一些重要问题：企业是否有可持续且不断扩大的护城河？未来五年中最薄弱的环节是什么？是否存在隐藏的路径依赖？企业是否有定价权，如何行使？企业有多（反）脆弱，是否能在下一次衰退中保持繁荣？要复制这一企业需要什么条件？五年后，企业是否会拥有更广阔的护城河？

<!--en-->
Performing this detailed research via filings and channel checks enables you to gain comfort in your understanding of the business. Doing thorough work enables an investor toconfidently answer some really important questions: Does the business have a sustainable and/or expanding moat? What are the weakest links over the next five years? Are there hidden path dependencies? Does the business have pricing power, and how has it been exercised? How (anti) fragile is the business, and will it thrive in the next downturn? What would it take to replicate this business? Will the business be in a better position with an even wider moat five years from now?

如果你能自信地回答这些问题，就能明确真正重要的事项，并逐步准确评估内在价值。记住，简单通常更好；投资中，难度并不加分。你可以找到拥有强大、可持续护城河的简单企业，同时避免“强大的管理团队遇到糟糕的企业，企业会胜出”这一说法。这些并不能保证成功，但确实有帮助。

<!--en-->
If you can answer these questions with confidence, you will have clarity on the things that truly matter and be well on your way to accurately assessing intrinsic value. Remember that simple is usually better; in investing, there is no extra credit for degree of difficulty. You can find straightforward businesses with strong, sustainable moats and franchises while avoiding the axiom, “when a strong management team meets a bad business, the business wins.” None of this guarantees a good result, but it certainly helps.

### 确定内在价值

<!--en-->
*Determining Intrinsic Value*

正如沃伦·巴菲特在1989年给伯克希尔哈撒韦股东的信中所说：“以合理价格购买优秀企业，比以昂贵价格购买普通企业要好得多。”

<!--en-->
As Warren Buffett wrote in his 1989 letter to the Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, “It’s far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.”

一家企业的价值等于其永续现金流的现值。这个概念听起来很简单，但计算过程中涉及几个关键变量：使用的折现率以及对永续现金流的评估。估算未来现金流需要确定公司的资本密集度、增长率和管理层的目标分配。几个例子可以说明这些估算的重要性。

<!--en-->
A business is worth the sum of its discounted cash flows in perpetuity. This concept sounds simple enough, but there are a few key variables involved in this calculation: the discount rate to be used and one’s assessment of those cash flows in perpetuity. Estimating future cash flows entails a determination of a company’s capital intensity, its growth rate, and management’s allocation objectives. A couple of examples may demonstrate the power of these estimates.

假设恒定的10%折现率，一家每年增长15%且不需要额外资本的企业，其价值约为当前收益的26倍；而同一家企业若需将大部分甚至全部收益用于再投资以实现该增长，其价值仅约为当前收益的16倍。一家每年增长5%且不需要资本的企业，其价值约为当前收益的14倍；而同一家企业若需将所有收益用于再投资，其价值仅约为当前收益的7倍。30年内复合15%的回报，其价值超过初始投入的87倍；而相同时间内复合5%的回报，其价值仅略低于4.5倍。在这个例子中，复合利率提高三倍（从5%到15%），回报几乎增加二十倍（87倍对比4.5倍）。

<!--en-->
Assuming a constant 10% discount rate, a business that will grow at 15% a year without requiring any additional capital is worth ≈26x its current earnings, whereas the same business growing at 15% but needing to reinvest much or all of its earnings to achieve that growth would be worth only ≈16x. A business that grows at 5% and doesn’t need any capital would be worth ≈14x its current earnings, and the samebusiness needing all of its earnings reinvested would be worth ≈7x. A return of 15% compounded over 30 years is worth over 87x the initial stake, whereas 5% compounded over the same period is worth just under 4.5x. In this example, a threefold increase in the compound rate (from 5% to 15%) leads to an almost twentyfold increase in return (87x vs 4.5x).

这个例子说明了寻找能够长期增长的低资本需求企业的力量。相反，最糟糕的企业实际上是那些增长过程中消耗越来越多资本，但回报无法超过其资本成本的企业。当然，有些企业需要资本才能增长，如铁路公司、金融机构或沃尔玛、亚马逊等零售商，它们对新投入资本的投资回报完全可接受；这种增长资本会随着时间的推移产生经济价值。但价格对于确定回报至关重要。这是格雷厄姆和多德的重要见解：好的企业可能在错误价格下成为糟糕的投资，而普通企业可能在正确价格下成为优秀投资。快速增长的企业可能具有吸引力，但只有处于正确价格时才会如此。近年来，在长期低利率时期，许多投资者基于“收益率加增长率”这一简单且有缺陷的公式，不惜一切代价追求增长。由于价格是关键，还必须通过比较当前价格与公司的内在价值来调整增长率。因为你已经提前支付了较高的价格，所以增长的价值会降低。

<!--en-->
This example illustrates the power of finding capital light businesses that can grow for prolonged periods of time. Conversely, the worst business is actually one that grows and consumes increasing amounts of capital at returns that fail to exceed its cost of capital. There are, of course, businesses that require capital to grow, like a railroad, a financial institution, or retailers like Walmart or Amazon, where the returns on the newly deployed capital are perfectly acceptable; this growth capital will over time produce economic value. But price is paramount in determining returns. This was the great insight of Graham and Dodd. Great businesses can be terrible investments at the wrong price, and an average business can be a great investment at the right price. Fast-growing businesses can be attractive, but only at the right price. In recent years, during long periods of low interest rates, many investors flocked to growth at all costs under the simple and flawed formula of earnings yield plus growth rate. Because price is key, one must additionally adjust the growth rate by comparing today's price relative to a company's intrinsic value. The value of the growth is diminished because you've paid a significant price for it up front.

历史上，市场通常以15倍的收益倍数作为参考，相当于6.7%的收益率。如果你能找到比平均水平更好的企业，且管理也优于平均水平，但成本低于此收益倍数，那很可能是一个好的开始。格雷厄姆和多德称此为安全边际。

<!--en-->
The market has historically traded around a 15x earnings multiple which equates to a 6.7% earnings yield. If you can find a better than average business with better than average management for less than this earnings multiple, it is likely a good start. Graham and Dodd called this a margin of safety.

还有两个考虑因素。一是必须考虑所有者收益，而不是EBITDA，甚至更有害的调整EBITDA（所有者收益定义为未调整的报告收益加上折旧、摊销和其他某些非现金费用，减去维持竞争地位所需的平均年度维护资本支出）。二是需要审视整个企业资本结构。过度负债的公司，即使所有者收益略有变化，其股权估值也会发生巨大变化。不结合完整资本结构来看股票的投资者可能会错过关键要素，因为股权价值是依赖性的，而债务则是永久的。

<!--en-->
There are two other considerations. One is to be sure to consider owner earnings and not EBITDA or even the more pernicious adjusted EBITDA (owner earnings is defined as unadjusted reported earnings plus depreciation, amortization, and certain other noncash charges less average annual maintenance capex required to fully maintain its competitive position). The other is the need to look at the entire corporatecapital structure. Companies that are overlevered can experience large changes in their equity valuations with only the slightest change to owner earnings. Investors who look at a stock without incorporating the complete capitalization picture can miss a key component, because equity values are contingent, while debt is forever.

### 最终产品：什么重要

<!--en-->
*THE FINAL PRODUCT: WHAT MATTERS*

人类不断处理关于世界的复杂信息，将其简化以便理解并纳入上下文。这使我们能够做出决策。我早上出门看我的车，这是一个由金属部件和功能组成的复杂网络，但我只是将其视为“汽车”这一概念，然后开车去工作。很简单，对吧？但出于某种原因，投资者倾向于使概念复杂化。就我而言，我相信按照我描述的过程，我可以最接近现实情况，而内在价值和安全边际在投资中至关重要。例如，我会问自己：该公司真正从事的是什么业务？哪些关键因素将决定其成功？

<!--en-->
Human beings constantly process complex information about the world and simplify it to make sense of it and put it into context. This allows us to make decisions. I go outside in the morning and look at my car, an intricate and complex network of metal parts and functions, but I simply process it as a thing called “car” and drive off to my job. Easy, right? But for whatever reason, investors tend to complexify a concept. In my own case, I am convinced following the process I’ve described allows me to get closest to the reality of what’s in front of me, and the realities of intrinsic values and margins of safety are critical in investing. For example, I ask myself, what business is the company really in? What are the key drivers that will determine its success?

我现在处于独特的位置，同时担任GEICO的CEO和伯克希尔哈撒韦大量资本责任投资的责任人。这两种角色相互影响。作为CEO，我更加意识到CEO面临的关键挑战，即短期需求与长期目标之间的持续平衡。作为CEO，我非常清楚电子表格中固有的危险简化现象。但作为投资者，我始终关注风险和回报。CEO可能会陷入日常细节中；而戴上投资者的帽子，则始终强调底线。

<!--en-->
I’m now in a unique position of serving in two roles: as both the CEO of GEICO, and in my responsibility investing a substantial portfolio pool of capital at Berkshire Hathaway. Each of these roles impacts the other. My CEO role makes me more aware of the key challenges facing a CEO, the constant balancing act between short-term exigencies and long-term imperatives. As a CEO, I’m intensely aware of the dangerous oversimplification inherent in a spreadsheet. But being an investor maintains my focus on both risk and on return. A CEO can be lost in the daily minutiae; wearing an investment hat places a consistent emphasis on the bottom line.

沃伦·巴菲特曾说过：“我是一个更好的投资者，因为我是商人；而我是更好的商人，因为我是投资者。”投资者试图了解公司运营的幕后情况，但往往意识到自己实际上知道得太少。从这一视角来看，可以明白即使进行广泛研究，也只能揭示出关于企业信息的一小部分。投资者必须找到方法应对不确定性和随机性。每天都有决策被做出，有时甚至是在几十年前做出的决策，至今仍影响着每个行业和企业的结果。存在复杂的路径依赖关系，通常连经验丰富的高层管理人员也难以完全理解其中的权衡。完美的信息并不存在；只有置信区间。这当然也是为什么投资中安全边际如此重要的核心原因。如果你以“能知道的信息有限”为前提，当然需要误差范围。你知道得越少，所需的误差范围就越大。[^1591]：1 理查德·P·费曼，《货船崇拜科学》，《加州理工学院杂志》，加州理工学院，1974年6月1日，http://calteches.library.caltech.edu/3043/.

<!--en-->
Warren Buffett has famously stated, “I am a better investor because I am a businessman, and a better businessman because I am an investor.” Investors attempt to look behind the curtain of a company’s operations, but they often realize how little they actually know. From this vantage point, one can appreciate that even extensive research will uncover onlya small fraction of what one can possibly know about a business. Investors must find a way to navigate through uncertainty and randomness. There are decisions being made every day, and sometimes made decades earlier, that are still affecting outcomes today in every business and industry. There are intricate path dependencies that are often too complex even for very skilled upper management to fully understand the trade-offs involved. Perfect information does not exist; there are only confidence intervals. This is, of course, at the heart of why a margin of safety matters so greatly in investing. If you start with the premise that there is only so much one can know, of course you need a margin for error. The less you know, the greater the margin needed.

CHAPTER 27

## 普通股投资理论

<!--en-->
*The Theory of Common-Stock Investment*

在我们的介绍性讨论中，我们阐述了将分析技术应用于投机情境时存在的困难。由于投机因素在普通股中尤为突出，因此对这类问题的分析很可能会得出不明确的结论；即使看起来有结论，也可能产生误导。此时有必要更详细地考虑普通股分析的功能。我们必须从三个现实前提开始。第一，普通股在我们的金融体系中具有基本重要性，吸引了许多人的兴趣；第二，普通股的所有者和购买者通常希望准确了解其价值；第三，即使购买的根本动机只是投机欲望，人性也倾向于将这种不理想的冲动隐藏在看似合理的逻辑和理智的幌子之后。用伏尔泰的话来说，可以说如果没有普通股分析，就必须制造出这种分析。

<!--en-->
IN OUR INTRODUCTORY discussion we set forth the difficulties inherent in efforts to apply the analytical technique to speculative situations. Since the speculative factors bulk particularly large in common stocks, it follows that analysis of such issues is likely to prove inconclusive and unsatisfactory; and even where it appears to be conclusive, there is danger that it may be misleading. At this point it is necessary to consider the function of common-stock analysis in greater detail. We must begin with three realistic premises. The first is that common stocks are of basic importance in our financial scheme and of fascinating interest to many people; the second is that owners and buyers of common stocks are generally anxious to arrive at an intelligent idea of their value; the third is that, even when the underlying motive of purchase is mere speculative greed, human nature desires to conceal this unlovely impulse behind a screen of apparent logic and good sense. To adapt the aphorism of Voltaire, it may be said that if there were no such thing as common-stock analysis, it would be necessary to counterfeit it.

**普通股分析的广泛优点。** 因此我们提出这样一个问题：“普通股分析在多大程度上是有效且真正有价值的工具，在多大程度上只是用于押注商业和股市未来的空洞但不可或缺的仪式？”最终我们会发现答案大致如下：“对于*典型*的普通股——从列表中随机选取的一个案例——无论分析多么精细，都不太可能得出关于其吸引力或实际价值的可靠结论。但在个别案例中，数据可能足以让我们从分析过程中得出相当可靠的结论。”这意味着，分析只有在特殊的普通股情况下才具有积极或科学价值，对于一般普通股而言，它要么被视为对投机判断有些可疑的辅助工具，要么是一种高度虚幻的方法，试图达到无法计算的价值，但无论如何仍需进行计算。

<!--en-->
**Broad Merits of Common-Stock Analysis.** We are thus led to the question: “To what extent is common-stock analysis a valid and truly valuable exercise, and to what extent is it an empty but indispensable ceremony attending the wagering of money on the future of business and of the stock market?” We shall ultimately find the answer to run somewhat as follows: “As far as the *typical* common stock is concerned—an issue picked at random from the list—an analysis, however elaborate, is unlikely to yield a dependable conclusion as to itsattractiveness or its real value. But in individual cases, the exhibit may be such as to permit reasonably confident conclusions to be drawn from the processes of analysis.” It would follow that analysis is of positive or scientific value only in the case of the exceptional common stock, and that for common stocks in general it must be regarded either as a somewhat questionable aid to speculative judgment or as a highly illusory method of aiming at values that defy calculation and that must somehow be calculated none the less.

或许最有效的澄清方式是通过历史方法。这样的调查不仅会揭示普通股分析的变化状况，还会涉及一个密切相关的重要主题，即普通股投资理论。首先我们会遇到一套古老且看似合理的普通股投资原则。随着新条件的出现，我们发现这些原则的有效性受到了限制。它们的不足会导致一种完全不同的普通股选择概念，即所谓“新时代理论”，其表面合理性之下隐藏着不可预知的危害。随着战前理论过时和新时代理论被否定，我们最终必须尝试建立一套逻辑合理且相对可靠的普通股投资原则。

<!--en-->
Perhaps the most effective way of clarifying the subject is through the historical approach. Such a survey will throw light not only upon the changing status of common-stock analysis but also upon a closely related subject of major importance, *viz.*, the theory of common-stock investment. We shall encounter at first a set of old established and seemingly logical principles for common-stock investment. Through the advent of new conditions, we shall find the validity of these principles impaired. Their insufficiency will give rise to an entirely different concept of common-stock selection, the so-called “new-era theory,” which beneath its superficial plausibility will hold possibilities of untold mischief in store. With the prewar theory obsolete and the new-era theory exploded, we must finally make the attempt to establish a new set of logically sound and reasonably dependable principles of commonstock investment.

**普通股分析的历史。** 首先来看普通股*分析*的历史，我们会发现过去30年间存在两个相互矛盾的因素。一方面，作为一类股票，普通股的*投资价值*有所提升，这主要得益于：数量增加、盈利显著、持续派息以及财务状况良好。伴随这一进步的是公司报告的频率和完整性大幅提升，为公众和证券分析师提供了大量统计数据。最后，一种令人印象深刻的理论被提出，强调普通股作为长期投资的优势。但在普通股需求达到高峰的1927年至1929年期间，股票购买者使用的*估值基础*越来越偏离证券分析的实际方法和技术，更多地关注潜在性和预测因素。此外，工业公司和企业集团事务中不稳定性的加剧，普遍降低了债券的投资质量，当然也进一步阻碍了普通股真正投资质量的维持。

<!--en-->
**History of Common-Stock Analysis.** Turning first to the history of commonstock *analysis*, we shall find that two conflicting factors have been at work during the past 30 years. On the one hand there has been an increase in the *investment prestige* of common stocks as a class, due chiefly to the enlarged number that have shown substantial earnings, continued dividends, and a strong financial condition. Accompanying this progress was a considerable advance in the frequency and adequacy of corporate statements, thus supplying the public and the securities analyst with a wealth of statistical data. Finally, an impressive theory was constructed asserting the preeminence of common stocks as long-term investments. But at the time that the interest incommon stocks reached its height, in the period between 1927 and 1929, the *basis of valuation* employed by the stock-buying public departed more and more from the factual approach and technique of security analysis and concerned itself increasingly with the elements of potentiality and prophecy. Moreover, the heightened instability in the affairs of industrial companies and groups of enterprises, which has undermined the investment quality of bonds in general, has of course been still more hostile to the maintenance of true investment quality in common stocks.

**受两种不稳定性影响的分析。** 普通股分析如何受到这两种发展影响（1）有形资产的不稳定性；（2）无形资产的主导地位），可以通过对比1920年之前及较近时期的特定普通股来更好地理解。让我们考虑四个典型例子：宾夕法尼亚铁路公司；阿奇森、托皮卡和圣塔菲铁路公司；国家饼干公司；美国罐头公司。

<!--en-->
**Analysis Vitiated by Two Types of Instability.** The extent to which common-stock analysis has been vitiated by these two developments, (1) the instability of tangibles and (2) the dominant importance of intangibles, may be better realized by a contrast of specific common stocks prior to 1920 and in more recent times. Let us consider four typical examples: Pennsylvania Railroad; Atchison, Topeka, and Santa Fe Railway; National Biscuit; and American Can.

* 截至6月30日的财政年度。美国罐头公司是战前投机性股票的典型代表。它因三个充分合理的原因属于投机股：（1）不派息；（2）盈利少且不稳定；（3）发行规模被“稀释”，即其披露的价值中大部分并非实际业务投资。相比之下，宾夕法尼亚、阿奇森和国家饼干被视为投资型普通股——同样有三个充分合理的原因：（1）持续派息情况良好；（2）盈利相对稳定，平均超过派息额；（3）每1美元股票对应1美元或更多实际业务投资。

<!--en-->
* Fiscal years ended June 30.
American Can was a typical example of a prewar speculative stock. It was speculative for three good and sufficient reasons: (1) It paid no dividend; (2) its earnings were small and irregular; (3) the issue was “watered,” i.e., a substantial part of its stated value represented no actual investment in the business. By contrast, Pennsylvania, Atchison, and National Biscuit were regarded as investment common stocks—also for three good and sufficient reasons: (1) They showed a satisfactory record of continued dividends; (2) the earnings were reasonably stable and averaged substantially in excess of the dividends paid; and (3) eachdollar of stock was backed by a dollar or more of actual investment in the business.

If we study the range of market price of these issues during the decade preceding the World War (or the 1909–1918 period for National Biscuit), we note that American Can fluctuated widely from year to year in the fashion regularly associated with speculative media but that Pennsylvania,Atchison, and National Biscuit showed much narrower variations and evidently tended to oscillate about a base price (i.e., 97 for Atchison, 64 for Pennsylvania, and 120 for National Biscuit) that seemed to represent a well-defined view of their investment or intrinsic value.

## 战前对普通股投资的观念。

<!--en-->
*Prewar Conception of Investment in Common Stocks.*

因此，战前分析与投资之间的关系，以及价格变动与投机行为的关系可以如下描述：普通股投资仅限于那些股息稳定且收益相当稳定的股票；这些股票又被认为能维持相对稳定的市场水平。分析的主要功能是寻找图中的“弱点”。如果收益表述不清晰；如果资产负债表显示当前状况不佳；或者债务增长过快；如果工厂维护不当；如果有危险的新的竞争者威胁到公司；或者公司在行业中的地位正在下降；如果管理层状况恶化或可能进一步恶化；如果有理由担心整个行业的未来——这些缺陷或任何其他问题都可能足以让谨慎投资者拒绝购买该股票。

<!--en-->
Hence the prewar relationship between analysis and investment on the one hand and price changes and speculation on the other may be set forth as follows: Investment in common stocks was confined to those showing stable dividends and fairly stable earnings; and such issues in turnwere expected to maintain a fairly stable market level. The function of analysis was primarily to search for elements of *weakness* in the picture. If the earnings were not properly stated; if the balance sheet revealed a poor current position, or the funded debt was growing too rapidly; if the physical plant was not properly maintained; if dangerous new competition was threatening, or if the company was losing ground in the industry; if the management was deteriorating or was likely to change for the worse; if there was reason to fear for the future of the industry as a whole—any of these defects or some other one might be sufficient to condemn the issue from the standpoint of the cautious investor.

从积极方面看，分析的重点是找出符合投资所有要求，*并且*未来有最佳发展潜力的股票。这一过程主要是比较投资类别中类似的股票，例如支付股息的西北铁路集团。主要关注过去几年的表现，特别是平均收益与价格的关系、收益的稳定性和趋势。在较小程度上，分析师还会研究未来，选择可能实现最快增长的行业或单个公司。

<!--en-->
On the positive side, analysis was concerned with finding those issues which met all the requirements of investment and *in addition* offered the best chance for future enhancement. The process was largely a matter of comparing similar issues in the investment class, *e.g.*, the group of dividend-paying Northwestern railroads. Chief emphasis would be laid upon the relative showing for past years, in particular the average earnings in relation to price and the stability and the trend of earnings. To a lesser extent, the analyst sought to look into the future and to select the industries or the individual companies that were likely to show the most rapid growth.

*以未来前景为重点的投机行为。* 战前时期，人们认为当*重点放在对未来预期上*，而不是过去已取得的成绩时，就形成了投机态度。词源上，“投机”意味着展望未来；投资与“既得利益”相关——即过去已根深蒂固的财产权和价值。未来不确定，因此属于投机；过去已知，因此具有安全性。以1910年购买American Can普通股的人为例，他可能认为股价会上涨或“上涨”，收益会增加，很快会派发股息，或者注定会发展成国家最强大的工业企业之一。从战前的视角来看，虽然其中一些理由可能比其他理由更合理或值得称赞，但每一个都构成了购买的*投机*动机。

<!--en-->
*Speculation Characterized by Emphasis on Future Prospects.* In the prewar period it was the well-considered view that when *prime emphasis* was laid upon what was expected of the future, instead of what had been accomplished in the past, a speculative attitude was thereby taken. Speculation, in its etymology, meant looking forward; investment was allied to “vested interests”—to property rights and values taking root in the *past*. The future was uncertain, therefore speculative; the past was known, therefore the source of safety. Let us consider a buyer of American Can common in 1910. He may have bought it believing that its price was going to advance or be “put up” or that its earnings were going to increase or that it was soon going to pay a dividend or possibly that it was destined to develop into one of the country’s strongest industrials. From the prewar standpoint, although one of these reasons may have been moreintelligent or creditable than another, each of them constituted a *speculative* motive for the purchase.

*普通股投资技术与债券投资类似。* 显然，普通股投资技术与债券投资技术非常相似。普通股投资者也希望拥有稳定的业务，且收益超过股息需求。自然，他不得不接受比债券更小的安全边际，但这一劣势被更高的收益回报（优质普通股的标准为6%，高等级债券为4½%）和如果业务持续繁荣则有可能获得更高股息的机会所抵消；在他眼中，利润的可能性通常是最不重要的。普通股投资者可能认为自己的处境与第二级债券购买者没有太大区别；本质上，他的投资相当于牺牲一定程度的安全性以换取更高的收益。1904-1913年期间宾夕法尼亚和Atchison的例子可以具体证实上述描述。

<!--en-->
*Technique of Investing in Common Stocks Resembled That for Bonds.* Evidently there was a close similarity between the technique of investing in common stocks and that of investing in bonds. The common-stock investor, also, wanted a stable business and one showing an adequate margin of earnings over dividend requirements. Naturally he had to content himself with a smaller margin of safety than he would demand of a bond, a disadvantage that was offset by a larger income return (6% was standard on a good common stock compared with 4½% on a high-grade bond), by the chance of an increased dividend if the business continued to prosper, and—generally of least importance in his eyes—by the possibility of a profit. A common-stock investor was likely to consider himself as in no very different position from that of a purchaser of second-grade bonds; essentially his venture amounted to sacrificing a certain *degree* of safety in return for larger income. The Pennsylvania and Atchison examples during the 1904–1913 decade will supply specific confirmation of the foregoing description.

*购买普通股被视为参与企业投资。* 关于战前普通股投资者的态度，另一种有用的视角是从参与私人企业的角度来思考。典型的普通股投资者是商人，对他来说，以与评估自己企业相同的方式评估任何企业似乎很合理。这意味着他至少会像关注自身企业的盈利记录一样关注股票背后的资产价值。必须记住，私人企业始终主要依据其财务报表中显示的“净资产值”来评估。打算购买私人企业合伙关系或股份的人，通常会从该股份在“账本”上显示的价值开始考虑，然后判断其记录和前景是否足够吸引人。当然，私人企业的股份可以按与其资产价值比例不同的价格出售；但账面价值始终是计算的起点，交易最终是根据与账面价值相比的溢价或折价来进行的。

<!--en-->
*Buying Common Stocks Viewed as Taking a Share in a Business.* Another useful approach to the attitude of the prewar common-stock investor is from the standpoint of taking an interest in a private business. The typical common-stock investor was a business man, and it seemed sensible to him to value any corporate enterprise in much the same manner as he would value his own business. This meant that he gave at least as much attention to the asset values behind the shares as he did to their earnings records. It is essential to bear in mind the fact that a private business has always been valued primarily on the basis of the “net worth” as shown by its statement. A man contemplating the purchase of a partnership or stock interest in a private undertaking will always start with the value of that interest as shown “on the books,” *i.e.*, the balance sheet, and will then consider whether or not the record and prospects are good enough to make such a commitment attractive. An interest in a private business may of course be sold for more or less than its proportionate assetvalue; but the book value is still invariably the starting point of the calculation, and the deal is finally made and viewed in terms of the premium or discount from book value involved.

总的来说，过去在投资购买可交易普通股时也采用同样的态度。第一个参考点是面值，大概代表最初投入企业的现金或财产金额；第二个基本数字是账面价值，即面值加上累计盈余的分配价值。因此，在考虑普通股时，投资者会问自己：“这个股票是在账面价值之上有溢价、还是低于账面价值有折扣，即市场价格所显示的那种情况，值得购买？”“水分过重的股票”常被指责为欺骗投资者，他们被股票背后真实资产价值的虚假报表所误导。因此，证券分析的一个保护功能就是确认公司资产负债表上显示的固定资产价值是否真实反映了这些资产的实际成本或合理价值。

<!--en-->
Broadly speaking, the same attitude was formerly taken in an investment purchase of a marketable common stock. The first point of departure was the par value, presumably representing the amount of cash or property originally paid into the business; the second basal figure was the book value, representing the par value plus a ratable interest in the accumulated surplus. Hence in considering a common stock, investors asked themselves: "Is this issue a desirable purchase at the premium above book value, or the discount below book value, represented by the market price?" "Watered stock" was repeatedly inveighed against as a deception practiced upon the stock-buying public, who were misled by a fictitious statement of the asset values existing behind the shares. Hence one of the protective functions of security analysis was to discover whether or not the value of the fixed assets, as stated on the balance sheet of a company, fairly represented the actual cost or reasonable worth of the properties.

*基于三重概念的普通股投资。* 可见，过去的普通股投资基于以下三重概念：（1）合适的、稳定的股息回报；（2）稳定且充足的盈利记录；（3）有满意的有形资产支撑。这三个要素都可以作为研究对象进行仔细分析，从单独角度以及与其他同类股票比较来看。由其他观点驱动的普通股投资被归类为投机行为，认为它们无法通过认真分析得到支持。

<!--en-->
*Investment in Common Stocks Based on Threefold Concept.* We thus see that investment in common stocks was formerly based upon the threefold concept of: (1) a suitable and established dividend return, (2) a stable and adequate earnings record, and (3) a satisfactory backing of tangible assets. Each of these three elements could be made the subject of careful analytical study, viewing the issue both by itself and in comparison with others of its class. Common-stock commitments motivated by any other viewpoint were characterized as speculative, and it was not expected that they should be justified by a serious analysis.

### 新时代理论

<!--en-->
*THE NEW-ERA THEORY*

战后时期，特别是在1929年牛市后期，公众对普通股的投资价值有了完全不同的看法。上述三个要素中的两个几乎失去了所有重要性，第三个——盈利记录——则呈现出全新的面貌。新的理论或原则可以用一句话概括：“普通股的价值完全取决于它未来能创造多少收益。”

<!--en-->
During the postwar period, and particularly during the latter stage of the bull market culminating in 1929, the public acquired a completely different attitude towards the investment merits of common stocks. Two of the three elements above stated lost nearly all their significance, and thethird, the earnings record, took on an entirely novel complexion. The new theory or principle may be summed up in the sentence: "The value of a common stock depends entirely upon what it will earn in the future."

由此得出以下推论：

<!--en-->
From this dictum the following corollaries were drawn:

1. 股息率应对价值有轻微影响。
2. 由于资产与盈利能力之间似乎没有关联，因此资产价值完全不再重要。
3. 过去的收益数据之所以重要，仅在于它们表明未来可能出现的收益*变化*。这种普通股投资理念上的彻底变革，实际上并未得到股票购买者的充分认识，金融观察者也仅进行了最表面的关注。必须努力全面理解这种转变后的观点真正含义。为此，我们需要从三个角度进行思考：其原因、后果及其逻辑合理性。**这种转变观点的原因。**为何*投资*大众将注意力从股息、资产价值以及平均收益转向几乎完全关注收益*趋势*，即未来预期的收入*变化*？答案首先是，过去的记录证明无法作为投资的可靠依据；其次，未来带来的回报变得难以抗拒且极具吸引力。新时代的概念首先源于旧有标准的过时。在上一代人中，经济变化的节奏加快到如此程度，以至于"长期存在"这一事实已不再像过去那样能保证*稳定性*。享受了十年之久的繁荣的企业，在几年内就陷入了破产状态。其他原本规模小或经营不成功、信誉存疑的企业，同样迅速获得了主导地位、可观的收益和最高评级。投资兴趣主要集中的群体——即铁路公司，明显未能参与国家财富与收入的扩张，并多次表现出明显的衰退迹象。街道铁路作为1914年之前的重要投资工具，由于新型运输机构的出现，迅速失去了大部分价值。电力和燃气公司在这段时期走势不稳定，因为战争及战后通货膨胀对它们不利，它们的显著增长也是相对较新的现象。工业公司的历史充满了剧烈的变化，繁荣带来的好处分配极不均匀且短暂，导致既出现最意外的失败，也出现最令人瞩目的成功。面对如此的不稳定局面，普通股投资的三种基础显然完全不够用了。过去的收益和股息再也不能单独被视为未来收益和股息的指标。此外，这些未来的收益并不受实际业务投资金额——即资产价值——的控制，而完全取决于有利的产业地位以及有能力的或幸运的管理政策。在许多公司破产案例中，流动资产减少，固定资产几乎变得毫无价值。由于破产时资产与收益之间、资产与可变现价值之间缺乏任何联系，金融评论家和公众对曾经重要的"净资产"或"账面价值"问题关注越来越少；可以说，到1929年，账面价值实际上已不再成为决定证券吸引力的重要因素。一个重要的佐证是，"稀释股票"这一曾经备受关注的术语现在已被遗忘。**注意力转向收益趋势。**因此，基于过去记录和实际事实的战前投资方法已经过时并被抛弃。还能找到替代方案吗？一个新的概念被赋予核心地位——即收益*趋势*。 过去的重要性仅在于它能指示未来可能发展的方向。利润的持续增长表明公司正在发展壮大，并预示着未来将取得比目前更好的业绩。相反，如果在经济繁荣时期利润出现下降甚至停滞不前，那么未来前景必然不容乐观，这样的投资显然应当避免。

<!--en-->
1. That the dividend rate should have slight bearing upon the value.
2. That since no relationship apparently existed between assets and earning power, the asset value was entirely devoid of importance.
3. That past earnings were significant only to the extent that they indicated what *changes* in the earnings were likely to take place in the future.
This complete revolution in the philosophy of common-stock investment took place virtually without realization by the stock-buying public and with only the most superficial recognition by financial observers. An effort must be made to reach a thorough comprehension of what this changed viewpoint really signifies. To do so we must consider it from three angles: its causes, its consequences and its logical validity.
**Causes for This Changed Viewpoint.** Why did the *investing* public turn its attention from dividends, from asset values, and from average earnings to transfer it almost exclusively to the earnings *trend*, i.e., to the *changes* in earnings expected in the future? The answer was, first, that the records of the past were proving an undependable guide to investment; and, second, that the rewards offered by the future had become irresistible alluring.
The new-era concepts had their root first of all in the obsolescence of the old-established standards. During the last generation the tempo of economic change has been speeded up to such a degree that the fact of being *long established* has ceased to be, as once it was, a warranty of *stability*. Corporations enjoying decade-long prosperity have been precipitated into insolvency within a few years. Other enterprises, which had been small or unsuccessful or indoubtful repute, have just as quickly acquired dominant size, impressive earnings, and the highest rating. The major group upon which investment interest was chiefly concentrated, *viz.*, the railroads, failed signally to participate in the expansion of national wealth and income and showed repeated signs of definite retrogression. The street railways, another important medium of investment prior to 1914, rapidly lost the greater portion of their value as the result of the development of new transportation agencies. The electric and gas companies followed an irregular course during this period, since they were harmed rather than helped by the war and postwar inflation, and their impressive growth was a relatively recent phenomenon. The history of industrial companies was a hodge-podge of violent changes, in which the benefits of prosperity were so unequally and so impermanently distributed as to bring about the most unexpected failures alongside of the most dazzling successes.
In the face of all this instability it was inevitable that the threefold basis of common-stock investment should prove totally inadequate. Past earnings and dividends could no longer be considered, in themselves, an index of future earnings and dividends. Furthermore, these future earnings showed no tendency whatever to be controlled by the amount of the actual investment in the business—the asset values—but instead depended entirely upon a favorable industrial position and upon capable or fortunate managerial policies. In numerous cases of receivership, the current assets dwindled, and the fixed assets proved almost worthless. Because of this absence of any connection between both assets and earnings and between assets and realizable values in bankruptcy, less and less attention came to be paid either by financial writers or by the general public to the formerly important question of “net worth,” or “book value”; and it may be said that by 1929 book value had practically disappeared as an element in determining the attractiveness of a security issue. It is a significant confirmation of this point that “watered stock,” once so burning an issue, is now a forgotten phrase.
**Attention Shifted to the Trend of Earnings.** Thus the prewar approach to investment, based upon past records and tangiblefacts, became outworn and was discarded. Could anything be put in its place? A new conception was given central importance—that of *trend of earnings*. The past was important only in so far as it showed the direction in which the future could be expected to move. A continuous increase in profits proved that the company was on the upgrade and promised still better results in the future than had been accomplished to date. Conversely, if the earnings had declined or even remained stationary during a prosperous period, the future must be thought unpromising, and the issue was certainly to be avoided.

## 普通股作为长期投资的学说。

<!--en-->
*The Common-Stocks-as-Long-Term-Investments Doctrine.*

随着关于普通股选择依据的概念出现，还有一种相关理论认为，普通股是最具盈利潜力、因此最适合进行长期投资的投资工具。这一理论基于大量研究，表明多年来，多样化持有的普通股在一段时间内的价值持续上升。数据表明，这种多样化的普通股投资不仅能带来更高的收益回报，还能比购买标准债券获得更大的本金收益。

<!--en-->
Along with this idea as to what constituted the basis for common-stock selection emerged a companion theory that common stocks represented the most profitable and therefore the most desirable media for long-term investment. This gospel was based upon a certain amount of research, showing that diversified lists of common stocks had regularly increased in value over stated intervals of time for many years past. The figures indicated that such diversified common-stock holdings yielded both a higher income return and a greater principal profit than purchases of standard bonds.

这两种概念的结合构成了1927–1929年股市运行的“投资理论”。该理论进一步强化了之前《新时代理论》中提出的原则，具体如下：

<!--en-->
The combination of these two ideas supplied the “investment theory” upon which the 1927–1929 stock market proceeded. Amplifying the principle stated found in “The New-Era Theory” earlier, the theory ran as follows:

1. “普通股的价值取决于其未来能带来的收益。”
2. “好的普通股是那些表现出持续上涨收益趋势的。”
3. “好的普通股将证明是稳健且有利可图的投资。”这些陈述听起来无懈可击且合理。然而，它们隐藏了两个理论上的缺陷，可能导致不可预见的后果。第一个缺陷是它们取消了投资和投机之间的基本区别。第二个缺陷是它们在确定股票是否值得购买时，忽视了股票的*价格*。**新时代投资等同于繁荣前的投机。**稍加思考就会发现，公众和投资信托所进行的“新时代投资”，实际上与繁荣前人们所理解的投机几乎相同。这种“投资”意味着购买普通股而非债券，强调增加本金而非收益，并强调未来的变化而非已确立的过去事实。可以说，新时代投资不过是旧式投机的延续，仅限于那些收益趋势令人满意的通俗股。历史上最大规模股市繁荣背后的新概念，似乎只是老套讽刺格言的伪装：“投资就是成功的投机。”**无论价格如何，股票都被视为有吸引力。**认为普通股的可取性完全独立于其价格的观点似乎极其荒谬。然而，新时代理论直接推导出这一论点。如果一种公用事业股的售价是其*最高*记录收益的35倍，而不是繁荣前标准的10倍平均收益，那么得出的结论不是该股票现在太贵，而是价值标准已经提高。新时代不再以既定价值标准来评判市场价格，而是以市场价格作为价值标准。因此，不仅股票*可能*出售的价格上限消失了，甚至股票*应*出售的价格上限也消失了。这种荒谬的逻辑实际上导致人们以每股100美元的价格购买每股收益为2.50美元的普通股。同样的逻辑可以支持以200美元、1000美元或任何可想象的价格购买这些股票。这一原则的一个诱人推论是：在股市赚钱现在变得非常简单。只需购买“好”的股票，无论价格如何，然后让市场自然发展。这种学说的结果必然是悲剧性的。无数人问自己：“当在华尔街不工作就能获利时，为什么还要工作？”随后从商业领域向金融区的迁移，就像著名的金矿热到克朗代克地区一样，只不过黄金被带到华尔街，而不是从那里获取。
1. 在经济萧条、价格低的时候买入，在繁荣、价格高的时候卖出。
2. 在多个领域、可能是在多个国家进行多样化投资。
3. 通过全面、专业的统计调查，发现并获取被低估的个股。这些传统原则在投资信托体系中迅速、完全消失，这是那个时代的诸多奇迹之一。在经济萧条时期进行投资显然不适用。投资信托存在一个致命缺陷：它们只能在经济繁荣时期成立，因此实际上被迫在牛市期间做出初始承诺。全球地理分布的理念从未对那些地方观念较强的美国人产生强大吸引力（他们在这方面可能确实正确），而国内情况比国外好得多，因此这一理念被普遍放弃。*投资信托放弃了分析工作*。但最矛盾的是，早期就放弃了用于指导投资信托政策的研究与分析。然而，由于这些金融机构的存在依赖于这种新哲学，它们紧密遵循它自然且可能是合理的。根据这一准则，投资变得如此简单，研究不再必要，复杂的统计数据也成了负担。投资过程仅包括寻找盈利增长明显的公司，然后无论价格如何都购买其股票。因此，正确的政策是只购买其他人正在购买的股票——一份高受欢迎但价格极高的股票精选名单，被称为“蓝筹股”。寻找被低估和忽视的股票的原始理念完全消失了。投资信托实际上声称，他们的投资组合仅包含活跃和标准（即最受欢迎、价格最高）普通股。稍加夸张地说，在这种便利的投资方式下，一千万美元的投资信托事务可由一名每周三十美元的职员通过智慧、培训和实际工作来管理。普通民众被说服将资金委托给投资专家的高超技能——作为丰厚报酬——很快被告知，信托会小心只购买普通民众自己正在购买的股票。*所提出的理由*。非理性无法继续发展；但重要的是要注意，大规模投机只能在这种非逻辑和不现实的环境中繁荣发展。不过，大规模投机者的自我欺骗必然有某种理由。这通常是一种概括性陈述，在其适用范围内足够合理，但被扭曲以适应投机狂热。在房地产繁荣时期，“理由”通常基于土地价值的固有持久性和增长。在新时代牛市中，“理性”基础是多样化普通股持有所显示的长期改善记录。**用于支持不合理结论的合理前提**。然而，这种历史事实的新时代应用中存在一个根本性的谬误。即使从对那本小而简略的书籍中所含数据的表面审查来看，这一点也很明显。这本书名为《普通股作为长期投资》，作者是埃德加·劳伦斯·史密斯，于1924年出版。¹研究表明，普通股具有随时间增值的趋势，原因很简单：它们的收益超过分红金额，因此再投资收益增加了其价值。在一个典型的案例中，公司平均获得9%的收益，支付6%的分红，并增加3%的盈余。在良好的管理和合理运气下，股票的公允价值将以每年3%的复合率高于账面价值。 这当然是一种理论上的模式，而非标准模式，但许多结果低于“正常水平”的情况，可能可以通过更快增长的例子来抵消。因此，普通股票对长期投资的吸引力本质上在于：它们的收益超过其成本对应的债券利率。通常来说，如果一只股票收益为10美元，售价达到100美元，情况就是如此。但当价格相对于收益大幅提升时，这种优势就消失了，*随之消失的还有投资购买普通股票的整个理论依据*。例如，在1929年，投资者以每股200美元的价格购买一只收益为8美元的股票，他们购买的是一种收益能力并不高于债券利率、且缺乏先前保护作用的股票。因此，用过去普通股票的表现作为定价为收益20到40倍的理由，新时代的理论家们从合理的前提开始，却将其扭曲成完全不可靠的结论。实际上，他们急于利用普通股票本身的固有吸引力，导致了与产生这种吸引力的条件截然不同的局面，即收益平均约为市场价的10%。正如我们所见，埃德加·劳伦斯·史密斯合理地解释了普通股票价值的增长源于剩余收益的再投资导致的资产价值提升。矛盾的是，利用这一发现的新时代理论，却不愿给予所支持的股票背后的资产价值丝毫重视。此外，史密斯结论的有效性必然基于一个假设，即普通股票未来会像过去一样表现。然而，新时代理论忽略了公司的过去收益，除非这些收益被视为指向未来的*趋势*。*展示收益趋势的例子*。以三家公司为例：*每股收益*

<!--en-->
1. “The value of a common stock depends on what it can earn in the future.”
2. “Good common stocks are those which have shown a rising trend of earnings.”
3. “Good common stocks will prove sound and profitable investments.”
These statements sound innocent and plausible. Yet they concealed two theoretical weaknesses that could and did result in untold mischief. The first of these defects was that they abolished the fundamental distinctions between investment and speculation. The second was that they ignored the *price* ofa stock in determining whether or not it was a desirable purchase.
**New-Era Investment Equivalent to Prewar Speculation.** A moment's thought will show that “new-era investment,” as practiced by the public and the investment trusts, was almost identical with speculation as popularly defined in preboom days. Such “investment” meant buying common stocks instead of bonds, emphasizing enhancement of principal instead of income, and stressing the changes of the future instead of the facts of the established past. It would not be inaccurate to state that new-era investment was simply old-style speculation confined to common stocks with a satisfactory trend of earnings. The impressive new concept underlying the greatest stock-market boom in history appears to be no more than a thinly disguised version of the old cynical epigram: “Investment is successful speculation.”
**Stocks Regarded as Attractive Irrespective of Their Prices.** The notion that the desirability of a common stock was entirely independent of its price seems incredibly absurd. Yet the new-era theory led directly to this thesis. If a public-utility stock was selling at 35 times its *maximum* recorded earnings, instead of 10 times its *average* earnings, which was the preboom standard, the conclusion to be drawn was not that the stock was now too high but merely that the standard of value had been raised. Instead of judging the market price by established standards of value, the new era based its standards of value upon the market price. Hence all upper limits disappeared, not only upon the price at which a stock *could* sell but even upon the price at which it would *deserve* to sell. This fantastic reasoning actually led to the purchase at $100 per share of common stocks earning $2.50 per share. The identical reasoning would support the purchase of these same shares at $200, at $1,000, or at any conceivable price.
An alluring corollary of this principle was that making money in the stock market was now the easiest thing in the world. It was only necessary to buy “good” stocks, regardless of price, and then to let nature take her upward course. The results of such a doctrine could not fail to be tragic. Countless people asked themselves, “Why work for a living when afortune can be made in Wall Street without working?” The ensuing migration from business into the financial district resembled the famous gold rush to the Klondike, except that gold was brought to Wall Street instead of taken from it.
**Investment Trusts Adopted This New Doctrine.** An ironical sidelight is thrown on this 1928–1929 theory by the practice of the investment trusts. These were formed for the purpose of giving the untrained public the benefit of expert administration of its funds—a plausible idea and one that had been working reasonably well in England. The earliest American investment trusts laid considerable emphasis upon certain time-tried principles of successful investment, which they were much better qualified to follow than the typical individual. The most important of these principles were:
1. To buy in times of depression and low prices and to sell out in times of prosperity and high prices.
2. To diversify holdings in many fields and probably in many countries.
3. To discover and acquire undervalued individual securities as the result of comprehensive and expert statistical investigations.
The rapidity and completeness with which these traditional principles disappeared from investment-trust technique is one of the many marvels of the period. The idea of buying in times of depression was obviously inapplicable. It suffered from the fatal weakness that investment trusts could be organized only in good times, so that they were virtually compelled to make their initial commitments in bull markets. The idea of world-wide geographical distribution had never exerted a powerful appeal upon the provincially minded Americans (who possibly were right in this respect), and with things going so much better here than abroad this principle was dropped by common consent.
*Analysis Abandoned by Investment Trusts.* But most paradoxical was the early abandonment of research and analysis in guiding investment-trust policies. However, since these financial institutions owed their existence to the new-eraphilosophy, it was natural and perhaps only just that they should adhere closely to it. Under its canons investment had now become so beautifully simple that research was unnecessary and elaborate statistical data a mere incumbrance. The investment process consisted merely of finding prominent companies with a rising trend of earnings and then buying their shares regardless of price. Hence the sound policy was to buy only what every one else was buying—a select list of highly popular and exceedingly expensive issues, appropriately known as the “blue chips.” The original idea of searching for the undervalued and neglected issues dropped completely out of sight. Investment trusts actually boasted that their portfolios consisted exclusively of the active and standard (i.e., the most popular and highest priced) common stocks. With but slight exaggeration, it might be asserted that under this convenient technique of investment, the affairs of a ten-million-dollar investment trust could be administered by the intelligence, the training and the actual labors of a single thirty-dollar-a-week clerk.
The man in the street, having been urged to entrust his funds to the superior skill of investment experts—for substantial compensation—was soon reassuringly told that the trusts would be careful to buy nothing except what the man in the street was buying himself.
*The Justification Offered.* Irrationality could go no further; yet it is important to note that mass speculation can flourish only in such an atmosphere of illogic and unreality. The self-deception of the mass speculator must, however, have its element of justification. This is usually some generalized statement, sound enough within its proper field, but twisted to fit the speculative mania. In real estate booms, the “reasoning” is usually based upon the inherent permanence and growth of land values. In the new-era bull market, the “rational” basis was the record of long-term improvement shown by diversified common-stock holdings.
**A Sound Premise Used to Support an Unsound Conclusion.** There was, however, a radical fallacy involved in the new-era application of this historical fact. This should be apparent from even a superficial examination of the datacontained in the small and rather sketchy volume from which the new-era theory may be said to have sprung. The book is entitled *Common Stocks as Long Term Investments*, by Edgar Lawrence Smith, published in 1924.¹ Common stocks were shown to have a tendency to increase in value with the years, for the simple reason that they earned more than they paid out in dividends and thus the reinvested earnings added to their worth. In a representative case, the company would earn an average of 9%, pay 6% in dividends, and add 3% to surplus. With good management and reasonable luck the fair value of the stock would increase with its book value, at the annual rate of 3% *compounded*. This was, of course, a theoretical rather than a standard pattern, but the numerous instances of results poorer than “normal” might be offset by examples of more rapid growth.
The attractiveness of common stocks for the long pull thus lay essentially in the fact that they earned more than the bond-interest rate upon their cost. This would be true, typically, of a stock earning $10 and selling at 100. But as soon as the price was advanced to a much higher price in relation to earnings, this advantage disappeared, *and with it disappeared the entire theoretical basis for investment purchases of common stocks*. When in 1929 investors paid $200 per share for a stock earning $8, they were buying an earning power no greater than the bond-interest rate, without the extra protection afforded by a prior claim. Hence in using the past performances of common stocks as the reason for paying prices 20 to 40 times their earnings, the new-era exponents were starting with a sound premise and twisting it into a woefully unsound conclusion.
In fact their rush to take advantage of the inherent attractiveness of common stocks itself produced conditions entirely different from those which had given rise to this attractiveness and upon which it basically depended, *viz.*, the fact that earnings had averaged some 10% on market price. As we have seen, Edgar Lawrence Smith plausibly explained the growth of common-stock values as arising from the building up of asset values through the reinvestment of surplus earnings. Paradoxically enough, the new-era theory thatexploited this finding refused to accord the slightest importance to the asset values behind the stocks it favored. Furthermore, the validity of Mr. Smith's conclusions rested necessarily upon the assumption that common stocks could be counted on to behave in the future about as they had in the past. Yet the new-era theory threw out of account the past earnings of corporations except in so far as they were regarded as pointing to a *trend* for the future.
