## 价值投资者的成长历程

<!--en-->
*The Evolution of a Value Investor*

作者：Steven Romick

<!--en-->
by Steven Romick

在西北大学获得教育科学学士学位并非金融职业最传统的路径。然而，一位成功的投资合伙企业管理人于1985年从我大学毕业后雇佣了我作为实验对象。他说他厌倦了“重新学习”MBA们错误的理论。幸好他与我父亲是朋友。

<!--en-->
Earning a Bachelor of Science degree in education from Northwestern University is not the most traditional path to a career in finance. Nonetheless, a manager of a successful investment partnership hired me out of college in 1985 as an experiment. He said that he was tired of “unlearning” MBAs of their erroneous theories. It helped that he was friends with my father.

当我收到那份工作邀请时，我已经被一所顶尖法学院录取，原本打算同时获得法学学士和MBA学位，但我认为投资事业可能很刺激。上班第一天后，我带回家几十份招股说明书，因为我完全不知道什么才是好的投资或好的企业，也不了解如何阅读财务报表。希望当初接纳我的那所法学院如果这次实验失败，还会再次接纳我。在此期间，我决心尽可能多地学习投资知识。有人推荐我读本杰明·格雷厄姆的《聪明的投资者》，这又让我接触到了格雷厄姆和戴维·多德编写的《证券分析》。再加上在加州大学洛杉矶分校上夜校会计课程，这些成为了我作为投资者教育的基础。

<!--en-->
At the time I received that job offer, I had already been accepted to a top law school and had intended to get both JD and MBA degrees, but I thought that a career in investing could be exciting. I lugged home a few dozen prospectuses after my first day on the job, since I didn’t have a clue as to what makes something a good investment or a good business, and I had no understanding of how to read a financial statement. Hopefully, the law school that saw fit to accept me once would do so again if this experiment didn’t work out. In the meantime, I committed myself to learning as much as I could about investing. Someone directed me to Benjamin Graham’s *The Intelligent Investor*, which in turn led me to Graham and David Dodd’s *Security Analysis*. And that, along with night classes in accounting at UCLA, became the basis for my education as an investor.

格雷厄姆和多德向我介绍了价值投资的基础理念。我了解到，如果你以足够的安全边际购买一家企业股份，就很难亏损。如果支付价格与内在价值之间的差距缩小，就能盈利。如果这家企业增长超出预期，你可能会赚得更多。

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd introduced me to the foundations of value investing. I learned that if you were to buy a stake in a business with enough of a margin of safety, it would be hard to lose money. If the gap between the price paid and intrinsic value narrowed, then money would be made. If that business were to grow beyond expectations, you’d likely make even more.

我从格雷厄姆和多德那里学到的知识对我很有帮助，但我意识到自己过于专注于资产负债表、账面价值和当前现金流或收益的重要性。虽然我作为价值投资者的成长始于格雷厄姆和多德，但在现实世界的持续学习让我对价值有了更细致的理解。例如，随着职业生涯的发展，我逐渐明白世界上许多优秀企业几乎从不以低于账面价值的价格交易，更不用说低于营运资本了；许多这类企业似乎也从未以低于当前现金流的倍数出售。虽然格雷厄姆和多德让我关注与资产负债表指标相比的支付价格，作为风险保护的关键标准，但我现在认识到企业的实质——如竞争地位、利润率和增长率等——更为重要。

<!--en-->
What I learned from Graham and Dodd has served me well, but I came to realize that I had remained anchored for longer than I should have to their tight focus on the importance of balance sheets, book value, and current cash flow or earnings. While my evolution as a value investor began with Graham and Dodd, my continuing education in the real world fostered a more nuanced understanding of value. For example, as my career progressed, it became clear to me that many of the better businesses in the world hardly ever trade at a discount to book value, let alone below net working capital, and many of these businesses never seemed to sell at a low multiple of current cash flow. While Graham and Dodd got me to focus on the price paid in comparison to balance sheet metrics as the essential arbiter of downside protection, I've come to appreciate that the substance of a business—things like its competitive position, its profit margins, and its growth rate—has greater importance.

我还意识到另外两点：(1) 包含当前和预计未来收益的企业价值评估，也能为投资者提供宝贵的安全边际；(2) 看似便宜、有可观当前收益和表面资产负债表保护的企业，如果基本商业模式受到冲击，仍可能成为不吸引人的投资。

<!--en-->
I also came to realize two other things: (1) an assessment of a business's value that includes both its current and estimated future earnings could also provide a valuable margin of safety for the investor, and (2) a seemingly inexpensive business with significant current earnings and apparent balance sheet protection could nonetheless prove to be an unattractive investment if its basic business model is disrupted.

许多投资者认为价值投资就是持有普通成熟企业的股票，通常是周期性行业中的企业，没有太多增长潜力。相反，他们把成长股视为那些能在多年内保持强劲增长、同时经济周期影响有限的企业。但我认识到，不存在明确的界限区分成长股和价值股。快速成长的企业也可以属于价值投资范畴，而看似传统价值投资的产品中也可能存在成长机会。

<!--en-->
Many investors tend to think of value investing as the practice of owning the shares of humdrum established businesses, often those in cyclical industries, that are not experiencing much growth. Conversely, they consider growth stocks to be those businesses that can grow at a vigorous rate for years while experiencing limited economic cyclicality. But I've come to appreciate that there is not a bright line that divides growth and value. Value can be found in rapidly growing businesses, and growth can be found in what appear to be more traditional value investments.
PHILOSOPHY

投资者不应依赖标签，而需要拥有自己的哲学理念，以帮助识别机会，使日常工作更加高效。否则，正如刘易斯·卡罗尔在《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的柴郡猫所说：“如果你不知道要去哪里，任何道路都能带你到那里。”我自称价值投资者，但这个标签并没有明确的定义。成长投资者大概也像价值投资者一样，认为他们所持有的公司具有“价值”。我的策略是在风险有限且存在非对称上涨潜力的机会上投入资金。我在哲学上与那些天生不会亏损的投资者一致。拥有安全边际的意义在于，即使一切不如预期，投资者仍可能保持盈利。

<!--en-->
Rather than relying on labels, investors need to have their own philosophical paradigm to help frame opportunities and make more productive the quotidian work that occurs day-to-day. Otherwise, as to paraphrase Lewis Carroll's Cheshire Cat in *Alice's Adventures in Wonderland*, "If you don't know where you are going, any road will get you there." I call myself a value investor, but that label does not offer a clear-cut definition. The growth investor presumably believes the companies they own are a "value" as much as a value investor does. My approach is to commit capital to an opportunity when the risk of losing money is limited, while at the same time, there is asymmetric upside potential. I am philosophically aligned with those investors genetically predisposed to not losing money. The whole point of having a margin of safety is that even if everything doesn't go according to plan, investors may still come out close to whole.

我公司的策略是寻找质量良好的企业，并以合理的价格购买。我们评估企业的质量，包括资本回报率、市场地位的可持续性、定价能力、管理水平以及增长潜力等要素。长期持有优质且成长中的企业股票，比长期持有看似“便宜”但处于劣质企业的证券并频繁交易更有利。事实上，拥有高质量且增长前景良好的企业股票的优势在于，这些股票可以持有多年，企业还能持续为投资者增值。对于需要缴纳税项的投资者来说，这种策略特别具有税务效率。

<!--en-->
My firm's approach is to seek out good quality businesses at a reasonable price. We assess quality in terms of such attributes as a business's return on capital, the defensibility of its market position, its pricing power, the caliber of management, and its growth potential. Holding a concentrated portfolio of shares in good, growing businesses for longer periods is likely to be more beneficial than holding superficially "cheap" securities in inferior businesses and trading them frequently. Indeed, a benefit of owning a high-quality business with favorable growth prospects is that the shares can be held for many years and the business does the work of compounding investors' capital. For taxable investors, this approach is a particularly tax-efficient one.

当投资者能够保持较长期的时间视野时，效果最佳。我认为5到7年的时间范围属于典型的市场周期。这可以帮助投资者避免在高波动时期常见的糟糕交易决策。短期思维，通常源于一种认为可以精准把握市场时机的虚幻信念，会扭曲思考，偏离长期投资目标。

<!--en-->
Investors are best off when they can maintain a longer-term time horizon. I consider time horizons of five to seven years to be a typical market cycle. This can help investors avoid the poor trading decisions that become commonplace in periods of high volatility. A short-term orientation, generally rooted in what I regard as an illusory belief in being able to time a market, can distort thinking and distract from long-range investment goals.

长期成功需要接受业绩不佳的时期。投资者必须保持决心和坚持力，避免被市场潮流和泡沫所影响。这类情况并不少见：最近的例子包括1997–2000年科技股/互联网泡沫中的不合理估值、2005–2007年达到顶峰的房地产泡沫及相关次级贷款、2020年对新冠疫情影响的过度反应，以及同年许多新技术公司因赌场心态而达到不可理喻的高度。

<!--en-->
Longer-term success requires accepting periods of underperformance. An investor must maintain the resolve andstaying power to avoid market fads and bubbles. There are no shortages of these: recent examples include the whimsical valuations found in the tech-stock/ internet bubble of 1997–2000, the housing bubble and associated subprime lending that reached its zenith in 2005–2007, the overreaction to Covid-19’s impact in 2020, and the casino mentality that drove many new technology companies to unjustifiable heights that same year.

耐心是投资的必要要素，但这种耐心会受到严峻考验。公司的运营变化可能需要比预期更长时间才能产生影响。经济疲软可能会给即使是最优秀的企业战略带来意外挑战。整体市场状况不佳、波动或负面新闻都可能让投资者不安。虽然以合理价格购买的优质成长型企业股票会随时间表现良好，但这并不意味着它们会一直表现良好。

<!--en-->
Great patience is a necessary ingredient in investing, and that patience can be sorely tested. Operational changes at a company might take longer than expected to have an impact. A weak economy might create unexpected challenges to even the best corporate strategies. General market malaise, volatility, or discordant news can vex an investor. While shares in a high quality, growing business purchased at a reasonable price should perform well over time, that doesn’t mean they will perform well all of the time.

投资成功通常不是线性的；它表现为阶段性成果，往往之后会有挫折。投资者应关注目标，同时做好旅途准备。即使是最成功的长期投资也会有长时间的业绩不佳期。

<!--en-->
Investment success is usually not linear; it comes in bursts and is often followed by setbacks. Investors should focus on the destination while bracing themselves for the journey. Even the most successful long-term investments have prolonged periods of underperformance.

## 案例研究：微软

<!--en-->
*Case Study: Microsoft*

我发现，长期跟踪那些多年来以稳健速度为投资者增值的优秀企业，有助于识别对投资者有吸引力的进入点。我们以微软作为案例研究。

<!--en-->
I find that tracking exceptional businesses over time—those that have compounded investor capital at robust rates for a number of years—helps in identifying attractive entry points for investors. Let’s consider Microsoft as a case study.

虽然其最快的增长可能在2010年之前就停止了，但我相信这一优秀企业将继续实现合理增长。市场确实对近期发展存在担忧，如从台式电脑向平板电脑的转变、苹果iOS对Windows操作系统的竞争，以及谷歌Chrome可能夺走Office文字处理市场份额的潜在威胁。此外，微软管理团队也没有过分自夸。

<!--en-->
While its fastest growth might have been behind it by 2010, I believed this great business franchise would deliver reasonable growth. The market had legitimate fears about recent developments, like the transition from desktop PCs to tablets, real operating system competition for Windows from Apple’s iOS, and the potential for Google Chrome to take word-processing market share from Office. Moreover, the Microsoft management team had not been covering itself in glory.

尽管股市认为该公司的前景已黯淡，但我们认为微软被低估了。例如，收入达20亿美元的领先云业务Salesforce.com，其估值超过未来收益的100倍。微软也是领先的云企业，按用户数量和收入衡量，但市场给予它的市盈率仅为Salesforce的十二分之一。为了加强在云领域的地位，2010年微软表示将把年度96亿美元研发预算的90%用于云战略（这一金额是Salesforce总收入的4倍以上）。凭借4万人的研发团队和几乎涉及所有组织的产品组合，我们确信该公司将在蓬勃发展的企业云计算领域保持相关性。虽然微软从1999年到2009年的收益年化增长率为17.4%，但其股价年化下跌率为5.3%。根据格雷厄姆和多德的原则，我们确定微软的内在价值远高于市场价值，而且具有良好的增长前景。我们在2010年以12倍历史收益净值（报告值为13.4倍）购买股票，比当时P/E约为15倍的S&P 500低20%。

<!--en-->
While the stock market was pricing the company as one whose prospects had dimmed, we felt that Microsoft was underappreciated. For example, Salesforce.com, a leading cloud player with $2 billion in revenues, was valued at more than 100x forward earnings. Microsoft was also a leading cloud player, as measured by number of users and revenue, yet the market awarded it just one-twelfth the P/E of Salesforce. To bolster its place in the cloud, in 2010 Microsoft said it would spend 90% of the company's annual $9.6 billion R&D budget on its cloud strategy (a sum more than 4x Salesforce.com total revenues). With Microsoft's R&D staff of 40,000 and a portfolio of product offerings that touches almost every organization in one way or another, we were confident the company would remain relevant in the burgeoning world of corporate cloud computing
While Microsoft's earnings grew at an annualized rate of 17.4% from 1999 to 2009, its stock price declined at an annualized 5.3%. Applying the principles of Graham and Dodd, we determined that Microsoft's intrinsic value was well in excess of its market value and moreover, it had good growth prospects. We bought the stock in 2010 at 12x trailing earnings net of cash (13.4x reported), a 20% discount to the S&P 500 that traded at a P/E of around 15x at that time.

从2010年到2020年，该公司的每股收益以10.8%的年度增长率增长，这得益于几乎回购了13%的股份。其市盈率扩展到过去收益的38.3倍，使得整个十年期间（包括股息）的年化总回报达到25.9%。

<!--en-->
From 2010 to 2020, the company's earnings per share grew at a 10.8% annual rate, aided by repurchasing almost 13% of its shares. Its price earnings multiple expanded to 38.3x trailing earnings, which drove a 25.9% annualized total return over the decade, inclusive of dividends.

微软是成长股还是价值股？它两者都是！虽然公司实现了稳健的收益增长，但购买股票的价格使其具有良好价值。购买一家发展速度超过市场、价格有折扣的优质企业股份，长期来看是赚钱的好方法。

<!--en-->
Was Microsoft a growth stock or a value stock? It was both! While the company delivered sound earnings growth, the price at which we were able to acquire the shares made it a good value. Purchasing shares in a durable, good quality business that is growing faster than the market but trades at a discount should be a recipe for making money over time.

寻找风险/回报比例不对称且有利结果概率高于50%的机会，可以提高成功概率。我们认为微软就是这种情况，我们觉得成功的概率被低估了。即使收益低于我们的预期，负面影响也会有限，提供安全边际，而上涨潜力很大。我们还认为，2014年新领导层上任后，公司的成功前景进一步改善。

<!--en-->
Finding opportunities with asymmetric risk/reward ratios and better than a 50/50 likelihood of a favorable outcome should improve one's slugging percentage. We believed that it was the case with Microsoft, where we felt the odds of successhad been miscalculated. The downside would have been limited even if earnings had fallen below our estimates, providing a margin of safety, while the potential for upside was sizable. We also believed the prospects for corporate success improved further once new leadership was put in place in 2014.

尽管如此，遵循这一过程时总会犯错。有句古老的意第绪语谚语：“人计划，上帝笑”——“人规划，上帝嘲笑。”新竞争对手出现并颠覆市场。老对手提升水平。管理层会犯错。宏观经济环境带来意外。由于世界处于不断变化的状态，定期重新审视投资理论并积极寻求确认至关重要。

<!--en-->
Nonetheless, there will always be mistakes while abiding by this process. There’s an old Yiddish adage, *Mann tracht, un Gott lacht*—“Man plans, and God laughs.” New competitors emerge and disrupt. Venerable competitors raise their game. Management makes mistakes. The macroeconomic environment unleashes a surprise. Since the world is in a constant state of flux, it is imperative to regularly revisit an investment thesis and actively seek reconfirmation.

我也犯过一些错误。对Circuit City、Semi-Tech Global和Conseco的投资都是以亏损出售的。我没有正确权衡竞争变化、管理不善和糟糕承销等关键因素。

<!--en-->
I have made my share of mistakes. Investments in Circuit City, Semi-Tech Global, and Conseco were all sold at a loss. I failed to properly weigh such crucial elements as changing competition, weak management, and poor underwriting.

擅长投资并不意味着永远完美；即使是美国职业棒球大联盟的全明星球员，只有30%的时间能上垒。我的前合作伙伴鲍勃·罗德里格斯管理FPA资本基金，在1984年至2010年的25年间表现最佳，但仍有两个头寸归零。承认会犯大错是投资的一部分。

<!--en-->
Being good at investing doesn’t mean batting 1,000; even Major League Baseball’s All-Stars get on base only 30% of the time. One of my former partners, Bob Rodriguez, managed the FPA Capital Fund and delivered the best performance of any diversified mutual fund over the quarter century between 1984 and 2010, yet he also had two positions that went to zero. Accepting that you will make some big mistakes is part of investing.

由于我们认为投资者无法成功“预测市场”，我们认为现金应该是投资过程的剩余部分。当没有 compelling机会时，我们选择等待。当看到他人投资组合增值时，坐视不理可能会很困难，但我们认为这比持有你不喜欢的头寸更好。在2000年年度致股东信中，Leucadia National Corporation的前董事长伊恩·卡明和前总裁约瑟夫·斯坦伯格描述了这种动态，将他们比作土拨鼠：“我们每天早晨从洞穴里出来，在市场上寻找投资机会。我们首先问的是：‘我们看到什么能获得高于无风险利率（调整风险后）的收益？’当市场像过去许多年那样高时，我们很少看到值得投资的，于是回到洞穴里……这个过程需要耐心，但并不复杂。”不幸的是，大多数投资者更喜欢在投资前看到股价上涨，通常在感到害怕时会卖出，这通常是在他们的投资组合价值出现明显下降之后。结果，普通投资者的表现低于股票指数和自身目标，错过了许多市场向上的大波动，同时仍参与下跌行情。

<!--en-->
Since we believe investors cannot successfully “time” the market, we believe cash should be the residual component of the investment process. When there are no compelling opportunities at hand, we choose to wait. Sitting on your hands can be difficult when you see the portfolios of others increase in value, but we believe this is better than owning positions you don’t find attractive. In their fiscal year 2000 Annual Letter to Shareholders, Leucadia National Corporation’s former chairman, Ian Cumming, and former president, Joseph Steinberg, spoke to this dynamic, likening themselves to groundhogs: “We pop out of our holes each and every morning and look around the marketplace forinvestment opportunities.¹ The first question we ask is, ‘Do we see anything that can earn more than the risk-free rate, adjusted for risk?’ When the markets are as high as they have been in the last many years, we saw very little of interest and went back down our holes.... Patience is required for this process, but it is not complicated.” Unfortunately, most investors prefer to see stock prices appreciating before they invest, and they usually sell when they get scared, which is often after experiencing a measurable decline in the value of their portfolio. As a result, the average investor underperforms stock indexes and their own goals, missing many large market moves to the upside, while still participating in the downside.

如果你最终能够匹配市场的回报，同时缩短市场下跌的最坏时期，你就能为客户创造巨大价值。广泛的、无限制的投资策略使我们能够做到这一点，通过多样化的工具组合投资于各种市场和工具。我们在公司的资本结构中分配资金。我们投入资金于公共和私人信贷，以及不同市值、行业、地区和资产类别。有时我们甚至持有空头头寸。

<!--en-->
If you can ultimately match the return of the market while truncating the worst periods of market downside, you’re delivering considerable value to your clients. A broad, unfettered mandate has allowed us to accomplish this, using a diverse tool kit to invest in a broad range of markets and instruments. We have allocated capital across a company’s capital structure. We have put money into public and private credit, as well as in a variety of market capitalizations, industries, geographies, and asset classes. We have even had short positions from time to time.

我认为给投资经理过于狭窄的投资范围是很愚蠢的。营销层面的沟通可能更容易，但投资结果很可能较差。我相信我们的客户从我们广泛的投资范围中受益。以房地产市场为例：选择购买10层、30层或70层的办公楼，就像选择购买小型、中型或大型公司一样。决定这些商业建筑价值的因素相同，包括分析市场可比销售数据、资本化率、重建成本以及当地使用率。价值投资者应该投资于价格与价值关系最佳的建筑，无论规模大小。如果没有任何建筑提供有利机会，则不应进行投资。

<!--en-->
I believe it is foolish to give a money manager an overly narrow mandate. The marketing conversations may be easier, but the investment outcomes are likely to be poorer. I’m confident our clients benefit from our broad mandate. Consider the real estate market; the decision to buy a 10-story, 30-story, or 70-story office building is analogous to buying a small, medium, or large-cap company. The factors are the same in determining the value of these commercial buildings and include examining comparable in-market sales, capitalization rates, replacement costs, and local occupancy levels. A value investor should invest in the building that has the best relationship of price to value, regardless of size. If none of the buildings offer a favorable opportunity, then an investment should not be made.

但如果70层的建筑定价并不吸引人，或者因为无法出售而无法购买呢？如果首笔抵押贷款可以以如此低的折扣购买，以至于建筑所有者出现违约时，你可以实施止赎并以极低的价格控制该建筑，这样很难亏损呢？1995年洛克菲勒中心就发生了这种情况，其前主要所有者三菱地产公司申请了破产保护。持有抵押贷款的房地产投资信托基金洛克菲勒中心物业公司的债务以低于面值的价格交易，在最坏情况下可以获得双位数回报。如果发生止赎，我们有良好的下行风险保护：我们将以低于重建成本的价格控制洛克菲勒中心。

<!--en-->
But what if the 70-story building wasn’t priced at a level where you would want to own it, or you can’t buy it because it isn’t available for sale? What if its first mortgage can bepurchased at such a discount that if the building owner were to default, you could foreclose and take control of the building at a price that would make it very hard to lose money? That's what happened to Rockefeller Center in 1995 when Mitsubishi Estate Company, its former majority owner, filed for bankruptcy protection. The debt of Rockefeller Center Properties Inc., the real estate investment trust that held its mortgage, traded at a discount to par, allowing for a double-digit rate of return in a worst-case scenario. In the event of a foreclosure, we had good downside protection: we would have taken control of Rockefeller Center at a discount to replacement cost.

# 识别机会

<!--en-->
*RECOGNIZING OPPORTUNITY*

虽然投资者需要开放接受机会，但他们也需要了解限制条件。正如我们所提到的，我们在多种国家、市场、证券和策略中寻找机会。但仅仅因为我们能进行如此广泛的投资，并不意味着我们应该总是这样做。相反，我们只会在我们认为有良好回报前景且具备安全边际的地方投资。这适用于许多资产类别。

<!--en-->
While investors need to be open to opportunities, they also need to be aware of limitations. As we've noted, we seek opportunity across a broad range of countries, markets, securities, and strategies. But simply because we can invest with such breadth does not mean we always should. Instead, we only invest where we believe there is an excellent prospect for return combined with a margin of safety. This applies to a number of asset classes.

# 股权

<!--en-->
*Equity*

当我们对企业进行股权投资时，我们会超越资产负债表分析和寻找安全边际，寻找具有可防御细分市场、良好资本回报和合理估值的成长型企业。这类企业还应位于法律执行严格的国家的扩展行业中。我们避免那些潜在结果范围特别广泛的企业和行业，完全避免那些我们的技能限制了我们评估企业或影响特定结果可能性的领域。多年来，我们发现更好的投资是那些有多种盈利方式且具有巨大上涨潜力的企业，如果情况有利，可以赚取大量利润。

<!--en-->
When we make an equity investment in a business, we go beyond balance sheet analyses and the search for a margin of safety to seek out growing businesses with defensible niches, good returns on capital, and reasonable valuations. Such businesses should also be involved in expanding industries in countries where the rule of law is strongly enforced. We shy away from those businesses and industries where the potential range of outcomes is particularly wide and avoid entirely those where our skill set limits our ability to either evaluate the business or handicap the likelihood of a particular outcome. Over the years, we have found our better investments have been those with more than one way to win and with substantial upside potential so that a lot of money can be made if things turn out favorably.

CVS Health是美国两大药房零售商之一，具有许多我们喜欢的特性，包括低成本的现金流和收益倍数、行业增长以及良好的管理。除了遍布各地的药店外，它还拥有 Pharmacy Benefit Management（PBM）业务Caremark。为了评估其股票价值，我们将业务分为两个主要部分。2010年，该公司整体估值约为一年预期收益的11.5倍；然而，如果我们用与同行相同的估值标准来评估CVS的PBM业务，那么剩余业务（主要是CVS药房和零售业务）的估值仅为一年预期收益的9.4倍——也就是说，价格较低且存在安全边际。

<!--en-->
CVS Health, one of the nation's two largest pharmacy retailers, had many of the characteristics we like to see, including inexpensive multiples of cash flow and earnings, industry growth, and good management. Besides its ubiquitous drugstores, it owned Caremark, a pharmacy benefit management (PBM) business. To assess the value of its shares, we separated the business into its two primary parts. In 2010, the company as a whole traded at about 11.5x estimated one-year forward earnings; however, if we applied the same valuations to CVS's PBM that were applied to its peers, then the valuation of the remaining business (primarily CVS pharmacy and retail) was just 9.4x one-year forward earnings —that is, it was inexpensive and there was a margin of safety.

药房业务处于有利位置，可以受益于多个行业宏观趋势，包括美国人口老龄化导致对处方药需求增加、联邦医疗改革将大幅增加参保人数及处方购买者数量，以及转向仿制药带来的利润率提升。CVS的私人品牌占总销售额的17%。相比之下，经营包含药店的杂货店的Kroger，私人品牌渗透率为28%。而英国Tesco的私人品牌渗透率为50%，相比之下CVS有很多扩展利润空间。我们预计零售业务将继续受益于更多私人品牌产品，使毛利率提高约10个百分点。

<!--en-->
The pharmacy segment was well-positioned to benefit from several industry macro trends, including an aging U.S. population that would be needing more prescription medicines, Federal healthcare reform that would dramatically increase the number of insured and therefore the number of prescription buyers, and improved profit margins from the continuing shift to generic drugs. CVS's private brands represented 17% of total sales. By contrast, Kroger, which operated grocery stores that included drugstores, had 28% private brand penetration. That, in turn, paled next to UK-based Tesco's 50%. This left CVS with a lot of runway for margin expansion. We expected the retail segment to continue to benefit from a greater volume of private label products that would offer a roughly 10 percentage point increase in gross margin.

与此同时，CVS通过收购实现了历史性增长，其管理层开始关注运营改进的巨大潜力。曾有一段时间，零售和药店部门使用七种库存管理系统，而Caremark拥有五种不同的理赔平台。到2013年，他们的目标是将每个部门缩减至一个平台，这应能使他们减少20亿美元的零售店库存，相当于每股CVS约1.50美元，占当时股价的4.2%。此外，我们认为CVS的Caremark PBM能够提升其每股收益贡献，并在三年内可能使股价增加3-4美元/股。

<!--en-->
Meanwhile, CVS had historic growth through acquisitions, and its management was beginning to focus its attention on the substantial potential for operational improvements. At one point, the retail and pharmacy division operated with seven inventory management systems, while Caremark had five different claims platforms. By 2013, their goal was to be down to one platform each, which should allow them to reduce retail store inventories by $2 billion, representing about $1.50 per CVS share, or 4.2% of the share price at that time. Moreover, we believed that CVS's Caremark PBM could improve itscontribution to CVS EPS and potentially add an additional $3–$4 per share in value over three years.

我们还赞赏CVS的精英管理团队以所有者/运营商的心态行事。他们拥有公司的大量财务权益，这很可能确保他们追求股东的最佳利益。

<!--en-->
We also liked that CVS’s skilled management acted with the mentality of an owner/operator. They had substantial financial stakes in the company, which was likely to ensure they pursued what was in the best interests of shareholders.

我们认为CVS的药店和零售业务拥有比PBM业务更大的护城河，并为销售增长和运营改进提供了清晰的路线图。由于存在Medco Containment和Express Scripts等公开上市的PBM同行企业，我们认为通过做空这些估值较高的公司，可以以相对保守的CVS自身PBM内在价值评估，获得较低估值的企业机会。

<!--en-->
We believed CVS’s pharmacy and retail business had a larger moat than its PBM segment and offered a clear road map for sales growth and operational improvement. Given that there were publicly traded PBM peers like Medco Containment and Express Scripts, we believed we gained exposure to a business at a lower valuation by shorting these more highly valued companies in rough proportion to our conservative view of the intrinsic value of CVS’s own PBM.

简而言之，我们认为CVS面临的任何风险都被较低的估值所抵消，这既保证了投资成功的可能性，也提供了安全边际。然而，成功的投资不仅要求在合适的时候进入，还要求在合适的时候退出。我们在2010年积累了CVS的仓位，大约五年后，我们意识到已经充分享受到了管理层扎实执行业务计划的效果，以及我们所预期的有利宏观趋势。未来，我们认为不断变化的竞争环境意味着CVS将面临更多在线零售商的挑战，这些零售商能提供更多便利服务，且价格通常更低，这将对门店内通用商品销售造成压力。

<!--en-->
In short, we felt whatever risks CVS faced were outweighed by a low valuation that provided both a likelihood of investment success and a margin of safety. However, successful investing requires not only getting in at a good time but exiting at a good time as well. We accumulated our CVS position in 2010, and about five years later, we concluded that we had received the full benefits of management’s solid execution of its business plan, as well as the favorable macro trends we had expected. Going forward, we also felt the changing competitive landscape meant CVS would face more online retailers offering more convenience, often at better prices, and that would put pressure on the sales of its general merchandise in the front of the store.

由于价格不再具有吸引力，我们在2015年决定出售CVS的仓位。到那时，CVS的收益增长和P/E倍数扩大使股价从2010年到2015年增长了三倍。同时，短期销售我们大致实现了收支平衡。²

<!--en-->
With the price no longer compelling, we decided to sell our position in CVS in 2015. By then CVS’s earnings growth and P/E multiple expansion translated into a stock price thattripled from 2010 to 2015. Meanwhile, we achieved a roughly breakeven result on the short sales.²

# 信贷

<!--en-->
*Credit*

类似原则也指导了我们的固定收益投资。我们通常投资三种类型的信贷工具：表现良好的债券、困境债务和私人信贷。购买表现良好的债券时，我们努力确保不仅能按时获得回报，还能获得“类似股权”的到期收益率，通常为9%至11%。由于困境信贷相关的风险更高，我们通常将目标收益率设定为十几%或更高的到期收益率。我们的经验表明，私人信贷市场可能特别低效，因此能带来与风险相称的高额回报。

<!--en-->
Similar principles have informed our investing in fixed income. There are three types of credit instruments in which we generally traffic: performing bonds, distressed debt, and private credits. In buying a performing bond, we strive to ensure not only that we will be repaid on a timely basis, but also that we can obtain a yield-to-maturity that is “equity-like,” generally 9% to 11%. Given the greater risks associated with distressed credits, we have generally set the target yield at a mid-teens or higher yield to maturity. Our experience is that private credit markets can be particularly inefficient, thereby offering excess returns for the risk involved.

金融市场就像情绪摆锤，从繁荣转向恐惧。例如，在2008年大金融危机前的狂热时期，金融股被严重高估，随后又过度下跌。但这种定价错误创造了企业债务和困境抵押贷款的机会。我们知道次级抵押贷款特别受厌恶，因此我们调查了投资者担忧是否过度。

<!--en-->
The financial markets can be an emotional pendulum that swings from exuberance to fear. Financial stocks were greatly overvalued in the euphoric conditions that preceded 2008’s Great Financial Crisis, for example, and then they swung too far in the other direction. But that mispricing created opportunities in the corporate debt of financials and distressed mortgages. We knew that subprime mortgages were particularly hated, so we investigated whether investor fears might be overblown.

到2009年底，最大的20个都市市场的住房市场下降了约29.5%。我们找到了一批困境抵押贷款（Alt-A），以原始评估房屋价值的66%折扣以及2009年底低迷房屋价值的37%折扣进行购买。我们得出结论，相关房屋价格还需要再下降30%，否则我们可能会亏损。有了这个安全边际，我们很可能在仓位上获得有吸引力的固定收益回报，损失可能性极小。困境抵押贷款池#1

<!--en-->
By the end of 2009, the housing market has declined approximately 29.5% in the largest 20 metro markets. We identified a basket of distressed mortgages (Alt-A) that we purchased at a 66% discount to the original appraised home value and a 37% discount to the 2009 year-end depressed home value. We concluded that the underlying group of homes would have to decline an additional 30% before we would be at risk of losing money. With this margin of safety, we were likely to earn an attractive fixed-income return on our position with a minimal potential for loss.
Distressed Mortgage Pool #1

以我们的购买价格，我们实际上拥有这些抵押贷款所涉及的房产，平均每套房产的价值约为99,000美元。这一房产价值为我们提供了额外的安全边际，因为以这个价格，这些房产与公寓租金相比具有竞争力。

<!--en-->
At our purchase price, we effectively owned the homes underlying these mortgages at an average value of approximately $99,000 per home. This home value provided us an additional margin of safety because these homes were competitive with apartment rentals at this price.

到2010年年中时，我们发现该抵押贷款池的表现，包括利息，已经返还了初始资本投资超过30%。仅看已收回的房产，它们为我们的投资带来了超过24%的总回报。此外，我们剩余资产组合的当前收益率超过了8%。

<!--en-->
By midyear 2010, we saw that the performance of this mortgage pool, including interest, had returned more than 30% of our initial capital investment. Looking just at the properties unwound, they generated a total return on our investment of more than 24%. In addition, we earned a better than 8% current yield on our remaining basis in the portfolio.

由于早期回报验证了我们的初始论点，我们继续购买更多资产池，汇集了数千笔大多表现不佳的抵押贷款。虽然早期结果比我们预期的要好，但现在还无法宣布胜利。投资组合的艰难后期阶段（延迟维护、财产损坏和诉讼情况）仍然存在。幸运的是，这些困难情况在预期范围内结束，这些困境抵押贷款的加权平均回报为12.5%。

<!--en-->
Since the early returns validated our initial thesis, we continued to buy additional pools, aggregating thousands of mostly nonperforming mortgages. While the early results were better than we would have expected, it was too soon to declare victory. The difficult tail end of the portfolio (deferred maintenance, property damage, and litigious situations) remained. Fortunately, the tail played out within the range of expectations, and the weighted average return of these distressed mortgages turned out to be 12.5%.

查理·芒格曾解释道：“我们取得良好业绩的部分原因是我们选择容易的事情。其他人认为他们非常聪明，可以承担真正困难的任务。但这反而更危险。你必须机智且要有耐心。”³他补充说：“对于普通人来说，你能想象坐五年什么都不做吗？这完全违背人性。你不会感到活跃，也不会觉得有用，所以会做出愚蠢的事情。”投资的重要部分确实在于耐心等待“绝佳机会”，然后果断行动。

<!--en-->
Charlie Munger once explained, “Part of the reason we have a decent record is we pick things that are easy. Other people think they’re so smart that they can take on things that are really difficult. That proves to be more dangerous. You have to be shrewd and you have to be patient.”³ He added, “For an ordinary person, can you imagine just sitting there for five years doing nothing? It’s so contrary to human nature. You don’t feel active. You don’t feel useful, so you do something stupid.” A big part of investing is indeed waitingpatiently for a “fat pitch” right over home plate and then swinging aggressively.

## 严谨的评估/流程

<!--en-->
*DUE DILIGENCE/PROCESS*

作为价值投资者，我们专注于那些不受欢迎或被误解的领域。我们开始确定哪些资产类别、行业或地区可能提供最佳机会，以实现我们既定的长期目标：获得类似股票的回报，同时风险低于市场水平，并据此分配时间。我们花大量时间询问关于潜在投资的问题：什么力量将决定其命运？有哪些风险？如果……会怎样？我们经常寻求相反的观点，避免陷入回音室效应，并反转我们的论点，从不同的角度看待投资，可能会看到不太乐观的情况。这些努力帮助我们识别机会领域，比如2009年初，困境债务被定价为萧条情景；同时避免了其他领域，比如2000年代初期至中期，金融领域，当时价格未能反映次级债务扩散和房地产泡沫的风险。

<!--en-->
As value investors, we focus on what is out of favor or misunderstood. We begin our process of determining which asset classes, industries, or regions might offer the best opportunities to reach our established longer-range goal of equity-like returns with less than market risk and allocate our time accordingly. We spend a lot of time asking a lot of questions about both the problems and prospects of a potential investment: What are the forces that will shape its fate? What’s the downside? What if ... ? We regularly seek a contrary view to avoid the positive reinforcement of an echo chamber, and we invert our thesis to see the investment from a different lens, where things may not look as rosy. These efforts have helped us identify areas of opportunity, like in early 2009 when distressed debt was priced for a depression scenario, while avoiding others like financials for much of the early to mid 2000s when prices failed to reflect the risk of subprime debt proliferation and the interrelated housing bubble.

我们很少与公司外的“投资专业人士”交流。我们更愿意在华尔街花费较少时间，与街头的人——客户、竞争对手、公司高管和行业专家——交流，因为我们相信这种互动能提升我们对企业和行业的理解。我们阅读很多资料，从SEC文件、电话会议记录，到相关期刊和行业研究。我们努力获得知识优势——对某个企业或行业的理解可能并非普遍适用。当然，有些公司被关注得如此深入，以至于我们无法通过这种方式区分自己。

<!--en-->
We speak to relatively few “investment professionals” outside our firm. We prefer to spend less time on Wall Street and more time with people on Main Street—customers, competitors, company executives, and industry experts—because we believe this interaction improves our understanding of businesses and industries. We read a lot, everything from SEC filings and conference call transcripts, to pertinent periodicals and industry studies. We work to gain a knowledge edge—a level of understanding of a business or industry that may not be universal. Of course, some companies are followed so extensively that we can’t differentiate ourselves in this fashion.

在分析企业时，有时财务报表能说明问题；在这种情况下，我们倾向于选择根据报告财务结果看起来“便宜”的投资。但在其他情况下，财务报表中未包含的信息可能最为重要，例如关于公司在行业成本曲线上的位置、总可销售市场的特征、客户获取成本和生命周期价值，以及按市场价值计量的实物资产数据。在这种情况下，基于报告财务结果，我们的持有资产可能看起来“昂贵”，但深入观察这些其他因素后，你可以理解为什么我们认为这些公司被低估了。

<!--en-->
When analyzing businesses, sometimes financial statements tell the story; in those cases, we favor investments that typically appear “cheap” based on reported financial results. But in other situations, information not in the financialstatements might be most relevant, such as data regarding a company's position on the industry cost curve, characteristics of its total addressable market, its customer acquisition costs and lifetime value, and real assets marked-to-market. In these situations, our holding might appear "expensive" based on reported financial results, but when you look deeper into these other factors, you can discern why we think such companies are undervalued.

由于我们的知识存在不完美，我们更倾向于设定一个潜在的结果范围。我们构建财务模型，预测未来几年中低、基线和高三种情景。好的投资是指能在基线情景下获得可接受的回报，且高情景发生的可能性高于低情景。在寻找优质企业并了解它时，我们特别关注其自由现金流——而不是净收入，因为净收入指标没有考虑资本支出和营运资金等因素。

<!--en-->
Since we operate with imperfect knowledge, we prefer to establish a potential range of outcomes. We build financial models that look out a few years with low, base, and high cases. A good investment is one where an acceptable return can be had in the base case, and where the high case scenario should be more likely than that of the low case. As we seek to find a good business and understand it, one thing we pay close attention to is its free cash flow—rather than net income, a metric that does not, among other things, take into account capital spending and working capital.

我们认为，所有合理的基本面投资都属于价值投资，即以低于合理情景下的价值价格购买企业或资产。购买具有足够安全边际的成长型企业，同样属于价值投资，例如，以低于有形账面价值的价格购买金融公司，或以低于可轻易确定的净资产价值的价格购买控股公司。

<!--en-->
In our view, all sensible fundamental investing is value investing, by which we mean buying a business or asset for less than what it is worth under reasonable scenarios. Buying growing businesses with an adequate margin of safety is just as much value investing as buying, for example, a financial firm at a discount to tangible book value or a holding company at a discount to readily ascertainable net asset value.

相反，虽然成长型股票投资通常表现为高估值，但这并不意味着价格不合理。一家当前股价为收益额50倍、未来五年每年增长30%的公司，即使其市盈率在五年后降至30倍，仍可能实现17.4%的回报。然而，这种高估值在初期具有不可持续性。如果该公司仅以15%的稳健增长率发展，但市盈率降至20倍，那么股价将下降近20%，这五年内的内部收益率将为负4.3%。而且这仅基于你在五年期间对收益的判断正确。

<!--en-->
Conversely, while growth stock investing is often characterized by high valuations, that doesn't mean the prices are unwarranted. A company trading at 50x earnings that grows 30% annually over the next five years could still deliver a 17.4% return even if its P/E falls to 30x at the end of that span. However, there is a perishability to such high valuations on the front end. If that company grows at a respectable 15% but its P/E shrinks to 20x, then the stock price would be lower by almost 20%, a negative 4.3% IRR in those five years. And that's only if you were right about the earnings over that five-year period.

## 心理学/风险

<!--en-->
*PSYCHOLOGY/RISK*

充分理解企业和行业竞争环境是必要的，但还不够。通过能够解读公司财务报表（包括脚注）来显著提升这一过程。

<!--en-->
Thoroughly understanding a business and the competitive landscape of its industry is necessary but not sufficient. This process is significantly enhanced by an ability to work through corporate financial statements (including the footnotes).

成功的投资还有一项关键技能——理解投资者心理，包括你自己的以及他人的心理。你是否可能会在没有充分论点和对投资进行适当尽职调查的情况下，仅仅因为听到好故事就采取行动？或者你更可能根本不采取行动，因为你害怕亏损？你能识别错误并卖出股票，还是更可能继续持有，希望获得更高价格，认为直到实际卖出才真正经历亏损？在过去几十年里，被称为行为金融学的投资者心理学研究在该领域发挥着越来越重要的作用。虽然我们无法摆脱让人类如此的情感，但我们应认识到那些可能影响投资者的心理因素——恐惧与贪婪、惰性以及过度交易——这些都与形成投资决策的尽职调查和理性决策密切相关。投资者需要认识到自己的行为模式和偏见，并在必要时加以纠正。

<!--en-->
There's another crucial skill in successful investing—understanding investor psychology, both your own and that of others. Are you likely to act without a good thesis and proper due diligence, just because you heard a good story? Or are you more apt to not act at all, because you are fearful of losing money? Can you recognize a mistake and sell a stock, or are you more likely to hold on, hoping for a higher price, believing you haven't really experienced a loss until you actually sell the holding? In the last few decades, the study of investor psychology called behavioral finance has taken on a growing role in the field. While we will not rid ourselves of emotions, which make us human, we should recognize the psychological factors—the fear and greed, the inertia as well as hyperactive trading—that can weigh on investors. These are necessarily bound up with the due diligence and rational decision-making that shape investment decisions. Investors need to recognize their own behavioral settings and biases, and compensate for them as warranted.

对风险的态度始终是投资的核心。我们无法消除风险，但可以尝试识别风险、理解风险、最小化风险，并获得合理的补偿。我们认识到错误定价的风险可以创造买入机会。我们在投资中考虑的风险包括信用风险、货币风险、业务过时风险、欺诈风险、主权风险、利率风险、通货膨胀风险、诉讼风险、征用风险、客户集中度风险、供应商中断风险、竞争风险、经济风险、资产负债表风险以及政治风险。我们认为，最终的投资风险是资本的永久损失。

<!--en-->
Attitudes toward risk are always at the core of investing. We cannot eliminate risk, but we can seek to identify it, understand it, minimize it, and be adequately compensated for it. We recognize that mispriced risk can create a buying opportunity. The risks we consider in our investing include credit, currency, business obsolescence, fraud, sovereign, interest rate, inflation, litigation, expropriation, customer concentration, vendor disruption, competition, economic, balance sheet, and political. We believe the ultimate investment risk is a permanent loss of capital.

有些人混淆了风险和波动性，但短期市场波动的结果完全无关紧要。如果你今天的投资组合价格为1000美元，明年跌至750美元，但五年后你以2000美元出售，你的资本几乎增长了15%。另一方面，如果25%的下跌导致你卖出，那你不幸让价格而非价值成为你的指导标准。在这种情况下，波动性成了你的敌人。如果你有充分的理由相信你的投资论点，最好让波动性成为你的朋友，在750美元时买入更多，从而在接下来的四年中实现28%的增量投资回报。

<!--en-->
Some confuse risk and volatility, but what happens as a result of short-term market volatility should be entirely irrelevant. If your portfolio is traded at $1,000 today, and it drops to $750 next year, but you ultimately sell it for $2,000 five years from now, you've compounded your capital at almost 15%. If, on the other hand, the 25% drop to $750 leads you to sell, then you've unfortunately let price, rather thanvalue, be your guide. In this case, volatility has become your enemy. If you have good reason to trust your investment thesis, better to make volatility your friend and buy more at $750, and thereby achieve a 28% return on your incremental investment for the next four years.

虽然股市每天都像投票机一样运作，但正如格雷厄姆和多德所著名指出的那样，从长期来看，它实际上是一个称重机。就像温度计今天给出温度读数，但无法说明明天的情况一样，股票价格或其短期走势无法说明该企业未来可能值多少。就像我们之前的格雷厄姆和多德一样，他人非理性的行为让我们既能以折扣价买入，也能以溢价卖出。

<!--en-->
While the stock market functions as a voting machine from day to day, it's effectively a weighing machine over the long term, as Graham and Dodd famously observed. Just as a thermometer gives you a temperature reading today but says nothing about tomorrow, a stock price or its movement over shorter time frames say nothing about how much that business might be worth in the future. Like Graham and Dodd before us, the irrational behavior of others has allowed us to both buy at a discount and sell at a premium.

愚蠢的投资行为普遍存在。例如，共同基金投资者在业绩表现优异后往往会过度崇拜那些管理者——这恰恰是最糟糕的时刻。Morningstar发布了一份有启发性的报告，以某只特定共同基金为明确例证：⁴ “某基金的资金流入在2007年达到顶峰，那一年由于商品投资带来了80%的回报，恰好在2008年基金价值下跌了一半。过去十年中，大多数投资者并未获得该基金18%的收益，而该基金的典型投资者每年损失了近14%——这是一个惊人的32个百分点的投资回报与总回报差距。”该基金有LIFO投资者，即最后购买者优先，他们在不同时间进入和离开。

<!--en-->
Foolish investing behavior exists broadly. Investors in mutual funds, for example, have a tendency to deify those managers after a great run—the worst possible time. Morningstar developed an illuminating report that held up one particular mutual fund as an unambiguous example of this behavior:⁴ “Assets flowing into a certain fund peaked in 2007, following an 80% commodity-fueled return that year, just in time for the fund to shed half its value in 2008. Not only have most investors not pocketed any of the fund's 18% gain during the past decade, but the typical investor in the fund has lost nearly 14% per year—a stunning 32-percentage-point investor return/total return gap.” This fund had LIFO investors, last-in first-out, and they came and went at precisely the wrong times.

正如容易过于活跃，也容易因懈怠而重复昨天的行为。这适用于投资过程以及个人投资选择。惯性可能让我继续坚持资产负债表导向的价值投资方式，但我意识到需要改变。我认识到，商业世界的变化速度比历史上任何时期都快，如果不随之改变，我很可能会长期表现不佳且变得无关紧要。这一点尤其体现在技术变革方面。尽管有许多社会、政治和经济力量在冲击市场，但日复一日的技术创新持续损害许多企业的经济表现，使其他企业变得过时。

<!--en-->
Just as it's easy to be too active, it's also easy to allow complacency to lead you to do the same things tomorrow that you did yesterday. That's true with investment processes, as well as with the choice of individual investments. Inertia could have kept me in my balance-sheet centric value investing box, but I recognized the need to change. I recognized that the world of business was changing around me at a more accelerated rate than at any point in history, and if I didn't change with it, then I would likely suffer long-term underperformance and irrelevancy. This is particularly true with regard to technological change. While there are a host ofsocial, political, and economic forces buffeting markets, day-by-day technological innovation continues to impair the economics of many businesses and render others obsolete.

近期加速的技术创新速度创造了大量新企业，而长期存在的企业正以加快的速度衰落。我本可以更快意识到历史性的技术进步对传统价值投资企业产生了负面影响。我在哲学上比一位表现出更大灵活性的合作伙伴更为固守旧观念，他帮助将投资组合向更合理的价格、更高品质、具有无可争议竞争力、稳健资产负债表和股东中心管理的成长型公司方向推进，这对投资者有利。投资的重要要素包括与聪明的人相处、考虑多种观点，并愿意承认自己的错误。

<!--en-->
The recent accelerated pace of technological innovation has created a multitude of new businesses, while long-established businesses are eroding at an accelerating rate. I could have appreciated more quickly that historic technological advances were adversely impacting the businesses of our more traditional value investments. I was more entrenched philosophically than one of my partners who exhibited greater flexibility and helped move our portfolio, to the benefit of our investors, further in the direction of reasonably priced, higher quality, growing companies characterized by unquestionable competitive strength, solid balance sheets, and shareholder-centric management. An important component of investing includes surrounding yourself with smart people, considering diverse points of view, and being willing to admit when you are wrong.

虽然企业每天都要决定如何快速自我革新，投资者同样如此。他们不仅必须在心理上准备好质疑现状（包括自身现状），还要准备应对不可避免地发生的、影响投资组合的意外情况。正如罗马哲学家老普林尼两千年前所说：“唯一确定的是，没有什么是确定的”，或者如现代哲学家迈克·泰森所说：“每个人都有计划，直到被打在脸上。”⁵知道会有意外情况，可以在意外发生时减少情感冲击，使投资方式更加冷静。它既防止我们因恐惧而放弃投资，也防止我们因恐惧而盲目投资。提前知道我们会偶尔不受欢迎，有助于我们在适当时做出理性决策。你不能控制整体投资者行为，但你可以控制自己。

<!--en-->
While businesses face the daily choice of how fast to reinvent themselves, the same can be said of investors, who must not only psychologically condition themselves to question the status quo (including their own) but to gird for the surprises that will inevitably occur that will impact positions in their portfolio. As the Roman philosopher Pliny the Elder noted two thousand years ago, “The only certainty is that nothing is certain,” or as has been attributed to that modern-day philosopher Mike Tyson: “Everyone has a plan till they get punched in the mouth.”⁵ Knowing there will be surprises takes some of the emotional sting out of them when they occur, allowing for a more clinical approach to investing. It keeps us from getting scared out of investments as much as it keeps us from getting scared into them. Knowing in advance that we will periodically be out of favor helps us act rationally when we are. You can’t control broad investor behavior but you can control your own.

# 结论

<!--en-->
*CONCLUSION*

最终，我是一名价值投资者，因为这对我来说有意义，符合我风险厌恶的性格。尽管自Graham和Dodd撰写经典著作以来发生了很多变化，以安全边际价格投资企业仍然能很好地服务投资者。我认为价值投资是我长期保护资本和产生吸引人回报的最佳方式。最相关的财务变量和指标可能会变化，但原则依然有效。[^1875]：1 Leucadia National现在属于Jefferies Financial Group。

<!--en-->
At the end of the day, I am a value investor because it makes sense to me and fits my risk-averse personality. While much has changed since Graham and Dodd wrote their masterwork, investing in companies at a price that offers a margin of safety continues to serve investors well. I believe that value investing is, for me, the best means to preserve capital and generate attractive returns over the long term. The most relevant financial variables and indicators may change, but the principles remain sound.
[^1875]: 1 Leucadia National is now part of Jefferies Financial Group.

2 CVS后记：管理层于2018年收购了Aetna，尽管他们声称这将创建更整合的解决方案以提供给客户，我们认为这次收购是防御性举措。我们无法预测其成功的可能性，这验证了我们之前清算该头寸的决定。

<!--en-->
2 CVS epilogue: Management went on to purchase Aetna in 2018, and despite their claims that this would create a more integrated solution that they could offer their customers, we felt the acquisition was defensive. Our inability to underwrite the likelihood of its success validated our earlier decision to liquidate the position.

3 查理·芒格，Daily Journal Corporation年度会议，2014年9月10日。

<!--en-->
3 Charlie Munger, Daily Journal Corporation Annual Meeting, September 10, 2014.

4 我隐藏了基金名称，因为买卖时机不当是基金投资者的问题，而非投资组合经理的问题。

<!--en-->
4 I've hidden the fund name as the inappropriate timing of purchases and sales was the fault of the fund's investors rather than its portfolio manager.

5 迈克·泰森，“每个人都有计划，直到被打在脸上。#Miketyson #Vintagetyson Pic.twitter.com/Yjghgqxrkk”，Twitter，2018年10月17日，https://twitter.com/MikeTyson/status/1052665864401633299.

<!--en-->
5 Mike Tyson, "Everyone Has a Plan till They Get Punched in the Mouth. #Miketyson #Vintagetyson Pic.twitter.com/Yjghgqxrkk," Twitter, October 17, 2018, https://twitter.com/MikeTyson/status/1052665864401633299.

## 与所有者经营者一起投资

<!--en-->
*Investing with Owner-Operators*

## 对齐的重要性

<!--en-->
*The Importance of Alignment*

作者：Benjamin Stein和Zachary Sternberg  我们两人非常幸运，受益于价值投资中智力慷慨与指导的传统，这一传统可追溯至Benjamin Graham和David Dodd出版《安全分析》的时候。2004年夏天，作为17岁的我们在海滩上学习时，其中一人研读了1940年版的书籍，重点标注了这部永恒经典中的以下两部分内容。

<!--en-->
by Benjamin Stein and Zachary Sternberg
The two of us have been very fortunate beneficiaries of the tradition of intellectual generosity and mentorship among value investors, a tradition whose roots date back to Benjamin Graham and David Dodd's publication of *Security Analysis*. In the summer of 2004, as a 17-year-old on the beach, one of us worked through the 1940 edition, underlining the following two sections of this timeless classic.

然而，我们必须认识到，内在价值是一个难以捉摸的概念……关键点是，安全分析并不试图精确确定某只证券的内在价值。它只需确定该价值是否足以保护债券，或证明购买股票是合理的——或者该价值比市场价格高得多或低得多。

<!--en-->
We must recognize, however, that intrinsic value is an elusive concept ... The essential point is that security analysis does not seek to determine exactly what is the intrinsic value of a given security. It needs only to establish either that the value is *adequate* to protect a bond or to justify a stock purchase—or else that the value is considerably higher or considerably lower than the market price.

从图表中可以明显看出，我们所说的分析因素对市场价格的影响既是部分的，也是间接的——部分是因为它与纯粹投机性因素竞争，后者以相反方向影响价格；也是因为它通过人们的情感和决策来发挥作用。换句话说，市场不是一台“称重机”，不是根据特定品质通过精确、非个人化的机制记录每种资产的价值。我们应该说，市场是一台“投票机”，无数人登记选择，这些选择部分出于理性，部分出于情感。

<!--en-->
It will be evident from the chart that the influence of what we call analytical factors over the market price is both *partial* and *indirect*—partial, because it frequently competes with purely speculative factors which influence the price in the opposite direction; and indirect because it acts through the intermediary of people's sentiments and decisions. In other words, the market is not a *weighing machine*, on which the value of each issue is recorded by an exact and impersonal mechanism, in accordance with its specific qualities. Rather should we say that the market is a *voting machine*, whereon countless individuals register choices which are the product partly of reason and partly emotion.

（《调查与方法》，第20–22页，第27页，1940年版）今天阅读这些文字，它们依然适用。它们清楚地阐述了安全分析师的目标，并提供了应用其最简单信息的框架：以低于实际价值的价格购买公司，并明白这样做是一门艺术而非科学。之前提到的图表列出了Graham和Dodd认为的“内在价值因素”。这些包括收益、股息、资产、资本结构、发行条款等。还有“未来价值因素”，包括管理和声誉、竞争环境和前景，以及数量、价格和成本可能发生的变化。未来价值因素介于“投机”和“投资”之间，但由于每种资产的价值都是其未来现金流的现值，我们专注于我们认为会影响未来现金流的定量和定性因素。

<!--en-->
(Survey and Approach, pp. 20–22, 27, 1940 edition)
Reading these lines today, they ring as true as ever. They clearly lay out the goal of the security analyst and offer a framework for applying its simplest message: buy companies for less than they are worth, and understand that doing so is an art and not a science. The chart previously referenced sets out the elements that Graham and Dodd considered “intrinsic value factors.” These include earnings, dividends, assets, capital structure, terms of the issue, and others. And then there are “future value factors,” including management and reputation, competitive conditions and prospects, and possible and probable changes in volume, price, and costs. Future value factors straddle the labels “speculation” and “investment,” but since the value of every asset is the present value of its future cash flows, we focus our efforts on the quantitative and qualitative inputs that in our judgment will affect future cash flows.

最初启发我们走上价值投资道路的是Graham最著名的学生Warren Buffett撰写的伯克希尔哈撒韦年度股东信。拥有能够长期增长并提升价值的企业的股权这一基本理念立刻让我们觉得合理。当你投资正在成长的企业时，时间对你有利；对于停滞不前的企业来说，时间显然不利。与像Warren Buffett这样优秀的管理者建立长期商业合作关系，与我们最契合，也符合我们的性格；相比之下，押注股价走势则显得短期化且过于交易化。

<!--en-->
It was the Berkshire Hathaway annual shareholder letters, written by Graham's best-known student, Warren Buffett, that initially inspired us to go down the value investing path. The basic premise of owning equity in businesses that can grow and increase in value for long periods of time made sense to us immediately. When you invest in a business that is growing, time is your friend; for a stagnant business, it decidedly is not. The idea of long-term business partnership with great managers, such as Warren Buffett has done with Berkshire Hathaway, resonated most with us and felt in sync with our personalities; betting on the movement of share prices, by contrast, felt short-term oriented and unnecessarily transactional.

我们于2004年在宾夕法尼亚大学大一期间相识，后来在Spruce House宿舍成为朋友。20岁时，我们做数学计算，发现1美元按每年20%的利率复利计算，到70岁时将变成9,100美元。即使按15%的利率计算，每美元也将值1,084美元。我们很快得出结论，应该立即开始行动。时间确实站在我们这边，只要我们保持自律和专注，就有机会实现目标。

<!--en-->
The two of us met in 2004 during our freshman year at the University of Pennsylvania, and we became friends living in the Spruce House dormitory. At age 20, we ran the math and realized that $1 compounded in value at 20% per year would turn into $9,100 by the time we were 70. Even at 15%, each dollar would be worth $1,084. We quickly came to the conclusion that we should get started immediately. Time really was our friend, and so long as we remained disciplined and focused, we would have a chance to begin to achieve our goals.

我们意识到，每一天都是研究一家上市公司并可能得出其股票值得持有的新机会。我们知道可以在几秒钟内查看任何公司的年度信函和财务报表。当时（现在仍然如此），我们几乎每天都可以决定持有世界上任何行业、任何领域的任何企业的一小部分股份，这是一个令人兴奋的想法。于是我们凑了一些自己的资金，开了E*TRADE账户，一年后，我们带着诚意去寻求亲友的支持。

<!--en-->
We realized that each day was a fresh opportunity to study a publicly owned business and perhaps reach the conclusion that its shares were worth owning. We knew that we could pull up the annual letters and financial statements of any company in a matter of seconds. It was an exciting idea then (and still is today) that almost every day we could decide to own a small piece of almost any business, in any industry, in any part of the world. So we put some of our own capital together, opened an E*TRADE account, and a year later went around hat in hand to try and gather support from friends and family.

我们喜欢在宿舍里进行投资，多年后依然如此喜爱。我们的原始理念和文化至今仍是我们价值观的一部分。Spruce House 并非对冲基金，而是朋友与家庭式的投资合作模式，仅有少数大型机构合作伙伴，投资组合集中在由创始人完全管理的公共和私人公司中。我们没有投资者关系部门或融资活动，希望未来几十年都能保持同样的合作伙伴关系。从一开始，我们的想法就是只拥有少数可靠且以长期为导向的合作伙伴，以便能在很长的时期里对他们产生实质性积极影响。

<!--en-->
We loved investing from our dorm rooms and love it even more years later. Our original mindset and culture remain part of our value system today. Spruce House is not a hedge fund, but a friends-and-family investment partnership, with only a handful of large institutional partners, and a concentrated portfolio composed of holdings in a group of public and private companies run exclusively by founders. We have no investor relations function or capital raising effort, and we hope to have the same group of partners around the table for decades to come. From the beginning, the idea was to have only a few reliable and long-term oriented partners for whom we could have a material beneficial impact over a very long period of time.

如今，自我们开始共同投资已过去17年，我们仍像终身合作伙伴一样管理委托给我们的资金，仿佛这些资金完全属于我们自己。因为我们的唯一使命一直是创造一种环境，让我们可以以最高可能的速度使资本增值，而不是建立资产管理业务。

<!--en-->
Today, 17 years after we started investing together, we continue to manage the capital entrusted to us as if the two of us would be lifelong partners and the capital were all our own. This is because our sole mission has always been to create an environment that allows us to compound our capital at the highest rate possible, not to build an asset management business.

多年来，我们投资了多种不同类型的企业。虽然我们总是能准确判断价格，但最成功的投资都源于两个关键因素的精准把握：确定要投资哪些企业，更重要的是，确定要让资产投资于谁。我们称之为“把合适的牌交给合适的人”。

<!--en-->
Over the years we have invested in many different types of businesses, and while we have always had a sharp pencil on price, our most successful investments have all been the result of being right on two essential factors: figuring out *which* businesses we wanted our net worths invested in, and even more important, *whom* we wanted our net worths invested alongside. We call this having the right cards in the right hands.

在伯克希尔哈撒韦1987年的年报中，沃伦·巴菲特指出：“许多首席执行官在资本分配方面的能力不足，这非常重要：在任职十年后，一个公司每年保留收益相当于净资产10%的CEO，将负责部署该业务中超过60%的资本。”这一简单事实对长期股权所有者有重大影响：随着时间的推移，整个业务的资本回报将与这些额外资本投入的回报趋于一致。要么管理层理性地考虑在其四个选择中重新投资资本——重新投资业务、收购其他业务、回购股票或支付股息——要么就不这么做。

<!--en-->
In Berkshire Hathaway's 1987 annual report, Warren Buffett pointed out "the lack of skill that many CEOs have at capital allocation is no small matter: after ten years on the job, a CEO whose company annually retains earnings equal to 10% of net worth will have been responsible for the deployment of more than 60% of all the capital at work in the business." This simple truth has major consequences for a long-term owner of equity: over time, the returns on capital of the entire business will converge with the returns from these additional capital commitments. Either management thinks rationally about reinvesting capital at satisfactory returns across their four options—to reinvest in the business, acquire other businesses, repurchase shares, or pay dividends—or they don't.

格雷厄姆对此持怀疑态度。在《普通股投资理论》中题为“‘回拨”收益的优点”的部分，格雷厄姆指出了许多人对管理层保留收益假设的弱点：“无论企业给所有者带来什么好处，只要这种好处不是以牺牲股东利益为代价获得的。”这个例外情况非常重要。无论是投资市场还是企业，利益一致性在投资资本时至关重要。如果你打算长期持有企业的权益，实际上你拥有了组织每天所做所有决策的总和，因此理解管理层及其思维方式对我们来说非常重要。

<!--en-->
Graham was skeptical on this subject. In the section on the Theory of Common-Stock Investment entitled "The Merits of 'Plowing-back' Earnings," Graham points out the weakness in the assumptions many make regarding managements retaining earnings: "Whatever benefits a business benefits its owners, provided the benefit is not conferred upon the corporation at the expense of the shareholders." That exception is no small matter. Alignment of interests is essential in investing capital, whether in markets or in businesses. If you are going to own interests in companies for the long term, you effectively own the sum of all the decisions made in the organization each day, so understanding managements and how they think seemed very important to us.

我们认为，日夜专注于企业的创始人是最优秀的商业伙伴。他们能够清晰表达组织的真实目标，这增加了商业决策以该目标为导向的可能性。相比之下，被聘请来管理公司的CEO可能有多重目标，且更关注短期利益。以长期为导向、专注的创始人更有可能成为优秀的资本分配者，而非不持有太多股票的董事会成员。（我们开玩笑称这些为“星号董事会”，因为代理声明中将董事持股低于1%列为*）。

<!--en-->
We developed the view that founders who live and breathe their businesses 24/7 make the best business partners. They are able to clearly articulate a true-north goal within their organizations, which increases the likelihood that business decisions are made with that goal in mind. By contrast, a CEO hired to run a company may have multiple objectives as well as a shorter-term orientation. A long-term oriented and focused founder is more likely to be an excellent allocator of capital than committees of board members who do not own much stock in the company. (We jokingly call these "asterisk boards" because the proxy statement lists director ownership of less than 1% as an *.)

我们总是问公开上市公司创始人一个问题：如果他们自己拥有100%股权，而公司是私有企业，他们会做出哪些不同的决定？理想情况下，他们说几乎没有差异。他们必须避免许多CEO和上市公司董事会所存在的短期导向。这些创始人知道，一家公司的价值不在于其短暂股价，而在于其长期现金流生成前景。

<!--en-->
One question we always ask public company founders is which decisions they would make differently if they owned 100% of the equity themselves and the company were private. Ideally, they say there are few, if any, differences from what they are already doing. It is crucial that they avoid the short-term orientation that afflicts so many CEOs and boards of publicly traded companies. These founders know that the truth about a company's value resides not in its ephemeral share price but in its prospects for longer-term cash flow generation.

例如，几年前，Spruce House是XPO Logistics的最大股东之一。XPO Logistics是美国最大的物流公司之一，由Brad Jacobs管理。2018年12月，注重细致收购的Jacobs即将完成XPO历史上最大规模的收购案。然而，几天内XPO的股价下跌了42%，Jacobs没有继续追求这笔交易，而是几乎一夜之间回购了10亿美元的XPO股票，最终回购了公司24%的股份。正如Jacobs当时向我们解释的那样，他从资本回报和时间回报的角度来审视每个决策，两者都表明应该进行大量股份回购而非收购。他无法通过打电话给经纪人并以折扣价购买更多自己熟悉的业务来获得更好的时间回报。这与谈判、融资和整合一项他本身了解较少的收购项目所付出的努力相比，结果非常有利。我们认为这种清晰性和敏捷性很罕见，确实并不存在于大多数董事会的集体意识中。自Jacobs在2011年9月掌控XPO以来，到2021年底的复合年回报率达到了36%，这并非巧合。

<!--en-->
For example, several years ago, Spruce House was one of the largest shareholders of XPO Logistics, one of the largest logistics companies in the United States, run by Brad Jacobs. In December 2018, Jacobs, a meticulous acquirer of businesses, was about to close the largest acquisition in XPO's history. However, XPO's share price dropped 42% in a matter of days, and instead of chasing the deal, Jacobs pivoted virtually overnight and repurchased $1 billion of XPO shares instead, ultimately buying back 24% of the company. As Jacobs explained to us at the time, he looks at each decision through the lens of return on capital and return on time, and both pointed to a large share repurchase instead of the acquisition. He could not beat the return on time achieved by calling his broker and owning a lot more of a business he already knew intimately at a discounted price. This compared very favorably to the effort involved in negotiating, financing, and integrating an acquisition he inherently knew less about than his own business. We find this type of clarity and agility to be rare, and it certainly does not reside in the collective consciousness of most boards. It is not a coincidence that since Jacobs took control of XPO in September of 2011, the compound annual return through year-end 2021 was 36%.

我们在寻找创始人时，主要看重理性思维和知识诚信。当头脑清晰同时具备领导能力和运营技能，以及明确的资本分配框架——以每股现金流来衡量商业价值——我们会特别感兴趣。

<!--en-->
The main qualities we are looking for in founders are rational thinking and intellectual honesty. We get particularly interested when clarity of mind is accompanied by leadership and operating skills and a clear framework for allocating capital to build business value as measured by cash flow per share.

在宾夕法尼亚大学读书的夏天，我们为著名价值投资者Bob Robotti工作，他后来成为了我们的导师和朋友。我们永远感激并欠Bob很多。他给我们提供了办公室，花尽可能多的时间教我们，始终以卓越的诚信作为榜样。我们还和他一起参观企业，环球旅行非常有趣。多年来，Bob在他的办公室主持了许多投资合作项目；每个项目的策略略有不同，但都深受《安全分析》中奠定的知识基础影响。当然，我们也研究了Bob长期持有的许多公司。他对这些企业运作方式及其所处生态系统的经济情况有近乎无限的细节了解，这使他能深刻理解行业竞争动态如何演变并影响未来回报。

<!--en-->
During our summers at Penn, we worked for the noted value investor Bob Robotti, who would come to be both amentor and a friend. We are eternally grateful and indebted to Bob. He gave us an office, spent as much time teaching us as we could absorb, and always set an example of extraordinary integrity. We also had so much fun traveling around the world with him visiting companies. Bob has hosted many investment partnerships in his office over the years; each of them had a slightly different strategy, but all were heavily influenced by the intellectual roots laid down in *Security Analysis*. Naturally, we studied many of the companies that Bob had owned for years. He knew virtually limitless details on how these businesses worked and the economics of the eco-systems in which they operated, which gave him a nuanced understanding of how the competitive dynamics of an industry were likely to evolve and affect future returns.

Robotti的方法让我们早期就研究并投资多种不同类型的企业。像许多受Graham和Dodd影响的投资者一样，我们最初专注于购买资产负债表处于折价、有硬资产价值支撑的下行风险保护的公司。我们持有在海外石油钻探、石油天然气服务、保险和航运领域经营的公司股份，还有2008年金融危机后经过重组的住房分销企业。这些企业通常依赖大量融资，拥有周期性终端市场，且客户具有强大的议价能力。虽然我们可以数学上评估有限的下行风险，但长期持有后的回报主要取决于管理层的再投资决策。在某些情况下，这类公司的再投资机会主要集中在资本密集型、周期性资产上，这可能是一个艰巨的任务。尽管我们在这些企业中取得了一些成功，但这往往是因为我们买入后成功出售了它们。我们认为无法指望这种情况在未来持续下去。我们更愿意尝试找到那些可能由优秀的CEO带领，可以持有十年或更长时间的企业。

<!--en-->
Robotti's approach led us to study and invest in many different types of businesses early on. Like so many influenced by Graham and Dodd, we began by focusing on buying companies with balance sheets trading at a discount, with downside protection supported by hard asset value. We owned shares in companies operating in offshore oil drilling, oil and gas services, insurance, and shipping, as well as a housing distribution businesses coming out of the other side of the 2008 financial crisis post their restructuring. These businesses often relied on large amounts of financing, had cyclical end markets, and had customers with substantial bargaining power. While we could mathematically assess the limited downside, the reality was that realizing a return over a long-term holding period would be based largely on management's reinvestment decisions. In some cases, the reinvestment opportunities for such companies were primarily in capital-intensive, cyclical assets, which could be a daunting prospect. Although we experienced some success in such businesses, this tended to be a result of us buying into and then selling them well. We did not think we could count on that continuing into the future. We felt more comfortable trying to identify businesses we might be able to own for a decade or more with excellent-owner operator CEOs at the helm.

一个例子可以追溯到2011年，当时我们开始购买FirstService Corporation的股票。该公司市值略超10亿美元，拥有多家业务，包括商业房地产服务经纪公司Colliers International；美国最大的住宅单位管理公司FirstService Residential；以及几家知名的房地产相关特许经营企业，如California Closets。但最重要的是，FirstService Corporation有Jay Hennick，自1995年该公司上市以来，他每年让股价增长20%。Hennick是天生的企业家。他在高中当救生员时萌生的清洁泳池生意的想法，让他意识到销售各种房地产服务的机会。Hennick采取了“一步创造价值”的方法。到2015年，FirstService和Colliers已成为独立上市公司，合并市值超过100亿美元。此后，Colliers发展出了房地产基金管理业务，管理资产达880亿美元，还有另一项房地产服务业务——在我们购买第一批股票时这项业务并不存在。当你与合适的人一起投资时，好事情就会发生。（反之亦然——不幸的是，我们以惨痛代价学到了这一教训。）

<!--en-->
One example dates back to 2011, when we began buying shares in FirstService Corporation, which had a market capitalization of just over $1 billion and owned several businesses, including the commercial real estate services brokerage Colliers International; FirstService Residential, the largest manager of housing units in the United States; and several well-known housing-related franchise businesses, such as California Closets. But most important, FirstService Corporation had Jay Hennick, who had compounded the share price since the company went public in 1995 at 20% per year. Hennick is a natural entrepreneur. His first job as a lifeguard in high school sparked the idea of starting a pool-cleaning business, which opened his mind to the opportunities available in selling a broad array of real estate services. Hennick has taken the approach of “creating value one step at a time.” By 2015, FirstService and Colliers had become separate public companies, with a combined market capitalization of over $10 billion, and Colliers has since developed a real estate fund management business with $88 billion of assets under management, another real estate services business, which did not exist when we purchased our first shares; good things happen when you invest with good people with the right priorities. (The opposite is also true—unfortunately, we have learned this lesson the hard way.)

我们倾向于投资那些既有安全边际又有多重盈利途径的项目。Jay Hennick将资本严格用于价格具有吸引力的收购项目，并制定合同条款以保护下行风险，这带来了广泛、低风险的增长。公司有一个天然的增长机会：作为Colliers本地市场分支的最佳且唯一的流动性买家。这使我们能够通过评估公司的当前运营和收购特许经营商的过往成功来预测未来。有时，我们能以远低于我们对其各业务未来现金流的保守估计价格，甚至以高于最初成本数倍的价格购买Colliers股票，因为随着Hennick找到下一个战略举措，增长空间似乎不断扩大。如今，其中一位成员担任Colliers董事会成员，我们对Colliers的未来感到兴奋，就像10年前一样。

<!--en-->
We are attracted to investments in which we have both a margin of safety and multiple ways to win. Jay Hennick’s disciplined deployment of capital into attractively priced acquisitions, with contractual terms structured to protect the downside, has led to extensive, low-risk growth. The company had one built-in opportunity to expand—as the best and only liquid buyer of Colliers’ local market affiliates. This allowed us to project the future by evaluating the company’s current operations and past success acquiring franchisees. From time to time we were able to purchase Colliers shares at significant discounts to our conservative estimate of the future cash flows of its various businesses, and even at multiples of our original cost, because of the growth runway that continually seemed to grow longer as Hennick figured out the next strategic move. Today, one of us serves on the Colliers board of directors, andwe are as excited about the future of Colliers today as we were 10 years ago.

我们投资的许多公司都采用自然增长+收购的模式。它们可能不属于最令人兴奋的行业，但在房地产服务、地板、隔热和物流等领域处于领先地位。这些公司拥有庞大的最终市场，提供基本且必要的产品或服务，面临高度行业分化，并能利用规模经济。然而，如果没有一位拥有高资本增值使命的业主经营者，这些投资就不会特别吸引人。我们认为重要的是要认识到，创始人并非进入这些业务，而是根据特定属性精心选择这些行业，从而通过整合实现大规模财富创造，并持续提升相对于竞争对手的客户价值主张。

<!--en-->
A number of the companies we have invested in follow an organic-growth-plus-acquisitions model. They may not be in the most exciting industries, but are leaders in areas such as real estate services, flooring, insulation, and logistics. Each enjoys large end markets, provides a basic and necessary product or service, experiences high levels of industry fragmentation, and can capture economies of scale. However, without an owner-operator on a mission to compound capital at high rates, these would not be particularly exciting investments. We think it is important to recognize that the founders did not fall into these businesses, but rather hand-picked these industries for their specific attributes, which would enable large-scale wealth creation through consolidation and continually improving their customer value proposition relative to competitors.

随着我们与创始人CEO相处时间越长，继续调整我们希望净资产如何投资，我们开始更认真思考未来，并设想可能的情景。例如，我们是Wayfair和Carvana的长期股东，我们认为它们是很难建立、但能带来难以竞争的消费产品，并通过规模效应改善（消费者和股东利益）的物流网络。这两个由创始人运营的企业都在大量投资，为消费者提供两种非常基础的产品——家居用品和二手车——的最大选择量和最快配送服务，竞争对手无法通过外包关键功能给第三方来复制这一点。我们学会了分解和重新编制损益表，以便识别可量化的增长投资。目标是了解底层单位经济模型，确定我们愿意以什么价格和什么增长率购买股票，同时了解长期下行保护的来源。由于增长前景尚未转化为当前现金流，Ben Graham会称这是投机行为。我们曾经（现在仍然）愿意相信，经济中的变化动态——比如从大型分散线下市场到线上市场的转变——将带来超过相应回报的收益。这对那些具有盈利运营能力、明确选择再投资当前现金流以满足客户需求的业务尤其如此。

<!--en-->
As we spent more and more time with founder CEOs and continued to calibrate how we wanted our net worths invested, we started thinking harder about the future and handicapping what it could look like. For example, we have been long-term shareholders in Wayfair and Carvana, which we see as logistics networks that are very difficult to build and which enable a consumer offering that is hard to compete with and improves (for both the consumer and for shareholders) with scale. Both of these founder-run businesses are investing heavily in providing consumers the largest selection and fastest delivery of two very basic products, home goods and used cars, which simply cannot be replicated by competitors outsourcing key functions to third parties. We learned to disaggregate and re-create income statements in order to unmask quantifiable growth investments. The goal was to understand underlying unit economics and figure out at what price and what growth rates we would be willing to purchase shares, while also understanding the sources of downside protection in the long term. Because the growth prospects had not yet turned into current cash flows, Ben Graham would call this speculation. We were (and still are) willing to bet that the winner-takes-most dynamics of shifts in the economy, such asthose from large, fragmented, offline markets to online markets, will provide more than a commensurate return. This is particularly true for businesses that have a proven ability to operate profitably and are clearly choosing to reinvest current cash flows to meet customer demand.

在许多方面，我们的方法仍在不断发展，以反映我们对格雷厄姆观点的理解。例如，他写道：“投资在最务实的情况下最为明智。”多年来，我们非常敬仰的一些人告诉我们，作为商人能让我们成为更好的投资者，而作为投资者又能让我们成为更好的商人。我们真正重视这一点，并试图将其应用于格雷厄姆的观点。

<!--en-->
In many ways, parts of our approach continue to evolve to reflect our own interpretation of Graham, such as when he writes that “investment is most intelligent when it is most businesslike.” Over the years, some of the people we look up to most have told us being a businessperson has made them a better investor, and being an investor has made them a better businessperson. We have really taken that to heart and tried to apply it to Graham’s observation.

近年来，一些不可预测的因素使投资变得更加困难，比如新冠疫情、政府的货币和财政政策反应、乌克兰战争，以及随之而来的通货膨胀和央行紧缩政策。在这种环境下，首席执行官们更难进行预测和经营企业，我们也清楚地意识到未来还存在其他未知挑战。截至2022年，我们拥有并关注的多家企业都处于看似极低的价格水平，而管理团队正在根据预测收入不足调整运营费用。同时，许多公司的短期投机头寸常常升至异常水平，暂时进一步压低股价。虽然当卖空者在我们投资的公司中持有头寸时，我们非常谦逊，并始终努力理解自己可能出错的地方，但同样重要的是要记住格雷厄姆和多德那句智慧的话：市场价格是为了服务你，而不是告诉你信息。

<!--en-->
In recent years, a number of wild cards have made investing more challenging, namely the Covid-19 pandemic and the government’s monetary and fiscal response, the war in Ukraine, and then the ensuing inflation and central bank tightening. It has become more difficult for CEOs to forecast and operate their businesses amid such conditions, and we are keenly aware that other unknown challenges certainly lie ahead. As we write, in 2022, many of the businesses we own and follow are available at what appear to be deep bargain levels while management teams adjust operating expenses in the light of shortfalls in forecasted revenues. Meanwhile, short interest has often risen to extraordinary levels across many of these companies, temporarily depressing share prices further. While we have great humility when short sellers take a position in one of our investments and always challenge ourselves to understand where we could be wrong, it is also important to remember Graham and Dodd’s sage observation that market prices are there to serve you, not to inform you.

格雷厄姆在31岁时开始他的投资事业，三年后他在1929年经济崩溃、大萧条和第二次世界大战期间管理着这家公司。很难想象在那些时期投资有多么困难。在1934年5月《安全分析》第一版的前言中，格雷厄姆和多德写道：“当我们写作时，我们必须对抗一种普遍观点，即金融灾难将成为永久趋势……”当头条新闻和日常商业对话不可避免地转向对宏观经济环境的恐惧时，我们会想起沃伦·巴菲特在伯克希尔哈撒韦1994年年度报告中的评论：³我们将继续忽视政治和经济预测，这对许多投资者和商人来说是一种昂贵的干扰。三十年前，没有人能预见越南战争的巨大扩展、工资和价格控制、两次石油危机、总统辞职、苏联解体、道琼斯指数一天内下跌508点（22.6%），或国库券利率在2.8%到17.4%之间波动这些重大事件。然而令人惊讶的是，这些重大事件都没有对本·格雷厄姆的投资原则产生丝毫影响。它们也没有破坏以合理价格购买优质企业的策略。因此，如果因为对未知事物的恐惧而推迟或改变资本配置，对我们来说代价会有多大呢？实际上，通常在对某种宏观事件担忧最严重的时候，我们做出最佳投资决策。恐惧是流行趋势的敌人，但也是基本主义者的朋友。

<!--en-->
Graham started his partnership when he was 31 years old, and three years later he managed it through the crash of 1929, followed by the Great Depression and then World War II. It’s difficult to imagine how much of a challenge it was investing in those times. In the preface to the first edition of *Security Analysis* in May of 1934, Graham and Dodd wrote, “While we were writing, we had to combat a wide-spread conviction that financial debacle was to be the permanent order ... .” Whenheadlines and casual business conversations cannot help but turn to fear of the macroeconomic environment, we are reminded of Warren Buffett's comment in Berkshire Hathaway's 1994 annual report:¹
We will continue to ignore political and economic forecasts, which are an expensive distraction for many investors and businessmen. Thirty years ago, no one could have foreseen the huge expansion of the Vietnam War, wage and price controls, two oil shocks, the resignation of a president, the dissolution of the Soviet Union, a one day drop in the Dow of 508 points (22.6%), or treasury bill yields fluctuating between 2.8% and 17.4%. But, surprise—none of these blockbuster events made the slightest dent in Ben Graham's investment principles. Nor did they render unsound the negotiated purchases of fine businesses at sensible prices. Imagine the cost to us, then, if we had let a fear of unknowns cause us to defer or alter the deployment of capital. Indeed, we have usually made our best purchases when apprehensions about some macro event were at a peak. Fear is the foe of the faddist, but the friend of the fundamentalist.

不过，我们注意到，这些宏观冲击对高成长型企业尤其有害，因为需求的急剧下降对其资产负债表的影响比几年前要大得多。他们的收入和支出项目所涉及的金额都比公司规模较小时要多得多。因此，我们一直鼓励高成长型企业在其资产负债表中建立额外的安全边际，尤其是在资本容易获得且似乎不需要的时候。虽然我们清楚地认识到维持强劲资产负债表带来的稀释成本，但我们认为管理层应始终优先投资于技术、系统和人才。如果不这样做，可能会削弱公司的竞争优势；如果依赖债务融资，还会限制公司未来投资新想法、潜在高回报项目的灵活性。对于未来不久可能产生大量自由现金流的高成长型企业来说，确保运营财务实力和人才储备至关重要。保持处于优势地位所带来的所有灵活性，使我们拥有的几家企业能够进行收购、以非常优惠的价格回购股票，并在经济困难时期继续增强未来盈利能力。同时努力改善分子和分母，确实非常有效。

<!--en-->
We would note, however, that these macro shocks can be particularly painful for higher-growth businesses, because a steep and sudden reduction in demand can have larger implications for their balance sheets than just a few years earlier. All of their revenue and expense line items have so many more dollars running through them than when the firms were smaller. As a result, we have been encouraging faster-growing companies to build in an extra margin of safety in their balance sheets, especially at times when capital is readily available to them and there seems to be no immediate need for it. While we are acutely aware of the costs of dilution from maintaining a stronger balance sheet, we believe managements should always prioritize investing in technology, systems, and talent. Failure to do so can erode a company's competitive advantage and if funded with debt, can limit the company's future flexibility to invest in new, potentially high-returning ideas. In high-growth businesses,which are likely to produce growing sums of free cash flow in the not-too-distant future, ensuring the operating financial strength and depth of talent must be paramount. Maintaining all of the flexibility that comes with being in a position of strength has allowed several of the businesses we own to make acquisitions, repurchase shares at very attractive prices, and continue to build up future earnings power through difficult economic periods. It's powerful if you can work on the numerator and the denominator at the same time.

投资很困难，往往令人感到谦逊。我们经常被提醒，必须保持思想开放，不断学习，专注于筛选众多潜在机会，确保每一分委托给我们的资金都能得到有效利用。随着我们逐渐扩大客户群体，我们会思考新的合作伙伴在困难时期会如何表现。我们只寻求那些真正具备数十年视野的合作伙伴。如果你拥有像我们这样高度集中的企业组合，且不进行空头交易或对冲操作，那么你的收益肯定会存在显著波动；这是无法避免的。沃伦·巴菲特曾著名地提到，他一生中有三次净资产减半；本·格雷厄姆据说两次差点破产。当前，在2022年秋季，我们正在经历一次非常痛苦的下跌期。真正的长期视角是我们所知的唯一方法，可以让我们超越短期业务表现和股价短期波动，对五年后的价值做出可操作的预测。对每个企业有深入的基本理解、拥有紧密合作的合作伙伴团队，以及不使用杠杆，这些都是度过这些时期的关键要素。重要的是要记住，没有企业能直线增长。今天拥有成功企业看似明显的回报，实际上在过程中多次经历了焦虑、不确定和压力。我们最钦佩的投资者具有稳定的性格，不会在好时光中过于兴奋，也不会在艰难时期过于情绪化。他们有耐心和纪律，只参与他们熟悉的项目；他们已经做好了应对不受欢迎观点的准备；或许最重要的是，他们都拥有强烈的乐观意识，认为每天都有伟大的投资等待被发现。

<!--en-->
Investing is hard and often humbling. We are regularly reminded that we must remain intellectually open, constantly learning, and focused on calibrating a multitude of potential opportunities to ensure that each dollar entrusted to us is hard at work. As we have slowly grown our client base over time, we think about how any new partner might behave in difficult times. We seek only those partners who truly have a multidecade view. If you own a very concentrated portfolio of companies as we do, and don't short or hedge, you are guaranteed to have significant volatility in your returns; there is no way around it. Warren Buffett has famously written about having his net worth cut in half three times in his life; Ben Graham reportedly nearly went broke twice. As we write, in the fall of 2022, we are going through one of these very painful drawdowns. A truly long-term view is the only way we know of to look past near-term business performance and short-term share price volatility and to make actionable estimates of value five years from now. Investing with a deep fundamental understanding of each business, a tightly aligned group of partners, and not using leverage are the key ingredients needed to get through these periods. It's crucial to remember that no business grows in a straight line. What might look like obvious rewards from owning successful businesses today were nonetheless tested more than once with periods of anxiety, uncertainty, and stress along the way. The investors we admire most have an even temperament that means not getting too excited in the good times, or too downtrodden and emotional in the tough times. They have the patience and discipline to swing only at pitches they are comfortable with, they have done the work to ride out often unpopular views, and perhaps most important, they all possessa deep sense of optimism that each day the next great investment is out there waiting to be discovered.

巴菲特，沃伦。《主席信》。伯克希尔哈撒韦公司，1995年3月7日。https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1994.html. 第31章

<!--en-->
Buffett, Warren. "Chairman's Letter." Berkshire Hathaway Inc., March 7, 1995. https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/letters/1994.html.
CHAPTER 31

## 收入账户分析

<!--en-->
*Analysis of the Income Account*

在我们关于普通股投资理论的历史讨论中，我们探讨了重点从企业净资产转移到其资本收益能力的过程。尽管这种发展有充分且有力的理由，但它确实消除了过去投资分析所依赖的许多基础，使其面临更多风险。当投资者在评估股票时，能够采取与评估自身企业相同的态度时，他处理的是与其个人经验和成熟判断相关的概念。如果有足够的信息，他不太可能偏离太远，除了对未来收益能力的估计之外。资产负债表和损益表之间的关联为他提供了对内在价值的双重验证，这对应于银行或信用机构评估企业信贷资格的公式。

<!--en-->
IN OUR HISTORICAL DISCUSSION of the theory of investment in common stocks we traced the transfer of emphasis from the net worth of an enterprise to its capitalized earning power. Although there are sound and compelling reasons behind this development, it is none the less one that has removed much of the firm ground that formerly lay—or seemed to lie—beneath investment analysis and has subjected it to a multiplicity of added hazards. When an investor was able to take very much the same attitude in valuing shares of stock as in valuing his own business, he was dealing with concepts familiar to his individual experience and matured judgment. Given sufficient information, he was not likely to go far astray, except perhaps in his estimate of future earning power. The interrelations of balance sheet and income statement gave him a double check on intrinsic values, which corresponded to the formulas of banks or credit agencies in appraising the eligibility of the enterprise for credit.
