* 1925年支付的5%股票股息为1,737,770美元。两个数字之间存在无法解释的差异，其他年份则相同。† 不包括前几年适用的229,017美元联邦税退还。在判断联合雪茄店当前收益中是否包含租赁权增值时，可能需要考虑多个因素。
1. 租赁权本质上既是负债也是资产。它们是对所占用场所支付租金的义务。具有讽刺意味的是，正是这些租赁权最终导致联合雪茄店破产。
2. 假设租赁权可以为承租人带来资本价值，这种价值是非常无形的，在资产负债表上将此类无形资产的价值高于实际成本是违反会计原则的。
3. 如果任何资本资产的价值要被高估，这种增加必须计入资本盈余。无论如何都不能将其视为*收入*。
4. 联合雪茄店租赁权的20,000,000美元增值发生在1924年5月之前，但在后续年份中被*当作收入处理*。因此，1927年利润中包含的2,437,000美元增值与那一年的经营或发展情况并无关联。
5. 如果租赁权确实增加了价值，其影响应该体现在从这些有利地点获得的*更高收益*中。如果因这种增值而再次确认收益，意味着重复计算同一价值。然而实际上，考虑到通过额外资本化进行的业务扩展，联合雪茄店的每股收益并没有上升趋势。
6. 任何给予租赁权的价值都必须在租赁期间进行摊销。如果联合雪茄店投资者为这些有价值的租赁权支付了高价格，那么他们应该从收益中扣除一笔费用，以在租赁到期时冲减这一资本价值。⁴ 联合雪茄店公司继续按*原始成本*来摊销其租赁权，显然这个成本几乎为零。因此，令人惊讶的事实是：如果租赁权价值有所增值，那么这种增值的影响应该会*减少*后续经营利润，因为需要更多的摊销费用。
7. 联合雪茄店1924–1927年的收入虚增行为，因未能在年度报告中清晰披露事实而更加可耻。⁵ 在开始披露基本信息近三年后，才向纽约证券交易所进行了披露。这可能是由于当时公开发行由大型金融机构包销的优先股，出于法律考虑而不得不这样做。第二年，将租赁权增值纳入收益的政策被停止了。因此，联合雪茄店的这些会计操作可以恰当地描述为：在当期收益中*未解释地*包含*虚拟*的*无形资产*增值——实际上该资产是一种*负债*，这种增加与*之前*的时期有关，如果真的发生增值，其正确影响将是由于更高的摊销费用而*减少*后续实际收益。如Park和Tilford案例所述，联邦所得税检查也会在应用于联合雪茄店时产生有趣的结果，如下表所示。**从前述案例中得出的教训。**联合雪茄店的案例可以给出具有重大实用价值的教训：当企业采用可疑的会计政策时，投资者必须避免所有相关证券，无论其中一些看起来多么安全或吸引人。联合雪茄店优先股的情况很好地说明了这一点，它在连续多年中提供了非常令人印象深刻的统计数据，但后来勉强避免了完全破产。面对上述详细账目，投资者可能会认为该股票仍然完全可靠，因为当收益虚报被纠正后，安全边际仍然足够大。但这种推理是错误的。你不能进行定量推断来容忍不道德的管理；处理这种情况的唯一方法是避免它。

<!--en-->
* The 5% stock dividend paid in 1925 amounted to $1,737,770. There is an unexplained difference between the two figures, which in the other years are identical.
† Excluding refund of federal taxes of $229,017 applicable to prior years.
In passing judgment on the inclusion of leasehold appreciation in the current earnings of United Cigar Stores, a number of considerations might well be borne in mind.
1. Leaseholds are essentially as much a liability as they are an asset. They are an obligation to pay rent for premises occupied. Ironically enough, these very leaseholds of United Cigar Stores eventually plunged it into bankruptcy.
2. Assuming leaseholds may acquire a capital value to the occupant, such value is highly intangible, and it is contrary to accounting principles to mark up above actual cost the value of such intangibles in a balance sheet.
3. If the value of any capital asset is to be marked up, such enhancement must be credited to Capital Surplus. By no stretch of the imagination can it be considered as *income*.
4. The $20,000,000 appreciation of the United Cigar Stores leases took place prior to May 1924, but it was *treated as income in subsequent years*. There was thus no connectionbetween the $2,437,000 appreciation included in the profits of 1927 and the operations or developments of that year.
5. If the leaseholds had really increased in value, the effect should be visible in *larger earnings* realized from these favorable locations. Any other recognition given this enhancement would mean counting the same value twice. In fact, however, allowing for extensions of the business financed by additional capitalization, the per-share earnings of United Cigar Stores showed no advancing trend.
6. Whatever value is given to leaseholds must be amortized over the life of the lease. If the United Cigar Stores investors were paying a high price for the shares because of earnings produced by these valuable leases, then they should *deduct* from earnings an allowance to write off this capital value by the time it disappears through the expiration of the leases.⁴ The United Cigar Stores Company continued to amortize its leaseholds on the basis of *original cost*, which apparently was practically nothing.
The surprising truth of the matter, therefore, is that the effect of the appreciation of leasehold values—if it had occurred—should have been to *reduce* the subsequent operating profits by an increased amortization charge.
7. The padding of the United Cigar Stores income for 1924–1927 was made the more reprehensible by the failure to reveal the facts clearly in the annual reports to shareholders.⁵ Disclosure of the essential facts to the New York Stock Exchange was made nearly three years after the practice was initiated. It may have been compelled by legal considerations growing out of the sale to the public at that time of a new issue of preferred stock, underwritten by large financial institutions. The following year the policy of including leasehold appreciation in earnings was discontinued.
These accounting maneuvers of United Cigar Stores may be fairly described, therefore, as the *unexplained* inclusion in current earnings of an *imaginary* appreciation of an *intangible* asset—the asset being in reality a *liability*, the enhancement being related to a *previous* period and the proper effect of theappreciation, if it had occurred, being to *reduce* the subsequent realized earnings by virtue of higher amortization charges.
The federal-income-tax check, described in the Park and Tilford example, will also give interesting results if applied to United Cigar Stores as shown in the table below.
**Moral Drawn from Foregoing Examples.** A moral of considerable practical utility may be drawn from the United Cigar Stores example. When an enterprise pursues questionable accounting policies, *all* its securities must be shunned by the investor, no matter how safe or attractive some of them may appear. This is well illustrated by United Cigar Stores Preferred, which made an exceedingly impressive statistical showing for many successive years but later narrowly escaped complete extinction. Investors confronted with the strange bookkeeping detailed above might have reasoned that the issue was still perfectly sound, because, when the overstatement of earnings was corrected, the margin of safety remained more than ample. Such reasoning is fallacious. You cannot make a quantitative deduction to allow for an unscrupulous management; the only way to deal with such situations is to avoid them.

* 排除229,000美元的退税，显然适用于前几年。† 调整后，这也报告为2,947,000美元。**对收到的股票红利进行虚拟估值。**从1922年开始，联合雪茄店的大部分普通股由烟草产品公司持有，该公司由相同利益集团控制。这是一家重要公司，1926年和1927年其股票平均市值超过100,000,000美元。烟草产品的会计做法又引入了另一种虚增收入账户的方法，即对收到的股票红利进行虚拟估值。1926年的公司收益表如下：

<!--en-->
* Eliminating tax refund of $229,000 evidently applicable to prior years.
† This is also reported as $2,947,000, after an adjustment.
**Fictitious Value Placed on Stock Dividends Received.** From 1922 on most of the United Cigar Stores common shares were held by Tobacco Products Corporation, an enterprisecontrolled by the same interests. This was an important company, the market value of its shares averaging more than $100,000,000 in 1926 and 1927. The accounting practice of Tobacco Products introduced still another way of padding the income account, *viz.*, by placing a fictitious valuation upon stock dividends received.
For the year 1926 the company's earnings statement read as follows:

<table><tr><td>净利润</td><td>$10,790,000</td></tr><tr><td>所得税</td><td>400,000</td></tr><tr><td>A类股息</td><td>3,136,000</td></tr><tr><td>普通股的余额</td><td>7,254,000</td></tr><tr><td>每股收益</td><td>11</td></tr><tr><td>普通股的市场范围</td><td>117-95</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>Net income</td><td>$10,790,000</td></tr><tr><td>Income tax</td><td>400,000</td></tr><tr><td>Class A dividend</td><td>3,136,000</td></tr><tr><td>Balance for common stock</td><td>7,254,000</td></tr><tr><td>Earned per share</td><td>11</td></tr><tr><td>Market range for common</td><td>117-95</td></tr></table>

关于该时期公司事务的详细信息从未发布（纽约证券交易所似乎不愿意在提交极其简略的信息后上市新股票）。然而，有足够的信息表明，净收入大致由以下部分组成：

<!--en-->
Detailed information regarding the company's affairs during that period has never been published (the New York Stock Exchange having been unaccountably willing to list new shares on submission of an extremely sketchy exhibit). Sufficient information is available, however, to indicate that the net income was made up substantially as follows:

<table><tr><td>从向美国烟草公司出租资产中获得的租金</td><td>$ 2,500,000</td></tr><tr><td>联合雪茄店普通股的现金股息（总支付的80%）</td><td>2,950,000</td></tr><tr><td>联合雪茄店普通股的股票红利（面值184万美元），减去费用</td><td>5,340,000</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>$10,790,000</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>Rental received from lease of assets to American Tobacco Co.</td><td>$ 2,500,000</td></tr><tr><td>Cash dividends on United Cigar Stores common (80% of total paid)</td><td>2,950,000</td></tr><tr><td>Stock dividends on United Cigar Stores common (par value $1,840,000), less expenses</td><td>5,340,000</td></tr><tr><td></td><td>$10,790,000</td></tr></table>

需要注意的是，Tobacco Products将从联合雪茄店收到的股票红利估值约为面值的三倍，即相当于联合雪茄店将其作为盈余列账的价值的三倍。Tobacco Products的估值基础可能是联合雪茄店股票的市场价格，但由于Tobacco Products并不持有大量股份，该价格很容易被操纵。

<!--en-->
It is to be noted that Tobacco Products must have valued the stock dividends received from United Cigar Stores at about three times their face value, *i.e.*, at three times the value at which United Cigar charged them against surplus. Presumably the basis of this valuation by Tobacco Products was the market price of United Cigar Stores shares, which price was easily manipulated due to the small amount of stock not owned by Tobacco Products.

当控股公司将收到的股票红利计入高于子公司所确定的价值时，就会出现一种特别危险的收益金字塔式操作形式。自1929年起，纽约证券交易所就制定了严格规定禁止这种行为。（这一点在第30章中讨论过。）对于Tobacco Products来说，这种操作尤其不可接受，因为股票红利最初是为了体现一种虚构的收益要素，即租赁权益的增值。通过不道德利用控股公司机制，这些虚拟利润实际上被放大了三倍。

<!--en-->
When a holding company takes into its income account stock dividends received at a higher value than that assigned them by the subsidiary that pays them, we have a particularly dangerous form of pyramiding of earnings. The New YorkStock Exchange, beginning in 1929, has made stringent regulations forbidding this practice. (The point was discussed in Chap. 30.) In the case of Tobacco Products the device was especially objectionable because the stock dividend was issued in the first instance to represent a fictitious element of earnings, *i.e.*, the appreciation of leasehold values. By unscrupulous exploitation of the holding-company mechanism these imaginary profits were effectively multiplied by three.

按合并收益计算，Tobacco Products 1926年的报告内容如下：

<!--en-->
On a consolidated earnings basis, the report of Tobacco Products for 1926 would read as follows:

<table><tr><td>American Tobacco Co. lease income, less income tax, etc.</td><td style="text-align: right;">$2,100,000</td></tr><tr><td>80% of earnings on United Cigar Stores common</td><td style="text-align: right;">6,828,000*</td></tr><tr><td></td><td style="text-align: right; border-top: 1px solid black;">$8,928,000</td></tr><tr><td>Class A dividend</td><td style="text-align: right;">3,136,000</td></tr><tr><td>Balance for common</td><td style="text-align: right;">$5,792,000</td></tr><tr><td>Earned per share</td><td style="text-align: right;">$7.27</td></tr></table>

* 不包括租赁权益增值。Tobacco Products报告的普通股收益为每股11美元，实际上被高估了约50%。可以说，华尔街有一句格言：如果发现账目操纵，那么某种形式的股票操作也会存在。熟悉可疑金融手段有助于分析师甚至公众发现此类行为。⁶

<!--en-->
* Excluding leasehold appreciation.
The reported earnings for Tobacco Products common given as $11 per share are seen to have been overstated by about 50%.
It may be stated as a Wall-Street maxim that where manipulation of accounts is found, stock juggling will be found also in some form or other. Familiarity with the methods of questionable finance should assist the analyst and perhaps even the public, in detecting such practices when they are perpetrated.⁶

## 子公司和合并报告

<!--en-->
*SUBSIDIARY COMPANIES AND CONSOLIDATED REPORTS*

本标题介绍第二种报告收益的调整方式。当一家企业控制一个或多个重要子公司时，需要采用“合并”收入账户来真实反映全年经营情况。仅显示母公司业绩的数据是不完整的，可能具有很大误导性。如前所述，它们要么因未显示子公司的所有当前利润而低估收益，要么因未扣除子公司的亏损或将子公司的股息计入超出当年实际收入的金额而高估收益。

<!--en-->
This title introduces our second general type of adjustment of reported earnings. When an enterprise controls one or more important subsidiaries, a *consolidated* income account is necessary to supply a true picture of the year's operations. Figures showing the parent company's results only are incomplete and may be quite misleading. As previously remarked, they may either understate the earnings by notshowing all the current profits made by the subsidiaries, or they may overstate the earnings by failure to deduct subsidiaries' losses or by including dividends from subsidiaries in excess of their actual income for the year.

**过去和现在的做法。**在早些年，子公司业绩的披露是管理层任意选择的，许多重要数据被保密。⁷在1933年之前的一段时间里，纽约证券交易所要求“新上市”公司要么在合并报表中展示子公司业绩，要么单独列出。但自1934年法案通过后，所有注册公司都必须在年度报告中向委员会提供这些信息，因此实际上所有公司都在向股东陈述时遵循相同程序。

<!--en-->
**Former and Current Practices.** In earlier years disclosure of subsidiaries' results was a matter of arbitrary election by management, and in many cases important data of this kind were kept secret.⁷ For some time prior to 1933 the New York Stock Exchange had insisted in connection with *new* listings that the results of subsidiaries be presented either in a consolidated statement or separately. But since passage of the 1934 act, all registered companies are required to supply this information in their annual reports to the Commission, and therefore practically all follow the same procedure in their statements to stockholders.

**合并程度。**即使在所谓的“合并报表”中，合并程度也差异很大。Woolworth合并了国内和加拿大子公司，但不合并海外关联公司。美国烟草仅合并完全控股的国内子公司。现在大多数公用事业公司都发布合并报告，包括其控制的所有公司（通过多数投票权），并在“少数权益”标题下扣除适用于其他公司的收益部分。⁸在铁路领域，除非子公司100%由该公司拥有且作为系统的一部分运营，否则很少进行合并。因此，Atlantic Coast Line并未反映路易斯维尔和纳什维尔公司分红后的份额，后者由该公司51%拥有但独立运营。Wheeling and Lake Erie公司53%的投票控制权也类似，该控制权由Nickel Plate（纽约、芝加哥和圣路易斯铁路公司）持有。

<!--en-->
**Degree of Consolidation.** Even in so-called "consolidated statements" the degree of consolidation varies considerably. Woolworth consolidates its domestic and Canadian subsidiaries but not its foreign affiliates. American Tobacco consolidates only its wholly owned domestic subsidiaries. Most utilities now issue consolidated reports including all companies controlled by them (by ownership of a majority of the voting stock) and deduct the portion of the earnings applicable to others under the heading of "minority interest."⁸ In the railroad field results are rarely consolidated unless the subsidiary is both 100% owned and also operated as an integral part of the system. Hence, Atlantic Coast Line does not reflect its share of the results after dividends of Louisville and Nashville, which is 51% owned but separately operated. The same is true with respect to the 53% voting control of Wheeling and Lake Erie held by the Nickel Plate (New York, Chicago, and St. Louis Railroad Company).

**非合并利润和亏损的调整。**现在，工业公司通常会在收入账户或脚注中说明在扣除股息后，对非合并子公司的利润或亏损所持有的权益。

<!--en-->
**Allowance for Nonconsolidated Profits and Losses.** It is now frequent procedure for industrial companies to indicate either in the income account or in a footnote thereto their equity in the profits or losses of nonconsolidated subsidiaries after allowance for dividends.

*示例：* 美国烟草公司1938年的报告在脚注中指出，非合并子公司派发的股息超过其收益427,000美元。赫拉克勒斯火药公司也以脚注形式报告了当年类似的数字257,514美元，而1937年之前，它会将这些关联公司的未分配收益份额列在“其他收入”标题下。铁路公司处理这一事项的方式不同。例如，阿奇森铁路现在在其报告的附录中提供关联公司的完整资产负债表和收入账户数据，但数据仍仅反映从这些公司派发的股息。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* The 1938 report of American Tobacco Company showed by way of footnote that dividends received from nonconsolidated subsidiaries exceeded their earnings by $427,000. Hercules Powder reported a similar figure of $257,514 for that year, in footnote form, whereas prior to 1937 it had included its share of the undistributed earnings of such affiliates under the heading “Other Income.” Railroad companies handle this matter differently. The Atchison, for example, now supplies full balance sheet and income account data of affiliates in an Appendix to its own report, which continues to reflect only the dividends received from these companies.

如果收入账户中尚未调整非合并关联公司的业绩，且涉及金额较大，分析师应调整报告的收益，以反映非合并关联公司的业绩。这里的标准不是控制的技术问题，而是持股的*重要性*。

<!--en-->
The analyst should adjust the reported earnings for the results of nonconsolidated affiliates, if this has not already been done in the income account and if the amounts involved are significant. The criterion here is not the technical question of control but the *importance* of the holdings.

*示例：* 一方面，对联合太平洋在伊利诺伊中央铁路等铁路公司的持股进行此类计算并不常见，也不值得这样做。这些持股虽然数量庞大，但规模不足以显著影响联合太平洋的普通股。另一方面，北方太平洋和大北方公司持有芝加哥、伯灵顿和昆西股票，各自持股比例低于控制性权益（48.6%），调整结果清晰可见。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* On the one hand it is not customary, nor does it seem worth while, to make such calculations with respect to the holdings of Union Pacific in Illinois Central and other railroads. These holdings, although substantial, do not bulk large enough to affect the Union Pacific common stock materially. On the other hand, the adjustment is clearly indicated in the case of the ownership of Chicago, Burlington, and Quincy stock by Northern Pacific and Great Northern, each holding less than a controlling interest (48.6%).

同样，杜邦在通用汽车中的权益约占总发行股份的23%，其对控股公司的影响无疑足够大，需要调整收益以反映通用汽车的业绩。实际上，杜邦每年都会通过调整*盈余*来反映前一年通用汽车持股的账面价值变化。不过，分析师更希望同时进行调整，并纳入杜邦计算的收益中。此类调整对1929–1938年杜邦收益的影响见上表。

<!--en-->
Similarly, the interest of Du Pont in General Motors, representing about 23% of the total issue, is undoubtedly significant enough in its effect on the owning company to warrant adjustment of its earnings to reflect the results of General Motors. This is actually done by Du Pont each year in the form of an adjustment of *surplus* to reflect the previous year's change in the book value of its General Motors holdings. The analyst would prefer, however, to make the adjustment concurrently and to include it in the calculated earnings of Du Pont. The effect of such adjustments on the earnings of Du Pont for 1929–1938 is shown in the previous table.

通用汽车公司1931年的报告值得关注，因为它包含了本章及前一章建议的那种补充计算——即不包括特殊和非经常性利润或损失，但包含通用汽车在非合并子公司业绩中的权益。报告中包含1931年和1930年的每股收益声明：

<!--en-->
The report of General Motors Corporation for 1931 is worthy of appreciative attention because it includes a supplementary calculation of the kind suggested in this and the previous chapter *i.e.*, exclusive of special and nonrecurring profits or losses and inclusive of General Motors' interest in the results of nonconsolidated subsidiaries. The report contains the following statement of per-share earnings for 1931 and 1930:

*包括非合并子公司未分配利润或损失的权益的每股收益*

<!--en-->
*Earnings per Share, Including the Equity in Undivided Profits or Losses of Nonconsolidated Subsidiaries*

**统计机构的建议程序。** 尽管此程序可能使报告复杂化，但实际上它是对抗单纯关注每股收益这一单一数字的普通股票分析过度简化的有效方法。统计手册和机构自然会在对公司进行分析时强调每股收益。然而，如果公司在以下任何方面报告存在异常或复杂性，且无法进行令人满意的修正，他们可以省略所有情况下的每股收益计算，从而提供更实用的服务：

<!--en-->
**Suggested Procedure for Statistical Agencies.** Although this procedure may seem to complicate a report, it is in fact a salutary antidote against the oversimplification of common-stock analysis which resulted from exclusive preoccupation with the single figure of per-share earnings. The statistical manuals and agencies have naturally come to feature the per-share earnings in their analyses of corporations. They might, however, perform a more useful service if they omitted a calculation of the per-share earnings in all cases where the company's reports appear to contain irregularities or complications in any of the following directions and where a satisfactory correction is not practicable:

1. 由于收入中包含非经常性项目，或由于可能应计入收入账户的盈余费用。
2. 因为子公司的当前业绩未能准确反映在母公司的报表中。
3. 因为折旧和其他摊销费用的计算并不规律。⁹ **子公司支付的特别股息。**当非合并子公司收益能够累积到其盈余账户中时，它们之后可以通过向母公司支付大量特别股息来弥补糟糕年度的业绩。*示例：*1922年，Erie Railroad Company从Pennsylvania Coal Company和Hillside Coal and Iron Company那里获得了总计11,000,000美元的此类股息。Northern Pacific Railway Company同样在1930年和1931年通过从Chicago, Burlington, and Quincy Railroad Company、Northern Express Company以及 Northwestern Improvement Company（后者是房地产、煤炭和铁矿石子公司）处获取大量特别股息来弥补亏损。New York, Chicago, and St. Louis Railroad Company在1931年的业绩中，包括对其持有的Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway Company优先股票进行的约1,600,000美元的回溯股息，其中只有一部分是Wheeling公司当年赚取的。这种在好年份隐藏子公司利润、在坏年份利用它们的做法，作为稳定报告业绩的方法似乎值得称赞。但这种善意的欺骗行为受到开明界的反对，纽约证券交易所较近的规定就说明了这一点，该规定要求充分披露子公司的业绩。管理层的责任是披露每个时期的真实情况；股东的职责是通过平均繁荣与萧条时期的业绩来推断公司的"正常盈利能力"。即使是为了保持业绩平衡而操纵报告业绩，也是不可接受的，因为它可能轻易导致更邪恶的操纵行为。**通过母子公司关系扭曲业绩。**已有实例表明，母子公司关系可用于造成报告收入的惊人扭曲。我们将举两个来自铁路行业的例子。这些案例尤为突出，因为Interstate Commerce Commission严格的会计规定本应防止任何业绩误导行为。*示例：*1925年，Western Pacific Railroad Corporation向其优先股支付7.56美元股息，普通股支付5美元股息。其收入账显示，收益略高于所支付的股息。这些收益几乎完全来自其运营子公司Western Pacific Railroad Company收取的4,450,000美元股息。然而，铁路公司本身的年度收益仅为2,450,000美元。此外，其累计盈余不足以支持母公司希望报告的年度收入中的更大股息。为此，母公司不惜采取极端措施，向运营公司"捐赠"1,500,000美元，并立即将其作为股息从子公司收回。该捐赠被计入其"盈余"；收到这笔钱则作为股息报告为"收益"。通过这种方式，它能够报告普通股"赚取"了5美元，实际上适用收益仅约为每股2美元。为了支持我们之前关于不良会计行为具有传染性的观点，我们可以指出，1925年的Western Pacific案例在1930年和1931年被New York, Chicago, and St. Louis Railroad Company（“Nickel Plate”）所效仿。细节如下：1929年，Nickel Plate通过子公司将其持有的Pere Marquette股票出售给同样受控制的Chesapeake and Ohio。 此次销售实现了10,665,000美元的利润，该收益被正确计入盈余中。1930年，Nickel Plate需要增加收入，于是从盈余中提取了10,665,000美元的利润，将其返还给子公司的资金库，然后以"股息"的形式从该子公司获得3,000,000美元，并将其纳入1930年的*收入*中。1931年的收入账户中又包含了2,100,000美元的类似股息。这些特殊手段可能是为了实现一个必要目的——获得足够大的净收入，使公司的债券能够用于信托基金投资。¹⁰然而，结果与其他所有误导性的会计做法相同：即误导公众，让内部人员获得不公平的优势。**子公司亏损的更广泛意义**。在本章中，我们指出安全分析必须充分考虑子公司的结果，无论是利润还是亏损。但可能会提出这样一个问题：子公司的亏损是否必然直接抵消母公司的收益？为什么一家公司因为拥有某些东西——在这种情况下是无利可图的权益——而价值降低？它能否随时通过出售、清算甚至放弃子公司来结束亏损？因此，如果假设管理良好，我们是否也应认为子公司亏损最多是暂时的，应被视为非经常性项目，而非正常收益的扣除项？这一点与前章讨论的闲置工厂费用以及企业无利可图的*部门*问题类似，将在后续中探讨。对于我们提出的这些问题，没有简单的答案。实际上，如果子公司可以清算而不会对整个业务产生不利影响，将这种亏损视为暂时性的是合理的——因为合理的判断是，在短期内，子公司要么会变得盈利，要么会被处置。但如果母公司与子公司之间存在重要的业务关系，例如后者提供商品渠道、供应廉价材料或承担重要开销，那么结束其亏损就不是那么简单的事情。进一步分析后，可能会发现子公司所有的或大部分亏损都是母公司利润中必要的因素。确定每个案例中涉及哪些业务关系并非易事。像分析中的许多其他要素一样，这一点通常需要超出报告数字范围的调查。以下例子将说明我们一直在处理的类型的情况和分析。*示例A：Purity Bakeries Corporation*。这家大型面包和蛋糕制造商通过多个子公司运营，其中最大的一个是位于纽约的Cushman's Sons, Inc.。Cushman's拥有由Purity不担保的7美元和8美元累积优先股。Purity的年度报告以合并形式呈现，显示扣除Cushman's优先股的全部股息后的收益，无论这些股息是赚得还是已支付。Cushman's的独立报告显示，在1934年至1937年间，其运营给Purity带来了相当大的亏损，按Purity的会计标准来看，即：（000省略）

<!--en-->
1. By reason of nonrecurrent items included in income or because of charges to surplus that might properly belong in the income account.
2. Because current results of subsidiaries are not accurately reflected in the parent company's statements.
3. Because the depreciation and other amortization charges are irregularly computed.⁹
**Special Dividends Paid by Subsidiaries.** When earnings of nonconsolidated subsidiaries are allowed to accumulate in their surplus accounts, they may be used later to bolster up the results of a poor year by means of a large special dividend paid over to the parent company.
*Examples:* Such dividends, amounting to $11,000,000, were taken by the Erie Railroad Company in 1922 from the Pennsylvania Coal Company and Hillside Coal and Iron Company. The Northern Pacific Railway Company similarly eked out its depleted earnings in 1930 and 1931 by means of large sums taken as special dividends from the Chicago, Burlington, and Quincy Railroad Company, the Northern Express Company, and the Northwestern Improvement Company, the last being a real-estate, coal and iron-ore subsidiary. The 1931 earnings of the New York, Chicago, and St. Louis Railroad Company included a back dividend of some $1,600,000 on its holdings of Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway Company Prior Preferred Stock, only a part of which was earned in that year by the Wheeling road.
This device of concealing a subsidiary's profits in good years and drawing upon them in bad ones may seem quite praise-worthy as a method of stabilizing the reported earning power. But such benevolent deceptions are frowned upon by enlightened opinion, as illustrated by the more recent regulations of the New York Stock Exchange which insist upon full disclosure of subsidiaries' earnings. It is the duty of management to disclose the truth and the whole truth about the results of each period; it is the function of the stockholders to deduce the "normal earning power" of their company by averaging out the earnings of prosperity and depression. Manipulation of the reported earnings by the managementeven for the desirable purpose of maintaining them on an even keel is objectionable none the less because it may too readily lead to manipulation for more sinister reasons.
**Distorted Earnings Through Parent-Subsidiary Relationships.** Examples are available of the use of the parent-subsidiary relationship to produce astonishing distortions in the reported income. We shall give two illustrations taken from the railroad field. These instances are the more impressive because the stringent accounting regulations of the Interstate Commerce Commission might be expected to prevent any misrepresentation of earnings.
*Examples:* In 1925 Western Pacific Railroad Corporation paid dividends of $7.56 upon its preferred stock and $5 upon its common stock. Its income account showed earnings slightly exceeding the dividends paid. These earnings consisted almost entirely of dividends aggregating $4,450,000 received from its operating subsidiary, the Western Pacific Railroad Company. The year's earnings of the railroad, itself, however, were only $2,450,000. Furthermore its accumulated surplus was insufficient to permit the larger dividend that the parent company desired to report as its income for the year. To achieve this end, the parent company went to the extraordinary lengths of *donating* the sum of $1,500,000 to the operating company, and it immediately took the same money back as a *dividend* from its subsidiary. The donation it charged against its *surplus*; the receipt of the same money as dividends it reported as *earnings*. In this devious fashion it was able to report $5 "earned" upon its common stock, when in fact the applicable earnings were only about $2 per share.
In support of our previous statement that bad accounting practices are contagious, we may point out that the Western Pacific example of 1925 was followed by the New York, Chicago, and St. Louis Railroad Company ("Nickel Plate") in 1930 and 1931. The details are briefly as follows:
In 1929 Nickel Plate sold, through a subsidiary, its holdings of Pere Marquette stock to Chesapeake and Ohio, which was under the same control. A profit of $10,665,000 was realized on this sale, which gain was properly credited tosurplus. In 1930 Nickel Plate needed to increase its income; whereupon it took the $10,665,000 profit out of its surplus, returned it to the subsidiary's treasury and then took $3,000,000 thereof in the form of a "dividend" from this subsidiary, which it included in its 1930 *income*. A similar dividend of $2,100,000 was included in the income account for 1931.
These extraordinary devices may have been resorted to for what was considered the necessary purpose of establishing a net income large enough to keep the company's bonds legal for trust-fund investments.¹⁰ The result, however, was the same as that from all other misleading accounting practices, *viz.*, to lead the public astray and to give those "on the inside" an unfair advantage.
**Broader Significance of Subsidiaries' Losses.** We have suggested in this chapter that security analysis must make full allowance for the results of subsidiaries, whether they be profits or losses. But the question may well be raised: Is the loss of a subsidiary necessarily a direct offset against the parent company's earnings? Why should a company be worth *less* because it owns something—in this case, an unprofitable interest? Could it not at any time put an end to the loss by selling, liquidating or even abandoning the subsidiary? Hence, if good management is assumed, must we not also assume that the subsidiary losses are at most temporary and therefore to be regarded as nonrecurring items rather than as deductions from normal earnings?
This point is similar to that discussed in the previous chapter relative to idle-plant expense and similar also to the matter of unprofitable *divisions* of a business, to be touched upon later. There is no one, simple answer to the questions that we have raised. Actually, if the subsidiary could be wound up *without an adverse effect upon the rest of the business*, it would be logical to view such losses as temporary—since good sense would dictate that in a short time the subsidiary must either become profitable or be disposed of. But if there are important business relations between the parent company and the subsidiary, *e.g.*, if the latter affords an outlet for goods or supplies cheap materials or absorbs an important share ofthe overhead, then the termination of its losses is not so simple a matter. It may turn out, upon further analysis, that all or a good part of the subsidiary's loss is a necessary factor in the parent company's profit. It is not an easy task to determine just what business relationships are involved in each instance. Like so many other elements in analysis, this point usually requires an investigation going well beyond the reported figures. The following examples will illustrate the type of situation and analysis with which we have been dealing.
*Example A: Purity Bakeries Corporation.* This large maker of bread and cake operates through a number of subsidiaries, of which one of the largest is Cushman's Sons, Inc., of New York. Cushman's has outstanding $7 and $8 cumulative preferred stock, not guaranteed by Purity. The annual reports of Purity are on a consolidated basis and show earnings after deduction of full dividends on those Cushman's preferred shares not owned by Purity, whether earned or paid. The separate reports of Cushman's reveal that between 1934 and 1937 its operations resulted in a considerable loss to Purity, on its accounting basis, *viz.*:
(000 omitted)

因此，排除Cushman后，Purity的收益是包含Cushman时的三倍。分析师是否可以认为，前者更能真实反映Purity的盈利能力？因为预计该公司要么仍会从该子公司获得收入（如过去直到1934年那样），要么会失去该收入？企业间关系的问题需要考虑。Cushman在1937年的报告中指出，Purity在其子公司的运营中收取了相当大的服务费，这表明Cushman可能在承担间接费用方面具有额外价值。此事需要仔细调查。

<!--en-->
The earnings are thus seen to be three times as large excluding Cushman's as they were including Cushman's. Could the analyst have reasoned that the former provides the truer measure of Purity's earning power, since the company can be expected either again to earn money from that subsidiary (as it had earned it in the past up to 1934) or to drop it? The question of inter-corporate relationships would have to be considered. A note in the 1937 report of Cushman's indicated that Purity was making a fairly large service charge in connection with its subsidiaries' operations, which suggests that Cushman's might be of some extra value in absorbing overhead. This matter would call for a careful inquiry.

但1938年的报告显示：首先，Cushman已扣除优先股息；其次，两个无利润的零售工厂（位于费城和芝加哥）已被关闭。因此，分析师可能推断，子公司的亏损并非永久性的，对1934–1937年的报告结果应结合这一点看待。

<!--en-->
But the report for the next year, 1938, showed, first, that Cushman's had earned the preferred dividend deduction, and secondly, that two unprofitable retail plants (in Philadelphia and Chicago) had been closed. Subject to further investigation, therefore, the analyst might well infer that the subsidiary's losses were nonpermanent in nature and that the reported results for 1934–1937 are to be viewed with this point in mind.

*示例B：Lehigh Coal and Navigation Company。* 该企业的收入来自多种来源，主要方式是将其铁路资产租给新泽西中央铁路公司，年租金为2,268,000美元。其第二大资产是无烟煤煤矿，自1930年以来一直处于亏损状态。1937年，这一亏损相当于Lehigh股票每股约90美分。因此，该公司全年报告合并净亏损为306,000美元，而母公司层面仅盈利1,125,000美元，即每股64美分。

<!--en-->
*Example B: Lehigh Coal and Navigation Company.* This enterprise has derived its income from various sources, chief of which has been the lease of its railroad property to the Central Railroad of New Jersey for an annual rental of $2,268,000. Its next largest holding consists of anthracite coal mines, which since 1930 have been operated at a loss. In 1937 this loss was equivalent to about 90 cents per share of Lehigh stock. As a result the company reported a *consolidated* net loss of $306,000 for the year, as contrasted with a profit on a parent-company basis only of $1,125,000, or 64 cents per share.

但在这种情况下，分析师不能安全地假设Lehigh股票因拥有煤矿资产而价值低于没有这些资产时的价值。煤矿运营为铁路部门提供了重要吨位。如果煤矿被关闭，Jersey Central支付年租金的能力可能会受到严重影响，尤其是因为租户铁路过去几年经营状况不佳。（实际上，Jersey Central后来声称Lehigh Coal and Navigation在租赁协议中有义务提供一定吨位的煤炭。）因此，在这种复杂的架构下，投资者不能安全地忽视合并结果，包括无烟煤子公司的亏损。

<!--en-->
But in this case the analyst could not safely make the assumption that the Lehigh stock was not worth *less* by reason of its ownership of the mining properties than it would be worth without them. Operation of the mines supplied an important tonnage to the railroad division. If the mines were shut down, the ability of the Jersey Central to pay the annual rental might have been critically impaired, especially since the lessee road had been doing poorly for some years past. (In fact the claim was later made by the Jersey Central that the Lehigh Coal and Navigation was obligated in connection with the lease to supply a certain tonnage from its coal properties). Hence, in this rather complicated set-up the investor could not safely go behind the consolidated results, including the losses of the anthracite subsidiary.

*示例C：Barnsdall Oil Company。* 这里的情况与另外两种相反。Barnsdall Oil同时拥有精炼和生产资产，后者盈利，前者亏损。1935年，它将精炼厂（及营销部门）分离为独立公司，并将普通股分配给自己的股东，但仍保留优先股和对新公司的重大权利主张。1936–1938年，精炼厂和站点持续亏损；Barnsdall Oil投入大量资金弥补这些亏损，先通过资本储备项，然后通过已赚盈余项冲减。另一方面，其“收入账户”摆脱了精炼亏损的负担，从1933年6月1日到1938年底，生产业务始终保持稳定利润。

<!--en-->
*Example C: Barnsdall Oil Company.* We have here a situation opposite from the other two. Barnsdall Oil owned both refining and producing properties, the latter profitable, the former unprofitable. In 1935 it segregated the refineries (and marketing units) in a separate company, of which it distributed the common stock to its own stockholders, retaining, however, the preferred stock and substantial claims against the new company. In 1936–1938 the refineries and stations continued to lose; Barnsdall Oil advanced considerable sums to cover these losses and wrote them off by charges first against capital surplus and then against earned surplus. On the other hand, its *income account*, freed from the burden of these refining losses, showed profits from producing operations at a steady rate from June 1, 1933, to the end of 1938.

然而，1939年，纽约证券交易所要求公司向股东修正报表，告知他们将精炼公司投资减值计入报告利润的影响。这些亏损会使报告利润减少超过三分之一。

<!--en-->
In 1939, however, the New York Stock Exchange called upon the company to correct its statements to stockholders by advising them of the effect upon the reported profits of charging there-against the write-downs of the investment in the refining company. These losses would have reduced the indicated profits by more than one-third.

从正确会计的角度来看，*只要一家公司继续控制亏损部门，其亏损必须作为其他收益的扣除项显示。*分析师必须判断未来消除亏损的可能性，并据此评估股票当前价格。因此，Barnsdall Oil公司采用的方法显然存在批评点，因为它只是停止了*报告*精炼亏损，并未真正消除亏损本身。（1939年底，公司开始采取步骤，似乎要彻底分离并出售精炼和营销部门。）

<!--en-->
It is clear, from the standpoint of proper accounting, *that as long as a company continues to control an unprofitable division*, its losses must be shown as deductions from its other earnings. The analyst must decide what the chances are of terminating the losses in the future, and view the current price of the stock accordingly. The method followed by the Barnsdall Oil Company appears therefore clearly open to criticism, since it served merely to terminate the *reporting* of its refining losses without really terminating the losses themselves. (At the end of 1939 the company set steps into motion for an apparent complete divorcement and sale of the refining and marketing divisions.)

**总结。** 为了避免留下困惑，我们总结处理方式如下：

<!--en-->
**Summary.** To avoid leaving this point in confusion, we shall summarize our treatment by suggesting:

1. 首先，在每次分析中都应扣除子公司亏损。
2. 如果涉及金额较大，分析师应调查这些亏损是否可能提前终止。
3. 如果检查结果有利，分析师可以认为子公司全部或部分亏损相当于非经常性项目。[^2139]：¹ 在1930年的报告中，资产负债表中的表述从“商誉和商标”改为“Tintex商誉和商标”。1939年，商誉项目被注销，1929–1930年的100万美元计提额从经营盈余中扣除。

<!--en-->
1. In the first instance, subsidiary losses are to be deducted in every analysis.
2. If the amount involved is significant, the analyst should investigate whether or not the losses may be subject to early termination.
3. If the result of this examination is favorable, the analyst may consider all or part of the subsidiary's loss as the equivalent of a nonrecurring item.
[^2139]: ¹ In the 1930 report the wording in the balance sheet was changed from “Good-will and Trade-marks” to “Tintex Good-will and Trade-marks.” In 1939 the Good-will item was written off, and the $1,000,000 write-up of 1929–1930 deducted from earned surplus.

<!--en-->

<!--en-->

⁶ 为了避免暗示不一致性，由于在前一章节中对2022年到期的烟草产品公司6 1/2s股票发表了积极评论，我们必须指出，在1930年期间，这种情况发生了管理上的彻底变化。联合烟草商店及其继任者也经历了两次彻底的管理变更。

<!--en-->
⁶ To avoid an implication of inconsistency, because of our favorable comments on Tobacco Products Corporation 6 1/2s, due 2022, in a previous chapter, we must point out that a complete change of management took place in this situation during 1930. There have also been two complete changes in the management of United Cigar Stores and its successor.

⁷ 关于过去几年此类政策带来的误导效应，请参阅本著作第一版第380–381页对阅读公司、综合燃气公司（现称为综合爱迪生公司）和沃伦兄弟公司的分析。在SEC法规出台之前，大多数铁路公司未能提供其非运输子公司盈利信息，其中一些子公司具有重大重要性。*示例：*北方太平洋公司、阿奇森公司。

<!--en-->

Prior to the S.E.C. legislation, most railroad companies failed to supply any information regarding the earnings of their nontransportation subsidiaries, some of which were of substantial importance. *Examples:* Northern Pacific, Atchison.

The Wabash owned 99% of both the preferred and the common stock of the Ann Arbor. In December 1930 the Ann Arbor directors declared a $5 dividend per share on the preferred and a $27 dividend per share on the common. This action was taken in the face of a working-capital deficit and net earnings available of little over 10% of the dividends thus declared. Neither dividend was ever paid. This maneuver, however, enabled the Wabash to credit its share of the dividends declared to its income account as “dividend income” to the extent of $1,073,455, which was sufficient to raise the fixed-charge coverage of the Wabash from about 1.3 times to a figure slightly in excess of 1.5 times.
CHAPTER 34

# 折旧与类似费用与盈利能力的关系

<!--en-->
*The Relation of Depreciation and Similar Charges to Earning Power*

对收入账户进行关键分析时，必须特别关注扣除的折旧和类似费用金额。这些项目与普通运营费用不同，因为它们并不表示当前的现金支出。它们代表固定或资本资产价值的估计减少，由于磨损、消耗或任何原因而接近消亡。这类重要费用可分类如下：

<!--en-->
A CRITICAL ANALYSIS of an income account must pay particular attention to the amounts deducted for depreciation and kindred charges. These items differ from ordinary operating expenses in that they do not signify a current and corresponding outlay of cash. They represent the estimated shrinkage in the value of the fixed or capital assets, due to wearing out, to using up or to their approaching extinction for whatever cause. The important charges of this character may be classified as follows:

1. 折旧（及过时）、更换、更新或退役。
2. 耗竭或消耗。
3. 租赁权益、租赁权益改进、许可等摊销。
4. 专利摊销。所有这些项目都可以归类为"摊销"，但有时我们会笼统地称它们为"折旧项目"，或者简称为"折旧"，因为后者是更常见的术语。**与折旧相关的关键问题。** 管理折旧费用的会计理论相当简单：如果资本资产的使用寿命有限，就必须通过在其使用寿命期间分配的收入来冲减该资产的成本。但这一简单的陈述背后存在三重复杂性。首先，我们发现会计规则本身允许以除成本以外的价值作为摊销的基础。其次，我们发现许多公司未能遵循公认的会计惯例，在收益表中表述其折旧扣除额。第三，有时从会计角度来说有理由进行的调整，从投资角度来看却无法恰当地满足需求。这些问题将在接下来两章中讨论。我们的讨论将首先针对一般工业公司，随后将探讨与石油公司、矿业公司和公共事业公司相关的特殊问题。¹

<!--en-->
1. Depreciation (and obsolescence), replacements, renewals or retirements.
2. Depletion or exhaustion.
3. Amortization of leaseholds, leasehold improvements, licenses, etc.
4. Amortization of patents.
All these items may properly be embraced under the title "amortization," but we shall sometimes refer to them generically as "depreciation items," or simply as "depreciation," because the latter is a more familiar term.
**Leading Questions Relative to Depreciation.** The accounting theory that governs depreciation charges is simple enough. If a capital asset has a limited life, provision must be made to write off the cost of that asset by charges against earnings distributed over the period of its life. But behind thisinnocent statement lie complications of a threefold character. First we find that accounting rules themselves may permit a value other than cost as the base for the amortization charge. Second, we find many ways in which companies fail to follow accepted accounting practice in stating their depreciation deduction in the income account. Third, there are occasions when an allowance that may be justified from an accounting standpoint will fail to meet the situation properly from an investment standpoint. These problems will engage our attention in this and the next two chapters. Our discussion will be directed first towards industrial companies generally, following which we shall consider special aspects having to do with oil companies, mining companies and public utilities.¹

## 折旧基础

<!--en-->
*THE DEPRECIATION BASE*

**非成本的折旧基础。** 会计界支持这样一种理论：折旧备抵的作用是确保资产在寿命结束时进行*替换*，而不仅仅是冲减其*成本*。如果真的遵循这一理念，当前或预期的未来替换成本将成为折旧费用的基础，并且不仅取决于相同资产的价值，还取决于预期替换旧资产的物品性质的变化。

<!--en-->
**Depreciation Base Other than Cost.** There is support in accounting circles for the theory that the function of the depreciation allowance is to provide for the *replacement* of the asset at the end of its life rather than merely to write off its *cost*. If this idea were actually followed, the current or expected future replacement cost would be the basis for the depreciation charge, and it would vary not only with the value of the identical asset but also with changes in the character of the item that is expected to replace the one worn out.

无论对这种理论持何种看法，²它实际上从未以所述形式被采用。但在实践中，我们会遇到这一概念的变体，即*即在资产负债表上用特定日期所有固定资产的替换价值代替成本，通常随后根据新价值计算年度折旧费用。*

<!--en-->
Whatever may be said for or against this theory,² it is virtually never followed in the form stated. But we do meet in practice with a variant of the idea, *viz.*, the substitution of the replacement value of all the fixed assets *as of a given date* in place of cost on the balance sheet, followed usually by annual depreciation charges based on the new value.

自1914年以来，有过两次这样的重新评估。第一次发生在1920年代，将战前成本提高至当前较高的水平。第二次出现在1931-1933年，将财产账户价值下调至大萧条时期较低的估值。³*示例：* 1926年美国冰业公司将其固定资产估值提高了7,868,000美元，1935年则相应调低，使估值恢复至成本基础。1926年的估值上调导致此后收益项中的折旧费用增加，而1935年的调低则导致折旧费用减少。1933年美国机车公司将其股票面值从每股50美元降至5美元，并利用由此产生的大部分资本盈余，将固定资产减记近26,000,000美元，对其在通用钢铁铸造公司的投资减记约6,200,000美元。对收益表的净影响是使折旧费用降至之前水平的约40%。

<!--en-->
Since 1914 there have been two waves of such revaluations. The first, taking place in the 1920's, marked up prewar costs to the higher values currently prevailing. The second, appearing in 1931–1933, marked down property accounts to the much lower valuations associated with the depression.³
*Examples:* In 1926 American Ice Company wrote up its fixed assets by $7,868,000, and in 1935 it wrote them down correspondingly to restore the valuations to a cost basis. The 1926 write-up resulted in larger depreciation charges thereafter against income, and the 1935 reduction resulted in lower depreciation charges. In 1933 American Locomotive Company reduced the stated value of its stock from $50 to $5 a share and utilized most of the capital surplus thus created to write down fixed properties by nearly $26,000,000 and its investment in General Steel Castings Corporation by about $6,200,000. The net effect on the income account was to reduce depreciation charges to about 40% of their former level.

会计界对折旧基础偶尔从原始成本发生变化是否合适存在一些批评。我们认为，*只要满足以下条件*，这些变化并不令人反感：

<!--en-->
There is some criticism in accounting circles of the propriety of such sporadic changes in the depreciation base from original cost. In our opinion they are not objectionable *provided*:

1. 新价值的设定基于*真诚*的信念，即它们能比旧价值更公平地反映现实情况。
2. 针对这些新数值，正确的折旧费用会计入收入账户。然而在许多情况下，我们发现公司重新评估固定资产时，并未满足上述条件之一。**降低折旧费用以优化表现。**在折旧会计领域，最显著的现象是近期对固定资产进行了大幅减记，并非出于谨慎原则，而是为了提升收益表现，从而*增加*股票的表面价值。我们认为，如果我们将对这些措施重要性的讨论推迟到我们关于“投资者视角下的摊销费用”的章节中，对读者的来说会更方便。目前由于我们讨论的是会计方法，我们仅指出：我们认为，为了降低折旧费用、提高报告收益而进行的过度资产减记，是一种不可原谅的借口，会计界不应容忍这种行为。提交给SEC的注册报表中包含了一句话，说明如果保留之前的资产价值，收益本会低多少。我们认为，此类信息也应作为股东年度报告收入账户的脚注显示，但更合理的做法是由会计师拒绝确认包含此类减记的报告，并坚持将正确数据恢复至公司账目中。**资产负债表与收入账户差异。**许多夸大固定资产价值的公司，并未相应增加收入账户中的折旧费用。实际上，它们试图在资产负债表中享受更高的估值利益，而不承担随之增加的折旧费用对收益的影响。这种做法在矿业和石油公司中尤为普遍。这里给出两个来自一般工业领域的例子：*示例：*霍尔印刷公司在1926年和1931年高估了其财产账户，约6,222,000美元，并将这一“估值增加”计入资本储备。随后，基于这一增值额进行的折旧被计入资本储备，而非收入；例如，通常在截至1938年3月的年度中，公司将406,000美元用于此类折旧计入储备，将864,000美元用于“常规”折旧计入收入。1938年4月，通过减少财产账户和资本储备，取消了估值增加的余额；随后停止了特殊折旧费用。自1935年以来，博格·沃纳每年向“增值储备”支付约102,000美元（前几年也有不同金额），用于摊销1927年进行的固定资产高估。显然，任何公司都不应用一套数值用于资产负债表，再用另一套用于收入账户。较新的趋势是通过从资产负债表中删除之前的高估值来纠正这些差异，从而恢复到原始成本。

<!--en-->
1. The new values are set up in the *bona fide* conviction that they represent existing realities more fairly than the old values.
2. Proper depreciation against these new values is charged in the income account.
In many cases, however, we find that companies revaluing their fixed assets fail to observe one or the other of these conditions.
**Mark-Downs to Reduce Depreciation Charges.** Perhaps the most striking phenomenon in the field of depreciation accounting is the recent marking down of the fixed assets, not in the interests of conservatism but with the precisely opposite intent of making a better earnings exhibit and thereby *increasing* the apparent value of the shares.
We believe that it will be more convenient for the reader if we defer consideration of the significance to security analysis of these devices until our chapter devoted to “Amortization Charges from the Investor’s Standpoint.” At this time, since we are dealing with accounting methods, we shall merely remark that in our opinion excessive write-downs of fixedassets, for the avowed or obvious purpose of decreasing depreciation and increasing reported earnings, constitute an inexcusable subterfuge and should not be condoned by the accounting profession. Registration statements submitted to the S.E.C. include a statement of how much lower the earnings would have been if the former plant values had been retained. We think that such information should also appear as a footnote to the income account in the annual reports to stockholders, but it would be better practice still if accountants refused to certify a report containing such mark-downs and insisted on restoration of the proper figures to the company's accounts.
**Balance Sheet–Income Account Discrepancies.** Many corporations that have marked up their fixed assets fail to increase correspondingly their depreciation charges against the income account. They are in effect attempting to get the benefit of the higher valuation in their balance sheet without accepting the burden of consequently higher depreciation charges against earnings. This practice has been especially prevalent in the case of mining and oil companies. Two examples drawn from the general industrial field are given here:
*Examples:* Hall Printing Company wrote up its property account by $6,222,000 in 1926 and 1931, crediting this “appraisal increment” to capital surplus. Depreciation on this appreciated value was then charged to capital surplus, instead of to income; e.g., typically, in the year ended March 1938 the company charged $406,000 for such depreciation against surplus and $864,000 for “regular” depreciation against income. In April 1938 the balance of the appraisal increment was eliminated by writing down both property account and capital surplus; and the special depreciation charge was then discontinued.
Borg Warner has been charging about $102,000 per annum since 1935 (and various amounts in prior years) to “Appreciation Surplus,” instead of to income, to amortize a write-up of fixed assets made in 1927.
It should be obvious that no company should use one set of values for its balance sheet and another for its income account. The more recent tendency is to correct these disparities by eliminating the previous write-up from the balance sheet, thus returning to original cost.

## 折旧率。标准与非标准做法

<!--en-->
*THE RATE OF DEPRECIATION. STANDARD AND NONSTANDARD PRACTICE*

**1. 如上市报表所示。**绝大多数工业公司都遵循标准政策，对各类可折旧资产收取适当的折旧率。分析师可以通过参考纽约证券交易所上市申请或招股说明书或注册报表来轻松验证这一点。

<!--en-->
**1. As Shown by Listing Statements.** The vast majority of industrial companies follow the standard policy of charging an appropriate depreciation rate against each class of depreciable asset. The analyst can readily check this fact by reference to New York Stock Exchange listing applications or to a prospectus or registration statement.

*示例：*如果遵循标准方法，通常会以以下方式公布：

<!--en-->
*Examples:* If standard methods are followed, they are likely to be announced in somewhat the following manner:

（来自1928年12月17日电储电池公司的上市申请）

<!--en-->
(From listing application of Electric Storage Battery Company, dated December 17, 1928.)

该公司关于折旧的政策如下：对于建筑物，使用寿命为20至33年，取决于建筑类型。机械、工具和固定装置按设备类型的不同，以1至10年为单位进行折旧。办公家具和固定装置按10年进行折旧。对于所有可折旧资产，折旧率由实际经验和工程师对设备使用周期的估计确定。关于流动资产折旧，会预留一笔资金以覆盖可能的坏账损失。

<!--en-->
The policy of this Company in regard to depreciation ... is as follows: On buildings the term of life is twenty to thirty-three years, depending upon the character of construction. Machinery, tools and fixtures are written off at the rate of one to ten years, depending upon the character of the equipment. Office furniture and fixtures are written off in ten years. On all depreciable properties rates are determined by actual experience and engineers' estimates as to the productive life of the equipment. In respect to depreciation of current assets, a reserve is set aside to cover probable loss from bad debts.

（来自1930年2月11日米德兰钢铁产品公司的上市申请）

<!--en-->
(From the listing application of Midland Steel Products Company, dated February 11, 1930.)

以下是使用的折旧率：

<!--en-->
The following are the rates of depreciation used:

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Rate of depreciation<br>per year, %</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Buildings</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>Grounds, driveways and walks</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>Machinery</td><td>7</td></tr><tr><td>Furniture and fixtures</td><td>10</td></tr><tr><td>Railroad sidings</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>Automobiles and trucks</td><td>25</td></tr></tbody><tfoot><tr><td colspan="2">Tools and dies—amortized over life of job when number of units required can be determined, otherwise written off at close of each fiscal year.</td></tr></tfoot></table>

公司已采用这些费率多年，这是行业的标准做法。

<!--en-->
These rates have been used by the Company for several years, being standard practice in the industry.

这些费率基于相关资产的预计使用寿命确定。因此，对于建筑物，成本在50年内进行折旧；场地、车道和步道，在50年内；机械，在14年以上；家具和固定装置，在10年以上；铁路旁区域，在50年以上。在确定所采用的费率时，不考虑上述期间结束后的残值。

<!--en-->
The rates are based upon the estimated life of the respective property involved. Thus, with respect to buildings, the cost is depreciated, over 50 years; grounds, driveways, and walks, over 50 years; machinery over 14 years; furniture and fixtures, over 10 years; railroad sidings, over 50 years. No residual value at the expiration of said periods is considered in determining the rates used.

与现在几乎普遍遵循的这一标准政策相比，我们可以指出，以前像American Car and Foundry、American Sugar Refining和Baldwin Locomotive Works这样的重要公司曾采用过在此重要问题上存在问题的做法。

<!--en-->
In contrast with this standard policy, now all but universally followed, we may point to the questionable practice on this important point formerly resorted to by such important companies as American Car and Foundry, American Sugar Refining and Baldwin Locomotive Works.

American Sugar Refining Company于1923年12月6日提交的上市申请中包含以下陈述：

<!--en-->
The American Sugar Refining Company's listing application, dated December 6, 1923, contained the following statement:

正如过去几年的年度损益表所示，公司在折旧方面采取非常宽松的政策。通过对所有必要的维修以及更新和更换进行维护，其资产价值始终得到充分保障。

<!--en-->
The Company maintains a very liberal policy as to depreciation as shown by the annual profit and loss statement of past years. The value of its properties is at all times fully maintained by the making of all needful and proper repairs thereto and renewals and replacements thereof.

这一声明听起来令人安心，但过于模糊，无法让分析师满意。如下记录所示的实际折旧费用表明，其政策异常任意且不稳定。

<!--en-->
This declaration sounds reassuring, but it is far too indefinite to satisfy the analyst. The actual depreciationcharges, as shown in the following record, disclose an unusually arbitrary and erratic policy.

1926年至1930年（包含这两年）产生的额外费用，似乎进一步支持了我们的观点：American Sugar的折旧拨备既随意又不足。

<!--en-->
The additional charges to surplus made in the years 1926–1930, inclusive, appear to strengthen our contention that American Sugar’s depreciation allowances have been both arbitrary and inadequate.

American Car and Foundry于1925年4月2日提交的申请中包含以下内容：

<!--en-->
The American Car and Foundry’s application, dated April 2, 1925, contains the following:

该公司没有专门的折旧账户。然而，其等效机制体现在公司的政策与实践中：公司始终通过维修、更新和更换设备与建筑来保持工厂和资产处于一流的物理状态并维持高效率水平，当物理状况需要时；当更换设施能带来更经济生产效果时，会更换为更现代类型的设施。这一程序充分涵盖折旧与过时情况，成本计入运营费用。

<!--en-->
The Company has no depreciation account as such. However, its equivalent is found in the policy and the practice of the Company to maintain at all times its plants and properties in first class physical condition and in a high state of efficiency by repairing, renewing and replacing equipment and buildings as their physical conditions may require, and by replacing facilities with those of more modern type, when such action results in more economical production. This procedure amply covers depreciation and obsolescence and the cost is charged to Operating Expenses.

分析师持怀疑态度再次是有道理的。American Can在1926年2月26日的上市申请中，未能解释说明其折旧政策，但提到自1907年2月以来，公司已花费约5000万美元用于扩建与改善资产，并且“在此期间，资产折旧至少达2000万美元”。

<!--en-->
Here again a sceptical attitude on the part of the analyst is “amply” warranted. The same is true in respect of American Can which managed—inexplicably—to avoid all reference toits depreciation policy in its listing application dated February 26, 1926, although it did mention that the company had spent approximately $50,000,000 on extensions and improvement of properties since February 1907 and that “during this period properties have been depreciated by at least $20,000,000.”

Baldwin Locomotive Works在1929年10月3日的上市申请中，对折旧做出了相当惊人的表述：

<!--en-->
Baldwin Locomotive Works, in its listing application dated October 3, 1929, makes the following rather astonishing statement on depreciation:

联邦政府确定的1924年至1928年五年的设备和设施折旧金额总计5,112,258.09美元，该金额从收入或盈余中扣除的方式如下：

<!--en-->
The amount of the depreciation upon plant and equipment as determined by the Federal Government for the five years 1924 to 1928 inclusive has totaled $5,112,258.09 which has been deducted either from income or surplus as follows:

预计未来几年，基于联邦政府确定的可折旧资产预计使用寿命、税务专员认可为合理收入扣除项且得到工程师同意的折旧金额，将作为工厂计算折旧的依据。

<!--en-->
It is expected that in future years the amount of depreciation based upon the estimated useful life of depreciable properties as determined by the Federal Government, allowed by the Commissioner of Taxes as a proper deduction from income and agreed to by our engineers, will govern the amount to be used by the Works in its calculation of depreciation.

显然，Baldwin在这一时期的损益表并不准确。向股东报告의 1924-1928年普通股平均年每股收益远高于下一页顶部的正确数据。

<!--en-->
Evidently the income statements of Baldwin for this period were anything but accurate. The average annual earnings per share of common stock for 1924–1928, as reported to the stockholders, were strikingly higher than the correct figure, as shown at the top of the next page.

**2. 通过两家公司的比较可见。** 当分析师知道某公司的折旧政策与标准不同时，就有特殊理由检查拨备的合理性。与同一领域的单一公司进行比较可能得出重要结果，如下一页中间表格所示，涉及American Sugar和American Car and Foundry的情况。*普通股每股收益*

<!--en-->
**2. As Shown by Comparisons of Two Companies.** When the analyst knows that a company’s depreciation policy differs from the standard, there is special reason to check the adequacy of the allowance. Comparison with a single company in the same field may yield significant results, as isshown by the table in the middle of the next page respecting American Sugar and American Car and Foundry.

## 折旧费用往往是合并中的问题。

<!--en-->
*Depreciation Charges Often an Issue in Mergers.*

比较性折旧费用有时会成为确定合并条款是否公平的重要因素。

<!--en-->
Comparative depreciation charges at times become quite an issue in determining the fairness of proposed terms of consolidation.

*示例：* 1924年，一项合并计划被宣布，涉及Chesapeake and Ohio、Hocking Valley、Pere Marquette、“Nickel Plate”和Erie铁路公司。一些Chesapeake and Ohio的股东反对该计划，并说服州际商业委员会认为合并条款对他们的铁路公司极为不公平。

<!--en-->
*Example:* In 1924 a merger plan was announced embracing the Chesapeake and Ohio, Hocking Valley, Pere Marquette, “Nickel Plate,” and Erie railroads. Some Chesapeake and Ohio stockholders dissented, and they convinced the Interstate Commerce Commission that the terms of the consolidation were highly unfair to their road.

他们还指出，由于对Chesapeake and Ohio的折旧和设备报废费用过高，前三年其收入实际上比报告的数字要高得多。⁵ 1929年Bethlehem Steel与Youngstown Sheet and Tube的合并计划也因类似反对意见而失败。关于这两家钢铁生产企业的数据如下表所示。

<!--en-->
Among other matters they pointed out that the earnings of Chesapeake and Ohio in the preceding three years had in reality been much higher than stated, due to the unusually heavy charges made against them for depreciation and retirement of equipment.⁵ A similar objection was made in connection with the projected merger of Bethlehem Steel and Youngstown Sheet and Tube in 1929, which plan was also defeated. Some figures on these two steel producers are given as shown in the following table.

**隐藏的折旧。** 证券分析中没有任何事情可以视为理所当然，American Can的奇怪案例就说明了这一点。直到1937年，该公司一直未向股东透露其折旧政策的细节。在1922–1936年间，它每年固定提取200万美元用于折旧。若与 Continental Can相比——后者对规模小得多的工厂投资只提取相近金额——似乎表明American Can的收益能力被高估了。但1934年的年度报告首次向股东披露，该公司还从运营费用中计提了“更换设备”的费用，但未说明具体金额。1935年和1936年也出现了此类费用，1935年的10-K文件向SEC提交的报告中显示，额外费用约为240万美元。最后，1937年的年度报告告知股东，1936年相应的额外费用约为327.5万美元。从1937年开始，公司开始进行“常规”折旧，当年为570.2万美元，1938年为608.5万美元。因此，企业所有者逐渐了解到与其资产相关的实际情况。

<!--en-->
**Concealed Depreciation.** That nothing can be taken for granted in security analysis is shown by the strange case of American Can, which until 1937 had failed to reveal details of its depreciation policy to its shareholders. During the years 1922–1936 it deducted annually a flat $2,000,000 for this purpose. A comparison with Continental Can—which charged about the same amount against a much smaller plant investment—would have suggested that American Can’s earning power had been overstated. But the annual report for 1934 disclosed to stockholders for the first time that the company had also been charging sums to operating expenses for “replacements,” without giving the amount. The fact (but not the amounts) that such charges had been made in 1935 and 1936 was also revealed in those years. Meanwhile Form 10-K for 1935, filed with the S.E.C., revealed that the amount of these extra charges was about $2,400,000. Finally the annual report for 1937 advised the stockholders that the corresponding extra charge-off amounted to approximately $3,275,000 for the year 1936. Beginning with 1937 the company made “regular” depreciation charges, amounting to $5,702,000 in that year and to $6,085,000 in 1938. Thus, by easy stages, the owners of the business were told the facts of life bearing on their property.

<table><thead><tr><th>1928</th><th>Bethlehem Steel</th><th>Youngstown Sheet & Tube</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>资产账户，1927年12月31日</td><td>$673,000,000</td><td>$204,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>销售额</td><td>295,000,000</td><td>141,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>折旧、损耗与陈旧化</td><td>13,658,000</td><td>8,321,000</td></tr><tr><td>比率：折旧与资产账户之比</td><td>2.03%</td><td>4.08%</td></tr><tr><td>比率：折旧与销售额之比</td><td>4.63%</td><td>5.90%</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th>1928</th><th>Bethlehem Steel</th><th>Youngstown Sheet & Tube</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Property account, Dec. 31, 1927</td><td>$673,000,000</td><td>$204,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>Sales</td><td>295,000,000</td><td>141,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>Depreciation, depletion, and obsolescence</td><td>13,658,000</td><td>8,321,000</td></tr><tr><td>Ratio: depreciation to property account</td><td>2.03%</td><td>4.08%</td></tr><tr><td>Ratio: depreciation to sales</td><td>4.63%</td><td>5.90%</td></tr></tbody></table>

根据这一后续披露，之前关于American Can低估折旧费用的推断⁶ 必须被改为该公司未能透露事实的结论。

<!--en-->
In the light of this later disclosure, the earlier inference⁶ that American Can had understated its depreciation charges must give way to the remark that the company had failed to reveal the facts.

**会计方法隐藏的过度折旧案例。** American Can的案例表明应与National Biscuit Company的早期做法进行比较，后者由相同利益集团控制。在1922年之前多年，该公司不断增加工厂数量，但资产账户并未显示出明显增长，只有1920年一年有所上升。向股东提供的折旧报告非常模糊，⁷ 但根据财务手册，该公司的政策是：“折旧为每年30万美元，所有更换和建筑改造项目直接计入运营费用。”

<!--en-->
**A Case of Excessive Depreciation Charges Concealed by Accounting Methods.** The American Can example suggests comparison with the earlier practice of National Biscuit Company, an enterprise controlled largely by the same interests. For many years prior to 1922 the company was constantly adding to the number of its factories, but its property account failed to show any appreciable increase, except in the single year 1920. The reports to stockholders were supremely ambiguous on the matter of depreciation charges,⁷ but according to the financial manuals the company's policy was as follows: "Depreciation is $300,000 per annum, and all items of replacement and building alterations are charged direct to operating expense."

然而，很难避免得出结论：对额外工厂的资本投资实际上是从利润中扣除的，实际收益很可能远高于向公众报告的数值。随着1922年一股股票发行七股以及现金股息率翻三番，这种低估收益的政策被终止。结果，表面收益能力突然翻倍，工厂账户也同步扩张。两个时期之间的对比在此页表格中清晰可见。National Biscuit Company

<!--en-->
It is difficult to avoid the conclusion, however, that the capital investments in additional plants were actually being charged against the profits and that the real earnings were in all probability much larger than those reported to the public. Coincident with the issuance of seven shares of stock for one and the tripling of the cash-dividend rate in 1922, this policy of understating earnings was terminated. The result was a sudden doubling of the apparent earning power, accompanied by an equally sudden expansion in the plant account. The contrast between the two periods is shown forcibly in the table on this page.
National Biscuit Company

**未说明折旧费用。** 在SEC法规出台之前，一些重要公司虽然报告了扣除折旧后的收益，但未能说明为此目的扣除了多少金额。幸运的是，现在所有注册公司都必须提供这一信息。⁸

<!--en-->
**Failure to State Depreciation Charges.** Prior to the S.E.C. regulation some of the important companies reported earnings after depreciation but failed to state the amount deducted for this purpose. Fortunately, this information must now be supplied in the case of every registered company.⁸

## 石油和矿业公司的摊销费用

<!--en-->
*AMORTIZATION CHARGES OF OIL AND MINING COMPANIES*

工业领域这些重要行业受影响摊销的特殊因素。除了常规意义上的折旧——它们通常与其他公司相同的方式计算⁹，还必须考虑矿石或石油储备的消耗。对于矿业企业来说，还有开发费用的因素。而石油生产商则还有无形的钻探成本和无收益的租赁费用等额外费用。这些项目对真实利润有重要影响，且由于不同企业采用的方法不同，会带来麻烦。

<!--en-->
These important sectors of the industrial field are subject to special factors bearing on amortization. In addition to depreciation in the ordinary sense—which they usually calculate in the same way as do other companies⁹ they must allow for depletion of their ore or oil reserves. In the case of mining concerns there is also the factor of development expense. Oil producers, on the other hand, have additional charges for intangible drilling costs and for unproductive leases. These items are important in their bearing on the trueprofits, and they are troublesome because of the varying methods that are followed by different enterprises.

**矿业公司的消耗费用。** 消耗是指通过将资本资产转化为销售产品而使其消耗的过程。适用于生产金属、石油和天然气、硫磺、木材等产品的公司。当这些产品的储量耗尽时，其价值必须通过费用从收益中扣除。对于老牌矿业公司（尤其是铜和硫磺生产商），消耗费用由联邦所得税法中的某些技术要求确定，依据的是1913年3月1日所存在的储量数量和价值，或按产品价值的一定比例计算。由于这些计算中使用了人为的基础，许多公司未在向股东报告中省略消耗费用。

<!--en-->
**Depletion Charges of Mining Companies.** Depletion represents the using up of capital assets by turning them into products for sale. It applies to companies producing metals, oil and gas, sulphur, timber, etc. As the holdings, or reserves, of these products are exhausted, their value must gradually be written off through charges against earnings. In the case of the older mining companies (including particularly the copper and sulphur producers) the depletion charges are determined by certain technical requirements of the federal income tax law, which rest upon the amount and value of the reserves as they were supposed to exist on March 1, 1913, or by applying certain percentages to the value of the product. Because of the artificial base used in these computations, many companies have omitted the depletion charge from their reports to stockholders.

**投资者必须独立计算。** 如我们稍后将说明，矿业公司的投资者通常必须根据自己为采矿资产支付的金额，自行计算消耗预留额。因此，基于公司原始账面成本或为所得税目的设定的特殊数值来计算消耗费用，会令人困惑而非有帮助。因此，不提及矿业公司的消耗费用并不值得批评；但股东在研究报告时必须清楚这一点。此外，在比较矿业公司时，必须正确区分哪些公司在报告收益时扣除了消耗费用，哪些没有。以下是遵循其中一种政策的公司示例：

<!--en-->
**Independent Calculation by Investor Necessary.** As we shall show later, the investor in a mining concern must ordinarily compute his own depletion allowance, based upon the *amount that he has paid* for his share of the mining property. Consequently a depletion charge based either on the company's original book cost or on the special figure set up for income-tax purposes would be confusing rather than helpful. The omission of the depletion charge of mining companies is not to be criticized, therefore; but the stockholder in such enterprises must be well aware of the fact in studying their reports. Furthermore, in any comparison of mining companies a proper distinction must be drawn between those which do and those which do not deduct their depletion charges in reporting their earnings. Following are some examples of companies that pursue one or the other policy:

**石油行业的消耗及类似费用。** 在石油行业，消耗费用与实际经营成本的关系比矿业企业更为密切。后者通常只投资一项或一组资产，其成本会在相当长的时间内逐步扣除。但典型的大型石油生产商每年都会投入大量资金用于新租赁和新井建设。这些新增资产是为了弥补生产导致的储量减少。因此，消耗费用在某种程度上相当于维持储量和生产所需的当前现金支出。新井在第一年可能产出总产量的80%。因此，几乎所有这种“满产”成本都必须在一个财政期间扣除，而来自这一来源的大部分“收益”实际上只是所投入资本的回报。如果投资不能通过消耗和其他费用迅速扣除，利润和资产价值都将严重高估。对于积极参与开发的石油公司，需要扣除的费用包括以下项目：

**Depletion and Similar Charges in the Oil Industry.** In the oil industry depletion charges are more closely related to the actual cost of doing business than in the case of mining enterprises. The latter ordinarily invest in a single property or group of properties, the cost of which is then written off over a fairly long period of years. But the typical large oil producer normally spends substantial sums each year on new leases and new wells. These additional holdings are needed to make up for the shrinkage of reserves through production. The depletion charge corresponds in some measure, therefore, to a current cash outlay for the purpose of maintaining reserves and production. New wells may yield as high as 80% of their total output during the first year. Hence nearly all the cost of such "flush production" must be written off in a single fiscal period, and most of the "earnings" from this source are in reality a return of the capital expended thereon. If the investment is not written off rapidly through depletion and other charges, the profit and the value of the property account will both be grossly overstated. In the case of an oil company actively engaged in development work, the various headings under which write-offs must be made include the following:

1. 有形资产的**折旧**。
2. 基于租赁成本的石油和天然气储备的**消耗**。
3. 被扣除的**无收益租赁**。部分收购和勘探活动始终完全无价值，必须从有收益租赁的收入中扣除。
4. *无形的钻井成本*。这些成本要么一次性作为运营费用冲销，要么在井的寿命期间进行摊销。*示例：*1926年Marland Oil的案例表明，石油公司的报告收益在很大程度上取决于关于摊销的会计政策。这家公司每年花费大量资金购买新租赁权和井位，以维持生产水平。在1926年之前，它把所谓的“无形钻井成本”计入资本账户，然后通过年度摊销费用从收益中冲销。1926年，Marland采用了更保守的政策，将所有这些“无形成本”直接计入收益。对利润的影响如下表所示。*Marland Oil Company*

<!--en-->
1. *Depreciation* of tangible assets.
2. *Depletion* of oil and gas reserves, based upon the cost of the leases.
3. *Unprofitable leases* written off. Part of the acquisitions and exploration will always prove totally valueless and must be charged against the revenue from the productive leases.
4. *Intangible drilling costs*. These are either written off at one time, as equivalent to an operating expense, or amortizedover the life of the well.
*Example:* The case of Marland Oil in 1926 illustrates the extent to which reported earnings of oil companies are dependent upon the accounting policies with respect to amortization. This company spent large sums annually on new leases and wells to maintain its rate of production. Prior to 1926 it charged the so-called “intangible drilling costs” to capital account and then wrote them off against earnings through an annual amortization charge. In 1926 Marland adopted the more conservative policy of charging off all these “intangible costs” currently against earnings. The effect on profits is shown in the following table.
*Marland Oil Company*
