CHAPTER 39

# 普通股的价格收益比率。资本化的调整

<!--en-->
*Price-Earnings Ratios for Common Stocks. Adjustments for Changes in Capitalization*

在前几章中，已经多次提到华尔街关于收益与价值关系的观点。通常认为，某只普通股的价值相当于其当前收益的若干倍。这个倍数部分取决于当时的心理状况，部分取决于企业的性质和业绩。在1927-1929年的牛市期间，十倍收益是公认的衡量标准。更准确地说，这是评估普通股的起点，因此要证明更高的比率，该股票必须被视为特别理想；反之亦然。

<!--en-->
IN PREVIOUS CHAPTERS various references have been made to Wall Street's ideas on the relation of earnings to values. A given common stock is generally considered to be worth a certain number of times its current earnings. This number of times, or multiplier, depends partly on the prevailing psychology and partly on the nature and record of the enterprise. Prior to the 1927–1929 bull market ten times earnings was the accepted standard of measurement. More accurately speaking, it was the common point of departure for valuing common stocks, so that an issue would have to be considered exceptionally desirable to justify a higher ratio, and conversely.

从大约1927年开始，十倍收益标准被一套相当混乱的新标准所取代。一方面，人们倾向于比以前更宽松地评估普通股的价值。这被一位金融领袖的著名格言总结为：好股票的价值是其收益的十五倍。¹ 还有一种趋势是对不同类型普通股进行更全面的区分。例如，1928-1929年，公共事业和连锁店等特别受青睐的公司，以当前收益的25到40倍价格出售。包括“蓝筹股”在内的各类领先企业也是如此。如前所述，这些慷慨的估值基于过去较长或较短时期内出现的上升趋势的假设。1932年之后，由于长期利率急剧下降，价格相对于收益呈现更高趋势的趋势出现了。

<!--en-->
Beginning about 1927 the ten-times-earnings standard was superseded by a rather confusing set of new yardsticks. On the one hand, there was a tendency to value common stocks in general more liberally than before. This was summarized in a famous dictum of a financial leader implying that good stocks were worth fifteen times their earnings.¹ There was also the tendency to make more sweeping distinctions in the valuations of different kinds of common stocks. Companies in especially favored groups, e.g., public utilities and chain stores, in 1928–1929, sold at a very high multiple of current earnings, say, twenty-five to forty times. This was true also of the “blue chip” issues, which comprised leading units in miscellaneous fields. As pointed out before, these generous valuations were based upon the assumed continuance of the upward trendshown over a longer or shorter period in the past. Subsequent to 1932 there developed a tendency for prices to rule higher in relation to earnings because of the sharp drop in long-term interest rates.

**无法准确评估。**证券分析不能假定为任何特定普通股设定“正确价值”的一般规则。实际上，不存在这样的东西。价值基础变化太快，无法形成甚至看似合理的准确公式。以当前收益为基础评估价值的整个概念本身似乎荒谬，因为我们知道当前收益在不断变化。而倍数应该是十、十五还是三十，最终似乎纯粹是任意选择的问题。

<!--en-->
**Exact Appraisal Impossible.** Security analysis cannot presume to lay down general rules as to the “proper value” of any given common stock. Practically speaking, there is no such thing. The bases of value are too shifting to admit of any formulation that could claim to be even reasonably accurate. The whole idea of basing the value upon current earnings seems inherently absurd, since we know that the current earnings are constantly changing. And whether the multiplier should be ten or fifteen or thirty would seem at bottom a matter of purely arbitrary choice.

但股市本身没有时间考虑这种科学上的顾虑。它必须先确定其价值，再寻找依据。它的运作方式类似于法庭中审理违约案件时的陪审团；无法可靠地衡量相关价值，但必须找到某种方式来计算并作出裁决。因此，普通股票的价格并非经过仔细计算的结果，而是无数人类反应的总和。股市更像是一个投票机而非称重机——它根据实际数据做出反应，但不是直接基于这些数据，而是取决于它们对买家和卖家决策的影响。

<!--en-->
But the stock market itself has no time for such scientific scruples. It must make its values first and find its reasons afterwards. Its position is much like that of a jury in a breach-of-promise suit; there is no sound way of measuring the values involved, and yet they must be measured somehow and a verdict rendered. Hence the prices of common stocks are not carefully thought out computations but the resultants of a welter of human reactions. The stock market is a voting machine rather than a weighing machine. It responds to factual data not directly but only as they affect the decisions of buyers and sellers.

**分析师在股票价格评估领域有限的功能。**面对不断变化的事实和波动的人类观念，证券分析师显然无法对普通股票价格做出普遍判断。不过，他可以在这一领域承担一些具体但有限的职能，以下是其中一些代表性的职能：

<!--en-->
**Limited Functions of the Analyst in Field of Appraisal of Stock Prices.** Confronted by this mixture of changing facts and fluctuating human fancies, the securities analyst is clearly incapable of passing judgment on common-stock prices generally. There are, however, some concrete, if limited, functions that he may carry on in this field, of which the following are representative:

1. 他可以建立*保守型*或*投资型*普通股票估值的基础，与投机性估值区分开来。
2. 他可以指出以下因素的重要性：(a)资本结构；(b)收入来源，因为这些因素会影响特定股票的估值。
3. 他可以发现资产负债表中的异常元素，这些元素会影响收益情况的含义。

<!--en-->
1. He may set up a basis for *conservative* or *investment* valuation of common stocks, as distinguished from speculative valuations.
2. He may point out the significance of: (a) the capitalization structure; and (b) the source of income, as bearing upon the valuation of a given stock issue.
3. He may find unusual elements in the balance sheet which affect the implications of the earnings picture.

## 投资估值的最高建议标准。

<!--en-->
*A Suggested Basis of Maximum Appraisal for Investment.*

普通股票投资者与投机者一样，依赖未来收益而非过去收益。他的基本估值基础必须是对未来盈利能力的明智且保守的估计。但他的未来收益*衡量标准*只有受到一段时间实际表现的限制才能算是保守的。然而，我们建议，如果(1)该年的整体商业状况不是特别好，(2)公司过去几年收益呈上升趋势，以及(3)投资者对行业的分析让他相信行业将继续发展，那么最近一年的利润单独来看，可以被接受为未来收益的衡量标准。在非常特殊的情况下，投资者可能认为未来收益会高于过去任何时期。这可能是由于专利开发、矿山发现新矿石或类似重大事件导致的。但在大多数情况下，他将根据五到十年期间的平均收益来估算普通股票的投资价值。这并不意味着所有平均收益相同的普通股票都具有相同价值。普通股票投资者（即*保守型买家*）会给予那些当前收益高于平均水平或被认为具有比平均水平更好的前景或内在稳定盈利能力的股票更宽松的估值。但我们的观点核心是：为了保持保守估值的范围，*在任何情况下*都必须对倍数设定一个适度上限。我们建议，*约20倍于平均收益*是投资购买普通股票所能达到的最高价格。

<!--en-->
The investor in common stocks, equally with the speculator, is dependent on future rather than past earnings. His fundamental basis of appraisal must be an intelligent and conservative estimate of the future earning power. But his *measure* of future earnings can be conservative only if it is limited by actual performance over a period of time. We have suggested, however, that the profits of the most recent year, taken singly, might be accepted as the gage of future earnings, *if* (1) general business conditions in that year were not exceptionally good, (2) the company has shown an upward trend of earnings for some years past and (3) the investor's study of the industry gives him confidence in its continued growth. In a very exceptional case, the investor may be justified in counting on higher earnings in the future than at any time in the past. This might follow from developments involving a patent or the discovery of new ore in a mine or some similar specific and significant occurrence. But in most instances he will derive the investment value of a common stock from the average earnings of a period between five and ten years. This does not mean that all common stocks with the same average earnings should have the same value. The common-stock investor (*i.e.*, the *conservative buyer*) will properly accord a more liberal valuation to those issues which have current earnings above the average or which may reasonably be considered to possess better than average prospects or an inherently stable earning power. But it is the essence of our viewpoint that some moderate upper limit must *in every case* be placed on the multiplier in order to stay within the bounds of conservative valuation. We would suggest that *about 20 times average earnings* is as high a price as can be paid in an *investment* purchase of a common stock.

虽然这条规则在性质上必然具有任意性，但并非完全如此。投资需要可证明的价值，典型普通股票的价值只能通过已确立的、即平均盈利能力来证明。但很难理解，市场价低于5%的平均收益如何能被视为该价格的合理依据。显然，这样的市盈率无法提供我们与投资者立场相关的*安全边际*。它可能被购买者接受，期望未来收益会高于过去。但在术语原始且最实用的意义上，这种估值基础属于*投机性*的。它不属于普通股票投资的范畴。

<!--en-->
Although this rule is of necessity arbitrary in its nature, it is not entirely so. Investment presupposes demonstrable value, and the typical common stock's value can be demonstrated only by means of an established, *i.e.*, an average, earning power. But it is difficult to see how average earnings of *less*than 5% upon the market price could ever be considered as vindicating that price. Clearly such a price-earnings ratio could not provide that *margin of safety* which we have associated with the investor's position. It might be accepted by a purchaser in the expectation that future earnings will be larger than in the past. But in the original and most useful sense of the term such a basis of valuation is *speculative*.² It falls outside the purview of common-stock investment.

*投机性投资可能会面临更高的价格。* 这种区别的含义必须明确理解。我们并不认为以平均收益的20倍以上价格购买普通股票是错误行为。我们只是认为这样的价格属于投机行为。虽然购买后可能获得巨大利润，但那样的话就证明这是一次明智或幸运的投机。此外，应该指出，很少有人在投机操作中始终能保持明智或幸运。因此，我们可以得出一个具有重大实际意义的结论：*那些经常以平均收益的20倍以上价格购买普通股票的人，从长远来看很可能会损失大量资金。*这种情况更有可能发生，因为如果没有这种机械性的约束，他们容易反复被牛市吸引，而牛市总是能找到一些看似合理的理由，为支付高昂的普通股票价格提供借口。

<!--en-->
*Higher Prices May Prevail for Speculative Commitments.* The intent of this distinction must be clearly understood. We do not imply that it is a mistake to pay more than 20 times average earnings for any common stock. We do suggest that such a price would be speculative. The purchase may easily turn out to be highly profitable, but in that case it will have proved a wise or fortunate speculation. It is proper to remark, moreover, that very few people are consistently wise or fortunate in their speculative operations. Hence we may submit, as a corollary of no small practical importance, *that people who habitually purchase common stocks at more than about 20 times their average earnings are likely to lose considerable money in the long run.* This is the more probable because, in the absence of such a mechanical check, they are prone to succumb recurrently to the lure of bull markets, which always find some specious argument to justify paying extravagant prices for common stocks.

*投资级普通股的其他要求及其推论*。需要指出的是，如果将平均收益的20倍作为投资购买价格的*上限*，那么通常支付的价格应远低于此最大值。这表明，对于前景中性的公司而言，平均收益的约12或$12\frac{1}{2}$倍可能较为合适。我们还必须强调，市场价格与平均收益的合理比例并非投资普通股的唯一要求。这是必要条件，但非充分条件。该公司在财务结构和管理方面也必须令人满意，其前景也不应不乐观。

<!--en-->
*Other Requisites for Common Stocks of Investment Grade and a Corollary Therefrom.* It should be pointed out that if 20 times average earnings is taken as the *upper limit* of price for an investment purchase, then ordinarily the price paid should be substantially less than this maximum. This suggests that about 12 or $12\frac{1}{2}$ times average earnings may be suitable for the typical case of a company with neutral prospects. We must emphasize also that a reasonable ratio of market price to average earnings is not the only requisite for a common-stock investment. It is a necessary but not a sufficient condition. The company must be satisfactory also in its financial set-up and management, and not unsatisfactory in its prospects.

根据这一原则，还有另一个重要推论：具有吸引力的普通股投资就是有吸引力的投机行为。这是正确的，因为如果普通股能够满足保守型投资者的需求——即让他获得足够的投资回报，并且未来前景令人满意，那么这种股票必然也有合理的机会在市场价值上上升。

<!--en-->
From this principle there follows another important corollary, *viz.: An attractive common-stock investment is an attractive speculation*. This is true because, if a common stock can meet the demand of a conservative investor that he get full value for his money *plus* not unsatisfactory future prospects, then such an issue must also have a fair chance of appreciating in market value.

# 投机股与投资型普通股的示例。

<!--en-->
*Examples of Speculative and Investment Common Stocks.*

我们对购买普通股的投资依据的定义，与华尔街对于高评级普通股的运作方式存在差异。对于这类股票，人们认为价格需达到平均收益的20倍以上才具有合理性；此外，无论以什么价格出售，这些股票都被定义为“投资股票”。我们认为，为“最优质普通股”支付的高价使得这些购买行为本质上属于投机行为，因为它们需要未来的增长来证明其合理性。因此，按照我们的定义，普通股投资操作将在市场处于中间状态，介于因质量存疑而属于投机的低价股票，以及因价格过高而同样属于投机的稳固股票之间。

<!--en-->
Our definition of an investment basis for common-stock purchases is at variance with the Wall Street practice in respect to common stocks of high rating. For such issues a price of considerably more than 20 times average earnings is held to be warranted, and furthermore these stocks are designated as “investment issues” regardless of the price at which they sell. According to our view, the high prices paid for “the best common stocks” make these purchases essentially speculative, because they require future growth to justify them. Hence common-stock investment operations, as we define them, will occupy a middle ground in the market, lying between low-price issues that are speculative because of doubtful quality and well-entrenched issues that are speculative, none the less, because of their high price.

<!--en-->
These distinctions are illustrated by³ the accompanying nine examples, taken as of December 31, 1938.

**B组：由于记录不规律，1938年12月存在投机行为的普通股***关于各组的评论。* A组列出的公司代表了所谓的“一级”或“蓝筹股”工业企业，在1928–1929年的大规模投机以及随后几年的市场中特别受青睐。它们以强大的财务状况、看似良好的前景以及大多数情况下过去相对稳定或增长的收益为特征。*然而，股票的*市场价格*高于其平均收益所能解释的水平。实际上，1929–1938十年中*最佳*一年的利润仅相当于1938年12月市场价格的8%以下。这类股票的另一个特点是，其售价远高于实际投资资本。

<!--en-->
**Group B: Common Stocks Speculative in December 1938 Because of Their Irregular Record***Comments on the Various Groups.* The companies listed in Group *A* are representative of the so-called “first-grade” or “blue chip” industrials, which were particularly favored in the great speculation of 1928–1929 and in the markets of ensuing years. They are characterized by a strong financial position, by presumably excellent prospects and in most cases by relatively stable or growing earnings in the past. *The market price* of the shares, however, was higher than would be justified by their average earnings. In fact the profits of the *best* year in the 1929–1938 decade were less than 8% of the December 1938 market price. It is also characteristic of such issues that they sell for enormous premiums above the actual capital invested.

*B组*中分析的公司显然属于投机性质，因为其收益记录极不稳定。它们显示出市场价格与平均收益、最高收益及资产价值之间的不同关系。

<!--en-->
The companies analyzed in Group *B* are obviously speculative, because of the great instability of their earnings records. They show varying relationships of market price to average earnings, maximum earnings, and asset values.

*C组*中显示的普通股是符合特定投资质量测试的示例。这些测试包括以下内容：

<!--en-->
The common stocks shown in Group *C* are examples of those which meet specific and quantitative tests of investment quality. These tests include the following:

1. 尽管在十年期间商业状况存在巨大波动，但收益仍保持相对稳定。
2. 平均收益与市场价格的比例令人满意。⁴
3. 财务结构足够保守，营运资本状况良好。虽然我们不建议用于投资的普通股必须*要求*其资产价值等于支付价格，但*C组*中的股票整体特征在于，其售价不会远高于公司实际资源。我们所设想的普通股*投资*将仅限于*C组*所展示的那种股票。但实际购买此类股票时，购买者还必须认为企业前景至少相当有利。

<!--en-->
1. The earnings have been reasonably stable, allowing for the tremendous fluctuations in business conditions during the ten-year period.
2. The average earnings bear a satisfactory ratio to market price.⁴
3. The financial set-up is sufficiently conservative, and the working-capital position is strong.
Although we do not suggest that a common stock bought for investment be *required* to show asset values equal to the price paid, it is none the less characteristic of issues in Group *C* that, as a whole, they will not sell for a huge premium above the companies' actual resources.
Common-stock *investment*, as we envisage it, will confine itself to issues making exhibits of the kind illustrated by Group *C*. But the actual purchase of any such issues must require *also* that the purchaser be satisfied in his own mind that the prospects of the enterprise are at least reasonably favorable.

## 资本变动允许范围

<!--en-->
*ALLOWANCES FOR CHANGES IN CAPITALIZATION*

在处理按股计算的过去收益记录时，基本需要调整数据以反映该期间发生的重大资本变化。最简单的情况下，仅涉及因股票分红、分拆等导致的普通股数量变化。此时只需根据当前股数重新计算整个期间的资本。（一些统计机构会进行此类重新计算，但其他机构则不会。）

<!--en-->
In dealing with the past record of earnings, when given on a per-share basis, it is elementary that the figures must be adjusted to reflect any important changes in the capitalization which have taken place during the period. In the simplest case these will involve a change only in the number of shares of common stock due to stock dividends, split-ups, etc. All that is necessary then is to restate the capitalization throughout the period on the basis of the current number of shares. (Such recalculations are made by some of the statistical services but not by others.)

当资本变动是由于以相对较低价格出售额外股票（通常是通过行使认购权或认股权证）或转换高级证券所致时，调整较为困难。在这种情况下，早期期间可用于普通股的收益必须加上因发行额外股份可能带来的收益。当债券或优先股转换为普通股时，之前支付的费用需加回收益中，然后应用于更多数量的股份。如果股票以相对较低的价格出售，适当的调整可让出售所得收益达到5%至8%。（除非所示变化显著，否则无需进行此类重新计算。）

<!--en-->
When the change in capitalization has been due to the sale of additional stock at a comparatively low price (usually through the exercise of subscription rights or warrants) or to the conversion of senior securities, the adjustment is more difficult. In such cases the earnings available for the common during the earlier period must be increased by whatever gain would have followed from the issuance of the additional shares. When bonds or preferred stocks have been converted into common, the charges formerly paid thereon are to beadded back to the earnings and the new figure then applied to the larger number of shares. If stock has been sold at a relatively low price, a proper adjustment would allow earnings of, say, 5 to 8% on the proceeds of the sale. (Such recalculations need not be made unless the changes indicated thereby are substantial.)

有时必须对每股收益进行相应调整，以反映由于转换或行使期权认股权证可能导致流通股数量*未来*增加的情况。当其他证券持有者有权选择时，合理分析必须考虑行使期权可能对普通股每股收益产生的不利影响。

<!--en-->
A corresponding adjustment of the per-share earnings must be made at times to reflect the possible *future* increase in the number of shares outstanding as a result of conversions or exercise of option warrants. When other security holders have a choice of any kind, sound analysis must allow for the possible adverse effect upon the per-share earnings of the common stock that would follow from the exercise of the option.

*示例：* 在分析美国航空公司截至1939年9月30日的12个月报告收益时，必须进行此类调整。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* This type of adjustment must be made in analyzing the reported earnings of American Airlines, Inc., for the 12 months ended September 30, 1939.

报告收益................... 每股1,128,000美元，约300,000股流通股。3.76美元（1939年12月价格约为37美元）。但还有2,600,000美元4 1/2%债券在流通，可转换为每股12.50美元的普通股。分析师必须*假设*债券转换，得到以下调整后结果：

<!--en-->
Earnings as reported................... $1,128,000
Per share on about 300,000 shares outstanding.. $3.76
(Price December 1939 about 37)
But there were outstanding $2,600,000 of 4 1/2% debentures, convertible into common stock at $12.50 per share. The analyst must *assume* conversion of the bonds, giving the following adjusted result:

收益加上回拨117,000美元利息...... 每股1,245,000美元，508,000股................. 2.45美元。进行必要调整后，报告每股收益的三分之一以上会损失。

<!--en-->
Earnings, adding back $117,000 interest ....... $1,245,000
Per share on 508,000 shares ................. $2.45
More than one-third of the reported earnings per share are lost when the necessary adjustment is made.

美国水厂电力公司可用于说明两种调整类型。（见下一页。）

<!--en-->
American Water Works and Electric Company can be used to illustrate both types of adjustment. (See the next page.)

调整*A*反映了1928年、1929年和1930年的股票分红支付。

<!--en-->
Adjustment *A* reflects the payment of stock dividends in 1928, 1929 and 1930.

调整*B*假设1934年发行的15,000,000美元可转换5s债券进行转换，从而增加了收益中的利息费用，同时增加了750,000股普通股发行量。（上述调整与之前讨论的关于折旧费用质疑可能对报告收益产生的任何修改无关。）

<!--en-->
Adjustment *B* assumes conversion of the $15,000,000 of convertible 5s, issued in 1934, thus increasing the earnings by the amount of the interest charges but also increasing the common-stock issue by 750,000 shares. (The foregoingadjustments are independent of any possible modifications in the reported earnings arising from the questioning of the depreciation charges, etc., as previously discussed.)

## 参与权益的预留

<!--en-->
*ALLOWANCES FOR PARTICIPATING INTERESTS*

计算普通股的收益时，必须充分承认参与发行股票的持有人的权利，无论相关金额是否实际支付。对于管理合同规定将大部分利润作为补偿的情况，也应进行类似的预留，如投资信托的情况。有时会出现涉及“受限股票”的特殊情况，其股息取决于收益或其他因素。

<!--en-->
In calculating the earnings available for the common, full recognition must be given to the rights of holders of participating issues, whether or not the amounts involved are actually being paid thereon. Similar allowances must be made for the effect of management contracts providing for a substantial percentage of the profits as compensation, as in the case of investment trusts. Unusual cases sometimes arise involving “restricted shares,” dividends on which are contingent upon earnings or other considerations.

*示例：* Trico Products Corporation是一家大型汽车配件制造商，其普通股的资本化为675,000股。其中450,000股（由总裁持有）最初被限制分红。非受限股票首先有权获得每股2.50美元的股息，之后两类股票平等分享后续股息。此外，根据1925年及后续几年的收益达到特定规定数值，逐步解除受限股票的限制。（到1938年底，共有239,951股被解除限制。）

<!--en-->
*Example:* Trico Products Corporation, a large manufacturer of automobile accessories, is capitalized at 675,000 shares of common stock, of which 450,000 shares (owned by the president) were originally “restricted” as to dividends. The unrestricted stock is first entitled to dividends of $2.50 per share, after which both classes share equally infurther dividends. In addition, successive blocks of the restricted stock were to be released from the restriction according as the earnings for 1925 and successive years reached certain stipulated figures. (To the end of 1938, a total of 239,951 shares had been thus released.)

**General Rule.** The material in the last few pages may be summarized in the following general rule:

在可转换证券之前，或因行使股票期权或其他证券持有者享有的参与特权而受到稀释的情况下，普通股的内在价值，无法合理评估得高于如果完全行使所有此类特权的数值。[^2423]：¹ 1928年3月26日《华尔街日报》中引用的这句话是：“根据道琼斯、琼斯公司的平均数据，通用汽车股票应以15倍的收益能力价格出售，即约每股225美元；而目前价格为180美元，大约只以12倍的当前收益价格出售。”

<!--en-->
The intrinsic value of a common stock preceded by convertible securities, or subject to dilution through the exercise of stock options or through participating privileges enjoyed by other security holders, cannot reasonably be appraised at a higher figure than would be justified if all such privileges were exercised in full.
[^2423]: ¹ The wording of this statement, as quoted in the *Wall Street Journal* of March 26, 1928, was as follows: “‘General Motors shares, according to the Dow, Jones & Co. averages,’ Mr. Raskob remarked, ‘should sell at fifteen times earning power, or in the neighborhood of $225 per share, whereas at the present level of $180 they sell at approximately only twelve times current earnings.’”

CHAPTER 40

## 资本化结构

<!--en-->
*Capitalization Structure*

公司总资本化在高级证券和普通股之间的分配，对每股收益能力的重要性有重要影响。一组假设示例有助于阐明这一点。为此，我们假设有三家工业公司A、B和C，每家的收益能力（即平均和近期收益）为1,000,000美元。它们在资本化结构方面完全相同。公司A仅以100,000股普通股进行资本化。公司B有600,000美元4%债券和100,000股普通股。公司C有12,000,000美元4%债券和100,000股普通股。

<!--en-->
THE DIVISION of a company's total capitalization between senior securities and common stock has an important bearing upon the significance of the earning power per share. A set of hypothetical examples will help make this point clear. For this purpose we shall postulate three industrial companies, A, B and C, each with an earning power (i.e., with average and recent earnings) of $1,000,000. They are identical in all respects save capitalization structure. Company A is capitalized solely at 100,000 shares of common stock. Company B has outstanding $6,000,000 of 4% bonds and 100,000 shares of common stock. Company C has outstanding $12,000,000 of 4% bonds and 100,000 shares of common stock.

我们假设债券按面值计价，普通股的价值约为其每股收益的12倍。那么三家公司的价值如下：

<!--en-->
We shall assume that the bonds are worth par and that the common stocks are worth about 12 times their per-share earnings. Then the value of the three companies will work out as follows:

<table><thead><tr><td>公司</td><td>普通股的收益</td><td>普通股的价值</td><td>债券的价值</td><td>公司总价值</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>A</td><td>$1,000,000</td><td>$12,000,000</td><td></td><td>$12,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>B</td><td>760,000</td><td>9,000,000</td><td>$6,000,000</td><td>15,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>C</td><td>520,000</td><td>6,000,000</td><td>12,000,000</td><td>18,000,000</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><td>Company</td><td>Earnings for common stock</td><td>Value of common stock</td><td>Value of bonds</td><td>Total value of company</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>A</td><td>$1,000,000</td><td>$12,000,000</td><td></td><td>$12,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>B</td><td>760,000</td><td>9,000,000</td><td>$6,000,000</td><td>15,000,000</td></tr><tr><td>C</td><td>520,000</td><td>6,000,000</td><td>12,000,000</td><td>18,000,000</td></tr></tbody></table>

这些结果令人困惑。具有相同盈利能力的企业，似乎因资本结构的不同而拥有截然不同的价值。但资本结构本身也是管理层自愿决定的结果。这是否意味着，通过调整优先股和普通股的相对比例，企业公允价值可以任意增加或减少？

<!--en-->
These results challenge attention. Companies with identical earning power appear to have widely differing values, due solely to the arrangement of their capitalization. But the capitalization structure is itself a matter of voluntary determination by those in control. Does this mean that the fair value of an enterprise can be arbitrarily increased or decreasedby changing around the relative proportions of senior securities and common stock?

**企业价值能否通过资本结构的任意调整而改变？** 要正确回答这个问题，我们必须更仔细地分析我们的例子。在计算三家公司的价值时，我们假设债券价值等于面值，而股票价值为其盈利的十二倍。这些假设是否合理？我们先考虑 *B* 公司的情况。如果情况没有不利因素，债券的价格可能会达到约100，因为利息是盈利的四倍。此外，这种有融资债务的存在通常不会阻止普通股以其既定盈利能力为基准的十二倍价格出售。

<!--en-->
**Can the Value of an Enterprise Be Altered Through Arbitrary Variations in Capital Structure?** To answer this question properly we must scrutinize our examples with greater care. In working out the value of the three companies we assumed that the bonds would be worth par and that the stocks would be worth twelve times their earnings. Are these assumptions tenable? Let us consider first the case of Company *B*. If there are no unfavorable elements in the picture, the bonds might well sell at about 100, since the interest is earned four times. Nor would the presence of this funded debt ordinarily prevent the common stock from selling at 12 times its established earning power.

不过，有人会指出：如果公司 *B* 的股价是其收益的12倍，那么公司 *A* 的股价应该高于这个倍数，因为公司 *A* 没有债务负担。因此风险更小，其收益下降的影响也小于公司 *B* 的股票。这显然是正确的，但同样正确的是，公司 *B* 的股价会对收益**增长**有更大的反应。以下数据清楚地说明了这一点：

<!--en-->
It will be urged however, that, if Company *B* shares are worth 12 times their earnings, Company *A* shares should be worth more than this multiple because they have no debt ahead of them. The risk is therefore smaller, and they are less vulnerable to the effect of a shrinkage in earnings than is the stock of Company *B*. This is obviously true, and yet it is equally true that Company *B* shares will be more responsive to an *increase* in earnings. The following figures bring this point out clearly:

<table><thead><tr><th rowspan="2">假设收入</th><th colspan="2">每股收益</th><th colspan="2">每股收益的变化情况</th></tr><tr><th>公司 A</th><th>公司 B</th><th>公司 A</th><th>公司 B</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>$1,000,000</td><td>$10.00</td><td>$ 7.60</td><td>(基础)</td><td>(基础)</td></tr><tr><td>750,000</td><td>7.50</td><td>5.10</td><td>-25%</td><td>-33%</td></tr><tr><td>1,250,000</td><td>12.50</td><td>10.10</td><td>+25%</td><td>+33%</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th rowspan="2">Assumed earnings</th><th colspan="2">Earned per share</th><th colspan="2">Change in earnings per share from base</th></tr><tr><th>Co. A</th><th>Co. B</th><th>Co. A</th><th>Co. B</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>$1,000,000</td><td>$10.00</td><td>$ 7.60</td><td>(Base)</td><td>(Base)</td></tr><tr><td>750,000</td><td>7.50</td><td>5.10</td><td>-25%</td><td>-33%</td></tr><tr><td>1,250,000</td><td>12.50</td><td>10.10</td><td>+25%</td><td>+33%</td></tr></tbody></table>

是否公平地认为，公司 *B* 对利润可能下降的更敏感程度，会被其对利润可能增长更敏感程度所抵消呢？此外，如果投资者预计未来收益会更高——并且他选择普通股时也是基于这一预期——他是否应该选择能从一定程度的改善中获得更多好处的股票呢？因此，我们回到最初的结论：仅因公司 *B* 在债券和股票之间的资本分配方式不同，其价值可能高达 3,000,000 美元，比公司 *A* 高出 25%。

<!--en-->
Would it not be fair to assume that the greater sensitivity of Company *B* to a possible decline in profits is offset by its greater sensitivity to a possible increase? Furthermore, if the investor expects higher earnings in the future—and presumably he selects his common stocks with this in mind—would he not be justified in selecting the issue that will benefit more from a given degree of improvement? We are thus led back to the original conclusions that Company *B* may beworth $3,000,000, or 25% more than Company *A* due solely to its distribution of capitalization between bonds and stock.

### 最优资本结构原则。

<!--en-->
*Principle of Optimum Capitalization Structure.*

尽管这一结论可能看起来矛盾，但它得到了市場中普通股的实际表现的支持。如果我们对这种矛盾进行更深入的分析，会发现它源于对公司 *A* 资本结构的一种*过度简化*。公司 *A* 的普通股显然包含了公司 *B* 债券和股票所代表的两种要素。公司 *A* 的部分股票实际上相当于公司 *B* 的债券，*理论上*应该按照相同的标准进行估值，即 4%。那么，公司 *A* 的剩余部分则应按收益的 12 倍进行估值。这种理论推理会得出总价值为 15,000,000 美元，即公司 *A* 股票两个组成部分的平均$6^{2/3}\%$价值，当然这与公司 *B* 债券和股票的整体价值相同。

<!--en-->
Paradoxical as this conclusion may seem, it is supported by the actual behavior of common stocks in the market. If we subject this contradiction to closer analysis, we shall find that it arises from what may be called an *oversimplification* of Company *A*'s capital structure. Company *A*'s common stock evidently contains the two elements represented by the bonds and stock of Company *B*. Part of Company *A*'s stock is at bottom equivalent to Company *B*'s bonds and should *in theory* be valued on the same basis, *i.e.*, 4%. The remainder of Company *A*'s stock should then be valued at 12 times earnings. This theoretical reasoning would give us a combined value of $15,000,000, *i.e.*, an average $6^{2/3}\%$ basis, for the two components of Company *A* stock, which, of course, is the same as that of Company *B* bonds and stock taken together.

但对于公司 *A* 股票的 15,000,000 美元价值，实际上通常无法实际实现。明显的原因是：普通股投资者很少意识到普通股票发行中存在“债券成分”，而且无论如何，由于不希望有这种债券成分，他们也不愿意额外支付费用。¹这一事实让我们得出一个重要原则，既适用于证券购买者，也适用于企业管理层，即：

<!--en-->
But this $15,000,000 value for Company *A* stock would not ordinarily be realized *in practice*. The obvious reason is that the common-stock buyer will rarely recognize the existence of a “bond component” in a common-stock issue, and in any event, not wanting such a bond component, he is unwilling to pay extra for it.¹ This fact leads us to an important principle, both for the security buyer and for corporate management, *viz.*:

*任何企业的最佳资本结构包括高优先级证券，使其可以安全发行和购买用于投资。* 具体来说，从股东角度而言，*B公司*的资本配置比*A公司*更优，前提是两种情况下600万美元的债券发行都能被视为稳健的投资。（这可能需要企业根据第13章推荐的严格标准，证明其营运资金净额不少于600万美元。）在这种条件下，普通股股东提供全部资本的做法可能被称为*过于保守的安排*，因为通常会导致股东每单位资本的收益低于借入合理部分资本的情况。类似情况也存在于大多数私营企业中，人们认为使用保守的银行信贷满足季节性需求，而不是完全依赖所有者资本来融资，是一种有利且合理的政策。

<!--en-->
*The optimum capitalization structure for any enterprise includes senior securities to the extent that they may safely be issued and bought for investment.*
Concretely this means that the capitalization arrangement of Company *B* is preferable to that of Company *A* from the stockholder's standpoint, assuming that in both cases the $6,000,000 bond issue would constitute a sound investment. (This might require, among other things, that the companies show a net working capital of not less than $6,000,000 in accordance with the stringent tests for sound industrial issues recommended in Chap. 13.) Under such conditions the contribution of the entire capital by the common stockholders may be called an *overconservative set-up*, as it tends generallyto make the stockholder's dollar less productive to him than if a reasonable part of the capital were borrowed. An analogous situation holds true in most private businesses, where it is recognized as profitable and proper policy to use a conservative amount of banking accommodation for seasonal needs rather than to finance operations entirely by owners' capital.

## 导致稳健债券短缺的企业行为

<!--en-->
*Corporate Practices Resulting in Shortage of Sound*

**工业债券。** 此外，从银行角度而言，稳健的企业应季节性借款也是可取的；从投资者角度而言，强大的工业公司通过出售债券筹集适当比例的资本同样是可取的。这种政策将增加市场上优质债券的数量，为债券投资者提供更多选择，使出售劣质债券变得困难。不幸的是，近年来工业公司的做法往往导致优质工业债券短缺。强大企业通常避免发行新债券，在许多情况下还退出了旧债券。但最强大的工业公司避免债务债券的做法，实际上在多个方面对投资者和投资政策产生了负面影响。1934年写的以下观点至今仍大部分适用：

<!--en-->
**Industrial Bonds.** Furthermore, just as it is desirable from the bank's standpoint that sound businesses borrow seasonally, it is also desirable from the standpoint of investors generally that strong industrial corporations raise an appropriate part of their capital through the sale of bonds. Such a policy would increase the number of high-grade bond issues on the market, giving the bond investor a wider range of choice and making it deservedly difficult to sell unsound bonds. Unfortunately the practice of industrial corporations in recent years has tended to produce a shortage of good industrial bond issues. Strong enterprises have in general refrained from floating new bonds and in many cases have retired old ones. But this avoidance of bonded debt by the strongest industrial companies has in fact produced results demoralizing to investors and investment policies in a number of ways. The following observations on this point, written in 1934, are still applicable in good part:

1. 这种做法倾向于将新的工业债券融资限制在实力较弱的公司身上。优质债券的相对稀缺促使投资机构出售、投资者购买劣质债券，不可避免地导致灾难性后果。
2. 优质债券短缺也促使投资者转向优先股领域。正如之前详细阐述的（第14章），纯优先股在理论上是不可靠的，因此作为一类投资工具，它们很可能无法获得满意的投资回报。
3. 在许多大型公司的设立中，高级证券的剔除（或虚拟剔除）当然提升了其普通股的投资价值，但进一步增加了投资者对这些普通股的需求。这反过来导致那些因情况需要购买稳健债券的人大量买入普通股。此外，它为这些普通股定价过高提供了表面上的理由；最后，它强烈加剧了投资动机与投机动机之间的混淆，在1927–1929年间，这种混淆使得国家中很大一部分曾经谨慎的投资者受到损害。**当资本结构偏重时对收益的评估**。为了进一步推进这一资本结构理论，让我们以*C公司*为例进行分析。我们假设*C公司*1200万美元的债券发行将以面值出售，股票价格为每股5.20美元收益的12倍，从而得出该企业的估值为1800万美元。但关于债券价格的这一假设显然是错误的。两倍于利息支出的收益不足以作为工业债券的保障，因此投资者不应以面值购买此类债券。实际上，这个例子很好地证明了我们的观点：两倍于利息支出的覆盖程度是不够的。如果足够——正如一些投资者所认为的那样——任何经营状况尚可、投资获得8%收益的企业，通过出售4%的债券发行就能收回全部资本，并且还能保持对企业的控制权及一半的收益。这样的安排对企业家来说非常吸引人，但从购买债券的人来说却很愚蠢。*C公司*的例子也揭示了利率对高级证券表面安全性的影响。如果1200万美元的债券发行附带6%的票面利率，那么720000美元的利息支出将低于0倍。假设*D公司*有如此的债券发行。一个谨慎的投资者，看到这两份资料，可能会因为*D公司*6%的债券只有1.39倍的利息覆盖而认为它们不安全，但会因为对两倍固定支出的收益感到满意而接受*C公司*的债券面值。这种区分几乎不明智。我们的投资者会仅仅因为债券支付慷慨的票面利率就拒绝它，而仅仅因为低利率就接受另一只债券。然而，真正重要的是，债券发行的最低安全边际必须设定得足够高，以避免仅通过降低利率就似乎实现了安全的情况。同样的推理当然也适用于优先股的分红率。由于*C公司*的债券因发行规模过大而不安全，它们很可能以比面值低得多的价格出售。我们无法建议此类发行的适当价格水平，但在第26章中指出，由于安全性不足而具有投机性的债券通常不应以70以上价格购买。此外，这种过度债券发行的存在也可能阻止股票以收益12倍的价格出售，因为保守的股票买家会避免*C公司*，因为它面临财务困难的风险过高。结果很可能是，*C公司*的债券和股票发行综合价格不会像最初假设的1800万美元，而是低于1500万美元（*B公司*的估值），甚至低于1200万美元（*A公司*的价值）。事实上，应该认识到，这种不利结果未必必然发生。 如果投资者足够粗心，而投机者足够热情，那么*C*公司的证券可能会在市场上以18,000,000美元甚至更高的价格出售。但这种情况是不合理的，也不合理。²我们的资本结构理论无法接受*C*公司的这种安排，因为从任何意义上讲，它都不符合标准或合适的要求。这表明，使用优先证券所能获得的优势存在明确的限制。我们已经在最优资本结构原则中表达了这一事实：当优先证券的数量超过可以安全发行或用于投资的数量时，它们就不再具有优势。我们将*A*类型的资本安排称为“过于保守”；*C*类型可称为“投机性”，而*B*类型的则完全可以称为“合适”或“恰当”。**投机性资本结构中的杠杆因素**。虽然投机性资本结构将公司的所有证券排除在投资范围之外，但它仍可能给普通股带来一定的投机性优势。*C*公司收益增加25%（从1,000,000美元增至1,250,000美元），意味着普通股每股收益约增加50%（从5.20美元增至7.70美元）。因此，在良好时期或良好市场条件下，投机性资本的企业有某种倾向以相对较高的价格出售。当然，在经济萧条期间，它们也可能面临更大的低估风险。不过，一个实际的优势在于，这种发行在通货紧缩基础上出售时，其上涨幅度可能远远超过下跌幅度。**美国水厂与电力公司**

<!--en-->
1. It has tended to restrict new industrial-bond financing to companies of weaker standing. The relative scarcity of good bonds impelled investment houses to sell and investors to buy inferior issues, with inevitably disastrous results.
2. The shortage of good bonds also tended to drive investors into the preferred-stock field. For reasons previously detailed (in Chap. XIV) straight preferred stocks are unsound in theory, and they are therefore likely to prove unsatisfactory investment media as a class.
3. The elimination (or virtual elimination) of senior securities in the set-up of many large corporations has, of course, added somewhat to the investment quality oftheir common stocks, but it has added even more to the investor's demand for these common stocks. This in turn has resulted in a good deal of common-stock buying by people whose circumstances required that they purchase sound bonds. Furthermore it has supplied a superficial justification for the creation of excessive prices for these common stocks; and finally it contributed powerfully to that confusion between investment motives and speculative motives which during 1927–1929 served to debauch so large a proportion of the country's erstwhile careful investors.
**Appraisal of Earnings Where Capital Structure Is Top-Heavy.** In order to carry this theory of capitalization structure a step further, let us examine the case of Company *C*. We arrived at a valuation of $18,000,000 for this enterprise by assuming that its $12,000,000 bond issue would sell at par and the stock would sell for 12 times its earnings of $5.20 per share. But this assumption as to the price of the bonds is clearly fallacious. Earnings of twice interest charges are not sufficient protection for an industrial bond, and hence investors would be unwise to purchase such an issue at par. In fact this very example supplies a useful demonstration of our contention that a coverage of two times interest is inadequate. If it were ample—as some investors seem to believe—the owners of any reasonably prosperous business, earning 8% on the money invested, could get back their entire capital by selling a 4% bond issue, and they would still have control of the business together with one-half of its earnings. Such an arrangement would be exceedingly attractive for the proprietors but idiotic from the standpoint of those who buy the bonds.
Our Company *C* example also sheds some light on the effect of the rate of interest on the apparent safety of the senior security. If the $12,000,000 bond issue had carried a 6% coupon, the interest charges of $720,000 would then be earned less than $1\frac{1}{2}$ times. Let us assume that Company *D* had such a bond issue. An unwary investor, looking at the two exhibits, might reject Company *D*'s 6% bonds as unsafe because their interest coverage was only 1.39 but yet accept the Company *C*bonds at par because he was satisfied with earnings of twice fixed charges. Such discrimination would be scarcely intelligent. Our investor would be rejecting a bond *merely because* it pays him a generous coupon rate, and he would be accepting another bond *merely because* it pays him a low interest rate. The real point, however, is that the minimum margin of safety behind bond issues must be set high enough to avoid the possibility that safety may even *appear* to be achieved by a mere lowering of the interest rate. The same reasoning would apply of course to the dividend rate on preferred stocks.
Since Company *C* bonds are not safe, because of the excessive size of the issue, they are likely to sell at a considerable discount from par. We cannot suggest the proper price level for such an issue, but we have indicated in Chap. 26 that a bond speculative because of inadequate safety should not ordinarily be purchased above 70. It is also quite possible that the presence of this excessive bond issue might prevent the stock from selling at 12 times its earnings, because conservative stock buyers would avoid Company *C* as subject to too great hazard of financial difficulties in the event of untoward developments. The result may well be that, instead of being worth $18,000,000 in the market as originally assumed, the combined bond and stock issues of Company *C* will sell for less than $15,000,000 (the Company *B* valuation), or even for less than $12,000,000 (the value of Company *A*).
As a matter of cold fact, it should be recognized that this unfavorable result may not necessarily follow. If investors are sufficiently careless and if speculators are sufficiently enthusiastic, the securities of Company *C* may conceivably sell in the market for $18,000,000 or even more. But such a situation would be unwarranted and unsound.² Our theory of capitalization structure could not admit a Company *C* arrangement as in any sense standard or suitable. This indicates that there are definite limits upon the advantages to be gained by the use of senior securities. We have already expressed this fact in our principle of the optimum capitalization structure, for senior securities cease to be anadvantage at the point where their amount becomes larger than
can safely be issued or bought for investment.
We have characterized the Company *A* type of
capitalization arrangement as “overconservative”; the
Company *C* type may be termed “speculative,” whereas that
of Company *B* may well be called “suitable” or “appropriate.”
**The Factor of Leverage in Speculative Capitalization Structure.** Although a speculative capitalization structure throws all the company’s securities outside the pale of investment, it may give the common stock a definite speculative advantage. A 25% increase in the earnings of Company *C* (from $1,000,000 to $1,250,000) will mean about a 50% increase in the earnings per share of common (from $5.20 to $7.70). Because of this fact there is some tendency for speculatively capitalized enterprises to sell at relatively high values in the aggregate during good times or good markets. Conversely, of course, they may be subject to a greater degree of undervaluation in depression. There is, however, a real advantage in the fact that such issues, when selling on a deflated basis, can advance much further than they can decline.

Staley Manufacturing Company分析得到了很好的说明，该公司生产玉米产品。作为对比，还给出了同一领域的保守型资本企业美国玉米产品公司的相应分析。Staley案例最显著的特点是普通股每股收益的异常波动。业务本身显然受净利润的广泛变化影响，而由于普通股数量相对于高级证券较少，这些变化对普通股的影响被极大放大。⁴ 较大的折旧准备也相当于沉重的固定费用。因此，折旧前的净收入从1929年的3,266,000美元下降到下一年的1,540,000美元，下降了约50%以上，导致普通股每股收益从84美元降至仅3.74美元。美国玉米产品的净收益同样具有波动性，但由于前期费用很少，普通股收益的波动远不那么显著。

The record of American Water Works and Electric Company common stock between 1921 and 1929 presents an almost fabulous picture of enhancement in value, a great part of which was due to the influence of a highly speculative capitalization structure. Four annual exhibits during this period are summarized in the table above.
The purchaser of 1 share of American Water Works common stock at the high price of $6\frac{1}{2}$ in 1921, if he retained the distributions made in stock, would have owned about $12\frac{1}{2}$ shares when the common sold at its high price of 199 in 1929. His $6.50 would have grown to about $2,500. While the market value of the common shares was thus increasing some 400-fold, the gross earnings had expanded to only 2.6 times the earlier figure. The tremendously disproportionate rise in the commonstock value was due to the following elements, in order of importance:1. A much higher valuation placed upon the per-share earnings of this issue. In 1921 the company's capitalization was recognized as top-heavy; its bonds sold at a low price, and the earnings per share of common were not taken seriously, especially since no dividends were being paid on the second preferred. In 1929 the general enthusiasm for public utility shares resulted in a price for the common issue of nearly 50 times its highest recorded earnings.
2. The speculative capitalization structure allowed the common stock to gain an enormous advantage from the expansion of the company's properties and earnings. Nearly all the additional funds needed were raised by the sale of senior securities. It will be observed that whereas the gross revenues increased about 160% from 1921 to 1929, the balance per share of old common stock grew 14-fold during the same period.
3. The margin of profit improved during these years, as shown by the higher ratio of net to gross. The speculative capital structure greatly accentuated the benefit to the common stock from the additional net profits so derived.³
*Other Examples:* The behavior of speculatively capitalized enterprises *under varying business conditions* is well illustrated by the appended analysis of A. E. Staley Manufacturing Company, manufacturers of corn products. For comparison there is given also a corresponding analysis of American Maize Products Company, a conservatively capitalized enterprise in the same field.
The most striking aspect of the Staley exhibit is the extraordinary fluctuation in the yearly earnings per share of common stock. The business itself is evidently subject to wide variations in net profit, and the effect of these variations on the common stock is immensely magnified by reason of the small amount of common stock in comparison with the senior securities.⁴ The large depreciation allowance acts also as the equivalent of a heavy fixed charge. Hence a decline in net before depreciation from $3,266,000 in 1929 to $1,540,000 the next year, somewhat over 50%, resulted in a drop in earnings *per share of common* from $84 to only $3.74. The netprofits of American Maize Products were fully as variable, but the small amount of prior charges made the fluctuations in commonstock earnings far less spectacular.

E. Staley公司在1933年1月相对于美国玉米产品公司被低估的事实，通过对比当前资产状况和总资源得到进一步证实。按净资产值计算，Staley公司的售价仅为美国玉米产品的三分之一。像Staley这样在不利市场中常见的投机性发行出现过度紧缩，当形势改善时，有可能出现惊人的价格上涨，因为那时每股收益会急剧增加。注意，1927年初Staley普通股的价格约为75，一年后价格接近300。同样，股票从1932年的33低价上涨到1939年的相当于320。*一个相应的例子*。另一个因相同原因导致价格剧烈变化的例子是莫霍克橡胶公司。1927年，普通股售价为15美元，表示次级发行的估值仅为300,000美元，之后还有1,960,000美元的优先股。该公司于1926年因销售6,400,000美元而亏损610,000美元。1927年销售额降至5,700,000美元，但净利润为630,000美元。这相当于少量普通股每股超过23美元。因此，价格从1927年的低点15美元上涨到1928年的高点251美元。1930年，公司再次亏损669,000美元，第二年价格下降至仅相当于4美元。在投机化资本化的企业中，普通股股东受益——或有可能受益——是以高级证券持有人的损失为代价的。普通股股东用自己少量的钱运作，却使用了大量高级证券持有人的资金；在他们之间，情况就是“我赢头，你输尾”。普通股股东相对较小的投入这一战略地位，是所谓“基于权益交易”的极端形式。用另一种说法，可以说他对企业的未来利润有“廉价看涨”的权利。**考虑了“细绳式”普通股的投机吸引力**。我们对固定价值投资的讨论尽可能强调了高级证券持有人地位的劣势（即不公平性），因为次级资本比例较小。如果这种安排中普通股没有相应的*优势*，那么问题就会自然产生，因为普通股获得了极高的投机吸引力。 这种探讨显然会让我们完全脱离普通股票的*投资*领域，而进入智能或科学推测的范畴。从A. E. Staley的例子中我们已经看到，在糟糕时期，投机性资本结构可能会对优先证券和普通股的市场价格产生负面影响。因此，在这样一个时期，普通股股东不会以债券持有人的利益为代价获得当前收益。这一事实明显削弱了这类普通股票所固有的投机优势。人们很容易认为，只有在因暂时不利条件而以异常低价格出售时，才应购买这些股票。但这实际上是在提出一个反问，因为它假设智能投机者能够持续识别并等待这些异常且暂时的状况。如果真是这样，无论购买哪种普通股票，他都能赚大钱；在这种条件下，他或许应该选择优质普通股票，以低价购买，而不是这些更具投机性的股票。*前述内容的实际方面*。从实际角度来看，购买投机性资本化的普通股票必须在看似正常的整体或市场条件下进行，即那些没有明显被高估或低估的条件下。假设（1）多元化，以及（2）在选择具有良好前景的公司时具备合理的判断力，那么投机者似乎从这种承诺中可以在长期内获得相当可观的利润。进行此类购买时，显然应该优先选择那些大部分优先资本以优先股而非债券形式存在的公司。这种安排可以消除或最小化恶劣时期因违约而导致次级股权消亡的风险，从而让普通股持有人能够保持自己的立场，直到经济好转。（但仅仅因为优先股合同以这种方式使普通股股东受益，对优先股持有人本身显然是不利的。）然而，我们绝不能忘记，在任何一次购买中实现全部预期收益นั้น存在特殊的实际困难。正如我们在可转换债券类似案例中指出的那样，一旦出现可观利润，持有者就会陷入困境，因为他只能通过承担已产生的风险来继续持有以获得更多收益。就像可转换债券在价格上涨到明显超出直接投资类别时失去独特优势一样，随着价格持续上涨，普通股的投机性承诺也会转化为越来越大的承诺。在我们的Mohawk Rubber例子中，聪明的购买者在15美元时无法预期能持有到100美元以上——即使其报价确实达到了250美元——因为在100美元或更低价格时，这些股票已经失去了投机性资本化次级股票的独特特征。[^2478]：1 关于从全股票结构转变为股票与债券组合的结构变化可能产生的影响的说明，请参阅1934年版本书第505–507页关于American Laundry Machinery Company的讨论。美国锌公司（于1916年通过优先股分红）和梅塔格公司（于1928年通过类似分配）都曾进行过此类实际变更。将投机性资本化结构引入保守架构公司的常规方法是通过成立控股公司，该控股公司发行自己的优先证券和普通股票，以换取收购运营公司的普通股份。*例子：*1927年的Chesapeake Corporation，1925年的Kaufmann Department Stores Securities Corporation。 2 1925年，Dodge Brothers（汽车公司）的证券以债券和优先股160,000,000美元本金价值、普通股市场价值约50,000,000美元的价格向公众出售。有形净资产仅为80,000,000美元，平均收益约为16,000,000美元。这种明显过重的资本结构最初并未对证券价值产生负面影响，但1927年收益的显著下降很快揭示了财务结构的缺陷。（1928年，该公司被Chrysler收购。）

**Speculative Capitalization May Cause Valuation of Total Enterprise at an Unduly Low Figure.** The market situation of the Staley securities in January 1933 presents a practical confirmation of our theoretical analysis of Company *C* above. The top-heavy capitalization structure resulted in a low price for the bonds and the preferred stock, the latter being affected particularly by the temporary suspension of its dividend in 1931. The result was that, instead of showing an increased total value by reason of the presence of senior securities, the company sold in the market at a much lower relative price than the conservatively capitalized American Maize Products. (The latter company showed a normal relationship between average earnings and market value. It should not properly be termed *overconservatively* capitalized because the variations in its annual earnings would constitute a good reason for avoiding any substantial amount of senior securities. A bond or preferred stock issue of very small size, on the other hand, would be of no particular advantage or disadvantage.)
The indication that the A. E. Staley Company was undervalued in January 1933 in comparison with American Maize Products is strengthened by reference to the relative current-asset positions and total resources. Per dollar of netasset values the Staley company was selling only one-third as high as American Maize.
The overdeflation of a speculative issue like Staley common in unfavorable markets creates the possibility of an amazing price advance when conditions improve, because the earnings per share then show so violent an increase. Note that at the beginning of 1927 Staley common was quoted at about 75, and a year later it sold close to 300. Similarly the shares advanced from a low of 33 in 1932 to the equivalent of 320 in 1939.
*A Corresponding Example.* A more spectacular instance of tremendous price changes for the same reason is supplied by Mohawk Rubber. In 1927 the common sold at 15, representing a valuation of only $300,000 for the junior issue, which followed $1,960,000 of preferred. The company had lost $610,000 in 1926 on $6,400,000 of sales. In 1927 sales dropped to $5,700,000, but there was a net profit of $630,000. This amounted to over $23 per share on the small amount of common stock. The price consequently advanced from its low of 15 in 1927 to a high of 251 in 1928. In 1930 the company again lost $669,000, and the next year the price declined to the equivalent of only $4.
In a speculatively capitalized enterprise, the common stockholders benefit—or have the possibility of benefiting—at the expense of the senior security holders. The common stockholder is operating with a little of his own money and with a great deal of the senior security holder's money; as between him and them it is a case of “Heads I win, tails you lose.” This strategic position of the common stockholder with relatively small commitment is an extreme form of what is called “trading on the equity.” Using another expression, he may be said to have a “cheap call” on the future profits of the enterprise.
**Speculative Attractiveness of “Shoe-String” Common Stocks Considered.** Our discussion of fixed-value investment has emphasized as strongly as possible the disadvantage (amounting to unfairness) that attaches to the senior security holder's position where the junior capital is proportionatelyslight. The question would logically arise if there are not corresponding *advantages* to the common stock in such an arrangement, from which it gains a very high degree of speculative attractiveness. This inquiry would obviously take us entirely outside the field of common-stock *investment* but would represent an expedition into the realm of intelligent or even scientific speculation.
We have already seen from our A. E. Staley example that in bad times a speculative capitalization structure may react adversely on the market price of both the senior securities and the common stock. During such a period, then, the common stockholders do not derive a present benefit at the expense of the bondholder. This fact clearly detracts from the speculative advantage inherent in such common stocks. It is easy to suggest that these issues be purchased only when they are selling at abnormally low levels due to temporarily unfavorable conditions. But this is really begging the question, because it assumes that the intelligent speculator can consistently detect and wait for these abnormal and temporary conditions. If this were so, he could make a great deal of money regardless of what type of common stock he buys, and under such conditions he might be better advised to select high-grade common stocks at bargain prices rather than these more speculative issues.
*Practical Aspects of the Foregoing.* To view the matter in a practical light, the purchase of speculatively capitalized common stocks must be considered under general or market conditions that are supposedly normal, *i.e.*, under those which are not obviously inflated or deflated. Assuming (1) diversification, and (2) reasonably good judgment in selecting companies with satisfactory prospects, it would seem that the speculator should be able to profit rather substantially in the long run from commitments of this kind. In making such purchases, partiality should evidently be shown to those companies in which most of the senior capital is in the form of preferred stock rather than bonds. Such an arrangement removes or minimizes the danger of extinction of the junior equity through default in bad times and thus permits the shoe-string common stockholder to maintain his position untilprosperity returns. (But just because the preferred-stock contract benefits the common shareholder in this way, it is clearly disadvantageous to the preferred stockholder himself.)
We must not forget, however, the peculiar practical difficulty in the way of realizing the full amount of prospective gain in any one of the purchases. As we pointed out in the analogous case of convertible bonds, as soon as a substantial profit appears the holder is in a dilemma, because he can hold for a further gain only by risking that already accrued. Just as a convertible bond loses its distinctive advantages when the price rises to a point that carries it clearly outside of the straight investment class, so a shoe-string common-stock commitment is transformed into a more and more substantial commitment as the price continues to rise. In our Mohawk Rubber example the intelligent purchaser at 15 could not have expected to hold it beyond 100—even though its quotation did reach 250—because at 100, or before, the shares had lost the distinctive characteristics of a speculatively capitalized junior issue.
[^2478]: 1 See our discussion of American Laundry Machinery Company on pp. 505–507 of the 1934 edition of this work for an illustration of the possible effect of a change of capital structure from an all-stock to a stock-and-bond combination. Actual changes of this kind were made by American Zinc (through a dividend in preferred stock in 1916) and by Maytag Company through similar distributions in 1928. The usual method of introducing a speculative capitalization structure into a company with a conservative set-up is through formation of a holding company that issues its own senior securities and common stock against acquisition of the operating company’s common. *Examples:* Chesapeake Corporation in 1927, Kaufmann Department Stores Securities Corporation in 1925.
2 In 1925 Dodge Brothers (motor) securities were sold to the public on the basis of $160,000,000 principal value of bonds and preferred stock and about $50,000,000 market value of common. Net tangible assets were only $80,000,000, and average earnings about $16,000,000. This obviously top-heavy capitalization structure did not militate against the security values at first, but a severe decline in earnings in 1927 soon revealed the unsoundness of the financial setup. (In 1928 the company was taken over by Chrysler.)

CHAPTER 41

# 低价普通股。

<!--en-->
*Low-Priced Common Stocks.*

收入来源分析

<!--en-->
Analysis of the Source of
Income

## 低价股票

<!--en-->
*LOW-PRICED STOCKS*

前章讨论的特征，公众通常将之与*低价股票*联系起来。大多数投机性资本型股票都处于低价区间销售。当然，“低价”的定义有些主观性。股价低于10美元/股显然属于这一类别；而高于20美元的通常被排除在外，因此分界线可能设置在10美元至20美元之间。

<!--en-->
The characteristics discussed in the preceding chapter are generally thought of by the public in connection with *low-priced stocks*. The majority of issues of the speculatively capitalized type do sell within the low-priced range. The definition of “low-priced” must, of course, be somewhat arbitrary. Prices below $10 per share belong to this category beyond question; those above $20 are ordinarily excluded; so that the dividing line would be set somewhere between $10 and $20.

**低价股票的算术优势**。低价普通股似乎具有固有的算术优势，因为它们上涨的幅度远大于下跌的幅度。证券市场的一个常见现象是，股票从10到40的涨幅比从100到400的涨幅更大。这部分是因为投机性公众的偏好，他们通常更倾向于10到40区间的股票，而非100以上的股票。但事实也是，在许多情况下，低价普通股让持有者以相对较小的成本，获得对较大企业的权益或“认购”机会。

<!--en-->
**Arithmetical Advantage of Low-Priced Issues.** Low-priced common stocks appear to possess an inherent arithmetical advantage arising from the fact they can advance so much more than they can decline. It is a commonplace of the securities market that an issue will rise more readily from 10 to 40 than from 100 to 400. This fact is due in part to the preferences of the speculative public, which generally is much more partial to issues in the 10-to-40 range than to those selling above 100. But it is also true that in many cases low-price common stocks give the owner the advantage of an interest in, or “call” upon, a relatively large enterprise at relatively small expense.

1936年4月《芝加哥大学商业杂志》刊登了关于不同价格区间工业股票价格行为统计研究。¹ 该研究针对1926–1935年时期²，发现多元化低价股票作为投机工具，始终优于多元化高价股票。以下引文总结了作者得出的结论：

<!--en-->
A statistical study of the relative price behavior of industrial stocks in various price groups was presented in theApril 1936 issue of *The Journal of Business of the University of Chicago*.¹ The study was devoted to the period 1926–1935² and revealed a continuous superiority of diversified, low-priced issues over diversified, high-priced issues as speculative media. The following quotation from the study summarizes the results and conclusions reached by the author:

除非此处呈现的统计工作存在严重的未补偿错误，否则这项调查似乎证明了价格水平与价格波动之间存在某些关系，这些关系此前未被股市现象研究者报道。这些关系可简要表述如下：

<!--en-->
Unless there are serious uncompensated errors in the statistical work here presented, this investigation would seem to establish the existence of certain relationships between price level and price fluctuations which have hitherto gone unreported by students of stock-market phenomena. These relationships may be briefly stated as follows:

1. 低价股票的价格波动通常比高价股票更明显。
2. 在“牛市”中，低价股票往往比高价股票上涨幅度更大，并且在随后的经济衰退中也不会失去这些优势收益。换句话说，与高价股票的上行和下行波动相比，低价股票的下行波动比例较小。• • • 假设（1）未来各价格区间的行为将与其过去行为相似，且（2）根据当年活动情况选择股票，并未完全或根本考虑到低价组股票的优势表现，那么可以得出以下结论：
1. 低价工业股票比高价工业股票提供更大的投机获利机会。
2. 如果两种或多种工业股票看似具有相同的潜在利润，投机者应购买价格最低的股票。

<!--en-->
1. Low-price stocks tend to fluctuate relatively more than high-price stocks.
2. In a “bull” market the low-price stocks tend to go up relatively more than high-price stocks, and they do not lose these superior gains in the recessions which follow. In other words, the downward movement of low-price stocks is less than proportional to their upward movement, when compared with the upward and downward movement of high-price stocks.
• • •
Assuming (1) that the future behavior of the various price groups will be similar to their past behavior and (2) that the selection of stocks on the basis of the activity for the current year does not account completely, if at all, for the superior performance of the stocks in the low-price groups, it seems logical to conclude the following:
1. Low-price industrial stocks offer greater opportunities for speculative profits than high-price industrial stocks.
2. In case two or more issues of industrial stocks seem to offer equal prospective profits, the speculator should purchase the shares selling at the lowest price.

## 大多数低价股票买家亏损的一些原因

<!--en-->
*Some Reasons Why Most Buyers of Low-Priced Issues Lose Money.*

公众对“廉价股票”的强烈偏好似乎有合理的逻辑基础。然而，确实大多数购买低价股票的人会在购买中亏损。为什么如此？根本原因是公众购买的是*出售给他们的*股票，销售努力是为了帮助卖方而非买方。因此，公众购买的大部分低价股票都是错误的类型；即，它们并不提供这种证券类型的真正优势。原因可能是公司财务状况不佳，或者普通股仅外观上低价，实际上代表与企业规模相比过大的承诺。后者尤其适用于低价范围内的*新*证券发行。在这种情况下，通过制造大量股份，简单利用技巧使价格显得“伪低价”，即使每股几美元，总价值也过高。这种情况在古代矿业股票发行中常见，在1933年的酒类股票发行和1938–1939年的飞机股票发行中也出现过。

<!--en-->
The pronounced liking of the public for “cheap stocks” would therefore seem to have a sound basis in logic. Yet it is undoubtedly true that most people who buy low-priced stocks lose money on their purchases. Why is this so? The underlying reason is that the public buys issues that are *sold* to it, and the sales effort is put forward to benefit the seller and not the buyer. In consequence the bulk of the low-priced purchases made by the public are of the wrong kind; *i.e.*, they do not provide the real advantages of this security type. The reason may be either because the companies are in bad financial condition or because the common stock is low-priced in appearance only and actually represents a full or excessive commitment in relation to the size of the enterprise. The latter is preponderantly true of *new* security offerings in the low-priced range. In such cases, a *pseudo-low* price is accomplished by the simple artifice of creating so large a number of shares that even at a few dollars per share the total value of the common issue is excessive. This has been true of mining-stock flotations from of old and was encountered again in the liquor-stock offerings of 1933 and in the airplane issues in 1938–1939.

*真正的*低价普通股，其总价值相对于公司的资产、销售额及过去或预期利润来说很小。这里提供的例子将说明“真正”与“伪低价”价格的区别。

<!--en-->
A *genuinely* low-priced common stock will show an aggregate value for the issue which is small in relation to the company’s assets, sales and past or prospective profits. The examples shown herewith will illustrate the difference between a “genuine” and “pseudo-low” price.

* 在耗尽之前。Wright-Hargreaves的股票表面上看价格较低，但实际上，与公司的财务数据相比，其估值非常高。Barker Brothers的情况则相反，因为普通股所代表的743,000美元估值，相对于企业规模来说非常小。（注意，同样的结论也适用于Barker Brothers Preferred，其报价为18，具有普通股的低价特性。）³观察股市可以发现，面临破产清算的公司股票可能比价格非常低的股票更活跃，仅仅因为当前盈利能力较差。这种现象是由于内部人士希望在破产清算前出售持股，因此导致大量低价股票供应，有时还伴随着不道德的行为，试图说服不明事理的公众购买。但当低价股票符合我们的投机吸引力条件时，通常不会有卖压，也不会有买入努力。因此，这些股票缺乏活力，很少受到公众关注。这一分析可以解释为什么公众几乎总是购买错误的低价股票，而忽视该领域真正有潜力的机会。

<!--en-->
* Before depletion.
The Wright-Hargreaves issue was low-priced in appearance only, for in fact the price registered a very high valuation for the company as compared with all parts of its financial exhibit. The opposite was true of Barker Brothers because here the $743,000 valuation represented by the common stock was exceedingly small in relation to the size of the enterprise. (Note also that the same statement could be applied to Barker Brothers Preferred, which at its quotation of 18 partook of the qualities of a low-priced common stock.)³
Observation of the stock market will show that the stocks of companies facing receivership are likely to be more active than those which are very low in price merely because of poor current earnings. This phenomenon is caused by the desire of insiders to dispose of their holdings before the receivership wipes them out, thus accounting for a large supply of these shares at a low level and also sometimes for unscrupulous efforts to persuade the unwary public to buy them. But where a low-priced stock fulfills our conditions of speculative attractiveness, there is apt to be no pressure to sell and no effort to create buying. Hence the issue is inactive and attractslittle public attention. This analysis may explain why the public almost always buys the wrong low-priced issues and ignores the really promising opportunities in this field.

## 低价伴随投机性资本化。

<!--en-->
*Low Price Coupled with Speculative Capitalization.*

根据我们的定义，投机性资本化的企业特点是高级证券数量相对较多，普通股发行量较小。虽然大多数情况下普通股会以低单价出售，但如果股份数量较少，不一定如此。例如Staley案例（见第40章），即使1933年普通股单价为50美元，资本化结构仍属于投机性，因为债券和优先股占总额超过90%。同样，即使没有高级证券，普通股也可能具有与投机性资本化企业相同的可能性。只要普通股的市场价值相对于企业规模来说金额较小，无论其资本结构如何，都会出现这种可能性。

<!--en-->
Speculatively capitalized enterprises, according to our definition, are marked by a relatively large amount of senior securities and a comparatively small issue of common stock. Although in most cases the common stock will sell at a low price per share, it need not necessarily do so if the number of shares is small. In the Staley case, for example (referred to in Chap. 40) even at $50 per share for the common in 1933 the capitalization structure would still have been speculative, since the bonds and preferred at par would represent over 90% of the total. It is also true that even where there are no senior securities the common stock may have possibilities equivalent to those in a speculatively capitalized enterprise. These possibilities will occur wherever the market value of the common issue-represents a small amount of money in relation to the size of the business, regardless of how it is capitalized.

为了说明这一点，我们附上对Mandel Brothers, Inc.和Gimbel Brothers, Inc.两家百货商店企业的简析，时间为1939年9月。

<!--en-->
To illustrate this point we append a condensed analysis of Mandel Brothers, Inc., and Gimbel Brothers, Inc., two department-store enterprises, as of September 1939.

<!--en-->
* Based on report for succeeding Jan. 31.
Gimbel Brothers presents a typical picture of a speculatively capitalized enterprise. On the other hand Mandel Brothers has no senior securities ahead of the common, but despite this fact the relatively small market value of the entire issue imparts to the shares the same sort of speculative possibilities (though in somewhat lesser degree) as are found in the Gimbel Brothers set-up. Note, however, that the rental payments of Mandel Brothers are proportionately much higher than those of Gimbel Brothers and that these rental charges are equivalent in good part to senior securities.
**Large Volume and High Production Cost Equivalent to Speculative Capital Structure.** This example should lead us to widen our conception of a speculatively situated common stock. The speculative or *marginal* position may arise from any cause that reduces the percentage of gross available forthe common to a subnormal figure and that therefore serves to create a subnormal value for the common stock in relation to the volume of business. Unusually high operating or production costs have the identical effect as excessive senior charges in cutting down the percentage of gross available for common. The following hypothetical examples of three copper producers will make this point more intelligible and also lead to some conclusions on the subject of large output versus low operating costs.

需要指出的是，*C*公司的较高生产成本将产生与*B*公司债券利息要求相同的效果（假设产出和生产成本如所述继续不变）。

<!--en-->
It is scarcely necessary to point out that the higher production cost of Company *C* will have exactly the same effect as the bond-interest requirement of Company *B* (assuming output and production costs to continue as stated).

*推导出的通用原则*。上述表格更有助于具体说明单位利润与每股股票价值产出之间通常存在的反向关系。

<!--en-->
*General Principle Derived.* The foregoing table is perhaps more useful in showing concretely the inverse relationship that usually exists between profit per unit and output per dollar of stock value.

通用原则可表述为：单位成本越低，每股股票市场价值产出就越低，反之亦然。由于*A*公司的成本为7美分，其股票自然以*每磅产出*更高的价格出售，而成本为9美分的*C*公司则不然。相反，*C*公司每美元股票价值的产出量比*A*公司更多。从投机技术角度来看，这一事实具有重要意义。当商品价格上涨时，高成本生产商的股票通常会比低成本生产商的股票上涨幅度更大。上述表格表明，铜价从10美分升至13美分时，*A*公司股票价值将增加100%，*B*和*C*公司股票价值将增加300%。与华尔街普遍印象相反，当买家确信产品价格即将上涨并希望充分利用这一信念时，高成本生产商的股票比低成本生产商的股票更具逻辑性承诺。⁴当预计销售和利润将显著改善时，购买投机性资本化的普通股也享有同样的优势。

<!--en-->
The general principle may be stated that the lower the unit cost the lower the production per dollar of market value of stock and *vice versa*. Since Company *A* has a 7-cent cost, its stock naturally sells at a higher price *per pound of output* than Company *C* with its 9-cent cost. Conversely, Company *C* produces more pounds per dollar of stock value than Company *A*. This fact is not without significance from the standpoint of speculative technique. When a rise in the price of the commodity occurs, there will ordinarily be a larger advance, percentagewise, in the shares of high-cost producers than in the shares of low-cost producers. The foregoing table indicates that a rise in the price of copper from 10 to 13 cents would increase the value of Company *A* shares by 100% and the value of Company *B* and *C* shares by 300%. Contrary to the general impression in Wall Street, the stocks of high-cost producers are more logical commitments than those of the low-cost producers when the buyer is convinced that a rise in the price of the product is imminent and he wishes to exploit this conviction to the utmost.⁴ Exactly the same advantage attaches to the purchase of speculatively capitalized common stocks when a pronounced improvement in sales and profits is confidently anticipated.

### 收入来源

<!--en-->
*THE SOURCES OF INCOME*

“收入来源”通常被认为与“业务类型”含义相同。这一考虑在很大程度上影响公众对特定普通股每股利润的评估依据。不同业务使用不同的“乘数”，但我们必须指出，这些差异本身会随时代变化而变化。⁵第一次世界大战前，铁路股票因被认为稳定而被给予最慷慨的估值。1927-1929年，公用事业集团因持续稳定的增长而获得最高的每股收益比率。1933年至1939年间，不利法规尤其是政府竞争担忧大大降低了公用事业股票的相对受欢迎程度。最近，对大型、根基稳固的工业企业给予最宽松的估值，这些企业在经济萧条期间仍能保持可观收益，并被认为具有良好的长期前景。由于相对行为和受欢迎程度的反复变化，证券分析不得轻易规定任何确定规则来比较不同业务的估值标准。可以说，记录越令人印象深刻，稳定性和增长前景越有希望，每股利润的估值应越慷慨，但始终遵循原则：超过约20的乘数（即低于5%的“收益基础”）将使估值超出*投资*价格范围。

<!--en-->
The “source of income” will ordinarily be thought of as meaning the same thing as the “type of business.” This consideration enters very largely into the basis on which the public will value the earnings per share shown by a given common stock. Different “multipliers” are used for different sorts of enterprise, but we must point out that these distinctions are themselves subject to change with the changing times.⁵ Prior to the World War the railroad stocks were valued most generously of all, because of their supposed stability. In 1927–1929 the public-utility group sold at the highest ratio to earnings, because of their record of steady growth. Between 1933 and 1939 adverse legislation and, in particular, the fear of government competition greatly reduced the relative popularity of the utility stocks. The most liberal valuations have recently been accorded to the large and well-entrenched industrial enterprises which were able to maintain substantial earnings during the depression and are considered to possess favorable long-term prospects. Because of these repeated variations in relative behavior and popularity, security analysis must hesitate to prescribe any definitive rules for valuing one type of business as against another. It is a truism to say that the more impressive the record and the more promising the prospects of stability and growth the more liberally the per-share earnings should be valued, subject always to our principle that a multiplier higher than about 20 (i.e., an “earnings basis” of less than 5%) will carry the issue out of the *investment* price range.

**一个特殊阶段：三个例子。**分析技术的更有成效领域在于那些必须根据公司拥有的特定资产研究收入来源的情况，而不仅仅是业务总体性质。当大部分收入来自投资资产或其他固定可靠来源时，这一点可能非常重要。将用三个例子来说明普通股分析的这一微妙方面。

<!--en-->
**A Special Phase: Three Examples.** A more fruitful field for the technique of analysis is found in those cases where the source of income must be studied in relation to specific assets owned by the company, instead of in relation merely to the general nature of the business. This point may be quite important when a substantial portion of the income accrues from investment holdings or from some other fixed and dependable source. Three examples will be used to illuminate this rather subtle aspect of common-stock analysis.

1. *北方管道公司*。1923-1925年期间，北方管道公司报告的收入和股息如下：

* Capitalization, 40,000 shares of common stock.
In 1924 the shares sold as low as 72, in 1925 as low as 67½ and in 1926 as low as 64. These prices were on the whole somewhat less than ten times the reported earnings and reflected a lack of enthusiasm for the shares, due to a pronounced decline in profits from the figures of preceding years and also to the reductions in the dividend.
Analysis of the income account however, would have

这个收入账户的特殊之处在于，大部分利润来自管道业务之外的其他来源。公司通常能定期获得每股约4美元的投资利息和租金收入。资产负债表显示，公司持有近320万美元的自由债券及其他有息证券，每股价值约80美元，相关利息收入约为4%。

<!--en-->
This income account is exceptional in that the greater part of the profits were derived from sources other than the pipe-line business itself. About $4 per share were regularly received in interest on investments and rentals. The balance sheet showed holdings of nearly $3,200,000 (or $80 per share) in Liberty Bonds and other gilt-edged marketable securities, on which the interest income was about 4%.

这一事实意味着必须对每股收益采用特殊的估值基础，因为通常的“十倍收益”基础会得出荒谬的结论。每股80美元的金条投资将产生每股3.20美元的收入，按十倍收益计算，这80美元仅“值”每股32美元，这是一种归谬推理。显然，北方管道公司收入中来自债券持有部分的部分，逻辑上应采用比来自波动的管道业务部分的更高估值基础。因此，对北方管道公司股票进行合理的估值必须遵循以下建议的方法：由于管道业务的趋势不理想，其收益必须采用较低的估值基础。利息和租金收入想必应依据产生这些收入的资产的实际价值来估值。这项分析清楚地表明，在1926年64美元的价格水平下，北方管道公司股票的售价远低于其内在价值。<sup>7</sup>

<!--en-->
This fact meant that a special basis of valuation must be applied to the per-share earnings, inasmuch as the usual “ten-times-earnings” basis would result in a nonsensical conclusion. Gilt-edged investments of $80 per share would yield an income of $3.20 per share, and at ten times earnings this $80 would be “worth” only $32 per share, a *reductio ad absurdum*. Obviously, that part of the Northern Pipe Line income that was derived from its bond holdings should logically be valued at a higher basis than the portion derived from the fluctuating pipe-line business. A sound valuation of Northern Pipe Line stock would therefore have to proceed along the lines suggested below. The pipe-line earnings would have to be valued at a low basis because of their unsatisfactory trend. The interest and rental income must presumably be valued on a basis corresponding with the actual value of the assets producing the income. This analysis indicated clearly that, at the price of 64 in 1926, Northern Pipe Line stock was selling considerably below its intrinsic value.<sup>7</sup>

2. *Lackawanna Securities Company*。该公司成立是为了持有大量Glen Alden Coal Company 4%债券，这些债券此前由Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad Company持有；其股份按比例分配给Delaware, Lackawanna and Western的股东。该证券公司拥有844,000股普通股。1931年12月31日，其唯一资产——除了每股约1美元的现金——是面值为51,000,000美元的Glen Alden 4%第一抵押贷款债券。1931年度的收入情况如下：

2. *Lackawanna Securities Company.* This company was organized to hold a large block of Glen Alden Coal Company 4% bonds formerly owned by the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad Company, and its shares were distributed pro rata to the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western stockholders. The Securities Company had outstanding 844,000 shares of common stock. On December 31, 1931 its sole asset—other than about $1 per share in cash—consisted of $51,000,000 face value of Glen Alden 4% first mortgage bonds. For the year 1931, the income account was as follows:

从表面上看，1932年23美元的价格对于收益为2.15美元的股票来说并不过高。但这一收益并非来自普通的商业或制造业务，而是来自发行债券的行为，该债券显然属于高等级投资。（1931年，Glen Alden煤炭公司获得9,550,000美元收益，其中2,151,000美元用于利息支付，因此足以满足债券要求4<sup>1</sup>/2倍。）通过约10%的利率计算，市场实际上将Glen Alden债券的价值仅定为每美元37美分。（23美元购买Lackawanna证券公司的股票，相当于Glen Alden债券面值为37美元的60美元价值，再加上1美元现金）同样，如北方管道线案例所示，分析会清楚地表明，按照常规的十倍收益标准计算，这种特殊发行的债券被严重低估了。*烟草产品公司*

<!--en-->
Superficially, the price of 23 in 1932 for a stock earning $2.15 did not appear out of line. But these earnings were derived, not from ordinary commercial or manufacturing operations, but from the holding of a bond issue which presumably constituted a high-grade investment. (In 1931 the Glen Alden Coal Company earned $9,550,000 available for interest charges of $2,151,000, thus covering the bond requirements 4<sup>1</sup>/2 times.) By valuing this interest income on about a 10% basis the market was in fact valuing the Glen Alden bonds at only 37 cents on the dollar. (The price of 23 for a share of Lackawanna Securities was equivalent to $60 face value of Glen Alden bonds at 37, plus $1 in cash)
Here again, as in the Northern Pipe Line example, analysis would show convincingly that the customary ten-times-earnings basis resulted in a glaring undervaluation of this specially situated issue.
*Tobacco Products Corporation*
