3. *弗吉尼亚烟草产品公司*。在这个例子中，就像其他两个例子一样，该公司在市场上出售的价格约为最新报告收益的十倍。但1931年烟草产品的收益完全来自将其某些资产租赁给美国烟草公司，从1923年开始，双方约定99年期间每年租金为2,500,000美元。由于美国烟草公司能够毫无问题地履行这一义务，因此这笔年度租金收入相当于高等级投资的利息。因此，其价值远远超过由此产生的收益的十倍。这意味着1931年12月烟草产品股票的市场估值远低于该公司的实际状况所支撑的价值。（实际上，租赁价值的摊销计算约为35,600,000美元。该公司还持有大量联合雪茄店的股票，后来证明几乎无价值，但这些额外资产当然不会降低其美国烟草租赁的价值。）**此类情况的相对重要性**。上述例子所代表的研究领域在数量上并不重要，因为毕竟只有很少比例的被考察公司属于这一类别。然而，这种情况频繁出现，足以使这一讨论具有实际意义。它也有助于再次说明证券分析的关键方法与股票市场的肤浅反应和估值之间巨大的技术差异。**建议的两种行为方式**。当可以证明某些条件（如最后讨论的那些条件）会导致市场低估时，就可以提出两种不同的行为方式。首先，证券分析师有机会发现这些低估情况并从中获利。但也有迹象表明，导致这种低估的财务安排是错误的，股东利益需要纠正这一错误。像北方管道公司或拉克瓦纳证券公司这样的公司，其市场售价远低于真实价值，这尽可能有力地证明了从企业所有者的角度来看，整个安排都是错误的。在这些案例中，有一个基本的一致性原则。管道企业的大部分资本被用于持有金边债券，这是不一致的。拉克瓦纳证券公司的整个安排也是不一致的，因为它用一种毫无特色的股票发行取代了原本可能是高等级债券发行——投资者可能愿意以合理价格购买债券——而股票发行除非以极低价格，否则没有人会购买。（此外，还涉及沉重的、不必要的公司所得税负担，正如烟草产品案例中所见。）这种不合逻辑的安排应该被真正利益相关方，即股东们识别出来，他们应坚持纠正这一异常现象。这三个例子最终都进行了纠正。在北方管道公司案例中，不需要用于管道业务的资金通过特别分配以每股70美元的金额返还给股东。拉克瓦纳证券公司被完全解散，其库中的格伦阿尔登债券按比例分配给股东作为股票的替代。最后，烟草产品公司通过重新资本化的方式进行重组：发行了6 1/2%的债券来替代美国烟草租赁，这样这种固定价值的资产就由固定价值证券代表（后来以面值赎回），而不是由一家受高度投机性影响的公司的股票代表。 通过这些公司重组，实际价值迅速体现在市场价格中。⁸我们刚刚分析的情况要求将注意力从收入数据转移到资产负债表中所揭示的某些相关特征上。因此，前面的主题——收入来源——将我们引向下一个研究领域：资产负债表。[^2537]： ¹ Fritzemeier, Louis H., "Relative Price Fluctuations of Industrial Stocks in Different Price Groups," *loc. cit.*, pp. 133–154. ² 参见本著作1934年版的第473–474页，可了解早些时候的一项研究，该研究探讨了1897年、1907年、1914年和1921年经济萧条底部时，低价和高价股票的相对表现。这项于1931年由J. H. Holmes and Company出版的研究，在其有限的范围内，得出了与Fritzemeier结论相似的结果。³ 有关这些例子的后续内容，请参见附录注60。对于更近期的类似对比，建议学生比较大陆汽车公司和吉尔克里斯特公司在1939年底均以5美元价格出售时的情况。除了基于公司估值与其资产和销售额关系的基本区别之外，这里还存在收益记录和营运资本状况上的显著差异。⁴ 市场将B公司股票价格从15美元提高到60美元的行为，因为铜价从10美分上升到13美分，本身极不理性，因为通常没有理由认为金属价格会持续上涨。然而，由于市场确实以这种非理性方式行事，投机者必须在计算中考虑这种行为。⁵ 关于1871年至1937年间不同工业集团连续几年的收益-价格比率研究，请参见Cowles, Alfred, 3d, and associates (*Common Stock Indexes*, 1871–1937), pp. 43–46, 404–418, Bloomington, Ind., 1938。1934–1938年和1936–1938年的比率数据见于附录注61中对纽约证券交易所工业名单的分析。⁶ 尽管该公司向股东提供的报告信息很少，但州际商业委员会保存了完整的财务和运营数据，可供公众查阅。⁷ 在1937–1938年向股东分配大量政府债券之前，戴维斯煤炭公司也存在类似的情况。就在这一行动之前不久，股票价格为35美元。从年度报告中可以看出，1934–1937年每股2.06美元的平均收益和2.56美元的平均股息完全来自煤炭业务以外的来源。⁸ 建议学生考虑1939年两个进一步说明这一点的例子。
1. Westmoreland Coal Company，股价为8美元，尽管该公司仅现金资产就达约18美元/股。此案例与我们的Davis Coal and Coke案例类似，但存在一些差异。请参见第588–589页关于该公司的讨论。
2. American Cigarette and Cigar。此案例中也有长期租约与American Tobacco Company的协议（如Tobacco Products案例所示），但情况因公司自身经营产生亏损以及其他资产所有权而变得复杂。第33章中我们对Lehigh Coal and Navigation Company的讨论也值得关注，我们指出采矿损失可能与铁路租赁带来的巨大收入密不可分。

<!--en-->
3. *Tobacco Products Corporation of Virginia.* In this example, as in the other two, the company was selling in the market for about ten times the latest reported earnings. But the 1931 earnings of Tobacco Products were derived entirely from a lease of certain of its assets to American Tobacco Company, which provided for an annual rental of $2,500,000 for 99 years from 1923. Since the American Tobacco Company was able to meet its obligation without question, this annual rental income was equivalent to interest on a high-grade investment. Its value was therefore much more than ten times the income therefrom. This meant that the market valuation of the Tobacco Products stock issues in December 1931 was far less than was justified by the actual position of the company. (The value of the lease was in fact calculated to be about $35,600,000 on an amortized basis. The company also owned a large amount of United Cigar Stores' stock, which later proved to be practically worthless, but these additional holdings did not, of course, detract from the value of its American Tobacco lease.)
**Relative Importance of Situations of This Kind.** The field of study represented by the foregoing examples is not important quantitatively, because, after all, only a very small percentage of the companies examined will fall within this group. Situations of this kind arise with sufficient frequency, however, to give this discussion practical value. It should beuseful also in illustrating again the wide technical difference between the critical approach of security analysis and the highly superficial reactions and valuations of the stock market.
**Two Lines of Conduct Suggested.** When it can be shown that certain conditions, such as those last discussed, tend to give rise to undervaluations in the market, two different lines of conduct are thereby suggested. We have first an opportunity for the securities analyst to detect these undervaluations and eventually to profit from them. But there is also the indication that the financial set-up that causes this undervaluation is erroneous and that the stockholders' interests require the correction of this error. The very fact that a company constituted like Northern Pipe Line or Lackawanna Securities tends to sell in the market far below its true value proves as strongly as possible that the whole arrangement is wrong from the stand-point of the owners of the business.
At the bottom of these cases there is a basic principle of consistency involved. It is inconsistent for most of the capital of a pipe-line enterprise actually to be employed in the ownership of gilt-edged bonds. The whole set-up of Lackawanna Securities was also inconsistent, because it replaced a presumably high-grade bond issue, which investors might be willing to buy at a fair price, by a nondescript stock issue which no one would purchase except at an exceptionally low price. (In addition a heavy and needless burden of corporate income tax was involved, as was true in the Tobacco Products case.)
Illogical arrangements of this kind should be recognized by the real parties in interest, i.e., the stockholders, and they should insist that the anomaly be rectified. This was finally done in the three examples just given. In the case of Northern Pipe Line the capital not needed in the pipeline business was returned to the stockholders by means of special distributions aggregating $70 per share. The Lackawanna Securities Company was entirely dissolved and the Glen Alden bonds in its treasury distributed pro rata to the stockholders in lieu of their stock. Finally, the Tobacco Products Corporation was recapitalized on a basis by which 6 1/2% bonds were issuedagainst the American Tobacco lease, so that this asset of fixed value was represented by a fixed-value security (which later were redeemed at par) instead of by shares of stock in a corporation subject to highly speculative influences. By means of these corporate rearrangements the real values were speedily established in the market price.⁸
The situations that we have just analyzed required a transfer of attention from the income account figures to certain related features revealed in the balance sheet. Hence the foregoing topic—Sources of Income—carries us over into our next field of inquiry: The Balance Sheet.

INTRODUCTION TO PART VI

## 资产负债表分析的逐步重要性

<!--en-->
*The Evolving Utility of Balance Sheet Analysis*

作者：Seth A. Klarman 在我职业生涯早期，我完全按照Graham和Dodd的方法行事。当他们建议仔细审查公司资产负债表以评估价值时，我将其视为必须遵循的原则。我会寻找那些股票因某种原因交易价格低于公司基础资产保守估计的清算价值的公司，然后购买它们，等待市场纠正错误定价。这看似简单明了。但随着时间的推移，我逐渐意识到这种方法过于简单化，大多数时候毫无实际意义，结果几乎为零。我意识到Graham本人也指出了资产负债表分析的局限性，例如他说：“公司资产在资产负债表上的价值几乎失去了所有意义……与这些资产将被出售的价格或能证明盈利的数字无关。”（第42章）自Graham时代以来，许多因素都发生了变化——管理方式、股东行动主义、技术创新速度、企业合并与收购活动规模——使得以资产负债表为导向的估值和风险保护方法变得不那么有用。研究这些变化很重要，但也需看到账面价值在某些行业分析中仍然具有重要作用，以及资产负债表在理解企业基本驱动因素方面的价值。

<!--en-->
by Seth A. Klarman
Early in my career, I took Graham and Dodd quite literally. When they advised close scrutiny of a company's balance sheet to assess value, I regarded that as a mandate. Find companies whose stocks were, for whatever reason, trading for less than the conservatively estimated liquidation value of those firm's underlying assets. Buy them, and then wait for the market to correct the mispricing. This seemed like a no-brainer. But over time, it became increasingly clear to me that this approach was overly simplistic and most of the time unactionable, a null or nearly null set. I realized that Graham himself had expressed the limitations of balance sheet analysis such as when he said, "The value of a company's assets as carried in its balance sheet has lost practically all its significance ... bearing no relationship to the figure at which they would be sold or the figure which would be justified by the earnings." (Chap. 42)
A lot had changed since Graham's day—management practices, shareholder activism, the rate of technological innovation, the volume of corporate merger and acquisition activity—rendering a balance-sheet-oriented approach to valuation and downside protection much less useful. It is important to examine those changes—but to also see the valuable role that book value still plays in analyzing companies in certain industries and the utility of a balance sheet in understanding the underlying drivers of a business.

《安全分析》写于大萧条时期，当时全球经济活动崩溃，美国股市在短短三年内下跌了80%以上。这种市场混乱造成了巨大的破坏。在不仅未来前景暗淡，甚至许多企业的生存前景也不明朗的时期，找到交易价格低于公司基础资产清算价值的股票是一个有效的筛选方法。许多证券以低价出现在市场上。在价格暴跌和经济不确定性加剧的情况下投资，当其他人担心会有更糟糕的情况时，这看起来可能很冒险，但实际上为那些有勇气买入的人提供了有利的收益与风险比。

<!--en-->
*Security Analysis* was written in the depths of the Great Depression, at a time when global economic activity had collapsed, and the U.S. stock market had plunged more than 80% in only three years. This market disarray left enormouscarnage in its wake. In a period when not only the future prospects but even the immediate viability of many businesses seemed dim, identifying stocks trading below the liquidation value of the underlying companies was a fruitful filter. A great many securities were available on the bargain counter. Investing amid plunging prices and significant economic uncertainty, when others were fearing there was worse to come, might have seemed risky but actually conferred a favorable ratio of reward to risk for those intrepid enough to buy in.

然而，大多数时候经济并未处于萧条状态，很少有证券符合Graham和Dodd的严格标准。如果投资者只专注于购买他们所谓的“净净值”——即交易价格低于公司营运资本扣除所有负债后的价值的公司——那么他们就会忽视大量潜在机会（且可能更有吸引力）——比如质量更高、增长前景更好的企业。像任何采用过于狭隘方法的人一样，投资者必须回答“当没有选择时该怎么办？”这个问题。

<!--en-->
However, most of the time, the economy is not in depression and relatively few securities meet the strict Graham and Dodd criteria. An investor focusing solely on buying what they called “net nets”—companies trading for less than the value of their working capital net of all liabilities —would be ignoring a vast universe of potential (and likely more attractive) opportunities—in higher quality businesses with better growth prospects. As with anyone following an overly narrow approach, investors must have an answer to the question, “What do you do when there’s nothing to do?”

投资方法不应只是用于应对某一时刻，而应是始终相关的。我们必须认为，以低于公司基础资产清算价值的价格购买普通股是一种罕见的异常现象，只能偶尔在少数公司中出现。即使发现这样的估值，我们也需谨慎判断该方法是否有效。通过这种筛选可能发现的公司，很可能是存在重大问题且长期生存能力不确定的企业。在当今经济环境下，它们更可能是陷入困境的企业，而非隐藏的瑰宝。

<!--en-->
Investment approaches should be built not just to navigate one moment in time but to be relevant all the time. We must consider the opportunity to buy common stocks for less than the liquidation value of the underlying companies to be a rare aberration, one to be found only sporadically and at a small number of companies. Even if such valuations were found, we would need to be circumspect about whether the approach would bear fruit. The companies such a screen might reveal are likely to be those with significant problems and uncertain long-term viability. In today’s economy, they are less likely to be hidden gems than deeply troubled enterprises.

与此同时，分析公司的理念和工具也得到了极大扩展。投资者——无论是个人还是机构——不再依赖计算尺或简单的计算器；他们可以依靠强大的Bloomberg终端和台式电脑。仅通过已发布的财务报表来分析公司并不能带来明显优势。要在资金充足且技术先进的竞争对手中成功投资，投资者必须采用某种差异化视角或独特的信息来源方式，而分析企业资产负债表不太可能提供独特见解。同样，通过屏幕筛选低于表面清算价值的公司也无法带来明显优势，因为每个人都能做到这一点，因此股票很少像几十年前那样被严重定价错误。

<!--en-->
Meanwhile, the ideas and tools for analyzing companies have been dramatically expanded. Investors—whether individuals or institutions—no longer depend on a slide rule or rudimentary calculator; they can rely on powerful Bloomberg terminals and desktop computers. Analyzing a company solely by its published financial statements confers no evident edge. To invest successfully amid deep-pocketed and technologically enabled competitors, investors must have anapproach involving some sort of differentiated view or unique sourcing capability, and analyzing corporate balance sheets is unlikely to provide unique insights. Similarly, running a screen to identify companies trading below apparent liquidation value confers no apparent edge, because everyone can do that, and as a result, stocks don't often become and stay egregiously mispriced the way they may have many decades ago.

### 资产负债表分析为何不占优势

<!--en-->
*WHERE BALANCE SHEET ANALYSIS FALLS SHORT*

一家公司远不止其财务报表上的数字。如今，公开信息的数量以及可用于评估这些信息的分析工具确实非常丰富。大量华尔街分析师专注于企业的质量。他们开发了复杂的、尽管远非完美的模型，用于预测短期增长、利润率和现金流。管理层不再难以接触，也不再只与特定股东交流。事实上，大多数上市公司CEO和CFO会与股东举行季度收益会议，提供预测，举办深入的投资者日活动。他们在大型二次发行、分拆和IPO之前还会进行路演，与投资者见面。同时，投资分析师利用“专家网络”来了解公司、竞争对手及其行业情况。每个投资者都可以立即查看数千家公司的财务报表；关于数千家上市公司的华尔街研究报告也很容易获取。广泛传播的信息如果没有以差异化方式分析，则不会带来特殊优势；在竞争激烈的世界中，独特的信息来源很难找到。

<!--en-->
A company is much more than the numbers on its financial statements. These days, the volume of public information and the analytical tools available to assess that information are truly extraordinary. Legions of Wall Street analysts focus intensely on the quality of businesses. They have developed sophisticated, albeit far from perfect, models for projecting near-term growth, profit margins, and cash flows. Managements are no longer inaccessible, nor can they speak only to favored shareholders. Indeed, most CEOs and CFOs of publicly traded companies hold quarterly earnings calls with shareholders, provide forecasts, and offer in-depth investor days. They also go on road shows to meet with investors in advance of large secondary offerings, spin-offs, and IPOs. Meanwhile, investment analysts use “expert networks” to gain insights into a company, its competitors, and its industry. Every investor is able to instantaneously call up financial statements for thousands of companies; Wall Street research reports on thousands of publicly traded firms are also readily available. Widely disseminated information confers no particular edge unless it is analyzed in differentiated ways; unique sources of information are hard to come by in a highly competitive world.

对投资洞察的竞争加剧，使得投资者持续保持谦逊至关重要。信息时代的讽刺是：你可以知道比以往更多的信息，甚至可能比任何人知道的都多，但现在这些信息却没什么用处，因为它们无法给你带来任何特殊优势。每个人都知道你所知道的。事实上，仅基于公司财务数据筛选机会的天真方法很可能是一个愚蠢的选择。沃伦·巴菲特经常指出，投资就像打扑克，在一个重要方面。在扑克桌旁，如果你看向左边和右边，却无法识别出那个被更有经验的玩家邀请来的“垫脚石”、标记者或新手，那么很可能就是你。每个投资者都应该担心这个想法，并努力避免处于这种境地。

<!--en-->
The intensified competition for investment insights makes it crucial for investors to consistently exhibit deep humility. The irony of the information age is that you can know more than you ever did before, and perhaps more than anyone ever did before, yet that wealth of information is less useful now,because it confers upon you no particular edge. Everybody knows what you know. Indeed, a naive approach based solely on using company financials to screen for opportunity could well be a sucker bet. Warren Buffett often notes that investing can be like playing poker, in one important sense. At a poker table, if you look to your left and to your right and you can't identify the patsy, the mark, the rube who has been invited to the game by the more experienced players, then it's probably you. Every investor should be worried by that thought and should work assiduously to never find themselves in that position.

即使你能找到低于潜在清算价值的被忽视公司的股票，从错误定价中获益也远非确定之事，因为清算价值变得越来越模糊。公司并不容易或频繁进行清算；所有负债，包括表外和或有负债，必须在清算程序向股东分配之前清除，而股东的权益优先级较低。租赁协议下可能需要支付租金，这些租赁可能持续到未来。员工可能被承诺延期补偿或离职福利。产品可能有延长保修期。资金不足的养老金计划必须补充资金。此外，许多根据资产负债表分析似乎有折扣潜力的公司，在达到未来盈利能力之前，现金消耗率很高。这尤其适用于许多较小的科技公司和生物科技初创企业，它们可能在2020-2021年的狂热环境中过早上市。对于这类公司来说，今天手头的现金可能明天就不足以分配给股东，如果用于研发、客户获取、新设施或收购，就会耗尽。

<!--en-->
Even if you could find shares in overlooked companies available below likely liquidation value, benefiting from their mispricing has become far from a sure thing, because liquidation value has become increasingly murky. Companies are not easily or frequently liquidated; all liabilities, including off-balance sheet and contingent ones, must be extinguished before liquidation proceeds are distributed to shareholders, whose interests are subordinated. Rent must be paid under leases that may extend well into the future. Employees may have been promised deferred compensation or termination benefits. Products may have extended warranties. Underfunded pension plans must be funded. Also, many companies that seem potentially discounted based on balance sheet analysis have a cash burn rate until the time that they achieve a future profitability. This especially applies to many of the smaller technology companies and biotech start-ups that may have prematurely come public in the euphoric environment of 2020–2021. For such companies, cash on hand today may not be available for shareholders tomorrow if it is spent on research and development, customer acquisition, new facilities, or acquisitions.

投资者过度关注账面价值另一个陷阱是，财务会计准则远非完美。充其量，它们是近似值，就像印象派绘画一样，能传达出现实感，但并非真实。会计有点像从房间另一端射箭。你几乎肯定不会击中靶心，甚至可能不会击中目标。希望你能接近目标，但有时不会。

<!--en-->
Another pitfall for investors overly focused on book value is that financial accounting standards are far from perfect. At best, they are an approximation that, like an Impressionist painting, can give a sense of reality without being reality. Accounting is a bit like throwing a dart from the far side of a room. You almost certainly won't hit the bull's-eye, and youmay not even hit the target. Hopefully, you'll be close enough, but sometimes you won't be.

与会计原则相关的诸多困难之一在于，它们只能反映公司在某一固定时间点的财务状况。但情况会发生变化：公司可能拥有快速过期的存货、无法收回的应收账款，以及效率越来越低、过时或淘汰的厂房和设备。一些公司可能拥有大量表外负债，这些负债源于环境损害、产品缺陷或持续的诉讼。在账目的另一面，有些公司持有“隐藏资产”，例如价格远高于摊销成本的房地产、对增长迅速的子公司拥有的所有权权益，或资金严重超支的养老金计划。

<!--en-->
One of the many difficulties associated with accounting principles is that they provide a snapshot of a company's finances at a fixed point in time. But things change: companies may have inventories that are subject to rapid obsolescence, receivables that have become uncollectable, and plant and equipment that have become increasingly inefficient, outmoded, or obsolete. Some firms may have large off-balance sheet liabilities, resulting from environmental damage, product defects, or ongoing litigation. On the other side of the ledger, some companies hold "hidden assets," such as real estate that has appreciated far above amortized cost, ownership interest in an increasingly valuable fast-growing subsidiary, or a significantly overfunded pension plan.

长期持续通胀的影响也破坏了按历史成本会计方法计算的资产准确性。因此，拥有相同资产的两家公司可能会报告截然不同的账面价值。当然，从整体来看，会计仍然非常有用。有近似数据显然比完全没有信息要好。此外，在一些国家，会计准则不够严格，投资者应该比平时更谨慎地对待报告的数据。验证审计师的可信度非常重要。投资者的任务不是简单接受GAAP数据，而是质疑并不断完善这些数据，以追求更高的准确性。

<!--en-->
The effects of sustained inflation over time have also wreaked havoc with the accuracy of assets accounted for using historic cost accounting. Consequently, two companies owning identical assets could report very different book values. Accounting is, of course, still very useful in the big picture. An approximation is obviously better than no information at all. Also, in some countries, accounting standards are less than rigorous, and investors would be wise to be even more skeptical than usual about the reported numbers. It pays to verify that the auditor is highly credible. The job of investors is not to simply accept the GAAP numbers, but rather to question and continuously refine them to achieve greater and greater accuracy.

投资者在使用账面价值估算企业价值时面临的另一个会计挑战是股票回购的影响。会计准则会将股票回购成本从股东权益中扣除，这意味着一个经常用自由现金流回购股票的盈利良好的公司，其账面价值可能较低甚至为负。对于长期进行大规模股票回购的公司，会计原则很容易产生误导性的结果。

<!--en-->
Another accounting challenge investors face in using book value as a means of estimating business value is the impact of share buybacks over time. Accounting standards adjust shareholder's equity down for the cost of stock repurchases, meaning that a very profitable company that regularly buys back shares with free cash flow may have a low or even negative stated book value. Accounting principles for companies that execute large share repurchases over time can easily yield a misleading result.

成立公司的目的就是打造一个价值远超过其组成部分总和的企业。目标是将价值增长到远高于账面价值的水平，远远超过企业所持有的实物资产的成本。成功企业的现金流现值将显著超过创建和建设企业的成本，理想情况下差距很大。当然，当企业以合理的价格提供可靠的产品或服务，满足客户的需求和期望时，价值就产生了。（这不是收购中偶尔记录的财务报表中的商誉，而是商誉的一般、通俗定义，即公司在其客户、供应商和其他利益相关者中引发的积极情感或“商誉”，表现为忠诚、信任和共生关系。）

<!--en-->
The whole point of forming a company is to build an enterprise that is worth much more than the sum of its parts. The goal is to grow value to a level far above book value, significantly eclipsing the cost of the physical assets held by the business. The present value of the cash flows generated by a successful business will significantly exceed the cost of forming and building it, ideally by a very substantial margin. Value is, of course, created when a business offers a reliable product or service at a reasonable price that meets the needs and aspirations of its customers. The value of a business above the balance sheet value of its hard assets can be thought of as goodwill. (Not the financial statement goodwill sometimes booked in a takeover, but the general, conversational definition of goodwill, that is, the positive feelings, or “goodwill” that a company has engendered among its customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders as expressed through loyalty, trust, and symbiotic relationships.)

关注账面价值的另一个问题是，它往往对应着被技术显著颠覆的工业模式。大型制造公司的账面价值必然很高，这是从事此类业务所需资源的体现。但世界上一些最优秀的企业是在互联网出现之后成立的，许多企业“资产较少”。它们将制造和其他活动外包；他们租赁而非拥有资产。他们的产品是知识产权，如计算机软件。对于这类企业而言，账面价值基本无关紧要；它们的商业价值远高于所拥有的实物资产。一些公司通过积累越来越多的客户数据，能够在业务周围构建越来越广泛的护城河，形成有价值的网络效应——今天的商业成功会带来未来的更大竞争优势。

<!--en-->
Another problem with focusing on book value is that it is often embodied by an industrial model that has been significantly disrupted by technology. The book value of large manufacturing companies is of necessity substantial, a measure of the resources necessary to be in such businesses. But some of the best businesses in the world have been formed since the advent of the internet, and many are “asset light.” They outsource manufacturing and other activities; they rent rather than own assets. Their products are intellectual property such as computer software. For such businesses, book value is essentially irrelevant; their business value is considerably greater than the hard assets they own. Some companies are able to build increasingly wide moats around their businesses as a result of accumulating more and more data from their customers, creating a valuable network effect whereby today’s commercial success leads to tomorrow’s even greater competitive advantage.

如今，当一家公司失去优势并面临更大的竞争威胁（通常由于技术颠覆），负面影响会突然且无情地出现。许多股票的交易价格远高于账面价值（很多是有充分理由的），在账面价值无法缓冲负面影响之前，还有很长的下跌空间。如今，少数交易价格极低的企业，其账面价值或清算价值高于股价，很可能是那些上升潜力较小、商业模式较差的企业。因此，账面价值不再能筛选有吸引力的机会，反而相反。无法产生现金流的公司的账面价值必然值得怀疑，其存货、应收账款以及厂房和设备也是如此。

<!--en-->
Today, when a company loses its edge and comes under increased competitive threat, often because of technological disruption, the downside comes suddenly and relentlessly. With so many stocks trading at a hefty premium to book value (many for good reason), there is a long way to fall before thevalue of hard assets cushions the downside. These days, the small number of businesses trading at very depressed levels, levels at which the book value or liquidation value exceeds the share price, are likely to be those with commensurately less upside potential and inferior business models. Thus book value is no longer a screen for attractive opportunity, but instead for its opposite. The book value of a company that cannot generate cash flow is necessarily suspect, as are its component parts—inventory, receivables, and plant and equipment.

但是请注意：对于某些企业来说，账面价值仍然非常重要。像公用事业这样的受监管企业有权获得法定资本回报，因此大多数公用事业企业的估值范围相对较窄。银行与保险公司需满足监管机构的要求，即股东风险资本与业务规模之间的比例有一定要求。虽然有些企业比其他企业建立了更持久的竞争优势，但如果这些公司的资产负债表上的资产至少与其报告的价值一致，那么账面价值对于金融机构而言比对于大多数其他企业来说更为重要——这需要一个“如果”。

<!--en-->
But wait: for certain businesses, it should be noted, book value does remain quite relevant. Regulated businesses such as utilities are entitled to a statutory return on capital, and most utilities trade in a reasonably narrow valuation range as a result. Banks and insurance companies are required by regulators to have a certain ratio of shareholder capital at risk compared to the size of the business. While some have created more enduring business moats than others, book value is a more relevant metric for financial institutions than for most other businesses if (and this is a big if) the assets on the balance sheet of those firms are worth at least their reported carrying value.

### 资产负债表分析最有用的方面

<!--en-->
*THE MOST USEFUL ASPECTS OF BALANCE SHEET ANALYSIS*

尽管账面价值已远不如过去重要，但资产负债表分析对所有投资者来说仍然是非常有价值且必要的做法。公司的资产负债表可以反映其财务健康状况甚至繁荣程度。债务较少的公司被称为拥有“清洁”的资产负债表，通常具有较大的借款能力储备，从而具备运营和战略灵活性。另一方面，高杠杆的资产负债表则缺乏灵活性，并增加了必须偿还到期债务的潜在风险。当经济下滑且运营表现不佳时，负债累累的公司会迅速陷入困境。这可能会引发恶性循环：到期债务需要以越来越高的成本进行再融资，导致利息支出消耗越来越多的公司现金流。

<!--en-->
While book value has become considerably less relevant than in the past, nonetheless balance sheet analysis remains a highly valuable and necessary practice for all investors. A company's balance sheet can be an indicator of its financial health and even prosperity. Companies with limited debt are said to have a “clean” balance sheet and usually significant borrowing capacity in reserve, which confers operating and strategic flexibility. On the other hand, a highly leveraged balance sheet offers less flexibility, while raising the prospect of looming debt maturities that must be met. A heavily indebted company runs into trouble quickly when the economy turns down and its operating performance stumbles. That may launch a spiral in which maturing debt must berefinanced at increasingly higher cost, causing interest expense to gobble up a growing portion of corporate cash flow.

对于处于财务困境或破产中的公司而言，资产负债表分析始终是一把有用的工具。它仍是理解对公司资产权利优先级以及确定企业价值的重要元素。股权投资者面临的风险是，业务状况恶化可能导致需要以折扣价格发行稀释性股票。

<!--en-->
Balance sheet analysis will always be a useful tool to an investor in financially distressed or bankrupt companies. It remains an essential element in understanding the hierarchy of claims on the company's assets and determining the value of a business. Equity investors bear the risk that a downturn in business results could drive the need for dilutive share issuance at discounted prices.

企业管理层经常试图优化其资产负债表。持有过多现金和其他流动资产会降低投资资本回报率。另一方面，流动性不足会使企业容易受到经济或市场突发事件的影响。拥有清洁资产负债表的公司比高杠杆公司拥有更多自由度。

<!--en-->
Corporate managements regularly seek to optimize their balance sheets. Holding too much cash and other liquid assets lowers the return on invested capital. On the other hand, holding insufficient liquidity could cause a business to be vulnerable to sudden economic or market shocks. A company with a clean balance sheet has more degrees of freedom than a highly leveraged one.

最后，资产负债表可以提供关于公司实际经营表现的线索。能够识别警示信号非常重要。报告的收益是否与公司产生的自由现金流一致？收账所需天数或库存存放天数是否比过去更长？负债增长是否快于业务发展速度？投资者在做出决策前应进行此类分析。

<!--en-->
Finally, a balance sheet can provide clues to a company's underlying business performance. It's important to be able to identify red flags. Are the reported earnings consistent with the free cash flow generated by a company? Are the days it takes to collect on receivables or the number of days that inventory is held longer than in the past? Are liabilities growing faster than the business is? Investors will want to conduct such analyses before taking a position.

格雷厄姆和多德对账面价值的重视可能被新的指标所取代，但他们对资产负债表分析的关注仍然有效。资产负债表审查是分析投资的重要步骤，但并非充分条件。成功的投资者应始终深入研究最小化的资产负债表细节，以发现企业的真实优势及面临的挑战。无论投资者的模型和算法多么完善，阅读脚注总是有必要的。第42章

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd's emphasis on book value may have been supplanted by newer metrics, but their focus on balance sheet analysis remains valid. Balance sheet scrutiny is a necessary though not sufficient step in analyzing investments. A successful investor should always delve into the smallest balance sheet details in order to ferret out clues as to the true merits of a business and the challenges facing it. No matter how robust an investor's models and algorithms may be, it always pays to read the footnotes.
CHAPTER 42

## 资产负债表分析

<!--en-->
*Balance-Sheet Analysis.*

# 账面价值的重要性

<!--en-->
*Significance of Book Value*

在此之前我们已经多次表达观点：资产负债表值得比华尔街多年来愿意给予的更多关注。作为本节引言，让我们列出投资者可以从资产负债表研究中获得的五种类型的信息和指导：

<!--en-->
ON NUMEROUS OCCASIONS prior to this point we have expressed our conviction that the balance sheet deserves more attention than Wall Street has been willing to accord it for many years past. By way of introduction to this section of our work, let us list five types of information and guidance that the investor may derive from a study of the balance sheet:

1. 它显示有多少资本投资于企业。
2. 它揭示了公司财务状况的宽松或紧张程度，即营运资本状况。
3. 它包含资本结构的具体信息。
4. 它是对报告收益有效性的重要检验。
5. 它为分析收入来源提供了基础。在讨论资产负债表的第一项功能时，我们将先介绍一些定义。股票的*账面价值*是指资产负债表中所显示的与股票相关的资产价值。通常将这一价值限定为有形资产，即排除商誉、商标、专利、特许权、租赁权等项目。账面价值也被称为“资产价值”，有时称为“有形资产价值”，以明确不包括无形资产。对于普通股，它通常被称为“权益”。**账面价值的计算。**普通股的*每股账面价值*是通过将所有有形资产相加，减去所有负债和已发行的股票数量，然后除以股份总数得到的。在许多情况下，以下公式可以简化计算过程：普通股每股账面价值

<!--en-->
1. It shows how much capital is invested in the business.
2. It reveals the ease or stringency of the company's financial condition, *i.e.*, the working-capital position.
3. It contains the details of the capitalization structure.
4. It provides an important check upon the validity of the reported earnings.
5. It supplies the basis for analyzing the sources of income.
In dealing with the first of these functions of the balance sheet, we shall begin by presenting certain definitions. The *book value* of a stock is the value of the assets applicable thereto as shown in the balance sheet. It is customary to restrict this value to the tangible assets, *i.e.*, to eliminate from the calculation such items as good-will, trade names, patents, franchises, leaseholds. The book value is also referred to as the “asset value,” and sometimes as the “tangible-asset value,” to make clear that intangibles are not included. In the case of common stocks, it is also frequently termed the “equity.”
**Computation of Book Value.** The *book value per share* of a common stock is found by adding up all the tangible assets, subtracting all liabilities and stock issues ahead of the common and then dividing by the number of shares.
In many cases the following formula will be found to furnish a short cut to the answer:Book Value per share of common

$$
= \frac{\text{Common Stock} + \text{Surplus Items} - \text{Intangibles}}{\text{Number of shares outstanding}}
$$

盈余项目不仅指明确标记为盈余的项目，还包括资本股本溢价以及确实属于盈余部分的储备金。例如，包括优先股赎回储备金、工厂改进储备金以及应急储备金（除非实际需要）。这种性质的储备金可称为“自愿储备金”。

<!--en-->
By Surplus Items are meant not only items clearly marked as surplus but also premiums on capital stock and such reserves as are really part of the surplus. This would include, for example, reserves for preferred-stock retirement, for plant improvement, and for contingencies (unless known to be actually needed). Reserves of this character may be termed “Voluntary Reserves.”

## 1938年12月31日美国钢铁普通股账面价值计算 1938年12月31日简明资产负债表（单位：百万）

<!--en-->

**计算普通股账面价值时优先股的处理方式。** 在计算可用于普通股的资产时，必须正确扣除优先股的价值。通常，这将为资产负债表上显示的优先股面值或规定价值。但越来越多的案例中，资产负债表上记录的优先股价值远低于其实际负债价值。

<!--en-->
**Treatment of Preferred Stock When Calculating Book Value of Common.** In calculating the assets available for thecommon stock, care must be taken to subtract preferred stock at its proper valuation. Ordinarily, this will be the par or stated value of the preferred stock as it appears in the balance sheet. But there is a growing number of cases in which preferred stock is carried in the balance sheet at arbitrary values far lower than the real liability attaching thereto.

Island Creek Coal Company的优先股面值为1美元，有权获得每年6美元的股息，并在公司解散时每股获得120美元。1939年该股票的发行价格约为120美元。在计算Island Creek Coal普通股资产价值时，应按100美元每股（即“真实”或“有效”面值）而非1美元每股来扣除优先股价值，或者按120美元扣除。Capital Administration Company, Ltd.是一家投资信托，拥有未偿还优先股，有权获得3美元累计股息和50或55美元的清算款，但其面值为10美元。它还有Class *A*股票，有权在清算时获得20美元，加上剩余资产的70%和优先股股息后支付的收益的70%，但该股票的面值为1美元。最后还有Class *B*股票，面值为1分，有权获得剩余收益和资产。显然，基于面值编制的资产负债表在这种情况下不如无意义的报表，分析师必须按以下方式进行修正：

<!--en-->
Island Creek Coal Company has a preferred stock of $1 par, which is entitled to annual dividends of $6 and to $120 per share in the event of dissolution. In 1939 the price of this issue ruled about 120. In the calculation of the asset value of Island Creek Coal Common the preferred stock should be deducted not at $1 per share but at $100 per share, its “true” or “effective” par, or else at 120. Capital Administration Company, Ltd., an investment trust, has outstanding preferred stock entitled to $3 cumulative dividends and to $50 or $55 in liquidation, but its par value is $10. It has also a Class *A* stock entitled to $20 in liquidation plus 70% of the assets remaining and to 70% of the earnings paid out after preferred dividends, but the par value of this issue is $1. Finally it has Class *B* stock, par 1 cent, entitled to the residue of earnings and assets. Obviously a balance sheet set up on the basis of par value is worse than meaningless in this case, and it must be corrected by the analyst somewhat as follows:

* 这些数值近似于发行股票的实际面值。可口可乐公司发行了无面值的A类*股票，有权获得每股3美元的累积优先股息，且可在55的价格赎回。该公司将这种发行视为负债，其“声明价值”为每股5美元。但实际面值显然是50美元。¹在上述所有情况下，必须为优先股设定一个“实际面值”，以正确反映其股息率。可以提出一个有力的论点：所有优先股应基于统一的股息标准进行估值，比如5%，除非可以较低金额赎回。这意味着100万美元5%的发行将被估值为100万美元，100万美元4%的发行将被赋予800,000美元的实际价值，100万美元7%不可赎回的发行将被赋予1,400,000美元的实际价值。但当然，使用面值更为方便，在大多数情况下结果也会足够准确。²一种更简单的方法适用于大多数实际用途：按面值（加上回溯股息）或市场价中较高者对优先股进行估值。**优先股账面价值计算**。在计算优先股的账面价值时，将其视为普通股处理，与其同等级以下的发行不纳入考虑。以下来自Tubize Chatillon公司1932年12月31日资产负债表的计算，将说明相关原则。*Tubize Chatillon公司资产负债表，1932年12月31日*

<!--en-->
* These approximate the effective par values of the issues.
Coca-Cola Company has outstanding a no-par Class *A* stock entitled to preferential dividends of $3 per share, cumulative, and redeemable at 55. The company carries this issue as a liability at its “stated value” of $5 per share. But the true par value is clearly $50.¹
In all instances such as the above an “effective par value” must be set up for the preferred stock that will correspond properly to its dividend rate. A strong argument may be advanced in favor of valuing all preferred stocks on a uniform dividend basis, say 5%, unless callable at a lower figure. This would mean that a $1,000,000 five per cent issue would be valued at $1,000,000, a $1,000,000 four per cent issue would be given an effective value of $800,000 and a $1,000,000 seven per cent non callable issue would be given an effective value of $1,400,000. But it is more convenient, of course, to use the par value, and in most cases the result will be sufficiently accurate.² A simpler method, which would work well for most practical purposes, is to value preferred issues at par (plus back dividends) or market, whichever is higher.
**Calculation of Book Value of Preferred Stocks.** In calculating the book value of a preferred stock issue it is treated as a common stock and the issues junior to it are left out of consideration. The following computations from the December 31, 1932, balance sheet of Tubize Chatillon Corporation will illustrate the principles involved.

在计算普通股账面价值时，若以1美元的非代表性面值来扣除第二优先股，将是一个明显的错误。考虑到7美元的股息，应取不低于每股100美元的“有效面值”。因此，普通股没有资产可计算，其账面价值为零。

<!--en-->
In computing the book value of the common it would be an obvious error to deduct the Second Preferred at its nonrepresentative par value of $1. The “effective par” should be taken at not less than $100 per share, in view of the $7 dividend. Hence there are no assets available for the common stock, and its book value is nil.

**当前资产价值和现金资产价值**。除了众所周知的账面价值概念外，我们还想提出两个类似的概念，即当前资产价值和现金资产价值。

<!--en-->
**Current-Asset Value and Cash-Asset Value.** In addition to the well-known concept of book value, we wish to suggest two others of similar character, *viz.*, current-asset value and cash-asset value.

股票的当前资产价值仅包括流动资产，减去发行前的所有负债和权益。它不仅不包括无形资产，还包括固定资产和其他资产。

<!--en-->
The current-asset value of a stock consists of the current assets alone, minus all liabilities and claims ahead of the issue. It excludes not only the intangible assets but the fixed and miscellaneous assets as well.

股票的现金资产价值仅包括现金资产，减去发行前的所有负债和权益。³除现金本身外，现金资产还包括与现金直接等价且作为现金持有的资产。这些包括定期存单、调用贷款、按市场价值计量的证券以及保险单的现金退保价值。

<!--en-->
The cash-asset value of a stock consists of the cash assets alone, minus all liabilities and claims ahead of the issue.³ Cash assets, other than cash itself, are defined as those directly equivalent to and held in place of cash. They include certificates of deposit, call loans, marketable securities at market value and cash-surrender value of insurance policies.

在这些计算中，首先要注意的是，通过恢复资产负债表上减去的425,000美元储备，存货增加了。这是因为公司所扣除的金额显然是为了应对尚未发生的潜在价值下降而设立的储备金。因此，这是完全任意或自愿的，方法的一致性要求分析师将其视为盈余项目。同样，210,000美元的“设备及其他费用储备”也并非实际负债，也不是从特定资产价值中必要的扣除。

<!--en-->
In these calculations it will be noted, first, that the inventory is increased by restoring the reserve of $425,000 subtracted therefrom in the balance sheet. This is done because the deduction taken by the company is clearly a reserve for contingent decline in value that has not yet taken place. As such it is entirely arbitrary or voluntary, and consistency of method would require the analyst to regard it as a surplus item. The same is true of the $210,000 "Reserve for Equipment and Other Expenses," which, as far as can be seen, represents neither an actual liability nor a necessary deduction from the value of any specific asset.

1929年6月，Otis公司的普通股售价为35。读者会注意到，这个市场价格与股票流动资产价值之间存在异常差异。其重要性将在后面讨论。

<!--en-->
In June 1929 Otis Company common stock was selling at 35. The reader will observe an extraordinary divergence between this market price and the current-asset value of the shares. Its significance will engage our attention later.

**账面价值的实际意义。** 普通股的账面价值最初是其财务展示中最重要的元素。它旨在显示“股份价值”，就像商人的资产负债表显示其业务价值一样。这一观念几乎完全从财务视野中消失。资产负债表中所列的公司资产价值实际上已失去所有意义。这种变化源于两个原因：第一，固定资产的价值往往与实际成本无关；第二，在更大比例的情况下，这些价值与出售价格或收益所能证明的数值无关。夸大固定财产账面价值的做法正在被相反的行为所取代——即将其削减到零，以避免折旧费用，但两者都导致账面数值失去实际意义。这有点奇怪，像过去遗留的奇特做法，主要的统计机构仍然坚持用他们发布的许多（可能是最多的）资产负债表来计算每股普通股的账面价值。

<!--en-->
**Practical Significance of Book Value.** The book value of a common stock was originally the most important element in its financial exhibit. It was supposed to show “the value” of the shares in the same way as a merchant’s balance sheet shows him the value of his business. This idea has almost completely disappeared from the financial horizon. The value of a company’s assets as carried in its balance sheet has lost practically all its significance. This change arose from the fact, first, that the value of the fixed assets, as stated, frequently bore no relationship to the actual cost and, secondly, that in an even larger proportion of cases these values bore no relationship to the figure at which they would be sold or the figure which would be justified by the earnings. The practice of inflating the book value of the fixed property is giving way to the opposite artifice of cutting it down to nothing in order to avoid depreciation charges, but both have the same consequence of depriving the book-value figures of any real significance. It is a bit strange, like a quaint survival from the past, that the leading statistical services still maintain the old procedure of calculating the book value per share of common stock from many, perhaps most, balance sheets that they publish.

在彻底摒弃这种历史悠久的账面价值概念之前，让我们先问一下，它是否可能对分析师有实际意义。通常情况下，可能没有。但极端或特殊情况下呢？让我们考虑下一页显示的四个案例，作为账面价值与市场价格之间极端关系的代表。

<!--en-->
Before we discard completely this time-honored conception of book value, let us ask if it may ever have practical significance for the analyst. In the ordinary case, probably not. But what of the extraordinary or extreme case? Let us consider the four exhibits shown on the following page, as representative of extreme relationships between book value and market price.

任何深思熟虑的观察者都会对例子中显示的差异印象深刻。在通用电气和Commercial Solvents案例中，数据表明市场对股份的估值远高于账面价值。股票代码似乎记录了这些企业的总体估值，这与它们作为普通企业的地位完全无关。换句话说，这些根本不是*商业估值*；它们是华尔街操纵的产物，或可能是其预知能力的结果。

<!--en-->
No thoughtful observer could fail to be impressed by the disparities revealed in the examples given. In the case of General Electric and Commercial Solvents the figures proclaim more than the bare fact that the market was valuing the shares at many times their book value. The stock ticker seems here to register an aggregate valuation for these enterprises that is totally unrelated to their standing as ordinary business enterprises. In other words, these are in no sense *business valuations*; they are products of Wall Street’s legerdemain, or possibly of its clairvoyance.

*财务推理与商业推理。* 这里有一个观点，或许比任何其他观点都更明显地揭示了财务思维与普通商业思维之间的巨大差距。一个几乎难以置信的事实是，华尔街从未问过：“企业售价是多少？”然而，这是考虑购买股票时第一个问题。如果一位商人被提供10,000美元购买某公司的5%权益，他的第一个心理过程将是将报价乘以20，从而确定整个企业的拟议价值为200,000美元。其余的计算则围绕这样一个问题：以200,000美元的价格购买是否是“好买卖”。

<!--en-->
*Financial Reasoning vs. Business Reasoning.* We have here the point that brings home more strikingly perhaps than any other the widened rift between financial thought and ordinary business thought. It is an almost unbelievable fact that Wall Street never asks, “How much is the business selling for?” Yet this should be the first question in considering a stock purchase. If a business man were offered a 5% interest in some concern for $10,000, his first mental process would be to multiply the asked price by 20 and thus establish a proposed value of $200,000 for the entire undertaking. The rest of his calculation would turn about the question whether or not the business was a “good buy” at $200,000.

这种基本且不可或缺的方法已被购买股票的人几乎放弃。在1929-1930年那些“投资”通用电气的人中，可能只有极少数人意识到，他们以约25亿美元的价格购买该公司——其中超过20亿美元是超出实际投入资金价值的溢价。1933年7月商业溶剂公司定下的57美元价格，更像是一种赌博行为，是由预期将废除禁酒令所引发的。但这次的赌徒们与那些自称为投资者的人并无不同，他们完全无视这样一个事实：他们为一家仅有1000万资源的企业支付1.4亿美元。（商业溶剂公司的固定资产在资产负债表中被减至零，当然具有实际价值，但不超过几百万美元。）

<!--en-->
This elementary and indispensable approach has been practically abandoned by those who purchase stocks. Of thethousands who “invested” in General Electric in 1929–1930 probably only an infinitesimal number had any idea that they were paying on the basis of about $2\frac{1}{2}$ billions of dollars for the company, of which over two billions represented a premium above the money actually invested in the business. The price of 57 established for Commercial Solvents in July 1933 was more of a gambling phenomenon, induced by the expected repeal of prohibition. But the gamblers in this instance were acting no differently from those who call themselves investors, in their blithe disregard of the fact that they were paying 140 millions for an enterprise with about 10 millions of resources. (The fixed assets of Commercial Solvents, written down to nothing in the balance sheet, had real value, of course, but not in excess of a few millions.)

我们示例中展示的另一种对比同样令人印象深刻。像宾夕法尼亚煤炭公司这样处于发展阶段但未能成功发展的企业，其市场价值可能仅为其声明资源的十六分之一，几乎与一项具有投机吸引力的资产以其净资产的十六倍进行竞购同一天发生。Pepperell案例或许更为突出，因为账面价值的数值具有无可争议的现实性，同时该企业多年来拥有良好的声誉、可观收益和慷慨的股息。然而，这家企业的部分股东——诚然，在经济萧条的压力下——仍愿意以仅相当于单个私人所有者会毫不犹豫赋予其价值的十分之一的价格出售股份。

<!--en-->
The contrast in the other direction shown by our examples is almost as impressive. A going but unsuccessful concern like Pennsylvania Coal and Coke can be valued in the market at about one-sixteenth of its stated resources almost on the same day as a speculatively attractive issue is bid for at sixteen times its net worth. The Pepperell example is perhaps more striking still, because of the unquestioned reality of the figures of book value and also because of the high reputation, large earnings, and liberal dividends of the enterprise covering a long stretch of years. Yet part owners of this business—under the stress of depression, it is true—were willing to sell out their interest at one-tenth of the value that a single private owner would have unhesitatingly placed upon it.

*建议。* 这些例子虽然极端，但强烈表明公众在购买或出售企业股份之前，至少应该简要了解账面价值。在任何具体情况下，账面价值所传达的信息可能并不重要，不值得关注。但在拒绝这一观点之前，应对其进行分析。如果股票买家声称自己有判断力，至少能够先确定自己实际上对这家企业赋予的价值，以及自己花钱后实际获得的有形资源是什么。

<!--en-->
*Recommendation.* These examples, extreme as they are, suggest rather forcibly that the book value deserves at least a fleeting glance by the public before it buys or sells shares in a business undertaking. In any particular case the message that the book value conveys may well prove to be inconsequential and unworthy of attention. But this testimony should be examined before it is rejected. Let the stock buyer, if he lays any claim to intelligence, at least be able to tell himself, first, what value he is actually setting on the business and, second, what he is actually getting for his money in terms of tangible resources.

确实有一些假设支持那些远低于资产价值的购买行为，而反对那些远高于资产价值的高价购买行为。（假设在常规情况下，财务报表可以大致反映实际投入企业的现金金额。）以高价出售的企业之所以如此，是因为其资本获得了高回报；这种高回报会吸引竞争，一般来说，这种状况不会无限期持续下去。相反，如果企业因异常低的收益而以大幅折扣价格出售，缺乏新竞争、原有竞争退出市场以及其他自然经济力量，最终可能会改善局势，恢复投资的正常利润水平。

<!--en-->
There are indeed certain presumptions in favor of purchases made far below asset value and against those made at a high premium above it. (It is assumed that in the ordinary case the book figures may be accepted as roughly indicative of the actual cash invested in the enterprise.) A business that sells at a premium does so because it earns a large return upon its capital; this large return attracts competition, and, generally speaking, it is not likely to continue indefinitely. Conversely in the case of a business selling at a large discount because of abnormally low earnings. The absence of new competition, the withdrawal of old competition from the field, and other natural economic forces may tend eventually to improve the situation and restore a normal rate of profit on the investment.

尽管这是正统的经济理论，且在广义上无疑是正确的，但我们怀疑它能否充分且迅速地应用于股票选择中作为重要因素。需要指出的是，在现代条件下，所谓的“非有形资产”，例如良好信誉或高效的组织结构，从实际价值角度来看，与建筑物和机器并无差异。基于这些非有形资产的收益可能比仅需要现金投资于生产设施的收入更不易受到竞争影响。此外，当条件有利时，资本投入相对较小的企业更有可能实现更快的增长速度。通常而言，这类企业可以在较小的成本下扩大销售和利润规模，因此对其股东来说，增长速度和盈利性都更高，相比那些每销售一美元都需要大量工厂投资的企业。

<!--en-->
Although this is orthodox economic theory, and undoubtedly valid in a broad sense, we doubt if it applies with sufficient certainty and celerity to make it useful as a governing factor in common-stock selection. It may be pointed out that under modern conditions the so-called “intangibles,” e.g., good-will or even a highly efficient organization, are every whit as real from a dollars-and-cents standpoint as are buildings and machinery.⁴ Earnings based on these intangibles may be even less vulnerable to competition than those which require only a cash investment in productive facilities. Furthermore, when conditions are favorable the enterprise with the relatively small capital investment is likely to show a more rapid rate of growth. Ordinarily it can expand its sales and profits at slight expense and therefore more rapidly and profitably for its stockholders than a business requiring a large plant investment per dollar of sales.

因此，我们认为无法合理制定关于账面价值与市场价格关系的规则，除了已经提出的强烈建议：购买者应清楚自己的决策，并确信自己的行为是明智的。[^2634]: ¹ 有趣的是，在1929年，该公司将194,000股A类股票回购股份作为资产，成本为9,434,000美元，尽管总共发行的1,000,000股股票仅被列为负债5,000,000美元。关于普通股中类似的会计荒谬现象，可参考Hecker Products 1939年6月的资产负债表——其中其资本股的净负债显示为负数。

<!--en-->
We do not think, therefore, that any rules may reasonably be laid down on the subject of book value in relation to market price, except the strong recommendation already made that the purchaser know what he is doing on this score and be satisfied in his own mind that he is acting sensibly.
[^2634]: ¹ Amusingly enough, in 1929 the company carried *as an asset* 194,000 repurchased shares of Class A stock at their cost of $9,434,000, although the entire issue of 1,000,000 shares appeared as a liability of only $5,000,000. For a similar accounting absurdity applied to common stocks, see the June 1939 balance sheet of Hecker Products—on which its net stated liability for its capital stock works out as a *minus* figure.

2 Standard Statistics Company, Inc.在计算普通股的账面价值时，采用在*强制清算情况下*按价值扣除优先股的做法。这似乎不合逻辑，因为解散或清算几乎总是遥远的事件，会在与分析时完全不同的条件下发生。Standard Statistics Company的方法导致Procter and Gamble Company的5美元第二优先股被定为每股115美元的价值，而同一公司的8美元第一优先股则只有每股100美元的价值。在这种情况下，优先股持有人的实际或实际价值更接近：第一优先股为160，第二优先股为100，两者的股息率均为5%。对于投资信托发行的股票，优先股的清算价值更为相关，通常应予以使用。

<!--en-->
2 Standard Statistics Company, Inc., follows the practice of deducting preferred stock at its value *in case of involuntary liquidation*, when computing the book value of the common. This is scarcely logical, because dissolution or liquidation is almost always a remote contingency and would take place under conditions quite different from those obtaining at the time of analysis. The Standard Statistics Company method results in placing a “value” of $115 per share on Procter and Gamble Company $5 Second Preferred and a value of only $100 per share on the same company’s $8 First Preferred. The real or practical value of the preferred stockholder’s claims in this case would be much nearer in the proportion of 160 for the First Preferred against 100 for the Second Preferred, a 5% dividend yield basis for both. In the case of investment-trust issues, liquidation values of preferred issues are more relevant and should generally be used.

3 普通股的每股现金资产有时不扣除任何负债来计算。我们认为，只有当其他*流动*资产超过普通股的所有负债时，这一概念才有意义。

<!--en-->
3 Cash assets per share of common are sometimes calculated without deduction of any liabilities. In our opinion this is a useful concept only when the other *current* assets exceed all liabilities ahead of the common.

4 无形资产的法律评估（针对紧密企业）似乎仍遵循旧观念，即无形资产比有形资产“不真实”，因此需要相对更多的收益来支撑。股市评估基础与企业家和法院评估基础之间的差异，应用于私营企业，将为批判性研究提供优秀素材。

<!--en-->
4 Judicial valuations of intangible assets (in the case of close corporations) still seem to adhere to the old concept that they are less “real” than tangible assets and thus need larger earnings, relatively, to support them. The divergence between the stock market’s bases of valuation and those of business men and the courts, as applied to private enterprises, would provide excellent material for a critical study.

关于一项定量研究，该研究表明“商誉”总体上比有形资产更有盈利潜力，可参考Lawrence N. Bloomberg的《商誉的投资价值》，巴尔的摩，1938年。第43章

<!--en-->
For a quantitative study leading to the conclusion that “good-will” has, on the whole, proved more profitable than tangible assets, see Lawrence N. Bloomberg, *The Investment Value of Goodwill*, Baltimore, 1938.
CHAPTER 43

## 当前资产价值的重要性

<!--en-->
*Significance of the Current-Asset Value*

普通股的当前资产价值可能比包含固定资产的账面价值更重要。我们对此的讨论将发展以下论点：

<!--en-->
THE CURRENT-ASSET VALUE of a common stock is more likely to be an important figure than the book value, which includes the fixed assets. Our discussion of this point will develop the following theses:

1. 当前资产值通常是一个*清算价值*的粗略指标。
2. 许多普通股的价格低于其当前资产价值，因此低于清算时可变现的金额。
3. 许多股票持续以低于清算价值的价格出售的现象从根本上说是不合逻辑的。这意味着正在发生严重的错误，可能源于：(a) 股市的判断错误；(b) 公司管理层的政策错误；或(c) 股东对其资产的态度错误。**清算价值**。我们所说的企业清算价值，指的是所有者如果愿意放弃企业，能够从中获得的资金。他们可能会以持续经营的方式，将全部或部分资产出售给其他人。或者，他们可能会逐步将各种资产转化为现金，需要一定时间来充分变现每项资产。这种清算在私营企业中很常见。然而，在上市公司中却非常罕见。确实，一家公司通常会被另一家公司收购，通常价格远高于清算价值，而且破产时也会进行资产的逐步出售；但自愿退出不盈利业务，并仔细清算资产的情况，在私营企业中比在上市公司中更为常见。这种差异有其原因和意义，我们稍后会说明。**资产的变现价值取决于其性质。** 公司的资产负债表并不能提供关于其清算价值的准确信息，但它提供了一些可能有用的线索或提示。计算清算价值的第一个规则是，负债是真实的，但资产的价值必须加以质疑。这意味着账面上显示的所有真实负债都必须按面值扣除。然而，资产应赋予的价值则取决于其性质。以下表格很好地显示了各种类型资产在清算中的相对可靠性。

<!--en-->
1. The current-asset value is generally a rough index of the *liquidating value*.
2. A large number of common stocks sell for less than their current-asset value and therefore sell below the amount realizable in liquidation.
3. The phenomenon of many stocks selling persistently below their liquidating value is fundamentally illogical. It means that a serious error is being committed, either: (a) in the judgment of the stock market, (b) in the policies of the company's management, or (c) in the attitude of the stockholders toward their property.
**Liquidating Value.** By the liquidating value of an enterprise we mean the money that the owners could get out of it if they wanted to give it up. They might sell all or part of it to some one else, on a going-concern basis. Or else they might turn the various kinds of assets into cash, in piecemeal fashion, taking whatever time is needed to obtain the best realization from each. Such liquidations are of everyday occurrence in the field of private business. By contrast, however, they are very rare indeed in the field of publicly owned corporations. It is true that one company often sells out to another, usually at a price well above liquidating value, also that insolvency will at timesresult in the piecemeal sale of the assets; but the voluntary withdrawal from an unprofitable business, accompanied by the careful liquidation of the assets, is an infinitely more frequent happening among private than among publicly owned concerns. This divergence is not without its cause and meaning, as we shall show later.
**Realizable Value of Assets Varies with Their Character.** A company's balance sheet does not convey exact information as to its value in liquidation, but it does supply clues or hints which may prove useful. The first rule in calculating liquidating value is that the liabilities are real but the value of the assets must be questioned. This means that all true liabilities shown on the books must be deducted at their face amount. The value to be ascribed to the assets, however, will vary according to their character. The following schedule indicates fairly well the relative dependability of various types of assets in liquidation.

<!--en-->
* Note: Retail installment accounts must be valued for liquidation at a lower rate. Range about 30 to 60%. Average about 50%.
*Calculation Illustrated.* The calculation of approximate liquidating value in a specific case is illustrated as follows:
*Example: White Motor Company. (See next page.)*
*Object of This Calculation.* In studying this computation it must be borne in mind that our object is not to determine the exact liquidating value of White Motor but merely to form a rough idea of this liquidating value *in order to ascertain whether or not the shares are selling for less than the stockholders could actually take out of the business.* The latterquestion is answered very definitely in the affirmative. With full allowance for possible error, there was no doubt at all (in 1931) that White Motor would liquidate for a great deal more than $8 per share, or $5,200,000 for the company. The striking fact that the cash assets alone considerably exceed this figure, *after deducting all liabilities*, completely clinched the argument on this score.
*Current-Asset Value a Rough Measure of Liquidating Value.* The estimated values in liquidation as given for White Motor are somewhat lower in respect of inventories and somewhat higher as regards the fixed and miscellaneous assets than one might be inclined to adopt in other examples. We are allowing for the fact that motor-truck inventories are likely to be less salable than the average. On the other hand some of the assets listed as noncurrent, in particular the investment in White Motor Securities Corporation, would be likely to yield a larger proportion of their book values than the ordinary property account. It will be seen that White Motor's estimated liquidating value (about $31 per share) was not far from the current-asset value ($34 per share). In the typical case it may be said that the noncurrent assets are likely to realize enough to make up most of the shrinkage suffered in the liquidation of the current assets. Hence our first thesis, *viz.*, that the current-asset value affords a rough measure of the liquidating value.

**股票低于清算价值的比例。** 我们的第二个观点是，过去几年中，大量普通股在市场上的售价远低于其清算价值。自然，在经济萧条期间这一比例最高。但即使在1926–1929年的牛市时期，这种现象也并不罕见。需要指出的是，上一章提到的Otis公司事件发生在1929年6月，即经济繁荣的顶峰时期。第41章中提到的Northern Pipe Line案例则来自1926年。另一方面，Pepperell和White Motor的案例属于1931–1933年的崩溃时期现象。

<!--en-->
**Prevalence of Stocks Selling Below Liquidating Value.** Our second point is that for some years past a considerable number of common stocks have been selling in the market well below their liquidating value. Naturally the percentage was largest during the depression. But even in the bull market of 1926–1929 instances of this kind were by no means rare. It will be noted that the striking case of Otis Company, presented in the last chapter, occurred during June 1929, at the very height of the boom. The Northern Pipe Line example, given in Chap. 41, dates from 1926. On the other hand, our Pepperell andWhite Motor illustrations were phenomena of the 1931–1933 collapse.

我们认为，那三年间股市最显著的特征就是大量股票以低于清算价值的价格出售。我们的计算表明，1932年纽约证券交易所上市的工业公司中，超过40%的公司在那时其净流动资产低于其市值。实际上，许多公司的售价低于现金资产价值，如White Motor的情况。¹ 仔细思考后，这似乎是一种异常现象。典型的美国企业显然其“死值”高于“活值”。这些大企业的所有者通过关闭工厂可能获得更多利益，而不是以持续经营的方式出售。

<!--en-->
It seems to us that the most distinctive feature of the stock market of those three years was the large proportion of issues which sold below their liquidating value. Our computations indicate that over 40% of all the industrial companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange were quoted at some time in 1932 at less than their net current assets. A considerable number actually sold for less than their cash-asset value, as in the case of White Motor.¹ On reflection this must appear to be an extraordinary state of affairs. The typical American corporation was apparently worth more dead than alive. The owners of these great businesses could get more for their interest by shutting up shop than by selling out on a going-concern basis.

在1937–1938年的经济衰退中，这种情况以较小规模再次出现。现有数据表明，1938年初，纽约证券交易所上市的工业公司中有20.5%的公司以低于其净流动资产价值的价格出售。（到1938年底，当整体价格水平并非异常低时，所研究的648家工业公司中共有54家公司以低于净流动资产价值的价格出售。²）重要的是要注意，这种价格与流动资产价值之间的广泛差异是相对较新的现象。在1921年的严重市场萧条中，这类股票的占比很小。显然，1932年（及1938年）的现象是新时代理论的直接结果，该理论将所有价值评估标准转移到收入账户中，完全忽略资产负债表情况。因此，没有当前盈利能力的公司被认为几乎没有实际价值，其市场售价很可能仅为其可变现资源的极小部分。大多数出售者并未意识到他们正在以远低于残值的价格出售权益。然而，许多可能知道这一事实的人会以清算价值没有实际意义为由，为低价辩护，因为公司并无清算意图。

<!--en-->
In the recession of 1937–1938 this situation was repeated on a smaller scale. Available data indicate that 20.5% of the industrial companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange sold in early 1938 at less than their net-current-asset value. (At the close of 1938, when the general price level was by no means abnormally low, a total of 54 companies out of 648 industrials studied sold for less than their net current assets.²)
It is important to observe that these widespread discrepancies between price and current-asset value are a comparatively recent development. In the severe market depression of 1921 the proportion of industrial stocks in this class was quite small. Evidently the phenomena of 1932 (and 1938) were the direct out-growth of the new-era doctrine which transferred *all* the tests of value to the income account and completely ignored the balance-sheet picture. In consequence, a company without current earnings was regarded as having very little real value, and it was likely to sell in the market for the merest fraction of its realizable resources. Most of the sellers were not aware that they were disposing of their interest at far less than its scrap value. Many, however, who might have known the fact would have justified the low price on the ground that the liquidating valuewas of no practical importance, since the company had no intention of liquidating.

**这种现象的逻辑意义。** 这引出了第三个观点，即从市场、管理层和股东的角度来看，这种“低于清算价值”现象的逻辑意义是什么。整个问题可以总结为一个基本原则，即：

<!--en-->
**Logical Significance of This Phenomenon.** This brings us to the third point, *viz.*, the logical significance of this “subliquidating-value” phenomenon from the standpoint of the market, of the managements and of the stockholders. The whole issue may be summarized in the form of a basic principle, *viz.*:

*当普通股持续以低于清算价值的价格出售时，要么价格过低，要么公司应该进行清算。* 可以从这一原则推导出两个推论：

<!--en-->
*When a common stock sells persistently below its liquidating value, then either the price is too low or the company should be liquidated.*
Two corollaries may be deduced from this principle:

*推论一。* 这样的价格应促使股东考虑是否继续经营符合他们的利益。

<!--en-->
*Corollary I.* Such a price should impel the stockholders to raise the question whether or not it is in their interest to continue the business.

*推论二。* 这样的价格应促使管理层采取一切适当措施，纠正市场报价与内在价值之间的明显差距，包括重新考虑自身政策，并向股东坦诚说明继续经营的决定。

<!--en-->
*Corollary II.* Such a price should impel the management to take all proper steps to correct the obvious disparity between market quotation and intrinsic value, including a reconsideration of its own policies and a frank justification to the stockholders of its decision to continue the business.

上述原则的真实性应该是显而易见的。没有*合理*的经济理由解释为什么股票持续以低于清算价值的价格出售。如果公司作为持续经营企业的价值低于清算价值，则应该进行清算。如果其作为持续经营企业的价值更高，那么股票的价格应该高于清算价值。因此，无论基于哪种前提，低于清算价值的价格都是不可解释的。

<!--en-->
The truth of the principle above stated should be self-evident. There can be no *sound* economic reason for a stock's selling continuously below its liquidation value. If the company is not worth more as a going concern than in liquidation, it should be liquidated. If it is worth more as a going concern, then the stock should sell for more than its liquidating value. Hence, on either premise, a price below liquidating value is unjustifiable.

*前述原则的双重应用。* 以逻辑替代形式表达，我们的原则鼓励双重应用。以低于清算价值的价格出售的股票在许多情况下价格过低，因此成为吸引购买的中间品。因此，这里为证券分析技术提供了有利领域。但在许多情况下，股票以低于清算价值的价格出售，也表明正在执行错误的政策，因此管理层应该采取纠正措施——即使不是自愿的，也要在股东的压力下采取行动。让我们依次考虑这两条研究路线。

<!--en-->
*Twofold Application of Foregoing Principle.* Stated in the form of a logical alternative, our principle invites a twofold application. Stocks selling below liquidation value are in many cases too cheap and so offer an attractive medium for purchase. We have thus a profitable field here for the technique of security analysis. But in many cases also the fact that an issue sells below liquidating value is a signal that mistaken policies are being followed and that therefore the management should take corrective action—if not voluntarily,then under pressure from the stockholders. Let us consider these two lines of inquiry in order.

## 承诺类问题的吸引力

<!--en-->
*ATTRACTIVENESS OF SUCH ISSUES AS COMMITMENTS*

此类股票的收益趋势通常不尽如人意。如果利润持续稳定增长，显然股票不会以如此低的价格出售。购买这些股票的反对理由在于：收益可能下降，或亏损持续，资源可能被浪费，最终内在价值会低于支付价格。不可否认，这种情况确实会在个别案例中发生。另一方面，还有更广泛的潜在发展情况可能导致更高的市场价格。包括以下内容：

<!--en-->
Common stocks in this category practically always have an unsatisfactory trend of earnings. If the profits had been increasing steadily, it is obvious that the shares would not sell at so low a price. The objection to buying these issues lies in the probability, or at least the possibility, that earnings will decline or losses continue and that the resources will be dissipated and the intrinsic value ultimately become less than the price paid. It may not be denied that this does actually happen in individual cases. On the other hand, there is a much wider range of potential developments which may result in establishing a higher market price. These include the following:

1. 创造与公司资产相称的盈利能力。这可能源于：a. 整个行业的整体改善；b. 公司经营政策的积极变化，无论是否更换管理层。这些变化包括更高效的方法、新产品推出、放弃无利可图的业务等。
2. 出售或合并，因为其他企业能够更好地利用资源，因此可以至少按清算价值支付资产价格。
3. 完全或部分清算。**有利发展对这类问题的影响示例。** *整个行业的整体改善。* 已给出的示例及某些其他案例将说明各种有利发展的作用。以Pepperell为例，$17\frac{1}{2}$的低价与1932年6月30日结束的年度大幅亏损相吻合。次年纺织行业状况改善；Pepperell每股盈利超过9美元并恢复分红；因此，1934年1月股价升至100，1936年升至149 3/4。*经营政策的变化。* 另一纺织领域的例子是汉密尔顿毛织公司，属于局部而非整体改善。1928年前几年，该公司一直处于重大亏损状态，1926年和1927年分别亏损近20美元和12美元。1927年末，普通股售价为每股13美元，尽管当时公司的净流动资产为每股38.50美元。1928年和1929年，公司进行了管理层及管理政策调整，引入新产品线和直接销售方式，重组了部分生产环节。这导致盈利能力大幅提升，后续四年平均每股约5.50美元，一年内股价就上涨至约40美元。*出售或合并。* White Motor的案例典型地展示了出售或合并的产生及即时影响，适用于以低于清算价值出售的股票。（不过后续发展相当不寻常。）White Motor在1930-1932年的巨大亏损促使管理层寻求新的合作方式。Studebaker公司认为可以将自身业务与White Motor的业务结合以互利方式发展，且对White Motor的大量现金非常感兴趣。因此，1932年9月，Studebaker提出购买White Motor的所有股票，每股支付如下费用：现金5美元；Studebaker公司10年期6%债券25美元；1股Studebaker普通股，售价约10美元。可以看出，这些购买条件并非基于White Motor近期价格——低于每股7美元——而是主要基于流动资产价值。White Motor的股价迅速升至27美元，后来以相当于31 1/2美元的价格出售。⁴ 一个类似但时间较近的有趣例子来自内布拉斯加标准石油公司。事实可概括如下：1939年初，股票售价约为6美元，总估值为1,000,000美元，对应161,000股股份，构成全部资本。1938年12月31日的资产负债表见附表。

<!--en-->
1. The creation of an earning power commensurate with the company's assets. This may result from:
a. General improvement in the industry.
b. Favorable change in the company's operating policies, with or without a change in management. These changes include more efficient methods, new products, abandonment of unprofitable lines, etc.
2. A sale or merger, because some other concern is able to utilize the resources to better advantage and hence can pay at least liquidating value for the assets.
3. Complete or partial liquidation.
**Examples of Effect of Favorable Developments on Such Issues.** *General Improvement in the Industry.* Examples already given, and certain others, will illustrate the operation of these various kinds of favorable developments. In the case of Pepperell the low price of $17\frac{1}{2}$ coincided with a large loss for the year ended June 30, 1932. In the following year conditions in the textile industry improved; Pepperell earned over $9 per share and resumed dividends; consequently theprice of the stock advanced to 100 in January 1934 and to 149 3/4 in 1936.
*Changes in Operating Policies.* Hamilton Woolen Company, another example in the textile field, is a case of individual rather than of general improvement. For several years prior to 1928 the company had operated at substantial losses, which amounted to nearly $20 and $12 per share in 1926 and 1927, respectively. Late in 1927 the common stock sold at $13 per share, although the company had net current assets of $38.50 per share at that time. In 1928 and 1929 changes in management and in managerial policies were made, new lines of product and direct sales methods were introduced, and certain phases of production were reorganized. This resulted in greatly improved earnings which averaged about $5.50 per share during the succeeding four years, and within a single year the stock had risen to a price of about $40.³
*Sale or Merger.* The White Motor instance is typical of the genesis and immediate effect of a sale or merger, as applied to an issue selling for less than liquidating value. (The later developments, however, were quite unusual.) The heavy losses of White Motor in 1930–1932 impelled the management to seek a new alignment. Studebaker Corporation believed it could combine its own operations with those of White to mutual advantage, and it was greatly attracted by White's large holdings of cash. Hence in September 1932 Studebaker offered to purchase all White Motor's stock, paying for each share as follows:
$5 in cash.
$25 in 10-year 6% notes of Studebaker Corporation.
1 share of Studebaker common, selling for about $10.
It will be seen that these terms of purchase were based not on the recent market price of White—below $7 per share—but primarily upon the current-asset value. White Motor shares promptly advanced to 27 and later sold at the equivalent of 31 1/2.⁴
An interesting example of the same kind, but of more recent date, is afforded by Standard Oil Company of Nebraska. The facts may be outlined as follows:
Early in 1939 the stock was selling at about $6, representing a total valuation of $1,000,000 for 161,000 shares comprising the entire capitalization. The December 31, 1938, balance sheet is summarized in the appended table.

该公司在内布拉斯加州从事石油产品分销业务。每年业务规模约5,000,000美元，但几乎没有利润。1935-1938年间，报告中的折旧前收益平均为每股0.69美元；扣除“已使用的折旧”后，平均收益为每股0.39美元；按公司计算的折旧后，平均亏损为每股0.39美元。

<!--en-->
The company was engaged in the distribution of petroleum products in Nebraska. It was carrying on an annual business of some $5,000,000 without appreciable profit. For the years 1935–1938 the reported earnings before depreciation averaged $0.69 per share; after “expended depreciation” there was an average profit of $0.39 per share; and after depreciation as taken by the company there was an average loss of $0.39 per share.

这家公司显然的售价远低于清算价值，原因是其盈利记录不佳。不过，有充分理由认为，该公司的实际价值远高于单纯的清算价值，因为其提供的汽油等销售渠道，使得其众多的零售和批发加油站会成为某家大型炼油公司的理想收购目标。

<!--en-->
Here was a company clearly selling for much less than liquidating value, the reason being its unsatisfactory earnings record. There was good reason to believe, however, that the company was really worth more than bare liquidating value, because the outlet it provided for gasoline, etc., would make its numerous retail and bulk stations a desirable acquisition for some large refining company.

1939年4月，私人机构提出以每股12美元的价格，收购66 2/3%的未发行股票。该出价未能获得足够多数人的接受，但紧接着，印第安纳标准石油公司提出了每股17.50美元的报价——该公司此前一直为内布拉斯加标准石油公司提供汽油，显然不希望失去这个重要销售渠道。这笔交易很快得到批准；因此，在内布拉斯加标准石油公司的股票价值在四个月的时间里几乎翻了三倍，而此时整体市场正处于下跌趋势。⁵ *完全清算*。莫霍克矿业公司就是一个很好的例子，说明通过企业的完全清算，可以带来相当于大幅提升市场价值的现金收益。

<!--en-->
In April 1939 private interests offered to pay $12 per share for $66 2/3\%$ of the outstanding stock. This bid failed of acceptance by a sufficient majority, but it was followed immediately by an offer to pay $17.50 per share, made by Standard Oil Company of Indiana, the refiner that had been supplying Standard Oil Company of Nebraska with its gasoline and that evidently was loath to lose this important outlet. The deal was promptly ratified; hence the stock ofStandard Oil Company of Nebraska nearly tripled in value during a four-month's period in which the general market had suffered a decline.⁵
*Complete Liquidation.* Mohawk Mining Company supplies an excellent example of a cash profit equivalent to a large advance in market value caused by the actual liquidation of the enterprise.

1931年12月，该股票售价为每股11美元，112,000股已发行股份的总估值为1,230,000美元。1931年底的资产负债表显示如下：

<!--en-->
In December 1931 the stock sold at $11 per share, representing a total valuation of $1,230,000 for the 112,000 shares outstanding. The balance sheet at the end of 1931 showed the following:

* 在将证券和铜库存降至市场价值后，不久管理层决定清算资产。在1932年至1934年期间，公司定期发放并清算股息，每股总计为28.50美元。需要注意的是，清算时实际收到的金额与清算开始前的资产价值相同，仅为当时市场价格的2½倍。*部分清算*。已讨论过的北方管道公司和奥蒂斯公司就是通过部分清算实现更高市场价值的例子。这两家公司的情况如下表所示：1929年9月，奥蒂斯公司发放了每股4美元的特别股息；1930年，它通过部分清算分配了20美元，使面值从100美元降至80美元。1931年4月，股票售价为45美元；1932年4月，售价为41美元。尽管在此期间每股分配了24美元，且*整体*市场水平已从疯狂通胀转变为同样疯狂的通缩，这些价格仍高于1929年6月的报价。后来，该公司彻底倒闭，向股东额外支付了每股74美元作为清算款——因此自1929年6月以来（包括1929-1934年其他股息，每股4美元），股东总共收到102美元。⁶

<!--en-->
* After reducing securities and copper inventory to market value.
Shortly thereafter the management decided to liquidate the property. Within the years 1932–1934 regular and liquidating dividends were paid, aggregating $28.50 per share. It will be noted that the amount actually received in liquidation proved identical with the current-asset value just before the liquidation began, and it was $2\frac{1}{2}$ times the ruling market price at that time.
*Partial Liquidation.* Northern Pipe Line Company and Otis Company, already discussed, are examples of the establishment of a higher market value through partialliquidation. The two companies made the exhibits as shown in the table following.
In September 1929 Otis Company paid a special dividend of $4 per share, and in 1930 it made a distribution of $20 in partial liquidation, reducing the par value from $100 to $80. In April 1931 the shares sold at 45 and in April 1932 at 41. These prices were higher than the quotation in June 1929, despite the distributions of $24 per share made in the interim, and despite the fact also that the *general* market level had changed from fantastic inflation to equally fantastic deflation. Later the company went out of business altogether and paid its stockholders an additional $74 per share in liquidation—making the total received by them $102 per share since June 1929 (inclusive of other dividends in 1929–1934 amounting to $4 per share).⁶

1928年，北方管道公司向股东分配了每股50美元，作为资本回报，即部分清算。这一举措导致1926年至1928年间市场价格大约翻了一番。后来又进行了第二次分配，每股20美元，使股东获得的现金比1925年和1926年的低市场价格更高，同时他们仍保留对管道业务的全部权益。所谓标准石油集团中的大多数管道公司也进行了类似的慷慨分配。（注意第44章注释5中描述的戴维斯煤炭与焦炭公司的部分清算情况。）

<!--en-->
Northern Pipe Line Company distributed $50 per share to its stockholders in 1928, as a return of capital, *i.e.*, partial liquidation. This development resulted in an approximate doubling of the market price between 1926 and 1928. Later a second distribution of $20 per share was made, so that the stockholders received more in cash than in the low market price of 1925 and 1926, and they also retained their full interest in the pipe-line business. Similar liberal distributions were made by most of the pipe-line companies of the so-called Standard Oil group. (Note also the partial liquidation of Davis Coal and Coke Company, described in Chap. 44 Note 5.)

**选择此类股票时需要进行辨别。**几乎没有任何疑问，售价远低于清算价值的普通股总体上属于被低估的证券。它们的价格下跌程度超过了实际情况所显示的。这意味着*总体上*这些股票提供了值得购买的盈利机会。然而，证券分析师在选择这类股票时应尽可能进行辨别。他会倾向于那些他认为上述有利发展态势较为临近的股票。或者，他会对那些除了资产状况之外还显示出其他吸引人的统计特征的股票感兴趣，例如令人满意的当前收益和股息，或过去的高平均盈利能力。分析师会避免选择那些当前资产正在快速减少且没有明确停止迹象的股票。

<!--en-->
**Discrimination Required in Selecting Such Issues.** There is scarcely any doubt that common stocks selling well below liquidating value represent on the whole a class of undervalued securities. They have declined in price more severely than the actual conditions justify. This must meanthat *on the whole* these stocks afford profitable opportunities for purchase. Nevertheless, the securities analyst should exercise as much discrimination as possible in the choice of issues falling within this category. He will lean toward those for which he sees a fairly imminent prospect of some one of the favorable developments listed above. Or else he will be partial to such as reveal other attractive statistical features besides their liquid-asset position, e.g., satisfactory current earnings and dividends or a high average earning power in the past. The analyst will avoid issues that have been losing their current assets at a rapid rate and show no definite signs of ceasing to do so.

*示例：*后一点将通过以下两家公司在1933年初以远低于清算价值的价格出售股票的情况来说明。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* This latter point will be illustrated by the following comparison of two companies, the shares of which sold well below liquidating value early in 1933.

这两家公司都披露了1932年底流动资产与市价之间的有趣关系。但与三年前的资产负债表情况相比，Manhattan Shirt的情况更为令人满意。后者在经济萧条期间失去了超过一半的现金资产和超过60%的净流动资产。另一方面，Manhattan Shirt的普通股流动资产价值在这段艰难时期仅减少了10%，且现金资产状况得到了显著改善。这一结果是通过清理应收款项和存货获得的，所得款项用于偿还1929年的银行贷款，并大幅增加了现金资源。

<!--en-->
Both of these companies disclose an interesting relationship of current assets to market price at the close of 1932. But a comparison with the balance-sheet situation of three years previously will yield much more satisfactoryindications for Manhattan Shirt than for Hupp Motors. The latter concern had lost more than half of its cash assets and more than 60% of its net current assets during the depression period. On the other hand, the current-asset value of Manhattan Shirt common was reduced by only 10% during these difficult times, and furthermore, its cash-asset position was greatly improved. The latter result was obtained through the liquidation of receivables and inventories, the proceeds of which paid off the 1929 bank loans and largely increased the cash resources.

因此，从过去的数据来看，这两家公司应被归为不同类别。在Hupp Motors案例中，我们必须考虑流动资产超过市价的部分可能很快会消耗掉。但对于Manhattan Shirt来说并非如此，实际上，该公司在经济萧条期间加强现金状况的表现应得到重视。我们稍后会回到安全分析的这一阶段，即比较不同时间段的资产负债表，以确定企业的真实发展情况。前一点——即也应关注过去的盈利记录——可以通过对1939年初两家公司的简要比较来体现。

<!--en-->
From the viewpoint of past indications, therefore, the two companies must be placed in different categories. In the Hupp Motors case, we should have to take into account the possibility that the remaining excess of current assets over market price might soon be dissipated. This is not true so far as Manhattan Shirt is concerned, and in fact the achievement of the company in strengthening its cash position during the depression must be given favorable consideration. We shall recur later to this phase of security analysis, *viz.*, the comparison of balance sheets over a period in order to determine the true progress of an enterprise. The former point —that attention should be paid also to the past earnings record —may be brought home by a brief comparison of two companies in early 1939.
