除交通和地理差异（例如Pocahontas软煤运输船）外，铁路应被视为高度同质的群体。大型轻工、热力及电力企业也是如此。在工业领域，同质群体的最佳例子是原材料和其他标准化产品的生产商，其中商标名称是次要因素。这包括糖、煤炭、金属、钢铁产品、水泥、棉布等的生产商。大型石油公司可视为相当同质；小型企业不适合比较，因为它们面临生产、储量及相对价格突然重大变化的影响。大型烘焙、乳制品和包装企业属于相当同质的群体。与同一子组中的其他单位（如杂货店、五分店、餐厅等）相比，大型连锁商店企业也是如此。百货商店的同类企业较少同质，但这一领域的比较并非毫无依据。

<!--en-->
With certain exceptions for traffic and geographical variations, e.g., in particular, the Pocahontas soft-coal carriers, the railroads must be considered a highly homogeneous group. The same is true of the larger light, heat and power utilities. Inthe industrial field the best examples of homogeneous groups are afforded by the producers of raw materials and of other standardized products in which the trade name is a minor factor. These would include producers of sugar, coal, metals, steel products, cement, cotton print cloths, etc. The larger oil companies may be considered as fairly homogeneous; the smaller concerns are not well suited to comparison because they are subject to sudden important changes in production, reserves and relative price received. The larger baking, dairy and packing companies fall into fairly homogeneous groups. The same is true of the larger chain-store enterprises when compared with other units in the same subgroups, e.g., grocery, five-and-ten-cent, restaurant, etc. Department stores are less homogeneous, but comparisons in this field are by no means far-fetched.

以广告商标销售制造品的厂商通常应被视为异质群体。在这些领域，一家企业常常以竞争对手为代价繁荣发展，因此行业内的企业不会同步发展或衰退。例如，汽车制造商的相对地位一直存在持续且明显的变化。各类机械和设备生产商也面临类似条件。制药企业也是如此。从这一角度来看，轮胎、烟草产品、鞋类等大型制造商处于中间位置，其相对地位变化并不频繁。² 分析师在处理异质群体中的公司时，必须从统计数据中得出比较结论时格外谨慎。无疑，在这些领域，应优先选择那些定量表现最好的公司（除非被已知的定性因素抵消）——因为这种选择依据似乎比其他任何依据都更可靠——但分析师和投资者必须充分意识到，这种优势可能短暂。一般来说，群体越不同质，在比较时必须更加关注定性因素。

<!--en-->
Makers of manufactured goods sold under advertised trade-marks must generally be regarded as belonging to heterogeneous groups. In these fields one concern frequently prospers at the expense of its competitors, so that the units in the industry do not improve or decline together. Among automobile manufactures, for example, there have been continuous and pronounced variations in relative standing. Producers of all the various classes of machinery and equipment are subject to somewhat the same conditions. This is true also of the proprietary drug manufacturers. Intermediate positions from this point of view are occupied by such groups as the larger makers of tires, of tobacco products, of shoes, wherein changes of relative position are not so frequent.²
The analyst must be most cautious about drawing comparative conclusions from the statistical data when dealing with companies in a heterogeneous group. No doubt preference may properly be accorded in these fields to the companies making the best quantitative showing (if not offset by known qualitative factors)—for this basis of selection would seem sounder than any other—but the analyst and the investor should be fully aware that such superiority may prove evanescent. As a general rule, the less homogeneous the groupthe more attention must be paid to the qualitative factors in making comparisons.

**关于比较分析价值的更多一般限制。** 我们再次提醒学生：不要被比较表的数学精确性所迷惑，认为其结论同样准确。我们已经提到需要考虑定性因素和异质性问题。但除此之外，我们还详细介绍了第一章中提到的分析师成功的所有各种障碍。比较分析技术可能减少一些风险，但永远无法使其免受未来变化、股市本身的顽固性，或自己无法掌握所有重要事实的必然后果的影响——这些往往是不可避免的。他必须预期经常出错，偶尔也会犯错；但凭借智慧与谨慎，他的工作应能取得比典型股票买家猜测或肤浅判断更好的整体结果。[^3207]: ¹ 有关术语和本讨论中提到的关键测试的解释，请参阅前几章。² 当然，确实会发生显著变化。例如，在提到的三个领域，Philip Morris相对于其大型竞争对手实现了惊人增长，General Shoe的发展则稍显平淡，Lee Tire的比较表现异常突出。这三家都是相对较小的企业。第50章

<!--en-->
**More General Limitations on the Value of Comparative Analysis.** It may be well once again to caution the student against being deluded by the mathematical exactitude of his comparative tables into believing that their indicated conclusions are equally exact. We have mentioned the need of considering qualitative factors and of allowing for lack of homogeneity. But beyond these points lie all the various obstacles to the success of the analyst that we presented in some detail in our first chapter. The technique of comparative analysis may lessen some of the hazards of his work, but it can never exempt him from the vicissitudes of the future or the stubbornness of the stock market itself or the consequences of his own failure—often unavoidable—to learn all the important facts. He must expect to appear wrong often and to be wrong on occasion; but with intelligence and prudence his work should yield better over-all results than the guesses or the superficial judgments of the typical stock buyer.
[^3207]: ¹ Reference is made to earlier chapters for explanation of the terminology and the critical tests referred to in this discussion.
² But significant changes do occur, of course. Note, for example, the phenomenal growth of Philip Morris, relative to its large competitors, the somewhat less spectacular development of General Shoe and the exceptional comparative showing of Lee Tire, in the three fields mentioned. All three of these were relatively small enterprises.
CHAPTER 50

### 价格与价值之间的差异

<!--en-->
*Discrepancies Between Price and Value*

我们对安全分析技术的阐述中包含了许多估值过高或过低的例子。显然，证券市场做出评估的过程往往不合逻辑且存在错误。正如我们在第一章所指出的，这些过程并非自动或机械的，而是心理性的，因为它们发生在购买或出售的人的头脑中。因此，市场的错误实际上是群体或大量个人的错误。大多数错误可以归因于三个基本原因之一或多个：夸大、过度简化或忽视。

<!--en-->
OUR EXPOSITION of the technique of security analysis has included many different examples of overvaluation and undervaluation. Evidently the processes by which the securities market arrives at its appraisals are frequently illogical and erroneous. These processes, as we pointed out in our first chapter, are not automatic or mechanical but psychological, for they go on in the minds of people who buy or sell. The mistakes of the market are thus the mistakes of groups or masses of individuals. Most of them can be traced to one or more of three basic causes: exaggeration, oversimplification or neglect.

在本章及下一章中，我们将尝试对证券市场的各种异常现象进行简洁回顾。我们将从分析师实际工作的角度来探讨这一主题，试图确定每种情况在多大程度上为分析师提供了有利行动的机会。这种研究将是对我们关于安全分析范围与限制的早期章节的补充，会引用后续讨论中发展的材料，并会提及一些参考文献。

<!--en-->
In this chapter and the next we shall attempt a concise review of the various aberrations of the securities market. We shall approach the subject from the standpoint of the practical activities of the analyst, seeking in each case to determine the extent to which it offers an opportunity for profitable action on his part. This inquiry will thus constitute an amplification of our early chapter on the scope and limitations of security analysis, drawing upon the material developed in the succeeding discussions, to which a number of references will be made.

**分析师的一般程序**。由于我们已经强调，分析只有在特殊情况下才能得出积极结论，因此必须检查许多证券，才能找到对分析师有实际潜力的证券。他通过什么实际方法来进行发现？主要是通过艰苦而系统的工作。他可以遵循两种主要方法。第一种是按照前一章所述，由行业集团进行一系列比较分析。这样的研究能让他大致了解每个群体的标准或常见特征，并指出那些与模式明显偏离的公司。例如，如果他发现某只钢铁普通股的市场价格约为整个行业的两倍，他就有了研究方向——或者更确切地说，他有了一个建议，需要通过对与该企业相关的所有重要质量和数量因素进行彻底调查来继续探索。

<!--en-->
**General Procedure of the Analyst.** Since we have emphasized that analysis will lead to a positive conclusion only in the exceptional case, it follows that many securities must be examined before one is found that has real possibilities for the analyst. By what practical means does he proceed to make his discoveries? Mainly by hard andsystematic work. There are two broad methods that he may follow. The first consists of a series of comparative analyses by industrial groups along the lines described in the previous chapter. Such studies will give him a fair idea of the standard or usual characteristics of each group and also point out those companies which deviate widely from the modal exhibit. If, for example, he discovers that a certain steel common stock has been earning about twice as much on its market price as the industry as a whole, he has a clue to work on—or rather a suggestion to be pursued by dint of a thoroughgoing investigation of all the important qualitative and quantitative factors relating to the enterprise.

同样类型的系统式调查也可以应用于债券和优先股领域。可以通过对由十家主要运输公司发行的类似等级债券进行比较分析，来最好地探索破产铁路债券的范围。或者，大量公用事业优先股可以根据以下标准进行分类：(1) 总体股息和利息覆盖率；(2) 股票价值比率；(3) 价格和收益率。这种简单的分组可能表明有些发行物要么有良好保障且回报高于平均水平，要么由于统计保护不足而明显定价过高。等等。

<!--en-->
The same type of methodical inquiry may be applied to the field of bonds and preferred stocks. The wide area of receivership railroad bonds can best be explored by means of a comparative analysis of the showing of the bonds of roughly the same rank issued by, say, a dozen of the major carriers in trusteeship. Or a large number of public-utility preferred stocks could be listed according to: (1) their over-all dividend and interest coverage, (2) their stock-value ratio and (3) their price and yield. Such a simple grouping might indicate a few issues that either were well secured and returned more than the average or else were clearly selling too high in view of their inadequate statistical protection. And so on.

第二种通用方法是在企业报告发布时仔细分析，并将其表现与债券或股票的市场价格联系起来。这些报告至少可以概括地出现在各种日报中；更全面的介绍可以在金融服务的每日公司报告表中找到，或每周在《商业与金融纪事》中看到。快速浏览一百份此类报告，可能会发现五到十份从收益或资产现状来看足够值得进一步研究的报告。

<!--en-->
The second general method consists in scrutinizing corporate reports as they make their appearance and relating their showing to the market price of their bonds or stocks. These reports can be seen—in summary form, at least—in various daily papers; a more comprehensive presentation can be found in the daily corporation-report sheets of the financial services or weekly in the *Commercial and Financial Chronicle*. A quick glance at a hundred of such reports may reveal between five and ten that look interesting enough from the earnings or current-asset standpoint to warrant more intensive study.

**能否利用价格的周期性波动？** 最明显的价格与价值差异是伴随市场周期性大波动（繁荣与萧条）出现的差异。在牛市中股票定价过高，在熊市中定价过低，这只是一个显而易见的事实。因为从根本上说，这相当于说价格的任何上涨或下跌最终都会达到一个极限，由于价格不会长期停留在这些极限（或其他水平），回顾起来会发现价格已经上升或下降得太远了。

<!--en-->
**Can Cyclical Swings of Prices Be Exploited?** The best understood disparities between price and value are those which accompany the recurrent broad swings of the market through boom and depression. It is a mere truism that stockssell too high in a bull market and too low in a bear market. For at bottom this is simply equivalent to saying that any upward or downward movement of prices must finally reach a limit, and since prices do not remain at such limits (or at any other level) permanently, it must turn out in retrospect that prices will have advanced or declined too far.

分析师能否成功利用市场的反复夸大行为？经验表明，以下类似的程序应该相当令人满意：

<!--en-->
Can the analyst exploit successfully the repeated exaggerations of the general market? Experience suggests that a procedure somewhat like the following should turn out to be reasonably satisfactory:

1. 选择一份多样化的领先普通股清单，例如“道琼斯工业指数”中的股票。
2. 通过将平均收益乘以合适的倍数，确定该群体的所谓“正常”值。该倍数可以相当于将收益按当前最高等级工业债券利率的两倍进行资本化。平均收益的时间通常为期七到十年，但如1931–1933年那样的特殊情况可能需要采用不同的方法，例如以1934年开始的时间段作为平均基础，即1939年或之后开始运营的情况。
3. 当股票能以远低于正常价值的折扣价格购买时，可对该清单中的股票进行组合购买，比如以$2/3$这样的价值。或者，购买规模可以较小，比如从正常价值的80%开始。
4. 当价格大幅高于正常价值时，例如$1/3$以上，或按规模比例从20%到50%更高时，应出售这些购买的股票。这是罗杰·巴布森多年前制定的通用操作方案。在1925年之前，它取得了相当令人满意的结果。但是——正如我们在第37章中指出的——在1921–1933年的周期中（从低点到低点衡量），需要于1921年进行购买，可能于1926年出售，因此需要在1927–1929年的大繁荣期间完全避免市场参与，并在1931年重新购买，随后市场价值会严重下降。这种计划对人的毅力要求过高。自1933年以来市场的表现使得应用这些机械公式——尤其是确定用于计算正常值的正常收益——变得困难。几乎无法期望如此基本简单的方案能在捕捉市场波动方面达到高度准确性。但对于理解其固有限制的人来说，它仍可能有很大实用价值，因为至少平均而言，它可能导致以具有内在吸引力的水平进行购买——这在普通股投资中至关重要。

<!--en-->
1. Select a diversified list of leading common stocks, e.g., those in the “Dow-Jones Industrial Average.”
2. Determine an indicated “normal” value for this group by applying a suitable multiplier to average earnings. The multiplier might be equivalent to capitalizing the earnings at, say, twice the current interest rate on highest grade industrial bonds. The period for averaging earnings would ordinarily be seven to ten years, but exceptional conditions such as occurred in 1931–1933 might suggest a different method, e.g., basing the average on the period beginning in 1934, when operating in 1939 or later.
3. Make composite purchases of the list when the shares can be bought at a substantial discount from normal value, say, at $2/3$ such value. Or purchases may be made on a scale downwards, beginning say, at 80% of normal value.
4. Sell out such purchases when a price is reached substantially above normal value, say, $1/3$ higher, or from 20% to 50% higher on a scale basis.
This was the general scheme of operations developed by Roger Babson many years ago. It yielded quite satisfactory results prior to 1925. But—as we pointed out in Chap. 37—during the 1921–1933 cycle (measuring from low point to low point) it would have called for purchasing during 1921, selling out probably in 1926, thus requiring complete abstinence from the market during the great boom of 1927–1929, and repurchasing in 1931, to be followed by a severe shrinkage inmarket values. A program of this character would have made far too heavy demands upon human fortitude.
The behavior of the market since 1933 has offered difficulties of a different sort in applying these mechanical formulas—particularly in determining normal earnings from which to compute normal values. It is scarcely to be expected that an idea as basically simple as this one can be utilized with any high degree of accuracy in catching the broad market swings. But for those who realize its inherent limitations it may have considerable utility, for at least it is likely on the average to result in purchases at intrinsically attractive levels —which is more than half the battle in common-stock investment.

### “捕捉波动”基于保证金操作不可行。

<!--en-->
*“Catching the Swings” on a Marginal Basis Impracticable.*

从普通投机者的角度来看，涉及保证金购买和卖空，这种方法必须被视为不可行。直接持有者可以承受过早购买和过早出售。实际上，他必须预期同时做这两件事，并看到购买后市场进一步下跌，出售后进一步上涨。但保证金交易者必须关注即时结果；他随波逐流，希望准确判断潮水转向的时机，并在即将改变方向时立即调整操作。他很少成功，因此典型的经验是短暂的成功最终导致彻底失败。投机者的本质在于，他购买是因为认为股票会上涨，而不是因为价格便宜；相反，他出售也是基于这一原因。因此，投机者和证券分析师之间存在根本的观点分歧，这强烈反对他们之间建立持久满意的合作关系。

<!--en-->
From the ordinary speculative standpoint, involving purchases on margin and short sales, this method of operation must be set down as impracticable. The outright owner can afford to buy too soon and to sell too soon. In fact he must expect to do both and to see the market decline farther after he buys and advance farther after he sells out. But the margin trader is necessarily concerned with immediate results; he swims with the tide, hoping to gage the exact moment when the tide will turn and to reverse his stroke the moment before. In this he rarely succeeds, so that his typical experience is temporary success ending in complete disaster. It is the essential character of the speculator that he buys because he thinks stocks are going up not because they are cheap, and conversely when he sells. Hence there is a fundamental cleavage of viewpoint between the speculator and the securities analyst, which militates strongly against any enduringly satisfactory association between them.

债券价格无疑会像股票一样通过周期波动，通常建议债券投资者在周期顶部附近出售资产，在底部附近重新购买。我们怀疑在典型情况下能否取得令人满意的结果。对于何时债券价格处于便宜或昂贵状态，与普通股收益比率测试相对应，没有明确的标准，操作主要需依靠一种似乎与“投资”相去甚远的市场走势判断技术。出售和重新购买之间的资金利息损失是一个重要的负面因素，我们认为净收益不足以承受投资者关注市场波动所固有的心理风险。

<!--en-->
Bond prices tend undoubtedly to swing through cycles in somewhat the same way as stocks, and it is frequently suggested that bond investors follow the policy of selling their holdings near the top of these cycles and repurchasing them near the bottom. We are doubtful if this can be done with satisfactory results in the typical case. There are no well-defined standards as to when high-grade bond prices are cheap or dear corresponding to the earnings-ratio test for commonstocks, and the operations have to be guided chiefly by a technique of gaging market moves that seems rather far removed from “investment.” The loss of interest on funds between the time of sale and repurchase is a strong debit factor, and in our opinion the net advantage is not sufficient to warrant incurring the psychological dangers that inhere in any placing of emphasis by the investor upon market movements.

### “次级”或小众股票的机会。

<!--en-->
*Opportunities in “Secondary” or Little-Known Issues.*

回到普通股票方面，虽然头部股票的高估或低估只会在股市周期的特定阶段出现，但大量“非代表性”或“次要”股票很可能始终存在低估的情况。当市场龙头股票价格低廉时，一些不太突出的普通股票价格可能会更低。例如，在1932-1933年，像Plymouth Cordage、Pepperell Manufacturing、American Laundry Machinery等股票，其售价相对于过去价格和当前财务数据来说低得令人难以置信。投资者是否应该以约50%的保守估值购买通用汽车这样优秀的股票，还是选择像Pepperell这样不太突出的股票，以约25%的估值，这或许取决于个人偏好。

<!--en-->
Returning to common stocks, although overvaluation or undervaluation of leading issues occurs only at certain points in the stock-market cycle, the large field of “nonrepresentative” or “secondary” issues is likely to yield instances of undervaluation at all times. When the market leaders are cheap, some of the less prominent common stocks are likely to be a good deal cheaper. During 1932–1933, for example, stocks such as Plymouth Cordage, Pepperell Manufacturing, American Laundry Machinery and many others, sold at unbelievably low prices in relation to their past records and current financial exhibits. It is probably a matter for individual preference whether the investor should purchase an outstanding issue like General Motors at about 50% of its conservative valuation or a less prominent stock like Pepperell at about 25% of such value.

*领导的不可持续性*。市场领导者群体的构成每年都有很大差异，尤其是考虑到最近人们的关注点从过去的表现转向了预期前景。如果我们查看1937-1938年经济衰退期间的名单，会发现许多曾经表现突出的股票，其售价相对于统计数据显示的水平来说异常低。

<!--en-->
*The Impermanence of Leadership.* The composition of the market-leader group has varied greatly from year to year, especially in view of the recent shift of attention from past performance to assumed prospects. If we examine the list during the decline of 1937–1938, we shall find quite a number of once outstanding issues that sold at surprisingly low prices in relation to their statistical exhibits.

1938年1月31日的资产负债表显示，现金资产为8500万，流动资产净额为1.34亿。在1938年的低价格水平下，优先股和普通股的总价值仅为1.26亿。这家公司正是美国商业史上最引人注目的成长案例之一——无疑它是美国乃至全球最大的零售企业，多年来一直保持稳定的盈利和分红记录——然而其售价却低于其流动资产净值。因此，在1938年，华尔街认为这家国家杰出企业作为持续经营企业的价值，甚至低于其被清算的价值。为什么？首先，因为连锁店税收的威胁；其次，因为近期盈利下降；第三，因为整体市场处于低迷状态。

<!--en-->
The balance sheet of January 31, 1938, showed cash assets of 85 millions and net current assets of 134 millions. At the 1938 low prices, the preferred and common together were selling for 126 millions. Here, then, was a company whose spectacular growth was one of the great romances of American business, a company that was without doubt the largest retail enterprise in America and perhaps in the world, that had an uninterrupted record of earnings and dividends for many years—and yet was selling for less than its net current assets alone. Thus one of the outstanding businesses of the country was considered by Wall Street in 1938 to be worth less as a going concern than if it were liquidated. Why? First, because of chain-store tax threats; second, because of a recent decline in earnings; and, third, because the general market was depressed.

我们认为，很难找到更能说明股市真实本质的例子：股市并非旨在准确评估企业，而是通过每日变化的股价来表达其喜好与厌恶、期望与恐惧。市场的运作中确实包含足够的理性与选择性判断，在大多数情况下，市场价格与可确定的内在价值会存在一定对应关系。正如第4章所指出的，当我们面对未来前景这样难以把握且非数学化的问题时，我们通常倾向于接受市场的结论，认为它比分析师的任何判断都更可靠。但在某些时候，由于市场情绪的影响，分析师会陷入超出合理判断范围的极端情况。

<!--en-->
We doubt that a better illustration can be found of the real nature of the stock market, which does not aim to evaluate businesses with any exactitude but rather to express its likes and dislikes, its hopes and fears, in the form of daily changing quotations. There is indeed enough sound sense and selective judgment in the market's activities to create on most occasions some degree of correspondence between market price and ascertainable or intrinsic value. In particular, as was pointed out in Chap. 4, when we are dealing with something as elusive and nonmathematical as the evaluation of future prospects, weare generally led to accept the market's verdict as better than anything that the analyst can arrive at. But, on enough occasions to keep the analyst busy, the emotions of the stock market carry it in either direction beyond the limits of sound judgment.

*Opportunities in Normal Markets.* During the intermediate period, when average prices show no definite signs of being either too low or too high, common stocks may usually be found that seem definitely undervalued on a statistical basis. These generally fall into two classes: (1) Those showing high current and average earnings in relation to market price and (2) those making a reasonably satisfactory exhibit of earnings and selling at a low price in relation to net-current-asset value. Obviously, such companies will not be large and well known, or else the trend of earnings will not have been encouraging. 勤奋的分析师很容易找到有趣的统计数据，如我们表格中展示的那样。但更困难的是判断定性因素是否足以支持定量结论——换句话说，投资者是否对公司的未来有足够信心，认为在看似低于正常水平的价格下购买股票是划算的。

<!--en-->
It is not difficult for the assiduous analyst to find interesting statistical exhibits such as those presented in our table. Much more difficult is the task of determining whether or not the qualitative factors will justify following the quantitative indications—in other words, whether or not the investor may have sufficient confidence in the company's future to consider its shares a real bargain at the apparently subnormal price.

关于这个问题，财务意见倾向于普遍悲观的结论。投资信托基金虽然拥有发现此类机会的设施，但很少关注它们——部分原因是因为它们难以以信托基金偏好的大数量进行买卖，也因为他们相信，无论一家次要公司的统计数据多么好，除非有具体的乐观理由，否则不太可能成为盈利的投资。

<!--en-->
On this question the weight of financial opinion appears inclined to a generally pessimistic conclusion. The investment trusts, with all their facilities for discovering opportunities of this type, have paid little attention to them—partly, it is true, because they are difficult to buy and sell in the large quantities that the trusts prefer, but also because of their conviction that however good the statistical exhibit of a secondary company may be it is not likely to prove a profitable purchase *unless there is specific ground for optimism regarding its future*.

典型小型公司的主要缺点是其容易突然且可能永久失去盈利能力。毫无疑问，这类不利情况在该群体中发生的比例高于大型企业。但与之相对的是，成功的小型公司可以比已非常庞大的公司更显著地提升价值。例如，Philip Morris, Inc.在1934年的市场价值为500万，到1939年增至9000万，净利润增长1200%，这在American Tobacco身上是难以想象的。同样，Pepsi-Cola的增长幅度远远超过Coca-Cola；General Shoe与International Shoe的情况也是如此。

<!--en-->
The main drawback of a typical smaller sized company is its vulnerability to a sudden and perhaps permanent loss of its earning power. Undoubtedly such adverse developments occur in a larger proportion of cases in this group than among the larger enterprises. As an offset to this we have the fact that thesuccessful small company can multiply its value far more impressively than those which are already of enormous size. For example, the growth of Philip Morris, Inc., in market value from 5 millions in 1934 to 90 millions in 1939, accompanying a 1,200% increase in net earnings, would have been quite inconceivable in the case of American Tobacco. Similarly, the growth of Pepsi-Cola has far outstripped in percentage that of Coca-Cola; the same is true of General Shoe vs. International Shoe; etc.

但大多数投资者会试图通过或多或少仔细分析未来可能性来寻找Philip Morris的机会，然后即使以相当高的价格购买股票——而不是将投资集中在只有普通前景的“便宜股票”组合中。我们的经验表明，我们更倾向于后一种方法，尽管无法保证在当前条件下能取得出色结果。然而，根据多年观察，似乎在平均警觉性和良好判断力指导下，对看似被低估普通股的投资可以取得相当不错的结果——同时要避免在整体市场水平过高时进行投资。这里给出两个较早的此类机会例子，让读者了解过去股市的情况。

<!--en-->
But most students will try to locate the potential Philip Morris opportunities, by gaging future possibilities with greater or less care, and will then buy their shares even at a fairly high price—rather than make their commitments in a diversified group of “bargain issues” with only ordinary prospects. Our own experience leads us to favor the latter technique, although we cannot guarantee brilliant results therefrom under present-day conditions. Yet judging from observations made over a number of years, it would seem that investment in apparently undervalued common stocks can be carried on with a very fair degree of over-all success, provided average alertness and good judgment are used in passing on the future-prospect question—and provided also that commitments are avoided at times when the general market is statistically much too high. Two older examples of this type of opportunity are given here, to afford the reader some notion of former stock markets.

1. 标准或领先股几乎总是迅速响应其报告利润的变化——以至于它们常常过度强调年度收益波动的重要性。
2. 不太熟悉的股票走势很大程度上取决于专业市场参与者对其的态度。如果缺乏兴趣，价格可能远远低于统计数据。如果专业投资者关注该股票，无论是通过操纵还是更合法的方式，都会得到相反的结果，价格会极快地响应公司业绩的变化。*非标准股行为的例子。*以下两个例子将说明非代表性普通股行为的多样性。*布特和苏必利尔铜（实际上是锌）公司普通股*

<!--en-->
* Earnings before contingency reserves were $40.95 per share.
In these cases the market price had failed to reflect adequately the indicated earning power.
**Market Behavior of Standard and Nonstandard Issues.** A close study of the market action of common stocks suggests the following further general observations:
1. Standard or leading issues almost always respond rapidly to changes in their reported profits—so much so that they tend regularly to exaggerate marketwise the significance of year-to-year fluctuations in earnings.
2. The action of the less familiar issues depends largely upon what attitude is taken towards them by professional market operators. If interest is lacking, the price may lag far behind the statistical showing. If interest is attracted to the issue, either manipulatively or more legitimately, the opposite result can readily be attained, and the price will respond in extreme fashion to changes in the company's exhibit.
*Examples of Behavior of Nonstandard Issues.* The following two examples will illustrate this diversity of behavior of nonrepresentative common stocks.
*Butte and Superior Copper (Actually Zinc) Company Common*

这些收益和股息极其巨大。即使考虑到这是因战争期间锌价上涨导致的，市场价格仍明显忽视了公司出色的表现。原因是缺乏普遍兴趣或市场支持。

<!--en-->
These were extraordinarily large earnings and dividends. Even allowing for the fact that they were due to wartime prices for zinc, the market price showed none the less a striking disregard of the company's spectacular exhibit. The reason was lack of general interest or of individual market sponsorship.

与以下Mullins Body（后来为Mullins Manufacturing）公司普通股的走势对比。

<!--en-->
Contrast the foregoing with the appended showing of the common stock of Mullins Body (later Mullins Manufacturing) Corporation.

在1924年至1926年间，我们观察到低价“次级”普通股发行时的典型市场波动。1927年初，股票在投机角度上无疑具有吸引力，价格约为10美元，因为与前三年相比价格较低。1927-1928年间利润显著但并未达到惊人水平，导致典型的股市炒作现象。价格从1927年的10美元升至1928年的95美元，又在1929年回落至10美元。

<!--en-->
Between 1924 and 1926 we note the characteristic market swings of a low-priced “secondary” common-stock issue. At the beginning of 1927 the shares were undoubtedly attractive, speculatively, at about 10, for the price was low in relation to the earnings of the three years previously. A substantial, but by no means spectacular, rise in profits during 1927–1928 resulted in a typical stock-market exploitation. The price advanced from 10 in 1927 to 95 in 1928 and fell back again to 10 in 1929.

另一种对比是1938-1939年飞机制造股的表现，与1915-1918年战争受益股的表现相比。以下两个例子将说明1938年和1939年市场价格与实际业绩之间的关系。

<!--en-->
A contrast of another kind is afforded by the behavior of the aircraft-manufacturing stocks in 1938–1939, as compared with that of war beneficiaries in 1915–1918. The two following examples will illustrate the relationship between market price in 1938 and 1939 and actual performance at the time.

在这些情况下，市场显然将战争订单尚未实现的利润作为未来收益的*永久*基础。1915–1916年Butte和Superior的市盈率与1938–1939年这些飞机制造商的市盈率对比非常明显。

<!--en-->
In these cases the market was evidently capitalizing the as yet unrealized profits from war orders as if they supplied a *permanent* basis of future earnings. The contrast between the Butte and Superior price-earnings ratio in 1915–1916 and that of these aircraft concerns in 1938–1939 is very striking.

*分析师面对此类情况的态度。* 分析师可以明智、公平地应对如Wright Aeronautical、Bangor and Aroostook、Firestone和Butte及Superior等公司在相关时期的情况。他甚至可以在1927年初对Mullins形成有价值的评价。但一旦这个问题落入市场操作者的手中，它就超出了分析判断的范围。对于华尔街来说，Mullins已不再是一个企业，而成了股票行情表上的符号。买入或卖出它同样危险；分析师可以警告这种风险，但他无法了解其涨跌的极限。（事实上，该公司于1928年发行了可转换优先股，使得进行有利的对冲操作成为可能，即购买优先股并出售普通股。）同样，对于1939年的飞机制造商股票，分析师只能指出将某种业务来源视为永久性的明显风险——全世界都必然希望这种业务本质上是暂时的。

<!--en-->
*Relationship of the Analyst to Such Situations.* The analyst can deal intelligently and fairly successfully with situations such as Wright Aeronautical, Bangor and Aroostook, Firestone and Butte and Superior at the periods referred to. He could even have formed a worth-while opinion about Mullins early in 1927. But once this issue fell into market operators' hands it passed beyond the pale of analytical judgment. As far as Wall Street was concerned, Mullins had ceased to be a business and had become a symbol on the ticker tape. To buy it or to sell it was equally hazardous; the analyst could warn of the hazard, but he could have no idea of the limits of its rise or fall. (As it happened, however, the company issued a convertible preferred stock in 1928 which made possible a profitable hedging operation, consisting of the purchase of the preferred and the sale of the common.) Similarly with the airplane issues in 1939, the analyst could go no further than to indicate the obvious hazard that lay in treating as permanent a source of business that the whole world must necessarily hope was essentially temporary.

当整体市场对分析师来说显得危险地高时，即使某些普通股看似便宜，他也不应推荐它们。整体市场的剧烈下跌会对所有股票价格产生不利影响，不太活跃的股票可能特别容易受到必要抛售的影响。

<!--en-->
When the general market appears dangerously high to the analyst, he must be hesitant about recommending unfamiliar common stocks, even though they may seem to be of the bargain type. A severe decline in the general market will affect all stock prices adversely, and the less active issues may prove especially vulnerable to the effects of necessitous selling.

**因收益变化之外的因素导致的市场夸大：*股息变化。*** 股市长期倾向于夸大收益变化之外其他因素。人们过度关注股息变化、股票分割、合并和分离等问题。现金股息增加是积极趋势，但仅仅因为股息率从每年5美元增加到6美元，就给股票价格增加20美元，这是荒谬的。以更高价格购买的投资者正在提前支付他在新利率下*未来20年内*将收到的所有额外股息。对股票股息经常做出的兴奋反应更不逻辑，因为它们本质上只是几张纸而已。股票分割也是如此，它创造了更多股份，但股东并没有获得之前没有的东西——除了由于价格较低而可能获得更广泛的市场优势这一小好处。¹ *合并和分离。* 华尔街对合并很容易兴奋，对分离则同样热情，这两种情况完全相反。把两加两往往会在股市中得到五，而这五后来可能被分割成三和三。对合并后结果进行的这类归纳研究似乎对合并作为增强盈利能力手段的有效性提出了重大质疑。² 还有理由认为，企业管理中的个人因素常常阻碍真正有利的合并，而那些完成的合并有时是由于控制不利条件的人掌握了知识。

<!--en-->
**Market Exaggerations Due to Factors Other than Changes in Earnings: *Dividend Changes.*** The inveterate tendency of the stock market to exaggerate extends to factors other than changes in earnings. Overemphasis is laid upon such matters as dividend changes, stock split-ups, mergers and segregations. An increase in the cash dividend is a favorable development, but it is absurd to add $20 to the price of a stock just because the dividend rate is advanced from $5 to $6 annually. The buyer at the higher price is paying out in advance all the additional dividends that he will receive at the new rate *over the next 20 years*. The excited responses often made to stock dividends are even more illogical, since they are in essence nothing more than pieces of paper. The same is true of split-ups, which create more shares but give the stockholdernothing he did not have before—except the minor advantage of a possibly broader market due to the lower price level.¹
*Mergers and Segregations.* Wall Street becomes easily enthusiastic over mergers and just as ebullient over segregations, which are the exact opposite. Putting two and two together frequently produces five in the stock market, and this five may later be split up into three and three. Such inductive studies as have been made of the results following mergers seem to cast considerable doubt upon the efficacy of consolidation as an aid to earning power.² There is also reason to believe that the personal element in corporate management often stands in the way of really advantageous consolidations and that those which are consummated are due sometimes to knowledge by those in control of unfavorable conditions ahead.

股市对看似相对不重要的发展做出夸张反应，可以用投机者的心理来解释。他首先想要“行动”；如果他能得到任何推动看涨情绪的借口，他愿意为此做出贡献。（无论是出于虚伪还是自我欺骗，经纪公司客户通常拒绝承认他们只是在赌博股票行情，坚持他们的购买有某种所谓的“理由”。）股票股息和其他此类“有利发展”提供了所需的借口，专业市场操作者利用这些借口，有时还得到企业高管的纵容。如果不是如此恶劣，这一切都会显得幼稚。证券分析师应该理解华尔街这些荒谬现象是如何产生的，但他最好避免与它们有任何接触。

<!--en-->
The exaggerated response made by the stock market to developments that seem relatively unimportant in themselves is readily explained in terms of the psychology of the speculator. He wants “action,” first of all; and he is willing to contribute to this action if he can be given any pretext for bullish excitement. (Whether through hypocrisy or self-deception, brokerage-house customers generally refuse to admit they are merely gambling with ticker quotations and insist upon some ostensible “reason” for their purchases.) Stock dividends and other “favorable developments” of this character supply the desired pretexts, and they have been exploited by the professional market operators, sometimes with the connivance of the corporate officials. The whole thing would be childish if it were not so vicious. The securities analyst should understand how these absurdities of Wall Street come into being, but he would do well to avoid any form of contact with them.

*诉讼问题。* 华尔街倾向于走向极端的一个表现，就是他们极度厌恶诉讼。任何重大诉讼都会对受影响的证券造成负面影响，其下跌程度可能与案件实质无关。这类发展可能为分析师提供实际机会，尽管它们属于专业领域。最重要的方面是接管问题。由于由此导致的低估几乎总是局限于债券发行，我们将在本章后面与高级证券相关地讨论这一主题。

<!--en-->
*Litigation.* The tendency of Wall Street to go to extremes is illustrated in the opposite direction by its tremendous dislike of litigation. A lawsuit of any significance casts a damper on the securities affected, and the extent of the decline may be out of all proportion to the merits of the case. Developments of this kind may offer real opportunities to the analyst, thoughof course they are of a specialized nature. The aspect of broadest importance is that of receivership. Since the undervaluations resulting therefrom are almost always confined to bond issues, we shall discuss this subject later in the chapter in connection with senior securities.

*例子：* 诉讼对普通股价值影响的一个显著例子是Reading公司案。1913年，美国政府提起诉讼，要求分离该公司的铁路和煤炭资产。股市有自己的判断标准，认为这一举措是对Reading公司的危险攻击，尽管实际上分离通常被视为“利好”。后来（1921年）达成了一项协议：煤炭子公司股票实际上将按比例分配给Reading公司的普通股和优先股股东。这被视为积极进展，但实际上这是政府对公司的胜利。

<!--en-->
*Example:* A rather striking example of the effect of litigation on common-stock values is afforded by the Reading Company case. In 1913 the United States government brought suit to compel separation of the company's railroad and coal properties. The stock market, having its own ideas of consistency, considered this move as a dangerous attack on Reading, despite the fact that the segregation would in itself ordinarily be considered as “bullish.” A plan was later agreed upon (in 1921) under which the coal subsidiary's stock was in effect to be distributed pro rata among the Reading Company's common and preferred shareholders. This was hailed in turn as a favorable development, although in fact it constituted a victory for the government against the company.

然而，一些普通股股东反对优先股参与煤炭公司的“权利”分配。有人提起诉讼，试图将这些权利限制在普通股范围内。有趣的是，但也在意料之中，这一举措导致Reading普通股价格下跌。从逻辑上讲，普通股应该上涨，因为如果诉讼成功，次级股的价值会更高；如果失败（实际情况也如此），其价值也不会降低。但股市仅认为这是新的诉讼，因此应“不予考虑”。

<!--en-->
Some common stockholders, however, objected to the participation of the preferred stock in the coal company “rights.” Suit was brought to restrict these rights to the common stock. Amusingly, but not surprisingly, the effect of this move was to depress the price of Reading common. In logic, the common should have advanced, since, if the suit were successful, there would be more value for the junior shares, and, if it failed (as it did), there would be no less value than before. But the stock market reasoned merely that here was some new litigation and hence Reading common should be “let alone.”

涉及诉讼的情况常常让分析师能够利用定量分析方法，与一般证券持有人的定性态度形成对比。假设一家破产企业的资产已转化为现金，可供债券持有人分配的金额约为净资产的50%。但存在另一方的诉讼，试图收回这笔钱的大部分。这种诉讼可能非常牵强，甚至荒谬；也可能已在较低层级法院被驳回，甚至在上诉也被驳回，现在只有极小的机会能由美国最高法院审理。尽管如此，仅此诉讼的待处理状态就会严重降低债券的市场价值。在上述条件下，债券价格可能降至每美元35美分而非50美分。这里的异常之处在于，一个原告认为几乎没有实际价值的遥远索赔，在市场上相当于被告的重大责任。因此，我们看到了数学上可证明的低估情况，把这些作为一类，它们非常适合被证券分析师利用。

<!--en-->
Situations involving litigation frequently permit the analyst to pursue to advantage his quantitative approach in contrast with the qualitative attitude of security holders in general. Assume that the assets of a bankrupt concern have been turned into cash and there is available for distribution to its bondholders the sum of, say, 50% net. But there is a suit pending, brought by others, to collect a good part of this money. It may be that the action is so far-fetched as to be almost absurd; it may be that it has been defeated in the lower courts, and even on appeal, and that it has now but amicroscopic chance to be heard by the United States Supreme Court. Nevertheless, the mere pendency of this litigation will severely reduce the market value of the bonds. Under the conditions named, they are likely to sell as low as 35 instead of 50 cents on the dollar. The anomaly here is that a remote claim, which the plaintiff can regard as having scarcely any real value to him, is made the equivalent in the market to a heavy liability on the part of the defendant. We thus have a mathematically demonstrable case of undervaluations, and, taking these as a class, they lend themselves exceedingly well to exploitation by the securities analyst.

*示例：* Island Oil and Transport 8%债券。1933年6月，这些债券以18的价格出售。发行时，接收方持有约45%的现金储备，从中可扣除部分费用和补贴，表明债券的净分配余额约为30。由于多次败诉的损害赔偿诉讼，分配被推迟，现在即将进入最终裁决阶段。该诉讼对债券的市场价值产生了与其实质无关的不利影响，这一点可以从诉讼本可以通过支付相对较小的金额解决这一事实中看出。在高级法院最终维持先前的判决后，债券持有人于1934年4月获得了每1000美元分配290美元的分配额。还预计会有少量额外分配。³ 1938年，当United Shipyards Corporation将其资产出售给Bethlehem Steel Company后，其股票也出现了类似情况。反对者提起诉讼，以价格严重不足为由要求撤销出售。这场诉讼的影响是在1939年1月将B类普通债券的价格压低至$1\frac{1}{4}$，而如果出售得到支持，可实现的价值应在$2\frac{1}{2}$到$3$之间。显然，如果诉讼有道理，股票的价值应该比$2\frac{1}{2}$更高；或者，如果毫无道理，如显然的那样，那么股票的价值显然高于其售价。（A类股票也存在类似的差异。）

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Island Oil and Transport 8% Notes. In June 1933 these notes were selling at 18. The receiver held a cash fund equivalent to about 45% on the issue, from which were deductible certain fees and allowances, indicating a net distributable balance of about 30 for the notes. The distribution was being delayed by a suit for damages that had been repeatedly unsuccessful in its various legal stages and was now approaching final determination. This suit was exerting an adverse effect upon the market value of the notes out of all proportion to its merits, a statement that is demonstrable from the fact that the litigation could have been settled by payment of a relatively small amount. After the earlier decisions were finally sustained by the higher courts, the noteholders received a distribution of $290 per $1,000 in April 1934. A small additional distribution was indicated.³
A similar situation arose in the case of United Shipyards Corporation stock after ratification of the sale of its properties to Bethlehem Steel Company in 1938. Dissenting holders brought suit to set the sale aside on the ground that the price was grossly inadequate. The effect of this litigation was to hold down the price of the Class B common to $1\frac{1}{4}$ in January 1939, as against a realizable value of between $2\frac{1}{2}$ to $3$ if the sale was upheld. Obviously, if the suit had any merit, the stock should have been worth more rather than less than $2\frac{1}{2}$; alternatively, if it had no merit, as seemed clear, then the shares were clearly worth twice their selling price. (A similardisparity existed in connection with the price of the Class A stock.)

**低估的投资品种。** 通过仔细搜索，任何时期都可能发现低估的投资级债券和优先股。在许多情况下，债券或优先股的低价是由于市场表现不佳，而市场不佳又源于发行规模小，但如此小的规模可能带来更高的内在安全性。第26章中描述的1936年到期的Electric Refrigeration Building Corporation 6s就是这种悖论的很好例子。

<!--en-->
**Undervalued Investment Issues.** Undervalued bonds and preferred stocks of investment caliber may be discovered in any period by means of assiduous search. In many cases the low price of a bond or preferred stock is due to a poor market, which in turn results from the small size of the issue, but this very small size may make for greater inherent security. The Electric Refrigeration Building Corporation 6s, due 1936, described in Chap. 26, are a good example of this paradox.

有时某些特定发展会极大增强高级发行的地位，但价格却难以及时反映这种改善，因此会出现便宜购买的情况。这些发展通常与资本结构或企业关系有关。几个例子可以说明我们的观点。

<!--en-->
At times some specific development greatly strengthens the position of a senior issue, but the price is slow to reflect this improvement, and thus a bargain situation is created. These developments relate usually to the capitalization structure or to corporate relationships. Several examples will illustrate our point.

*示例：* 1923年，Youngstown Sheet and Tube Company购买了Steel and Tube Company of America的资产，并承担后者的1951年到期的General Mortgage 7s责任。Youngstown以99的价格出售了6%的债券来为这次购买提供资金。当时的价格关系如下：

<!--en-->
*Examples:* In 1923 Youngstown Sheet and Tube Company purchased the properties of Steel and Tube Company of America and assumed liability for the latter's General Mortgage 7s, due 1951. Youngstown sold a 6% debenture issue at 99 to supply funds for this purchase. The following price relationship obtained at the time:

<table><thead><tr><td>公司</td><td>价格</td><td>产量，%</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Youngstown Sheet and Tube Debenture 6s</td><td>99</td><td>6.02</td></tr><tr><td>Steel and Tube General 7s</td><td>102</td><td>6.85</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><td>Company</td><td>Price</td><td>Yield, %</td></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Youngstown Sheet and Tube Debenture 6s</td><td>99</td><td>6.02</td></tr><tr><td>Steel and Tube General 7s</td><td>102</td><td>6.85</td></tr></tbody></table>

市场未能认识到Steel and Tube债券的变化状态，因此以高于同一发行人的无担保债券的高收益率出售。这为分析师提供了明确的机会，建议购买或交换。

<!--en-->
The market failed to realize the altered status of the Steel and Tube bonds, and thus they sold illogically at a higher yield than the unsecured issue of the same obligor company. This presented a clear-cut opportunity to the analyst to recommend a purchase or an exchange.

1922年，底特律市购买了Detroit United Railway Company的城市线路，并同意支付足够金额以偿还1932年到期的Detroit United Railway First 4 1/2s。购买合同中包含了异常强的保护条款，实际上，即使不是技术上，也使底特律市对债券负责。但在交易完成后，债券以82的价格出售，收益率超过7%。债券市场未能认识到它们实际上是底特律市的虚拟债务。

<!--en-->
In 1922 the City of Detroit purchased the urban lines of Detroit United Railway Company and agreed to pay therefor sums sufficient to retire the Detroit United Railway First 4 1/2s, due 1932. Unusually strong protective provisions were inserted in the purchase contract which practically, if not technically, made the City of Detroit liable for the bonds. But,after the deal was consummated, the bonds sold at 82, yielding more than 7%. The bond market failed to recognize their true status as virtual obligations of the City of Detroit.

1924年，Congoleum Company拥有180万美元的7%优先股票，低于289万美元的债券，后面还有960,000股平均市场价值约4800万美元的普通股。同年10月，该公司为Nairn Linoleum Company发行了681,000股普通股，后者是同一领域的较大单位，拥有1500万美元的有形资产。这样为小型高级发行创造的巨大权益使其安全无疑，但优先股票的价格仍低于面值。

<!--en-->
In 1924 Congoleum Company had outstanding $1,800,000 of 7% preferred stock junior to $2,890,000 of bonds and followed by 960,000 shares of common stock having an average market value of some $48,000,000. In October of that year the company issued 681,000 additional shares of common for the business of the Nairn Linoleum Company, a large unit in the same field, with $15,000,000 of tangible assets. The enormous equity thus created for the small senior issues made them safe beyond question, but the price of the preferred stock remained under par.

1927年，Electric Refrigeration Corporation（现Kelvinator Corporation）以660万美元出售了373,000股普通股，使普通股总数达到1,000,000股。每股平均市场价值约为21,000美元，仅比1936年到期的6%债券少2,880,000美元。然而，这些债券的实际售价仅为74，收益率为11%。低价原因是在1927年公司出现了较大的运营亏损，但市场并未考虑到通过出售额外股票获得大量新现金，这为发行小规模债券提供了非常坚实的支撑。

<!--en-->
In 1927 Electric Refrigeration Corporation (now Kelvinator Corporation) sold 373,000 shares of common stock for $6,600,000, making a total of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, with average market value of about $21,000,000, coming behind only $2,880,000 of 6% notes, due in 1936. The notes sold at 74, however, to yield 11%. The low price was due to a large operating deficit incurred in 1927, but the market failed to take into account the fact that the receipt of a much greater amount of new cash from the sale of additional stock had established a very strong backing for the small note issue.

这四个高级问题均已按面值或更高价格结清。（1934年，Congoleum-Nairn优先债券在107的价格被要求支付。）这类例子对作者来说很方便，因为它们不会带来后续意外情况可能质疑其判断的风险。为了避免让骰子结果过于有利于我们，我们增加了另一个示例，该示例与本章撰写时的情况一致。

<!--en-->
These four senior issues have all been paid off at par or higher. (The Congoleum-Nairn Preferred was called for payment at 107 in 1934.) Examples of this kind are convenient for the authors since they do not involve the risk of some later mischance casting doubt upon their judgment. To avoid loading the dice too heavily in our favor, we add another illustration which is current as this chapter is written.

*一个当前案例。* Choctaw和Memphis铁路公司发行的"First 5s"债券于1949年到期，在1939年时以约35的价格出售，包含超过5年的未偿还利息。这些债券是芝加哥、Rock Island和Pacific系统底层里程的优先留置权。自1930年以来，Rock Island一直报告收入不佳，其所有债务均已违约。然而，对1937年收入的抵押部门划分显示，Choctaw和Memphis的里程业务非常盈利，尽管公司仅赚取了2,700,000美元，相对于总利息14,080,000美元而言，当年的利息费用已支付2.6次。此外，截至1939年提出的多项重组计划，包括I.C.C.审查员的方案，都完全涵盖了此问题的本金和后续利息，尽管几乎整个剩余债券结构将被大幅削减，总利息费用将降至每年不到2,500,000美元。

<!--en-->
*A Current Example.* Choctaw and Memphis Railroad Company First 5s, due 1949, were selling in 1939 at about 35, carrying more than 5 years' unpaid interest. They were a first lien on underlying mileage of the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific System. The Rock Island had been reporting poor earnings since 1930, and all its obligations were in default. However, a segregation of the 1937 earnings by mortgagedivisions showed that the Choctaw and Memphis mileage was very profitable and that its interest charges had been covered 2.6 times in that year even though the company had earned only $2,700,000 toward total interest of $14,080,000. Furthermore, the several reorganization plans presented up to 1939, including that of the I.C.C. examiner, had all provided for principal and back interest on this issue in full, although virtually the entire remaining bond structure was to be drastically cut down, and total interest charges were to be reduced to less than $2,500,000 annually.

正如看似不可避免的那样，公司将按照提议的方案进行重组。显然，这些Choctaw和Memphis债券将处于非常有利的地位：要么让它们保持对重要路段的优先权利及已偿还的利息不变；要么以面值价格，在整个系统上发行新的小额首笔抵押贷款。除非事实是，一家总收入仅为6500万美元的铁路公司无法负担每年250万美元的费用——这还不到其过去负担的1/5，否则这一结论是不可避免的。

<!--en-->
Assuming, as seemed inevitable, that the company was to be reorganized along the lines proposed, it was clear that these Choctaw and Memphis bonds would enjoy a very strong position, whether they were to be left undisturbed with their lien on a valuable mileage and their back interest paid off, or were to be given par for par in a new, small first mortgage on the entire system. This conclusion would be inescapable unless it were true that a railroad with minimum gross earnings of 65 millions could not be counted on to meet charges of $2\frac{1}{2}$ millions annually—less than *one-fifth* its former burden.

因此，所有定量数据都强烈表明，Choctaw和Memphis 5s的估值被严重低估，为35美元；*一旦重组完成*，该问题的根深蒂固状况将变得明显。⁴ **接管过程中的价格与价值差异**。在第18章中，我们讨论了重组程序，并给出了两个在接管过程中出现的差异案例：Fisk Rubber案例，其中债务以极低价格出售，而可用于偿还的流动资产却很多；以及Studebaker案例，其中6%债券的价格明显低于股票价格。可以合理地说，在接管过程中最终实现了较大价值的情况下，优先证券的出售价格会低得离谱。这一特征具有双重影响。它之前促使我们强烈建议不要以投资水平购买任何可能陷入财务困境公司的证券；现在它又提示我们，在这些困境出现之后，这些公司可能会提供有吸引力的分析机会。

<!--en-->
Thus all the quantitative factors would seem to indicate strongly that the Choctaw and Memphis 5s were greatly undervalued at 35 and that *once the recapitalization was completed* the entrenched position of this issue should become manifest.⁴
**Price-Value Discrepancies in Receiverships.** In Chap. 18, dealing with reorganization procedure, we gave two diverse examples of disparities arising under a receivership: the Fisk Rubber case, in which the obligations sold at a ridiculous low price compared with the current assets available for them; and the Studebaker case, in which the price of the 6% notes was clearly out of line with that of the stock. A general statement may fairly be made that in cases where substantial values are ultimately realized out of a receivership, the senior securities will be found to have sold at much too low a price. This characteristic has a twofold consequence. It has previously led us to advise strongly against buying atinvestment levels *any* securities of a company that is likely to fall into financial difficulties; it now leads us to suggest that *after* these difficulties have arisen they may produce attractive analytical opportunities.

这不仅适用于那些根深蒂固、即使进行重组也不会受到严重影响的证券（例如第2章中描述的布鲁克林联合高架5号证券），也适用于在调整计划中被"缩减规模"或以其他方式受影响的高级证券。这一规则在清算或向外部利益方出售最终导致现金分配或其等价物的情况下，似乎最为适用。

<!--en-->
This will be true not only of issues so strongly entrenched as to come through reorganization unscathed (e.g., Brooklyn Union Elevated 5s, as described in Chap. 2) but also of senior securities which are “scaled down” or otherwise affected in a readjustment plan. It seems to hold most consistently in cases where liquidation or a sale to outside interests results ultimately in a cash distribution or its equivalent.

*示例：* 以下给出了三个此类完成的典型示例。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Three typical examples of such a consummation are given herewith.

1. *安大略电力服务公司首期5½期债券，到期日期为1950年。* 该批次债券的利息支付于1932年7月1日开始。大约在同一时期，这些债券的价格低至21。不久之后，安大略水电委员会购买了该资产，每1000美元安大略电力服务债券可获得900美元的新债券，由安大略省完全担保。1933年12月，新债券的价格报为90，相当于旧债券价格的81。未进行交换的少量债券持有人获得了70%的现金。
2. *Amalgamated Laundries, Inc.，6¹/₂年到期，到期年份为1936年。* 接收人于1932年2月被指定。1932年4月，这些债券报价为4。1932年6月，这些资产被出售给外部投资者，1932年8月和1933年3月分别支付了12¹/₂%和2%的清算股息。1933年12月，债券仍报价为4，表明人们预计后续分配金额至少会达到这个水平。
3. *Fisk Rubber Company的8美元债券和5½美元债券，到期日期分别为1941年和1931年。*关于这些债券的信息见第18章。1931年1月宣布了接管程序。1932年，8美元债券和5½美元债券的价格分别低至16美元和10½美元。1933年进行了重组，对8美元债券以现金形式分配了40%，对5½美元债券分配了37%，同时还附带了两家继承公司的证券。到1933年底，现金及新证券的总价值：8美元债券接近100%，5½美元债券接近70%。**破产产生的价格模式。**在接管或破产程序中，可能会出现某些价格模式，尤其是当程序持续较长时间时。首先，股票发行往往会出现价格过高的情况，不仅与债券发行价格相关，甚至与它们的最终价值完全不符。这是由于投机性兴趣的影响，人们会被看似较低的价格吸引。对于优先发行的股票，投机兴趣会逐渐减弱，随着程序继续推进，价格也会随之下降。因此，在重组计划宣布之前不久，价格可能会降至最低水平。因此，分析活动的一个有益方向是密切关注此类情况，努力发现那些价格远低于其内在价值的证券，并大致确定投资的最佳时机。但就像所有分析场景一样，我们必须警惕过度预测正确的买入时机。我们所理解的证券分析的一个重要特征就是，时间因素属于次要考虑因素。因此，我们使用“大约”这一限定词，旨在为判断“最佳投资时机”留出几个月甚至更长的缓冲期。**铁路托管公司的机会。**1932年之后的几年里，国家大部分铁路里程被托管方掌控。到1938年底，共有111家铁路公司运营着78,016英里（占美国总铁路里程的31%）的线路，由接管人或托管方管理。这是法院在任何时期所掌控的最大铁路里程。每次重组都因复杂的资本结构以及未来正常收益的不确定性而长期延迟。结果，许多债券的价格降到了极低水平——如果铁路整体收益数年来一直低于一般商业水平，无疑会为精明的投资者提供绝佳机会。从1939年末的情况来看，许多重要路段的首次抵押债券价格已降至远低于对铁路未来前景最悲观预期所能支撑的水平。当然，这些债券比有清偿能力的铁路公司的债券和股票便宜，后者大多以相对合理的价格出售，且在未来情况如托管债券价格所预示的那样糟糕时，许多公司可能面临破产风险。后一组债券的分析方法见第12章和附录注66。[^3295]：1 在1933年的Atlas Tack操作中，试图通过承诺分拆股票来吸引公众购买，1股股票换3股。显然，这种举措对30年代出售的债券来说不会产生任何实际影响。 1933年，Atlas Tack从价格$1\frac{1}{2}$升至$34\frac{3}{4}$，随后迅速跌至10的价格，这一情况值得研究，可作为操纵模式的典型例子。比较1929年之前同一只股票的价格收益比率和价格资产比率关系非常具有启发性。例如，可参考Arthur S. Dewing在《季度经济杂志》1921年11月发表的《合并成功的统计检验》，该文也收录于他1926年出版的《公司的财务政策》一书中，第885-898页；另可参考Henry R. Seager和Charles A. Gullick所著的《信托与公司问题》，第659-661页，纽约，1929年，以及《近期经济变化委员会报告》，第一卷，第194页及以后，纽约，1929年。1938年，National Bondholders Corporation发行各种债券时也存在类似情况，该公司正在清算各种资产和债权。这些证券的售价远低于清算时可变现金额，主要因为存在涉及大量现金资金的诉讼。如同Island Oil案例一样，这些诉讼正处于上诉阶段，此前所有判决都对债券持有人有利。最终判决后，典型债券的投标价从1938年的26投标从上升到1939年的相当于41投标。关于1934年版中有关Fox Film 6%债券的资料，该债券于1936年到期，1933年时售价为75，到期收益率为20，可参见附录注67。*另一个例子：*1938年，Tung Sol Lamp公司4%债券于1941年到期，当时售价为50。由于该债券规模极小，相对于公司资源和收入而言，支付似乎必然实现。（实际上，它们在1939年到期前就提前赎回了。）第51章

<!--en-->
1. *Ontario Power Service Corporation First 5¹/₂s, Due 1950.* This issue defaulted interest payment on July 1, 1932. About this time the bonds sold as low as 21. The Hydro-Electric Commission of Ontario purchased the property soon afterwards, on a basis that gave $900 of new debentures, fully guaranteed by the Province of Ontario, for each $1,000 Ontario Power Service bond. The new debentures were quoted at 90 in December 1933, equivalent to 81 for the old bonds. The small number of bondholders not making the exchange received 70% in cash.
2. *Amalgamated Laundries, Inc., 6¹/₂s, Due 1936.* Receivers were appointed in February 1932. The bonds were quoted at 4 in April 1932. In June 1932 the properties were sold to outside interests, and liquidating dividends of 12¹/₂% and 2% were paid in August 1932 and March 1933. In December 1933 the bonds were still quoted at 4, indicating expectation of at least that amount in further distributions.
3. *Fisk Rubber Company First 8s and Debenture 5¹/₂s, Due 1941 and 1931.* Information regarding these issues was given in Chap. 18. Receivership was announced in January 1931. In 1932 the 8s and 5¹/₂s sold as low as 16 and 10¹/₂ respectively. In 1933 a reorganization was effected, which distributed 40% in cash on the 8s and 37% on the 5¹/₂s, together with securities of two successor companies. Theaggregate values of the cash and the new securities at the close of 1933 came close to 100% for the 8% bonds and 70% for the debenture 5 1/2s.
**Price Patterns Produced by Insolvency.** Certain price patterns are likely to be followed during receivership or bankruptcy proceedings, especially if they are protracted. In the first place, there is often a tendency for the stock issues to sell too high, not only in relation to the price of the bond issues but also absolutely, *i.e.*, in relation to their probable ultimate value. This is due to the incidence of speculative interest, which is attracted by a seemingly low price range. In the case of senior issues, popular interest steadily decreases, and the price tends to decline accordingly, as the proceedings wear on. Consequently, the lowest levels are likely to be reached a short time before a reorganization plan is ready to be announced.
A profitable field of analytical activity should be found therefore in keeping in close touch with such situations, endeavoring to discover securities that appear to be selling far under their intrinsic value and to determine approximately the best time for making a commitment in them. But in these, as in all analytical situations, we must warn against an endeavor to gage too nicely the proper time to buy. An essential characteristic of security analysis, as we understand it, is that the time factor is a subordinate consideration. Hence our use of the qualifying word "approximately," which is intended to allow a leeway of several months and sometimes even longer, in judging the "right time" to enter upon the operation.
**Opportunities in Railroad Trusteeships.** In the years following 1932 a large part of the country's railroad mileage went into the hands of trustees. At the close of 1938 a total of 111 railway companies operating 78,016 miles (31% of the total railway mileage in the United States) were in the hands of receivers or trustees. This is the greatest mileage ever in the hands of the courts at any one time. Reorganization in every case has been long delayed, owing on the one hand to the complicated capital structures to be dealt with and on the other to the uncertainty as to future normal earnings. As a result theprice of a great many issues fell to extremely low levels—
which would undoubtedly have presented excellent
opportunities for the shrewd investor, had it not been that the
earnings of the railroads as a whole continued for some years
to make disappointing showings as compared with general
business.
Viewing the situation about the end of 1939, it appeared
that many of the first-mortgage liens on important mileage had
fallen to lower levels than were warranted by anything but a
most pessimistic view of the future of the carriers. Certainly,
these issues were cheaper than the bonds and stocks of solvent
roads, which sold for the most part at liberal prices in relation
to their current exhibits and which in many cases would be in
danger of insolvency if future conditions turned out as badly
as the low price of trusteeships issues seemed to anticipate.
The technique of analyzing issues of the latter group is
covered in Chap. 12 and in Appendix Note 66.

The circumstances surrounding the rise of Atlas Tack from $1\frac{1}{2}$ to $34\frac{3}{4}$ in 1933 and its precipitous fall to 10 are worth studying as a perfect example of the manipulative pattern. It is illuminating to compare the price-earnings and the price-assets relationships of the same stock prior to 1929.

These securities were selling at considerably less than the amount realizable for them in liquidation, chiefly because of certain suits involving a substantial cash fund. As in the Island Oil example, this litigation was in the last stages of appeal, and the decisions theretofore had all been favorable to the bondholders. Following the final decision the value of a typical issue advanced from 26 bid in 1938 to the equivalent of 41 bid in 1939.

CHAPTER 51

### 价格与价值之间的差异（继续）

<!--en-->
*Discrepancies Between Price and Value (Continued)*

我们在上一章中在主要普通股和次要普通股之间做出的实际区分，在高级证券领域也有对应之处，即成熟发行和未成熟发行的区分。成熟发行可以定义为一家公司长期且被投资公众广泛认可的发行。（证券本身可能是新发行的，只要公司在投资者中享有良好声誉。）成熟发行和未成熟发行在市场中有时会表现出不同的行为模式，即：

<!--en-->
THE PRACTICAL DISTINCTIONS drawn in our last chapter between leading and secondary common stocks have their counterpart in the field of senior securities as between seasoned and unseasoned issues. A seasoned issue may be defined as an issue of a company long and favorably known to the investment public. (The security itself may be of recent creation so long as the company has a high reputation among investors.) Seasoned and unseasoned issues tend at times to follow divergent patterns of conduct in the market, *viz.*:

1. 尽管投资地位显著减弱，成熟发行的价格往往仍能保持稳定。
2. 未成熟发行对任何形式的负面发展都非常敏感。因此，它们的价格常常低于统计数据显示的水平。**成熟发行的价格惯性**。这些相反的特性至少部分归因于典型投资者的惰性和缺乏进取性。他们通过声誉而非分析进行购买，并坚持持有所购买的股票。因此，长期存在的发行股票不会轻易出售，即使价格略有下降，也吸引到熟悉该证券的买家。*示例：*美国橡胶公司8%非累积优先股的市场历史很好地说明了这一特性。该股票在1905年至1927年间一直获得全额股息。在这一时期内的每一年，除了1924年，都有投资者以高于面值的价格购买该股票。其受欢迎程度完全基于声誉和股息记录，因为该公司在这段时期的大部分统计表现并不令人满意，甚至对于工业债券来说也相当糟糕，因此根本不足以证明购买非累积工业优先股是合理的。在1922年至1927年间，利息费用和优先股息的综合覆盖率如下：

<!--en-->
1. The price of seasoned issues is often maintained despite a considerable weakening of their investment position.
2. Unseasoned issues are very sensitive to adverse developments of any nature. Hence they often fall to prices far lower than seem to be warranted by their statistical exhibit.
**Price Inertia of Seasoned Issues.** These opposite characteristics are due, in part at least, to the inertia and lack of penetration of the typical investor. He buys by reputation rather than by analysis and he holds tenaciously to what he has bought. Hence holders of long-established issues do not sell them readily, and even a small decline in price attracts buyers long familiar with the security.
*Example:* This trait of seasoned issues is well illustrated by the market history of the United States Rubber Company 8% Noncumulative Preferred. The issue received full dividends between 1905 and 1927. In each year of this periodexcept 1924 there were investors who paid higher than par for this stock. Its popularity was based entirely upon its reputation and its dividend record, for the statistical exhibit of the company during most of the period was anything but impressive, even for an industrial bond, and hence ridiculously inadequate to justify the purchase of a noncumulative industrial preferred stock. Between the years 1922 and 1927, the following coverage was shown for interest charges and preferred dividends combined:

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>1922</td><td>1.20 times</td></tr><tr><td>1923</td><td>1.18 times</td></tr><tr><td>1924</td><td>1.32 times</td></tr><tr><td>1925</td><td>1.79 times</td></tr><tr><td>1926</td><td>1.00 times</td></tr><tr><td>1927</td><td>1.01 times</td></tr></table>

1928年，该股票售价高达109。那一年，公司遭受了巨大损失，优先股息也被停止支付。尽管表现糟糕且没有股息，但1929年该股票的实际售价仅为92½。（1932年售价为3⅛。）¹ **未成熟发行的可怕性。** 关于未成熟发行，我们可以指出，它们几乎完全属于工业领域。在铁路的各种高级证券中，成熟因素的作用非常小；而在公用事业集团中（即电力、制气、电话和水务公司），价格变化会相对紧密地跟随统计数据，不会受到知名度或熟悉度因素的强烈影响——除了非常小的企业。

<!--en-->
In 1928 the stock sold as high as 109. During that year the company sustained an enormous loss, and the preferred dividend was discontinued. Despite the miserable showing and the absence of any dividend, the issue actually sold at 92½ in 1929. (In 1932 it sold at 3⅛.)¹
**Vulnerability of Unseasoned Issues.** Turning to unseasoned issues, we may point out that these belong almost entirely to the industrial field. The element of seasoning plays a very small part as between the various senior issues of the railroads; and in the public-utility group proper (i.e., electric, manufactured gas, telephone and water companies) price variations will be found to follow the statistical showing fairly closely, without being strongly influenced by the factor of popularity or familiarity—except in the case of very small concerns.

工业融资使市场上不断有新的公司债券和优先股发行。投资者之所以购买这些产品，主要是因为其收益率比类似等级的老牌证券更高。如果发行后盈利能力持续稳定，新的证券自然能证明是可靠的投资。但任何负面发展通常会导致市场价格急剧下跌。未成熟发行的这种可怖性使得我们得出一个实际结论：直接购买*新*工业债券或优先股作为投资是不明智的。

<!--en-->
Industrial financing has brought into the market a continuous stream of bond and preferred stock issues of companies new to the investment list. Investors have been persuaded to buy these offerings largely through the appeal of a yield moderately higher than the standard rate for seasoned securities of comparable grade. If the earning power is maintained uninterruptedly after issuance, the new security naturally proves a satisfactory commitment. But any adversedevelopment will ordinarily induce a severe decline in the market price. This vulnerability of unseasoned issues gives rise to the practical conclusion that it is unwise to buy a *new* industrial bond or preferred stock for straight investment.

由于这类证券对不利发展过于敏感，价格常常会跌得太低，在这种情况下，它们提供了有利的购买机会。这无疑是正确的，但在利用这些差异时需要非常谨慎。首先，市场中对未成熟证券的不喜欢不仅仅是由于知识不足的主观问题。成熟通常被视为一种客观品质，源于能够经受商业风暴的能力。虽然这个定义并不完全准确，但其中有足够的道理可以解释为什么投资者更倾向于选择成熟发行。

<!--en-->
Since such issues are unduly sensitive to unfavorable developments, it would seem that the price would often fall too low and in that case they would afford attractive opportunities to purchase. This is undoubtedly true, but there is great need of caution in endeavoring to take advantage of these disparities. In the first place, the disfavor accorded to unseasoned securities in the market is not merely a subjective matter, due to lack of knowledge. Seasoning is usually defined as an objective quality, arising from a demonstrated ability to weather business storms. Although this definition is not entirely accurate, there is enough truth in it to justify in good part the investor's preference for seasoned issues.

或许更重要的是，成熟证券与未成熟证券之间可以区分出规模和重要性上的明显差异。规模较大的公司通常是较老的公司，其高级债券早已为公众所熟知。因此，未成熟的债券和优先股大多属于次要重要性的证券。但我们在讨论工业投资时（第7章）指出，在这一领域，规模大可以被视为最理想的特性。因此，在这方面，未成熟证券作为一个类别，必然面临相当大的劣势。

<!--en-->
More important, perhaps, is the broad distinction of size and prominence that can be drawn between seasoned and unseasoned securities. The larger companies are generally the older companies, having senior issues long familiar to the public. Hence unseasoned bonds and preferred stocks are for the most part issues of concerns of secondary importance. But we have pointed out, in our discussion of industrial investments (Chap. 7), that in this field dominant size may reasonably be considered a most desirable trait. It follows, therefore, that in this respect unseasoned issues must suffer as a class from a not inconsiderable disadvantage.

*未成熟的工业证券很少值得给予投资评级。* 逻辑上和实际上的结果是，未成熟的工业证券非常少值得给予投资评级，因此只能以投机性方式购买。这反过来要求市场价格足够低，以便能够大幅上涨；例如，价格通常必须低于70。

<!--en-->
*Unseasoned Industrial Issues Rarely Deserve an Investment Rating.* The logical and practical result is that unseasoned industrial issues can very rarely deserve an investment rating, and consequently they should only be bought on an admittedly speculative basis. This requires in turn that the market price be low enough to permit of a substantial rise; e.g., the price must ordinarily be below 70.

大家会记得，在讨论投机性高级债券时（第26章），我们将约70到100的价格区间称为“主观波动范围”，在这个范围内，证券可能因为对是否合理的合理意见差异而正常出售。然而，对于未成熟的工业债券或优先股来说，即使定量表现相当满意，分析师也不应被这个价格范围所吸引。他只应在能够以纯粹的投机性价格购买时，才选择这些证券。

<!--en-->
It will be recalled that in our treatment of speculative senior issues (Chap. 26), we referred to the price sector of about 70 to 100 as the “range of subjective variation,” in which an issue might properly sell because of a legitimatedifference of opinion as to whether or not it was sound. It seems, however, that in the case of unseasoned industrial bonds or preferred stocks the analyst should not be attracted by a price level within this range, even though the quantitative showing be quite satisfactory. He should favor such issues only when they can be bought at a frankly speculative price.

当统计数据异常强劲时，可以例外，比如前章提到的、并在附录注67中描述的Fox Film 6%债券。我们怀疑这样的例外能否合理包括任何未成熟的工业优先股，因为这类证券的合约强度较低。（上述Congoleum优先股的情况，该公司在其领域规模较大，优先股并非“未成熟”，而是市场活跃度较低。）

<!--en-->
Exception may be made to this rule when the statistical exhibit is extraordinarily strong, as perhaps in the case of the Fox Film 6% notes mentioned in the preceding chapter and described in Appendix Note 67. We doubt if such exceptions can prudently include any unseasoned industrial preferred stocks, because of the contractual weakness of such issues. (In the case of Congoleum preferred, described above, the company was of dominant size in its field, and the preferred stock was not so much “unseasoned” as it was inactive marketwise.)

**比较价格中的差异。** 比较可能令人厌恶，也可能不令人厌恶，但会对分析师产生某种欺骗性的吸引力。似乎决定证券*A*比证券*B*更优，比认定证券*A*本身具有吸引力要简单得多。但在我们的比较分析章节中，我们提到了证券交易所推荐所附带的特殊责任，并警告不要过度接受纯粹的数量优势。未来往往不尊重统计数据。我们可以用另一种方式表达这一警告：建议分析师不应推动证券交易所进行交易，除非（1）要购买的证券本身具有吸引力，或（2）两个证券之间存在明确的合约关系。让我们通过两个来自我们记录的比较示例来说明（1）。

<!--en-->
**Discrepancies in Comparative Prices.** Comparisons may or may not be odious, but they hold a somewhat deceptive fascination for the analyst. It seems a much simpler process to decide that issue *A* is preferable to issue *B* than to determine that issue *A* is an attractive purchase in its own right. But in our chapter on comparative analysis we have alluded to the particular responsibility that attaches to the recommendation of security exchanges, and we have warned against an overready acceptance of a purely quantitative superiority. The future is often no respecter of statistical data. We may frame this caveat in another way by suggesting that the analyst should not urge a security exchange unless either (1) the issue to be bought is attractive, regarded by itself, or (2) there is a definite contractual relationship between the two issues in question. Let us illustrate consideration (1) by two examples of comparisons taken from our records.

*示例：I. 1932年3月进行的比较。*

<!--en-->
* Including guaranteed stock.
In this comparison the Ward Baking issue made a far stronger statistical showing than the Bethlehem Steel bonds. Furthermore, it appeared sufficiently well protected to justify an investment rating, despite the high return. The qualitative factors, although not impressive, did not suggest any danger of collapse of the business. Hence the bonds could be recommended either as an original purchase or as an advantageous substitute for the Bethlehem Steel 5s.

* 包括第二优先股，预计价格为50。在此比较中，Spear and Company发行的股票无疑比Republic Iron and Steel Preferred的统计表现更好。然而，单独来看，其表现并不足以证明投资价值，因为考虑到业务类型以及我们处理的是优先股这一事实。该股票的发行价格不足以作为完全投机性推荐的依据，即没有充分强调本金增值的机会。这意味着无法将其作为与Republic Iron and Steel Preferred等其他股票交换的推荐对象。**相关股票的比较**。当所考察的股票确实存在关联时，情况会有所不同。此时，可以仅从给定情境下的各自优势角度来考虑该股票；分析师无需承担进入或保持这种状况的责任。在之前的章节中，我们讨论过许多相对价格明显偏离正常水平的案例，可以据此做出权威的推荐。这些差异源于一般市场经常无法识别合同条款的影响，也往往源于投机市场倾向于关注普通股票而忽视高级证券。第一种类型的例子我们在第17章讨论有保证发行的定价差异时给出。附录注56中讨论的Interborough Rapid Transit Company多种股票的定价差异，以及第2章提到的Brooklyn Union Elevated Railroad 5s和Brooklyn-Manhattan Transit Corporation 6s之间的差异，都是此类案例的例证。²第25章讨论的高级可转换股票与普通股票之间不合逻辑的价格关系，是投机兴趣集中在更活跃的次级股票时产生的机会的例子。同一趋势的不同表现体现在1933年8月，American Water Works and Electric Company“有保证”普通股票的价格与同一股票的不太活跃投票信托证书之间的7点差距。这类现象不仅引发直接交易，还引发对冲操作。1933年7月，还可以对比Southern Railway 5%非累积优先股——不支付股息，售价为49——与Mobile and Ohio Stock Trust Certificates，后者是同一公司的义务债券，拥有4%股息的永久保证，同时售价为$39\frac{3}{4}$。即使优先股股息立即恢复并持续不变，其收益率也不会高于高级固定利率义务债券。（1939年，仍不支付股息的Southern Railway Preferred，售价为35，而Mobile and Ohio 4%证书的价格约为40。在这些价格下，有保证发行的优势仍然明显。）*其他不太确定的差异*。在上述例子中，这些偏差在数学上是可以证明的。还有一类高级与次级证券之间的差异虽然可能无法如此明确证明，但对于实际用途来说足够确定。例如，考虑Colorado Industrial Company 5s，到期日为1934年8月1日，由Colorado Fuel and Iron Company提供担保。1933年5月，该债券以43的价格出售，而Colorado Fuel and Iron 8%优先股不支付股息，售价为45。该债券必须在14个月内全部偿还，否则优先股可能面临通过接管公司而完全消失的风险。 为了使优先股的价值高于以相同价格购买的债券，不仅必须让债券在一年多时间内按面值偿还，还必须在该短时间内恢复优先股息并支付回溯股息。这几乎是不可想象的。当比较同一公司的不可转换优先股与普通股票时，我们发现后者在投机基础上发行时，相对价格往往过高。然而，这种比较只有在优先股具有累积股息时才能安全进行。（这一限制的原因将在第15章对非累积股票的缺陷详细讨论中清楚说明。）1933年4月，美国及外国电力公司普通股的股价为10美元，而累积第二优先股的股价为11美元，这显然不合理。1927年2月，芝加哥大西部铁路公司普通股的股价为$21 1/2$美元，而4%优先股的股价为$32 1/2$美元，该优先股已累积了每股44美元的股息，同样可以提出类似观点。确实，如果在这种情况下出现异常繁荣，普通股最终可能价值远高于优先股。但即使发生这种情况，公司仍会经历一个过渡期，在此期间情况改善后，公司可以恢复优先股息并释放累积收益。由于这类发展直接有利于优先股，它们可能会（至少一段时间内）使高级股票的市场价值远高于普通股。因此，假设有显著改善，在低价购买优先股比购买普通股更明智。

<!--en-->
* Includes Second Preferred estimated at 50.
In this comparison the Spear and Company issue undoubtedly made a better statistical showing than Republic Iron and Steel Preferred. Taken by itself, however, its exhibit was not sufficiently impressive to carry conviction of investment merit, considering the type of business and the fact that we were dealing with a preferred stock. The price of the issue was not low enough to warrant recommendation on a fully speculative basis, *i.e.*, with prime emphasis on the opportunity for enhancement of principal. This meant in turn that it could not consistently be recommended in exchange for another issue, such as Republic Iron and Steel Preferred.
**Comparison of Definitely Related Issues.** When the issues examined are definitely related, a different situation obtains. An exchange can then be considered solely from the standpoint of the respective merits within the given situation; the responsibility for entering into or remaining in the situation need not be assumed by the analyst. In our previous chapters we have considered a number of cases in which relative prices were clearly out of line, permitting authoritative recommendations of exchange. These disparities arise from the frequent failure of the general market to recognize theeffect of contractual provisions and often also from a tendency for speculative markets to concentrate attention on the common stocks and to neglect the senior securities. Examples of the first type were given in our discussion of price discrepancies involving guaranteed issues in Chap. 17. The price discrepancies between various Interborough Rapid Transit Company issues, discussed in Appendix Note 56, and between Brooklyn Union Elevated Railroad 5s and Brooklyn-Manhattan Transit Corporation 6s, referred to in Chap. 2, are other illustrations in this category.²
The illogical price relationships between a senior convertible issue and the common stock, discussed in Chap. 25, are examples of opportunities arising from the concentration of speculative interest on the more active junior shares. A different manifestation of the same general tendency is shown by the spread of 7 points existing in August 1933 between the price of American Water Works and Electric Company “free” common and the less active voting trust certificates for the same issue. Such phenomena invite not only direct exchanges but also hedging operations.
A similar comparison could be made in July 1933 between Southern Railway 5% Noncumulative Preferred, paying no dividend and selling at 49, and the Mobile and Ohio Stock Trust Certificates, which were an obligation of the same road, bearing a perpetual guaranty of a 4% dividend and selling concurrently at $39\frac{3}{4}$. Even if the preferred dividend had been immediately resumed and continued without interruption, the yield thereon would have been no higher than that obtainable from the senior fixed-interest obligation. (In 1939 Southern Railway Preferred, still paying no dividend, sold at 35 against a price of about 40 for the Mobile and Ohio 4% certificates. At these prices the advantage still appeared clearly on the side of the guaranteed issue.)
*Other and Less Certain Discrepancies.* In the foregoing examples the aberrations are mathematically demonstrable. There is a larger class of disparities between senior and junior securities that may not be proved quite so conclusively but are sufficiently certain for practical purposes. As an example ofthese, consider Colorado Industrial Company 5s, due August 1, 1934, guaranteed by Colorado Fuel and Iron Company, which in May 1933 sold at 43, while the Colorado Fuel and Iron 8% Preferred, paying no dividend, sold at 45. The bond issue had to be paid off in full within 14 months' time, or else the preferred stock was faced with the possibility of complete extinction through receivership. In order that the preferred stock might prove more valuable than the bonds bought at the same price, it would be necessary not only that the bonds be paid off at par in little over a year but that preferred dividends be resumed and back dividends discharged within that short time. This was almost, if not quite, inconceivable.
In comparing nonconvertible preferred stocks with common stocks of the same company, we find the same tendency for the latter to sell too high, relatively, when both issues are on a speculative basis. Comparisons of this kind can be safely drawn, however, only when the preferred stock bears cumulative dividends. (The reason for this restriction should be clear from our detailed discussion of the disabilities of noncumulative issues in Chap. 15.) A price of 10 for American and Foreign Power Company common when the $7 Cumulative Second Preferred was selling at 11 in April 1933 was clearly unwarranted. A similar remark may be made of the price of $21 1/2$ for Chicago Great Western Railroad Company common in February 1927, against $32 1/2$ for the 4% preferred stock on which dividends of $44 per share had accumulated.
It is true that if extraordinary prosperity should develop in situations of this kind, the common shares might eventually be worth substantially more than the preferred. But even if this should occur, the company is bound to pass through an intermediate period during which the improved situation permits it to resume preferred dividends and then to discharge the accumulations. Since such developments benefit the preferred stock directly, they are likely to establish (for a while at least) a market value for the senior issues far higher than that of the common stock. Hence, assuming any appreciable degree of improvement, a purchase of thepreferred shares at the low levels should fare better than one made in the common stock.

### 因特殊供需因素导致的差异。

<!--en-->
*Discrepancies Due to Special Supply and Demand Factors.*

我们一直在考虑的不合理关系，源于供需状况，而这些供需状况又是无意识投机性购买的结果。有时差异是由影响需求或供给的特殊临时因素引起的。

<!--en-->
The illogical relationships that we have been considering grow out of supply and demand conditions that are, in turn, the product of unthinking speculative purchases. Sometimes discrepancies are occasioned by special and temporary causes affecting either demand or supply.

*示例：*在1933年Interboro Rapid Transit Company 5s和7s价格的不合理关系中，由于有一个重大偿债基金购买了5s而非7s，这无疑导致前者的价格异常上涨。1921–1922年战后调整期间，United States Liberty 4 1/4s的市场表现就是这样一个例子。大量这些债券在战争期间因爱国原因被购买，并由银行贷款融资。后来人们普遍希望清偿这些贷款，导致大量出售，使价格下跌。这种特殊的销售压力实际上使得Liberty债券的价格低于高等级铁路债券——后者在安全性和税收方面显然更差。对比1920年9月的以下同时价格。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* In the illogical relationship between the prices of Interboro Rapid Transit Company 5s and 7s in 1933, the operations of a substantial sinking fund, which purchased the 5s and not the 7s, were undoubtedly instrumental in raising the price of the former disproportionately. An outstanding example of this kind is found in the market action of United States Liberty 4 1/4s during the postwar readjustment of 1921–1922. Large amounts of these bonds had been bought during the war for patriotic reasons and financed by bank loans. A general desire to liquidate these loans later on induced a heavy volume of sales which drove the price down. This special selling pressure actually resulted in establishing a lower price basis for Liberty Bonds than for high-grade railroad issues, which were, of course, inferior in security and at a greater disadvantage also in the matter of taxation. Compare the following simultaneous prices in September 1920.

<!--en-->
* Not allowing for tax exemption.
This situation supplied an excellent opportunity for the securities analyst to advise exchanges from the old-line railroad issues into Liberty Bonds.
A less striking disparity appeared a little later between the price of these Liberty Bonds and of United States Victory 4 3/4s, due 1923. This state of affairs is discussed in a circular, prepared by one of the authors and issued at that time, a copyof which is given in Appendix Note 68 as an additional example of “practical security analysis.”

### United States Savings Bonds也提供类似机会。

<!--en-->
*United States Savings Bonds Offer Similar Opportunity.*

对于中等财力的投资者来说，近年来美国政府和企业债券之间的差异再次显现。United States Savings Bonds的收益率（每年每个个人可持有10,000美元本金）按常规复合利息计算为2.90%，按单利计算为3.33%。这一收益率明显高于最佳评级的公共事业和工业债券。除了当前必须明确高于任何企业债券的安全系数外，United States Savings Bonds还有两个优势：可免税；以及持有人有权随时选择赎回，从而保障其市场价值不会中间下降。

<!--en-->
For the investor of moderate means the disparity between United States government and corporate obligations has reappeared in recent years. The yield on United States Savings Bonds (available to any one individual to the extent of $10,000 principal amount each year) is 2.90% on the regular compound-interest basis of calculation and 3.33% on a simple-interest basis. This yield is definitely higher than that returned by best-rated public-utility and industrial issues.³ In addition to their safety factor, which at present must clearly be set higher than that of any corporate issue, the United States Savings Bonds have the minor advantage of exemption from normal income tax and the major advantage of being redeemable *at the option of the holder* at any time, thus guaranteeing him against intermediate loss in market value.

    *¹ A more recent example of the same kind is presented by Curtis Publishing 7% Preferred, which sold at 114 in 1936 and 109 1/2 in 1937, despite an exceedingly inadequate showing of earnings (and tangible assets). The high price of many railroad bonds in those years, notwithstanding their unsatisfactory earnings exhibit, illustrates this point more broadly.*
