CHAPTER 52

### 市场分析与证券分析

<!--en-->
*Market Analysis and Security Analysis*

预测证券价格并非证券分析的必要部分。不过，这两种活动通常被认为密切相关，且往往由同一人或同一组织进行。预测价格走势的努力具有多种目标和多种技术方法。华尔街普遍重视对“整体市场”即时走势的预测这一科学、艺术或娱乐活动，这通过金融媒体使用的各种平均值来体现。一些服务或专家则专注于预测市场的长期趋势，试图忽略日常波动，关注持续几个月的更广泛“波动”。人们还非常关注预测个别证券的市场行为，与整体市场区分开来。

<!--en-->
FORECASTING SECURITY PRICES is not properly a part of security analysis. However, the two activities are generally thought to be closely allied, and they are frequently carried on by the same individuals and organizations. Endeavors to predict the course of prices have a variety of objectives and a still greater variety of techniques. Most emphasis is laid in Wall Street upon the science, or art, or pastime, of prophesying the immediate action of the “general market,” which is fairly represented by the various averages used in the financial press. Some of the services or experts confine their aim to predicting the longer term trend of the market, purporting to ignore day-to-day fluctuations and to consider the broader “swings” covering a period of, say, several months. A great deal of attention is given also to prophesying the market action of individual issues, as distinct from the market as a whole.

**市场分析作为证券分析的替代或补充。**假设这些活动被认真对待，不仅仅是猜测，我们可以把全部或任何此类活动称为“市场分析”。在本章中，我们想探讨市场分析在多大程度上可以被视为证券分析的替代或补充。这个问题很重要。如果如许多人所认为的那样，可以可靠地预测股票价格走势而无需参考基础价值，那么将证券分析局限于固定价值投资的选择就更为合理。因为对于普通股票而言，掌握何时买入或卖出，或选择未来增长最显著或最快的证券的技术，显然比费力得出内在价值结论更有利。许多人认为，结合对证券市场地位的分析和对其内在价值的分析，可以获得最佳结果。如果真是这样，那些涉足固定价值领域的证券分析师也必须具备市场分析师的能力，同时准备好从两个角度同时看待每种情况。

<!--en-->
**Market Analysis as a Substitute for or Adjunct to Security Analysis.** Assuming that these activities are carried on with sufficient seriousness to represent more than mere guesses, we may refer to all or any of them by the designation of “market analysis.” In this chapter we wish to consider the extent to which market analysis may seriously be considered as a substitute for or a supplement to security analysis. The question is important. If, as many believe, one can dependably foretell the movements of stock prices without any reference to the underlying values, then it would be sensible to confine security analysis to the selection of fixed-value investments only. For, when it comes to the common-stock type of issue, itwould manifestly be more profitable to master the technique of determining when to buy or sell, or of selecting the issues that are going to have the greatest or quickest advance, than to devote painstaking efforts to forming conclusions about intrinsic value. Many other people believe that the best results can be obtained by an analysis of the market position of a stock in conjunction with an analysis of its intrinsic value. If this is so, the securities analyst who ventures outside the fixed-value field must qualify as a market analyst as well and be prepared to view each situation from both standpoints at the same time.

我们无法详细批评所有市场分析方法的理论和技术基础。我们将只讨论价格预测主要前提中涉及的更广泛推理思路。即使只是简要介绍，也应能就市场分析与证券分析关系这一复杂问题得出一些有用的结论。

<!--en-->
It is not within our province to attempt a detailed criticism of the theories and the technique underlying all the different methods of market analysis. We shall confine ourselves to considering the broader lines of reasoning that are involved in the major premises of price forecasting. Even with this sketchy treatment it should be possible to reach some useful conclusions on the perplexing question of the relationship between market analysis and security analysis.

**两种市场分析。**可以区分两种市场分析。第一种仅从股市过去的行为中寻找预测依据。第二种则考虑各种经济因素，例如商业状况（一般和具体）、利率、政治形势。（市场行为本身只是众多研究要素之一。）第一种方法的理论基础可以概括为“市场是自身最好的预测者”。市场行为通常通过图表进行研究，这些图表上绘制了单个股票或“平均值”的走势。主要研究这些价格走势的人被称为“图表分析师”，他们的方法常称为“看图表”。

<!--en-->
**Two Kinds of Market Analysis.** A distinction may be made between two kinds of market analysis. The first finds the material for its predictions exclusively in the past action of the stock market. The second considers all sorts of economic factors, e.g., business conditions, general and specific; money rates; the political outlook. (The market's behavior is itself only one of these numerous elements of study.) The underlying theory of the first approach may be summed up in the declaration that "the market is its own best forecaster." The behavior of the market is generally studied by means of charts on which are plotted the movements of individual stocks or of "averages." Those who devote themselves primarily to a study of these price movements are known as "chartists," and their procedure is often called "chart reading."

但必须指出，当今许多市场分析实际上结合了上述两种类型，即市场行为本身构成主要但非唯一的研究领域。一般经济指标起着次要但重要的作用。因此，在解释市场行为的技术指标以及将这些指标与外部因素相结合时，都留有很大的个人判断空间。“道氏理论”是最著名的市场分析方法，它本质上仅限于研究市场行为。因此，我们有理由单独讨论仅适用于股票价格的看图表方法。

<!--en-->
But it must be pointed out that much present-day market analysis represents a combination of the two kinds described, in the sense that the market's action alone constitutes the predominant but not the exclusive field of study. General economic indications play a subordinate but still significant role. Considerable latitude is therefore left for individualjudgment, not only in interpreting the technical indications of the market's action but also in reconciling such indications with outside factors. The "Dow theory," however, which is the best known method of market analysis, limits itself essentially to a study of the market's behavior. Hence we feel justified in dealing separately with chart reading as applied exclusively to stock prices.

*第一种市场分析的含义。* 必须认识到，这种“技术研究”的流行程度在过去十五年中急剧上升。而证券分析从约1927年开始显著失去声望——至今尚未完全恢复——但图表分析在长期经济衰退期间及之后仍增加了追随者数量。诚然，许多怀疑者倾向于认为整个过程类似于占星术或巫术，但华尔街对其重要性的绝对地位要求我们必须谨慎对待其宣称。为了将讨论限制在逻辑推理框架内，我们甚至会刻意省略对图表分析主要原则的简单总结。¹ 我们只考虑这样一个总体观点：仅限于过去价格走势的研究可以有益地用于预测未来走势。

<!--en-->
*Implication of the First Type of Market Analysis.* It must be recognized that the vogue of such "technical study" has increased immensely during the past fifteen years. Whereas security analysis suffered a distinct loss of prestige beginning about 1927—from which it has not entirely recovered—chart reading apparently increased the number of its followers even during the long depression and in the years thereafter. Many sceptics, it is true, are inclined to dismiss the whole procedure as akin to astrology or necromancy, but the sheer weight of its importance in Wall Street requires that its pretensions be examined with some degree of care. In order to confine our discussion within the framework of logical reasoning, we shall purposely omit even a condensed summary of the main tenets of chart reading.¹ We wish to consider only the implications of the general idea that a study confined to past price movements can be availed of profitably to foretell the movements of the future.

我们认为，这种思考应得出以下结论：

<!--en-->
Such consideration, we believe, should lead to the following conclusions:

1. 图表分析不可能成为一门科学。
2. 过去它并未证明自己是股市中可靠的利润获取方法。
3. 其理论基础基于错误的逻辑，或仅仅是主观断言。
4. 其流行源于相对于随机投机的一些优势，但这些优势随着图表研究者的增加而逐渐减弱。
1. *图表分析不是科学，其实践无法持续成功。* 图表分析不可能成为科学这一点显然可以证明。如果它是科学，其结论通常应该是可靠的。那样的话，每个人都可以预测明天或下周的价格变化，从而通过正确时机买卖来持续获利。这显然是不可能的。稍加思考即可发现，人类无法对受人类控制的经济事件进行科学预测。这种预测的“可靠性”本身就会导致人类行为使其失效。因此，有思想的图表分析师承认，持续成功取决于只有少数人知晓的成功方法。
2. 由于这一事实，可以得出：没有一种广为人知的图表分析方法能在长期内持续成功。² 如果存在这样的方法，无数交易者会迅速采用它。但这种跟随会导致其效用消失。
3. *理论基础存在疑问。* 图表分析的理论基础大致如下：a. 市场（或特定股票）的行为反映了相关方的活动和态度。b. 因此，通过研究市场行为的记录，我们可以判断市场接下来会发生什么。前提可能正确，但结论未必成立。通过研究股票图表，你可以了解很多关于该股票的技术状况，但可能并不足以让你在市场中获利。一个很好的类比就是赛马“过往表现”，赛马爱好者会仔细研究这些数据。毫无疑问，这些图表提供了大量关于参赛马匹相对优点的信息；它们常常能帮助学生选出比赛冠军；但问题是，它们并没有足够频繁地提供有价值的信息，使赌马成为有利的娱乐。更贴近现实的是，证券分析本身也有类似情况。公司的过去收益提供了其未来收益的有用指示——有用但不绝对准确。因此，证券分析和市场分析都涉及对未来没有决定性意义的数据。不同之处在于，证券分析师可以通过“安全边际”保护自己，而市场分析师则无法做到这一点。无疑，有时市场行为在图表上显示出具有特定价值的意义，对于擅长解读的人来说非常重要。如果仅依赖图表指示的情况很少，那么就可以更有力地支持“技术研究”。但如此明确的信号似乎只出现在较长时间的间隔中，同时人类的急躁以及图表分析师的职业需求促使他从不太令人信服的数据中频繁得出结论。
4. *其他理论与实践上的弱点。* 对于股市交易者来说，分析图表就像治绝症用的特效药一样具有吸引力。实际上，股票投机者确实患有几乎无法治愈的疾病。但他所寻求的“治疗”并非避免投机，而是获取利润。尽管有所有经验，他仍说服自己这些利润是可以获得并保留的；他盲目而贪婪地抓住一切可能的手段。我们认为，分析图表的合理性主要源于它坚持"损失应迅速停止，利润应持续积累"这一正确的投资原则。这一原则通常能防止突然的巨大损失，有时也能让投资者获得可观的利润。因此，其结果可能比盲目跟随"市场提示"要好。交易者们意识到这一优势后，认为通过进一步发展图表分析技术，可以使其可靠性大幅提升，从而确保持续盈利。但这一结论中暗藏双重错误。许多轮盘赌玩家也采用类似系统，这限制了单次交易的损失，有时还能带来可观收益。但最终，他们的总损失往往超过少数大额利润（因为从长期来看，数学上的不利概率是不可阻挡的）。股票交易者也是如此，交易成本会严重抵消他们的优势。第二个问题是，随着图表分析方法的普及，无利可图的交易损失会增加，利润也会减少。因为越来越多的人按照同一系统操作，当大量人同时发出买入信号时，竞争性购买的结果就是群体支付更高的平均价格。相反，当这个更大的群体同时决定卖出，为了缩短损失或保护利润时，结果就是收到更低的平均价格。（"止损订单"的使用增加，原本是交易者有用的技术工具，却大大降低了其作为保护手段的价值。）我们认为，更聪明的图表研究者能够认识到这些理论上的弱点，并认为市场预测是一种需要天赋、判断力、直觉及其他个人品质的*艺术*。他们承认无法制定固定的规则，机械地遵循这些规则并不能保证成功。因此，华尔街圈子里普遍倾向于综合或折衷的方法，即结合对市场表现的全面研究与整体经济背景，由经验丰富的判断来评估整个情况。**第二种机械预测方式。**在讨论加入判断因素的重要性之前，让我们先看看另一种基于市场之外因素的机械预测方式。就整体市场而言，常规做法是构建代表各种经济因素的指数，例如利率、汽车产量、钢铁生产，然后通过观察这些指数近期的变化来推断市场的即将变化。³最早的一种方法非常简单，就是基于正在运行的高炉比例。这一理论是由Col.提出的。 克利夫兰信托公司的Leonard P. Ayres指出，安全资产价格通常会在运行中的高炉产量下降至总产量的60%时达到底部；相反，当高炉在使用量上升过程中超过60%的水平时，价格通常会达到顶部。⁴ Ayres上校还提出一种观点：债券价格的高点通常出现在生铁产量低点之后约14个月，而股票价格的高峰则出现在生铁产量低点之后约两年。⁵ 这种简单的方法适用于所有机械预测系统，因为：(1) 基于先验推理，它听起来略显*可信*；(2) 它的*说服力*依赖于多年来它确实有效的事实。所有这些系统的共同弱点在于时间因素。例如，很容易且安全地预测高利率时期会导致市场急剧下跌。问题是：“多久会这样？”没有科学方法可以回答这个问题。因此，许多预测服务趋向于一种伪科学，它们认为过去多次发生的某些时间滞后或某些巧合（或通过反复试验得出），将来很可能以类似方式再次发生。总的来说，通过机械指数来预测安全资产价格变动的方法，同样存在与图表分析方法的相同缺陷。它们并非真正科学，因为缺乏令人信服的推理支持；此外，真正科学的（即完全可靠的）经济领域预测在逻辑上是不可能的。**与安全资产分析相比，市场分析的缺点。**因此，我们回到之前的结论：市场分析是一种需要特殊才能才能成功进行的艺术。安全资产分析也是一门艺术；除非分析师具备能力和知识，否则也无法取得满意的结果。然而，我们认为安全资产分析比市场分析有若干优势，这些优势可能使前者成为训练有素、聪明的人更成功的领域。在安全资产分析中，重点在于防范意外事件。我们通过坚持安全边际（即价格远高于支付价格）来实现这种保护。基本思想是：即使安全资产不如最初看起来有吸引力，承诺仍可能仍然令人满意。在市场分析中，没有安全边际；你要么正确，要么错误，如果错了，就会亏损。⁶ 市场分析师的核心原则是尽快减少损失并保护利润（在下跌开始时卖出）。这引导人们进行主动交易。这意味着买卖成本成为总体结果中非常不利的因素。基于安全资产分析的操作通常是投资型操作，不涉及主动交易。市场分析的第三个缺点是，它本质上是一场智斗。在市场上交易获得的利润，大多是以其他试图做同样事情的人为代价实现的。交易者必然倾向于更活跃的问题，而这些问题的价格变化是由众多同类操作者的活动造成的。市场分析师只有假设自己比竞争对手更聪明或更幸运，才能对成功抱有希望。另一方面，证券分析师的工作与同行分析师的工作并无竞争关系。 在典型情况下，他选择购买的股票并非由某位对其价值进行了同样细致分析的人所推荐。必须强调一点：证券分析师所审查的证券清单比市场分析师的清单要庞大得多。在这庞大的清单中，他会筛选出那些市场价格严重低于内在价值的特殊情况——可能是因为忽视因素，也可能是因为过度关注可能只是暂时的不利因素。市场分析似乎比证券分析更容易，收益也可能更快获得。但正因如此，从长远来看，市场分析可能会更令人失望。无论是在华尔街还是其他任何地方，都没有可靠的方法能轻松快速赚钱。**基于短期前景的预测**。金融区提供的分析和建议，很大一部分都基于所分析的公司的短期业务前景。假设如果前景表明收益将增加，那么人们会购买该股票，期望在实际报告更高收益时获得更高价格。在这种推理下，证券分析和市场分析被认为是一致的。市场前景被认为与业务前景相同。但我们认为，仅基于即时前景来购买股票的理论，使得投机性证券的选择变得过于简单。其弱点在于当前市场价格已经考虑了关于未来前景的普遍意见。在许多情况下，这些前景被给予了*超出*其实际需要的认可程度。当推荐某只股票是因为预计明年的收益会改善时，存在双重风险：首先，对明年业绩的预测可能不正确；其次，即使正确，也可能会在当前价格中被低估甚至过度低估。如果市场通常只反映今年的收益，那么对明年收益的准确估计将具有不可估量的价值。但这一前提并不正确。我们下面的表格一方面显示了美国钢铁公司普通股的年每股收益，另一方面显示了1902-1939年该股票的价格范围。排除1928-1933年时期（在此期间业务变化极为剧烈，必然导致股票价格相应变化），很难建立收益波动与市场报价波动之间的明确关联。在附录注70中，我们转载了1933年末一家重要统计和咨询机构针对两只普通股所进行的分析和建议的重要部分。这些建议主要基于1934年的表面前景。没有迹象表明有人试图确定业务的真实价值，并将此价值与当前价格进行比较。全面的统计分析会得出这样的结论：建议出售的股票因即时不利前景而低于其内在价值，而作为值得持有的普通股票则相反，因为其前景令人满意。我们对分析师能否成功预测个别股票在短期内的市场行为表示怀疑——无论他的预测是基于市场的技术状况、整体业务前景还是个别公司的具体前景。我们认为，通过将分析师的积极结论限制在以下领域，可以获得更令人满意的结果：
1. 选择符合严格安全标准的标准高级债券。
2. 发现值得投资评级，但具有显著价值提升潜力的高级债券。
3. 发现看似以远低于内在价值价格出售的普通股或投机性高级债券。
4. 确定相关证券之间存在的明确价格差异，这些情况可能证明进行交换、对冲或套利操作是合理的。

<!--en-->
1. Chart reading cannot possibly be a science.
2. It has not proved itself in the past to be a dependable method of making profits in the stock market.
3. Its theoretical basis rests upon faulty logic or else upon mere assertion.
4. Its vogue is due to certain advantages it possesses over haphazard speculation, but these advantages tend to diminish as the number of chart students increases.
1. *Chart Reading Not a Science and Its Practice Cannot Be Continuously Successful.* That chart reading cannot be a science is clearly demonstrable. If it were a science, itsconclusions would be as a rule dependable. In that case everybody could predict tomorrow's or next week's price changes, and hence everyone could make money continuously by buying and selling at the right time. This is patently impossible. A moment's thought will show that there can be no such thing as a scientific prediction of economic events under human control. The very "dependability" of such a prediction will cause human actions that will invalidate it. Hence thoughtful chartists admit that continued success is dependent upon keeping the successful method known to only a few people.
2. Because of this fact it follows that there is no generally known method of chart reading that has been continuously successful for a long period of time.² If it were known, it would be speedily adopted by numberless traders. This very following would bring its usefulness to an end.
3. *Theoretical Basis Open to Question.* The theoretical basis of chart reading runs somewhat as follows:
a. The action of the market (or of a particular stock) reflects the activities and the attitude of those interested in it.
b. Therefore, by studying the record of market action, we can tell what is going to happen next in the market.
The premise may well be true, but the conclusion does not necessarily follow. You may learn a great deal about the technical position of a stock by studying its chart, and yet you may not learn *enough* to permit you to operate profitably in the issue. A good analogy is provided by the "past performances" of race horses, which are so assiduously studied by the devotees of the race track. Undoubtedly these charts afford considerable information concerning the relative merits of the entries; they will often enable the student to pick the winner of a race; but the trouble is that they do not furnish that valuable information *often enough* to make betting on horse races a profitable diversion.
Coming nearer home, we have a similar situation in security analysis itself. The past earnings of a company supplya useful indication of its future earnings—useful, but not infallible. Security analysis and market analysis are alike, therefore, in the fact that they deal with data that are not conclusive as to the future. The difference, as we shall point out, is that the securities analyst can protect himself by a *margin of safety* that is denied to the market analyst.
Undoubtedly, there are times when the behavior of the market, as revealed on the charts, carries a definite and trustworthy meaning of particular value to those who are skilled in its interpretation. If reliance on chart indications were confined to those really convincing cases, a more positive argument could be made in favor of “technical study.” But such precise signals seem to occur only at wide intervals, and in the meantime human impatience plus the exigencies of the chart reader’s profession impel him to draw more frequent conclusions from less convincing data.
4. *Other Theoretical and Practical Weaknesses.* The appeal of chart reading to the stock-market trader is something like that of a patent medicine to an incurable invalid. The stock speculator does suffer, in fact, from a well-nigh incurable ailment. The cure he seeks, however, is not abstinence from speculation but profits. Despite all experience, he persuades himself that these can be made and retained; he grasps greedily and uncritically at every plausible means to this end.
The plausibility of chart reading, in our opinion, derives largely from its insistence on the sound gambling maxim that losses should be cut short and profits allowed to run. This principle usually prevents sudden large losses, and at times it permits a large profit to be taken. The results are likely to be better, therefore, than those produced by the haphazard following of “market tips.” Traders, noticing this advantage, are certain that by developing the technique of chart reading farther they will so increase its reliability as to assure themselves continued profits.
But in this conclusion there lurks a double fallacy. Many players at roulette follow a similar system, which limits their losses at any one session and permits them at times to realize asubstantial gain. But in the end they always find that the aggregate of small losses exceeds the few large profits. (This must be so, since the mathematical odds against them are inexorable over a period of time.) The same is true of the stock trader, who will find that the expense of trading weights the dice heavily against him. A second difficulty is that, as the methods of chart reading gain in popularity, the amount of the loss taken in unprofitable trades tends to increase and the profits also tend to diminish. For as more and more people, following the same system, receive the signal to buy at about the same time, the result of this competitive buying must be that a higher average price is paid by the group. Conversely, when this larger group decides to sell out at the same time, either to cut short a loss or to protect a profit, the effect must again be that a lower average price is received. (The growth in the use of “stop-loss orders,” formerly a helpful technical device of the trader, had this very effect of detracting greatly from their value as a protective measure.)
The more intelligent chart students recognize these theoretical weaknesses, we believe, and take the view that market forecasting is an *art* that requires talent, judgment, intuition and other personal qualities. They admit that no rules of procedure can be laid down, the automatic following of which will insure success. Hence the widespread tendency in Wall Street circles towards a composite or eclectic approach, in which a very thorough study of the market’s performance is projected against the general economic background, and the whole is subjected to the appraisal of experienced judgment.
**The Second Type of Mechanical Forecasting.** Before considering the significance of this injection of the judgment factor, let us pass on to the other type of mechanical forecasting, which is based upon factors outside of the market itself. As far as the general market is concerned, the usual procedure is to construct indices representing various economic factors, *e.g.*, money rates, carloadings, steel production, and to deduce impending changes in the market from an observation of a recent change in these indices.³ One of the earliest methods of the kind, and a very simple one, was based upon the percentage of blast furnaces in operation.
This theory was developed by Col. Leonard P. Ayres of the Cleveland Trust Company and ran to the effect that security prices usually reached a bottom when blast furnaces in operation declined through 60% of the total and that conversely they usually reached a top when blast furnaces in operation passed through the 60% mark on the upswing in use thereof.⁴ A companion theory of Colonel Ayres was that the high point in bond prices is reached about 14 months subsequent to the low point in pig-iron production and that the peak in stock prices is reached about two years following the low point for pig-iron production.⁵
This simple method is representative of all mechanical forecasting systems, in that (1) it sounds vaguely *plausible* on the basis of *a priori* reasoning and (2) it relies for its *convincingness* on the fact that it has “worked” for a number of years past. The necessary weakness of all these systems lies in the time element. It is easy and safe to prophesy, for example, that a period of high interest rates will lead to a sharp decline in the market. The question is, “How soon?” There is no scientific way of answering this question. Many of the forecasting services are therefore driven to a sort of pseudo-science, in which they take it for granted that certain time lags or certain coincidences that happened to occur several times in the past (or have been worked out laboriously by a process of trial and error), can be counted upon to occur in much the same way in the future.
Broadly speaking, therefore, the endeavor to forecast security-price changes by reference to mechanical indices is open to the same objections as the methods of the chart readers. They are not truly scientific, because there is no convincing reasoning to support them and because, furthermore, really scientific (i.e., entirely dependable) forecasting in the economic field is a logical impossibility.
**Disadvantages of Market Analysis as Compared with Security Analysis.** We return in consequence to our earlier conclusion that market analysis is an art for which special talent is needed in order to pursue it successfully. Security analysis is also an art; and it, too, will not yield satisfactoryresults unless the analyst has ability as well as knowledge. We think, however, that security analysis has several advantages over market analysis, which are likely to make the former a more successful field of activity for those with training and intelligence. In security analysis the prime stress is laid upon protection against untoward events. We obtain this protection by insisting upon margins of safety, or values well in excess of the price paid. The underlying idea is that even if the security turns out to be less attractive than it appeared, the commitment might still prove a satisfactory one. In market analysis there are no margins of safety; you are either right or wrong, and, if you are wrong, you lose money.⁶
The cardinal rule of the market analyst that losses should be cut short and profits safeguarded (by selling when a decline commences) leads in the direction of active trading. This means in turn that the cost of buying and selling becomes a heavily adverse factor in aggregate results. Operations based on security analysis are ordinarily of the investment type and do not involve active trading.
A third disadvantage of market analysis is that it involves essentially a battle of wits. Profits made by trading in the market are for the most part realized at the expense of others who are trying to do the same thing. The trader necessarily favors the more active issues, and the price changes in these are the resultant of the activities of numerous operators of his own type. The market analyst can be hopeful of success only upon the assumption that he will be more clever or perhaps luckier than his competitors.
The work of the securities analyst, on the other hand, is in no similar sense competitive with that of his fellow analysts. In the typical case the issue that he elects to buy is not sold by some one who has made an equally painstaking analysis of its value. We must emphasize the point that the security analyst examines a far larger list of securities than does the market analyst. Out of this large list, he selects the exceptional cases in which the market price falls far short of reflecting intrinsic value, either through neglect or because of undue emphasis laid upon unfavorable factors that are probably temporary.
Market analysis seems easier than security analysis, and its rewards may be realized much more quickly. For these very reasons, it is likely to prove more disappointing in the long run. There are no dependable ways of making money easily and quickly, either in Wall Street or anywhere else.
**Prophesies Based on Near-Term Prospects.** A good part of the analysis and advice supplied in the financial district rests upon the near-term business prospects of the company considered. It is assumed that, if the outlook favors increased earnings, the issue should be bought in the expectation of a higher price when the larger profits are actually reported. In this reasoning, security analysis and market analysis are made to coincide. The market prospect is thought to be identical with the business prospect.
But to our mind the theory of buying stocks chiefly upon the basis of their immediate outlook makes the selection of speculative securities entirely too simple a matter. Its weakness lies in the fact that the current market price already takes into account the consensus of opinion as to future prospects. And in many cases the prospects will have been given *more* than their just need of recognition. When a stock is recommended for the reason that next year's earnings are expected to show improvement, a twofold hazard is involved. First, the forecast of next year's results may prove incorrect; second, even if correct, it may have been discounted or even overdiscounted in the current price.
If markets generally reflected only this year's earnings, then a good estimate of next year's results would be of inestimable value. But the premise is not correct. Our table that follows shows on the one hand the annual earnings per share of United States Steel Corporation common and on the other hand the price range of that issue for the years 1902–1939. Excluding the 1928–1933 period (in which business changes were so extreme as necessarily to induce corresponding changes in stock prices), it is difficult to establish any definite correlation between fluctuations in earnings and fluctuations in market quotations.
In Appendix Note 70, we reproduce significant parts of the analysis and recommendation concerning two common stocks made by an important statistical and advisory service in the latter part of 1933. The recommendations are seen to be based largely upon the apparent outlook for 1934. There is no indication of any endeavor to ascertain the fair value of the business and to compare this value with the current price. A thorough-going statistical analysis would point to the conclusion that the issue of which the sale is advised was selling below its intrinsic value, just because of the unfavorable immediate prospects, and that the opposite was true of the common stock recommended as worth holding because of its satisfactory outlook.
We are sceptical of the ability of the analyst to forecast with a fair degree of success the market behavior of individual issues over the near-term future—whether he base his predictions upon the technical position of the market or upon the general outlook for business or upon the specific outlook for the individual companies. More satisfactory results are to be obtained, in our opinion, by confining the positive conclusions of the analyst to the following fields of endeavor:
1. The selection of standard senior issues that meet exacting tests of safety.
2. The discovery of senior issues that merit an investment rating but that also have opportunities of an appreciable enhancement in value.
3. The discovery of common stocks, or speculative senior issues, that appear to be selling at far less than their intrinsic value.
4. The determination of definite price discrepancies existing between related securities, which situations may justify making exchanges or initiating hedging or arbitrage operations.

<!--en-->
If we transfer our attention, finally, from the analyst to the owner of securities, we may briefly express our views on what he may soundly do and not do. The following résumé makes some allowance for different categories of investors.

**A. 资金有限的投资者。** 1. *收入型投资*。在当前情况下，对他来说，唯一合理的安全与积累收入投资是*美国储蓄债券*。其他良好投资几乎无法带来更多收益，且无法同等保护投资者免受最终和中间损失。表面提供更高回报的纯债券和优先股几乎肯定涉及显著风险。推销员提供的各种“储蓄计划”和类似证券充满陷阱；被其丰厚收益承诺所吸引而选择它们而非美国储蓄债券的投资者，极有可能后悔自己的选择。

<!--en-->
**A. The Investor of Small Means.** 1. *Investment for Income.* In his case the only sensible investment for safety and accumulated income, under present conditions, is found in *United States Savings Bonds*. Other good investments yield little if any more, and they have not equal protection against both ultimate and intermediate loss. Straight bonds and preferred stocks ostensibly offering a higher return are almost certain to involve an appreciable risk factor. The various types of “savings plans” and similar securities offered by salesmen are full of pitfalls; the investor persuaded by their promise of liberal income to prefer them to United States Savings Bonds is very, very likely to regret his choice.

2. *利润型投资*。小型和大型投资者都有四种选择：a. 当市场水平根据客观的长期标准明显较低时，购买代表性普通股。此策略需要耐心和勇气，并非没有严重误算的可能性。我们认为长期来看会取得良好效果。b. 购买具有特殊增长潜力的单个债券，如果这些债券能以合理价格获得，且与实际表现相符。如果预计有*普遍*增长，价格很少合理。如果购买基础是公众并不持有的未来增长信心，该操作可能既合理又盈利；也可能毫无依据且成本高昂。c. 购买安全性良好的特权高级债券。真正足够的担保与有前景的转换或类似权利相结合，是一种罕见但绝非不常见的现象。在此领域进行仔细选择的政策应会带来良好效果，前提是投资者具备寻找机会所需的耐心和坚持。美国钢铁普通股，1901–1939

<!--en-->
2. *Investment for Profit.* Four approaches are open to both the small and the large investor:
a. Purchase of representative common stocks when the market level is clearly low as judged by objective, long-term standards. This policy requires patience and courage and is by no means free from the possibility of grave miscalculation. Over a long period we believe that it will show good results.
b. Purchase of individual issues with special growth possibilities, when these can be obtained at reasonable prices in relation to actual accomplishment.
Where growth is *generally* expected, the price is rarely reasonable. If the basis of purchase is a confidence in future growth not held by the public, the operation may prove sound and profitable; it may also prove ill-founded and costly.
c. Purchase of well-secured privileged senior issues. A combination of really adequate security with a promising conversion or similar right is a rare but by no means unknown phenomenon. A policy of careful selection in this field should bring good results, provided the investor has the patience and persistence needed to find his opportunities.
United States Steel Common, 1901–1939

* 在考虑40%股票股息之前。† 在考虑40%股票股息之后。d. 购买价格远低于内在价值的证券。内在价值不仅考虑过去的收益和流动资产价值，还考虑未来盈利能力——即保守估计的，包括质量和数量因素。我们认为，由于如今大部分发行证券都不受欢迎，必然有许多情况下市场会明显且严重偏离方向，从而为有辨别力的投资者创造实际机会。这些可能出现在债券、优先股和普通股中。我们认为，寻找并评估上述类型的证券价值，并不超出希望以非专业方式进行证券分析的小投资者的能力，尽管他无疑需要比平均水平更高的智力与培训。但我们认为，非专业投资者应将自己的想法提交给专业分析师（如纽约证券交易所公司的统计师）批评，这是必要规则。当然，谦逊与自信并不矛盾；认为除非一个人具备专业建议他人的能力，否则不应独自做出决策，也是合理的。
3. *投机行为。* 资金有限的投资者当然有特权跳出角色，成为投机者。（他也有特权事后后悔自己的决定。）投机有多种类型，成功机会也各不相同：a. 购买新成立或几乎新成立的企业的股票。我们可以毫不犹豫地强烈谴责这种行为。对于参与这些新企业的人而言，胜算极小，他们不妨把四分之三的钱扔出窗外，只留一部分存银行。b. 在市场上交易。对华尔街机构来说幸运的是，少数人能成功交易，许多人也认为自己可以。普遍观点认为，股票交易和其他事情一样；即，通过智慧和应用，或良好的专业指导，可以获利。我们自己的观点持怀疑态度，甚至有些偏颇。我们认为，无论准备和方法如何，交易成功要么是偶然且短暂的，要么源于极其罕见的才能。因此，绝大多数股票交易者注定会失败。我们不认为这一结论会对公众产生太大影响。（注意我们之间的基本区别：以客观低价购买股票并高价出售——我们称之为投资；而常见的做法是在市场“预期上涨”时买入，在市场“预期下跌”时卖出——我们称之为投机。）c. 以优惠价格购买“成长型股票”。称此为“投机”，我们违背了大多数权威观点。基于之前提到的原因，我们认为这种流行方式本质上很危险，而且随着其越来越流行，风险更大。但在此种投机中，个人成功的机会比其他形式更乐观，也有更好的空间发挥预见、判断和节制能力。**B. 资金充裕的个人投资者。** 虽然他相比小投资者有明显的技术优势，但他面临三个特殊障碍：
1. 他无法仅通过购买美国储蓄债券来解决纯投资问题，因为个人可购买的数量有限。因此，他必须考虑更广泛的固定价值投资领域。我们认为，严格应用定量测试，加上在质量方面合理的判断力，应该能取得满意的结果。
2. 然而，可能的通货膨胀这一外部问题对他来说比小投资者更严重。自1932年以来，一直有强烈的常识性理由认为，持有部分普通股是一种防御措施。此外，大量持有普通股符合富裕个人的传统态度和做法。
3. 他投资单位的规模更可能促使大型投资者关注热门且活跃的股票。因此，在运用低估证券策略方面，他在一定程度上存在限制。不过，我们认为，更严重的障碍可能在于他的偏好和偏见。**C. 企业投资。**我们认为，免除公司所得税的美国政府债券，几乎是这类企业资金进行长期投资的唯一合理选择。（在1940年之前的条件下，短期投资带来的麻烦与收益相当。）总体而言，其他类型的企业投资——无论是债券还是股票——只有在面临风险和批评的情况下，才能提供明显更高的回报。**D. 机构投资。**我们不敢为那些以投资理论和实践为业务的金融机构提出政策建议。慈善和教育机构也是如此，因为它们通常可以借助经验丰富的金融家来制定财务政策。但为了不完全回避这个非常困难的问题，我们提出以下最终观点：我们认为，能够依靠高质量固定价值证券提供的低收入生活的机构，应将其投资范围限定于这一领域。我们怀疑，普通股票指数过去的表现良好，是否本身就足以证明普通股票投资计划所必然伴随的沉重责任和反复出现的不确定性是合理的。如果大家普遍认为必须防范通货膨胀，或者收入不足迫使人们寻求更高回报，这一结论或许可以被修改。在这种情况下，负责人或许有理由将部分机构资金用于固定价值以外的领域管理，遵循证券分析的标准和技术。⁷ [^3402]: ¹ 关于图表解读的理论与实践的详细论述，学生可参考：R. Tighe于1940年2月14日在美国银行家协会信托分会发表的演讲《当今捐赠机构的投资问题》，该演讲被1940年2月20日的《纽约太阳报》摘要报道。

* Before allowing for 40% stock dividend.
† After allowing for 40% stock dividend.
d. Purchase of securities selling well below intrinsic value. Intrinsic value takes into account not only past earnings and liquid asset values but also future earning power,conservatively estimated—in other words, qualitative as well as quantitative elements. We think that since a large percentage of *all* issues nowadays are relatively unpopular, there must be many cases in which the market goes clearly and crassly astray, thus creating real opportunities for the discriminating student. These may be found in bonds, preferred stocks and common stocks.
In our view, the search for and the recognition of security values of the types just discussed are not beyond the competence of the small investor who wishes to practice security analysis in a nonprofessional capacity, although he will undoubtedly need better than average intelligence and training. But we think it should be a necessary rule that the nonprofessional investor submit his ideas to the criticism of a professional analyst, such as the statistician of a New York Stock Exchange firm. Surely modesty is not incompatible with self-confidence; and there is logic in the thought that unless a man is qualified to advise others professionally, he should not, unaided, prescribe for himself.
3. *Speculation.* The investor of small means is privileged, of course, to step out of his role and become a speculator. (He is also privileged to regret his action afterwards.) There are various types of speculation, and they offer varying chances of success:
a. Buying stock in new or virtually new ventures. This we can condemn unhesitatingly and with emphasis. The odds are so strongly against the man who buys into these new flotations that he might as well throw three-quarters of the money out of the window and keep the rest in the bank.
b. Trading in the market. It is fortunate for Wall Street as an institution that a small minority of people can trade successfully and that many others think they can. The accepted view holds that stock trading is like anything else; *i.e.*, with intelligence and application, or with good professional guidance, profits can be realized. Our own opinion is sceptical, perhaps jaundiced. We think that, regardless of preparation and method, success in trading is either accidental and impermanent or else due to a highlyuncommon talent. Hence the vast majority of stock traders are inevitably doomed to failure. We do not expect this conclusion to have much effect on the public. (Note our basic distinction between purchasing stocks at objectively low levels and selling them at high levels—which we term investment—and the popular practice of buying only when the market is “expected” to advance and selling when it is “due” to decline—which we call speculation.)
c. Purchase of “growth stocks” at generous prices. In calling this “speculation,” we contravene most authoritative views. For reasons previously expressed, we consider this popular approach to be inherently dangerous and increasingly so as it becomes more popular. But the chances of individual success are much brighter here than in the other forms of speculation, and there is a better field for the exercise of foresight, judgment and moderation.
**B. The Individual Investor of Large Means.** Although he has obvious technical advantages over the small investor, he suffers from three special handicaps:
1. He cannot solve his straight investment problem simply by buying nothing but United States Savings Bonds, since the amount that any individual may purchase is limited. Hence he must, perforce, consider the broader field of fixed-value investment. We believe that strict application of quantitative tests, plus reasonably good judgment in the qualitative area, should afford a satisfactory end result.
2. However, the extraneous problem of possible inflation is more serious to him than to the small investor. Since 1932 there has been a strong common-sense argument for *some* common-stock holdings as a defensive measure. In addition, a substantial holding of common stocks corresponds with the traditional attitude and practice of the wealthy individual.
3. The size of his investment unit is more likely to induce the large investor to concentrate on the popular and active issues. To some extent, therefore, he is handicapped in the application of the undervalued-security technique. However, we imagine that a more serious obstacle thereto will be found in his preferences and prejudices.
**C. Investment by Business Corporations.** We believe that United States government bonds, carrying exemption from corporate income taxes, are almost the only logical medium for such business funds as may properly be invested for a term of years. (Under 1940 conditions short-time investment involves as much trouble as income.) It seems fairly evident, on the whole, that other types of investments by business enterprises—whether in bonds or in stocks—can offer an appreciably higher return only at risk of loss and of criticism.
**D. Institutional Investment.** We shall not presume to suggest policies for financial institutions whose business it is to be versed in the theory and practice of investment. The same might be said for philanthropic and educational institutions, since these generally have the benefit of experienced financiers in shaping their financial policies. But in order not to dodge completely a very difficult issue, we venture the following final observation: An institution that can manage to get along on the low income provided by high-grade fixed-value issues should, in our opinion, confine its holdings to this field. We doubt if the better performance of common-stock indexes over past periods will, in itself, warrant the heavy responsibilities and the recurring uncertainties that are inseparable from a common-stock investment program. This conclusion may perhaps be modified either if there is substantial unanimity of view that inflation must be guarded against or if the insufficiency of income compels search for a higher return. In such case those in charge may be warranted in setting aside a portion of the institution's funds for administration in other than fixed-value fields, in accordance with the canons and technique of security analysis.⁷
[^3402]: ¹ For detailed statements concerning the theory and practice of chart reading the student is referred to: R. W. Shabacker, *Stock Market Profits*, B. C. Forbes, New York, 1934; Robert Rhea, “The Dow Theory,” *passim*, *Barron's*, New York, 1932; H. M. Gartley, “Analyzing the Stock Market,” a series of articles in *Barron's* beginning with the issue of Sept. 19, 1932 and ending with the issue of Dec. 5, 1932. See Appendix Note 69 for a brief statement of the main tenets of the Dow theory.
2 Adherents of the Dow theory claim that it has been continuously successful for a great many years. We believe this statement to be open to much doubt—turning, in part, on certain disputed interpretations of what the theory indicated on various key occasions.
3 These indices may also be plotted on charts, in which case the forecasting takes on the aspect of chart reading. *Examples:* The *A*, *B*, and *C* lines of the *Harvard Economic Service* which were published in weekly letters from Jan. 3, 1922, to Dec. 26, 1931 (since continued through 1939 at less frequent intervals in *The Review of Economic Statistics*); also the single composite Index Line in the “Investment Timing Service” offered by Independence Fund of North America, Inc., in 1939.
4 See *Bulletin of the Cleveland Trust Company*, July 15, 1924, cited by David F. Jordan, in *Practical Business Forecasting*, p. 203n, New York, 1927.
5 See *Business Recovery Following Depression*, a pamphlet published by the Cleveland Trust Company in 1922. The conclusions of Colonel Ayres are summarized on p. 31 of the pamphlet.
6 Viewing the two activities as possible professions, we are inclined to draw an analogous comparison between the law and the concert stage. A talented lawyer should be able to make a respectable living; a talented, *i.e.*, a “merely talented,” musician faces heartbreaking obstacles to a successful concert career. Thus, as we see it, a thoroughly competent securities analyst should be able to obtain satisfactory results from his work, whereas permanent success as a market analyst requires unusual qualities—or unusual luck.
7 Yale University now follows a policy of investing part of its funds in “equities”—defined as common stocks and nonpaying senior issues. The percentage varies in accordance with a fixed formula, somewhat as follows: The initial proportion is 30% of the total fund. Whenever a rise in the market level advances this figure to 40%, one-eighth of each stock holding is switched into bonds. Conversely, whenever a decline in the market reduces the proportion to 15%, bonds are sold and one-third additional of each stock is bought. See address of Laurence G. Tighe, Associate Treasurer of Yale University entitled “Present Day Investment Problems of Endowed Institutions,” delivered on February 14, 1940 before the Trust Division of the American Bankers Association. It was summarized in the *New York Sun* of February 20, 1940.

## 第八部分

<!--en-->
*PART VIII*

价值投资中的当代概念

<!--en-->
Contemporary Concepts in
Value Investing

### 国际投资

<!--en-->
*International Investing*

作者：Bill Duhamel、Ashish Pant、Jason Moment  

Benjamin Graham和David Dodd在《安全分析》的前四版中并未讨论国际投资。1934年他们撰写第一版时，不仅在美国境外进行投资困难且成本高昂，而且除了英国、法国和日本之外，几乎没有规模较大的国际市场。¹ 然而，如今世界更加互联互通，经济活动已变得更具全球性。例如，如今半导体通常在加利福尼亚设计，在台湾制造，在马来西亚或越南包装和测试，在中国组装成智能手机和电脑，然后由美国、韩国和中国跨国公司全球销售。出口比例已从1930年代的全球GDP的5%上升到今天的25%。² S&P 500指数中的公司，其收入中有超过30%来自海外市场，而技术、材料、消费必需品等行业的许多公司，其收入和利润有超过一半来自海外。³ 同时，全球各公司都在美国开展大量业务，因此分析美国公司时，不能忽略其国际供应商、竞争对手和客户。简而言之，美国投资者必须将“外国”公司视为其视野的一部分，并将全球经济视为许多“美国”企业的重要组成部分。

<!--en-->
by Bill Duhamel, Ashish Pant, and Jason Moment
Benjamin Graham and David Dodd did not discuss international investments in any of the first four editions of *Security Analysis*. When they were writing the first edition in 1934, not only was investing in markets outside the United States difficult and costly, but there were few international markets of any size beyond Great Britain, France, and Japan.¹ However, the world today has become more interconnected and economic activity much more global. For instance, today semiconductors are often designed in California, fabricated in Taiwan, packaged and tested in Malaysia or Vietnam, and assembled into smartphones and PCs in China, before being sold globally by U.S., Korean, and Chinese multinationals. Exports have risen from just 5% of global GDP in the 1930s to 25% today.² Companies in the S&P 500 Index generate over 30% of their revenues from foreign markets, and many companies in such sectors as technology, materials, and consumer staples generate over half of their revenues and profits abroad.³ Meanwhile, companies around the world do a great deal of business in the United States, so any analysis of an American company is incomplete without considering its international suppliers, competitors, and customers. In short, American investors must consider “foreign” companies to be part of their purview and the global economy an essential component of many “American” businesses.

全球贸易和投资的快速增长也带来了金融市场的全球化。美国境外的市场变得更大、更易于进入，许多国家采用了与美国类似的国际财务报告准则和证券法规。此外，全球托管机构的出现、结算成本降低以及电子交易方式的普及，降低了跨境投资的成本和麻烦。国际市场的增长导致美国在全球市值中的占比从1970年的70%下降到今天的40%。如果包含国际投资，美国投资者的投资机会几乎翻了一番。

<!--en-->
The rapid growth in global trade and investment has also ushered in the globalization of financial markets. Markets outside the United States have become larger and more accessible, and many countries have adopted uniform IFRS global accounting standards and securities regulations akin to those of the United States. In addition, the emergence of global custodians, reduced settlement costs, and access toelectronic trading have reduced the costs and hassles of cross-border investing. The growth of international markets has resulted in the U.S. share of global market capitalization falling from 70% in 1970 to 40% today. When you include international investments, the investment opportunity set for U.S. investors has almost doubled since the days of Graham and Dodd.

如果Graham和Dodd今天写《安全分析》，国际投资的讨论肯定会在书中占据重要位置。虽然更新原版并加入国际投资章节任务艰巨，但让文本具有时代性仍然至关重要。尽管本章由美国全球投资者撰写，但其视角适用于任何国际投资者。

<!--en-->
Were Graham and Dodd writing *Security Analysis* today, a discussion on international investing would surely figure prominently in their book. While the task of updating the original edition to include a section on international investing is daunting, it is nonetheless essential for the text to be made contemporary. Though this chapter has been written by U.S.-based global investors, the perspective it offers should be applicable to any international investor.

### 为何进行国际投资？

<!--en-->
*WHY INVEST INTERNATIONALLY?*

尽管金融市场全球化程度提高，但仍有必要思考为什么美国投资者要关注海外市场。毕竟，美国提供了丰富的金融投资选择，拥有庞大的市场、充足的流动性和低交易成本。这里有大量的研究和分析资料、严格的披露要求以及详细且可执行的法规。美国经济多年来表现良好，政治和社会框架稳定，还有完善的商业法律和可预测的法律体系。事实上，美国长期以来一直是投资者在不确定时期寻求“优质资产”时的“安全避风港”。

<!--en-->
Despite the increased globalization of financial markets, it is still reasonable to ask why U.S. investors should bother looking beyond their home market. After all, the United States offers a vast array of financial investments in an immense marketplace characterized by substantial liquidity and low transaction costs. There is an enormous range of research and analysis, substantial disclosure requirements, and detailed and enforceable regulations. The U.S. economy has fared well over the years, its political and social framework has been stable, and it has a well-established body of business law and a predictable legal system. Indeed, the United States has long been the “safe haven” to which investors retreat in any “flight to quality” during times of uncertainty.

今天，美国投资者考虑海外投资有两个重要原因。第一个是可能获得比美国更高的风险调整回报。在《安全分析》中，Graham和Dodd指出，市场中的非理性抛售及股权资本减少为价值投资者提供了机会。（第4章）在许多国际市场中，由于国内风险资本有限，这些因素更为严重，使得这些市场的股价比美国更波动。这为耐心长期的价值投资者提供了机会，以非常优惠的价格获得优秀企业的股票。

<!--en-->
There are two compelling reasons for U.S. investors today to consider investments abroad. The first is the possibility of earning higher risk-adjusted returns than are available in the United States. In *Security Analysis*, Graham and Dodd pointed out that irrational selling and the associated reduction of equity capital in a market produces bargains for value investors. (Chap. 4) These factors are exacerbated in many international markets due to limited domestic risk capital, andthis makes stock prices in these markets more volatile than in the United States. This can present opportunities for patient long-term value investors to acquire shares in great businesses at very attractive prices.

第二个原因是，国际投资组合能够实现多元化，降低整体波动性，同时提高收益。有句谚语说：“美国打喷嚏，世界就感冒”；实际上，许多外国经济体的商业周期和市场周期并不总是与美国同步。国际投资提供了一个机会：当美国表现不佳时，国际投资可以表现出积极态势。尽管过去十年美国一直是表现最好的市场，但这种情况不一定会一直持续。事实上，自1950年以来大部分时间里，美国市场的表现都低于按权重平均的全球发达市场股票组合。⁴

<!--en-->
The second reason is that an international portfolio provides diversification that reduces overall volatility while enhancing returns. There is a saying that when the United States sneezes, the world catches cold; in reality, many foreign economies have business cycles—and market cycles—that are not always aligned with those in the United States. International investments provide an opportunity to zig when the United States zags. Although the United States has been the top-performing market over the past decade, this certainly will not always be the case. Indeed, for most of the decades since 1950, the U.S. market has underperformed an equal-weighted global basket of developed market stocks.⁴

### 国际市场的内在价值

<!--en-->
*INTRINSIC VALUE IN INTERNATIONAL MARKETS*

那些支持投资国际市场的人必须面对由此带来的分析挑战。评估国际市场上证券的内在价值比在美国更为困难。在《证券分析》中，格雷厄姆和多德指出了评估内在价值时的三个障碍。（第1章）第一个障碍是数据不足或错误，他们认为这对美国市场来说不是最重要的障碍，并得出结论：“故意篡改数据的情况很少”，因为“受到监管规定的影响”。虽然这对美国市场可能并不完全准确，但在许多国际市场中，获得充分且正确的数据确实是一个更大的挑战。更宽松的会计制度和监管执行要求管理层有更多空间在海外操纵或伪造财务结果，例如Wirecard（2020）⁵或Steinhoff（2017）⁶中的著名欺诈案。分析师在分析国际公司的账簿和记录时必须小心，寻找可疑行为的迹象，如异常反复出现的费用或其他关联方交易、可疑的诉讼模式以及频繁的大额内部股东交易。此外，高通胀、货币贬值以及资产和负债之间的货币不匹配，使得国际资产负债表难以用于确定内在价值和清算价值。

<!--en-->
Those who accept the case for investing in international markets must then grapple with the analytical challenges this presents. Assessing the intrinsic value of a security in international markets can be more difficult than in the United States. In *Security Analysis*, Graham and Dodd identify three obstacles in assessing intrinsic value. (Chap. 1) The first, inadequate or incorrect data, is an obstacle that they found to be the least important for the U.S. market, concluding that “deliberate falsification of data is rare” due to “the result of regulations.” While this may not be entirely accurate for the U.S. market, the availability of adequate and correct data is certainly a bigger challenge in many international markets. More lenient accounting practices and regulatory enforcement provide managements more leeway to manipulate or falsify financial results abroad, such as in the cases of prominent frauds like Wirecard (2020)⁵ or Steinhoff (2017).⁶ Analysts must take care when analyzing the books and records of international companies, looking for telltale signs of questionable practices, ranging from unusual recurringcharges or other related party transactions, suspicious patterns of litigation, and large and frequent insider share transactions. In addition, high inflation, currency devaluations, and currency mismatches between assets and liabilities make international balance sheets less useful for determining intrinsic and liquidation values.

格雷厄姆和多德将“未来的不确定性”称为确定内在价值的第二个挑战。动荡的经济环境、巨大的货币风险以及法规和政治方面的意外变化，使得美国以外的许多国家预测未来更加困难。

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd name “uncertainties of the future” as the second challenge in determining intrinsic value. Volatile economies, substantial currency risks, and unexpected changes in regulations and politics make predicting the future more challenging in many countries outside the United States.

格雷厄姆和多德指出的第三个挑战是：如果“市场的非理性行为”持续足够长的时间，那么在此期间公司基本面的变化可能导致证券的内在价值下降。这种风险在国际市场，尤其是发展中市场更为严重，不仅因为额外的宏观经济和金融风险，还因为控股股东可能采取损害小股东的行动。

<!--en-->
The third challenge Graham and Dodd identify is the risk that should “the irrational behavior of the market” persist long enough, then a security’s intrinsic value could decline due to changes in a company’s fundamentals in the interim. This risk is enhanced in international and especially developing markets, not only because of added macroeconomic and financial risks, but also due to potential actions by a controlling shareholder that can harm minority shareholders.

简而言之，显然国际市场的投资风险更大，这使得确定内在价值更加困难，其稳定性也更容易受到威胁。虽然投资管理良好的优质公司是对这些高风险的重要缓解措施，但谨慎的投资者在投资外国证券时，必须要求更高的内在价值折扣——更大的安全边际。

<!--en-->
In short, it is evident that investment risks are greater in international markets, which makes the determination of intrinsic value more difficult and its persistence more vulnerable. While investing in high quality companies with strong management is an important mitigant to these elevated risks, a prudent investor must demand a larger discount to intrinsic value—a greater margin of safety—when investing in a foreign security.

在国际市场寻求更大安全边际的另一个原因是，流动性不足和资本流动不稳定导致的更大波动性。这种波动性不仅限于新兴市场。阿姆斯特丹、布鲁塞尔和北欧国家的小规模市场由少数大型公司主导；这些市场中的其他上市公司只吸引有限的投资者兴趣。这些因素可能导致市场价格低于美国典型的内在价值水平。如图1所示，1998-1999年和2001-2002年，新兴市场的市盈率比美国市场低50%至60%。相反，在1995-1996年和2013年左右，新兴市场的价格与美国市场持平甚至更高。目前，市盈率约为40%至50%。这种估值高低波动为有纪律的投资者提供了机会，他们能够应对这种波动性。

<!--en-->
Another reason to seek greater margin of safety in international markets is the greater volatility caused by thin liquidity and more fickle capital flows. This volatility is not limited to emerging markets. The small markets of Amsterdam, Brussels, and the Nordic countries are dominated by a few major companies; the other listed companies in these markets attract only limited investor interest. These factors can drive market prices to deeper discounts to intrinsic value than is typical in the United States. As Figure 1 indicates, emerging markets traded at price-earnings multiples that were at a 50% to 60% discount to the U.S. market during 1998–1999 and 2001–2002. Conversely, during 1995–1996 and around 2013, emerging markets traded at parity or even a premium to the U.S. markets. As we write this, the current discount is 40% to 50%. These swings between undervalued and overvalued is a source of opportunity for disciplined investors who can handle the volatility.
