### 公共与私人投资的交汇点：一个案例研究

<!--en-->
*At the Intersection of Public and Private Investing: A Case Study*

作者：大卫·艾布拉姆斯 投资的目的是吃得好、睡得好，以不会威胁自身偿付能力或导致不安夜晚的方式获利。这就是《安全分析》的核心思想。其保守投资建议历经多代人的验证——实际上，正是因为自1934年本书首次出版以来发生的巨大变化。

<!--en-->
by David Abrams
The goal of investing is to eat well and sleep well, to generate profits in a way that never threatens your solvency or causes you a restless night. That is the essence of *Security Analysis*. Its prescription for conservative investing has served many generations well, despite—or, in fact, because of—the dramatic changes that have transpired since this book was first published in 1934.

在这些页面中，格雷厄姆和多德建议投资者持续寻求安全边际。这样做不是可盲目填入数字的公式，而是一种心态，有助于最小化损失概率并最大化收益。购买稳定资产的人主要关注折价进入价格，这意味着风险较低，潜在回报更高。购买股票（无论是公开交易还是私有企业）的人必须考虑许多定性因素，如管理团队的能力、公司的稳定性与增长前景、进入壁垒的程度、各利益相关方利益是否一致（或缺乏一致性），以及公司能否明智地分配资本。格雷厄姆和多德对这些无形资产持谨慎态度，更倾向于使用具体数字，如资产负债表或损益表上的数据，以及可识别的事实，如债务工具的条款。他们写道：“定量因素比定性因素更适合彻底分析。”（第2章）我们都是时代的产物。正如詹姆斯·格兰特所指出的，《安全分析》第一版诞生于经济萧条的背景下，随后很快引发了第二次世界大战；当时美国失业率超过25%，且股市在1929年高峰与1932年低谷之间下跌了87%。在这次崩盘及随后的大萧条之后，一代投资者几乎全军覆没，格雷厄姆和多德对股票投资极为谨慎。为了帮助读者避免同样的毁灭性损失，作者建议他们支付的金额应低于“净营运资本”的三分之二。¹以如此低的价格购买公司实物资产，很难亏损，尤其是如果能组合一系列同样被低估的证券来分散风险、降低单一企业带来的风险。然而，这种方法将运营公司变成了资产投资，这种策略在1934年很有意义，但现在已不再适用。如今股票以非常低的价格交易，通常是因为背后的企业正面临生存危机。

<!--en-->
Throughout these pages, Graham and Dodd advise investors to continually seek a margin of safety. Doing so is not a formula into which numbers can be blindly inserted; it is a mindset that helps one minimize the probability of loss and maximize gain. Those who buy stable assets focus mostly on a discounted entry price, which means less risk is incurred and greater potential return is available. Those who purchase companies, either publicly traded stocks or privately held enterprises, must weigh many qualitative considerations, such as the competency of management, the stability of the company and its growth prospects, the degree to which barriers to entry exist, the alignment of interests among the various constituencies (or lack thereof), and the ability of the company to allocate capital intelligently. Graham and Dodd were wary of these intangibles and preferred hard numbers, like entries on a balance sheet or income statement, and discernible facts, such as the terms of a debt instrument. Indeed, they wrote that “the quantitative factors lend themselves far better to thoroughgoing analysis than the qualitative factors.” (Chap. 2)
We are all products of our times. As James Grant has noted, the first edition of *Security Analysis* came into the world amid the challenging backdrop of economic depression and the sparks that would soon ignite into World War II, atime when national unemployment in the United States topped 25%, and in the immediate aftermath of a stock market crash that had seen the market plunge 87% between its 1929 peak and 1932 nadir. After this crash and the ensuing Great Depression that had just wiped out an entire generation of investors, Graham and Dodd approached stocks with extreme caution. To help their readers avoid the same devastating losses, the authors recommended they pay less than two-thirds of “net working capital.”¹ Buying at such a discount to the value of a company’s hard assets makes it difficult to lose money, especially if a portfolio of similarly undervalued securities can be assembled to diversify and mitigate the risk of owing a single enterprise. This approach, however, turns operating companies into asset plays, a strategy that made sense in 1934, but no longer does. When today’s stocks trade at a very distressed price, it’s typically because the underlying business is facing an existential struggle.

格雷厄姆和多德区分了投资与投机。“投资”他们写道，“基于过去，而投机则主要着眼于未来。”（第4章）然而，购买持续经营的公司（这是大多数投资者的做法）的人不得不考虑未来，并应对至少与价格同等重要的定性问题。²要求安全边际的目的是让结果对投资者有利。较高的初始估值并不保证糟糕的结果；只是降低了这种可能性。同样，平庸的管理、糟糕的资本配置和利益不协调并不能确保失败，但会降低成功的机会。相反，优秀的领导力、明智的资本运用和一致的利益关系则对投资者有利。尽管格雷厄姆和多德不愿考虑这些无形且有时短暂的因素，我认为《安全分析》中提出的保守原则可以也应该应用于它们。这样做是在当今投资环境中创造安全边际的一部分。

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd distinguished between investing and speculation. “Investment,” they wrote, “is grounded in the past whereas speculation looks primarily to the future.” (Chap. 4) Yet those who buy ongoing companies (which is what most investors do) have no choice but to contemplate the future and to wrestle with qualitative issues that are at least as important as price.² The purpose of demanding a margin of safety is to tip the odds in favor of the investor. A high going-in valuation does not guarantee a bad result; it just makes it less likely. Likewise, mediocre management, lousy capital allocation, and misaligned interests do not ensure failure, but they do lower the chances of success. Conversely, excellent leadership, intelligent capital deployment, and aligned interests put the wind at the investor’s back. Though Graham and Dodd were reticent to take these intangible and sometimes ephemeral factors into consideration, I believe the conservative principles espoused in *Security Analysis* can and should be applied to them. Doing so is part of creating a margin of safety in today’s investment landscape.

虽然这本书的核心主题仍然至关重要，但这些理念的实际应用随着时间必然发生变化。市场不断变动和发展。信息迅速传播；导致价格与价值之间存在巨大差距的情况很快被利用，随后迅速消失。发现有利细分市场的人通常会进一步利用它。这为资产类别带来额外资金，扩大其吸引力，加速机会窗口的关闭。在我自己的职业生涯中，我见过多次这样的机会出现又消失。

<!--en-->
While this book’s central themes remain critically important, the deployment of those ideas has necessarily changed over time. Markets shift and evolve. Information israpidly disseminated; dislocations that cause large discrepancies between price and value are rapidly exploited and then quickly disappear. Those who discover a profitable niche usually attempt to exploit it further. This brings additional capital to the asset class, spreads the word of its attractiveness, and hastens the closing of that window of opportunity. I have seen several such opportunities come and go during my own career.

在我来到华尔街之前的几年里，高盛的格斯·莱维等人意识到，一旦一家公司成为收购目标，投资者往往会毫不犹豫地抛售股票，留下“少量”资金。莱维明白，以20美元购买一家公司，然后以21美元被收购所获得的利润，能带来高年化回报，足以弥补交易失败带来的损失。这种情况适合分析，但并非每个人都能胜任。但当我来到华尔街，在一家精品公司合并套利部门工作时，局势已经基本形成。人们知道通过风险套利可以获得丰厚利润，于是从事这一策略的公司纷纷出现。不久之后，大部分超额收益都被挤掉，是时候寻找新的机会了。

<!--en-->
Years before I arrived on Wall Street, people like Gus Levy of Goldman Sachs figured out that once a company had become the subject of a takeover bid, investors would tend to dump the stock without much thought, leaving a “small” amount of money on the table. Levy understood that the dollar of profit gained by buying a company at $20 before it was to be acquired for $21 produced a high annualized return that more than compensated for the losses that occurred when deals fell apart. Such situations lent themselves to analysis that not everyone was equipped to perform. But by the time I got to Wall Street, where my first job was in the merger arbitrage department of a boutique firm, the jig was practically up. Word had gotten out that juicy profits could be had in risk arbitrage, and so firms dedicated to the strategy sprang up. Within a short while, most of the excess returns had been squeezed out and it was time to seek another hunting ground.

在20世纪80年代中期到晚期，大多数投资者都回避破产和困境中的证券。许多机构制定了内部规则，要求公司在破产或评级低于投资级时出售债券。此外，第11章程序的复杂性也促使许多人选择将处理过程交给他人。储蓄与贷款危机、1990-1991年的经济衰退以及德雷塞尔伯纳姆兰普顿的破产，导致市场上买家稀少，大量债券涌现。优质资产和公司可以以低价购买。成功的投资公司成立，职业生涯开始，财富积累。就像风险套利一样，人才和资金涌入，成立了负责购买困境债券的基金。如今，这些轻松机会早已消失，困境投资领域变得竞争异常激烈。

<!--en-->
In the mid-to-late 1980s, bankrupt and distressed securities were shunned by most investors. Many institutions had adopted internal rules forcing them to sell a company's bonds when it went bankrupt or got downgraded below investment grade. Furthermore, the complexity of Chapter 11 encouraged many to leave the court process and haggling to others. The savings and loan crisis, the recession of 1990–1991, and the bankruptcy of Drexel Burnham Lambert created a flood of bonds in a market with few buyers. Great assets and companies could be bought at bargain prices. Successful investment firms were formed, careers launched, and fortunes made. As with risk arbitrage, talent and capital rushed in, and funds were created with mandates to buy distressed bonds. Today, those easy pickings are long gone, and the world of distressed investing has become fiercely competitive.

在继续寻找有吸引力的投资时，近年来我开始积极追求私人资产。许多投资者认为公开投资和私人投资是相互独立的世界，但对我来说，两者的界限最差也是模糊的，往往不存在。两者基本原则相同，行业内的机会可以在其中找到，一种经验可以应用于另一种领域。我还了解到，在公开和私人资产之间切换可以帮助找到那些非有形因素更可能起到助力而非阻碍作用的投资，从而提高安全边际。世界上一些最成功的投资者，如沃伦·巴菲特，拥有灵活的指令。我的公司Abrams Capital已长期参与汽车零售业务——17年有余——这说明了这一点，也凸显了流动资产与非流动资产之间的某些权衡。

<!--en-->
As I continued the search for attractive investments, in recent years I have begun actively pursuing private assets. Many investors see public and private investing as separate and distinct worlds, but to me the line between them is blurry at best and often nonexistent. The fundamental principles of each are the same, opportunities within an industry can be found in both, and wisdom gleaned in one can be applied in the other. I have also learned that moving between public and private holdings can help one find investments whose intangible factors are more likely to act as a tailwind than a headwind, and thereby increase the margin of safety. Some of the most successful investors in the world, those such as Warren Buffett, enjoy a flexible mandate. The longtime involvement of my own firm, Abrams Capital—17 years and counting—in auto retailing illustrates this and highlights some of the trade-offs between liquid and illiquid assets.

2005年，Abrams Capital购买了两家公开交易的汽车零售公司的股份，因为这些股票的交易价格非常低，且我们对这家企业的看法比华尔街更高。当然，经销商负责销售和维修汽车。销售汽车具有波动性，这使得该业务难以估值，而维修则稳定、可预测且盈利。我们认为市场过于关注前者，忽视后者。在研究行业时，我们遇到了大卫·罗森伯格，他一生都在汽车行业工作。他的父亲伊拉是传奇汽车经销商，在新英格兰经营着知名连锁店，大卫在青少年时期就在那里工作过。我们第一次见到他时，他是我们拥有的公司之一——第一集团汽车公司的经理。他加深了我们对业务的了解，我们也建立了友谊。作为企业家的大卫，一两年后离开第一集团，希望找到经销商进行收购运营。不久他达成协议，从克莱尔家族手中购买11家分店和两家修理厂。其族长厄尼·克莱尔去世后，把店铺留给了子女，但他们并不热爱这份事业，运营陷入困境，利润减少，几年后他们准备退出。大卫需要资金完成交易，便向我们寻求融资。

<!--en-->
In 2005, Abrams Capital bought shares in two publicly traded auto retailers because the stocks were trading at bargain multiples and we had a higher opinion of the business than Wall Street did. Dealerships, of course, sell and repair cars. Selling cars is volatile, which makes this part of the business difficult to value, but fixing them is stable, predictable, and lucrative. We believed the market was too focused on the former, not enough on the latter. When researching the industry, we came across David Rosenberg, who has spent his life in the automobile business. His father, Ira, was a legendary auto dealer who operated a well-known chain in New England, and David had worked there as a teenager. When we first met him, he was a manager for Group 1 Automotive, one of the companies we owned. He deepened our understanding of the business, and we struck up a friendship. An entrepreneur at heart, David left Group 1 a year or two later, hoping to find dealerships to purchase and run. He soon reached an agreement to buy 11 franchises and two body shops from the Clair family. Its patriarch, Ernie Clair, had left the stores to his children when he died, but their heart wasn’t in it, operations languished, profits shrank, and within a few years they were ready to exit. David needed capital to complete the deal and approached us about providing it.

大卫认为这些特许经营企业业绩严重不佳，他认为自己可以扭转局面。这些年来我听过很多方案，其中收购方声称他们能让公司重新焕发生机，因为之前的管理层工作很糟糕。通常，期望的改善并不会实现，所以我对大卫的说法持怀疑态度。他逐条向我们解释他的分析，并说明如何在这里节省25万美元，在那里再节省50万美元。所有变化似乎都不难。尽管价格相对于公司当时的盈利水平较高，我们还是决定支持他。交易完成后，公司更名为Prime Motor Group。

<!--en-->
David believed the franchises were dramatically underperforming and thought he could turn them around. I have heard many pitches over the years, during which the buyer claims she or he can breathe life into a company's operations because prior management had done a poor job. Often, the hoped-for improvements don't materialize, so I was skeptical of David's claims. He took us through his analysis line by line and showed us how $250,000 could be saved here, another $500,000 there. None of the changes seemed difficult. We decided to back him even though the price was high relative to the company's then-current earnings. After closing, the company was renamed Prime Motor Group.

据报道，沃伦·巴菲特说过，你应该购买任何傻瓜都能管理的企业，因为最终总会有傻瓜来管理。但商业中无法去除人为因素。客户、员工和交易对手都必须被管理。此外，世界常常带来没有标准答案的挑战，个人必须运用判断力来制定定制解决方案。资本主义是竞争性的，许多企业都面临威胁。应对威胁需要情报、创造力和技能。领导力很重要。一些首席执行官，如大卫·罗森伯格，比其他人更有才华。企业管理就像复利，微小的回报率差异最终会导致截然不同的结果。在短期内，有能力的管理团队与无能的团队所取得的结果可能几乎无法区分，但从长远来看，有才能的管理者会取得巨大成就，普通管理者则只能勉强维持，最差的管理者则会把公司推向悬崖。然而，区分好坏并不容易。任何登上企业高层的人，即使不是超级明星，也肯定具备政治或演讲能力。企业管理者意识到投资者想听到什么，往往会调整言辞和演示方式以吸引听众。尽管听起来很精心策划，上市公司的声明很少反映其管理层的真实想法。这掩盖了管理的真实意图，使外部投资者难以正确判断和信任他们。

<!--en-->
Warren Buffett has reportedly said that you should buy a business any fool could run because eventually one will. But the human element can't be removed from commerce. Customers, employees, and counterparties must all be managed. Furthermore, the world often presents challenges for which there is no textbook answer, and individuals must exercise their judgment to develop custom solutions. Capitalism is competitive, and many businesses find their firms under attack. Fending off threats takes intelligence, creativity, and skill. Leadership matters. Some CEOs—such as David Rosenberg—are more talented than others. The management of companies is not unlike compound interest, where small differentials in rates of return eventually yield vastly disparate outcomes. The gap between what a capable executive team and an incompetent one achieve might be barely discernible in the short term, but in the long run talented managers soar, average ones muddle along, and the worst drive their companies off the cliff. Determining the good from the bad, however, is not easy. Someone who's risen to the top of the corporate ladder surely possesses political and oratorical skills even if she or he isn't a superstar. Aware of what investors want to hear, corporate managers tend to craft their words and presentations to resonate with their audience. Despite sounding polished, the pronouncements from public companies rarely reflect the unvarnished opinions of its executives. This obscures management's true thoughts and makes it hard for outside investors to correctly judge and trust them.

拥有私人公司，如Prime Motor Group，的一个好处是投资者可以非常确定地了解团队是否强大。投资者与董事会成员以及经理（通常也是重要投资者）的对话几乎总是诚实的。正面和负面问题都会坦诚讨论。复杂问题的讨论也很坦率。通过这种对话，投资者可以判断经理是否擅长定量和定性分析。在私人公司中，投资者可以依赖言谈和行动；在上市公司中，则更需重视行动。

<!--en-->
One benefit of owning private companies, such as Prime Motor Group, is that the investor gets to know with a great degree of certainty whether the team is strong. The conversations investors have with board members and with managers (who are typically also significant investors) are almost always honest. Negatives and positives are discussed candidly. Deliberations of difficult issues are frank. Privy to this dialogue, an investor can determine whether the managers are facile with both quantitative and qualitative analyses. In private companies, an investor can rely on both words and actions; in public companies, more weight must be placed on deeds.

决定公司吸引力的另一个关键因素是其合理分配资本的能力。来自运营的资金可以重新投入业务、投资其他项目或返还给股东。善于使用现金的企业为所有者创造价值，而使用不当则破坏财富。对于上市公司来说，很难知道他们的投资是否明智，或者管理层是否在损害股东利益进行帝国建设。对一家公司是否做出明智决策有深入了解的投资者，可能比市场能更清晰地预见未来。拥有私人汽车经销商让我们看到了汽车零售行业的机会，显著提升了Prime Motor Group的价值。后来，这些知识让我们有信心对两家上市公司Lithia和Asbury作出承诺。

<!--en-->
Another crucial factor in determining the attractiveness of a company is its ability to allocate capital intelligently. Funds generated from operations can be plowed back into the business, invested in other ventures, or returned to shareholders. Enterprises that deploy cash well create value for owners, while those that do it poorly destroy wealth. With public companies, it can be hard to know if their investments are thoughtful, or whether management is engaged in empire building at the expense of shareholders. An investor who has insights into whether a company is making sound decisions may be able to peer into the future with greater clarity than the market can. Owning private car dealerships opened our eyes to opportunities in the auto-retailing industry that dramatically increased the value of Prime Motor Group. Later, this knowledge gave us the confidence to make commitments to two public companies, Lithia and Asbury.

在我们拥有Prime Motor Group期间，我们了解了很多关于汽车经销商收购市场的知识。例如，行业中的大多数交易都需要制造商的批准，因此必须拥有良好的业绩记录和声誉才能获得这种同意。这一要求限制了买家数量。此外，一些卖家直接进行交易，无需中间人。因此，个人关系可以带来以优惠价格获得经销商的机会。最后，也有办法在看似成熟的业务中进行有利投资。有一天，David告诉我们，梅赛德斯-奔驰曾与科德角地区的经销商公司陷入纠纷，最终演变为诉讼，但双方现在准备和解。为了解决这一问题，梅赛德斯希望Prime Motor Group购买科德角那个规模较小的经销商公司，因为该公司没有太大发展潜力，本身也不具有吸引力。然而，作为交易的一部分，Prime Motor Group将获准在波士顿南岸建造新的梅赛德斯经销商店。这需要建设新设施。此外，Prime Motor Group将在新经销商店开始盈利前经历几年的运营亏损。设施和运营亏损的总成本意味着巨大的投资，但我们相信最终会实现盈利。

<!--en-->
We learned a lot about the acquisition market for car dealers during the time we owned Prime Motor Group. For example, most transactions in the industry require approval from the manufacturer, so it's necessary to have a successful track record and a good reputation to obtain that consent. This requirement limits the number of buyers. In addition, some sellers transact without an intermediary. Thus personal relationships can yield opportunities to acquire dealerships at attractive prices. Finally, there can be ways to profitably invest in a seemingly mature business. One day David told us that Mercedes-Benz had been embroiled in a dispute with adealership on Cape Cod that had devolved into litigation, but the parties were now ready to settle. To resolve the situation, Mercedes wanted Prime Motor Group to buy the small Cape Cod franchise, which didn't have much upside and wouldn't have been interesting in and of itself. As part of the deal, however, Prime Motor Group would be allowed to build a new Mercedes dealership on Boston's south shore. This required the construction of a new facility. Moreover, Prime Motor Group would incur a couple of years of operating losses before the new dealership turned a profit. Together, the cost of the facility and the operating losses meant a significant investment, yet we were confident it would ultimately be profitable. It was.

当我们首次收购Prime Motor Group时，我们专注于改善现有运营。后来我们意识到通过资本配置可以创造巨大价值，于是将所有利润再投资于房地产和收购项目长达10年。这些投资获得了丰厚回报。在我们的管理下，Prime成为新英格兰第二大经销商集团，也是全国50大集团之一。

<!--en-->
When we first purchased Prime Motor Group, we focused on improving the existing operations. After we realized how much value could be created through capital allocation, we reinvested all the profits into real estate and acquisitions for 10 years. These investments paid off handsomely. Under our stewardship, Prime became the second-largest dealership group in New England and one of the 50 largest in the country.

在持有Prime Motor Group期间，由于框架协议的限制，我们被禁止购买公开上市的汽车经销商股票。³2017年，在我们退出后不久，这些限制被解除，我们重新关注公开上市经销商。Lithia Motors有收购表现不佳的经销商并提升其业绩的历史——这与Prime Motor Group最初采用的策略相同。再加上Lithia的盈利增长记录以及管理层持有大量股份的情况，我们决定对该公司进行大规模投资。如果我们还没有拥有Prime Motor Group，我们可能会对Lithia激进的收购行为持谨慎态度，并质疑其资本配置计划是否合理。

<!--en-->
While we held Prime Motor Group, we were prohibited from buying shares in public auto dealers due to restrictions imposed by framework agreements.³ In 2017, shortly after we exited, these restrictions were lifted and we turned our attention back to publicly traded dealers. Lithia Motors had a history of buying underperforming dealerships and improving their performance—the same strategy Prime Motor Group first pursued. This, along with Lithia's track record of growing its earnings and management's ownership of a significant amount of stock, prompted us to make a large investment in that company. Had we not already owned Prime Motor Group, we probably would have been wary of Lithia's aggressive pursuit of acquisitions and doubted that its capital-allocation program made sense.

流动证券与非流动证券的最大区别在于，公开证券每天都有交易。投资中最具挑战性的部分是心理层面。市场波动常常引发强烈的贪婪和恐惧情绪。金钱是一个复杂的话题。无论你是投资自己的储蓄、管理大型捐赠基金还是管理对冲基金，你都必须应对自己的心态，以及家人、社区成员（如教职工、校友、董事会）和客户的心态。在帮助投资者理性思考市场走势时，Graham和Dodd强调，股票是对公司的一部分所有权，市场用他们常引用的话来说，短期内是投票机，长期则是称重机。拥有私人公司强化了这样一个观点：*所有*股票都是企业的一部分所有权，而不仅仅是屏幕上闪烁的代码。

<!--en-->
The biggest difference between liquid and illiquid securities, of course, is that public securities are traded daily. The most challenging part of investing is psychological. Market fluctuations often stimulate strong feelings of, yes,greed and fear. Money is a fraught topic. Whether you are investing your own savings, overseeing a large endowment, or managing a hedge fund, you must grapple with not only your own state of mind but also that of your family members, other community constituents (e.g., faculty, alumni, boards), and clients. In trying to help investors think intelligently about market movements, Graham and Dodd stressed that stocks are fractional ownership interests in companies and that the market is, in their oft-quoted phrase, a voting machine in the short term but a weighing machine in the long run. Owning private companies reinforces the idea that *all* equities are fractional interests in businesses, not just ticker symbols flashing on a screen.

私人投资的一个悖论是，无法出售也可能有积极的一面。企业经常遭遇不幸。我们对Prime Motor Group的初始投资是在2007年底进行的。我半开玩笑地告诉人们，该公司在经济衰退开始前大约五分钟关闭了。第二年，市场和经济都非常糟糕，没有哪个行业受到的影响比汽车行业更大。汽车经销商通过一种称为地面规划融资的结构来融资库存。像他们通常那样，当市场暴跌时，银行感到恐慌。危机期间的一天，我们的地面规划贷款机构打电话要求立即还款。如果我们被迫偿还贷款，公司将面临严重的财务困境，可能不得不申请破产保护。幸运的是，银行没有权利调用贷款，到债务到期时，危机已经过去，公司运营良好，贷款机构也愿意继续提供信贷。

<!--en-->
One paradox of private investing is that there can be a silver lining in *not* being able to sell. Bad things frequently happen to businesses. Our initial investment in Prime Motor Group was made at the end of 2007. I half-jokingly tell people that it closed about five minutes before the recession began. The next year was brutal for the markets and the economy, and no industry was hit harder than the automotive sector. Auto dealers finance their inventory through a structure called floor-plan financing. As is their tendency, the banks freaked out when the markets swooned. One day in the middle of the crisis, our floor-plan lender called and asked for immediate repayment. Had we been forced to pay off the loan, the company would have suffered severe financial distress and might have sought bankruptcy protection. Fortunately, the bank had no right to call the loan, and by the time the debt matured, the crisis had passed, the company was performing well, and the lender was happy to keep extending credit.

我们拥有Prime Motor Group超过十年，赚取了巨额利润。如果能在恐慌期间选择出售，我们或许会因恐惧而抛售股票。持有私人企业意味着必须应对道路上的不可避免的困难，不能急于脱身。这让我们在投资组合中的公共企业遭遇动荡时，能够保持长期视角。

<!--en-->
We owned Prime Motor Group for more than a decade and made many times our money. If we had had the option to sell during the panic, we might have succumbed to fear and dumped the stock. Owning private companies means you must ride out the inevitable bumps in the road and not seek a quick exit. This has helped condition us to take a longer view when the public enterprises in our portfolio experience turbulence.

在Abrams Capital，我们增加的耐心产生了有趣的效果。我注意到，与一些公共企业的高层管理者关系，已变得与我们与私人企业领导人的关系类似。目前我们持有股份的几家公共企业，在进行重大交易前都会定期寻求我们的意见；甚至有一位首席执行官要求我的合作伙伴加入其董事会，尽管我们没有主动请求席位。我认为，通过我们的行动和言论传达了我们的长期视角，管理者也给出了积极回应。

<!--en-->
At Abrams Capital, our increased patience has had an interesting effect. I have noticed that our relationships with thetop managers at some of our public companies have become more like the ones we have with the leaders of our private companies. Several public companies in which we hold shares now regularly seek our input before engaging in major transactions, and one CEO asked one of my partners to join his board even though we had not requested a seat. I believe what has happened is that we have communicated our long-term perspective through our actions and words, and managers have responded positively.

尽管上市证券存在心理挑战，但股票本身可以成为一种资产。就在我们购买Lithia的同时，我们还收购了另一家公共汽车经销商Asbury Group，该公司有两个优势：首先，其首席执行官David Hult非常有才华，公司的运营指标处于行业领先水平；其次，Asbury采用了创造价值的资本配置策略，尽管其路径与Lithia不同。多年来，Asbury利用市场先生的情绪化（他似乎总是对行业不满），通过回购大量股份。从2005年到2020年，Asbury的每股收益从1.84美元增至12.89美元，几乎增长了七倍。其中近一半的增长得益于公司的股份回购计划，在这15年间，已发行股份从3300万降至1900万。

<!--en-->
Despite the psychological challenges that come with publicly traded securities, the price of a stock itself can be an asset. Around the same time that we purchased Lithia, we also bought another public auto dealer, Asbury Group, which had two things going for it. First, its CEO, David Hult, is quite talented; the company's operating metrics are among the best in the industry. Second, Asbury had pursued a capital-allocation strategy that created value, although its path was different than Lithia's. For many years, Asbury took advantage of Mr. Market's grumpiness (he seems to perpetually frown on the industry) by repurchasing a significant portion of its shares. Between 2005 and 2020, Asbury increased its earnings per share from $1.84 to $12.89, a nearly sevenfold jump. Almost half of that growth was due to the company's share-repurchase program, which slashed the number of outstanding shares from 33 million to 19 million over those 15 years.

当管理层、董事会和投资者的激励目标一致时，公司的表现通常会比不一致时更好——往往好得多。私人企业投资者可以要求管理者将大部分储蓄投入公司，并设计薪酬方案使管理者和投资者的利益同步变化。但在公共企业中，主要利益相关方往往无法步调一致。有些董事主要关心保护自己的酬金和维持其他董事的好感；有些管理者希望公司发展，无论对股东有何影响，因为管理更大的企业通常能增加他们的收入。结果，股东可能会感到被边缘化。经过观察私人企业中共享激励带来的巨大成果，我现在愿意为那些高层管理者明显致力于企业长期价值发展的公共企业支付更高价格。

<!--en-->
When the incentives of management, the board of directors, and investors are all aligned, a company's performance tends to be better—often vastly better—than when they are not. The private-company investor can insist that managers invest a significant portion of their savings in the company and structure compensation packages so that the fortunes of managers and investors rise or fall together. In public companies, though, the major constituencies frequently don't march to the beat of the same drum. Some directors are primarily interested in protecting their fees and staying in the good graces of their fellow board members; some managers want the company to grow, regardless of the impact on shareholders, because managing a larger enterprise typicallymakes their paycheck swell. As a result, shareholders can become disenfranchised. Having witnessed the powerful effect of shared incentives in achieving great outcomes at private companies, I am now willing to pay a premium for public ones whose top managers are clearly cultivating the long-term value of the business.

我认识到投资私人企业的诸多好处，但也有值得提及的缺点。与我们合作的人并非所有都是出色的管理者。其中有一些糟糕的管理者，比如一个CEO欺骗了公司和美国政府，导致公司破产。如果情况开始恶化，摆脱困境需要很长时间；每一天都是痛苦，直到你的股份消失。每天早晨走进办公室，看到形势摆在眼前，你不禁问自己：“我当时在想什么？我怎么可能这么愚蠢？”

<!--en-->
I have noted the many benefits of investing in private companies, but there are downsides worth mentioning. Not all the individuals with whom we’ve worked are exceptional as managers. Among the duds was a CEO who defrauded the company (and the U.S. government) and ran it into bankruptcy. If things start to go badly, it takes a very long time to get out; every day is misery until your stake is gone. You come into the office each morning with the position staring you in the face, and you can’t help but ask yourself, “What was I thinking? How *could* I have been so dumb?”

在我近40年的投资生涯中，我经历了许多挑战：直接欺诈、普遍无能、破坏价值的资本配置、市场崩盘、恐怖袭击、深度经济衰退、疫情等等。我见过行业巨头在几周内从巅峰跌至破产或濒临破产。我也看到投资者因熊市而心理崩溃。这些事件留下了深刻伤痕。投资比看起来更艰难。留在投资领域是成功的先决条件。Seth Klarman曾说，投资的秘密就是没有所谓的秘密。相反，努力工作、智力诚实和灵活的思维才是成功的关键。投资者必须随着世界变化调整策略，但记住Graham和Dodd的核心概念，并寻求安全边际——无论是公开还是私人证券——将使他们能够在始终不确定的未来中舒适投资。[^3495]: 1 定义为营运资金减去所有负债（即所谓净负债）。

<!--en-->
In my nearly 40 years of investing, I have experienced many challenges: outright fraud, general incompetence, value-destroying capital allocation, market crashes, terrorist attacks, deep recessions, a pandemic, and more. I have watched masters of the universe go from the top of the hill to bankruptcy—or reach the edge of it—in a matter of weeks. I have seen investors get psychologically broken by a bear market. These events have left deep scars. Investing is harder than it looks. Staying in the game is a prerequisite to success. Seth Klarman once said that the secret to investing is that there is no secret to investing. Instead, hard work, intellectual honesty, and a flexible mind are what fuel success. Investors must modify their tactics as the world changes, but keeping Graham and Dodd’s essential concepts in mind, and seeking a margin of safety—whether in public or private securities—will enable them to invest comfortably in the face of a future which is always uncertain.
[^3495]: 1 Defined as working capital less all liabilities (so-called net-nets).

2 具有讽刺意味的是，尽管格雷厄姆建议避免“猜测”，但他最成功的投资成就还是拥有Geico这家运营企业，这让他赚的钱比所有他喜爱的网络产品还要多。³ 大型经销商通常会与制造商签订框架协议。这些协议限制经销商可以拥有的制造商（如丰田）门店数量。目的是防止零售商对制造商拥有过大的权力。

<!--en-->
2 The irony is that, despite his advice to avoid “speculation,” Graham’s greatest investing triumph was his ownership in Geico, an operating business, which made him more money than all his beloved net-nets.
³ Large dealers often enter into framework agreements with manufacturers. These agreements limit the number of stores of a manufacturer (e.g., Toyota) the dealer can own. The purpose is to prevent the retailer from gaining too much power vis-à-vis the manufacturer.

### 捐赠基金管理原则与实践

<!--en-->
*Endowment Management Principles and Practices*

作者：Seth Alexander 27年前我开始投资生涯时，我认为《安全分析》更适合金融史学家而非现代投资者。这本书看起来很过时，属于更简单、早已过去的金融时代。现代投资者从阅读关于铁路债券和账面价值低于资产负债表有形资产价值的公司的投资描述中能学到什么呢？

<!--en-->
by Seth Alexander
When I started my investment career 27 years ago, I viewed *Security Analysis* as better suited for financial historians than modern-day investors. The book seemed quaint, belonging to a simpler and very much bygone era of finance. What could a modern-day investor learn from reading descriptions of investments in railroad bonds and companies trading for less than the value of the tangible assets on their balance sheet?

如今，我的视角完全不同。通过审视近一个世纪前的原则和见解而非投资理念，格雷厄姆和多德的经验变得清晰可见。虽然许多人只将格雷厄姆和多德与过时的投资案例联系在一起，但更准确地说，这些案例反映了他们当时的投资理念，而不是他们思维必然的结果。就像那位告诉我他用沃伦·巴菲特办公室的照片来布置办公桌，使其朝向窗户一样，我显然没有理解重点。

<!--en-->
Today, I have a very different perspective. By looking at principles and insights as opposed to investment ideas from nearly a century ago, the lessons of Graham and Dodd spring to life. While many people only associate Graham and Dodd with outdated investment examples, it is more accurate to characterize these examples as expressions of their investment philosophy using the opportunity set at that time, not the inevitable output of their thinking. Like the investment manager who told me he used a photograph of Warren Buffett's office to position his desk in the same orientation to the window, I had definitely been missing the point.

我是从捐赠基金投资者的角度来写这篇文章的。我是帮助投资麻省理工学院的金融资产的团队成员之一。像许多美国大学一样，麻省理工学院也有捐赠基金——由捐款形成的资金池，用于支付财务援助、教师工资和建筑维护等费用。每年，麻省理工学院会花费约5%的捐赠基金来支持这些及其他紧急需求。我们将剩余资金进行投资，希望获得足够的投资回报，以维持捐赠基金的购买力。我们的目标是以通胀调整后的水平，永久支持麻省理工学院，让未来的学者能够以同样的方式推动我们的思想发展，就像麻省理工学院的过去研究人员在抗癌、替代能源研究、太空探索等领域取得进展一样。如果长期通胀平均为3%，且我们每年花费5%，那么我们需要获得约8%的年化回报率才能实现这一目标。

<!--en-->
I write from the perspective of an endowment investor. I am part of the team that helps invest MIT's financial assets. Like many American universities, MIT has an endowment, a pool of capital built from donations that has been set aside to pay for things such as financial aid, faculty salaries, and building maintenance. Each year, MIT spends around 5% of its endowment to support these and other immediate needs. We invest the remaining capital in hopes of generating sufficient investment returns to maintain the purchasing power of the endowment. Our goal is to support MIT in perpetuity with the same level of resources on an inflation-adjusted basis, allowing future scholars to advance our thinking in the sameway past researchers at MIT have made advancements in fighting cancer, alternative energy research, space exploration, and much more. If, over the very long term, inflation averages 3% and we spend 5% per year, we need to earn roughly 8% annualized returns to meet this goal.

一本关于股票和债券投资的书籍，一开始可能看似无法提供关于管理捐赠基金的建议。捐赠基金很少直接购买证券，因为他们在这一领域存在明显的竞争劣势。大学无法与顶尖投资经理通常获得的报酬相媲美。大学缺乏全球市场交易速度所需的内部文化和快速决策机制。在大多数投资领域，捐赠基金很难与更专业的本地投资者竞争。例如，从马萨诸塞州剑桥的办公室，我们很难成为班加罗尔或拉各斯初创企业的主要投资者。

<!--en-->
A book about investing in stock and bond instruments may not at first appear to offer insights into managing an endowment. Endowments are rarely direct purchasers of securities, because they maintain significant competitive disadvantages in that world. Universities cannot match the compensation commonly paid to the elite ranks of investment managers. Universities lack the internal culture and fast decision-making processes needed to move at the speed of trading in global markets. In most investment arenas, endowments are poorly situated to compete with more specialized local investors. For example, we would struggle to be a leading investor in start-up companies in Bangalore or Lagos from our office in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

虽然捐赠基金可能不适合直接购买资产，但他们在与优秀的外部投资经理建立合作关系方面拥有独特的竞争优势。由于捐赠基金是一个稳定的资金池，它们非常适合那些需要稳定资金来源的投资经理。捐赠基金的时间范围与建立持久、有价值且互利的外部经理关系这一长期过程相匹配。令人惊讶的是，麻省理工学院保持着多个已有超过35年历史的活跃投资经理关系。大学捐赠基金有时可以通过满足投资经理支持我们教育卓越和前沿研究双重使命的需求，获得有限能力下的投资策略。庞大的校友、教师、家长和朋友社区提供了内部网络，帮助我们寻找并筛选新的投资经理。因此，大多数捐赠基金构建的是投资经理组合，而不是直接购买资产。捐赠基金投资人员适当专注于外部投资经理选择过程以及在这些经理之间分配资金，以获得所需的投资机会。

<!--en-->
While they may not be well-suited to buy assets directly, endowments maintain distinct competitive advantages in establishing partnerships with exceptional external investment managers. Because an endowment is a stable pool of funds, they are a good fit for investment managers looking for a steadfast source of capital through thick and thin. An endowment's time horizon matches the long process of building enduring, valuable, and mutually beneficial relationships with external managers. Amazingly, MIT maintains several active investment manager relationships that date back over 35 years. University endowments can sometimes gain access to capacity-constrained investment strategies by appealing to an investment manager's desire to support our twin missions of educational excellence and cutting-edge research. Large communities of alumni, faculty, parents, and friends provide a built-in network of people who help us find and diligence new investment managers. As a result, most endowments build portfolios of investment managers, rather than buying assets directly. Endowment investment staff appropriately focus their time on the externalinvestment manager selection process and the allocation of capital between these managers to gain desired exposures.

捐赠基金的优势自然使其投资组合与普通 401(k) 退休账户截然不同。凭借稳定的资本基础和长周期视角，捐赠基金能够与基金经理合作，实施长期、流动性较低的投资策略。捐赠基金可与经理们一起参与房地产资产重新开发、私人企业收购、可持续采伐林地以及风险资本初创企业投资等项目。这些领域的主要吸引力在于它们允许积极参与，使投资经理能够在市场基准回报之上创造价值。例如，我们可能会与一位房地产经理合作，他购买了一栋破旧、空置的建筑。如果经理能成功翻新并重新出租该建筑，即使当地市场租金保持平稳，他们仍可能获得可观回报。由于有这些增值机会以及能够容忍流动性不足的情况，捐赠基金将大部分投资组合分配给私募股权、风险资本和房地产策略，而非仅投资于传统的股票和债券策略，这并不罕见。

<!--en-->
An endowment's competitive advantages naturally lead to portfolios that look very different from your average 401(k) retirement account. With a stable capital base and a long time horizon, endowments are able to invest with fund managers pursuing long-duration, more illiquid investment strategies. Endowments can participate with managers in the redevelopment of real estate assets, the purchase of private businesses, the sustainable harvesting of timberlands, and investment in venture capital start-ups. The main attraction of these arenas is that they lend themselves to active involvement, allowing investment managers to add value above baseline market returns. For example, we might work with a real estate manager who purchases a run-down, half-empty building. If the manager can successfully refurbish and re-lease the building, they may be able to earn compelling returns, even if market rents in the area remain flat. As a result of these opportunities to add value and the ability to tolerate illiquidity, it is not uncommon for endowments to allocate a significant portion of their portfolios to private equity, venture capital, and real estate strategies, rather than investing only in more traditional stock and bond strategies.

然而，尽管存在这些差异，捐赠基金仍能从《安全分析》中学到很多。任何行业成功的关键之一，就是理解推动行为的自然力量，无论是积极还是消极的。在捐赠基金领域，准学术式的辩论规范和集体决策方式，有助于捐赠基金做出谨慎的长期决策。同时，决策几乎总是可以推迟一周而不产生明显影响，这往往导致诸如构建内部数据系统、寻找新经理等领域出现次优结果，而在这些领域，强烈的紧迫感本可带来更好的成果。了解自身自然倾向，并适当创建流程和文化规范来对抗这些倾向的捐赠基金，更有可能取得成功。

<!--en-->
Yet even with these differences, endowments can learn a great deal from *Security Analysis*. One of the keys to success in any industry is to understand the natural forces that drive behavior, for good or for bad. In the endowment world, for example, quasi-academic norms of debate and deliberate, collective decision-making help endowments make carefully considered long-term decisions. At the same time, the fact that decisions can almost always be postponed another week without discernable impact often leads to suboptimal outcomes in areas such as building internal data systems and new manager sourcing, where a strong sense of urgency might lead to better results. Endowments that understand their natural tendencies and create processes and cultural norms to lean against them, where appropriate, have a better chance of success.

在格雷厄姆和多德的股票筛选和直接资产购买领域，以及捐赠基金的管理人选择领域，导致次优结果的一个因素就是选择过多。投资者有机会从数十个行业和国家的数千种不同证券中选择（对于捐赠基金而言，则是与数千位不同的投资经理合作投资）。虽然拥有大量选择似乎有益，但人类本性往往会将这种丰富的选择转化为缺乏专注力，无法在其他市场参与者中建立竞争优势。我们的好奇心、对新事物的热爱，以及新信息（或新推文）带来的多巴胺刺激，让我们倾向于考虑太多想法、收集太多不重要的数据，讨论太多不可知或无关紧要的问题。结果，很少有投资者能够发展出明确的、差异化的专业能力，从而带来出色的投资成果。

<!--en-->
In the Graham and Dodd world of stock picking and direct asset purchases, and in the endowment world of manager selection, one feature of the investment landscape that leads to suboptimal outcomes is an overabundance of choice. Investors have the opportunity to select from among thousands of different securities across dozens of industries and countries (or in the case of endowments, invest with thousands of different investment managers.) While it would seem beneficial to have a significant number of choices, human nature unfortunately tends to translate this cornucopia of riches into a lack of focus and a resulting inability to develop a competitive advantage over other market participants. Our curiosity, love of novelty, and the dopamine rush of a new piece of information (or new twitter post) push us to look at too many ideas, collect too many unimportant pieces of data, and debate too many unknowable or irrelevant issues. As a result, very few investors develop the well-defined, differentiated expertise that leads to compelling investment outcomes.

《安全分析》的篇幅和深度为这种选择过多问题提供了解决方案。一页页地，格雷厄姆和多德描述并举例说明他们认为优秀投资应具备的特征、应避免的特征，以及如何研究和收集所需信息。这种独特的筛选机制通过聚焦格雷厄姆和多德所关注的少数公司和有限的信息范围，来对抗选择过多的问题。

<!--en-->
The length and depth of *Security Analysis* provides a solution to this excess of choice. In page after page, Graham and Dodd describe and provide examples of the characteristics they are looking for in a compelling investment, what characteristics to avoid, and how to research and collect needed information. This distinct filter leans back against the overabundance of choice by focusing Graham and Dodd on a rare set of companies and a circumscribed set of information to be examined.

在为我们捐赠基金选择杰出投资经理时，我们将这种投资筛选概念作为过程的第一步。按照我们的思路，优秀的投资筛选应具备几个特征。首先，筛选机制必须让经理能够快速排除绝大多数潜在投资。不难想象，格雷厄姆和多德会迅速排除大多数被他们认为过于投机、从事低质量业务或价格不显眼的证券，而是将全部注意力集中在可管理的机会上。

<!--en-->
When trying to select exceptional investment managers for our endowment, we use this concept of an investment filter as a first step in our process. In our way of thinking, a compelling investment filter has several characteristics. First, the filter must allow a manager to quickly discard the vast majority of potential investments on offer. One can easily imagine Graham and Dodd fairly rapidly dismissing most securities they examined as overly speculative, or engaged in a low-quality business endeavor, or not obviously inexpensive, instead directing their full attention to a manageable set of opportunities.

其次，良好的投资筛选机制自然会带来丰富的投资机会。那些通过筛选机制找到被忽视领域、误解行业、动态变化领域或能带来显著价值的资产的投资经理，更有可能发现具有吸引力的回报机会的证券。最后，良好的投资筛选机制必须与投资者的性格、资源和能力相匹配。投资者可能在硅谷最新的初创企业中看到机会，但如果没有必要的网络来早期发现公司、评估机会所需的技术背景、为创始人提供有价值建议的运营背景、帮助公司从某位投资者转向另一位投资者的成功历史记录，以及支持初创企业实现盈利所需的充足资金，那么无论潜在机会多么诱人，投资者都不太可能在这个领域取得成功。

<!--en-->
Second, a good investment filter should lead naturally to a good universe of opportunities. Investment managers whose filters lead them to out-of-favor areas, misunderstood industries, arenas of dynamic change, or assets where significant involvement can add value are more likely to find securities with attractive return prospects. Finally, a good investment filter must match an investor's temperament, resources, and capabilities. An investor may see opportunity in Silicon Valley's latest start-ups, but without the network needed to find the company early, the technical background needed to assess the opportunity, the operating background needed to offer valuable advice to the founders, the prior track record of success that helps convince companies to take capital from one investor over another, and the deep-pocketed capital base needed to support start-up companies to profitability, investors are unlikely to succeed in this arena no matter how compelling the underlying opportunity set.

我们投资组合中的一些经理使用“所有者-运营商”筛选机制。采用这种筛选机制的投资经理会寻找由有影响力的创始人领导、且创始人持有公司重要比例的公开上市公司。由于大型创始人持股情况很少，这些投资经理可以将精力和注意力集中在数量可控的潜在机会上。因为卓越的所有者-运营商在运营和资本分配决策中所带来的长期利益不一定体现在企业的历史或当前财务报表中，因此存在发现定价错误的证券的可能性。可以想象，在1965年审查沃伦·巴菲特所持有的伯克希尔哈撒韦的财务记录，很难获得关于后续股价表现的任何线索。要理解这样的商业领袖——能够深入了解管理层的动机、决策纪律、愿意走与其他人不同的道路、长期愿景以及其他更软的因素——所需的技能非常难以获得。在波动和业绩不佳期间保持对这类公司的关注所需的耐心非常罕见。因此，采用这种专注方式的投资经理可能能够发展出区别于其他市场参与者的专业优势。

<!--en-->
A few managers in our portfolio use an owner-operator filter. Investment managers with this filter search for publicly listed companies led by an involved founder who owns a meaningful percentage of the company. Because large founder ownership stakes are rare, these investment managers can focus their energy and attention on a manageable number of potential opportunities. Because the long-term benefits of an exceptional owner-operator driving operating and capital allocation decisions do not necessarily show up in the historic or current financial statements of a business, there exist good possibilities of finding mispriced securities. You can imagine that examining the financial records of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway in 1965 would have provided few clues as to the subsequent record of stock price performance. The skills required to underwrite such a business leader—an ability to develop a deep understanding of management's motivations, decision-making discipline, willingness to chart a different path than others, long-term vision, and other softer factors—are difficult to acquire. The patience needed to hold onto these companies through bouts of volatility and underperformance is rare. Consequently, investment managers with this focus may be able to develop differentiated expertisein owning these types of companies versus other market participants.

良好的投资筛选机制并非基于固定规则。有许多由创始人主导的上市公司最终被证明是糟糕的投资选择。投资经理也不太可能只依靠一种策略取得成功——他们需要发展其他见解和其他类型的专业知识。然而，从明确的投资筛选机制开始，可以让投资经理有效利用时间，发展专注的专业知识，谨慎扩展投资范围，而不受选择过多的困扰。

<!--en-->
Good investment filters are not rules based. There are many examples of founder-led public companies that turn out to be bad investments. Nor are investment managers likely to thrive as one-trick ponies—they will need to develop other insights and other types of expertise. Starting with a clear investment filter, however, allows an investment manager to spend their time well, develop a focused expertise, and thoughtfully expand their investment universe without suffering from the overabundance of choice.

就像格雷厄姆和多德提供的其他建议一样，良好投资筛选机制的好处看似显而易见，但根据我们的经验，很少有投资经理真正坚持严格的筛选机制。更常见的是看到经理的目标领域会根据当下形势而变化——当技术蓬勃发展时，他们会对软件公司感兴趣；当中国经济似乎陷入困境时，他们会关注中国公司；当通胀即将出现时，他们会关注石油和天然气股票。这些投资者通过筛选高投资者兴趣和大量投资者资金流动的领域，并通过改变焦点而非发展深入专业知识，使自己处于寻找投资机会的最不利位置。因为我们也试图避免这种缺乏纪律的情况，却仍然受到其影响，我们认为我们理解了原因——人类自然行为的特性。人类很难识别潜在的赚钱机会，却以专注于竞争优势领域为理由不去追求它们。在市场上涨期间，这些情绪更难控制，因为其他人似乎在不加注意、缺乏纪律、特殊专业知识或竞争优势的情况下赚得大量金钱。

<!--en-->
Like other advice gleaned from Graham and Dodd, the benefits of a good investment filter appear obvious, yet in our experience few investment managers actually maintain a disciplined filter. It is far more common to see managers whose target universe changes based on the flavor of the day—they become excited about software companies when technology is booming, Chinese companies when China appears to be on an economic tear, and oil and gas stocks when inflation appears on the horizon. These investors put themselves in the worst position to find investment bargains by filtering for areas with high investor interest and large investor capital flows, and by shifting their focus instead of developing deep expertise. Because we also fall prey to this lack of discipline as hard as we try to avoid it, we think we understand the cause—the quirks of natural human behavior. It is difficult for humans to identify potential moneymaking opportunities but decide not to pursue them in the name of focusing on their areas of competitive advantage. These feelings are harder to control during market upswings, when other people appear to be making significant amounts of money without any discernible focus, discipline, special expertise, or competitive advantage.

Graham和Dodd还向捐赠基金投资者传授关于风险管理的宝贵知识。虽然风险管理对任何投资者都至关重要，但大学的预算结构使其对我们尤为重要。大学的预算主要由工资和福利组成。如果没有其他项目需要关注，预算削减往往会影响到我们最宝贵的资产——员工。鉴于这种趋势，终身职位的重要性、维护校园稳定与长期思维文化的需求，以及资金资源的有限性（捐赠基金通常有明确的法律指定用途，不能用于填补其他预算缺口），预算削减对大学来说尤其痛苦。因此，能够产生相对稳定投资结果、减少定期大规模预算削减需求的投资政策，对由捐赠基金支持的机构非常有益。

<!--en-->
Graham and Dodd also teach endowment investors valuable lessons in the area of risk management. Although risk management is of paramount importance to any investor, the budgetary structure of a university makes it particularly vital for us. A university's budget is composed primarily of salaries and benefits. Without other line items to focus on,budget reductions often fall on people, our greatest asset. Given this tendency, the sanctity of tenured positions, the desire to preserve a campus culture of stability and long-term thinking, and the restricted nature of funding resources (endowment funds usually have a specific legally designated purpose and cannot be shifted around to fill budgetary holes elsewhere), budget cuts are particularly painful to a university. As a result, investment policies that produce reasonably stable results, reducing the periodic need for large budget cuts, are of significant benefit to endowment-supported institutions.

捐赠基金最大的风险是资本遭受重大且长期的损害，从而无法维持年度支出对所支持机构的价值。捐赠基金存在多种导致资本受损的方式：可能选择管理团队持有估值过高的资产，导致回报不佳；投资组合可能过于波动，在市场底部因年度支出锁定损失；可能维持流动性过低的投资组合，被迫以大幅折扣出售优质资产以满足资金需求；或者持有投资组合缺乏充分分散化，无法应对通货膨胀、经济衰退、疫情、战争或其他负面冲击等环境变化。

<!--en-->
An endowment's biggest risk is a large and permanent impairment of capital that hinders its ability to maintain the value of annual spending to the institution it supports, and there are numerous ways endowments can impair capital. Endowments can invest with managers that hold overvalued assets and generate poor returns. Endowments can have an overly volatile portfolio and lock in losses at a market bottom through annual spending. Endowments can maintain an overly illiquid portfolio and be forced to sell good assets at large discounts to fund spending needs. Endowments can hold a portfolio that is not sufficiently diversified to protect against changes in the environment such as inflation, an economic downturn, pandemic, war, or other downside shock.

Graham和Dod在《安全分析》中的许多见解可直接用于规避这些风险。他们告诫不要过度自信地预测未来，而是建议进行能在多种潜在未来环境中获得良好回报的投资。通过保持安全边际、选择高质量资产及优质管理团队、谨慎使用财务杠杆和流动性不足，股票挑选者和捐赠基金投资者可以避免负面灾难情景。

<!--en-->
Many of Graham and Dodd's insights in *Security Analysis* are directly applicable to avoiding these risks. Graham and Dodd caution against overly confident predictions of the future, instead recommending investments that will produce good returns in a wide variety of potential future environments. By buying with a margin of safety, by favoring high quality assets with high quality management teams, by being prudent with financial leverage and illiquidity, stock pickers and endowment investors can avoid downside disaster scenarios.

捐赠基金的一个复杂问题是，它们通常无法直接控制所持有的资产——这些决策由与其合作的外部管理团队决定。因此，捐赠基金抵御风险的第一道防线是其管理团队选择机制。当我们决定是否与某位管理团队合作时，会问一个重要问题：我们是否愿意与这位管理团队共同经历危机？与那些借款过多、业务过于集中、仅计划正面收益的管理团队合作，会加剧风险。而与遵循Graham和Dod原则的团队合作，则有助于降低投资组合的风险。

<!--en-->
One complication for endowments is that they typically do not directly control which assets they own—those decisions are up to the external managers with whom they partner. As a result, an endowment's first line of defense against risk is its manager selection process. One important question we ask ourselves when deciding whether to partner with a manager isif we would be happy to go through a crisis with that manager. Partnering with managers who borrow too much money, overconcentrate in their positions, and plan only for upside scenarios will multiply risk. Partnering with managers who adhere to the principles of Graham and Dodd helps mitigate risk in the portfolio instead.

通过痛苦的经历，我们认识到我们的管理团队风险评估必须超越对管理团队基础投资的简单审查。2008-2009年全球金融危机中，我们留下的教训之一，是与一个管理团队合作进行的投资：该团队购买了公司资本结构中优先级较高的优质信用工具。不幸的是，该团队使用杠杆手段提升回报。结果，在那个时期信用市场崩溃时，该团队面临信贷额度不足的问题。尽管基础信用投资最终仍表现良好，但该团队却被迫在最糟糕的时刻出售许多资产，锁定无法挽回的损失。同样，我们也会因与那些在糟糕市场因大量投资者赎回、关键员工离职或其他业务不稳定因素而倒闭的管理团队合作而锁定损失。因此，我们会评估潜在管理合作伙伴是否具备持续经营的能力（能承受负收益期）、足够的经济能力在经济低迷时期保留人才、具有长期导向和决心度过困难时期的能力，以及拥有足够优质的投资者基础，避免出现投资者争相提取资金导致基金枯竭的情况。

<!--en-->
We have learned through painful experience that our manager risk assessments must go well beyond an examination of a manager's underlying investments. One of our scars from the Global Financial Crisis in 2008–2009 was an investment with a manager that purchased high quality credit instruments senior in the capital structure of a company. Unfortunately, the manager used leverage to boost their returns. As a result, when prices declined in the credit market meltdown of that era, the manager faced margin calls on the lines of credit it used to hold its investments. Although the underlying credit investments ultimately did fine, the manager was forced to sell many of them at the worst possible time, locking in losses that could not be recovered. We have similarly locked in losses by investing with managers who go out of business in bad markets due to large investor redemptions, key employee departures, or other types of business instability. As a result, we explore if potential manager partners are sufficiently capitalized as a business to endure periods of negative returns, sufficiently generous with economics to retain talented staff in a downturn, sufficiently long-term oriented and motivated to work through difficult times, and have a sufficiently high quality investor base to avoid run-on-the-bank scenarios where investors compete to pull money from a dying fund.

我们试图识别管理者其他有助于降低风险的特质。例如，我们更青睐那些热爱投资过程与挑战的管理者，而非仅仅追求财务回报的管理者。当投资机会很多但短期经济收益较低时，这类管理者更有可能坚持到底，甚至在困难市场中取得成功。我们更青睐那些愿意通过关闭基金、拒绝潜在投资者来限制资本规模的管理者。这些管理者通过保持投资者的超额需求来准备应对负面情景，这种需求可用于替代可能的未来赎回，从而在市场动荡期间保护自身免受业务中断的影响。我们更青睐那些关注绝对回报的管理者，而非那些将成功视为超越指数表现的管理者。根据我们的经验，具有绝对回报目标的管理者通常更清楚潜在的负面情景，因为他们不太可能认为长期亏损是好的结果，无论市场表现如何。

<!--en-->
We have tried to identify other attributes of managers that help mitigate risk. For example, we prefer managers who love the process and challenge of investing, not simply the financial rewards. These managers are more likely to stay the course and even thrive in difficult markets when investment bargains are rampant but near-term economic rewards are lower. We prefer managers with a willingness to limit their capital base by closing their funds and turning away potential investors. These managers prepare for downside scenarios bymaintaining excess demand from investors that can be used to replace possible future redemptions, protecting themselves from business disruptions during market dislocations. We prefer managers with a focus on absolute returns, rather than those who view success as outperforming an index. In our experience, managers with absolute return goals tend to be more aware of potential downside scenarios as they are unlikely to view losing money over the long term as a good outcome, regardless of how the market performs.

您可能会好奇风险投资如何融入这种管理者选择风险评估标准。风险投资家不是应该大胆冒险吗？没错，他们确实如此——但虽然谨慎的风险投资家可能会对缺乏经验的企业家和未经验证的商业模式进行投资，他们也会积极降低其他所有风险。他们预留现金储备以支持公司度过不可避免的艰难时期，帮助招募有经验的运营高管为有远见的创始人提供基础支持，倡导可持续的长期商业实践，并在良好时期推动公司筹集额外资金。通过准备应对负面情景，风险投资家让初创企业有机会在困难时期生存足够长的时间，以验证其颠覆性想法是否有效，从而保留风险投资著名的积极潜力。

<!--en-->
You may wonder how venture capital fits into this manager selection risk rubric. Aren't venture capitalists supposed to swing for the fences? Yes, they are—but while prudent venture capitalists may take bets on inexperienced entrepreneurs and unproven business models, they are also aggressive about mitigating every other risk they can. They set aside cash reserves to support companies through inevitable tough times, they help recruit proven operating executives to provide grounding to visionary founders, they advocate for sustainable long-term business practices, and they push companies to raise excess capital in good times. By preparing for downside scenarios, venture capitalists give start-up companies the best shot at surviving difficult times long enough to see if their disruptive idea works, preserving the upside potential for which venture capital is famous.

投资组合层面的风险控制是管理者选择之后的第二个防御机制。投资经理可能做出个别上策的决策，导致投资组合层面出现不健康的风险敞口，当这些决策汇总到多个经理身上时，捐赠机构必须采取行动限制这些风险敞口。周到的自上而下的限制措施可以实现投资组合的多元化，确保负面事件、政治变化或宏观经济不利因素不会同时损害整个投资组合。例如，在2013年，我们对中国投资设定了自上而下的限制。我们的投资委员会正确识别了可能损害美国投资者价值的未来负面情景，无论我们在中国境内的风险敞口多么分散。只关注自下而上投资机会的美国捐赠机构，可能在地缘政治变化使此类投资变得不那么吸引人之前，轻易面临对中国投资的过度风险。

<!--en-->
Portfolio-level risk controls represent an endowment's second line of defense after manager selection. Investment managers may make individually sensible decisions that create unhealthy portfolio-level exposures when aggregated across multiple managers, and an endowment must act to limit these exposures. Thoughtful top-down limits impose diversification on a portfolio, ensuring that negative events, political changes, or macroeconomic headwinds will not similarly impair all parts of the portfolio simultaneously. For example, in 2013, we established a top-down limit on our China exposure. Our investment committee correctly identified potential future downside scenarios that could impair value for a U.S. investor, no matter how well we diversified our exposure within China. A U.S.-based endowment that looked only at bottom-up investment opportunities could easily become overexposed toChina before changing geopolitics made such investments less attractive.

最后一套风险防御措施是捐赠机构的更广泛财务政策。除了限制风险的投资政策外，机构还可以通过审慎的支出和储备政策来防范预算削减。例如，机构可以通过不每年将捐赠支付提高到最高水平，为捐赠价值下降留出空间，而不导致支出削减。同样，机构可以建立备用财务储备，以便在经济困难时期支持预算。

<!--en-->
A final set of risk defenses are the broader financial policies of an endowed institution. In addition to investment policies that limit risk, institutions can protect against budgetary cuts through thoughtful spending and reserve policies. For example, institutions can leave room for endowment values to drop without leading to spending cuts, by not aggressively increasing endowment payouts to the maximum level each year. Similarly, institutions can build alternate financial reserves to be used to support the budget through difficult economic times.

各种类型的投资者都可以从格雷厄姆和多德的作品中学习。不幸的是，《安全分析》因其知名度而存在问题。格雷厄姆和多德的作品非常有名，在投资圈中被频繁引用，许多人可能认为他们在阅读任何一本书之前已经非常熟悉其中的教训。当我进入这个行业并寻找书籍阅读时，我也确实这么认为。然而，拿起《安全分析》后，我发现了一个远超金融媒体常见简单总结的世界。也许最令人惊讶的是，这部投资著作至今仍然具有相关性，甚至对捐赠管理这样的相关领域也如此。希望通过阅读这些页面，您也能经历类似的旅程。

<!--en-->
Investors of all types can learn from Graham and Dodd. Unfortunately, *Security Analysis* suffers from its own fame. The works of Graham and Dodd are so well-known and so well-referenced in investment circles that many people may believe they are already eminently familiar with the lessons contained within before reading any of their books. I certainly believed this when I entered the industry and looked around for books to read. Picking up *Security Analysis*, however, opened a world far beyond the simplistic summaries commonly cited in the financial press. Perhaps what was most surprising was how much of this investment tome remains relevant today, even to an adjacent field such as endowment management. I hope that by reading through these pages, you are enjoying a similar journey to mine.

## 关于本版

<!--en-->
*About This Edition*

自《安全分析》第六版出版以来已过去14年，那是在2008-2009年大金融危机前夕。在此期间发生了许多变化，因此2022年初我们决定推出第七版。还有许多新内容需要补充。

<!--en-->
It has been an unusual 14 years since the sixth edition of *Security Analysis* was published, shortly before the Great Financial Crisis of 2008–2009. So much has happened over this period that in early 2022 we made the decision to produce a seventh edition. There is much new ground to cover.

本版的核心是1940年出版的《安全分析》第二版，仅删除了我们认为过时的部分内容。与第六版一样，我们邀请了一些当今领先的投资者和金融思想家对原书进行评论。通过这种方式，我们希望读者能够了解自格雷厄姆和多德时代以来发生了哪些变化，以及哪些没有变化，同时获得对当代实践、创新、趋势和挑战的深刻认识。

<!--en-->
The backbone of this edition is the second edition of *Security Analysis*, published in 1940, with only sections we considered obsolete removed. As with the sixth edition, we recruited some of today's leading investors and financial thinkers to comment on the original. By proceeding in this fashion, we hope that readers will gain an appreciation for what has changed since the era of Graham and Dodd and what hasn't, while garnering insight into contemporary practices, innovations, trends, and challenges.

《安全分析》第六版出版后不久，一场由美国房地产市场严重过度行为引发的重大金融危机爆发了。大量住宅和商业抵押贷款被分割成多个档次，然后打包成证券出售给投资者。尽管信用机构给予这些新型证券投资级评级，但这些工具并非为雨天情况而设计；它们从未经历过全国范围内房价持续下跌的压力测试，很少有人认为这种情况会发生。当这种下跌发生时，这些证券价格暴跌，导致包括贝尔斯登、雷曼兄弟、AIG、房利美、房利美和美林在内的许多大型金融机构的资产负债表遭受重创。

<!--en-->
Soon after the sixth edition of *Security Analysis* was published, a major financial crisis ensued that was triggered by significant excesses in the U.S. housing market. Enormous volumes of residential and commercial mortgages had been sliced and diced into various tranches and then securitized for sale to investors. While credit agencies blessed the newfangled securities with investment grade ratings, these instruments were not created with a rainy day in mind; they had never been stress-tested by a widespread and sustained decline in housing prices nationally, which few imagined could happen. When such a decline occurred, these securities plummeted and bloodied the balance sheets of many major financial institutions, including Bear Stearns, Lehman Brothers, AIG, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, and Merrill Lynch.

损害很快蔓延到实体经济，引发股市崩盘、企业信贷普遍抛售以及严重的经济衰退，造成了半个世纪来最严重的金融危机。联邦储备委员会立即将利率降至接近零水平，美国国会通过多种法案，支持处于困境的企业和个人。全球各中央银行和立法者也采取了类似措施。

<!--en-->
The damage soon spread to the real economy, spurring a stock market collapse, a widespread sell-off in corporate credit, and a severe economic downturn, resulting in the worstfinancial crisis in three-quarters of a century. The Federal Reserve immediately cut interest rates to next to nothing, and the U.S. Congress passed a variety of bills to support both enterprises on the brink and individuals who were struggling. Central banks and legislators around the world responded similarly.

当美国和其他全球经济开始复苏时，金融市场在2020年3月经历了11年的牛市，这是有记录以来最长的股票牛市，期间标普500指数上涨五倍。从2020年4月到2022年1月，市场再次翻倍。持续的零利率政策、美联储对国债和抵押贷款证券的大规模购买以及其他前所未有的干预措施，推动了市场的繁荣。

<!--en-->
As the United States and other global economies began to recover, the financial markets went on an 11-year bender through March of 2020, the longest equity bull market on record, a period during which the S&P 500 rose fivefold. It then doubled again from April 2020 through January 2022. Continued zero interest rate policy, massive buying of Treasury bonds and mortgage securities by the Fed, and a variety of other unprecedented interventions fueled the market exuberance.

随着经济活动恢复正常，2020年3月出现的自1918-1919年流感疫情以来的首次全球大流行几乎关闭了美国和全球经济的部分领域，引发了另一系列刺激措施。到2022年初，巨大的经济刺激效果以及经济恢复不均导致的供应链困难、劳动力短缺、中国因新冠疫情的封锁以及俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵，导致了四十年来最严重的通货膨胀。这反过来又导致联邦储备委员会政策急剧逆转，利率大幅上升，股市出现剧烈抛售，尤其是那些表现最好的股票。之前前所未有的经济刺激和宽松货币政策措施才刚刚开始逆转，让投资者和市场处于更高不确定性的状态。经济衰退似乎越来越有可能发生。

<!--en-->
As economic activity was normalizing, the March 2020 emergence of the first global pandemic since the influenza of 1918–1919 essentially shut down parts of the United States and global economies, precipitating another series of stimulative measures. By early 2022, the ongoing impact of enormous economic stimulus as well as supply chain difficulties caused by an uneven economic recovery, growing worker shortages, Chinese Covid-related shutdowns, and the Russian invasion of Ukraine contributed to the worst bout of inflation in four decades. This, in turn, triggered a sharp reversal of Fed policy, leading to considerably higher interest rates and a sharp stock market sell-off, especially in the shares of the highest flyers. The previous, unprecedented economic stimulus and accommodative monetary policy measures are only starting to be reversed as we write, leaving investors and markets in a heightened state of uncertainty. An economic downturn seems increasingly likely.

2022年发生的通胀飙升能否得到控制，还是会根深蒂固？在撰写本文时，没有人知道联邦储备委员会能否控制它，或者如果市场陷入困境，他们是否会再次出手救援。但本版的作者们提供了一个基于格雷厄姆和多德永恒的常识原则的新框架，帮助读者应对未来可能出现的任何情况。

<!--en-->
Will the surge of inflation experienced as 2022 unfolded come under control, or will it become ingrained? At the time of this writing, no one knows if the Fed will be able to tame it or if they will come to the rescue once again if markets falter. But the contributors to this edition offer a fresh framework built upon Graham and Dodd's timeless commonsense principles to help readers navigate whatever may come next.

第七版的前言是对我为第六版撰写的文章进行了广泛更新和扩展。在其中，我试图说明价值投资者如何在第六版之后发生显著变化的世界中，以及比本杰明·格雷厄姆的时代截然不同的环境中，坚持格雷厄姆经过时间考验的原则。除了这篇文章外：*金融历史学家吉姆·格兰特对其出色的文章进行了重大更新，将本杰明·格雷厄姆置于历史背景下，揭示了他提出和践行投资方法那个时代的条件和环境。*

<!--en-->
The preface to the seventh edition is an extensive update and expansion of the one I wrote for the sixth edition. In it, I attempt to convey how value investors can and should adhere to Graham's time-tested principles in a world that has changed significantly since the sixth edition and is unimaginably different from Benjamin Graham's time. In addition to this essay:* Financial historian Jim Grant has significantly updated his exceptional piece that places Benjamin Graham in a historical perspective, shining light on the conditions and circumstances of the era in which he formulated and practiced his investment approach.

* 备受尊敬的金融作家兼历史学家罗杰·洛温斯坦提供了他对格雷厄姆方法的永恒智慧的看法，探讨了长期金融危机后的牛市期间出现的潮流与错误。
* 投资者兼作家霍华德·马克斯以其定期的投资信件和书籍而闻名，他提供了关于如何应对固定收益市场的全新视角，始终关注风险与潜在回报。
* 投资者兼作者Dominique Mielle分享了她对债务市场特定子领域的见解，即对困境信贷的投资。
* Todd Combs阐述了他对股票投资的观点。他讨论了识别投资机会的关键方法，并分享了评估企业价值的策略，还深入介绍了他的尽职调查与分析方法。
* Steve Romick介绍了他的价值投资策略，涵盖股票、债务和抵押贷款支持证券。
* Ben Stein和Zach Sternberg专注于可投资领域的特定子领域，与充满热情的业主经营者一起进行投资——这一策略是他们在华顿学院宿舍中形成的。他们重视这种策略带来的利益一致性，同时承认由于长期持有期和异常集中的投资组合，业绩存在显著波动。

* Nancy Zimmerman分享了她对特殊情况投资——套利投资——重要子领域的见解，讲述了证券如何偏离其基础价值，以及投资者如何利用这些价格差异获利。
* 我从角度谈谈资产负债表分析作为投资工具的重要性及其当前不足。
* 虽然Graham和Dodd没有涉及国际投资，但Bill Duhamel、Ashish Pant和Jason Moment提供了关于非美国市场所面临的挑战和机遇的视角。我们的经济视野已经走向全球；公司越来越多地在原籍国之外开展业务，大多数投资者也可以轻松进行国际投资。与所有市场一样，Graham和Dod的原则完全适用于发达市场和新兴市场的全球投资。但全球投资需要关注其他因素，如货币汇率、每个司法管辖区的不同法律和法规、不同的文化规范、通常流动性较低的市场，以及信息优势严重缺失的风险。在我的公司，我们常开玩笑说，在大多数国家，只有几十人知道实际情况，而我们知道我们不是其中之一。投资者必须找到应对这些挑战的方法，克服任何劣势。当然，这些挑战也可能使其他投资者避免那些问题尤为严重的市场，这反过来可能导致价格充分反映这些挑战。在这种情况下，价格才是真正的平等因素。
* David Abrams接着介绍了他对多策略投资方法的独特视角，描述了投资公开证券和私人股票之间的共生效应。
* 鉴于教育、慈善、医疗及其他基金目前持有的巨额且不断增长的资本，我请了麻省理工投资公司总裁塞斯·亚历山大分享他关于管理大量机构资本的最佳当代策略框架。塞斯展现了他的敏锐洞察力与宝贵视角——作为管理者，他不会亲自选择个别投资项目，而是致力于确定最佳行业、策略和管理者，以将资本分配到这些领域及相关人士手中。所有第七版的贡献者我都非常熟悉。他们都是优秀的投资思想家和出色的作家。读者可以从他们每个人那里学到很多东西。原始的格雷厄姆与多德文本与我们杰出贡献者撰写的文章相结合，提供了一个框架，让参与或仅观察金融市场的人员能够了解市场运作方式，以及投资者如何且应当成功参与市场。这个项目汇集了15位贡献者，体现了价值投资界的特性。我们中许多人都是投资竞争对手，但也是朋友和同事。我们经常互相学习；每个人都知道我们并不拥有所有答案。我们都清楚地记得自己最大的错误，仿佛它们发生在昨天。同样，我们也认识到没有人完全掌握价值投资的艺术；总是有新的挑战和考量，也有改进的空间。价值投资者必须不断进行自我革新，提升自己的能力，以适应新时代、新型证券、新兴企业、新兴行业、变化中的标准以及不断发展的市场条件。通过汇集这些经验丰富、能力出众的贡献者的不同观点，我们希望第七版《安全分析》能成为一部丰富、多样且信息丰富的投资思想集，成为前六版值得信赖且持久的续作。塞斯·A·克兰曼，马萨诸塞州波士顿，2022年11月

<!--en-->
* Acclaimed financial writer and historian Roger Lowenstein offers his perspective on the eternal wisdom of Graham's approach in the context of the fads and follies that arose during the lengthy post-financial crisis bull market.
* Investor and author Howard Marks, widely known for his regular missives and books on investing, provides a freshly updated perspective on navigating the fixed-income markets with a steady focus on risk as well as potential return.
* Investor and author Dominique Mielle shares her insights on a specialized subset of the debt markets, investing in distressed credit.
* Todd Combs offers his perspective on his stock-in-trade —equity investing. He discusses the keys to identifying investment opportunity and shares strategies for assessing the value of businesses, delving into his own approach to due diligence and analysis.
* Steve Romick discusses his opportunistic approach to value investment that includes equities, debt, and mortgage-backed securities.
* Ben Stein and Zach Sternberg focus on a narrow subset of the investable universe, investing alongside passionate owner-operators, an approach they hatched in their Wharton School dorm room. They value the alignment ofinterests that results from such an approach, while accepting significant volatility in performance as a result of a very long-term holding period and an unusually concentrated portfolio.

* Nancy Zimmerman shares her insights on an important subset of special situations—arbitrage investments—recounting the many ways securities can depart from their underlying value and how investors may profitably exploit those mispricings.
* I offer a perspective on the ongoing importance but also the contemporary shortcomings of balance-sheet analysis as an investment tool.
* While Graham and Dodd did not cover international investing, Bill Duhamel, Ashish Pant, and Jason Moment offer a perspective on the challenges and opportunities inherent in non-U.S. markets. Our economic horizons have gone global; companies increasingly do business beyond their countries of origin, and most investors can easily invest internationally. As with all markets, the basic principles of Graham and Dodd fully apply to global investing in both developed and emerging markets. But global investing requires attention to additional considerations, such as currency exchange rates, different laws and regulations in every jurisdiction, varying cultural norms, often much less liquid markets, and the risk of substantial information disadvantages. At my firm, we often joke that in most countries, only a couple of dozen people know what's really going on, and we know that we're not one of them. An investor must figure out how to deal with such challenges and overcome any disadvantages. Of course, such challenges may also cause other investors to shy away from markets where these issues are particularly profound, which, in turn, may lead to prices that more than fully discount such challenges. In such cases, price is truly the great equalizer.
* David Abrams follows with his unique perspective on a multistrategy investment approach, describing thesymbiotic effects of investing in both public securities and private equities.
* Given the large and growing amount of capital now held by educational, philanthropic, medical, and other endowments, I asked Seth Alexander, president of MIT Investment Company, to share his framework on the best contemporary strategies for the management of large pools of institutional capital. Seth demonstrates his acumen and invaluable perspective as a steward who doesn't pick individual investments himself but who seeks to determine the best sectors, strategies, and managers to which and whom to allocate capital.
All of the contributors to this seventh edition are well-known to me. They are superb investment thinkers as well as strong writers. Readers stand to learn a great deal from each of them. Together, the original Graham and Dodd text, combined with the essays written by our distinguished roster of contributors, offers up a paradigm through which those who are participants in, or simply observers of, financial markets can gain a sense of how these markets function and how investors can and should successfully engage with them.
This project has brought together 15 contributors in a collaboration that is emblematic of the nature of the value investing community. Many of us are investment rivals, but we are also friends and colleagues. We regularly learn from each other; each of us knows that we don't possess all the answers. We all vividly remember our biggest mistakes as if they happened yesterday. Similarly, we recognize that none of us has perfected the art of value investing; there are always new challenges and considerations, and there is always room to improve. A value investor must constantly be in the process of reinvention, of raising his or her game to navigate the terrain of new eras, novel securities, nascent businesses, emerging industries, shifting standards, and evolving market conditions. By assembling the diverse perspectives of these experienced and able contributors, we hope to make this seventh edition of *Security Analysis* a rich, varied, and highly informed tapestry of investment thinking that will be a worthy and long-lived successor to the six preceding editions.
Seth A. Klarman
Boston, MA
November, 2022
