CHAPTER 25

## 高级证券

<!--en-->
*Senior Securities with*

权证。参与式股票。转换和对冲 与可转换股票中存在的几乎所有变化一样，认购权证的条款也对应着这些变化。股票的购买价格通常会根据调整转换价格的标准规定，上下波动。

<!--en-->
Warrants. Participating Issues.
Switching and Hedging
NEARLY ALL THE VARIATIONS found in convertible issues have their counterpart in the terms of subscription warrants. The purchase price of the stock is ordinarily subject to change, up or down, corresponding to the standard provisions for adjusting a conversion price.

*示例：* 白鹰石油精炼公司债券，面值5\frac{1}{2}美元，到期日为1937年，于1927年3月发行。该债券附带认股权证，赋予持有人在1932年3月15日或之前，按以下价格认购该公司10股股本的权利：1928年3月15日及之后，每股32美元。

<!--en-->
*Example:* White Eagle Oil and Refining Company Debenture $5\frac{1}{2}$s, due 1937, were offered in March 1927 and carried warrants entitling the holder to subscribe on or before March 15, 1932, to 10 shares of the capital stock of the company at the following prices.
$32 per share to and including March 15, 1928, and thereafter at

每股 $34，涵盖1929年3月15日及之后。

<!--en-->
$34 per share to and including March 15, 1929, and thereafter at

每股36美元，涵盖1930年3月15日及之后。

<!--en-->
$36 per share to and including March 15, 1930, and thereafter at

从1931年3月15日及之后开始，每股价格为38美元；到1932年3月15日及之后，每股价格调整为40美元。

<!--en-->
$38 per share to and including March 15, 1931, and thereafter at
$40 per share to and including March 15, 1932.

1930年1月27日，纽约标准石油公司通过承担白鹰公司的债务，用$8\frac{1}{2}$股纽约标准石油股份换取每10股白鹰股份，从而获得了白鹰资产。

<!--en-->
On January 27, 1930, the Standard Oil Company of New York acquired the White Eagle properties by assuming the liabilities of the latter company and exchanging $8\frac{1}{2}$ shares of Standard Oil of New York for each 10 shares of White Eagle.

根据保护权证免受稀释、并在资产出售或公司合并时调整认购价格的债券条款，这些权证赋予持有人权利在1930年3月15日之前，以每股42.35美元的价格认购纽约标准石油（现Socony-Vacuum Corporation）$8\frac{1}{2}$股股票；次年价格为44.71美元，再后一年为47.06美元。

<!--en-->
In accordance with the terms of the indenture protecting the warrants against dilution and providing for readjustment of the subscription price in the case of a sale of the properties or merger of the company, the warrants thereafter entitled the holder to subscribe to $8\frac{1}{2}$ shares of Standard Oil of New York (now Socony-Vacuum Corporation) at $42.35 per share to and including March 15, 1930, at $44.71 for the next year and at $47.06 for the following year.

**两种滑动价格机制**。在期权权证发行中也会遇到这两种滑动价格机制。

<!--en-->
**Sliding Scales of Both Types.** Sliding-scale arrangements of both types are also encountered in option-warrant issues.

*示例：* 1928年发行的Interstate Department Stores, Inc. 7%优先股，附带不可分离权证，允许持有人按以下价格逐股购买普通股：1929年1月31日之前为每股37美元；1931年1月31日之前为每股42美元；1933年1月31日之前为每股47美元。Central States Electric Corporation可选$5\frac{1}{2}\%$债券，到期日为1954年，附带可分离权证，允许持有人在1934年9月15日或之前，以每1000美元债券对应10股普通股的价格购买；前25%的权证行使价为每股89美元；接下来25%的权证行使价为每股94美元；再接下来25%的权证行使价为每股99美元；最后25%的权证行使价为每股104美元。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Interstate Department Stores, Inc., 7% Preferred, issued in 1928, carried nondetachable warrants entitling the holder to purchase common stock, share for share, at the following prices:
$37 per share up to January 31, 1929.
$42 per share up to January 31, 1931.
$47 per share up to January 31, 1933.
Central States Electric Corporation Optional $5\frac{1}{2}\%$ Debentures, due 1954, carried detachable warrants entitling the holder to buy, on or before September 15, 1934, 10 shares of common stock for each $1,000 bond, at the following prices:
$89 per share for the first 25% of the warrants exercised.
$94 per share for the next 25% of the warrants exercised.
$99 per share for the next 25% of the warrants exercised.
$104 per share for the last 25% of the warrants exercised.

与可转换债券一样，基于“块”原则的滑动价格机制会大幅降低该特权的价值，直到达到最后一个“块”，即最高价格，此时它就变成了普通的购买期权。

<!--en-->
As with convertibles, a sliding scale based on the “block” principle detracts greatly from the value of the privilege until the last block, *i.e.*, the highest price, is reached, at which time it becomes an ordinary purchase option.

**支付方式。** 附在债券或优先股上的股票购买权证通常规定，普通股支付可以通过现金或按面值转让高级证券进行。这种安排直接相当于转换特权。例如，American and Foreign Power Second Preferred的每一股股票都附带权证，可按每股25美元的价格购买4股普通股。持有人无需支付现金，而是可以以每股100美元的价值转让优先股。如果他这样做，实际上是在用带权证的优先股转换为普通股。

<!--en-->
**Methods of Payment.** Stock-purchase warrants attached to bonds or preferred stocks frequently provide that payment for the common stock may be made either in cash or by turning in the senior security itself at par. Such an arrangement mayprove directly equivalent to a conversion privilege. For example, each share of American and Foreign Power Second Preferred was issued with warrants to buy 4 shares of common at $25 per share. Instead of paying cash, the holder can tender preferred stock at a value of $100 per share. If he does so, he is actually *converting* his preferred stock with warrants into common.

同样，第22章中描述的Rand Kardex$5\frac{1}{2}\%$债券，在行使权证时，可以以面值而非现金进行转让。由于附在1000美元债券上的权证要求支付900美元（即$22\frac{1}{2}$股，按40美元计算），以这种方式支付1000美元债券的人将剩下100美元债券。因此，这些条款相当于每支债券有90%可以转换为普通股。

<!--en-->
Similarly, the Rand Kardex $5\frac{1}{2}\%$ bonds, described in Chap. 22, could be tendered at par, in lieu of cash, upon exercising the warrants. Since the warrants attached to a $1,000 bond called for payment of $900 ($22\frac{1}{2}$ shares at 40), the owner of a $1,000 bond making payment in this fashion would have a $100 bond remaining. These provisions were thus equivalent to convertibility of 90% of each bond into common.

这种安排的最新例子包括Scullin Steel 6s和权证，以及Commercial Mackay Income 4s和权证。

<!--en-->
More recent examples of this arrangement are Scullin Steel 6s and warrants and Commercial Mackay Income 4s and warrants.

**支付现金的权重的优势。** 有权支付现金而非转让高级证券，必须被视为比纯转换特权更有优势——首先，因为债券或优先股“已附带权证”的价值可能高于面值，从而增加收益；其次，如前所述，持有人可以在实现投机性部分的现金收益的同时保留投资；第三，因为权证单独出售时的溢价可能高于纯可转换债券。所有这些优势都体现在第23章表格中的Mohawk Hudson Power Corporation Second Preferred上。该股票在行使权证时可以以面值而非现金进行转让，具有与转换权相当的权益，但权证安排比同等转换特权更盈利。

<!--en-->
**Advantage of Option to Pay Cash.** The option to pay cash instead of turning in the senior issue must be considered an advantage over a straight conversion privilege—first, because the bond or preferred, “ex-warrants,” may be worth more than par, thus increasing the profit; second, because, as previously explained, the holder may be glad to retain his investment while realizing a cash profit on its speculative component; and third, because the warrant is likely to sell separately at a greater premium over its realizable value than a pure convertible. All these advantages are illustrated by the Mohawk Hudson Power Corporation Second Preferred with warrants as shown in the table in Chap. 23. This stock was tenderable at par, in lieu of cash, upon exercise of the warrants, thus having rights equivalent to convertibility, but the warrant arrangement proved far more profitable than an equivalent conversion privilege.

**可分离性。** 股票购买权证分为可分离、不可分离，或在一定期限内可分离、之后不可分离。可分离的权证只需出示权证本身即可行使权利。因此，它可以与最初发行它的债券分开出售。不可分离的权证或权利必须与优先发行品一起行使；即，在支付普通股款项时，必须实际提交债券或优先股。因此，此类权证不能单独交易。例如，附属于Montecatini 7s的权证，到期日为1937年，以及附属于Fiat Debenture 7s的权证，到期日为1946年，在发行后立即即可分离。附属于Loews, Inc.的$6.50优先股，于1927年12月发行，直到1928年7月1日才可分离；而附属于Loews, Inc.的6%债券，到期日为1941年，也直到1926年10月1日，即发行六个月后，才可分离。另一方面，附属于Crown-Zellerbach Corporation Debenture 6s的权证，到期日为1940年，以及附属于Interstate Department Stores, Inc.的7%优先股，在权证有效期内不可分离，除非需要赎回与其相关的优先发行品。

<!--en-->
**Detachability.** Stock-purchase warrants are either detachable, nondetachable, or nondetachable for a certain period and detachable thereafter. A detachable warrant may be exercised upon presentation of the warrant alone. Hence it may be soldseparately from the issue of which it originally formed a part. A nondetachable warrant or right may be exercised only in conjunction with the senior issue; *i.e.*, the bond or preferred stock must be physically presented at the time of making payment for the common shares. Hence such warrants may not be dealt in separately. For example, the warrants attached to Montecatini 7s, due 1937, and those accompanying the Fiat Debenture 7s, due 1946, were detachable immediately after issuance. Those attached to Loews, Inc., $6.50 Preferred, offered in December 1927, were not detachable until July 1, 1928; and the warrants attached to the Loews, Inc., 6% Debentures, due 1941, were not detachable until October 1, 1926, also six months after their issuance. On the other hand, the warrants attached to Crown-Zellerbach Corporation Debenture 6s, due 1940, and to Interstate Department Stores, Inc., 7% Preferred were not detachable during the life of the warrant, unless the senior issue to which they were attached were called for redemption.

在活跃的股票市场中，单独的期权权证受到投机者的欢迎（如前所述），其售价远高于其即时可变现价值。因此，其他条件相同的情况下，具有可分离权证的发行品售价会高于具有不可分离权利的发行品。基于这一事实，可能会有人问：为什么并非所有认购权证都能立即分离，以让持有者获得更高的市场吸引力？使权证不可分离的原因是，公司和发行承销商都希望避免其权证债券出现过低价格。如果真正的投机者大量购买带权证的债券，很可能会形成如此低的价格。对于这些没有债券利益的持有者来说，他们可能会分离权证，以任意价格出售不带权证的债券。来自这一来源的销售压力，加上由于缺乏“市场培育”而缺乏稳定需求，可能导致价格极低，从而明显影响公司的信用状况，这显然是不理想的。

<!--en-->
In an active stock market, separate option warrants are popular with speculators (as pointed out before), and they sell at considerable premiums above their immediately realizable value. Other things being equal, therefore, an issue with detachable warrants will sell higher than one with a nonseparable right. In view of this fact it may be asked why all subscription warrants are not made immediately detachable, to give the holder the benefit of their superior market appeal. The reason for making a warrant nondetachable is that both the company and the underwriters of the issue wish to avoid the establishment of an unduly low price for its bonds ex-warrants. Such a low price is likely to follow if large purchases of the bond with warrants are made by out-and-out speculators. For these holders, having no interest in the bond as such, are likely to detach the warrant and sell the bond ex-warrants for whatever it will bring. Selling pressure from this source, coupled with the absence of any steady demand for the issue due to lack of “seasoning,” may result in so low a price as to constitute an apparent reflection upon the corporation’s credit, which is evidently undesirable.

这种折中安排——仅在一段时间后使权证可分离——是基于这样的假设：当证券在投资界已得到充分关注后，即使有从权证中获益的买家出售，也可以更容易地为不带权证的发行品确定合理价格。

<!--en-->
The compromise arrangement—which makes the warrant detachable only after an interval—is based upon the assumption that, after the security has had time to become fairly well known in the investment world, a proper price may more readily be established for the issue ex-warrants, even in the face of sales by those who have profited from the warrants.

一旦这些认购权证从相关优先发行品中分离出来，它们必然会拥有自己的存在和特性。从单纯的债券融资附属物，它们发展成独立的证券形式，并在1928-1929年的狂热时期成为重要的投机工具。令人惊讶的是，由American and Foreign Power公司创建的期权权证，在1929年的市场价值超过十亿美元，这一数字在三年后的1932年7月，超过了纽约证券交易所上市的美国所有铁路普通股的市值。

<!--en-->
When once these subscription warrants were made detachable from the related senior issue, they were bound to assume an existence and characteristics of their own. From a mere appendage of bond financing they developed into an independent form of security and a major vehicle of speculation during the madness of 1928–1929. It is an amazing fact that the option warrants created by one company, American and Foreign Power, reached an indicated market value in 1929 of over a billion dollars, a figure that exceeded the market value of all the railroad common stocks of the United States listed on the New York Stock Exchange in July 1932, less than three years later.

因此，在后续章节中，我们需要将股票购买权证作为独立投机工具来研究其特性。届时我们将讨论这类权证的价格与同一公司优先股和普通股价格之间的关系。

<!--en-->
It will be necessary, therefore, to consider in a later chapter the characteristics of stock-purchase warrants, viewed as an independent speculative medium. At that time we shall discuss the relationships between the prices of such warrants and of the preferred and common shares of the same corporations.

## 参与式发行品

<!--en-->
*PARTICIPATING ISSUES*

这种特权类型的大部分特征已在之前与其他形式的比较中体现。可以区分两种参与方式。更常见的安排取决于普通股的股息分配；较少情况下，利润分享取决于收益，而不考虑股息率。

<!--en-->
Most of the traits of this type of privilege have already been brought out in the preceding comparison with the other forms. A distinction may be made between two kinds of participation. The more usual arrangement depends upon the dividend paid upon the common; less frequently, the profit sharing is determined by the earnings without reference to the dividend rate.

*示例：* 前面提到的Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company Preferred是第一种类型的标准例子；Budd Wheel Company Preferred则体现了第二种类型。在后一种情况下，基本股息为7%累积，但如果前一年的净收益分别超过600,000美元、800,000美元和1,000,000美元，则比例分别增加到8%、9%和10%。Celanese Corporation Participating First Preferred和Celluloid Corporation Participating Second Preferred均有权获得7%的基本股息，再加上普通股的其余收益中的10%。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company Preferred, already described, is a standard example of the first type; Budd Wheel Company Preferred illustrates the second. In the latter case the basic dividend is 7% cumulative, but this rate increases to 8, 9, and 10%, accordingas the net earnings of the previous year exceed $600,000; $800,000 and $1,000,000, respectively. Celanese Corporation Participating First Preferred and Celluloid Corporation Participating Second Preferred are each entitled to a basic 7%, plus 10% of the earnings otherwise available for the common stock.

优先股构成了参与式发行的主要部分；参与式债券较为罕见，在其他方面可能与标准债券模式有很大差异。例如，Kreuger和Toll参与式债券虽然名义上是债券，但实际上属于无投票权的普通股。Green Bay和Western Railway（参与式）A系列及B系列债券实际上分别是优先股和普通股。Spanish River Pulp and Paper Mills, Ltd.的First 6s债券于1931年到期，但在1928年已赎回，这是少数具有参与权特征的投资型债券的例子之一。¹西门子与Halske A. G.（一家德国企业）发行了一系列于1930年到期的参与式债券，利息等于普通股支付的股息率，但不低于6%。

<!--en-->
Preferred shares constitute the great bulk of participating issues; participating bonds are rare and likely to deviate widely in other respects from the standard bond pattern. The Kreuger and Toll Participating Debentures, for example, although nominally a bond, were in essence a nonvoting common stock. The Green Bay and Western Railway (Participating) Debentures, Series A and Series B, are in reality preferred and common stocks respectively. Spanish River Pulp and Paper Mills, Ltd., First 6s, due 1931 but redeemed in 1928, are one of the few examples of an investment-type bond with a participating privilege.¹ Siemens and Halske A. G. (a German enterprise) issued a series of Participating Debentures, due 1930, carrying interest equal to the rate of dividend paid upon the common stock but not less than 6%.

参与式优先股最初有标准模式，以Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company优先股为例。支付顺序为：首先向高级股支付固定优先股收益，然后向普通股支付类似金额，最后按股份比例共同分享额外股息。这种模式源于所有股票类别均有权平等分享收入和资产的传统法律权利，除非协议另有规定。其他此类安排的例子包括Chicago、Milwaukee、St. Paul和Pacific Railroad Company优先股；Wabash Railway Company 5%优先股A；Consolidated Film Industries, Inc.优先股。

<!--en-->
Participating preferred stocks originally had a standard pattern, exemplified by Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company Preferred. The order of payment is first a fixed preference to the senior shares, then a similar amount on the common shares, and finally an equal participation, share for share, in additional dividends. This pattern arose from the common-law right of all classes of stock to share equally in earnings and assets, except as otherwise provided by agreement. Other examples of this arrangement are Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul, and Pacific Railroad Company Preferred; Wabash Railway Company 5% Preferred A; Consolidated Film Industries, Inc., Preferred.

然而，近年来出现了多种不同的参与式安排，因此现在没有标准模式。²参与式发行需要两种计算方式：一种显示固定利息或股息的赚取次数，另一种显示根据参与权可分配的每股或每枚债券金额。 *示例：*

<!--en-->
In recent years, however, a wide diversity of participating arrangements have made their appearance, so that there is now no standard pattern.²
Participating issues require two kinds of calculation: one showing the number of times the fixed interest or dividend isearned, and the other showing the amount per share or per bond available for distribution under the participation privilege.
*Example:*

## 美国CELANES公司，1938年

<!--en-->
*CELANESE CORPORATION OF AMERICA, 1938*

**特权发行与相关普通股的比较。**在之前关于特权发行作为一类产品的优势讨论中，我们指出它们有时能提供安全与盈利机会的非常吸引人的组合。更常见的是，可能会决定优先权的高级股比企业的普通股更有优势。由于这种结论仅基于*比较*要素，因此相比声称某项发行的*绝对*吸引力，其错误风险可能更小。

<!--en-->
**Privileged Issues Compared with the Related Common Stocks.** In our previous discussion of the merits of privileged issues as a class it was pointed out that they sometimes offer a very attractive combination of security and chance for profit. More frequently, a decision may be reached that the privileged senior security is preferable to the common stock of the enterprise. Since a conclusion of this kind is based on *comparative* elements only, it is likely to involve smaller risks of error than one that asserts the *absolute* attractiveness of an issue.

示例：Paramount Pictures Corporation的$6 First Preferred股票可随时转换为7股普通股。到1936年底，其售价约为普通股的七倍，尽管累积股息接近每股$12，当然在普通股获得任何收益之前必须先支付这些股息。（例如，1936年10月17日，优先股售价为113，而普通股为157/8。）

<!--en-->
Examples: Paramount Pictures Corporation $6 First Preferred is convertible at any time into 7 shares of common. Towards the end of 1936 it was selling at just about seven times the price of the common, although it carried accumulated dividends of nearly $12 per share, which of course would have to be paid before the common could receive anything. (*E.g.*, on October 17, 1936, the preferred sold at 113 against 157/8 for the common.)

显然，从普通股转向优先股是一个明智的选择。优先股的价值不可能低于普通股的七倍；如果普通股价格下跌，其售价可能超过这一比例；在普通股分配任何资金之前，优先股肯定能收到大量股息。该股票很快证实了这一分析。1936年12月，优先股每股支付了$12的回溯股息。1937年11月，优先股售价为$92\frac{1}{4}$，而普通股仅$10\frac{1}{4}$，价差为$20\frac{1}{2}$点。包括当时优先股额外支付的$4.50股息，优先股相对于普通股的总优势为每股完全$35。

<!--en-->
Clearly a switch from the common into the preferred would have been a wise move. The preferred stock could not be worth less than seven times the price of the common; it might sell at more than this ratio, especially if the common declined in price; it was certain to receive substantial dividends before anything was disbursed on the common. Thesequel promptly bore out this analysis. In December 1936 back dividends of $12 per share were paid on the preferred. In November 1937 the preferred sold at $92\frac{1}{4}$, vs. only $10\frac{1}{4}$ for the common, showing a spread of $20\frac{1}{2}$ points. Including $4.50 of additional dividends paid on the preferred up to that time, the aggregate advantage accruing to the preferred stock as against the common amounted to fully $35 per share of preferred.

在Studebaker Corporation的3–6%债券（到期日为1945年）和1936年的普通股中，存在几乎相同的情况。这些债券可以转换为80股普通股；它们具有3%固定利息和3%累积浮动利息，其中55/8%的利息已累积到11月18日。然而，它们的价格$120\frac{1}{2}$，实际上与15美元的普通股价格持平。不到一年后，这些债券以$59\frac{3}{4}$的价格出售，而普通股仅以3美元出售——这相当于$35\frac{1}{4}$点的“价差”或利润，不包括债券上的3%固定利息。³“平价”、“溢价”和“折价”。当可转换债券或优先股的价格在交易所基础上与普通股当前价格完全相等时，这两种证券被称为*平价*出售。⁴当高级发行物的价格高于平价时，称为*溢价*出售，其价格与转换平价之间的差额称为溢价金额，即“价差”。相反，如果可转换债券的价格低于平价，这种差额有时被称为折价。⁵ *可靠分析的重要领域*。Paramount和Studebaker的例子展示了这种罕见现象——通过证券分析得出的绝对可靠的结论。普通股持有者通过转换为可转换证券，不可能亏损，他们有极好的前景，事实上也确实获得了显著收益，包括收入增加和市场价值提升。在这方面，优先发行物为更科学地应用分析技术提供了重要领域。上述例子也体现了活跃且发展的市场所创造的价格关系。当存在可转换为普通股的高级发行物时，投机性兴趣的集中往往导致价格水平与高级发行物的价格接近（有时甚至更高），公众对此关注较少。

<!--en-->
A virtually identical situation existed in Studebaker Corporation 3–6% Debentures, due 1945, and the common stock in 1936. The bonds were convertible into 80 shares of common; they carried 3% fixed interest and 3% cumulative contingent interest, of which 55/8% had accrued by November 18. Yet their price was $120\frac{1}{2}$, practically on a parity with the price of 15 for the common. Less than a year later the bonds sold at $59\frac{3}{4}$ against only 3 for the common—a “spread,” or profit, on the exchange of $35\frac{1}{4}$ points, exclusive of 3% fixed interest received on the bonds.³
“Parity,” “Premium,” and “Discount.” When the price of a convertible bond or preferred is exactly equivalent, on an exchange basis, to the current price of the common stock, the two issues are said to be selling at a *parity*.⁴ When the price of the senior issue is above parity it is said to be selling at a *premium*, and the difference between its price and conversion parity is called the amount of the premium, or the “spread.” Conversely if the price of the convertible is below parity, the difference is sometimes called the discount.⁵
*A Fruitful Field for Dependable Analysis.* The Paramount and Studebaker examples give us that infrequent phenomenon—an absolutely dependable conclusion arrived at by security analysis. Holders of the common could not possibly lose by exchanging into the convertible issues, and they had excellent prospects, which in fact were realized, of deriving substantial benefits in the form of both increased income and greater market value. In this respect, privileged issues offer a fruitful field for the more scientific application of the technique of analysis. The foregoing examples are typical also of the pricerelationships created by an active and advancing market. When there is a senior issue convertible into common, the concentration of speculative interest in the latter often results in establishing a price level closely equivalent to (and sometimes even higher than) the price of the senior issue, to which the public pays little attention.

*前述内容的结论*。显然，与普通股价格持平的可转换发行物比普通股更优，除非其价格远高于投资水平，以至于仅仅成为普通股的一种形式。布鲁克林联合燃气公司5 1/2s可转换债券（到期日为1936年）就是后一种情况示例。这些债券从1929年1月1日起可转换为20股普通股，在1927年至1932年期间以147美元或更高价格出售，1929年价格为489美元。通常值得支付一定的适度溢价，以获得高级发行物的更高安全性。当可转换债券带来的收益回报高于普通股时，这一点确实如此；即使收益回报较低，部分情况下也是如此。

<!--en-->
*Conclusion from Foregoing.* It is clear that a convertible issue selling on a parity with the common is preferable thereto, except when its price is so far above an investment level that it has become merely a form of commitment in the common stock. (Brooklyn Union Gas Company Convertible 5 1/2s, due 1936, are an example of the latter type of situation. The bonds, convertible into 20 shares of common from January 1, 1929, sold at 147 or higher during the years 1927–1932, inclusive, and sold at 489 in 1929.) It is generally worth while to pay some moderate premium in order to obtain the superior safety of the senior issue. This is certainly true when the convertible yields a higher income return than the common, and it holds good to some extent even if the income yield is lower.

转换。因此，作为实际规则，希望保留对公司的权益的普通股持有者，每当企业同时以投资水平出售以及以转换基础接近平价出售可转换高级发行物时，应始终进行转换。普通股持有人愿意支付多少溢价进行此类转换，属于个人判断问题。由于他对公司未来的信心，他通常不愿意为防范价值下降而支付大量费用。但经验表明，为了获得即使相当稳健的可转换发行物相对于普通股所具有的战略优势，他应该放弃比他认为必要的更多的内容。⁶ **对冲**。当市场下跌时，强劲的可转换发行物相对于普通股的优势就会显现出来。高级发行物的价格通常会比普通股受的影响较小，因此可以形成较大的价差，而不是之前接近平价的状况。这种可能性暗示了一种特殊的市场操作形式，称为“对冲”，即操作者购买可转换债券，并反向卖空普通股，以近似平价进行交易。⁷如果市场持续上涨，他可以转换高级发行物，从而仅以轻微的损失结束交易，即原始价差加上持有成本。但如果市场大幅下跌，他可以通过出售高级发行物并回购普通股来“撤销”操作，获得可观利润。

<!--en-->
Switching. As a practical rule, therefore, holders of common stocks who wish to retain their interest in the company should always exchange into a convertible senior issue of the enterprise, whenever it sells both at an investment level on its own account and also close to parity on a conversion basis. Just how large a premium a common stockholder should be willing to pay in making such an exchange is a matter of individual judgment. Because of his confidence in the future of his company, he is usually unwilling to pay anything substantial for insurance against a decline in value. But experience shows that he would be wise to give up somewhat more than he thinks is necessary in order to secure the strategic advantages that even a fairly sound convertible issue possesses over a common stock.⁶
**Hedging.** These advantages of a strong convertible issue over a common stock become manifest when the market declines. The price of the senior issue will ordinarily suffer less severely than the common, so that a good-sized spread maythereby be established, instead of the near-parity previously existing. This possibility suggests a special form of market operation, known as “hedging,” in which the operator buys the convertible and sells the common stock short against it, at an approximate parity.⁷ In the event of a protracted rise, he can convert the senior issue and thus close out the transaction at only a slight loss, consisting of the original spread plus carrying expenses. But if the market declines substantially, he can “undo” the operation at a considerable profit, by selling out the senior issue and buying back the common.

Keith-Albee-Orpheum 7优先股是一种对冲操作的实际示例。该债券可在当时转换为3股Radio-Keith-Orpheum A股票，对冲操作于1929年3月1日建立，1929年3月26日头寸被逆转或“撤销”，如下所示：

<!--en-->
A practical illustration of a hedging operation is afforded by Keith-Albee-Orpheum $7 Preferred, convertible at the time into 3 shares of Radio-Keith-Orpheum A, the hedge being established on March 1, 1929, and the positions reversed or “undone” on March 26, 1929, as follows:

1. 在1929年3月1日以39⅞的价格出售300股R-K-O A，价格为11,962.50美元。减去佣金（45美元）和税（12美元）。所得款项为57.00美元。以折价方式出售的所得为11,905.50美元。于1929年3月26日以29的价格购买300股R-K-O A，价格为8,700.00美元。加上此次购买的佣金。所得款项为45.00美元。对冲成本为8,745.00美元。折价出售利润为3,160.50美元。
2. 于1929年3月1日购买100股Keith-Albee-Orpheum股票，价格为120美元，总费用为12,000.00美元。加上佣金（25美元）。长期股票成本为12,025.00美元。于1929年3月26日以98的价格出售100股Keith-Albee Orpheum股票，价格为9,800.00美元。减去佣金（20美元）和税（4美元）。所得款项为24.00美元。长期股票所得为9,776.00美元。加上长期股票收到的股息175.00美元（优先股于1929年3月19日除权）。长期股票出售及股息净收入为9,951.00美元。长期股票损失为2,074.00美元。
3. 折价出售利润为3,160.50美元。长期股票损失为2,074.00美元。对冲净利润为1,086.50美元。所示利润约为交易所占用资本的9%，且由于交易持续了26天，年利润率超过100%。由于交易无亏损可能，优先股的很大一部分本可以借入，从而大幅提高运营方所投入资本的利润率。在有利的环境下，这种操作能提供巨大收益与极小最大损失的机会。它们特别适合作为防范其他财务承诺的手段，因为在市场下跌时仍能获得利润，而其他资产可能面临亏损。*对冲的一些技术方面。*然而，对冲有许多技术层面，使其并不像我们简要描述那样简单和“防错”。对对冲的详尽讨论超出本书范围，因此下面仅列出有经验的对冲者在进行此类操作时会考虑的某些要素：
1. 能够借入已出售的股票并无限期维持空头头寸。⁸
2. 建立头寸的原始成本，包括价差和佣金。
3. 维持头寸的成本，包括长期股票的利息费用、空头股票的股息、可能的借股溢价、再借股票时的印花税——减去长期证券的股息或应收利息以及空头头寸可能的利息抵免。
4. 如果有机会，操作可能关闭时的利润水平。最大利润与最大可能损失之间的关系，由(2)加(3)组成。需要注意的是，就像证券操作的其余情况一样，需要考虑的潜在利润并非市场上可能达到的最大数字，而只是运营方可能等待关闭头寸的最高数字。一旦确定某个利润，随后可能实现的额外利润就只是理论意义了。*对冲的中间形式。*对冲的中间形式包括购买可转换债券，只出售相关普通股的部分份额，比如转换时应收金额的一半。基于这一基础，如果普通股大幅上涨或大幅下跌，都可能获得利润。这可能是最科学的对冲方法，因为它不需要对价格未来走势做出判断。理想的这种情况应满足以下两个要求：
1. 一种稳固的高级债券，即使普通股急剧下跌，也能确保价格接近面值。短期到期的高品质可转换债券是此目的的理想选择。
2. 一种投机性较强、因此价格可能大幅波动的股票。这种对冲方式的典型例子是1918-1919年皮尔斯石油6股股票（将于1920年发行）及其普通股的交易。⁹正如前面所述，可转换证券所具备的优势也适用于参与式权证和购买权发行。当然，这两种特殊证券也可作为对冲工具使用。同样，从普通股转换为此类证券可能更为理想。第22章中提到的Rand Kardex 5½股，在发行时不仅具有吸引力的直接投资价值，而且确实可以替代A类股票。此外，它还提供了有趣的对冲机会。类似地，如果有人打算长期投资西屋电气制造公司，那么在1929或1930年购买权证时，将其从普通股转换为参与式优先股显然更为明智——因为当时权证的价格低于普通股。然而，在这种情况下，优先股与普通股之间的对冲操作会涉及特殊风险，因为优先股无法转换为次级股。[^4256]：1 有关此问题的详细内容，请参见附录注释40。2 关于参与式证券的多种变体，请参阅附录注释3。3 在1938年末和1939年，1950年发行的鲍德温机车厂6股（可转换为65股普通股）的价格与普通股价格之间存在类似紧密关系。对比1938年股票的$17\frac{1}{4}$高点、债券的$116\frac{1}{2}$高点，以及1939年的$9\frac{1}{8}$和$82\frac{1}{2}$的低点以及随后的$21\frac{1}{4}$和139的高点。4 这不应与面值混淆，面值仅指相关证券的面值。"面值"用于普通股价格时，几乎总是指每股100美元，并不涉及股份的实际面值，后者可能完全不同。5 如果优先股能立即兑换为普通股，则折价会创造*套利*机会。这是一种无需承担损失风险即可获利（通常金额较小）的方式： (1) 同时购买优先股并出售普通股； (2) 立即将优先股转换为普通股； (3) 以普通股交换出售股票，从而完成交易。在活跃上涨市场中，这种"公开且确定"的套利行为非常普遍，但机会通常由专门从事此类操作的经纪人垄断。其他形式的证券间套利源于重组、合并、股票分割、新股票购买权等。详细讨论请参考迈耶·H·韦恩斯坦《证券套利》，哈珀兄弟出版社，1931年。在较旧的意义上，"套利"一词用于同一证券在不同市场（如纽约和伦敦）的同时买卖，以及涉及外汇的类似操作。6 当两种证券都明显具有投机性时，同样的推理仍然适用。*示例：*西部马里兰州铁路优先股可转换为普通股。在1928-1933年期间，其价格从未高于普通股。然而，如果有人愿意持有普通股，他应该转换为优先股，因为优先股拥有普通股的所有优势加上优先地位。1934年初，优先股以比普通股高23美元的合理溢价出售——普通股为17美元。7 商品领域的"对冲"是一种表面相似但本质不同的操作类型。一般来说，其目的是保护正常的制造或分销利润，防止因商品价格变动而遭受投机性损失。 一位磨坊主购买了小麦，几个月后将其作为面粉出售。他会买卖小麦期货，作为对冲手段，以防范小麦价格下跌导致利润减少的风险。当面粉销售完毕时，他会回购所售小麦，以此保护自己的利益。因此，大多数商品对冲措施都是为了提供安全保障，而证券对冲通常旨在获得直接收益。⁸自1934年以来，美国证券交易委员会和股票交易所的规定使得卖空变得更加困难。例如，卖空只能在特定时间内以高于上次交易价格进行。后来这一规则有所放宽，允许以不低于上次交易价格的价格进行卖空。这些规定带来的障碍在一定程度上得到了缓解，因为所讨论的那种对冲措施通常只会在上涨且活跃的市场中实施。⁹这一操作在附录注释41中进行了分析。

The profit indicated was about 9% on the capital tied up in the transaction, and, since it covered a period of 26 days, the profit was at the rate of over 100% per year. Since there was no chance of loss on the transaction, a considerable part of the cost of the preferred stock could properly have been borrowed, thus largely increasing the percentage of profit on the capital supplied by the operator. With favorable surrounding conditions, operations of this kind offer a chance for large gains against a small maximum loss. They are particularly suitable as a form of protection against other financial commitments, for they yield their profit in a declining market when other holdings are likely to show losses.
*Some Technical Aspects of Hedging.* Hedging has numerous technical aspects, however, which make it less simple and “fool-proof” than our brief description would indicate. An exhaustive discussion of hedging would fall outside the scope of this volume, and for this reason we shall merely list below certain elements that the experienced hedger will take into account in embarking upon such operations:
1. Ability to borrow stock sold and to maintain short position indefinitely.⁸
2. Original cost of establishing position, including spread and commissions.
3. Cost of maintaining the position, including interest charges on long holdings, dividends on short stock, possible premiums payable for borrowing stock, and stamp taxes in connection with reborrowings of stock—less offsets in the forms of dividends or interest receivable on long securities and possible interest credit on short position.
4. Amount of profit at which operation will probably be closed out if opportunity offers. Relationship between this maximum profit and probable maximum loss, consisting of (2) plus (3).
It should be borne in mind in these, as in all other operations in securities, that the potential profit to be taken into account is not the maximum figure that mightconceivably be reached in the market but merely the highest figure for which the operator is likely to wait before he closes out his position. Once a given profit is taken, the additional profit that might have been realized subsequently becomes of merely academic interest.
*An Intermediate Form of Hedging.* An intermediate form of hedging consists of purchasing a convertible issue and selling only part of the related common shares, say, one-half of the amount receivable upon conversion. On this basis a profit may be realized in the event of either a substantial advance or a substantial decline in the common stock. This is probably the most scientific method of hedging, since it requires no opinion as to the future course of prices. An ideal situation of this kind would meet the following two requirements:
1. A strongly entrenched senior issue that can be relied on to maintain a price close to par even if the common should drop precipitately. A good convertible bond, maturing in a short time, is an ideal type for this purpose.
2. A common stock in which the speculative interest is large and that is therefore subject to wide fluctuations in either direction.
An example of this form of hedge is supplied by operations carried on in 1918–1919 in Pierce Oil 6s, due in 1920, and the company’s common stock.⁹
The advantages possessed by convertibles, along the lines just described, are shared also by participating and purchase-warrant issues. The latter types of privileged securities may, of course, be used as media for hedging operations. Similarly, it may be found most desirable to switch from common stocks into such issues. The Rand Kardex 5½s, described in Chap. 22, were not only an attractive direct commitment at the time of issuance, but they were certainly a desirable substitute for the Class A stock. Furthermore they offered an interesting hedging opportunity. In like manner, persons committed to a permanent investment in Westinghouse Electric and Manufacturing Company would certainly have been wise toswitch from the common stock into the participating preferred when the latter sold at a lower price than the common in 1929 or 1930. In this case, however, a hedging operation between the preferred and common would have involved special hazards, because the senior issue was not convertible into the junior shares.
[^4256]: 1 See Appendix Note 40 for details concerning this issue.
2 For a number of variations of participating securities, see Appendix Note 3.
3 In the latter part of 1938 and 1939 a similar close relationship existed between the price of Baldwin Locomotive Works 6s, due 1950, convertible into 65 shares of common stock, and the price of the common. Compare the highs of $17\frac{1}{4}$ for the stock and $116\frac{1}{2}$ for the bonds in 1938, with the respective lows of $9\frac{1}{8}$ and $82\frac{1}{2}$ and the subsequent highs of $21\frac{1}{4}$ and 139 in 1939.
4 This should not be confused with par, which means simply the face value of the security in question. "Par," when applied to the price of a common stock, nearly always means $100 per share and has no reference to the real par value of the share, which may be quite different.
5 If the senior issue may be promptly exchanged for the common, a discount results in creating an *arbitrage* opportunity. This is a chance to make a profit (usually small) without risk of loss by: (1) simultaneously buying the senior issue and selling the common stock; (2) immediately converting the senior issue into the common stock; and (3) delivering the common stock against the sale, thus completing the transaction. Arbitraging of "open-and-shut" kind is done rather extensively in active, rising markets, but the opportunities are usually monopolized by brokers specializing in such operations. Other forms of intersecurity arbitrage operations arise from reorganizations, mergers, stock split-ups, rights to buy new stocks, etc. For detailed discussion see Meyer H. Weinstein, *Arbitrage in Securities*, Harper & Brothers, 1931. In the older sense, the term "arbitrage" applied to simultaneous purchases and sales of the same security in different markets (e.g., New York and London), and to similar operations involving foreign exchange.
6 The same reasoning holds true when both issues are confessedly speculative.
*Example:* Western Maryland Railroad Preferred is convertible into common share for share. It sold no higher than the common during the greater part of 1928–1933. Yet, if any one was willing to own the common, he should have switched into the preferred, which had all the possibilities of the common plus its senior position. Early in 1934 the preferred sold at a fair premium above the common—23 against 17.
7 "Hedging" in commodities is a superficially similar but basically different type of operation. Generally speaking, its purpose is to protect a normal manufacturing or distributing profit against the chance of speculative loss through commodity price
changes. A miller, having bought wheat that he will sell as flour some months later, will sell wheat futures as a “hedge” against the possibility of a decline in wheat destroying his profit margin. When the flour is disposed of, he covers (buys back) the wheat sold as protection. Most commodity hedging is thus designed as a safeguard, whereas security hedging is usually intended to yield direct profits.
⁸ Regulations of the S.E.C. and the stock exchanges have made short selling more difficult since 1934. For example, short sales could be made for a time only at a price higher than the last previous trade. The rule was later relaxed to permit short sales at a price no lower than the last trade. The obstacle imposed by these rules is mitigated in part by the fact that hedges of the kind under discussion are ordinarily set up only in a rising and fairly active market.
⁹ This operation is analyzed in the Appendix Note 41.

## 第30章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 30*

# 股票红利

<!--en-->
*Stock Dividends*

以股票而非现金形式进行的分配有两种类型，可称为*特别*红利和*定期*红利。特别股票红利可以定义为将过去几年的累积盈余部分转化为资本；即，它将大量累积盈余转移到资本中，并向股东提供额外股份以代表这些转移的资金。

<!--en-->
DISTRIBUTIONS MADE in the form of stock instead of cash are of two kinds, which may be called *extraordinary* and *periodic*. An extraordinary stock dividend may be defined as one that capitalizes part of the accumulated surplus of past years; *i.e.*, it transfers a substantial amount from the accumulated surplus to stated capital and gives the stockholders additional shares to represent the funds thus transferred.

定期股票红利可以定义为仅将*当前年度*的收益部分转化为资本。因此，它通常规模较小。被称为定期红利是因为根据既定政策，这种红利会在多年内重复发放。

<!--en-->
A periodic stock dividend may be defined as one that capitalizes part of only the *current year's* earnings. Hence it is almost always of relatively small size. It is called periodic because such dividends are usually repeated over a number of years in accordance with an established policy.

## 特别股票红利

<!--en-->
*EXTRAORDINARY STOCK DIVIDENDS*

特别股票红利是合法且合理的，但总体上会产生不良影响。这种红利之所以合理实用，唯一原因是它能将股票的市场价格调整至更合适的水平。广泛的公众兴趣和活跃的市场是普通股票的理想属性，当正常价格范围上升到如每股300美元或400美元这样的高数值时，这些属性就会减弱。因此，通过大量股票红利增加股份数量并降低每股价值，是一个合理的举措。

<!--en-->
Extraordinary stock dividends are legal and legitimate, but by and large they produce unfortunate effects. The only reason for such a dividend that is at once sound and practical is that it will adjust the market price of the shares to a more convenient level. Widespread public interest and an active market are desirable attributes of a common stock, and these are diminished when the normal price range has advanced to such a high figure as, say, $300 or $400 per share. Hence an increase in the number of shares and the reduction in value of each share, by means of a large stock dividend, would be a logical step to take.

*示例：* 1917年，贝塞斯达钢铁公司的股票售价超过每股500美元。支付了200%的股票红利（并按面值出售了额外股份），使市场价格降至约150美元。

<!--en-->
*Example:* In 1917 Bethlehem Steel stock was selling above $500 per share. A stock dividend of 200% was paid(and additional shares were sold at par) bringing the market price down to about 150.

**拆股。** 通过降低股份的面值也可以得到相同结果，这种操作通常称为“拆股”。在20世纪20年代的牛市期间，降低面值的情况比对面值股票进行大量股票红利更为常见，因为市场价格上涨幅度远远超过了累积盈余，分配盈余不足以达到目的。

<!--en-->
**Split-Ups.** Exactly the same result may be obtained by reducing the par value of the shares, such a move being referred to familiarly as a “splitup.” During the bull market of the 1920s reductions in par value were much more frequent than large stock dividends on stocks with par value, because the rise in market price had so far outstripped the accumulated surplus that a distribution of the latter would have been insufficient for the purpose.

*示例：* 1926年，通用电气公司的股票售价为360美元。每1股100美元面值的旧股对应4股无面值新股，从而使市场价格降至约90美元。若通过300%的股票红利实现同样效果，则需要从盈余中转移5.4亿美元到资本，但当时盈余仅为1亿美元。1930年，通用电气公司再次将1股股份拆分为4股，情况类似。

<!--en-->
*Example:* In 1926 General Electric stock was selling at 360. Four new shares of no-par value were given for each old share of $100 par value, thus reducing the market price to about 90. To have effected the same result by a 300% stock dividend would have required the transfer of 540 millions from surplus to capital, but the surplus was then only 100 millions. A similar situation existed in 1930 when General Electric shares were again split four for one.

对于伍尔沃斯公司，最初发行的500,000股普通股通过股票红利和拆股等步骤增加到9,750,000股。

<!--en-->
In the case of Woolworth, the original common issue of 500,000 shares was increased to 9,750,000 shares by the following steps, involving both stock dividends and split-ups.

<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>总股份数<br>已发行股份数</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1920年：股票红利为30%，价格从约140美元降至约110美元</td><td>650,000</td></tr><tr><td>1924年：面值从100美元降至25美元，价格从约320美元降至约80美元</td><td>2,600,000</td></tr><tr><td>1927年：股票红利为50%，价格从约180美元降至约120美元</td><td>3,900,000</td></tr><tr><td>1929年：面值从25美元降至10美元，价格从约225美元降至约90美元</td><td>9,750,000</td></tr></tbody></table>

<!--en-->
<table><thead><tr><th></th><th>Total Shares<br>Outstanding</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>1920: Stock dividend of 30%, reducing the price from about 140 to about 110</td><td>650,000</td></tr><tr><td>1924: Par value cut from $100 to $25, reducing the price from about 320 to about 80</td><td>2,600,000</td></tr><tr><td>1927: Stock dividend of 50%, reducing the price from about 180 to about 120</td><td>3,900,000</td></tr><tr><td>1929: Par value cut from $25 to $10, reducing the price from about 225 to about 90</td><td>9,750,000</td></tr></tbody></table>

美国罐装公司于1926年同时使用了这两种方式。它将面值从100美元降至25美元，并支付50%的股票红利。因此，1股原股对应6股新股，价格从约300美元降至约50美元。

<!--en-->
American Can combined both devices at one time in 1926. It reduced the par value from $100 to $25 and also paid a stock dividend of 50%. Hence six shares were issued for one, and the price was reduced from about 300 to about 50.

**无面值股票的拆股与股票红利。** 对于无面值普通股，拆股或股票红利会产生完全相同的结果，在实际用途上无法区分。虽然股票红利需要将一定金额从盈余转移到资本，但无面值股票允许的无限会计空间可能使这种转移纯粹是名义上的。

<!--en-->
**Stock Splits and Stock Dividends in No-Par Stock.** In the case of common stocks of no-par value, a split-up or a stockdividend leads to exactly the same results, and to all practical purposes they are indistinguishable. Although a stock dividend requires the transfer of a certain sum on the books from surplus to capital, the infinite latitude in accounting permitted by no-par stock may make this transfer a purely nominal affair.

*示例：* 中央州电力公司于1926年支付了900%的股票红利，无面值股份数量从109,000股增加到1,090,000股。1925年底，旧股的书面价值约为每股44美元，但新股以每股1美元的价格从盈余中扣除。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Central States Electric Corporation paid a 900% stock dividend in 1926, increasing the number of shares (no par) from 109,000 to 1,090,000. The old stock had a book value of about $44 per share at the end of 1925, but the new stock was charged against surplus at the rate of only $1 per share.

同样在1929年，可口可乐公司在无面值A类股票中支付了100%的股票红利。尽管A类股票具有50美元面值的6%优先股的所有特征，除了正式指定面值外，但这股股票的书面价值为每股5美元（低于普通股的标价）。（另见该公司1927年普通股100%股息的会计处理，以及第42章中对A类股票回购处理的讨论。）

<!--en-->
Similarly in 1929, the Coca-Cola Company paid a 100% stock dividend in Class *A* stock without par value. This stock was booked at $5 per share (lower than the stated value of the common) despite the fact that the Class *A* stock has all of the characteristics of a $50-par, 6% preferred issue, except formal designation of such a par figure. (See also the accounting by this company of its 100% dividend payable in common stock in 1927, and also our discussion of its treatment of repurchases of Class *A* shares in Chap. 42.)

**对特别股票股息和股票分割的反对意见。** 特别股票股息和股票分割都面临一个严重反对意见：其宣布会对市场价格产生不当影响，因此成为内部人员操纵和获取不公正利润的途径。显然，理论上，大量股票股息并不会给股东带来他之前没有拥有的东西。他现在的两张纸实际上代表了之前由一张纸所表达的同一种所有权。这种推理导致美国最高法院裁定，股票股息不属于收入，因此无需缴纳所得税。¹ 然而在实践中，股票股息很容易被赋予特殊的投机性意义。因为股票投机很大程度上是A试图判断B、C和D会怎么想——而B、C和D也试图做同样的事情。因此，即使股票股息没有任何实际意义，它仍然可以并确实成为促进那种*相互利用对方*行为的刺激因素，而这往往是投机者的活动基础。² **对现金股息率的影响。** 如果不存在具有真正重要性的投资因素，大量股票股息的本质模糊性就会更加明显。特别股票股息的支付通常预示着常规现金股息率的上升。由于投资者理所当然地关心现金股息，他们必然也关心任何股票股息，因为这可能影响到可能的现金股息。这有助于混淆问题，使股票股息宣布中的纯粹操纵性方面不那么明显。

<!--en-->
**Objections to Extraordinary Stock Dividends and Split-Ups.** Extraordinary stock dividends and stock split-ups are both open to the serious objection that their declaration exercises an undue influence upon market prices and hence that they afford an avenue for manipulation and for unfair profits by insiders. It is obvious that in theory a large stock dividend gives the stockholder nothing that he did not own before. His two pieces of paper now represent the same ownership formerly expressed by one piece of paper. This reasoning led the United States Supreme Court to decide that stock dividends are not income and consequently not subject to income tax.¹ In practice, however, a stock dividend may readily be given exceptional speculative importance. For stock speculation is largely a matter of A trying to decide what B, C and D are likely to think—with B, C, and D trying to do the same. Hence a stock dividend, even if it has no real significance of any kind, can and does serve as a stimulus tothat *mutual attempt at taking advantage of each other* which often lies at the bottom of speculators' activities.²
**Effect on the Cash Dividend Rate.** The essentially illusive character of large stock dividends would be more evident were it not for the fact that an investment element of real importance may also enter into the picture. The payment of an extraordinary stock dividend is usually the forerunner of an increase in the regular cash dividend rate. Since investors are legitimately interested in the cash dividend, they must necessarily be interested also in any stock dividend, for this may have a bearing upon the probable cash dividend. This serves to confuse the issue and to make less obtrusive the purely manipulative aspects of stock-dividend declarations.

一家成功工业公司的股息历史常常呈现以下顺序：

<!--en-->
The dividend history of a successful industrial corporation frequently discloses the following sequence:

1. 相对于收益而言股息较低且持续时间较长，同时积累大量盈余。
2. 突然支付大量股票股息。3. 常规现金股息支付立即增加。³ 没有哪种政策能更有助于混淆投资和投机态度，或更容易让控制者获取不公正利益。

<!--en-->
1. A protracted period of small dividends in relation to earnings, with the upbuilding of a huge surplus.
2. The sudden payment of a large stock dividend. 3. An immediate increase in the regular cash dividend payments.³
No policy could be more conducive to the confusion of investment and speculative attitudes or lend itself more easily to the taking of unfair advantage by those in control.

### 定期股票股息

<!--en-->
*PERIODIC STOCK DIVIDENDS*

这一政策在基本稳健性方面比我们一直在讨论的随意且往往不公平的做法有了巨大进步。这些做法首先包括将大量未分配收益积累在盈余账户中，其次是在任意时间和任意金额通过股票股息将其最终资本化。假设在许多情况下，保留每年大部分收益对于业务来说是可取的，那么让股东们现在获得他们对这些再投资收益的切实证明，将最有利于他们的利益。

<!--en-->
This policy represents a great advance in basic soundness over the haphazard and often inequitable practices that we have been discussing. Such practices involve first the large accumulation of undistributed earnings in the surplus account, and second the ultimate capitalization thereof through stock dividends at arbitrary times and in arbitrary amounts. Assuming that in many cases it may be desirable to retain a good part of each year's earnings in the business, then the interests of the stockholders would be best served by giving them currently a tangible evidence of their ownership of these reinvested profits.

如果一家企业每年每股赚12美元，只支付5美元现金，那么股东们每年收到代表公司资源增加的7美元中的大部分的股票股息，将会获得巨大好处。当然，理论上，额外的股票证书不会给他带来他没有证书时不会拥有的东西；换句话说，没有股票股息，他的旧证书仍然完全代表每股增加的7美元的所有权。但实际上，定期股票股息的支付会产生重要优势。其中包括以下几点：

<!--en-->
If an enterprise regularly earns $12 per share and pays out only $5 in cash, the stockholders would benefit greatly by receiving each year a stock dividend representing a good part of the $7 added to their company's resources. In theory, of course, the additional stock certificate gives him nothing that he would not own without it; in other words, without a stock dividend his old certificate would still fully represent the ownership of the added $7 per share. But in actuality the payment of periodic stock dividends produces important advantages. Among them are the following:

1. 股东可以出售股票股息证书，从而可以选择获得现金或更多的股票来代表再投资收益。如果没有股票股息，理论上他可以通过出售旧证书所代表的少量股份达到同样目的，但实践中这很难计算且执行不便。
2. 由于这种政策，他可能会获得更大的现金股息，因为确定的现金股息率通常会继续适用于增加的股份数量。例如，如果一家年收入12美元的公司支付5美元现金和5%股票，下一年它很可能会在新的资本基础上支付5美元现金，相当于之前持股时的5.25美元。如果没有股票股息，它可能会继续维持不变的5美元比率。⁴
3. 通过将再投资收益加到法定资本中（而不是盈余中），管理层直接有义务通过这些新增资源赚钱并支付股息。关于损益盈余则不存在这样的责任。股票股息程序不仅是对管理层效率的挑战，也是对再投资所涉及资金智慧的正确检验。
4. 支付定期股票股息的证券，其市场价值高于不支付此类股息的普通股票。**定期股票股息支付的实践变化。**从约1923年直到随后的经济萧条期间，定期股票股息的支付实践发展得非常迅速。采用了三种不同的做法：
1. 标准做法是除了常规现金股息外，再支付股票股息。这些股票股息按月、⁵季度、⁶半年或⁷年度支付。
2. 有时以定期股票股息代替常规现金股息。这表现为给予股东选择收取一定金额现金或股票的选择权。*示例：*Seagrave公司从1925年到1929年（包括这一年）按年度比例，以1.20美元现金或10%股票的形式每季度支付股息。⁹
3. 在少数情况下，只支付股票股息，不支付现金或提供选择权。定期股票股息最著名的实践者North American公司，在1923年至1933年间采用这种方式，每季度以21/2%的股票形式支付股息，后于1933年将比例降至2%。（1935年，该公司放弃了股票股息政策，恢复现金股息模式。）**定期股票股息的令人反感之处。**几乎每种财务实践都可能被滥用，定期股票股息也不例外。此情况下的令人反感之处在于：设定的定期股票股息比例在市场价值上超过留存收益的实际金额。这种做法使该证券对不明智的买家显得过于吸引人，因为当前以股票形式支付的现金价值很高，导致他们被误导。需要了解企业会计方法才能理解这种股票股息支付的真正意义。我们以North American公司的案例作为说明。如我们所言，这家公司连续十年对普通股按每年10%的比例支付股票股息。在这段时期的大部分时间里，从账面上看，10%的股票股息仅相当于每股1美元。这是因为1927年前股票的面值为10美元，而股票变为无面值后，账面上仍将其“名义价值”定为每股10美元。因此，无论是面值还是名义价值中的10%，都仅相当于每股1美元。但从投资者角度看，他实际获得的股息价值远高于每股1美元，因为North American普通股的市场价格远远高于其面值或名义价值。以下表格会显示具体数据。值得注意的是，从1931年的第三季度支付开始，用于股票股息的收益扣除额从每股1美元增加到每年1.468美元。这是应纽约证券交易所的要求，旨在让用于股票股息的收益扣除额反映新股份在资本盈余及名义资本中的权益。然而，即使进行了这一调整，账面上对股息的估值与股市、以及股东认为的股息价值之间仍存在巨大差异，直到价格进一步下跌。*恶性循环的风险。*这种安排可能会形成恶性循环。市场价格越高，股票股息的表面价值就越高，进而似乎可以证明更高的市场价格是合理的。（即使股票股息为10%，无论市场价格上升多高，股息回报显然仍为10%）。这种结果具有欺骗性，会为疯狂投机和无脑投资提供不良动力。实际上，这与许多年前American Can和National Biscuit等公司所采取的做法相反，当时它们通过过于“保守”的股息政策，将市场价格保持在远低于股份真实价值水平。当然，追求一种旨在创造高于收益和其他价值因素所支撑的市场价格的策略同样令人反感。这种不合理的价格必然是暂时的，并且像所有不当会计行为一样，可能导致参与者获得相对于投资公众的不公平优势。¹⁰

<!--en-->
1. The stockholder can sell the stock-dividend certificate, so that at his option he can have either cash or more stock to represent the reinvested earnings. Without a stock dividend he might in theory accomplish the same end by selling a small part of the shares represented by his old certificate, but in practice this is difficult to calculate and inconvenient in execution.
2. He is likely to receive larger cash dividends as a result of such a policy, because the established cash rate will usually be continued on the increased number of shares. For example, if a company earning $12 pays out $5 in cash and 5% in stock, in the next year it will most probably pay $5 in cash on the new capitalization, equivalent to $5.25 on the previous holdings. Without the stock dividend, it would probably continue the $5 rate unchanged.⁴
3. By adding the reinvested profits to the stated capital (instead of to surplus) the management is placed under a direct obligation to earn money and pay dividends on these added resources. No such accountability exists with respect to the profit and loss surplus. The stock-dividend procedure will serve not only as a challenge to the efficiency of the management but also as a proper test of the wisdom of reinvesting the sums involved.
4. Issues paying periodic stock dividends enjoy a higher market value than similar common stocks not paying such dividends.
**Variations in the Practice of Periodic Stock-Dividend Payment.** The practice of disbursing periodic stock dividendsdeveloped fairly rapidly from about 1923 until the subsequent depression. Three variations of the idea were resorted to:
1. The standard method was to pay a stock dividend in addition to the regular cash dividend. These stock dividends were paid either monthly,⁵ quarterly,⁶ semiannually,⁷ or annually.⁸
2. Sometimes a periodic stock dividend was offered in lieu of the regular cash dividend. This took the form of an option to the stockholder to take a certain amount of either cash or stock.
*Example:* The Seagrave Corporation paid a dividend quarterly at the annual rate of either $1.20 in cash or 10% in stock between 1925 and 1929, inclusive.⁹
3. In a few cases stock dividends only were paid, with no cash disbursement or option. The most prominent exponent of periodic stock dividends, the North American Company, followed this procedure by paying dividends of 21/2% in stock, quarterly, between 1923 and 1933, in which latter year the payment was reduced to 2% quarterly. (In 1935 the company gave up the stock-dividend policy and returned to a cash-dividend basis.)
**Objectionable Feature of Periodic Stock Dividends.** Nearly every financial practice is open to abuse, and periodic stock dividends have proved no exception. The objectionable feature in this case has been to establish a regular stock-dividend rate exceeding in market value the amount of the earnings carried to surplus. This practice makes the issue appear unduly attractive to the unintelligent buyer, who is deceived by the high cash value of the current payments in stock. It requires some insight into corporate accounting methods to realize the true significance of such stock-dividend payments.
Let us use the outstanding North American Company case as an illustration. As we have stated, this company paid continuous stock dividends on the common shares at the rate of 10% annually for ten years. During most of this period the 10% stock dividend represented a payment of only $1 pershare, as far as its books were concerned. This followed from the fact that prior to 1927 the par value of the stock was $10 and that after the shares were made no-par they were still given a "stated value" on the books at $10 per share. Hence 10% of either the par or the stated value amounted to only $1 per share. But from the investor's viewpoint he was receiving dividends worth much more than $1 per share, because the market price of North American common far exceeded its par or stated value.
The facts will appear from the table that follows.
It will be noted that beginning with the third quarterly payment in 1931, the amount charged against earnings for the stock dividend was advanced from $1 to $1.468 per share annually. This followed a request from the New York Stock Exchange that the charge against earnings or earned surplus covering the stock dividends reflect the interest of the new shares in the capital surplus as well as in the stated capital. Even after this change was made, however, there remained a wide discrepancy between the amount at which the dividends were valued on the books and the value given these dividends by the stock market, and presumably by the stockholders, until the quotation suffered a further severe decline.
*Danger of Vicious Circle Developing.* An arrangement of this kind is likely to develop into a vicious circle. The higher the market price the greater the apparent value of the stock dividends, which in turn will seem to justify a still higher market price. (With a 10% stock dividend the dividend return obviously remains at 10% regardless of how high the market price may climb.) Such a result is deceptive and supplies an unwholesome impetus to riotous speculation as well as to thoughtless investment. In effect it is the opposite of the practice followed many years ago by such companies as American Can and National Biscuit, when the market price was kept far below the true value of the shares by an unduly "conservative" dividend policy. It is fully as objectionable, of course, to pursue a policy calculated to create a market price higher than that warranted by the earnings and other value factors. Such an unjustified price must necessarily be of temporary duration and is likely to result (as does all improperaccounting) in giving the initiated an unfair advantage over the investing public.¹⁰

<!--en-->
* Based on the average number of shares outstanding during the year.
† First two quarterly dividends in 1931 were booked at $1 and last two at $1 to capital stock and 46.8 cents to capital surplus.
**Historical Development.** From the historical standpoint it is interesting to note that the North American Company began its stock-dividend policy at about the same time that the first protagonist of the idea had decided to abandon it. This was the American Light and Traction Company, which during 1910–1919 had paid dividends at the annual rate of both $10 in cash and 10% in stock. During 1916 when the stock sold at about 400, the stockholders were receiving dividends with a realizable value of some $50 annually, although the earnings were only about $25 per share. Such a dividend policy could be permanently successful only if the company could continuously reinvest in its business ever-increasing amounts of profits, upon which in turn it could realize 20% annually. The law of diminishing returns (and the voracious growth of compound interest) would clearly outlaw such a possibility. In the depression of 1920–1921 American Light and Traction found it necessary to reduce its dividend rate sharply. The market quotation fell below 80, an astounding decline for an *investment stock* during that period. (The price range ofAtchison during the years 1916–1921 was between 109 and 76.) This experience led the directors to give up the periodic stock-dividend idea in 1925, at the very time when it was coming into general favor among other public-utility holding companies. The abandonment of stock dividends by North American Company ten years later is a striking illustration of the way in which financial history repeats itself.

### 股票分红恶性金字塔式增长示例。

<!--en-->
*Example of Vicious Pyramiding on Stock Dividends.*

在繁荣时期，定期股票分红成为报告利润的特别恶性金字塔式增长的手段。运营公司会支付市场价值高于当前收益的股票分红，而投资信托或控股公司则将这些股票分红作为收入，金额等于市场价值。例如，作为北美公司普通股大持有者的中央州电力公司，在1928年的总收入（不包括证券销售收益）为7,188,178美元。其中，6,396,225美元由当年收到的北美公司股票构成，这些股票按每次季度分红记录日期后的北美公司市场价值计入接收方的账目。这些股票分红作为收入入账的平均价格为每股74美元，即10%分红为7.40美元。而在那一年，北美公司平均流通股数量下，每股收益为4.68美元。尽管如此，股市利用中央州电力公司的这些人为收益来评估该公司股票的价值。¹¹

<!--en-->
During the boom years periodic stock dividends were made the medium of an especially vicious pyramiding of reported profits. An operating company would pay out stock dividends with a market value more than its current earnings, and in turn an investment trust or holding company would report these stock dividends as income in an amount equal to the market value. For example, Central States Electric Corporation, which is a large holder of North American Company common stock, reported a total income in 1928 (exclusive of profits on the sale of securities) of $7,188,178. Of this sum, $6,396,225 was represented by stock of North American received during the year and taken on the recipient's books at the market value for North American immediately following the date of record for each quarterly dividend. The average price at which these stock dividends were taken on the books as income was $74 per share, or $7.40 for the 10% dividend, in a year in which North American earned $4.68 per share on the average number of shares outstanding. Nevertheless, the stock market capitalized these artificial earnings of Central States Electric Corporation to arrive at its valuation of that company's shares.¹¹

### 股票市场价格应被纳入股票分红支付中。

<!--en-->
*Market Price of Shares Should Be Recognized in Stock-Dividend Payments.*

纽约证券交易所最终采纳了新的上市要求，根据此要求，公司同意不将收到的市场价值高于“发行公司与其相关的收益、盈余或未分配利润”的数值的股票分红计入收入账户。

<!--en-->
The New York Stock Exchange finally adopted a new listing requirement under which corporations agree not to take into their income accounts stock dividends received, at a valuation greater than the amount at which such stock dividends were charged “against earnings, earned surplus or undivided profits by the issuing company in relation thereto.”

虽然这项规定设计合理，但并未触及问题的核心。通过简单的规则即可轻易防止定期股票分红程序的滥用：*按市场价值*支付的股票分红不得超过可用于分红的收益。声明可以如下形式表述：“特此宣布5%的股票分红。该分红的市场价值约为每股6美元，代表了从每股10美元当前收益中保留的每股7美元资本化收益。”

<!--en-->
Although this regulation was properly conceived, it does not go to the heart of the matter. The abuses of the periodicstock-dividend procedure may be readily prevented by the simple rule that stock dividends *at market value* must not exceed the earnings available for dividends. Declarations might well be made in the following form: "A stock dividend of 5% is hereby declared. The market value of this dividend is approximately $6 per share, and it represents the capitalization of $7 per share retained in the business out of current earnings of $10 per share."

**以优先股支付股票股息的优势。** 股息可以以优先股而非普通股的形式支付。这种方法的典型例子是通用电气公司，在1922年至1925年间，除了定期支付8美元现金股息外，还每年额外发放5%的股息。这些额外股息以6%的特殊股票形式支付，面值为10美元，实际上属于优先股。S. H. Kress公司和Hartman Corporation也采用了类似做法。这种方法的理论优势在于，支付的股息金额明确固定在所发行优先股的实际面值¹²上，因此避免了账面价值与市场价值差异带来的复杂性。如果公司没有高级证券，或只有少量高级证券，通过发行代表再投资收益的优先股，不会削弱资本结构。

<!--en-->
**Advantages of Stock Dividends Payable in Preferred Stock.** Dividends may be paid in preferred stock instead of common stock. The chief exemplar of this method is General Electric Company, which distributed extra dividends of 5% annually between 1922 and 1925, in addition to the regular payment of $8 in cash. These extra dividends were paid in 6% special stock, par value $10, which was in reality a preferred stock. A similar procedure was followed by S. H. Kress Company and by Hartman Corporation. The theoretical advantage of this method is that the amount of the dividend paid is clearly fixed at the effective par value¹² of the preferred shares issued, thus obviating the complication presented by differences between book value and market value. Where the company has no senior securities, or only a small amount, the issuance of preferred stock to represent reinvested earnings will not weaken the capital structure.

1934年，通用电气公司确定其营运资金状况非常良好，可以注销全部特殊股票，并于1935年4月进行了赎回。这可以说是从股东角度处理未分配收益的理想安排。两个步骤如下：

<!--en-->
In 1934 General Electric Company determined that its working-capital position was so comfortable as to permit the retirement of the entire issue of special stock, which was accordingly redeemed in April 1935. This may be said to represent the ideal arrangement from the stockholder's standpoint in dealing with undistributed earnings. The two steps involved are as follows:

1. 在繁荣年份，收益被保留用于扩张或增加营运资金，但股东会定期获得优先股，代表其中的一部分。
2. 如果后续业务发展表明不再需要额外资金，则通过赎回优先股的方式将资金分配给股东。**以上总结。** 我们在本章及前章中详细讨论的适当股息政策概念，可总结为以下三点：¹³
1. 必须向股东明确说明，保留并再投资大部分收益的理由，即从中获得的实际利益超过若支付给股东现金的价值。这种保留应得到股东的特别批准。
2. 如果保留利润在任何意义上属于必要而非选择，应告知股东这一事实，并将相关金额称为“储备金”，而非“超额利润”。
3. 自愿保留于业务的收益应通过定期发行额外股票来资本化，当前市场价值不应超过该再投资收益。如果后来发现额外资金不再需要，应将其分配给股东，以抵消之前发行的股票的赎回。[^4313]：¹ 这是1920年的著名*Eisner vs. Macomber*案（252 U. S. 189）。1936年，最高法院在*Koshland*案（297 U. S. 702）中裁定，给予股东与之前不同的比例权益的股票股息需征税。根据税务上诉委员会的裁决，例如，对于部分尚未发行的优先股所支付的股息，也应适用此规则。

<!--en-->
1. In prosperous years earnings are retained for expansion or added working capital, but the stockholders receive preferred shares periodically to represent a portion thereof.
2. If subsequent business developments show that the additional capital is no longer needed, it is paid out to the stockholders through the redemption of their preferred shares.
**The Foregoing Summarized.** Our conception of suitable dividend policies, discussed at length in this and the preceding chapter, may be summed up in the following three statements:¹³
1. Withholding and reinvestment of a substantial part of the earnings must be clearly justified to the stockholders on the grounds of concrete benefits therefrom exceeding the value of the cash if paid to the stockholders. Such withholding should be specifically approved by the stockholders.
2. If retention of profits is in any sense a matter of necessity rather than choice, the stockholders should be advised of this fact, and the amounts involved should be designated as “reserves” instead of as “surplus profits.”
3. Earnings voluntarily retained in the business should be capitalized in good part by the periodic issuance of additional stock, with current market value not exceeding such reinvested earnings. If the additional capital is subsequently found no longer to be needed in the business, it should be distributed to the shareholders against the retirement of the stock previously issued to represent it.
[^4313]: ¹ This was the famous *Eisner vs. Macomber* decision in 1920 (252 U. S. 189). In 1936 the Supreme Court decided, in the *Koshland* case (297 U. S. 702), that stock dividends that gave the stockholder a different pro-rata interest than he had before were taxable. Under a ruling of the Board of Tax Appeals this would apply, for example, to a dividend payable in preferred stock of which some was previously outstanding.

11 Middle West Utilities followed a similar practice between 1928 and April 1932 with respect to stock dividends received both from subsidiaries and from other companies. The receivers subsequently wrote down the corporate surplus to correct the overvaluation of these stock dividends received from subsidiaries.

12 如果以*可转换优先股*形式支付，当然无法完全消除高估的风险。例如，哥伦比亚煤气与电力公司于1932年向普通股股东支付了1.125美元，以5%的可转换优先股形式（面值100美元）。1932年，优先股价格高达108美元，1933年达到138美元，相当于那些年份公司普通股的收益数倍。

<!--en-->
12 If payment is made in a *convertible preferred stock* the danger of overvaluation is, of course, not fully eliminated. For example, Columbia Gas and Electric Corporation during 1932 paid $1.125 to common stockholders in 5% ConvertiblePreference Stock (par $100) common. The preference stock sold as high as 108 during 1932 and 138 in 1933, or at equivalents substantially in excess of the earnings of the company on its common stock during those years.

CHAPTER 35

### 公共公用事业折旧

<!--en-->
*Public-Utility Depreciation*

政策 **折旧费用的省略**。在任何行业，正确的折旧政策的重要性都不如公用事业行业。然而，在理论和实践方面，差异最为明显。几年前，例如城市服务公司，在年度报告中完全未计提折旧费用（及消耗费用），导致股票收益数据严重失真。¹ 人们常常认为可以忽略折旧费用，因为这只是记账项目，并不代表实际现金支出。这种说法非常不准确。折旧并非单纯的记账概念，因为大多数情况下，它反映了资本价值的真实减少，如果债权人或所有者不想自欺，就必须做好相应的准备。² 此外，在大多数情况下，折旧费用会在一段时间内被更大规模的现金支出所抵消，这些支出用于更换设备或扩展业务。因此，折旧费用最终往往与实际现金支出相关，就像工资或租金一样属于企业费用。少数情况下，很大一部分折旧储备在很长一段时间内未被使用。在这种情况下，投资者计算时有时可以认为减少年度折旧费用是合理的，我们稍后会解释。不过，基本原则仍然是：合理的折旧拨备对于得出公平的收益报告至关重要。

<!--en-->
Policies
**Omission of Depreciation Charges.** In no field does the question of proper depreciation policy have such practical importance as in the public-utility group. Yet nowhere have there been wider variations in both theory and practice. Some years ago there were instances—notably that of Cities Service Company—of complete failure to make any deduction for depreciation (and depletion) in the annual reports, with a resultant gross misstatement of the earnings for the stock.¹ The argument has often been advanced that depreciation charges may properly be ignored because they are mere bookkeeping entries and do not represent a real outlay of cash. This is a highly inaccurate statement of the case. Depreciation is not a mere bookkeeping conception, because for the most part it registers an actual diminution of capital values, for which adequate provision must be made if creditors or owners are to avoid deceiving themselves.²
Moreover, in the majority of cases the depreciation charges are consumed or offset over a period of time by even larger cash expenditures made for replacements or extensions. More often than not, therefore, depreciation charges are eventually found to be related to actual cash outlays and turn out to be as truly an expense of the business as wages or rents. Minority cases are fairly numerous in which a good part of the depreciation reserve remains unexpended over a long period of time. In these instances a reduction of the annual charges may sometimes be justified in the investor's calculations, as we shall later explain. The broad principle remains, however,that an adequate depreciation allowance is essential in arriving at a fair statement of earnings.

**其他误导性的做法**。另一种相当常见的做法是仅从收益中扣除部分折旧费用，剩余部分从盈余账户中扣除。在某些情况下，计入收入的金额基于所谓的“债券最低要求”——即根据债券发行条款，必须扣除的维护与折旧总收益的百分比。当这些债券最低要求低于实际需要的折旧额时，我们发现，表面上为保护投资者而设定的要求，实际上被用来误导他们。³ 不幸的是，保守管理的公司有时也会采用类似的做法。请参考1931年和1930年底特律爱迪生公司的报告中的内容。

<!--en-->
**Other Misleading Practices.** Another fairly prevalent practice was the deduction of only part of the depreciation charge from earnings, the balance being taken out of the surplus account. In some instances the amounts charged to income were based on the so-called “indenture minima”—a percentage of gross earnings for maintenance and depreciation combined required to be deducted under the terms of a bond issue. When these indenture minima were less than the depreciation actually needed and taken, we find that requirements ostensibly set up for the protection of investors were actually used to mislead them.³
It is unfortunate that something resembling this practice has been resorted to at times by conservatively managed companies. Note the following in the reports of the Detroit Edison Company for 1931 and 1930.

尽管底特律爱迪生的折旧费用相比行业平均水平较为宽松，但1931年（以及1934年）使用的会计方法可能因两个原因受到批评。首先，其效果甚至目的，都是掩盖前一年收益的真实下降。其次，由于公司声誉良好，这种手段可能会被其他企业模仿，从而为将费用转入盈余账户、夸大收益的新做法提供不良激励。

<!--en-->
Although Detroit Edison’s depreciation charges have been unusually liberal by comparison with the average for the industry, the accounting method employed for 1931 (and also in 1934) might well be criticized for two reasons. In the first place its effect, if not its purpose, was to disguise the actual decline in earnings from the previous year. Secondly, because of the high reputation of the company, this device was likely to be imitated by other enterprises, and thus it might furnish an unwholesome stimulus to the new practice of overstating earnings by the transfer of charges to the surplus account.

**复杂会计的一个例子**。爱荷华公共服务公司展示了复杂会计的一个典型例子。1929年，该公司报告称资产为25,200,000美元，总收入为4,200,000美元，折旧费用仅为78,000美元。这一数字明显不足。在后续几年中，折旧拨备逐渐增加，到1932年达到220,000美元，仍属较低水平。1932年，该公司通过以下独特方式正式承认过去折旧费用不足：

<!--en-->
**An Illustration of Tricky Accounting.** An extraordinary example of tricky accounting is displayed by Iowa Public Service Company. For 1929 this company reported a property account of $25,200,000, gross earnings of $4,200,000 and a depreciation charge of only $78,000. The inadequacy of this figure is patent. In succeeding years the depreciation allowance was gradually increased, reaching $220,000 in 1932, which was still a somewhat subnormal figure. In 1932, the company made formal confession of the insufficiency of its past depreciation charges, by the following unique procedure:

1. 它将普通股的价值减少了1,587,000美元，并将这笔金额转入资本盈余。
2. 它立即用这笔资本盈余资金，通过计提150万美元的额外折旧费用和87千美元的应急费用来消耗它。在这种情况下，我们看到大部分必要的折旧费用在多年间未被计入损益表，最终是通过减少普通股价值金额来处理的。这种错误的会计做法的一个附带后果是，使母公司（美国电力公司）通过分红分配的金额超过了真实收益和初始盈余的总和，严重损害了债券持有人和优先股票持有人的利益。⁴ **从盈余和储备中转移所揭示的不充分折旧。** *示例：*布鲁克林联合燃气公司案例可能是收入账户未能反映必要摊销扣除项的最令人印象深刻的例子。由于需要从盈余和应急储备中进行大量转移，收益的虚高程度被明显暴露出来。关于1929–1938年的十年期间，情况可以总结如下：**布鲁克林联合燃气公司**

<!--en-->
1. It reduced the stated value of its common stock by $1,587,000 and transferred this sum to capital surplus.
2. It immediately used up this capital surplus by charging against it $1,500,000 for additional depreciation and $87,000 for contingencies.
In this case we see a good part of the necessary depreciation charge excluded from the income statements over a period of years and finally allowed for by reducing the amount at which the common stock is valued. An incidental effect of this mischievous accounting was to permit the parent company (American Electric Power Corporation) to take out in dividends a sum exceeding the true earnings and the initial surplus combined, to the serious prejudice of the bondholders and the first preferred stockholders.⁴
**Inadequate Depreciation Revealed by Transfers from Surplus and Reserves.** *Example:* The case of Brooklyn Union Gas is perhaps the most impressive example of the failure of the income account to reflect the necessary deductions for amortization. The extent of the consequent overstatement of earnings has been glaringly revealed by the huge transfers required to be made from surplus and contingency reserves. The story may be summarized as follows, as regards the ten years 1929–1938:
