    ** In addition there were indicated appropriations from income of about $130,000 per annum for coke-oven relining and replacement reserves, which in 1938 were combined with the depreciation reserve in the balance sheet. If these are regarded as the equivalent of depreciation, then both the depreciation allowance and the “reserve consumed” would be increased by about $1,300,000 for the ten-year period. The foregoing figures are given in considerable detail, since they disclose a complicated but significant state of affairs bearing on the true earning power of the company. The reader will note the following points:*

1. 每股5.13美元的平均报告收益是在扣除与总收益和设备账户相比非常小的“退休储备”后计算得出的。
2. 用于退休的这些费用远远不足以覆盖该期间实际发生的退休支出。为支付这些费用，公司不得不耗尽大量应急储备（1928年底为13,800,000美元），并大量动用盈余。
3. 尽管公司向股东报告称，该期间总收益为每股51美元，支付股息40美元，并将每股11美元计入盈余，但其盈余和应急储备实际上减少了约每股26美元。因此，资产负债表显示的收益平均仅为每股1.36美元，而非收益表报告的每股5.13美元。⁶
4. 该期间实际资产退休金额平均为每年2,688,000美元，占总收益的11%，而收入中涉及的费用仅为729,000美元，占总收益的3.1%。1938年，公司表示根据纽约公共服务委员会的新要求，正在采用折旧政策，具体细节尚未确定，暂时每年拨款1,200,000美元用于此目的。从所述事实及之前讨论来看，即使这一金额比以往费用大得多，是否足够仍值得怀疑。⁷ **多种折旧政策。** 上述关于未在收益表中反映完整折旧费用的讨论引出了一个更广泛的话题，即公司制定折旧准备所依据的基础。所采用的方法多种多样，至少有七种需要描述，如下：

<!--en-->
1. The average reported earnings of $5.13 per share were computed after deduction of a “retirement reserve” of very small size in relation to both gross earnings and plant account.
2. These charges for retirements against income proved woefully inadequate to cover the actual retirements taking place during the period. To meet these charges the company had to exhaust a large contingency reserve⁵ ($13,800,000 at the end of 1928) and to draw heavily on surplus besides.
3. Although the company reported to stockholders that it had earned an aggregate of $51 per share during the period, paid dividends of $40 and carried $11 per share to surplus, its surplus and contingency reserve had really decreased about $26 per share. Hence the earnings as indicated by the balance sheet had averaged only $1.36 per share instead of $5.13 per share as reported in the income account.⁶
4. The actual retirements of property during this period averaged $2,688,000 per annum, or 11% of gross, as compared with the charge to income of $729,000, or 3.1% of gross. In the year 1938 the company stated that, in accordance with the new requirements of the Public Service Commission of New York, it was adopting a depreciation policy, that the details had not yet been worked out and that provisionally it was charging $1,200,000 per annum for the purpose. Judging from the facts stated and our previous discussion, there would seem to be grounds for doubt if even this amount, although much larger than former charges, is adequate.⁷
**A Variety of Depreciation Policies.** The foregoing discussion of failure to reflect full depreciation charges in the income account leads us into a broader topic, *viz.*, the basis used by a company in making its depreciation allowance. The methods employed reveal an extraordinary variety, no less than seven calling for description, as follows:

### A. *直接折旧法*。

<!--en-->
A. *Depreciation Proper.*

1. *直线法*。每一类可折旧资产在其预计使用寿命内通过相等的年度费用减至残值。这是计算折旧的标准方法，符合税收法规，所有公司在*所得税申报表*中普遍采用。然而，令人惊讶的是，很少有电力和燃气公司在其公开收益表中采用这种方法。*示例：*北美洲公司的子公司密苏里联合电力公司多年来一直采用直线法。但即便如此，公司报告의折旧准备也低于其所得税申报表中的金额（1937年为3,899,205美元，为5,549,109美元），差异显然是因为税务目的假设了较短的使用寿命，而年度报告则不然。如后文所述，州委员会和联邦电力委员会最近制定的规定，要求许多公司将其收益报告改为直线法或标准方法。
2. *沉没基金法*。这里考虑到用于折旧的金额会获得利息，直到资产被退休为止。这种方法的效果是，早期年份的扣除会稍小，后期年份则会稍大。加州公用事业公司通常根据与州铁路委员会的协议使用这种方法，允许利率为6%。（*示例：*圣地亚哥联合天然气电力公司。）即便如此，这些公司在税务申报中也采用直线法作为基础。
3. *总体方法。* 该方法对整个折旧资产账户应用单一的年度百分比率，而不是对不同类别资产使用不同的比率。其目的大概是得到实际折旧的简单近似值。 *示例：* Commonwealth Edison扣除可折旧资产平均账面价值的3%。 B. *退休储备方法。* 退休储备的特点在于，它并不旨在衡量由磨损或过时引起的特定时期的折旧。相反，它旨在提供管理层认为足以应对资产退休的资金，无论何时发生。在任何长时期内，适当的折旧和适当的退休津贴应该总和为同一数值。但退休储备政策显然允许每年有任意的变化，以反映良好的或糟糕的收益，或预期的短期退休需求。实际上，如将看到，大多数退休储备政策只是简单地低估了当前资产价值损失，从而高估了收益。计算退休储备的各种基础如下：
4. *毛额的百分比。* 如果所采用的百分比足够大，这种方法会倾向于近似于固定的折旧率。但通常情况并非如此。 *示例：* Duquesne Lighting Company扣除毛额的8%。另一方面，其1932–1934年的所得税扣除至少占毛额的30%。
5. *产品单位固定比率。* 这种方法明显与前述方法相似，也受到同样的批评。 *示例：* 1932年Brooklyn Union Gas Company表示，他们为退休储备预留了每千立方英尺3美分。（这一政策后来被更改。）Cincinnati Gas and Electric Company在1937年表示，他们按每千立方英尺售出的天然气5美分，以及每千千瓦小时售出的电力2.70美元的比例来准备退休储备。
6. *维护与折旧合并的毛额百分比。* 通过这种方法，用于维护的金额越大，用于折旧的储备就越少。⁸ *示例：* Third Avenue Railway在1912–1918年间，合并用于维护与折旧的扣除率为20%。Tidewater Power Company对不同服务采用不同的总比率，即：（1936年）：燃气与电力为15%；供水为12%；铁路为30%。
7. *自主扣除.* 大多数采用退休储备法的公司并未受任何数学公式约束，年度扣除金额主要依据管理层的判断。 *示例：* a. 逐年不同的金额：底特律爱迪生、费城电气、美国水厂与电气公司、美国电力照明公司。b. 年度固定金额不变：坦帕电气从1933年到1939年每年收取430,000美元。c. 当年实际退休人员对应的补贴：西联电报公司1932–1936年的情况。1936年其收入账户中的折旧费用为5,631,000美元，而纳税申报表中却列有11,190,000美元。差额将占当年报告的共同股收益7,199,000美元中的大部分。过去折旧补贴不足的情况体现在1937年从盈余中转移了30,000,000美元到折旧储备中。**折旧的双重会计政策。** 我们已经说明，无论年度报告中采用何种方法，实际上所有公司都在计算所得税时采用直线法折旧。⁹因此，投资者面临双重情况和紧迫问题。在许多情况下，了解哪种折旧方法正确至关重要，因为公司年度报表中看似足够的债券利息覆盖和共同股收益，如果接受所得税数据，可能会证明完全不足。示例：直到1933年法案下发布的首批招股说明书之一——即描述美国水厂与电气公司可转换5s股票（到期时间为1944年）的说明书——才让投资者了解到这种差异的存在。该文件显示，1932年“纳税申报表折旧”为7,023,000美元，而“收入账户折旧”仅为2,747,000美元。当时华尔街倾向于淡化这些差异的重要性，认为折旧是高度技术性和有争议的问题，同样有理由接受收入账户或纳税申报表折旧方法。 *普遍接受所得税折旧基础的原因。* 我们一直认为这种漠视是极其不合理的。自1934年以来的发展进一步支持我们的观点，我们现在可以提出至少五个普遍接受所得税数据而非收入账户折旧基础的主要理由。如下：
1. 直线法遵循明确的逻辑会计理论。如果导致过度扣除，财政部不会接受。各种退休储备法要么完全任意，要么在技术上不合理。
2. “退休储备”概念的整体不足已通过许多情况下需要从盈余中大量转移资金以加强退休账户的情况得到证明。 *示例：* 参见本章前面的布鲁克林联合燃气案例。
3. 自1934年以来，退休补贴的绝对值和百分比都几乎普遍增加。这可以被视为对过去不足的虚拟承认。这些增加的程度由下表所示，该表提供了1930年和1938年一些公用事业公司关于折旧或退休补贴以及维护费用的信息。需要注意的是，在前一年，使用退休方法的公司通常比使用折旧方法的公司支付更低的费用。此外，之前使用退休方法的许多公司后来已转向折旧方法。而且，1938年使用退休方法的许多公司也在联邦电力委员会和各种州委员会的推动下，即将转向折旧方法。
4. 目前，多个州委员会和联邦电力委员会已要求其管辖范围内的公司在其所有账目中采用常规折旧方法。*示例：*宾夕法尼亚州、密歇根州和纽约州。¹⁰一些重要公司将不得不在其年度报表中改用所得税折旧方法。例如，纽约康索利德爱迪生公司在1938年全年向股东提交的报告中，将退休储备费用记为18,829,000美元，而在所得税申报表中则按直线法计提折旧约26,800,000美元。在截至1939年9月30日的12个月内，该公司在向股东提交的中期报告中，折旧费用为24,217,000美元，而1938年同期报告中的折旧费用仅为17,737,000美元。后两个时期的营业总收入分别为248,666,000美元和239,413,000美元。
5. 如果存在任何真实的替代方案，固定价值证券的投资者必须始终采用更严格的稳健性测试标准。*示例：*我们第五个理由的实际意义可以通过两个例子说明——一个是在当前情况下，另一个来自1930年的证券市场。从上述数据很难理解，投资者如何能证明购买宾夕法尼亚电力照明公司5优先股是合理的，其收益率仅为5.26%。根据该公司自己的报告，固定费用与优先股息之间的差额完全不足；按所得税折旧方法计算，这一差额减少了超过一半；按照南加州爱迪生公司采用的百分比折旧方法，差额几乎消失。如果我们查看1930年类似的情况，如下表底部所示，就会明白投资者认识到这些数据含义的重要性。在这种情况下，有三个因素不利于美国电力照明优先股的投资价值：(1) 所声称的覆盖程度完全不足以确保实际安全。(2) 采用的折旧率过低。如果调整至太平洋照明公司的基准，差额将大幅减少。(3) 这些要求被临时低估了约2,000,000美元，因为当时大量发行的优先股仅有权获得3美元的股息，到1933年这一比例逐渐上升为5美元。1938年6美元优先股的市场价格下跌，是因为从1933年开始股息减少，而净收益降低又消耗了1929年存在的少量优先要求差额。1933年后报告的收益恢复，部分原因是由于需要逐步提高折旧准备金，使其符合现实情况。

<!--en-->
1. *Straight-Line Method.* Each class of depreciable property is written down to salvage value by equal annual charges during the period of its estimated life. This is the standard method of calculating depreciation, permitted by the revenue acts and generally followed by all companies in *their income tax returns*. Surprisingly few electric and gas companies, however, have employed this method in their published income accounts.
*Example:* Union Electric Company of Missouri, a subsidiary of North American Company, has used the straight-line method for a number of years. But even here the company's reported allowance is less than that claimed on its income tax return ($3,899,205 vs. $5,549,109 in 1937) the difference being due apparently to assuming a shorter life for tax purposes than for annual report purposes.
As will be pointed out later, recent regulations adopted by state commissions and by the Federal Power Commission are now necessitating a change-over by many companies to the straight-line or standard method in their reported earnings.
2. *Sinking-Fund Method.* Allowance is here made for the fact that amounts set aside for depreciation will earn interest until the property is retired. The effect of this method is to make the deductions somewhat smaller in the earlier years and correspondingly higher in the later years. It is generally used by California utility corporations under agreements with the Railroad Commission of the state, the rate of interest allowed being 6%. (*Examples:* Pacific Gas and Electric, San Diego Consolidated Gas and Electric.) Even here the companies take the straight-line basis in their tax returns.
3. *The Over-All Method.* This applies a single annual percentage to the entire depreciable property account, instead of varying rates to different classes of assets. The object, presumably, is to arrive at a simple approximation of the actual depreciation.
*Example:* Commonwealth Edison deducts 3% of the average book value of depreciable property.
B. *Retirement Reserve Methods.* The distinguishing feature of a retirement reserve is that it does not seek to measure the depreciation during a given period caused by wear and tear or obsolescence. Instead it is supposed to provide funds that, in the opinion of the management, will be adequate to take care of retirements of property when and as they occur. Over any long period of time, proper depreciation and proper retirement allowances should total the same amount. But a retirement reserve policy apparently permits arbitrary annual variations, to reflect good or bad earnings or the expected near term needfor actual retirements. In reality, as will be seen, the majority of retirement reserve policies operate simply to understate the current loss of property value and thus to overstate the earnings. Various bases of calculating retirement reserves are as follows:
4. *Percentage of Gross.* This method would tend to approximate a regular depreciation rate if the percentage taken were adequate. Generally this is not the case.
*Example:* Duquesne Lighting Company deducts 8% of gross. On the other hand, its income tax deduction for 1932–1934 equaled no less than 30% of gross.
5. *Fixed Rate per Unit of Product.* This method clearly resembles the preceding and is subject to the same criticism.
*Examples:* In 1932 Brooklyn Union Gas Company stated that it was reserving 3 cents per thousand cubic feet for retirements. (This policy has since been changed.) Cincinnati Gas and Electric Company stated in 1937 that it was making provision for retirement reserve at the rate of 5 cents per thousand cubic feet of gas sold and $2.70 per thousand kilowatt-hours of electricity sold.
6. *Over-All Percentage of Gross for Maintenance and Depreciation Combined.* By this method the larger the amount spent for maintenance the less is reserved for depreciation.⁸
*Examples:* Third Avenue Railway used a 20% deduction for maintenance and depreciation combined for the years 1912–1918. Tidewater Power Company uses varying total rates for different services, *viz.* (in 1936): Gas and Electric, 15%; Water, 12%; Railway, 30%.
7. *Discretionary Deductions.* The majority of companies following the retirement reserve method have been bound by no mathematical formula but have based the annual deduction largely on the judgment of the management.
*Examples: a.* Amounts varying year by year: Detroit Edison, Philadelphia Electric, American Water Works and Electric, American Power and Light.
b. Unchanged annual round amount: Tampa Electric charged $430,000 per annum from 1933 through 1939.
c. Allowance made equal to actual retirements during year: Western Union Telegraph Company in 1932–1936. The depreciation charge of $5,631,000 in its income account for 1936 compares with a provision of $11,190,000 in the tax return. The difference would account for most of the $7,199,000 reported as earned for the common stock that year. The inadequacy of past allowances for depreciation was shown by the transfer in 1937 of $30,000,000 from surplus to depreciation reserve.
**Double Accounting Policies on Depreciation.** We have already stated that, regardless of what method is followed in the annual reports, practically every company follows the straight-line basis of depreciation in computing its income tax.⁹ The investor is thus confronted with a dual situation and a pressing problem. In many cases it is of vital importance to know which basis of depreciation is correct, since bond-interest coverage and common-stock earnings which may appear adequate as reported in the company's annual statements would turn out to be entirely insufficient if the income tax figures are accepted.
Example: The existence of this disparity was unknown to investors generally until brought out into the open in one of the first prospectuses published under the terms of the 1933 act, *viz.*, that describing the American Water Works and Electric Company Convertible 5s, due 1944. This document revealed that in 1932 “tax-return amortization” had been taken at $7,023,000, as against “income-account amortization” of only $2,747,000. At that time there was a tendency in Wall Street to minimize the significance of these divergences, on the ground that depreciation was a highly technical and controversial matter and there was just as much reason to accept the income-account basis as the tax-return basis.
*Reasons for Accepting, in General, the Income Tax Base.* We have always been convinced that this heedlessness was dangerously unsound. Developments since 1934 have strongly buttressed our opinion, so that we now can advance no lessthan five major reasons for accepting, in general, the income tax figure rather than the income-account basis of depreciation. These are:
1. The straight-line basis follows a definite and logical accounting theory. If it resulted in an excessive deduction the Treasury Department would not accept it. The various retirement-reserve bases are either entirely arbitrary or technically unsound.
2. The inadequacy of the “retirement reserve” idea in general has been shown by the necessity in many cases of making large transfers from surplus to bolster the retirement account. *Example:* See Brooklyn Union Gas exhibit earlier in this chapter.
3. Since 1934 there has been an almost universal increase in the retirement allowances—both absolutely and percentagewise. This may be considered a virtual confession of past inadequacy. The extent of these increases is indicated by our table that follows, which supplies information concerning depreciation or retirement allowances, as well as maintenance charges, covering the years 1930 and 1938 for a number of utility companies. It is to be noted that in the earlier year the companies using the retirement basis generally made lower charges than those using the depreciation basis. Observe, also, that a number of the companies previously using the retirement method have since switched to a depreciation basis. Moreover, a considerable number of the companies that used the retirement basis in 1938 were on the verge of a transfer to a depreciation basis under the impetus of requirements of the Federal Power Commission and of various state commissions.
4. A number of state commissions and the Federal Power Commission have now ordered companies within their jurisdictions to follow a regular depreciation basis in all their accounts.
*Examples:* Pennsylvania, Michigan and New York.¹⁰ Some important companies are perforce switching over to the income tax basis in their annual statements. For example, Consolidated Edison Company of New York for the calendaryear 1938 charged $18,829,000 for retirement reserve in its report to shareholders and charged about $26,800,000 for depreciation on a straight-line basis in its income tax return. For the 12 months ending September 30, 1939, the company charged $24,217,000 for depreciation in its interim report to shareholders as against a charge of only $17,737,000 in its report for the corresponding period ending September 30, 1938. Gross operating revenues for the latter two periods were $248,666,000 and $239,413,000, respectively.
5. Where any real alternative exists, the investor in fixed-value securities must invariably apply the more stringent test of soundness.
*Examples:* The practical significance of our fifth reason is shown by two examples—one current as this is written, the other taken from the securities market of 1930.
It is difficult to understand from the foregoing figures how the investor could justify to himself the purchase of Pennsylvania Power and Light $5 Preferred at a price to yield only 5.26%. On the basis of the company's own report the margin above fixed charges and preferred dividends was entirely inadequate; on the income tax basis for depreciation this is cut by more than half; on the basis of the percentage of gross applied by Southern California Edison, the margin practically disappears.
If we examine a very similar situation existing in 1930, as shown in the bottom of the following table, we shall see how important it was for the investor to recognize the implication of the figures.
In this case we had three factors that militated against the investment merit of American Power and Light Preferred Stock: (1) The coverage as stated was entirely insufficient for real safety. (2) The depreciation rate taken was far too low. An adjustment to the Pacific Lighting basis would have sharply reduced the margin above preferred requirements. (3) These requirements were temporarily understated by about $2,000,000, because a large preferred issue was then entitled to only $3 in dividends, the rate advancing gradually to $5 in 1933.
The decline in the market price of the $6 preferred in 1938 was due to reductions in the dividend beginning in 1933, brought about in turn by lower net earnings which absorbed the small margin above preferred requirements existing in 1929. Recovery in reported earnings after 1933 was held back, in part, by the necessity of stepping up the depreciation allowance gradually to bring it in line with realities.

*何时应拒绝或质疑所得税基础。*读者可能会注意到，我们建议“通常”接受所得税基础。这一建议是有条件的，因为有时可能有理由接受年报数据，甚至寻求第三种折旧基础。

<!--en-->
*Instances When Income Tax Basis Should Be Rejected or Questioned.* The reader may note that we have counseled acceptance of the income tax basis “in general.” The suggestion is qualified because there may at times be reasons either to accept the annual report figures or even to seek a third basis of amortization.

用于上一个例子的太平洋照明案例，说明了我们的第一个例外。1929年的数据来自年报，基于加州委员会与加州公用事业公司共同采用的“资金减少”折旧方法。看起来，公司采取的折旧扣除额平均低于税务申报中的直线法扣除额。然而，在这种情况下，公司报告的数据很可能被接受，首先是因为它们源自可接受的会计方法，其次是因为这些金额相对于资产账户和毛额收入来看相当宽松。同样的推理适用于所有加州公用事业公司。

<!--en-->
The Pacific Lighting case, used for comparison in the last example, illustrates our first exception. The figures for 1929were taken from the annual report and are based on the “sinking-fund” depreciation method generally followed by agreement between the California Commission and California utility companies. It appears that the deductions for depreciation taken by the company average lower than the straight-line deduction taken on the tax returns. Nevertheless, in this case the company’s reported figures might well be accepted, first, because they result from applying an admissible accounting method and, second, because the amounts appear to be liberal in relation both to the property account and to the gross earnings. The same reasoning would apply to all the California utilities.

还有另一大组公司，它们采取的折旧扣除额看似宽松，但仍然远低于所得税扣除额。

<!--en-->
There is another large group of companies that have taken depreciation allowances that appear liberal in themselves but are still substantially less than the income tax deductions.

*示例：*1938年底特律爱迪生公司在向股东报告中将毛额计提了13.5%的折旧，而当年税务申报中仅计提了18.2%的毛额。1937年北美公司的相应数据为12.8%和14.8%。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* In 1938 Detroit Edison charged 13.5% of gross on its report to shareholders, vs. 18.2% of gross on its tax return for that year. Corresponding figures for North American Company for 1937 were 12.8 and 14.8%, respectively.

在这种情况下，投资者——尤其是普通股买家——可能认为所得税基础过于严格。由于缺乏对资产本身的详细了解，以及与我们相比对公共事业工程细节的更深入了解，很难对此作出判断。我们倾向于提出折中建议：当税务数字超过毛额的$12\frac{1}{2}\%$时，暂时使用后者作为分析依据。¹¹可以指出，几年前似乎10%到12%的毛额构成相对宽松的扣除。

<!--en-->
In these instances the investor—and particularly the common-stock buyer—may argue that the income tax basis is unduly severe. It is difficult to pronounce judgment on this point in the absence of detailed knowledge of the properties themselves and a better familiarity with public utility engineering details than we possess. We are inclined to advance the compromise suggestion that when the tax figure exceeds, say, $12\frac{1}{2}\%$ of gross, the latter rate be used provisionally for purposes of analysis.¹¹ It may be pointed out that several years ago it appeared that 10 to 12% of gross constituted a comparatively liberal deduction.

**不同折旧政策的实际影响。**读者可能认为这种公用事业折旧政策讨论非常技术化且无趣，但实际上，它对选择公共事业股票及其市场行为具有极其重要的实际意义。1934年前计提不足折旧的公司通常在股市中被高估，因为投资者同样没有重视这一点。严谨的分析师会发现许多机会，建议从不太保守的公司转向更保守的公司。在随后几年中，前一组公司大幅提高了折旧比例，其报告收益相应下降，市场价格也随之下降。以下例子将说明这一发展：

<!--en-->
**Practical Effect of Varying Depreciation Policies.** The reader may consider this discussion of utility depreciation policies to be highly technical and uninteresting, but the fact remains that it has a bearing of the greatest practical importance on the selection of public-utility stocks and on their market behavior. The companies that charged inadequate depreciation prior to 1934 were generally overvalued in the stock market, because investors gave equally inadequateattention to this point. A careful analyst would have found many occasions to suggest transfers from less conservative to more conservative companies. Since in the following years there has been a tendency for the former group to step up their charges substantially, their reported earnings have been correspondingly held down, and their market prices also. The following example will illustrate this development:

CHAPTER 46

#### 股票期权权证

<!--en-->
*Stock-Option Warrants*

在过去二十年里，股票期权权证的应用经历了显著发展。最初，它们被设计为与相关债券和优先股相关的参与性特权。在这种形式下，它们通常仅被视为高级证券的一个特征，类似于转换权，而权证本身对公司资本结构几乎没有重要意义。后来，人们想到将股票期权权证与其他证券分开，作为对承销商、发起人和高管们的补偿。从这一点出发，不可避免的下一步发展是像普通股票一样，通过销售或交换方式向公众发行独立的期权权证。因此，它们作为独立的“证券”形式、许多公司的财务结构中的重要组成部分，以及一种流行且重要的投机工具，获得了完整的地位。

<!--en-->
DURING THE LAST TWO DECADES the use of stock-option warrants has passed through an extraordinary development. They were devised originally as a form of participating privilege for bonds and preferred stocks to which they were attached. In this form they were commonly regarded only as a feature of the senior security, similar to a conversion right, and the warrants themselves had little significance in relation to the company's capitalization structure. Later the idea was hit upon of creating stock-option warrants separately from other securities and delivering them as compensation to underwriters, promoters and executives. From this point the inevitable next development was the issuance, through sale or exchange, of separate option warrants to the general public in the same manner as common stocks. They thus attained full stature as an independent form of "security," as an important part of the financial set-up of many corporations and as a popular and prominent medium of speculative activity.

在前一章中，我们讨论了期权权证作为高级证券辅助工具的技术方面。在本章中，我们将讨论期权权证作为独立金融工具的更重要作用。我们的论述分为三个部分：(1)描述，(2)作为投机工具的权证技术特性，(3)作为财务结构一部分的重要性。

<!--en-->
In a previous chapter we considered the technical aspects of option warrants as an adjunct of senior securities. In this chapter we shall discuss the more important role of option warrants as a separate financial instrument. Our treatment falls into three sections: (1) description, (2) technical characteristics of warrants as a vehicle of speculation, (3) their significance as a part of the financial structure.

## 描述性总结

<!--en-->
*DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY*

（可分离的）期权权证是一种可转让的购买股票的权利，通常有效期较长。

<!--en-->
A (detachable) option warrant is a transferable right to buy stock, originally running for a considerable period of time.

（与债券发行相关的权证有时被称为“债券权利”。另一种称呼是“股票购买权证”。）其条款包括：(1)股票类型，(2)数量，(3)价格，(4)支付方式，(5)特权的持续时间，以及(6)反稀释条款。（最后一项已在第25章中描述。）

<!--en-->
(Warrants attached to a debenture bond issue are sometimes called “Debenture Rights.” A third name for the same thing is “Stock-purchase Warrant.”) Its terms include: (1) the kind of stock, (2) the amount, (3) the price, (4) the method of payment, (5) the duration of the privilege, and (6) antidilution provisions. (The last were described in Chap. 25.)

**被特权覆盖的股票类型。**几乎所有期权权证都要求发行公司的普通股。在少数情况下，它们适用于优先股（例如，American Locker Company, Inc.），或其他公司的股票（例如，Central States Electric Corporation Preferred的权证要求北美洲公司股票，Solvay American Investment Corporation优先股的权证要求Allied Chemical and Dye Corporation股票）。权证没有收取利息、股息或本金支付的权利，也没有投票权。

<!--en-->
**Kind of Stock Covered by the Privilege.** Nearly all option warrants call for common stock of the issuing company. In rare instances they apply to preferred stock (e.g., American Locker Company, Inc.), or to stock of some other concern (e.g., warrants attached to Central States Electric Corporation Preferred called for North American Company stock and warrants attached to Solvay American Investment Corporation preferred stock called for Allied Chemical and Dye Corporation stock). Warrants have no right to receive interest, dividends or payments on account of principal, nor have they the right to cast any vote.

**与认购“权利”的相似性。** 期权权证与公司向其股东在出售额外股票时发放的“认购权利”有一些相似之处。然而，权证和权利之间存在两个重要差异：权证有效期很长，股票购买价格几乎总是高于发行时的报价。此外，价格通常根据权证的条款进行调整。认购权利有效期较短，需支付固定价格，通常等于授权时的市场价。因此，认购权利旨在确保其被行使以及公司能迅速获得资金。期权权证通常与公司的财务需求无关，也不预期会很快被行使。换句话说（指发行时的常见情况），除非市场在到期前大幅下跌，否则认购权利会被行使；除非近期或未来市场价大幅上涨，否则期权权证也不会被行使。¹ 认购权利通常有效期约为60天；期权权证的原始期限很少少于一年，许多是永久性的。

<!--en-->
**Resemblance to Subscription “Rights.”** Option warrants bear some resemblance to the “subscription rights” that are issued by corporations to their stockholders in connection with the sale of additional stock. There are two significant differences, however, between warrants and rights. Warrants run for a long period, and the stock-purchase price is almost always set higher than the quotation at the time of their issuance. Moreover, the price is frequently varied in accordance with the terms of the warrant. Subscription rights run for a short time and call for a fixed price, usually under the market at the time of their authorization. Subscription rights are devised, therefore, with the intent of assuring their exercise and the prompt receipt of funds by the company. Option warrants generally have no relation to the financial needs of the company, and they are not expected to be exercised in short order. Stated in a different way (and referring to the usual situation at the time of issuance) a subscription right will be exercised unless the market declines substantially before they expire; option warrants will not be exercised unless the market price advances substantially in the near or distant future.¹ Subscription rights generally run for about sixty days; the original duration of option warrants israrely, if ever, less than a year, and many of them are perpetual.

**支付方式。** 大多数期权权证要求以现金支付认购价格。原本附属于债券或优先股的部分，可能允许以现金支付，或提供按面值接受的优先证券进行支付。这种替代方式可能具有相当大的实际意义。

<!--en-->
**Method of Payment.** Most option warrants require payment of the subscription price in cash. Those originally attached to bonds or preferred shares may permit payment either in cash or by tender of the senior security which is accepted at its face value. This alternative may be of considerable practical importance.

*示例：* 电力与照明权证是一种以每股25美元的股价永久行使普通股的权证。支付可以是现金，也可以是以每股100美元的二级优先股进行支付。1939年11月，普通股售价为8美元，二级优先股售价为17美元。由于优先证券的价格非常低，尽管普通股售价比期权价格低17个点，权证仍具有“可行使价值”。计算方式如下：

<!--en-->
*Example:* Electric Power and Light Warrants are a perpetual call on common stock at $25 per share. Payment may be made either in cash or by tendering second preferred stock at $100 per share. In November 1939 the common stock sold at 8, and the second preferred at 17. Because of the very low price of the senior issue, the warrants had an “exercisable value,” even though the common was selling 17 points below the option price. The calculation is as follows:

1个权证加上1/4份二级优先股 = 1股普通股

<!--en-->
One warrant plus 1/4 share of second preferred = 1 share of common

$$
\text{Value of option warrant} = 8 - \frac{1}{4}(17) = 3\frac{3}{4}
$$

**权证的交易基础。** 期权权证在市场上的买卖方式与普通股相同。截至1939年底，只有两款权证在纽约证券交易所单独上市，²但许多在纽约Curb交易所及其他交易所活跃交易。这些工具的交易基础有些特殊，有时会导致严重错误。按照标准规则，“1个权证”是指购买1股股票的权利，而不是原本附属于1股股票的权利。

<!--en-->
**Basis of Trading in Warrants.** Option warrants are bought and sold in the market in the same way as common stocks. Up to the end of 1939 only two issues of warrants had been separately listed on the New York Stock Exchange,² but many were actively dealt in on the New York Curb Exchange and other exchanges. The basis of trading in these instruments is somewhat eccentric, and at times conducive to serious error. Under the standard rule, “one warrant” means the right to buy one share of stock, and not the right originally attached to one share of stock.

*示例：* Walgreen（药品）公司的优先股以带有权证的方式出售，持有人每持有1股优先股，有权购买2股普通股。按照常规交易规则，“1个Walgreen权证”意味着购买1股普通股的权利，即据说每1股优先股包含“2个权证”。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Walgreen (Drug) Company preferred stock was sold with warrants entitling the holder to buy two shares of common for each preferred share. Under the regular rule of trading, “one Walgreen warrant” meant the right to buy one share of common, *i.e.*, each share of preferred was said to carry “two warrants.”

同样，Consolidated Cigar Corporation的6 1/2%优先股也附带了每个股份对应的1个权证，要求购买1/2股普通股。这些权证也是基于“1个权证”意味着购买1股普通股的基础进行交易的；即据说每1股$6\frac{1}{2}\%$优先股包含“半个权证”。但这一标准规则存在许多例外情况。

<!--en-->
Similarly, Consolidated Cigar Corporation 6 1/2% Preferred Stock was issued with a warrant attached to each share calling for the purchase of one-half share of common. These warrantswere also traded in on the basis that one warrant was the right to buy one share of common; *i.e.*, each share of $6\frac{1}{2}\%$ preferred was said to carry “half a warrant.” But the exceptions to this standard rule are numerous.

*示例：* Commercial Investment Trust Corporation$6\frac{1}{2}\%$优先股也附带权证，要求每1股优先股购买1/2股普通股（与Consolidated Cigar Preferred的情况相同）。但纽约证券交易所的交易单位是原本附属于1股优先股的权证，即要求购买半股普通股。Niagara Hudson Power Corporation B Warrants、Loew's, Inc. Preferred Warrants、Safeway Stores, Inc. "Old Series" Warrants等交易规则也有类似差异。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Commercial Investment Trust Corporation $6\frac{1}{2}\%$ Preferred carried warrants to buy one-half share of common for each share of preferred (the same ratio as in the case of Consolidated Cigar Preferred). But the unit of trading on the New York Stock Exchange was the warrant originally attached to one share of preferred, *i.e.*, it called for half a share of common. Similar departures were made in the rules of trading for Niagara Hudson Power Corporation B Warrants; Loew's, Inc., Preferred Warrants; Safeway Stores, Inc., “Old Series” Warrants, etc.

当权证要求的股份数量发生变化时，常规做法是将“1个旧权证”继续视为“1个权证”进行交易。

<!--en-->
When a change is made in the number of shares called for by the warrant, the customary procedure is to continue to trade in “one old warrant” as “one warrant.”

*示例：* “One Loew's Bond warrant”最初要求以55美元购买1股普通股。它代表与200美元的Loew's 6%债券相关的权证，到期日为1941年。1928年支付25%的股票股息时，反稀释条款规定，每认购一份权证，还需免费提供四分之一股股票。“One Loew's Bond warrant”在物理上保持不变，此后代表以55美元购买$1\frac{1}{4}$股的权利。同样，在Commercial Investment Trust权证的案例中，普通股进行了$2\frac{1}{2}$的分割，变为1股新股份。此后，1份权证代表购买$1\frac{1}{4}$股新股份的权利，而不是$\frac{1}{2}$股旧股份。

<!--en-->
*Example:* “One Loew's Bond warrant” originally called for one share of common at $55. It represented the warrant attached to $200 of Loew's 6% Debentures, due 1941. When a 25% stock dividend was paid in 1928, the antidilution provision required that an additional quarter share be given free with each share subscribed for under the warrant. “One Loew's Bond warrant” remained physically unchanged and thereafter represented the right to purchase $1\frac{1}{4}$ shares for $55. Similarly in the case of Commercial Investment Trust warrants when the common stock was split $2\frac{1}{2}$ for 1. One warrant thereafter represented the right to buy $1\frac{1}{4}$ new shares instead of $\frac{1}{2}$ an old share.

但有时也会采用相反的做法。

<!--en-->
But the opposite practice is sometimes followed.

*示例：* Niagara Hudson Power A权证。这些要求以35美元购买1股普通股。该公司于1932年进行重组，发行了1股新股份以替代3股旧股份。因此，以前称为“1份权证”的现在要求以$\frac{1}{3}$股新股份购买，价格为$105$美元/股。纽约Curb交易所随后将“1份A权证”重新定义为购买1股*新*股份的权利。因此，3份旧权证变成了1份新权证。

<!--en-->
*Example:* Niagara Hudson Power A warrants. These called for one share of common at $35. The company recapitalized in 1932 and issued 1 new share for 3 old. Hence what was formerly “one warrant” now called for $\frac{1}{3}$ of a new share for $35, *i.e.*, at $105$ per share. The New York Curb Exchange thereupon redefined “one A warrant” as representing the rightto buy one *new* share. Hence three old warrants became one new warrant.

这些技术细节在此列出，因为标准描述性教科书中无法找到。那些买卖特定期权权证的人被提醒要仔细了解交易依据。³

<!--en-->
These technical details are given here because they are not available in standard descriptive textbooks. Those buying or selling a particular option warrant are cautioned to make careful inquiry into the basis of trading therein.³

### 为不同目的发行的权证示例。A.

<!--en-->
*Examples of Warrants Issued for Various Purposes. A.*

*与高级证券关联。* 最早的例子可能是1911年发行的American Power and Light票据。最著名的是American and Foreign Power公司发行的2.7亿美元Second Preferred股票，附带不少于7,100,000股普通股的权证。

<!--en-->
*Attached to Senior Securities.* Perhaps the earliest instance is the issue of American Power and Light notes in 1911. By far the most prominent is the sale by American and Foreign Power Company of $270,000,000 of Second Preferred stock carrying warrants for no less than 7,100,000 shares of common.

*B. 作为对承销商的补偿。* 第一个重要案例似乎是1926年Barnsdall Corporation 6%债券发行，金额为25,000,000美元。这里，银行家们作为补偿，获得了500,000股普通股的权证。在后续的高价时，这些权证价值约为13,000,000美元。National Fund, Inc.这家开放式投资信托公司在1936年向赞助方发行权证，以替代常规加载费。许多小型公司的发行中，除了给银行家的现金补偿外，还包含大量权证。例如：Aeronautical Corporation of America（1939年）；Triumph Explosives, Inc.（1939年）；Howard Aircraft Corporation（1939年）。

<!--en-->
*B. As Compensation to Underwriters.* The first important case seems to have been the $25,000,000 Barnsdall Corporation 6% bond issue of 1926. Here the bankers received, as part of their compensation, warrants for 500,000 shares of common. At the subsequent high price these warrants would have been worth $13,000,000. National Fund, Inc., an openend investment trust, issued warrants to the sponsors in 1936 in lieu of the customary loading charge. Many flotations of smaller companies now include large amounts of warrants in addition to cash compensation for bankers. Examples: Aeronautical Corporation of America (1939); Triumph Explosives, Inc. (1939); Howard Aircraft Corporation (1939).

*C. 作为对推动者和管理层的补偿。* 一个显著的例子是1929年1月成立的Petroleum Corporation of America。公众以每股34美元的价格获得了3,250,000股股票。推动者和管理层获得了五年期权证，可以以34美元购买1,625,000股股票。

<!--en-->
*C. As Compensation to Promoters and Management.* A striking case was the formation of Petroleum Corporation of America in January 1929. The public was offered 3,250,000 shares of stock at $34 per share. Five-year warrants to buy 1,625,000 shares at 34 were issued to the promoters and management.

*D. 在合并或重组计划中发行，以换取其他证券。* Commonwealth and Southern Corporation发行了约17,500,000份权证，以及34,000,000股普通股和1,500,000股优先股，主要是以换取六家组成公司的证券。有趣的是，它发行了*普通股*和权证，以换取Penn-Ohio Edison Company和Southeastern Power and Light Company的期权权证。

<!--en-->
*D. Issued in a Merger or Reorganization Plan, in Exchange for Other Securities.* Commonwealth and Southern Corporation issued about 17,500,000 warrants, together with 34,000,000 shares of common and 1,500,000 shares of preferred, mainly in exchange for securities of six constituent companies. It is interesting to note that it issued *common stock*and warrants in exchange for Penn-Ohio Edison Company and Southeastern Power and Light Company option warrants.

在1937年Baldwin Locomotive Works的重组中，旧的优先股和普通股都被交换为新的普通股和权证。1936年Colorado Fuel and Iron的重组中，只有旧优先股和普通股获得了权证。1938年为持有债券的保险公司提出的Erie Railroad重组计划很独特，它给予老股东权证，让他们从旧债权人处购买新普通股，而不是从公司本身购买。

<!--en-->
In the 1937 reorganization of Baldwin Locomotive Works the old preferred and common were both exchanged for new common and warrants. In the Colorado Fuel and Iron reorganization of 1936 only warrants were given for the old preferred and common. The reorganization plan for Erie Railroad, presented in 1938 in behalf of insurance companies holding bonds, was unique in that it gave old stockholders warrants to buy new common from the old creditors instead of from the company.

*E. 与原始普通股发行关联。* Public Utility Holding Corporation of America出售了2,500,000股普通股，附带权证，可以购买相同数量的额外普通股。此外，组织利益方购买了500,000股A类股票（具有投票控制权）以及权证，可以购买1,000,000股A类或普通股。

<!--en-->
*E. Attached to an Original Issue of Common Stock.* Public Utility Holding Corporation of America sold 2,500,000 shares of common stock, carrying warrants to buy an equal number of shares of additional common. In addition, the organizing interests purchased 500,000 shares of Class A stock (with voting control) together with warrants to buy 1,000,000 shares of either Class *A* or common stock.

*F. 单独出售以获取现金。* 1929年Fourth National Investors Corporation将其750,000份期权权证以3,000,000美元出售给母公司。1936年Phillips Packing Company将权证出售给银行家以获取现金。

<!--en-->
*F. Sold Separately for Cash.* In 1929 Fourth National Investors Corporation sold to its parent company 750,000 option warrants for $3,000,000. In 1936 Phillips Packing Company sold warrants to bankers for cash.

#### 权证作为投机工具

<!--en-->
*WARRANTS AS A VEHICLE OF SPECULATION*

从广义上讲，期权权证具有与低价普通股相同的普遍特征，相关理论已在第41章中讨论。从名称和形式上看，期权权证与低价股票类似——本质上都是对企业未来发展的长期预期。⁴事实上，权证与普通股之间的关系，大致类似于同一公司的普通股与投机性高级证券之间的关系。

<!--en-->
In a broad sense, option warrants possess the same general characteristics as low-priced common stocks, the theory of which was discussed in Chap. 41. Warrants are in name and in form, as low-priced stocks frequently are in essence, a long-term call upon the future of a business.⁴ It is true also that the relationship between a warrant and its common stock is roughly similar to that between a common stock and a speculative senior security of the same company.

**定性因素。**与其他所有投机性承诺一样，特定权证的吸引力取决于两个完全不同的因素：定性因素，即企业的性质，尤其是其有望实现巨大发展的可能性；定量因素，即权证提供的条款，包括其价格和所对应的普通股价格。证券分析无法准确揭示未来最有可能取得进展的企业。因此，关于选择用于投机的权证时的定性因素，我们很难给出明确结论。通常来说，权证只有通过收益增加才能获得实际价值，因此应关注变化前景而非稳定性。例如，1928–1929年，公用事业权证非常流行，并非因为公用事业企业本身稳定性更高，而是因为市场认为其收益将持续无限扩展。

<!--en-->
**The Qualitative Element.** As with all other speculative commitments, the attractiveness of a given warrant depends upon two entirely dissimilar factors: the qualitative element, being the nature of the enterprise, in relation particularly to its supposed chance of great improvement; and the quantitativeelement, being the terms on which the warrant is offered, including its price and the price of the common stock it calls for. Security analysis cannot be counted upon to reveal those businesses which are most likely to forge ahead in the years to come. There is not much we can say, therefore, about the qualitative element in selecting warrants for speculation. Since ordinarily a warrant can attain tangible value only through an increase in earnings, emphasis must be laid upon the prospects of change rather than upon stability. Public-utility warrants, for example, became extremely popular in 1928–1929 not because of the superior stability of utility enterprises but because the market was convinced that their earnings would continue to expand indefinitely.

就价格大幅上涨的算术概率而言，我们已经表明，这种情况最可能出现在投机性资本化的普通股上（例如第40章中讨论的A. E. Staley Company和American Water Works and Electric，见第六版教材）。因此，购买这类普通股的权证也可以说具有特殊的投机优势。但这本质上是定量而非定性问题。我们认为，很少能确定某条业务领域的长期前景是否明显优于平均水平，从而使与该领域相关的权证比其他权证更有吸引力。但如果个人投机者对这一方面有明确的看法和偏好，遵循这些看法是完全合理的。

<!--en-->
As far as the arithmetical chance of a large price advance is concerned, we have already shown that this is most likely to be found in the common stock of speculatively capitalized enterprises (e.g., A. E. Staley Company and American Water Works and Electric, discussed in Chap. 40, which can be found in sixth edition text). Hence warrants to buy common stocks of this kind may also be said to have a special speculative advantage. But this is at bottom a quantitative rather than a qualitative matter. In our view, it is rarely possible to say *with assurance* that the long-term prospects of a particular line of business are so much better than the average as to make warrants connected with that field more attractive than any others. But if the individual speculator has definite opinions and preferences on this score, it is perfectly logical for him to follow them.

**定量考虑：低价格的重要性。**从定量角度指出决定权证相对吸引力的因素较为容易。理想的品质包括：第一，低价；第二，长期限；第三，接近市场的期权（或购买）价格。从投机理论来看，三者中最重要的无疑是权证的低价。可以通过比较1917年Sinclair Oil and Refining Corporation Warrants的情况与1929年Niagara Hudson Power Corporation *B* Warrants的情况来体现这一点。

<!--en-->
**Quantitative Considerations: Importance of Low Price.** It is an easier matter to point out the elements that govern the relative attractiveness of warrants from a quantitative standpoint. The desirable qualities are: first, a low price; second, a long duration; and thirdly, an option (or purchase) price close to the market. From the standpoint of speculative theory, the most important of the three no doubt is a low price for the warrant. This may be brought out by a comparison of the situation existing in the Sinclair Oil and Refining Corporation Warrants in 1917 and Niagara Hudson Power Corporation *B* Warrants in 1929.

*示例：*1917年发行的每1000美元Sinclair Oil and Refining Corporation票据，赋予持有人权利在1918年8月1日前以每股45美元的价格购买25股股票；在$47 1/2$价格下至1919年8月1日；以及在$50$价格下至1920年2月1日。1917年12月，股票价格跌至$25 1/4$，可以以20美元的价格购买25股权证，即每股仅花费80美分。此时，股票的市场价格远低于期权价格，但期权可以以极低的每股成本获得。后续情况非常符合投机市场的特点。不到18个月，Sinclair Oil股票价格上涨至$69 3/4$，25股权证的实际价值超过550美元。股票价格上涨175%，权证价格则上涨了2,680%。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* The warrant attached to each $1,000 Sinclair Oil and Refining Corporation note, issued in 1917, entitled the holder to buy 25 shares of stock at $45 per share until August 1, 1918; at $47 1/2$ until August 1, 1919; and at $50$ until February 1, 1920. In December 1917 the stock had declined to $25 1/4$, and a warrant for 25 shares could be bought at $20, i.e., at a cost of only 80 cents per share. Here the market price of the stock was far below the option price, but the option could be acquired at a very low cost per share. The sequel was quite characteristic of speculative markets. In less than 18 months Sinclair Oil stock rose to $69 3/4$ giving a warrant for 25 shares a realizable value of over $550. An increase of 175% in the price of the stock produced an increase of 2,680% in the price of the warrant.

Niagara Hudson Power Corporation *B* Warrants赋予持有人权利以50美元购买$3 1/2$股普通股，即每股$14.285$美元。当这些权证在1929年在纽约Curb市场上市时，价格为60美元——相当于1股权证对应17股股票——而当时股票价格为$22 1/2$。在这种情况下，投机者购买权证的每股成本几乎与购买股票相同。后来，当股票达到年度最高价31美元时，权证价格仅上涨了较小比例，至21美元。同年晚些时候，股票价格跌至$11 1/4$，权证价格则跌至最低水平2美元。这些对比数据表明，相当于17美元时，Niagara Hudson *B* Warrants的售价极其不吸引人。

<!--en-->
The Niagara Hudson Power Corporation *B* Warrants entitled the holder to buy $3 1/2$ shares of common for $50, i.e., at $14.285$ per share. When the warrants were admitted to trading on the New York Curb in 1929, they sold at 60—equivalent to 17 for a one-share warrant—while the stock was selling at $22 1/2$. In this case the speculator was paying nearly as much per share for the warrants as for the stock. When the latter advanced to its high of 31 later in the year, the warrants rose by a much smaller percentage, to 21. Still later in the same year, the price of the stock broke to $11 1/4$, and then the warrants collapsed to a low of 2. These comparative figures show that at the equivalent of 17 the Niagara Hudson *B* Warrants were selling at an extraordinarily unattractive price.

*相对价格较低很重要。*从技术角度而言，权证的价格不仅本身要低，还要相对于普通股票的价格更低。可以通过对比1928年的商业投资信托公司权证与1933年的美国及外国力量公司权证来说明这一点。

<!--en-->
*Low Relative Price Important.* It is technically desirable that the price of a warrant be low not only in itself but also in relation to the price of the common stock. This point may be shown by a comparison of Commercial Investment Trust Corporation Warrants in 1928 with American and Foreign Power Company Warrants in 1933.

*示例：* 1928年8月，商业投资信托公司权证以每份6美元的价格出售。它们赋予持有者权利，在1929年底之前可以以每股90美元的价格购买半股普通股，之后直到1931年1月1日，价格降至100美元。此时普通股的价格约为70美元。因此，1股权证的购买成本相当于12美元，约相当于当前股票价值的1/6。尽管权证规定的购买价格相对较高，但由于资金成本要低得多，权证可能被认为具有相对于股票的投机优势。（实际上，1928-1929年间，权证的价格上涨了11倍，而普通股的价格上涨了3倍。）如第48章所示，1933年11月，1股美国及外国电力公司的权证可以以7美元购买，与普通股价格完全持平。但当时普通股本身仅以10美元的价格出售，使得7美元的权证不再具有特殊投机优势。正如我们稍后将看到的，这使股票和权证一起属于“伪”低价投机类别，即第41章开头讨论的那种类型。

<!--en-->
*Examples:* Commercial Investment Trust Corporation Warrants sold at $6 each in August 1928. They entitled the holder to buy $1/2$ share of common at $90$ per share until the end of 1929 and at 100 thereafter until January 1, 1931. Thecommon was then selling at about 70. The warrant for 1 share thus represented a commitment of $12, or about $1/6$ the current value of the stock. Despite the relatively high purchase price specified in the warrant, the latter might be considered as having a speculative advantage over the stock because of the much smaller money cost involved. (As it happened, the price of the warrants advanced elevenfold in 1928–1929 as against a threefold rise in the common.) As shown in Chap. 48, in November 1933, warrants for one share of American and Foreign Power could be bought at 7, representing exact parity with the common. But the fact that the common was itself selling at only 10 removed any special speculative advantage from the warrants at 7. As we shall see later, it throws the stock and the warrants together into the category of “pseudo” low-priced speculations, of the kind discussed at the beginning of Chap. 41.

上述讨论得出的结论是：从技术层面来看，某种股票认股权证只有具备低成本、长期权利，能够以与当前市场价格相差不大的价格购买股票时，才具有投机性吸引力。⁵ *示例：* 上文提到的Sinclair Oil and Commercial Investment Trust认股权证就是符合这些要求的例子。1927年的Barnsdall Oil认股权证则是一个不同寻常的例子。该认股权证以25美元的股票价格进行认购。当股票售价达到31美元时，认股权证的售价恰好为6美元，与股价持平。在这种情况下，股票价值的任何上涨都会意味着——后来确实也出现了——认股权证价格的更大比例上涨。

<!--en-->
The foregoing discussion leads to the conclusion that a given option warrant has speculative attractiveness, in a technical sense, only if it constitutes a low-cost, long-term right to purchase a stock at a price not too remote from the current market.⁵
*Examples:* The Sinclair Oil and Commercial Investment Trust Warrants, referred to above, are examples that met these requirements. An unusual example is furnished by the Barnsdall Oil warrants in 1927. These were a call on the stock at 25. When the shares were selling at 31, the warrants sold at 6, exactly at parity. In this case, any rise in the value of the stock would have meant—and later did mean—a much larger proportionate rise in the price of the warrants.

*技术优势往往不存在。*在1928-1929年权证交易最为活跃期间，这些金融工具往往以较高价格出售，无论是相对价格还是绝对价格，因此无法说它们具有比普通股票更的技术优势。在随后的经济大萧条时期，许多权证以非常低的价格发行，但此时相关普通股的价格也低得如此之低，以至于让人对权证的相对吸引力产生质疑。1939年底的情况可以通过下表中列出的代表性权证清单来说明。

<!--en-->
*Technical Advantages Often Absent.* During 1928–1929, when trading in warrants was most active, there was a tendency for these instruments to sell at high levels, both relatively and absolutely, so that they could not be said to possess any technical advantage over the typical common stock. During the ensuing depression many warrant issues were obtainable at very low prices, but here again the related common shares were also quoted so low as to call into question the comparative attractiveness of the warrant. Thesituation at the close of 1939 may be illustrated by the representative list of warrants shown in the table below.

需要指出的是，那些通过交付债券或优先发行股票来获得支付权利的权证，通常以相对于普通股的有趣价格出售。（实际上，电力与照明权证的报价低于面值。）其他低价权证则距离可实现价值太远，不值得关注。Baldwin机车和纽约市公共汽车权证的价格关系，反映了它们在市场价值规模中的不同阶段特征。⁶

<!--en-->
It is to be noted that the warrants carrying the right to make payment by turning in a bond or preferred issue at par were generally selling at an interesting price in relation to the common stock. (The Electric Power and Light warrants were actually quoted below parity.) The other low-priced warrants seemed too far away from realizable value to merit attention. The Baldwin Locomotive and New York City Omnibus price relationships are typical of their respective stages in the scale of market values.⁶

#### 认股权证作为资本结构的一部分

<!--en-->
*WARRANTS AS PART OF THE CAPITALIZATION STRUCTURE*

期权认股权证本质上是一种将未来前景要素独立化的工具。但从未来改进或提升中获益的权利本质上属于普通股股东。这是他投入资金并承担“第一风险”损失所得到的重要回报之一。因此，期权认股权证的基本事实是，它代表从普通股中*被拿走的东西*。公式很简单：

<!--en-->
Option warrants are essentially a device to give separate embodiment to the element of future prospects. But the right to benefit from future improvement or enhancement belongs inherently to the common stockholder. It is one of the important considerations that he receives in return for putting up his money and taking the “first risk” of loss. The basic factabout an option warrant, therefore, is that it represents *something that has been taken away* from the common stock. The equation is a simple one:

$$ \text{Value of common stock} + \text{value of warrants} = \text{value of common stock alone} $$

（即，如果没有认股权证的话）。

<!--en-->
(i.e., if there were no warrants).

### 认股权证代表相关股票的减项。

<!--en-->
*Warrants Represent a Subtraction from the Related Stock.*

*示例：* 这一点可以通过参考Barnsdall认股权证发行对股票价值的影响来具体说明。1926年的收益为6,077,000美元，在1,140,000股已发行股份中，每股价格为5.34美元。然而，还存在以25美元购买1,000,000股股份的认股权证，所得款项用于偿还6%的25,000,000美元债券。分析师本应假设认股权证会被行使，因此1926年的收益应从5.34美元降至每股3.54美元。到1929年，认股权证确实被行使了，收益为每股3.25美元；如果没有发行认股权证，收益将为4.76美元。全年35股认股权证的平均价格相当于认股权证的10美元价值。这意味着，由于认股权证的发行，每股约8美元从普通股价值中被扣除（否则普通股价值应为43美元）。

<!--en-->
*Example:* This point may be illustrated concretely by reference to the effect of the issuance of the Barnsdall warrants upon the value of the stock. The earnings reported for 1926 were $6,077,000, or $5.34 per share on 1,140,000 shares outstanding. However, there were also in existence warrants to buy 1,000,000 shares at $25, the proceeds to be applied to retire $25,000,000 of 6% bonds. The analyst should have assumed exercise of the warrants, thus reducing the 1926 earnings from $5.34 to $3.54 per share. In 1929, the warrants having actually been exercised, the earnings were $3.25 per share, as against $4.76 if there had been no warrants created. The average price of 35 for the year was equivalent to a value of 10 for the warrants. This meant, substantially, that about $8 per share had been taken away from the value of the common stock (which otherwise would have been worth 43) by the creation of the warrants.

这个示例清楚地表明，认股权证发行的效果是减少普通股从收益或企业价值大幅增长中获得的利益。即使以高于市场的价格购买股票，认股权证也会降低普通股的当前价值，因为这部分当前价值基于未来受益的权利。

<!--en-->
This illustration shows clearly that the effect of the creation of warrants is to diminish the benefits realized by the common from a large increase in the earnings or in the value of the business. Warrants to buy stock, even at a price above the market, therefore detract from the present value of the common stock, because part of this present value is based upon the right to benefit from future improvement.

## 稀释股票价值的危险工具。

<!--en-->
*A Dangerous Device for Diluting Stock Values.*

期权认股权证是一种根本危险且令人不满的工具，因为它会间接且通常未被察觉地稀释普通股价值。股东对认股权证发行漠不关心，没有意识到他们未来的股权部分正在被剥夺。股市通常缺乏责任感，无论是否有认股权证，都采用相同的估值标准对待普通股。因此，认股权证可能被用来向发起人或其他内部人员支付不合理的奖金，而普通股东无需担心受到理解和批评。此外，认股权证机制便于人为提高公司证券的整体市场估值，因为通过少量操纵，可以在大量发行认股权证的情况下建立较高的价值，而不降低普通股的报价。

<!--en-->
The option warrant is a fundamentally dangerous and objectionable device because it effects an indirect and usually unrecognized dilution of common-stock values. The stockholders view the issuance of warrants with indifference, failing to realize that part of their equity in the future is being taken from them. The stock market, with its usual heedlessness, applies the same basis of valuation to common shares whether warrants are outstanding or not. Hence warrants may be availed of to payunreasonable bonuses to promoters or other insiders without fear of comprehension and criticism by the rank and file of stockholders. Furthermore, the warrant device facilitates the establishment of an artificially high aggregate market valuation for a company's securities, because (with a little manipulation) large values can be established for a huge issue of warrants without reducing the quotation of the common shares.

股票期权权证在企业重组中已被证明是一种方便且吸引人的工具，因为它们使重组方能够向老股东提供某种补偿，同时表面上将公司完全移交给债权人。然而，美国证券交易委员会对此做法持反对态度，认为如果老股东确实没有权益，他们甚至无权获得权证。⁷ *归谬法*。公众未能理解，期权权证的全部价值是以普通股为代价获得的，这种做法即使不是如此有害，也显得荒谬。我们指的是最初出售附带权证的普通股以购买额外普通股的情况。这种安排并未给股东带来没有权证时不会得到的利益，也违反了合理的企业融资原则。管理得当的企业仅在需要新资本时才会出售额外股票，在这种情况下，股东通常有权按比例认购发行股票。⁸在不需要资金时给予股东认购权，从所有角度来看都是无意义的，除了欺骗人们认为正在提供有吸引力的东西。这类似于有时采用的“以票据形式支付股息”的做法，这种票据可由董事随意赎回。这种“票据”只是对普通股固有权利的另一种不必要表达，即董事认为合适时支付未来股息的权利。⁹同样，附在原始普通股发行上的期权权证也是股东参与未来股票发行的固有权利的多余表达。¹⁰对权证机制的不健康影响的进一步研究与两条更广泛的金融实践研究相结合——第一条涉及公众为企业的融资和管理所支付的价格；第二条涉及被称为“金字塔式融资”的操纵性且危险的企业行为。这些证券分析方面的内容将在后续章节中讨论。[^4453]：¹ 1936年发行的雷明顿-兰德权证是认购权和权证形式的复杂组合。如果持有人及时行使部分认购权（如实际情况那样，以市场下跌价格），则他还有权在一年后继续购买更多股票，以此类推。我们认为，这种复杂的机制要么制造不必要的投机局面，要么让熟练且知情的人比普通股东获得不当优势。

<!--en-->
Stock-option warrants have proved a convenient and appealing instrument in corporate reorganizations, because they have enabled the reorganizers to give the old stockholders a sop of some kind while ostensibly turning the company over entirely to the creditors. The S.E.C., however, has taken a stand against this practice, contending that if the old stockholders really have no equity they are not even entitled to warrants.⁷
*A Reductio ad Absurdum.* The public's failure to comprehend that all the value of option warrants is derived at the expense of the common stock has led to a practice that would be ridiculous if it were not so mischievous. We refer to the original sale of common stock carrying warrants to buy additional common stock. This arrangement gives nothing to the stockholders that they would not have without the warrant, and it violates an obvious rule of sound corporate financing. A properly managed business sells additional stock *only when new capital is needed*, and in that event the stockholders are usually entitled to subscribe pro rata to the offering.⁸ To give subscription rights to stockholders when the money is not needed is nonsensical from all viewpoints except that of deceiving people into believing that something attractive is being offered them. It resembles the practice, sometimes indulged in, of declaring dividends in "scrip" which is redeemable at the pleasure of the directors. This "scrip" is an unnecessary expression in separate form of a right that the common stock possesses inherently, *viz.*, to receive future dividends when the directors see fit to pay them.⁹ Similarly these option warrants attached to original issues of common stock are a superfluous expression of the stockholders' inherent right to participate in future stock offerings.¹⁰
A further study of the unwholesome implications of the warrant device is integrated with two broader lines of inquiry into financial practices—the first relating to the price paid by the public for the financing and management of business; the second relating to that group of manipulative and dangerous corporate practices referred to as “pyramiding.” These aspects of security analysis will be considered in the ensuing chapters.
[^4453]: ¹ The Remington-Rand rights, issued in 1936, were a somewhat overingenious combination of the subscription-right and the warrant forms. If the holder exercised part of his subscription right promptly (at an indicated market loss, as it happened), he would then have a further right to buy more stock up to a year later, and so on. In our view elaborate devices of this kind either create unnecessary speculative situations or give the adroit and the wellinformed an undue advantage over the ordinary stockholder.

But a warrant arrangement under which old stockholders can buy out old creditors at a price that will pay them off, e.g., the Erie plan, dated January 1939, has much more to recommend it.

## 注释 2

<!--en-->
*NOTE 2*

"弗里斯科6%优先股"在1931年跌至$4\frac{1}{2}$，1932年（道路进入破产程序的那一年）跌至每股1美元。根据I.C.C.重组审查计划，该股票将被注销。

<!--en-->
The 'Frisco 6% Preferred declined to $4\frac{1}{2}$ in 1931 and to $1 per share in 1932, the year in which the road went into receivership. The issue is to be wiped out under the I.C.C. examiner's plan of reorganization for the road.

欧文斯-伊利诺伊玻璃公司债券在次年（1933年7月）以$101\frac{1}{4}$的价格被赎回。

<!--en-->
The Owens-Illinois Glass Co. bonds were called the very next year (July 1933) at $101\frac{1}{4}$.

赖特航空股票在1925年跌至$32\frac{3}{8}$，1929年大幅升至$299$，并在那一年支付了100%的股票股息。新股票在1932年跌至$3\frac{7}{8}$（按旧基准相当于$7\frac{3}{4}$）。到1936年，价格回升至$140\frac{3}{4}$（按旧基准相当于$281\frac{1}{2}$），但尽管因战争订单导致收益大幅增加，仍无法在1939年恢复这一价格。1935–1939年收益急剧上升，加上已确认和潜在的战争业务，可能导致1939年底股票售价是1935–1939年平均收益的35倍。

<!--en-->
Wright Aeronautical stock rose to $32\frac{3}{8}$ in 1925 and spectacularly to $299$ in 1929 prior to a 100% stock-dividend payment in that year. The new stock collapsed to $3\frac{7}{8}$ in 1932 (equivalent to $7\frac{3}{4}$ on the old basis). It recovered in a manner suggestive of manipulation to $140\frac{3}{4}$ in 1936 (equivalent to $281\frac{1}{2}$ on the old basis), a price that it proved unable to regain in 1939 despite greatly increased earnings due to war orders. A sharply rising trend of earnings for the years 1935–1939, coupled with booked and prospective war business, may account for the fact that the stock at the end of 1939 was selling at thirty-five times the average earnings for 1935–1939.

在接下来的六年中，I.R.T.债券每年获得7%的利息，约1.7%用于偿还本金。1939年，纽约市同意购买I.R.T.资产，约定债券持有人可获得未付本金的87½%，5%债券持有人可获得本金的82½%，以3%纽约市债券（企业股票）形式支付。我们认为，债券背后的充足抵押品使其有权按面值偿还。然而，1933年购买7%股票的买家，相比以相同价格购买5%股票的买家，情况会好得多。假设以面值纽约市债券支付，债券持有人总共获得的金额（包括利息），每1000张债券约为1,340美元，而5%债券约为1,125美元。

<!--en-->
In the ensuing six years the I.R.T. Notes received 7% annually on account of interest and almost 1.7% annually applied against principal. In 1939 the city of New York contracted to purchase the I.R.T. properties on terms to realize 87½% of the unpaid principal for the noteholders and 82½% of the principal of the 5% bondholders, payable in 3% New York City bonds (Corporate Stock). In our view the ample collateral behind the notes entitled them to repayment at par. Nevertheless, the buyer of the 7s in 1933 would have fared substantially better than a purchaser of the 5s at the same price. Assuming payment in New York City bonds worth par, the total received by the noteholders, including interest, would be about $1,340 per $1,000 note against about $1,125 per 5% bond.

1936年12月，派拉蒙电影公司向第一优先股支付12美元的累计股息。此后一直定期支付该股票的股息，但直到1939年才支付普通股的股息。1937年初，第一优先股和普通股价格都大幅上涨，但同年晚些时候，优先股价格远高于普通股——这种情况自那时起一直持续。

<!--en-->
Paramount Pictures paid $12 of accumulated dividends on the First Preferred in December 1936. It has continued to pay dividends regularly on that issue since, but paid no dividends on the common until 1939. Early in 1937 both the First Preferred and common enjoyed a substantial rise in price, but later in the year the Preferred sold at a substantial premium over the common—a condition that has generally prevailed since then.

## 注释 3

<!--en-->
*NOTE 3*

### "便宜股票"与"贵股票"

<!--en-->
*“CHEAP STOCKS” vs. “DEAR STOCKS”*

在1936年和1938年，在作者的指导下，尝试测试以高于前一年收益的高倍数出售的股票与以低于该收益的低倍数出售的股票的相对表现。从1924年到1931年的每年3月1日进行了八项独立研究。所有在纽约证券交易所上市的工业股票按3月1日价格与前一年收益的比例排序。（财政年度不在12月31日结束的公司，以及前一年每股收益低于1美元的公司被排除。）从剩余公司中选取最高和最低四分位数进行后续比较。平均而言，最高四分位数最初相对于收益的价格约为最低四分度的三倍。

<!--en-->
An effort was made in 1936 and 1938 under the direction of the authors to test the relative performance of stocks selling at a high multiple of the previous year’s earnings and those selling at a low multiple of such earnings. Eight separate studies were made, as of March 1 in each year from 1924 through 1931. All the industrial shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange were arranged in order of the ratio of the March 1 price to the previous year’s earnings. (Companies with fiscal years not ending on December 31 and those earning less than $1 per share in the previous year were excluded.) Of the remaining companies the top and bottom quartiles were then taken for subsequent comparison. On theaverage, the top quartile sold originally about three times as high in relation to earnings as did the bottom quartile.

研究的因素包括市场价格的后续变化以及随后的收益和股息支付记录。我们试图确定购买高倍数（"贵"）或低倍数（"便宜"）股票的买家在以下方面表现是否更好：（1）未来价格变动及股息收入；（2）未来收益与支付价格的关系。研究从选定初始日期后的每年3月1日开始进行。

<!--en-->
The factors studied included later changes in market price and the ensuing record of earnings and dividend payments. We sought to determine whether the buyer of the high-multiple (“dear”) or low-multiple (“cheap”) stocks would fare better with respect to (1) future price changes plus dividend receipts and (2) future earnings in relation to price paid. Tests were made as of March 1 of each year following the initial date selected.

为节省空间，我们没有在此提供研究的详细结果。总体而言，这些结果并不具有决定性，因为它们没有表明某一组明显具有优势。可以得出的结论是，以前一年收益的低倍数出售的股票表现更好。虽然"贵股票"后来相对于更便宜的群体改善了收益和股息——这是预期之中的——但这种改善似乎不足以抵消这些股票最初的溢价。它们的表现在好年份和坏年份也未能持续足够长的时间，无法确保它们最终比"便宜股票"更便宜。

<!--en-->
To save space the detailed results of our study are not given here. On the whole they are inconclusive, in that they do not point to a consistent advantage enjoyed by one group or the other. Such inferences as can be drawn favor the stocks selling at the low multiple of the previous year’s earnings. Although the dear stocks later improved their earnings and dividends as against the cheaper group—which was to be expected—this improvement does not seem to be great enough (over an eight-year period) to offset the initial premium paid for these issues. Nor was their better showing sufficiently sustained, in good and bad years, to make certain that they would *eventually* prove cheaper than the cheap stocks.

感谢欧文·卡恩先生对本研究的帮助。

<!--en-->
Acknowledgments are due Mr. Irving Kahn for his aid in this study.

## 注释 4

<!--en-->
*NOTE 4*

美国快递公司部分财务历史显示，将财产权益从股票形式转换为债券形式，为新证券获得了买家，但这些新证券的安全性较低且收益也较低，比股票发行要差。

<!--en-->
A part of the financial history of the U.S. Express Co. shows how the conversion of an interest in property from the stock form to the bond form obtained buyers for the new securities which were both less safe and less profitable than the stock issue.

1918年，该公司的唯一资产是位于纽约市rector街2号的建筑物，以及价值相对较低的其他房地产。这些资产的所有权由100,000股股票代表，每股价格为15美元。次年，rector街的建筑物以3,725,000美元出售，买家通过以3,000,000美元按面值出售的抵押贷款来部分支付购买费用，该贷款以建筑物的留置权作为担保。在处置其他资产后，美国快递公司向股东支付了每股39.25美元的清算股息。

<!--en-->
In 1918 the sole assets of the company consisted of a building at 2 Rector Street, New York City, and miscellaneous real estate of relatively slight value. Ownership of these assets was represented by 100,000 shares of stock selling at $15 per share. The following year the Rector Street building was sold for $3,725,000, the buyer financing the purchase in part by thesale at par of $3,000,000 first-mortgage bonds secured by a lien on the building. After disposing of its other assets, U. S. Express Co. paid liquidating dividends to its shareholders of $39.25 per share.

15美元的美国快递公司股票与按面值出售的债券在本质优势方面存在显著差异。前者的买家为获得rector街物业及其他资产的*完全所有权*，需支付相当于1,500,000美元；而后者的买家仅为获得rector街物业的*有限权益*，需支付3,000,000美元。显然，15美元的股票比按面值出售的债券更安全、更具吸引力。显然，公众将股票视为投机工具，而债券则被视为对股票背后资产的部分权益投资。"债券"这一标题的神奇影响可能解释了这一异常现象。

<!--en-->
There is a striking contrast between the essential merits of the U. S. Express Co. stock at 15 and of these bonds at par. Buyers of the former were paying the equivalent of $1,500,000 for *complete ownership* of the Rector Street property, plus the other assets. Buyers of the latter were paying $3,000,000 for a *limited interest* in the Rector Street property alone. Obviously the stock at 15 was both a safer and a more attractive commitment than the bonds were at par. Apparently the public regarded the stock as a speculation and the bonds, representing only a part interest in the assets behind the stock, as an investment. A part of the explanation of this anomaly probably lay in the magic influence of the title “bond.”

关于这一例子的更详细说明及来源参考，请参见本著作1934年版第617–618页。

<!--en-->
For a more detailed statement of this example, with source references, see pp. 617–618 of the 1934 edition of this work.

布鲁克林Court-Livingston办公大楼的历史是这一原则的较近期例证。在最初的第一笔抵押贷款被取消后，除某些租赁土地外，该物业的所有权由3,880股股票代表。1939年初，股票价格为每股30美元，表明公司资产总价值为116,400美元。然而当时公司持有约180,000美元现金。1939年4月，该物业以250,000美元出售，股东后来收到每股约110美元的权益清算款。买家向储蓄银行办理了285,000美元的抵押贷款，覆盖整个物业，包括之前租赁的土地。由于部分地块存在租赁义务，这个例子不如美国快递大楼案例那么清晰。但Court-Livingston股票售价远低于公司现金持有量，表明在债券形式通常是常规融资方式的情况下，使用了股票形式导致了极端的低估。

<!--en-->
A more recent illustration of this principle is afforded by the history of the Court-Livingston Office Building in Brooklyn. After foreclosure of the original first mortgage, ownership of the property (except as to certain leased land) was represented by 3,880 shares of stock. Early in 1939 the stock was quoted at $30 per share, indicating a total value of $116,400 for the company’s assets. At that time, however, it held about $180,000 in cash. In April 1939 the property was sold for $250,000, and the stockholders later received about $110 per share in liquidation of their interest. The buyer placed a mortgage of $285,000 with a savings bank, covering the entire property including the land formerly leased. The rental obligation existing with respect to part of the plot makes this example less clear-cut than the U. S. Express building case. But the fact that the Court-Livingston stock sold for much less than the applicable cash holdings shows the extraordinary undervaluation resulting from the use of the *stock form* under conditions in which the *bond form* is the usual and expected medium of financing.

*NOTE 6*

National Biscuit Co. Preferred的投资属性有令人信服的证据，可通过其股价历史与股息记录证明。自1898年成立以来，公司一直定期支付每股7美元的年度股息。自1907年起，该股票从未以低于面值（$100）的价格出售。1908-1939年期间，年度最高价与最低价的平均值为140.6美元，此时每年7美元的股息收益率为5%。在纽约证券交易所的整个上市历史（1899-1939年）中，平均值为132.75美元，收益率为5.27%。这一平均值涵盖了1900年79$\frac{1}{2}$美元和1939年175美元的价格区间。自首次上市以来的41年中，只有5年是以低于面值的价格出售的。

<!--en-->
Convincing evidence of the investment character of National Biscuit Co. Preferred is found in the price history and dividend record of the issue. The annual dividend of $7 per share has been paid regularly since organization of thecompany in 1898. The issue has not sold below par ($100) since 1907. The average of the annual high and low prices for 1908–1939 was 140.6, on which the annual dividend of $7 has yielded 5%. A similar average for the entire history of the issue on the New York Stock Exchange (1899–1939) is 132.75 and a yield of 5.27%. This average covers a range of $79\frac{1}{2}$ in 1900 and 175 in 1939. In only five out of the forty-one years since the issue was first listed has it sold at a price below par.

## 注意 7

<!--en-->
*NOTE 7*

2500万美元的Seaboard-All Florida铁路第一抵押贷款6%黄金债券A系列，到期日为1935年8月1日。这些债券最初于1925年以价格$98\frac{1}{2}$和利息形式提供。这些债券是Seaboard-All Florida铁路公司、佛罗里达西部与北部铁路公司和东海岸与西海岸铁路公司的共同责任。此外，通过Seaboard航空铁路公司背书的无条件担保，进一步保障本金和利息的安全，该公司以至少每年净租金等于该抵押贷款下所有未偿还债券的年度利息费用的价格租赁了多条铁路的资产。

<!--en-->
Twenty-five million dollars of Seaboard-All Florida Railway First Mortgage 6% Gold Bonds, Series A, due Aug. 1, 1935, were originally offered in 1925 at $98\frac{1}{2}$ and interest. The bonds were joint and several obligations of the Seaboard-All Florida Ry., Florida Western & Northern R.R. Co., and the East & West Coast Ry. They were further secured by an unconditional guarantee with respect to both principal and interest, through endorsement by the Seaboard Air Line Ry. Co., which leased the properties of the several roads at a minimum annual net rental equal to the annual interest charges on all bonds outstanding under the mortgage.

出售这些债券所得款项主要用于偿还出租方道路的未偿还首笔抵押贷款债务，并建设约217英里的新铁路线路，位于佛罗里达州东海岸和西海岸。因此，这些债券对约475英里新建成和已开通的线路拥有优先留置权。

<!--en-->
The proceeds from the sale of these bonds were used mainly to redeem outstanding first-mortgage obligations of the lessor roads and to construct about 217 miles of new trackage along the east and west coasts of Florida. Thus the bonds had a first lien on approximately 475 miles of newly constructed and established lines.

1931年2月2日，Seaboard-All Florida Ry.被接管，此前Seaboard Air Line Ry. Co.已被接管，这些债券的利息已逾期未付。

<!--en-->
The Seaboard-All Florida Ry. went into the hands of receivers on Feb. 2, 1931, following receivership for the Seaboard Air Line Ry. Co. and a default in interest due on these bonds.

尽管这些债券的购买者提供了24,625,000美元用于支付收购和建设佛罗里达铁路资产的成本，但到1931年12月，他们的债券价格已跌至每美元仅1美分，市场对其投资价值的评估仅为250,000美元。到1939年底，评估价值已上升至940,000美元，即每美元3.875美分。

<!--en-->
Although the buyers of these bonds provided $24,625,000 to defray the cost of acquiring and constructing Florida railway properties, by December 1931 their bonds were selling as low as 1 cent on the dollar, the market appraising the value of their investment at only $250,000. At the end of 1939 the appraisal had risen to $940,000, or 3.875 cents on the dollar.

## 注意 10

<!--en-->
*NOTE 10*

密苏里、堪萨斯与德克萨斯铁路公司于1915年落入接管人手中。在此之前，1990年第4期债券在1905年的价格曾高达$104\frac{1}{4}$，而直到1914年，价格仍维持在$91\frac{7}{8}$。在导致1915年被接管的经济困难发生之前，该债券的记录明显属于高等级投资债券。在1903年至1912年这11年间，其最低出售价格为$98\frac{1}{2}$（即1907年恐慌年份）。

<!--en-->
The Missouri, Kansas & Texas Ry. Company went into the hands of receivers in 1915. Prior thereto the First 4s of 1990 had sold as high as $104\frac{1}{4}$ in 1905 and as late as 1914 had sold at $91\frac{7}{8}$. Before the financial difficulties leading to the 1915 receivership, the record of this issue was distinctly that of a high-grade, investment bond. During the eleven years 1903 to 1912, inclusive, the lowest price at which it sold was $98\frac{1}{2}$ (in the panic year 1907).

在漫长的接管期间，利息支付被推迟，债券在市场上以低价交易。虽然避免了技术性违约，但该债券的投资价值却消失了——在接管期间，债券售价低至52又1/8美元。1921年当重组计划宣布时，债券售价低至56美元；直到1927年，当售价超过90美元时，它们才重新恢复作为投资债券的风采。因此，最初的留置权并未能保护持有人免受财务困难期间市场大幅下跌的影响。

<!--en-->
During the protracted receivership interest payments were deferred and the bonds were traded “flat” in the market. Although technical default was avoided, the investment status of the issue disappeared, the bonds selling as low as $52\frac{1}{8}$ during the receivership. In 1921 when the plan ofreorganization was announced, the bonds sold as low as 56, and it was not until 1927 that they regained a semblance of their former prestige as an investment issue by selling above 90. Thus the first lien did not protect the holder from a substantial market decline during the period of financial difficulty.

正如文本第2章所述，《布鲁克林联合高架铁路第一五节债券》也展示了类似的债券情况，该债券预计于1950年发行。这是布鲁克林快速交通公司高架线路关键部分的担保债权，于1918年12月31日落入接管人手中，并于1923年重组为布鲁克林-曼哈顿交通公司。该债券在1903年至1917年间被归类为一级投资品种，在此期间从未低于90美元出售，除了1907年的恐慌时期降至85美元，以及1917年接管即将实施时。尽管重组并未影响该债券的情况，但在1920年，当接管仍生效时，其价格最低跌至55美元；直到1926年——即接管结束三年后，才恢复之前的水平。

<!--en-->
The same sort of picture is presented by the record of Brooklyn Union Elevated R.R. First 5s, due in 1950, described in Chap. 2 of the text. This was an underlying lien on essential parts of the elevated lines of the Brooklyn Rapid Transit Co. which went into the hands of receivers on Dec. 31, 1918 and was reorganized as the Brooklyn-Manhattan Transit Corp. in 1923. The issue ranked as a first-grade investment from 1903 to 1917 and never sold below 90 during this period, except in the panic of 1907 when it dropped to 85, and in 1917 when the receivership appeared imminent. Although the issue was not disturbed by the reorganization, it sold as low as 55 in 1920, while the receivership was still in effect, and did not regain its former standing until 1926, three years after the termination of the receivership.

Choctaw & Memphis R.R.的第一笔抵押贷款5s，到期日为1949年，于1934年7月1日利息部分违约。在1938年和1939年，最低出价分别为21和32。但芝加哥、Rock Island & Pacific铁路公司的重组计划，为它们作为系统中的一个小型基础环节得以平稳发展提供了重要支持。（关于此问题的讨论见第706页。）

<!--en-->
Choctaw & Memphis R.R. First Mortgage 5s, due 1949, defaulted as to interest on July 1, 1934. In 1938 and 1939 the low bids were 21 and 32, respectively. But the reorganization plan for the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Ry. Co. provides substantially for their emergence undisturbed as a small underlying issue of the system. (See discussion of this issue on p. 706.)

<!--en-->
*NOTE 12*

有关以下示例的更详细内容，请参见本著作1934年版的第640–641页。

<!--en-->
For more complete details concerning the following examples see pp. 640–641 of the 1934 edition of this work.

1. Gulf States Steel Co.在1927年以98又3/4美元出售了5½%债券，并在1930年再次发行了同一批次的债券。在1922-1929年间，该公司对相关风险的覆盖倍数平均为4.88倍；该时期的最低覆盖倍数是在1926年的3½倍。但公司在1930-1932年期间在利息费用之前仍处于亏损状态，债券数量在1932年降至最低的21只。
2. Marion Steam Shovel Co.，在1927年以$99\frac{1}{2}$的价格出售了预计于1947年发行的First 6s债券，在1922–1929年间平均对债券进行了4.11次覆盖。该时期的最低覆盖次数出现在1928年，为2.78次。但在接下来的九年中，有七年公司处于利息支出前的亏损状态，所售债券价格低至每美元仅20美分。
3. McCrory Stores Corp.在1926年以98的价格出售了一次Debenture 5 1/2s债券。在1922-1931年间，该公司用平均5.32倍的资金覆盖了1931年的固定债务。此后，收入急剧下降，公司未能偿还债务。1933年，该公司申请破产，债券价格最低跌至21 5/8。然而，这三次发行的债券在后续几年中都恢复了大部分或全部价格下跌幅度。

<!--en-->
1. Gulf States Steel Co., which sold an issue of $5\frac{1}{2}\%$ Debentures in 1927 at $98\frac{3}{4}$ and further bonds of the same issue in 1930, covered the 1929 charges thereon an average of 4.88 times in 1922–1929. The minimum coverage during that period was $3\frac{1}{2}$ times in 1926. But the company operated at a deficit before interest charges in 1930–1932, and the bonds declined to a low of 21 in 1932.
2. Marion Steam Shovel Co., which in 1927 sold an issue of First 6s, due 1947, at $99\frac{1}{2}$, covered the charges thereon an average of 4.11 times in 1922–1929. The minimum coverage during that period was 2.78 times in 1928. But in seven of the ensuing nine years the company operated at a deficit before interest charges, and the bonds sold as low as 20 cents on the dollar.
3. McCrory Stores Corp., which sold an issue of Debenture 5 1/2s at 98 in 1926, covered all its 1931 fixed charges an average of 5.32 times in the decade 1922–1931. Earnings declined sharply thereafter, and the company failed to earn its charges. In 1933 the company was petitioned into bankruptcy, and the bonds sold as low as 21 5/8.
All three of these issues, however, recovered all or most of their price decline in subsequent years.

<!--en-->

在*A组*中，只有8只债券的最大市场价格下降超过10%，而*B组*中只有9只债券没有出现这种价格下跌。在*A组*的8只债券中，除Gotham Silk Hosiery 5s和Jones & Laughlin 4 1/4s外，其余都恢复到了1937年高点的四点以内。在*B组*的9只保持价格的债券中，除Houston Oil 5 1/2s和Koppers Co. 4s外，其余在1936年一年内收益都超过3倍。

<!--en-->
Only eight issues in Group *A* lost more than 10% of their maximum market price, and only nine issues in Group *B* failed to suffer this percentage decline. Of these eight bonds in Group *A*, all but two (Gotham Silk Hosiery 5s and Jones & Laughlin 4 1/4s) later recovered to within four points of the1937 high. Of the nine bonds in Group *B* that maintained their price, all but two (Houston Oil 5 1/2s and Koppers Co. 4s) had earned their interest better than three times in the single year 1936.

## 注释14

<!--en-->
*NOTE 14*

关于经济衰退前收益能力崩溃的更多细节，请参见本著作1934年版第641–643页。

<!--en-->
See pp. 641–643 of the 1934 edition of this work for fuller details concerning the following examples of predepression collapses in earnings power:

1. Botany Consolidated Mills, Inc.的First 6 1/2s，到期日为1934年，于1924年发行。当年及之前七年的净可用资金平均约为债券费用的5 3/4倍，这些债券直到1926年以固定价值价格出售，之后公司出现运营亏损。此后（1927年有一个微小的例外），运营亏损持续扩大，直到1932年公司被接管。在1932年，这些债券以每美元5分的价格出售。在1928年和1929年经济繁荣时期，价格分别低至59和40。
2. R. Hoe & Co.的First 6 1/2s，到期日为1934年，于1924年发行。前三年平均收益为新债券利息费用与其他固定费用之和的3.2倍，未包含发行新资本带来的收益。1924年收益下降，随后几年继续下降，1929年除外。尽管如此，尽管覆盖率不足，这些债券直到1928年仍接近面值出售。之后在1929年价格降至75。1932年公司被接管，债券价格低至6 1/8。
3. Long-Bell Lumber Corp.在1922–1932年期间净收益几乎持续下降。当Long-Bell Lumber Co.（子公司）在1926年出售First Mortgage 6s时，平均覆盖率远高于工业产品所需的最低标准。但1926–1929年的平均覆盖率仅为1.37倍，此后公司一直存在运营亏损，直到1932年债券违约。
4. National Radiator Corp.的Debenture $6\frac{1}{2}$s，到期日为1947年，1927年以面值出售。1922–1926年的可用收益平均为债券费用的3.5倍，未包含新资本带来的额外收益。1927年固定费用覆盖率足够；但随后三年出现运营亏损，1931年任命了接管人。

<!--en-->
1. Botany Consolidated Mills, Inc., First 6 1/2s, due 1934, were issued in 1924. Net available for the charges thereon in that year and in the seven preceding years averaged close to 5 3/4 times the charges, and the bonds sold at fixed-value prices until 1926 when the company suffered an operating deficit. Thereafter (with an insignificant exception in 1927) large and growing operating deficits were shown until receivership overtook the company in 1932. In the latter year the bonds sold at 5 cents on the dollar. They had sold as low as 59 and 40, respectively, in the prosperous years 1928 and 1929.
2. R. Hoe & Co. First 6 1/2s, due 1934, were issued in 1924. Average earnings in the preceding three years were 3.2 times the sum of interest charges on the new bonds and other fixed charges, without allowance for any earnings from the new capital raised by the issue. Earnings declined in 1924 and continued to decline in the ensuing years with the exception of 1929. Nonetheless, the bonds continued to sell close to par, despite inadequate coverage, until 1928. Thereafter they declined to as low as 75 in 1929. In 1932 receivership intervened, and the bonds sold as low as 6 1/8.
3. Long-Bell Lumber Corp. showed an almost uninterrupted decline in net earnings for the period 1922–1932. When Long-Bell Lumber Co. (a subsidiary) sold First Mortgage 6s in 1926, average coverage was well above the minimum required for industrial exhibits. But average coverage for 1926–1929 was only 1.37 times, and the company exhibited operating deficits thereafter until default on the bonds in 1932.
4. National Radiator Corp. Debenture $6\frac{1}{2}$s, due 1947, were offered at par in 1927. Available earnings in 1922–1926 had averaged 3.5 times the charges on the bonds, without allowing for additional earnings on the new capital. Coverage of fixed charges was adequate in 1927; but operating deficits were encountered in the ensuing three years, and receivers were appointed in 1931.

First 7s的1932年8月1日优惠券，到期日为1955年，也因匈牙利政府颁布法令而未能支付：该法令规定，自1931年12月23日起，匈牙利对境外以外币承担的金融义务将暂停支付。Deutsche Bank 6% Notes的到期日为1932年9月1日，由于德国政府实施外汇限制，本金在到期时未得到支付。持有者可选择立即以马克支付并留在德国，或于1935年9月1日以美元支付，同时立即获得2%的现金溢价。Saxon Public Works, Inc. 5% Notes的到期日为1932年7月15日，也达成了类似的妥协。

For example, the Sept. 1, 1932 coupon on Alpine-Montan Steel Corp. First 7s, due in 1955, was not paid because of foreign exchange restrictions imposed by the Austrian government, although the corporation possessed sufficient domestic funds to make the payment. The Aug. 1, 1932 coupon on Rima Steel Corp. First 7s, due 1955, was not paid owing to a decree of the Hungarian government suspending payments abroad in foreign currencies on Hungarian financial obligations, from and after Dec. 23, 1931. The principal of Deutsche Bank 6% Notes, due Sept. 1, 1932, was not paid at maturity owing to exchange restrictions imposed by the German government. Holders were offered immediate payment in marks to be left in Germany or payment on Sept. 1, 1935 in dollars with an immediate payment of a cash premium of 2% in dollars. A similar compromise was worked out with respect to Saxon Public Works, Inc., 5% Notes due July 15, 1932.

## 注释17

<!--en-->
*NOTE 17*

关于投资素质和设备信托义务的详细分析，请参阅Kenneth Duncan所著的《设备义务》，第七章，纽约，1924年。关于自1900年以来铁路重组中设备义务违约及其处理情况，可参见本优秀著作第229–239页。简要引用Duncan在1924年撰写的内容（第199–200页）：“仅有三个案例中，设备证券持有人必须接受以其他证券代替现金的妥协方案；仅有两个案例中，他们不得不重新获取设备并出售它；在任何情况下，最终都不会无法支付，无论是以现金还是其他证券形式，这些证券后来可以出售并获得与违约设备义务本金相当的金额。”另见A.S. Dewing所著的《公司证券研究》，第九章，纽约，1934年。

<!--en-->
For a detailed treatment of the investment qualities and record of equipment-trust obligations the student is referred to Kenneth Duncan, *Equipment Obligations*, Chap. VII, New York, 1924. A case history of defaults on equipment obligations and their treatment in railroad reorganizations since 1900 will be found at pp. 229–239 of this excellent treatise. To quote briefly from Duncan, writing in 1924 (pp. 199–200), “In only three instances has it been necessary for the holders of equipment securities to accept a compromise in the form of receiving other securities instead of cash, in only two instances did they have to retake the equipment and sell it, and in no case did payment finally fail to be made, either in cash or in other securities which could later have been sold for as much as the principal of the equipment obligations on which default has occurred.” See also A.S. Dewing, *A Study of Corporation Securities*, Chap. IX, New York, 1934.
